https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Nsf6.label: Metal Window and Door Manufacturing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Nsf6.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing metal framed windows (i.e., typically using purchased glass) and metal doors. Examples of products made by these establishments are metal door frames; metal framed window and door screens; and metal molding and trim (except automotive).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/NtZn.label: Other Noncitrus Fruit Farming
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/NtZn.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in growing noncitrus fruits (except apples, grapes, berries, and fruit(s) and tree nut(s) combinations).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/NvJC.label: Industrial Design Services
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/NvJC.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in creating and developing designs and specifications that optimize the use, value, and appearance of products. These services can include the determination of the materials, construction, mechanisms, shape, color, and surface finishes of the product, taking into consideration human characteristics and needs, safety, market appeal, and efficiency in production, distribution, use, and maintenance. Establishments providing automobile or furniture industrial design services or industrial design consulting services are included in this industry.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/NwpC.label: Navigational, Measuring, Electromedical, and Control Instruments Manufacturing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/NwpC.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing navigational, measuring, electromedical, and control instruments. Examples of products made by these establishments are aeronautical instruments, appliance regulators and controls (except switches), laboratory analytical instruments, navigation and guidance systems, and physical properties testing equipment.
english_labels: Navigational, Measuring, Electromedical, and Control Instruments Manufacturing

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/NxFQ.label: Other Basic Organic Chemical Manufacturing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/NxFQ.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing basic organic chemicals (except petrochemicals, industrial gases, and synthetic dyes and pigments).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/O-vt.label: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services
english_labels: Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/O1Q0.label: Floriculture Production
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/O1Q0.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in growing and/or producing floriculture products (e.g., cut flowers and roses, cut cultivated greens, potted flowering and foliage plants, and flower seeds) under cover and in open fields.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/O2ux.label: Mattress Manufacturing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/O2ux.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing innerspring, box spring, and noninnerspring mattresses.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/OA1H.label: Promoters of Performing Arts, Sports, and Similar Events without Facilities
english_labels: Promoters of Performing Arts, Sports, and Similar Events without Facilities

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/OALn.label: Farm Product Raw Material Merchant Wholesalers
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/OALn.definition: This industry group comprises establishments primarily engaged in the merchant wholesale distribution of agricultural products (except raw milk, live poultry, and fresh fruits and vegetables), such as grains, field beans, livestock, and other farm product raw materials (excluding seeds).
english_labels: Farm Product Raw Material Merchant Wholesalers

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/ODSS.label: Coin-Operated Laundries and Drycleaners
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/ODSS.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in (1) operating facilities with coin- or card-operated or similar self-service laundry and drycleaning equipment for customer use on the premises and/or (2) supplying and servicing coin- or card-operated or similar self-service laundry and drycleaning equipment for customer use in places of business operated by others, such as apartments and dormitories.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/OE8w.label: Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing
english_labels: Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/OHRg.label: Aerospace Product and Parts Manufacturing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/OHRg.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in one or more of the following: (1) manufacturing complete aircraft, missiles, or space vehicles; (2) manufacturing aerospace engines, propulsion units, auxiliary equipment, or parts; (3) developing and making prototypes of aerospace products; (4) aircraft conversion (i.e., major modifications to systems); and (5) complete aircraft or propulsion systems overhaul and rebuilding (i.e., periodic restoration of aircraft to original design specifications).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/OJe1.label: Beverage Manufacturing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/OJe1.definition: This industry group comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing soft drinks and ice; purifying and bottling water; and manufacturing brewery, winery, and distillery products.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/OL-7.label: Stone Mining and Quarrying
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/OL-7.definition: This industry comprises (1) establishments primarily engaged in developing the mine site, mining or quarrying dimension stone (i.e., rough blocks and/or slabs of stone), or mining and quarrying crushed and broken stone and/or (2) preparation plants primarily engaged in beneficiating stone (e.g., crushing, grinding, washing, screening, pulverizing, and sizing).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/ORBf.label: Drugs and Druggists' Sundries Merchant Wholesalers
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/ORBf.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in the merchant wholesale distribution of biological and medical products; botanical drugs and herbs; and pharmaceutical products intended for internal and/or external consumption in such forms as ampoules, tablets, capsules, vials, ointments, powders, solutions, and suspensions.
english_labels: Drugs and Druggists' Sundries Merchant Wholesalers

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/OYSj.label: Transportation Equipment and Supplies (except Motor Vehicle) Merchant Wholesalers
english_labels: Transportation Equipment and Supplies (except Motor Vehicle) Merchant Wholesalers

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/O_Zc.label: Professional Employer Organizations
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/O_Zc.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in providing human resources and human resource management services to client businesses and households. Establishments in this industry operate in a co-employment relationship with client businesses or organizations and are specialized in performing a wide range of human resource and personnel management duties, such as payroll, payroll tax, benefits administration, workers' compensation, unemployment, and human resource administration. Professional employer organizations (PEOs) are responsible for payroll, including withholding and remitting employment-related taxes, for some or all of the employees of their clients, and also serve as the employer of those employees for benefits and related purposes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/O_oF.label: Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance
english_labels: Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/OcUX.label: All Other Textile Product Mills
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/OcUX.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing nonapparel textile products (except carpet, rugs, curtains, linens, bags, and canvas products) from purchased materials. This industry includes establishments primarily engaged in decorative stitching such as embroidery or other art needlework on textile products, including apparel.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Of7D.label: Creamery Butter Manufacturing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Of7D.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing creamery butter from milk and/or processed milk products.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Ojq6.label: Site Preparation Contractors
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Ojq6.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in site preparation activities, such as excavating and grading, demolition of buildings and other structures, and septic system installation. Earthmoving and land clearing for all types of sites (e.g., building, nonbuilding, mining) is included in this industry. Establishments primarily engaged in construction equipment rental with operator (except cranes) are also included.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/OrmR.label: Other Animal Food Manufacturing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/OrmR.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing animal food (except dog and cat) from ingredients, such as grains, oilseed mill products, and meat products.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/OwSV.label: Automobile and Other Motor Vehicle Merchant Wholesalers
english_labels: Automobile and Other Motor Vehicle Merchant Wholesalers

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Owb3.label: Wired Telecommunications Carriers
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Owb3.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in operating, maintaining, and/or providing access to transmission facilities and infrastructure that they own and/or lease for the transmission of voice, data, text, sound, and video using wired telecommunications networks. Transmission facilities may be based on a single technology or a combination of technologies. Establishments in this industry use the wired telecommunications network facilities that they operate to provide a variety of services, such as wired telephony services, including VoIP services; wired (cable) audio and video programming distribution; and wired broadband Internet services. By exception, establishments providing satellite television distribution services using facilities and infrastructure that they operate are included in this industry.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Oxj6.label: Lessors of Nonfinancial Intangible Assets (except Copyrighted Works)
english_labels: Lessors of Nonfinancial Intangible Assets (except Copyrighted Works)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/OzAy.label: Hunting and Trapping
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/OzAy.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in one or more of the following: (1) commercial hunting and trapping; (2) operating commercial game preserves, such as game retreats; and (3) operating hunting preserves.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/P0HD.label: Snack and Nonalcoholic Beverage Bars
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/P0HD.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in (1) preparing and/or serving a specialty snack, such as ice cream, frozen yogurt, cookies, or popcorn, or (2) serving nonalcoholic beverages, such as coffee, juices, or sodas for consumption on or near the premises. These establishments may carry and sell a combination of snack, nonalcoholic beverage, and other related products (e.g., coffee beans, mugs, coffee makers) but generally promote and sell a unique snack or nonalcoholic beverage.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/P0tX.label: Home Furnishings Retailers
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/P0tX.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in retailing new home furnishings (except furniture).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/P1cd.label: Other Aluminum Rolling, Drawing, and Extruding
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/P1cd.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in (1) rolling, drawing, or extruding shapes (except flat rolled sheet, plate, foil, and welded tube) from purchased aluminum and/or (2) recovering aluminum from scrap and rolling, drawing, or extruding shapes (except flat rolled sheet, plate, foil, and welded tube) in integrated mills.
english_labels: Other Aluminum Rolling, Drawing, and Extruding

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/P2ah.label: Plastics Product Manufacturing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/P2ah.definition: This industry group comprises establishments primarily engaged in processing new or spent (i.e., recycled) plastics resins into intermediate or final products, using such processes as compression molding; extrusion molding; injection molding; blow molding; and casting. Within most of these industries, the production process is such that a wide variety of products can be made.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/P4yL.label: Surveying and Mapping (except Geophysical) Services
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/P4yL.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in performing surveying and mapping services of the surface of the earth, including the sea floor. These services may include surveying and mapping of areas above or below the surface of the earth, such as the creation of view easements or segregating rights in parcels of land by creating underground utility easements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/P7RY.label: Process, Physical Distribution, and Logistics Consulting Services
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/P7RY.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in providing operating advice and assistance to businesses and other organizations in: (1) manufacturing operations improvement; (2) productivity improvement; (3) production planning and control; (4) quality assurance and quality control; (5) inventory management; (6) distribution networks; (7) warehouse use, operations, and utilization; (8) transportation and shipment of goods and materials; and (9) materials management and handling.
english_labels: Process, Physical Distribution, and Logistics Consulting Services

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/PAbS.label: Other Support Activities for Water Transportation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/PAbS.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in providing services to water transportation (except port and harbor operations; marine cargo handling services; and navigational services to shipping).
english_labels: Other Support Activities for Water Transportation

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/PDqO.label: Manufactured (Mobile) Home Dealers
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/PDqO.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in retailing new and/or used manufactured homes (i.e., mobile homes), parts, and equipment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/PLFH.label: Petroleum and Petroleum Products Merchant Wholesalers (except Bulk Stations and Terminals)
english_labels: Petroleum and Petroleum Products Merchant Wholesalers (except Bulk Stations and Terminals)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/POR-.label: Fluid Milk Manufacturing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/POR-.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in (1) manufacturing processed milk products, such as pasteurized milk or cream and sour cream and/or (2) manufacturing fluid milk dairy substitutes from soybeans and other nondairy substances.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/PU3g.label: Steel Product Manufacturing from Purchased Steel
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/PU3g.definition: This industry group comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing iron and steel tube and pipe, drawing steel wire, and rolling or drawing shapes from purchased iron or steel.
english_labels: Steel Product Manufacturing from Purchased Steel

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/PV3Z.label: Home and Garden Equipment and Appliance Repair and Maintenance
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/PV3Z.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in repairing and servicing home and garden equipment and/or household-type appliances without retailing new equipment or appliances. Establishments in this industry repair and maintain items, such as lawnmowers, edgers, snowblowers, leaf blowers, washing machines, clothes dryers, and refrigerators.
english_labels: Home and Garden Equipment and Appliance Repair and Maintenance

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/PWwZ.label: Heating Equipment (except Warm Air Furnaces) Manufacturing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/PWwZ.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing heating equipment (except electric and warm air furnaces), such as heating boilers, heating stoves, floor and wall furnaces, and wall and baseboard heating units.
english_labels: Heating Equipment (except Warm Air Furnaces) Manufacturing

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/PXFK.label: Motor Vehicle Electrical and Electronic Equipment Manufacturing
english_labels: Motor Vehicle Electrical and Electronic Equipment Manufacturing

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/PZ9J.label: Private Households Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/PZ9J.definition: This industry comprises private households primarily engaged in employing workers on or about the premises in activities primarily concerned with the operation of the household. These private households may employ individuals, such as cooks, maids, nannies, butlers, non-medical personal care aides, and outside workers, such as gardeners, caretakers, and other maintenance workers.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/PfSj.label: Cosmetics, Beauty Supplies, and Perfume Retailers
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/PfSj.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in retailing cosmetics, perfumes, toiletries, and personal grooming products.
english_labels: Cosmetics, Beauty Supplies, and Perfume Retailers

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Pfnj.label: Nonmetallic Mineral Mining and Quarrying
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Pfnj.definition: This industry group comprises establishments primarily engaged in developing mine sites, or in mining or quarrying nonmetallic minerals (except fuels). Also included are certain well and brine operations, and preparation plants primarily engaged in beneficiating (e.g., crushing, grinding, washing, and concentrating) nonmetallic minerals. Beneficiation is the process whereby the extracted material is reduced to particles which can be separated into mineral and waste, the former suitable for further processing or direct use. The operations that take place in beneficiation are primarily mechanical, such as grinding, washing, magnetic separation, and centrifugal separation. In contrast, manufacturing operations primarily use chemical and electrochemical processes, such as electrolysis and distillation. However, some treatments, such as heat treatments, take place in both the beneficiation and the manufacturing (i.e., smelting/refining) stages. The range of preparation activities varies by mineral and the purity of any given ore deposit. While some minerals, such as petroleum and natural gas, require little or no preparation, others are washed and screened, while yet others, such as gold and silver, can be transformed into bullion before leaving the mine site.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Pj1n.label: Burial Casket Manufacturing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Pj1n.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing burial caskets, cases, and vaults (except concrete).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Pl75.label: Stationery and Office Supplies Merchant Wholesalers
english_labels: Stationery and Office Supplies Merchant Wholesalers

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Pmiq.label: Rolled Steel Shape Manufacturing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Pmiq.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in rolling or drawing shapes (except wire), such as plate, sheet, strip, rod, and bar, from purchased steel.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Pt8L.label: Commercial Photography
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Pt8L.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in providing commercial photography services, generally for advertising agencies, publishers, and other business and industrial users.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Pu8m.label: Surgical and Medical Instrument Manufacturing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Pu8m.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing medical, surgical, ophthalmic, and veterinary instruments and apparatus (except electrotherapeutic, electromedical, and irradiation apparatus). Examples of products made by these establishments are syringes, hypodermic needles, anesthesia apparatus, blood transfusion equipment, catheters, surgical clamps, and medical thermometers.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/PuBa.label: Linen Supply
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/PuBa.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in supplying, on a rental or contract basis, laundered items, such as table and bed linens; towels; diapers; and uniforms, gowns, or coats of the type used by doctors, nurses, barbers, beauticians, and waitresses.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Pvd1.label: Motor Vehicle Towing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Pvd1.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in towing light or heavy motor vehicles, both local and long-distance. These establishments may provide incidental services, such as storage and emergency road repair services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Pvza.label: Sign Manufacturing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Pvza.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing signs and related displays of all materials (except printing paper and paperboard signs, notices, displays).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Pxa1.label: Support Activities for Rail Transportation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Pxa1.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in providing specialized services for railroad transportation, including servicing, routine repairing (except factory conversion, overhaul, or rebuilding of rolling stock), and maintaining rail cars; loading and unloading rail cars; and operating independent terminals.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Pxwt.label: Offices of Physical, Occupational and Speech Therapists, and Audiologists
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Pxwt.definition: This industry comprises establishments of independent health practitioners primarily engaged in one of the following: (1) providing physical therapy services to patients who have impairments, functional limitations, disabilities, or changes in physical functions and health status resulting from injury, disease or other causes, or who require prevention, wellness or fitness services; (2) planning and administering educational, recreational, and social activities designed to help patients or individuals with disabilities regain physical or mental functioning or adapt to their disabilities; and (3) diagnosing and treating speech, language, or hearing problems. These practitioners operate private or group practices in their own offices (e.g., centers, clinics) or in the facilities of others, such as hospitals or HMO medical centers.
english_labels: Offices of Physical, Occupational and Speech Therapists, and Audiologists

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Pz8v.label: Amusement Parks and Arcades
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Pz8v.definition: This industry group comprises establishments primarily engaged in operating amusement parks and amusement arcades and parlors.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Q0Ap.label: Automotive Repair and Maintenance
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Q0Ap.definition: This industry group comprises establishments involved in providing repair and maintenance services for automotive vehicles, such as passenger cars, trucks, and vans, and all trailers. Establishments in this industry group employ mechanics with specialized technical skills to diagnose and repair the mechanical and electrical systems for automotive vehicles, repair automotive interiors, and paint or repair automotive exteriors.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Q1Ca.label: Book Retailers and News Dealers
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Q1Ca.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in retailing new books, newspapers, magazines, and other periodicals (without publishing).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Q1UH.label: Irradiation Apparatus Manufacturing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Q1UH.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing irradiation apparatus and tubes for applications, such as medical diagnostic, medical therapeutic, industrial, research, and scientific evaluation. Irradiation can take the form of beta-rays, gamma-rays, X-rays, or other ionizing radiation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Q1nq.label: Structural Steel and Precast Concrete Contractors
english_labels: Structural Steel and Precast Concrete Contractors

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Q2UJ.label: Musical Groups and Artists
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Q2UJ.definition: This industry comprises (1) groups primarily engaged in producing live musical entertainment (except theatrical musical or opera productions) and (2) independent (i.e., freelance) artists primarily engaged in providing live musical entertainment. Musical groups and artists may perform in front of a live audience or in a studio, and may or may not operate their own facilities for staging their shows.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Q4Gw.label: All Other Animal Production
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Q4Gw.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in (1) raising animals (except cattle, hogs and pigs, poultry, sheep and goats, aquaculture, apiculture, horses and other equines; and fur-bearing animals including rabbits) or (2) raising a combination of animals, with no one animal or family of animals accounting for one-half of the establishment's agricultural production (i.e., value of animals for market).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Q4jH.label: HMO Medical Centers
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Q4jH.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments with physicians and other medical staff primarily engaged in providing a range of outpatient medical services to the health maintenance organization (HMO) subscribers with a focus generally on primary health care. These establishments are owned by the HMO. Included in this industry are HMO establishments that both provide health care services and underwrite health and medical insurance policies.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Q58o.label: Confectionery Manufacturing from Purchased Chocolate
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Q58o.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing chocolate confectioneries from chocolate produced elsewhere. Included in this industry are establishments primarily engaged in retailing chocolate confectionery products not for immediate consumption made on the premises from chocolate made elsewhere.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Q5vN.label: Navigational, Measuring, Electromedical, and Control Instruments Manufacturing
english_labels: Navigational, Measuring, Electromedical, and Control Instruments Manufacturing

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Q645.label: Commodity Contracts Intermediation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Q645.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in acting as principals (i.e., investors who buy or sell for their own account) in buying or selling spot or futures commodity contracts or options, such as precious metals, foreign currency, oil, or agricultural products, generally on a spread basis, or acting as agents (i.e., brokers) in buying or selling spot or futures commodity contracts or options on a commission or transaction fee basis.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Q9Uw.label: All Other Specialty Food Retailers
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Q9Uw.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in retailing miscellaneous specialty foods (except fruit and vegetables, meat, fish, seafood, confections, nuts, popcorn, and baked goods) not for immediate consumption and not made on the premises.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/QKre.label: Fats and Oils Refining and Blending
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/QKre.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in one or more of the following: (1) manufacturing shortening and margarine from purchased fats and oils; (2) refining and/or blending vegetable, oilseed, and tree nut oils from purchased oils; and (3) blending purchased animal fats with purchased vegetable fats.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/QSbL.label: Industrial Sand Mining

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R-l-.label: TR430 Official Communication - Domestic

Includes activities associated with Official Communications not affecting the merits of the application, such as reporting Notice of Allowance, receipt of Certificate of Registration, petitions, and other requests for supervisory action that are not decided by a quasi-judicial or appellate tribunal within the Trademark Office. Note that government fees and external expenses (or "disbursements" in the US) are included under E100.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R0Mo.label: False Claims Act Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R0Mo.definition: A False Claims Act Claim is a legal claim made by a whistleblower alleging that a person or entity has submitted false or fraudulent claims for payment to the government, in violation of the False Claims Act.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R0N9.label: Decedent
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R0N9.definition: A decedent is a legal term used to refer to a deceased person, particularly in the context of estate planning and probate law. https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R0OO.label: Actor Relationship
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R0OO.definition: Actor Relationship specifies the nature of the connection between individuals in a particular context, such as legal, familial, or social. Common examples include "spouse," "child," and "parent," which define how the individuals are related to each other. These terms often have legal implications, affecting rights, responsibilities, and eligibility for benefits or obligations, such as family law or immigration law.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R0P6.label: Welfare Fraud
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R0P6.definition: The use of deceitful statements, practices, or devices to unlawfully obtain welfare benefits.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R0RH.label: Goods Sold and Delivered

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R0SR.label: Associational Discrimination Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R0SR.definition: An associational discrimination claim is a legal action brought by an individual who alleges they have been subjected to unfair treatment or adverse actions by an employer or organization based on their association or relationship with a person who has a protected characteristic, such as race, disability, religion, or age. Under anti-discrimination laws like the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, it is unlawful for employers to discriminate against employees due to their association with someone who has a protected status, even if the employee themselves does not possess that status.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R0TZ.label: Human Rights
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R0TZ.definition: Human rights refer to the fundamental rights and freedoms to which all individuals are inherently entitled, regardless of nationality, sex, ethnicity, religion, or other characteristics. These rights are often upheld by international law and treaties, and they include, but are not limited to, the right to life, liberty, and security of person, as well as freedom from torture and discrimination.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R0Tb.label: Arkansas Circuit Court - Jefferson Cty.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R0VV.label: Future Advances Clause

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R0XL.label: Open Book Account
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R0XL.definition: An open book account is a type of civil claim where a plaintiff seeks payment for goods or services provided to a defendant on an ongoing basis, with the details of the transactions recorded in a book or other record that is open to inspection by both parties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R1nC.label: Full Faith & Credit Clause Claim

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R1x4.label: Lack of Warrant Claim

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R2Jt.label: Motion to Approve
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R2Jt.definition: A Motion to Approve is a formal request made in a bankruptcy case seeking the court's approval of a particular action or agreement, such as a proposed settlement or sale of assets.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R2KP.label: Universal Healthcare Coverage Policy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R2KP.definition: Universal healthcare coverage refers to a system where all residents of a country have access to healthcare services, usually funded by the government. In the U.S., Medicare is often cited as an example, though it primarily serves individuals 65 and older or those with specific disabilities, rather than the entire population.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R2Kr.label: Structured Certificate
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R2Kr.definition: A Structured Certificate is a financial instrument that combines features of fixed income securities and derivatives to offer customized risk-return profiles based on the performance of underlying assets. It typically provides exposure to various asset classes while offering some form of principal protection or enhanced returns under specific market conditions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R2Oc.label: Residuary Bequest
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R2Oc.definition: A Residuary Bequest is a provision in a will or trust that designates the distribution of the remainder of an estate after all specific, general, and demonstrative bequests have been fulfilled. This type of bequest ensures that any leftover assets are passed to the named beneficiary or beneficiaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R2Od.label: Convertible Share
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R2Od.definition: Convertible Shares are a type of equity that can be converted into a different form, typically common shares, at predetermined conditions and times. These shares provide the benefits of preferred shares, such as fixed dividends, along with the potential for capital appreciation through conversion to common equity.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R2Q4.label: Delay Rentals Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R2Q4.definition: A Delay Rentals Clause is a provision in a contract that requires one party to pay a specified amount of money to the other party if there is a delay in the performance of the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R2Q4.label: Monetary Consideration Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R2Q4.definition: A Monetary Consideration Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the specific amount of money that one party agrees to pay to the other party in exchange for goods or services rendered.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R2QZ.label: Labor Shortage Verification
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R2QZ.definition: A Labor Shortage Verification (in the U.S., a PERM labor certification) is a process where employers demonstrate that there are no qualified destination-country (e.g., U.S.) workers available to fill a specific job position and that hiring a foreign worker will not negatively impact the destination country's job market. In the United States, It's a crucial step in the employment-based immigration process, often required for certain employment-based green card applications (EB-2 and EB-3 categories). Employers must go through a series of recruitment efforts and file a Form ETA-9089 with the U.S. Department of Labor to obtain PERM labor certification before proceeding with the green card application for the foreign worker

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R2RJ.label: Georgia Superior Court - Ware County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R2Tl.label: Trademark Opposition Process
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R2Tl.definition: The trademark opposition process is a legal procedure that allows third parties to challenge the registration of a trademark before it is officially granted. This process typically occurs after the trademark application has been published, giving interested parties an opportunity to object based on potential conflicts with existing trademarks, likelihood of confusion, or other grounds.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Gj.label: Thyroid Gland Cancer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Gj.definition: Thyroid cancer is a type of cancer that originates in the thyroid gland, which is located at the base of the neck and produces hormones that regulate metabolism. It is typically treatable and often requires treatments such as surgery, radioactive iodine therapy, and hormone therapy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3JS.label: Journalist
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3JS.definition: A Journalist is a professional who researches, writes, and reports on news and current events for various media outlets, including newspapers, magazines, television, radio, and online platforms. Journalists play a critical role in gathering information, conducting interviews, and delivering news to the public in an accurate and unbiased manner.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Jd.label: X112 Delivery Services/Messengers
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Jd.definition: Any overnight delivery service like FedEx, UPS or DHL and messenger services including internal law firm or legal vendor messenger services. Excludes Postal Service charges (X113).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Jy.label: cl_matter_id
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Jy.definition: "The client assigned matter id or case reference number. Multiple cl_matter_id's can be billed in the same invoice. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Md.label: Corporate Representative Deposition Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Md.definition: The practice of conducting a deposition of a corporate representative, who is designated to testify on behalf of the corporation, in a legal matter.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3N9.label: Extension of Term Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3N9.definition: An Extension of Term Clause is a provision in a contract that allows for the lengthening of a specified period of time beyond its original expiration date.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Nr.label: School Funding Objective
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Nr.definition: The School Funding Objective pertains to the allocation of financial resources to educational institutions, particularly targeting areas of need, to enhance the quality of education and ensure equitable opportunities for all students. Notably, mechanisms like Title I provide additional funds to schools serving high percentages of low-income students, with the aim of bridging educational disparities and improving outcomes for these students.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3OI.label: Bequest
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3OI.definition: A Bequest is a provision in a will or trust that designates the transfer of specific assets, property, or money to a particular beneficiary upon the death of the testator. It ensures that the intended recipients receive the designated items as part of the estate distribution.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Op.label: Grand Jury
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Op.definition: A court-impaneled body of jurors that hears and examines evidence concerning alleged criminal offenses and misconduct, examining the validity of those accusations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Q1.label: Florida Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Q1.definition: The Florida Circuit Court is a state court in Florida that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its designated circuit.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Q9.label: DEPRECATED Wage Statement Violation Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Q9.definition: A wage statement violation claim is a legal action initiated by an employee against their employer for not complying with the legal requirement to provide accurate and complete wage statements or pay stubs. These statements typically include information about the employee's hours worked, wages earned, deductions taken, and other important employment-related information. The claim typically arises when an employer provides wage statements that do not accurately reflect the employee's earnings or deductions, or do not contain all the information required by law. Employers can face liability for failing to provide accurate and complete wage statements, which can result in financial harm to the employee.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Rp.label: New Jersey Superior Court - Camden County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Rp.definition: The New Jersey Superior Court - Camden County is a court of general jurisdiction within the New Jersey state court system, located in Camden County and serving the surrounding area.
english_labels: New Jersey Superior Court - Camden County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3SD.label: Trust and Estate Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3SD.definition: Trust and Estate Claims refer to legal actions related to disputes over the distribution of assets and property left behind by a deceased person, including challenges to the validity of wills, allegations of mismanagement by trustees, and interference with expected inheritances.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Ss.label: Real Estate Investment Trust
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Ss.definition: A Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT) is a company that owns, operates, or finances income-producing real estate, and allows individual investors to buy shares in residential, commercial, and industrial properties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Sy.label: Split-off
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Sy.definition: A split-off divestiture is a corporate action in which a company separates a business unit, division, or subsidiary into a standalone, independent entity, but unlike a spin-off, it requires existing shareholders to exchange their shares in the parent company for shares in the newly formed entity. This process effectively separates the ownership of the parent company and the newly created company. Split-off divestitures are undertaken for various reasons, such as to focus on core competencies, improve operational efficiency, or comply with regulatory requirements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3T7.label: Motion to Extend Time to File Reply
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3T7.definition: A Motion to Extend Time to File Reply is a formal request made to a court, either appellate or trial, to grant additional time beyond the original deadline for a party to submit a reply brief or response.
english_labels: Motion to Extend Time to File Reply

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3TY.label: Motion to Determine Tax Liability
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3TY.definition: A Motion to Determine Tax Liability is a legal request made in a bankruptcy case to determine the amount of taxes owed by the debtor.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3TZ.label: Visa Waived
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3TZ.definition: The Visa Waiver Program (VWP) allows citizens of participating countries to travel to the destination country for tourism or business purposes without obtaining a visa. In the United States, travel under the VWP is permitted for up to 90 days and does not allow for a change of status or an extension of stay

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Tt.label: Fee Credit Note
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Tt.definition: A Fee Credit Note is a type of discount or credit given to a client by a legal service provider, typically applied to future legal fees owed by the client.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Ua.label: X111 Online Legal Research
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Ua.definition: Any electronic legal research service charges, such as for LexisNexis or Westlaw

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Ux.label: Pullman Abstention
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Ux.definition: A legal doctrine known as Pullman Abstention allows a federal court to abstain from hearing a case that involves a state law that is unclear or unsettled, in order to allow the state court to clarify the law and avoid unnecessary federal constitutional issues.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Vi.label: Motion for Production of Documents
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Vi.definition: A Motion for Production of Documents is a formal request made in a bankruptcy case for the opposing party to provide specific documents or evidence relevant to the case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Vk.label: A125 Document Production Creation and Preparation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Vk.definition: For discovery and eDiscovery, the creation, export or delivery of a document production set including: creation of production export, metadata redaction, creation of delivery media and image branding. Excludes cost of printed set (X101 or X102).
english_labels: A125 Document Production Creation and Preparation

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Xg.label: Client Organizational Unit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Xg.definition: The particular company entity/division/unit (e.g., Sales, Human Resources) for which the legal work is being performed.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Xh.label: Children's Rights
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Xh.definition: Children's rights are the legal and moral entitlements specifically aimed at the protection and welfare of minors. These rights may include, but are not limited to, the right to education, healthcare, protection from abuse and exploitation, and participation in family and cultural life, often upheld by international law such as the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Xu.label: WC180 Alternative Fee Arrangements
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3Xu.definition: This code includes all non-hourly or other alternative fee arrangements for tasks and activities in this phase.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3a9.label: TR400 Domestic Trademark Prosecution and Renewal
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3a9.definition: All action associated with prosecuting and renewing a trademark application in the home country of an applicant, including initial review and any calendaring of any response deadline, report to client with any proposed response, review of applicant's instructions and comments, preparation of amendments and/or responsive arguments, examiner interviews, and report of actions to the client. Excludes any filings in response to Official Communications under TR430. Includes any affidavit, petition, extension, declaration and other requests for supervisory action that are not decided by a quasi-judicial or appellate tribunal within the Trademark Office. Note that governmental fees and external expenses (or "disbursements" in the US) are included under E100.
english_labels: TR400 Domestic Trademark Prosecution and Renewal

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3b7.label: Liver or Gallbladder Cancer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3b7.definition: Liver cancer is a type of cancer that originates in the liver cells, with the most common type being hepatocellular carcinoma. It often requires treatments such as surgery, chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and targeted therapy, depending on the stage and extent of the disease.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3bU.label: Negative Covenant
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3bU.definition: A Negative Covenant is a legal provision that prohibits a party from performing a certain action or engaging in a particular activity, as specified in a contract or agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3e2.label: Abandonment of Property
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3e2.definition: Escheatment is the legal process by which unclaimed or abandoned property reverts to the state. This occurs when the rightful owner of the property cannot be located or has failed to claim ownership within a specified period, resulting in the transfer of the property to government custody.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3er.label: Prehearing Conference
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3er.definition: A Prehearing Conference is a litigation event that occurs before a hearing, where the parties and the judge discuss the case and attempt to resolve any issues or streamline the hearing process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3gx.label: Judicial Discretion
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3gx.definition: Judicial discretion refers to the power and authority granted to judges to make decisions or take actions within the bounds of the law based on their interpretation, judgment, and application of legal principles. This discretion is exercised to ensure justice and fairness but is generally subject to appellate review to prevent arbitrary or capricious rulings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3h3.label: PA599 Other Patent Application Preparation - International
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3h3.definition: Use only for preparation activities in connection with patent applications that are to be filed outside the ('domestic') home country or region of the applicant, and that can not be included under a previous code, or as instructed by the client.
english_labels: PA599 Other Patent Application Preparation - International

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3ho.label: Bankruptcy Schedule - Executory Contracts and Unexpired Leases
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3ho.definition: Bankruptcy Schedule - Executory Contracts and Unexpired Leases, also known as Schedule G, requires the debtor to list all ongoing contracts and active leases that have not been fully performed or expired as of the bankruptcy filing date. This schedule provides details about each contract and lease, including the counterparty's name, the nature of the agreement, and any relevant terms.
english_labels: Bankruptcy Schedule - Executory Contracts and Unexpired Leases

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3i3.label: New Jersey Court of Common Pleas
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3i3.definition: The New Jersey Court of Common Pleas is a trial court within the New Jersey State Courts system that handles civil and criminal cases at the county level.
english_labels: New Jersey Court of Common Pleas

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3lz.label: Supplemental Appendix
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3lz.definition: A Supplemental Appendix is an additional section of a document or report that provides further information or data beyond what is included in the main body of the Appendix.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3mS.label: New York Town Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3mS.definition: New York Town Court is a court of limited jurisdiction within the New York State Courts system that handles minor civil and criminal matters at the local level.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3pD.label: Leave Eligibility Miscalculation Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3pD.definition: A leave eligibility miscalculation claim is a legal action initiated by an employee against their employer for improperly calculating their eligibility for protected leave under applicable laws. These laws may include the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA), the California Family Rights Act (CFRA), or other state and local laws that provide protected leave for certain reasons, such as for the employee's own serious health condition, to care for a seriously ill family member, or for the birth or adoption of a child. The claim typically arises when an employer miscalculates an employee's eligibility for protected leave, which can result in the employee being denied leave or having their leave prematurely terminated.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3uq.label: Collaborative
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3uq.definition: Collaborative negotiation is a negotiation approach where parties work together cooperatively to find mutually beneficial solutions, emphasizing communication, trust, and problem-solving. This style focuses on creating value and fostering long-term relationships, often characterized by open dialogue and a willingness to understand and accommodate each party's interests.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3vP.label: Nevada District Court - Clark County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3vP.definition: The Nevada District Court - Clark County is a specific court within the Nevada District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Clark County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3wL.label: Wrongful Death Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3wL.definition: A wrongful death claim is a legal action brought by the survivors of a deceased person against the party responsible for the death, seeking compensation for damages resulting from the loss of the individual's life.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3wh.label: Texas Court of Appeals - 4th
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3wh.definition: The Texas Court of Appeals - 4th is a specific intermediate appellate court in Texas that hears appeals from trial courts in its jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3yl.label: UK Financial Conduct Authority
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3yl.definition: The UK Financial Conduct Authority is an independent regulatory body responsible for overseeing the conduct of financial markets, firms, and individuals in the United Kingdom to ensure consumer protection and market integrity. The FCA regulates financial services providers and enforces rules to maintain fair, transparent, and competitive markets.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3zC.label: Underinsured Motorist Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R3zC.definition: A claim made by an insured individual against their own insurance policy when the at-fault driver in an accident does not have enough insurance coverage to fully compensate for the damages.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72A.definition: An American Depositary Receipt (ADR) is a negotiable certificate issued by a U.S. bank representing a specified number of shares of a foreign company's stock. ADRs trade on American financial markets as a convenient way for U.S. investors to purchase stock in foreign companies.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72B.definition: Bankruptcy Schedule - Property (Schedule A/B) is a form in bankruptcy filings that requires the debtor to list all real and personal property they own, including their estimated value. https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72G.label: Regulatory Application Service
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72G.definition: Regulatory application service refers to legal services related to governmental or regulatory administrative bodies for reviewing and processing applications related to various regulated activities or benefits. These can include applications for licenses, permits, public benefits, or intellectual property rights like patents and trademarks, and involve steps like form submission, documentation verification, and legal review to determine eligibility or compliance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72G.label: Respondeat Superior
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72G.definition: Respondeat Superior is a legal concept that holds an employer or principal liable for the wrongful acts or omissions committed by their employees or agents in the course of their employment or agency.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72J.definition: A transfer clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the conditions and terms for transferring ownership or rights to a third party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72L.label: Unclean Hands
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72L.definition: The concept of "Unclean Hands" refers to a legal defense in civil litigation where the plaintiff's own wrongful conduct or bad faith actions are used to argue against their claim.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72L.label: Motion for Continuation of Utility Service
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72L.definition: A Motion for Continuation of Utility Service is a request made in a bankruptcy case to continue receiving essential utility services, such as electricity or water, despite the debtor's inability to pay for them.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72U.label: Sensitive Personal Information
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72U.definition: Sensitive Personal Information refers to personal data that requires greater protection due to its nature and the potential harm that could result from its unauthorized disclosure. This includes data such as health records, financial information, racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious beliefs, and biometric data.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72X.label: Trial Brief
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72X.definition: A trial brief is a written document submitted to a court that summarizes the legal arguments and relevant facts of a case, typically prepared by an attorney for a trial.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72Y.label: Improper Habit Evidence Objection
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72Y.definition: An Improper Habit Evidence Objection is raised when a party in a legal proceeding believes that evidence being presented is being used to unfairly suggest that a person's actions in a specific incident were consistent with their habitual behavior or routine practice. This objection aims to prevent the misuse of habit evidence that may not be relevant or may lead to unfair conclusions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72a.label: Intersex

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72c.label: Legal Notice Letter
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72c.definition: A Legal Notice Letter is a written document that serves as a formal notification to an individual or entity regarding a legal matter, typically used in the context of litigation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72c.label: Balance Sheet
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72c.definition: A balance sheet is a financial statement that shows a company's assets, liabilities, and equity at a specific point in time, and is used to assess the financial health of the company.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72l.label: Icelandic
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72l.definition: Icelandic (Language) is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary used in Iceland and by Icelandic speakers.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72p.label: Employment Hierarchical Role
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72p.definition: Employment Hierarchical Role refers to an employee's position within the organizational structure in terms of authority and responsibility. Common hierarchical roles include managers, who have oversight and decision-making responsibilities for a team, and individual contributors, who are subject matter experts or skilled workers that focus on executing specific tasks without direct managerial duties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72t.label: Financing Contingency Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72t.definition: A financing contingency clause is a provision in a contract that allows a party to back out of the agreement if they are unable to secure financing for the transaction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72z.label: Tax Audit Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R72z.definition: Tax Audit Practice involves representing and advising clients during tax audits conducted by tax authorities to ensure compliance with tax laws and regulations. This practice includes preparing documentation, responding to audit inquiries, negotiating with tax authorities, and addressing any discrepancies or issues identified during the audit process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R730.label: Irish, Old
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R730.definition: Old Irish (to 900) is a form of structured communication system, consisting of grammar and vocabulary, used in Ireland before the year 900.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R736.definition: The concept of Rescission and Cancellation of Written Instruments refers to the legal act of revoking or terminating a written agreement or contract, typically due to a breach of terms or fraud.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R739.definition: A Consumer Price Index (CPI) Adjustment Clause is a provision in a contract that allows for adjustments to be made to the contract price based on changes in the CPI, which measures the average change in prices over time for goods and services commonly purchased by households.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R73C.label: Not for Distribution Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R73C.definition: A Not for Distribution Clause is a provision in a contract that prohibits the recipient from sharing or disseminating the information or materials provided to them.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R73N.definition: A document that provides answers to a list of typical questions that users might ask regarding a particular subject (e.g., legal processes, substantive legal topics).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R73c.label: Business Interruption Insurance Policy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R73c.definition: Business interruption insurance compensates for lost income and operating expenses when a business is unable to operate due to a covered event, such as a natural disaster, fire, or other insurable occurrences. This coverage helps to maintain financial stability during periods when normal business operations are adversely affected.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R73d.label: Cherries
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R73d.definition: Cherries are small, round stone fruits from the Prunus genus, characterized by their juicy flesh, smooth skin, and varying flavors from sweet to tart. They are widely consumed fresh, dried, or processed into products like jams, pies, and beverages, valued for their rich antioxidant content, vitamins, and dietary fiber.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R73e.label: Status - Approved
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R73e.definition: Status of "Approved" indicates that an application or request has been reviewed and granted approval by the relevant authority, confirming that the individual's request or application has met the necessary criteria and legal requirements, allowing them to proceed with the intended action, status change, or benefit. This tag is particularly relevant to regulatory agencies (e.g., immigration, patent, trademark).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R73f.label: Past Recollection Document
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R73f.definition: Past recollection recorded is a document that is a hearsay exception, allowing a witness to use a written or recorded statement to testify about a matter that they once knew but cannot recall during testimony. The statement must have been made when the event was fresh in the witness's memory and must accurately reflect their knowledge at that time.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R73h.label: Event
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R73h.definition: A matter's events, as well as collections of those events (often noted as "phases").

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R73j.label: Freedom from Slavery
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R73j.definition: Freedom from slavery is a basic human right that prohibits all forms of slavery, servitude, and forced or compulsory labor. This right is enshrined in various international instruments, such as the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and the United Nations Slavery Convention, and is considered a non-derogable right, meaning it cannot be suspended for any reason.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R73k.label: Mutual Waiver of Consequential Damages Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R73k.definition: A Mutual Waiver of Consequential Damages Clause is a provision in a contract where both parties agree to waive their right to seek damages for indirect or consequential losses resulting from a breach of the contract.
english_labels: Mutual Waiver of Consequential Damages Clause

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R73l.label: Cluttering
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R73l.definition: Cluttering is a speech disorder characterized by a rapid or irregular speech rate, which often results in disorganized speech patterns, including omitting or collapsing syllables and words. This disorder affects the clarity and fluency of speech, making it difficult for listeners to understand.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R73n.label: Germanic languages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R73n.definition: Germanic languages are a branch of the language family that includes English, German, Dutch, and Scandinavian languages.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R73n.label: Matter Narrative - Description of Matter Resolution
