https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7KL.definition: A deposition (L330) is a legal proceeding where a witness gives sworn testimony outside of court, typically in a lawyer's office, as part of the discovery (L300) process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7KR.label: Consumer Credit and Unfair Debt Collection Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7KR.definition: Consumer Credit and Unfair Debt Collection Claims refer to legal claims made by individuals against creditors or debt collectors for unfair or deceptive practices in the collection of debts or the provision of credit.
english_labels: Consumer Credit and Unfair Debt Collection Claims

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7KS.label: Legal Fraud
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7KS.definition: Fraud committed by a legal service provider, which involves intentional deception or misrepresentation of facts to gain an unfair advantage or benefit in a legal matter.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7KT.label: General Release
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7KT.definition: A General Release is a legal document that releases a party from all known and unknown claims, demands, and liabilities arising from a particular matter, without specifying the particular claims or demands being released.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7KY.label: Water Resources and Wetlands Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7KY.definition: Laws governing the ownership and use of water resources, including surface water and groundwater, oceans and seas.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7KY.label: National Labor Relations Act Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7KY.definition: A National Labor Relations Act (NLRA) claim is a legal action initiated by an employee or group of employees against an employer, alleging that the employer has violated their rights under the NLRA, which is a federal law enacted in 1935 to protect employees' rights to engage in collective bargaining, join or form labor unions, and participate in other concerted activities related to their employment conditions. The NLRA also prohibits employers from interfering with these rights or retaliating against employees for exercising them. An NLRA claim may be filed with the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB), which investigates the allegations and can impose legal remedies, such as reinstatement, back pay, or policy changes, to ensure compliance with the law and the protection of employees' rights.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7KZ.label: Railroad Negligence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7KZ.definition: The concept of Railroad Negligence refers to the legal responsibility of a common carrier, such as a railroad company, to exercise reasonable care in the operation and maintenance of its equipment and facilities to prevent harm to passengers and others.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Kd.label: Escrow Instructions Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Kd.definition: An Escrow Instructions Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the terms and conditions for the delivery of funds or property to a third-party escrow agent for safekeeping until certain conditions are met.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Kd.label: Intellectual Property Regulatory Documents
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Kd.definition: An Intellectual Property Regulatory Document, such as a Patent Application, Trademark Application, or Copyright Application, is a formal submission to a governmental body to secure legal protection for a specific piece of intellectual property. It outlines the details of the intellectual property, provides evidence of its originality or distinctiveness, and serves as the basis for granting or denying the intellectual property rights

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Kf.label: Common Law System
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Kf.definition: Common Law is a legal system characterized by case law developed by judges through decisions in individual cases, rather than through legislative statutes or executive branch action. This system relies heavily on the doctrine of precedent, where past judicial decisions are authoritative in future cases.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Kh.label: Motion for New Trial - Excessive Damages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Kh.definition: A Motion for New Trial - Excessive Damages is a legal request made by a party to a lawsuit asking the court to set aside a previous verdict and order a new trial due to the excessive amount of damages awarded.
english_labels: Motion for New Trial - Excessive Damages

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ki.label: Motion in Limine to Exclude Testimony
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ki.definition: A Motion in Limine to Exclude Testimony is a formal request made to a judge before a trial to prevent certain testimony or evidence from being presented to the jury.
english_labels: Motion in Limine to Exclude Testimony

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Kn.label: Supply Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Kn.definition: A supply agreement is a legally binding contract between two parties that outlines the terms and conditions for the supply and delivery of goods or services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ks.label: Multilateral Governmental Policy Representations
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ks.definition: Multilateral Governmental Policy Representations refer to the legal practice of representing a client's interests in multiple jurisdictions or before various international bodies simultaneously. This practice requires a comprehensive understanding of different legal systems, treaties, and international regulations to effectively advocate for the client across borders.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Kt.label: Vocational Student Visa
english_labels: The Vocational Student Visa (in the U.S., the M-1 visa) is a non-immigrant visa for students who wish to pursue vocational or non-academic training or education. This visa does not permit full-time university or college study, and its duration is generally for the length of the vocational program up to a maximum of one year, with some options for extension

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Kw.label: Librarian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Kw.definition: A Librarian is a professional who manages, categorizes, and provides accessto collections of legal resources, books, and documents, to ensure that legal practitioners can quickly and accurately access the information they need.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Kx.label: Demographic Market Segments
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Kx.definition: Demographic segments refer to divisions of the market that are categorized based on demographic characteristics such as age, gender, income, education level, and family status. These segments help marketers and businesses tailor their products and services to specific groups within the population, based on their unique needs and preferences.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Kx.label: AI Model
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Kx.definition: An AI Model is a core component of an AI system used to make inferences from inputs to produce outputs. It characterizes an input-to-output transformation designed to perform a specific computational task of the AI system, such as classifying an image, predicting the next word in a sequence, or selecting a robot's next action based on its state and goals.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7L5.label: Legal Entity
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7L5.definition: A person, company, organization, or other entity that has legal rights and obligations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7LA.label: Florida Court of Appeals - 4th District
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7LA.definition: The Florida Court of Appeals - 4th District is a specific court within the Florida District Court of Appeals that hears appeals from trial courts in its jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7LD.label: Tax Tier Total Taxable Amount
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7LD.definition: The Tax Tier Total Taxable Amount is a subcategory of Tax Tier Detail and refers to the total amount of taxable income subject to a specific tax rate.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7LE.label: Pay or Play Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7LE.definition: A Pay or Play Clause is a contractual provision that requires one party to either pay a specified amount or perform a specific action, typically related to employment or entertainment, in order to fulfill their obligations under the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7LI.label: Bankruptcy and Financial Restructuring Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7LI.definition: Any process that involves the liquidation or restructuring a business. The process usually has several parties - debtors, creditors and buyers.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7LM.label: 441 Voting (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7LM.definition: Action filed under Civil Rights Act, 52 U.S.C. § 10101, and Voting Rights Act, 52 U.S.C. § 10301

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7LQ.label: Independent Committee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7LQ.definition: An independent committee is a group of people assembled to conduct an activity independent of the management of a company, often in connection with an internal investigation or approval of an interested party transaction. Also known as a "special committee."

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7LR.label: Motion to Extend Time to File Response
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7LR.definition: A Motion to Extend Time to File Response is a formal request made to a court, either appellate or trial, to grant additional time beyond the original deadline for a party to submit a response to a motion or pleading.
english_labels: Motion to Extend Time to File Response

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7LR.label: Redaction Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7LR.definition: Redaction Management refers to the process of identifying and removing sensitive or confidential information from legal documents in order to protect the privacy of individuals or organizations involved in litigation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7LZ.label: Washington Superior Court - Island County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7LZ.definition: Washington Superior Court - Island County is a specific court within the Washington Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Island County, Washington.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7La.label: Invoice Reference
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7La.definition: A reference number or identifier used to track and identify a specific fee invoice within a legal engagement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Lc.label: Pediatrics Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Lc.definition: Pediatrics Malpractice refers to a type of medical malpractice claim that involves the negligent or wrongful actions of healthcare providers in the treatment of children.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ld.label: Litigation Document Number
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ld.definition: A Litigation Document Number is a specific identifier assigned to a document related to a legal dispute, used to track and reference the document within the litigation process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Le.label: Writ of Prohibition
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Le.definition: A Writ of Prohibition is a legal order issued by a higher court to prevent a lower court or tribunal from exceeding its jurisdiction or acting outside the scope of its authority.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Lx.label: Florida Circuit Court - Liberty County - 2nd Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Lx.definition: A court located in Liberty County, Florida that is part of the larger Florida Circuit Court system.
english_labels: Florida Circuit Court - Liberty County - 2nd Circuit Court

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7M0.label: L240 Dispositive Motions
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7M0.definition: A dispositive motion is a legal request made by a party in a case, asking the court to make a final decision on a particular issue or the entire case, before a trial takes place.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7M1.label: California Court of Appeal - 1st Dist.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7M1.definition: The California Court of Appeal - 1st Dist. is a specific division of the California Court of Appeal, which is a higher court that hears appeals from lower courts in California.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7M2.label: Breach of Covenant Not to Compete
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7M2.definition: The Breach of Covenant Not to Compete refers to a violation of an agreement between an employee and employer or principal, where the employee agrees not to engage in competitive activities with the employer or principal after leaving their employment or business relationship.
english_labels: Breach of Covenant Not to Compete

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7M8.label: Neurological Disorders
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7M8.definition: Neurological disorders encompass a broad range of conditions that affect the nervous system, including the brain, spinal cord, and peripheral nerves. These disorders can result in a variety of symptoms, such as muscle weakness, coordination issues, seizures, and cognitive impairments, requiring tailored medical and therapeutic interventions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7MA.label: Neural Network
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7MA.definition: A neural network consists of one or more layers of neurons connected by weighted links with adjustable weights. Neural networks receive input data and produce an output by passing it through the network, with each neuron performing a simple computation. Although some neural networks aim to simulate the functioning of biological neurons in the nervous system, most neural networks in artificial intelligence are engineering tools that draw only loose inspiration from biology.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ME.label: Pretrial Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ME.definition: Pretrial Practice refers to the legal work and procedures that take place before a trial, including but not limited to motions, pleadings, and discovery.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7MG.label: U.S. Constitutional Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7MG.definition: U.S. Constitutional Claims are claims that a person's rights guaranteed by the Constitution have been infringed upon by a government entity or individual acting under the authority of the government.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7MK.label: Personal Injury and Tort Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7MK.definition: Law which allows an injured person to obtain compensation from the person who caused the injury.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7MM.label: Washington Superior Court - Kitsap County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7MM.definition: Washington Superior Court - Kitsap County refers to a specific court within the Washington Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Kitsap County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7MO.label: Probate due to Substance Abuse
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7MO.definition: Probate due to Substance Abuse refers to the legal process of managing the estate of a deceased person who had substance abuse issues and ensuring that their assets are distributed according to their will or state law.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7MR.label: Financial Market Index
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7MR.definition: A Financial Market Index is a statistical measure that reflects the composite value of a selected group of stocks, bonds, or other financial instruments, representing a specific market or sector. Examples include the S&P 500 Index, which tracks the performance of 500 large-cap U.S. companies, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA), which measures the stock performance of 30 prominent U.S. companies.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7MX.label: Notary Public Officer Liability for Negligent Acknowledgment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7MX.definition: The liability of a notary public officer for negligent acknowledgment refers to the legal responsibility of such an officer for making a mistake or error while performing an acknowledgment, which can result in a malpractice claim or a judicial and procedural tort claim.
english_labels: Notary Public Officer Liability for Negligent Acknowledgment

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7MY.label: Underwriting Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7MY.definition: An Underwriting Agreement is a contract between a company issuing new securities and an underwriter, where the underwriter agrees to buy the securities and then resell them to the public or institutional investors. The agreement specifies the responsibilities, fees, and terms of the issuance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7MY.label: Privilege Objection
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7MY.definition: A Privilege Objection is raised when a party in a legal proceeding believes that the evidence being sought or presented is protected by a legal privilege, such as attorney-client privilege or spousal privilege. This objection seeks to uphold the confidentiality and integrity of certain relationships, preventing the disclosure of privileged communications.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Mb.label: Crimes Against People
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Mb.definition: Crimes Against People (Individuals) refers to a category of criminal offenses that involve harm or injury to an individual, including but not limited to assault, battery, sexual offenses, kidnapping, and false imprisonment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Mc.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Bates County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Mc.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Bates County refers to a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Bates County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Mc.label: Florida County Court - Pinellas County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Mc.definition: A court located in Pinellas County, Florida that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Mj.label: Indiana City. Court - Marion County, Beech Grove City
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Mj.definition: A court located in Marion County and serving the city of Beech Grove, Indiana.
english_labels: Indiana City. Court - Marion County, Beech Grove City

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Mj.label: Bankruptcy Chapter 15 Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Mj.definition: A Bankruptcy Chapter 15 Claim is a type of claim made in a bankruptcy case that involves international insolvency proceedings and seeks recognition of a foreign bankruptcy proceeding in the United States.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Mk.label: Quileute Tribe of the Quileute Reservation, Washington
english_labels: Quileute Tribe of the Quileute Reservation, Washington

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Mk.label: Emergency / Temporary / Special Probate
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Mk.definition: A type of probate filing for situations that require immediate action or attention, such as emergencies or temporary arrangements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ml.label: New York Supreme Court - Livingston County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ml.definition: The New York Supreme Court - Livingston County is a court of general jurisdiction located in Livingston County, New York, with authority to hear and decide a wide range of civil and criminal cases.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - Livingston County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Mm.label: Employer Withholding
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Mm.definition: Employer withholding refers to the process where employers deduct a portion of an employee's wages or salary to satisfy obligations (e.g., tax obligations, garnishment as a remedy from a prior judgment). In the case of tax obligations, this withheld amount is then remitted to the appropriate tax authorities on behalf of the employee, helping individuals meet their tax liabilities throughout the year.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Mm.label: National Governmental Body
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Mm.definition: A national governmental body refers to an organization or institution at the highest level of governance in a country, responsible for making, executing, or interpreting laws and regulations. These bodies often include the executive branch (headed by presidents or prime ministers), legislative branches (such as parliaments or congresses), and judicial branches (like supreme or constitutional courts). Their functions and structures vary depending on the specific form and constitution of each nation's government.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Mq.label: New York City Court - Batavia
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Mq.definition: A court located in Batavia, New York that operates under the jurisdiction of the New York City Court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ms.label: Product Liability Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ms.definition: Product Liability Claims refer to civil tort claims that arise when a consumer is injured or suffers damages due to a defective or dangerous product, and seeks compensation from the manufacturer or seller of the product.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Mw.label: Peremptory Challenge of Juror
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Mw.definition: The Peremptory Challenge of Juror is the right of a party in a trial to reject a potential juror without stating a reason, as long as the rejection is not based on race or gender.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Mx.label: Visa Priority Date
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Mx.definition: The immigration priority date is a critical concept in immigration system, marking the date when an individual's application for a visa or permanent residency (such as filing Form I-485) is first received by the relevant authority. This date determines the applicant's place in the queue for visa availability, as visas are allocated based on the priority date in conjunction with the visa bulletin.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7N1.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Livingston County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7N1.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Livingston County refers to a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Livingston County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7N3.label: Diversity and Inclusion Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7N3.definition: Diversity and Inclusion Management refers to the practice of promoting and maintaining a workplace culture that values and respects differences among employees, including but not limited to race, gender, age, religion, and sexual orientation, with the goal of creating a more inclusive and equitable environment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7N6.label: Exhibit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7N6.definition: An exhibit is a piece of evidence presented in a trial or appellate proceeding, which can include documents, objects, or other tangible items.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7N7.label: Civil Battery
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7N7.definition: The intentional and harmful physical contact with another person without their consent, resulting in injury or harm, which can be the basis for a personal injury claim.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7N9.label: Observing Deposition
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7N9.definition: Observing Deposition: The act of attending and watching a deposition, without actively participating, in a manner consistent with the posture of a deposition.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7NB.label: Objections to Direct Examination
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7NB.definition: Objections to Direct Examination are formal challenges raised by a party in a legal proceeding, questioning the propriety, relevance, or admissibility of questions or evidence presented during the direct examination of a witness. These objections aim to ensure the integrity and fairness of the examination process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ND.label: Credit Account
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ND.definition: A credit account is a contractual arrangement where a lender extends a line of credit to a borrower. This can be in the form of a credit card account, retail account, or other types of loans. The borrower is obligated to repay the borrowed amount along with any applicable interest and fees.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7NG.label: Destruction of Assets Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7NG.definition: A Destruction of Assets Claim is a legal action taken during divorce proceedings when one spouse alleges that the other spouse has intentionally damaged or destroyed marital property to reduce its value or prevent the other spouse from receiving their fair share in the divorce settlement. This claim seeks to address the consequences of such actions and may involve the court ordering compensation or adjustments in the division of assets to account for the damage or destruction of property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7NL.label: Negligent Failure to Warn of Dangerous Condition
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7NL.definition: Negligent Failure to Warn of Dangerous Condition refers to a legal claim made by an individual who has suffered harm due to a failure to warn of a dangerous condition, where the failure to warn was due to negligence.
english_labels: Negligent Failure to Warn of Dangerous Condition

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7NM.label: Commercial Mortgage-Backed Securities
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7NM.definition: Commercial Mortgage-Backed Securities (CMBS) are a type of asset-backed security backed by a pool of commercial real estate loans, such as those for office buildings, hotels, shopping centers, and other income-generating properties. Investors in CMBS receive payments from the principal and interest collected on the underlying commercial mortgages, offering exposure to the commercial real estate market.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7NP.label: Breach of Warranty
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7NP.definition: Breach of Warranty refers to a legal claim made by a party against another party for failing to fulfill the terms of a warranty, either express or implied, related to a product or service.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7NS.label: Fair Labor Standards Act Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7NS.definition: A Fair Labor Standards Claim is a legal claim made by an employee against an employer for violations of federal labor laws related to minimum wage, overtime pay, and other employment standards.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7NS.label: Tailgating Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7NS.definition: A Tailgating Claim involves allegations that a driver has followed another vehicle too closely, violating safe following distance regulations and potentially causing a safety hazard. This type of claim is typically addressed in traffic courts and can lead to penalties, including fines and driving record points, depending on the jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7NS.label: Escrow Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7NS.definition: An Escrow Clause is a provision in a contract that requires a third party to hold funds or property until certain conditions are met, providing security and assurance to both parties involved in the transaction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7NY.label: Emergency Motion
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7NY.definition: An Emergency Motion is a type of legal request made in an appellate court that seeks immediate relief due to an urgent situation or circumstance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7NY.label: Party-Appointed Expert
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7NY.definition: An expert who is appointed by a party

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7NZ.label: Motion to Expedite Discovery
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7NZ.definition: A Motion to Expedite Discovery is a legal request to speed up the process of obtaining evidence in a case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Nb.label: Lead Underwriter
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Nb.definition: A bookrunner, also known as a lead underwriter or lead manager, is a financial institution or investment bank responsible for managing the issuance of new securities, such as bonds or stocks, in a public offering. The bookrunner coordinates the syndicate of underwriters, sets the price of the securities, and allocates them to investors, playing a crucial role in the success of the offering.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Nb.label: Asset Redemption Right
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Nb.definition: Asset Redemption Right refers to the provisions and options available for the retirement or redemption of shares, allowing for the return of investment under specific conditions. These rights include various scenarios such as redeemable shares, extendible redemption dates, exchangeable shares, and perpetual shares with no fixed maturity date.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Nc.label: Arkansas District Court - Pulaski Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Nc.definition: The Arkansas District Court - Pulaski Cty. is a specific court within the Arkansas District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Pulaski County, Arkansas.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ne.label: Non-Standard Contractual Terms
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ne.definition: Non-Standard Contractual Terms refer to contract specifications that are variable and customized, differing from the standard predefined terms. These contracts include options traded on exchanges with non-standard delivery or expiry terms, tailored to meet specific needs and preferences of the contracting parties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Nh.label: Florida Court of Appeals - 1st District
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Nh.definition: The Florida Court of Appeals - 1st District is a specific court within the Florida District Court of Appeals that hears appeals from trial courts in its jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ni.label: Motion to File Complaint
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ni.definition: A Motion to File Complaint is a formal request made to a court to allow a plaintiff to submit a complaint or petition for legal action.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Nk.label: General Sales and Consumption Tax Payment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Nk.definition: General Sales and Consumption Tax Payment includes all taxes, other than import and export duties, levied on the production, leasing, transfer, delivery, or sale of a wide range of goods and the rendering of a wide range of services. These taxes apply to both domestically produced and imported goods, irrespective of the stage of production or distribution at which they are levied. This category covers value-added taxes, sales taxes, and multi-stage cumulative taxes, including adjustments for border transactions.
english_labels: General Sales and Consumption Tax Payment

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Nk.label: Director’s Liability to Shareholders
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Nk.definition: The legal responsibility of a director to act in the best interests of the shareholders of a corporation, and the potential consequences if they fail to do so.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7No.label: International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7No.definition: An ITAR Claim arises when an individual or entity violates the International Traffic in Arms Regulations, which control the export and import of defense-related articles and services. This claim involves allegations of unauthorized export, re-export, or transfer of defense articles or technical data to foreign nationals or countries.
english_labels: International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) Claim

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Nr.label: Certified Integration Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Nr.definition: A Certified Integration Clause is a specific type of Integration Clause in a legal contract that confirms the completeness of the agreement and prevents any prior or contemporaneous agreements from being considered part of the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Nu.label: Agreement Attributes
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Nu.definition: Agreement Attributes refer to the characteristics and forms in which agreements can exist, defining how they are communicated and understood between parties (e.g., whether the is agreement is oral or written). These attributes determine the enforceability and clarity of the agreements within legal contexts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Nw.label: Spoliation of Evidence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Nw.definition: The intentional or negligent destruction or alteration of evidence by a party in a legal matter, which may result in sanctions or adverse inferences against that party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7O2.label: Blood Disorders
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7O2.definition: Hematological Disorders encompass a range of conditions affecting the blood and its components, including red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets, and plasma. These disorders can impact blood production, function, and composition, leading to symptoms such as anemia, bleeding, or increased risk of infection.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7O4.label: Radio Broadcast
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7O4.definition: A Radio Broadcast is the transmission of audio content via radio waves to reach a wide audience, typically through AM or FM frequencies. This medium delivers a variety of programming such as news, music, talk shows, and advertisements, and can be received on radios, car stereos, and internet streaming platforms.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7O7.label: Lease Abstract
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7O7.definition: A Lease Abstract is a summary document that highlights the key terms, conditions, and provisions of a lease agreement. It serves as a quick reference guide for both landlords and tenants, often utilized for portfolio management or due diligence.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7O8.label: Trustee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7O8.definition: A trustee is an individual person or member of a board given control or powers of administration of property in trust with a legal obligation to administer it solely for the purposes specified.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7OA.label: Mining Industry (except Oil and Gas)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7OA.definition: Industries in this group primarily engage in mining, mine site development, and beneficiating (i.e., preparing) metallic minerals and nonmetallic minerals, including coal. The term 'mining' is used in the broad sense to include ore extraction, quarrying, and beneficiating (e.g., crushing, screening, washing, sizing, concentrating, and flotation), customarily done at the mine site.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7OF.label: Counterpart Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7OF.definition: A Counterpart Clause is a provision in a contract that allows for multiple identical copies of the contract to be signed by different parties, each copy being considered an original.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7OG.label: Lien
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7OG.definition: A lien is a legal claim or right that a creditor has over a debtor's property as security for a debt or obligation, which can be enforced through court action or other legal means.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7OJ.label: Garnishment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7OJ.definition: A garnishment is a legal process where a creditor can collect a debt owed by a debtor by seizing a portion of their wages or assets, as authorized by a court order.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7OJ.label: Cher-Ae Heights Indian Community of the Trinidad Rancheria
english_labels: Cher-Ae Heights Indian Community of the Trinidad Rancheria

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7OJ.label: 345 Marine Product Liability (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7OJ.definition: Action (Admiralty and Maritime) alleging personal injury or wrongful death from an accident involving a water vessel or harbor/dock facilities and caused by a defective product.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7OM.label: Ovarian Cancer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7OM.definition: Ovarian cancer is a type of cancer that begins in the ovaries, the female reproductive glands responsible for producing eggs. It is often diagnosed at an advanced stage and typically requires treatments such as surgery, chemotherapy, and targeted therapy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7OQ.label: Electoral System
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7OQ.definition: An electoral system is a set of rules and procedures used to conduct elections and determine the outcome of votes. Different systems can influence the election's outcome, voter behavior, and the overall representation in the elected body, ranging from single-member plurality systems to proportional representation systems.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7OQ.label: Blue Sky Filing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7OQ.definition: A Blue Sky Filing is a state-level or province-level regulatory filing required for the sale of securities to ensure compliance with securities laws, commonly referred to as "Blue Sky Laws." These filings are necessary to protect investors from fraudulent sales practices and ensure that securities offered or sold within a state meet specific disclosure and registration requirements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7OU.label: Motion to Extend Time to File Amendment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7OU.definition: A Motion to Extend Time to File Amendment is a request made to a trial court to allow additional time beyond the original deadline to file an amendment to a legal document.
english_labels: Motion to Extend Time to File Amendment

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ob.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Clark County Circuit 1
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ob.definition: The Indiana Circuit Court - Clark County Circuit 1 is a court of general jurisdiction in Indiana that hears civil and criminal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.
english_labels: Indiana Circuit Court - Clark County Circuit 1

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Oi.label: Amended Document
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Oi.definition: An amended document is a revised version of an original document that incorporates changes, corrections, or additions. The purpose of amending a document is to update or clarify its content, often to reflect new information or agreements between parties involved.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Om.label: Fee Pre or Post Split
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Om.definition: A fee that is either paid before or after a split between parties, and is categorized under discounts and credits in legal services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7On.label: Narrative Objection
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7On.definition: An objection to a narrative is raised when a party in a legal proceeding believes that a witness's response or a question posed by the opposing counsel is too lengthy, lacks focus, or provides information beyond what was requested. This objection aims to prevent the introduction of irrelevant or prejudicial details into the record.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Oo.label: "Entitled to" Specific Performance Language
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Oo.definition: The "Entitled to" Specific Performance Language refers to a clause in a legal contract that grants a party the right to demand specific performance of the terms of the contract, rather than seeking monetary damages.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Os.label: Faithfully Executed Clause Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Os.definition: A Faithfully Executed Clause claim is a legal argument asserting that a government official, typically the President, has failed to faithfully execute the laws as required by the Faithfully Executed Clause of the United States Constitution. This claim contends that the official's actions or omissions in implementing or enforcing the laws are in violation of the constitutional duty to faithfully execute the laws, potentially rendering their actions unconstitutional or invalid.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ot.label: Real Estate Operator
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ot.definition: A Real Estate Operator is a professional or entity responsible for the day-to-day management, maintenance, and operations of real estate properties. This role includes overseeing property functions, ensuring tenant satisfaction, handling leasing activities, and maintaining the physical condition of the property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ov.label: By Calendar Time Period
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ov.definition: A fixed fee for a calendar time range (e.g., each month, for six months, each calendar year) is also known as a "Subscription Fee".

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7P7.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Shannon County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7P7.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Shannon County: A specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Shannon County, Missouri.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7P7.label: Report
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7P7.definition: A formal record of factual findings, legal conclusions, or proceedings (e.g., meeting, session).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7P9.label: Georgia Superior Court - Effingham County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7P9.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Effingham County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Effingham County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7PH.label: Creditor
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7PH.definition: A creditor is a person or company to whom money is owed. Also, a party to which a bankruptcy debtor owes money.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7PL.label: Another Planned Permanent Living Arrangement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7PL.definition: A planned permanent living arrangement (APPLA) is an alternative option for a child in the foster care system who cannot be reunited with their birth family or adopted, and involves placing the child in a long-term, stable living situation with a caregiver who is not their legal guardian.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7PP.label: Trial Testimony Event
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7PP.definition: Trial Testimony Event refers to the phase of a trial where witnesses are questioned and provide evidence under oath, including both direct-examination and cross-examination.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7PX.label: Bus
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7PX.definition: A bus is a large, motorized vehicle designed to transport multiple passengers. It is commonly used for public transportation and can vary in size and configuration, including city buses, school buses, and long-distance coaches.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Pc.label: Indiana Superior Court - Daviess County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Pc.definition: A court located in Daviess County, Indiana that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Pd.label: Hemoglobin Deficiency
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Pd.definition: Thalassemia is a genetic blood disorder characterized by the reduced production of hemoglobin, leading to anemia and other related health issues. It is caused by mutations in the genes responsible for hemoglobin production, resulting in abnormal hemoglobin and red blood cells.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Pj.label: Application for National Interest Waiver
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Pj.definition: In the United States, an application for National Interest Waiver (NIW) is a request submitted by foreign nationals seeking an exemption from the labor certification requirement as part of the employment-based green card process in the United States. By applying for an NIW, applicants are essentially requesting that the requirement for a job offer and labor certification be waived due to their work being deemed in the national interest of the United States. The NIW is typically filed as part of the I-140 petition (Immigrant Petition for Alien Worker) and requires demonstrating how the applicant's work benefits the U.S. in a significant and unique manner

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Po.label: X126 Witness Fees
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Po.definition: Any sheriff or service fees and other costs associated with the testimony of a witness at court or in a similar legal proceeding

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Px.label: Cushitic languages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Px.definition: Cushitic languages are a group of languages within the broader category of Language, which are spoken primarily in the Horn of Africa and are characterized by shared grammatical features and vocabulary.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Py.label: Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Py.definition: Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD) is a chronic mental health condition characterized by uncontrollable, recurring thoughts (obsessions) and behaviors (compulsions) that the individual feels driven to perform. These obsessions and compulsions can significantly interfere with daily activities and cause distress.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Q3.label: Washo
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Q3.definition: A Native American language spoken by the Washo people in California and Nevada.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Q8.label: Payment Terms Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Q8.definition: A Payment Terms Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the specific conditions and requirements for payment between parties involved in the agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Q8.label: Georgia Superior Court - Lee County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Q8.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Lee County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Lee County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7QF.label: Restrictive Legend Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7QF.definition: A restrictive legend clause is a provision in a contract that limits the transferability of securities by requiring the purchaser to hold the securities for a certain period of time or to obtain the issuer's consent before selling them.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7QN.label: Waiver of Confidentiality Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7QN.definition: A Waiver of Confidentiality Clause is a provision in a legal agreement where a party agrees to release or give up their right to keep certain information confidential.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7QS.label: Ute Indian Tribe of the Uintah and Ouray Reservation, Utah
english_labels: Ute Indian Tribe of the Uintah and Ouray Reservation, Utah

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7QS.label: Avaric
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7QS.definition: Avaric is a language that belongs to the Northeast Caucasian language family.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7QW.label: Reptiles
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7QW.definition: Reptiles are a class of vertebrate animals characterized by their dry, scaly skin, laying of amniotic eggs, and ectothermic metabolism. This diverse group includes lizards, snakes, turtles, and crocodiles, and they are primarily found in terrestrial habitats, although some species are adapted to aquatic environments.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7QX.label: New York Supreme Court - Schenectady County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7QX.definition: The New York Supreme Court - Schenectady County is a court of general jurisdiction located in Schenectady County, New York, with authority to hear and decide legal disputes within its geographic jurisdiction.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - Schenectady County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Qd.label: Finance and Capital Tax Payment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Qd.definition: Finance and Capital Tax Payment refers to the settlement of taxes levied as a result of financial and capital transactions. This includes taxes on the sale or transfer of securities, bonds, and other financial instruments, as well as taxes on capital gains, dividends, and interest income.
english_labels: Financial and Capital Transfer Tax Payment

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Qf.label: Short Form Lease Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Qf.definition: A short form lease clause is a provision within a contract that outlines the terms and conditions of a lease agreement in a concise manner.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Qi.label: Bankruptcy First Day Motions
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Qi.definition: Bankruptcy First Day Motions are motions filed by a debtor on the first day of a bankruptcy case, seeking relief from certain requirements or restrictions, such as the automatic stay, to allow for the continued operation of the debtor's business.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Qj.label: Food Public Benefit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Qj.definition: Food public benefit refers to government programs specifically designed to provide food or food-purchasing assistance to individuals and families facing financial hardship. Programs like the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) in the United States or similar initiatives in other countries offer vouchers, electronic benefit transfer cards, or direct food provisions to help ensure access to adequate nutrition.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Qq.label: Proceeding Closed / Disposed
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Qq.definition: The concept of "Case Closed / Disposed" refers to the state or condition of a legal matter where all proceedings have been completed and the case has been resolved or dismissed.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Qr.label: Iban
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Qr.definition: A language spoken by the Iban people of Borneo, characterized by its unique grammar and vocabulary.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Qt.label: Release Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Qt.definition: A Release Clause is a contractual provision that relieves one party from liability or obligation, typically in exchange for a payment or other consideration, and may take various forms such as Release of All Claims Clause, Release of Liability Clause, Release of Security Interest Clause, Release of Obligations Clause, Release and Indemnity Clause, or Release Agreement Clause.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Qv.label: Kabardian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Qv.definition: Kabardian (Language) is a specific written or spoken structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary, belonging to the Language top-level class.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7R0.label: JM20 Points of dispute, Replies and Negotiations (UK J-CODE)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7R0.definition: Work on the formal procedural steps under CPR 47 following service of a bill of costs together with Part 36 and other offers to settle costs and consequent negotiations
english_labels: JM20 Points of dispute, Replies and Negotiations (UK J-CODE)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7R1.label: Witness Examination Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7R1.definition: The Witness Examination Practice is a legal practice that involves questioning a witness in a legal proceeding, either through cross-examination or direct-examination, and is a subset of Trial Practice.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7R4.label: New Mexico Magistrate Court - Cibola County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7R4.definition: A court located in Cibola County, New Mexico that has limited jurisdiction over certain types of cases.
english_labels: New Mexico Magistrate Court - Cibola County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7R7.label: inv_desc
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7R7.definition: "A descriptive summary of work performed. It is expected that this field will be picked up by receiving system and displayed to bill reviewers. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7R8.label: Negligent Supervision
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7R8.definition: Negligent Supervision refers to a legal claim that arises when a person or entity fails to properly supervise another person, resulting in harm or injury to a third party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7RE.label: 195 Contract Product Liability (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7RE.definition: Action concerning damages caused by a defective product, not primarily involving personal injury or property damage, and based primarily on breach of contract, breach of warranty, misrepresentation, and/or violation of consumer protection laws. Actions primarily alleging personal injury or property damage caused by a defective product should be classified under the appropriate nature of suit code under “TORTS.”

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7RI.label: Religious Belief Evidence Objection
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7RI.definition: A Religious Belief Evidence Objection is raised when a party in a legal proceeding believes that evidence regarding a person's religious beliefs or practices is being used unfairly to suggest credibility, believability, or character. This objection aims to prevent prejudice or bias based on religious affiliation and to ensure that the focus remains on relevant and admissible evidence.
english_labels: Objection to Evidence of Religious Affiliation

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7RJ.label: Matter Discount or Credit Total
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7RJ.definition: A Matter Discount or Credit Total is a type of discount or credit applied to a specific legal matter, reducing the overall cost of legal services provided.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7RN.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Bedford County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7RN.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court in Bedford County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court system that handles minor criminal offenses, traffic violations, and civil cases involving amounts up to $12,000.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Bedford County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7RO.label: Catastrophe Bonds
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7RO.definition: Catastrophe bonds, commonly known as cat bonds, are high-yield debt instruments designed to raise money for insurance companies in the event of a natural disaster. These bonds provide insurers with an alternative source of capital to cover significant losses from catastrophes, transferring some of the financial risk to investors who receive regular coupon payments unless a specified catastrophe event occurs.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7RS.label: Applicant/Petitioner
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7RS.definition: An applicant or petitioner is a person who files a petition or makes an application or the person who is applying for a legal remedy to a problem.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7RT.label: Speech Disability
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7RT.definition: Speech Disability refers to impairments that affect an individual's ability to produce sounds that create words, impacting verbal communication. These disabilities can result from various causes, such as neurological disorders, physical impairments, or developmental conditions, and may affect articulation, fluency, voice, or resonance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7RX.label: Liability for Injury to Pets
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7RX.definition: Liability for Injury to Pets refers to the legal responsibility for harm caused to a domesticated animal, such as a dog or cat, and the resulting damages that may be awarded to the pet owner.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7RY.label: Appellate Brief
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7RY.definition: A brief or memorandum of law filed in an appellate proceeding.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Rd.label: M&A Transactional Method
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Rd.definition: A M&A Deal Structure is the specific plan or arrangement for the merger or acquisition of companies, including the methods used to acquire the target company, such as tender offers or mergers, and the legal framework supporting the execution of the plan.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Re.label: Matter Narrative
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Re.definition: A textual narrative of a matter's factual and legal details.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Rh.label: JB10 Budgeting - own side's costs (UK J-CODE)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Rh.definition: Preparing budgets solely for the client and monitoring costs incurred for the purposes of any required variations. Performing budgetary work related to obtaining third party funding/ATE insurance.
english_labels: JB10 Budgeting - own side's costs (UK J-CODE)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Rh.label: Landscaping Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Rh.definition: A Landscaping Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the responsibilities and obligations of the parties involved with regards to the design, installation, and maintenance of the landscaping on a property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Rj.label: Privacy of School Records Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Rj.definition: The concept of "Privacy of School Records Claims" refers to legal claims made by parents regarding the protection of their children's educational records from unauthorized access or disclosure, which may result in liability for educational institutions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Rk.label: Deferred Sentence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Rk.definition: A Deferred Sentence is a form of sentencing in which the court postpones the imposition of a final judgment and punishment, typically allowing the offender to complete certain conditions or requirements. This approach gives the defendant an opportunity to demonstrate good behavior and compliance, potentially resulting in a reduced sentence or dismissal of charges upon successful completion.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Rm.label: Non-binary
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Rm.definition: Non-binary refers to a gender identity that is not exclusively male or female, and falls outside of the traditional binary gender system.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Rm.label: Zande languages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Rm.definition: The Zande languages refer to a group of structured systems of communication that are spoken by the Zande people in Central Africa and are part of the Language top-level class.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Rs.label: Strategic Alliance Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Rs.definition: A Strategic Alliance Agreement is a legal document that outlines the terms and conditions of a partnership between two or more companies for a specific purpose or project.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Rs.label: Arkansas District Court - Arkansas Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Rs.definition: A court located in Arkansas County that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7S4.label: D.C. Office of the Attorney General
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7S4.definition: The D.C. Office of the Attorney General is a government entity within the District of Columbia Courts that is responsible for administering legal proceedings and providing legal advice to the District of Columbia government.
english_labels: D.C. Office of the Attorney General

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7SE.label: Electric Power Generation, Transmission and Distribution Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7SE.definition: This industry group comprises establishments primarily engaged in generating, transmitting, and/or distributing electric power. Establishments in this industry group may perform one or more of the following activities: (1) operate generation facilities that produce electric energy; (2) operate transmission systems that convey the electricity from the generation facility to the distribution system; and (3) operate distribution systems that convey electric power received from the generation facility or the transmission system to the final consumer.
english_labels: Electric Power Generation, Transmission and Distribution Industry

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7SI.label: Native Village of Kluti Kaah (Copper Center)
english_labels: Native Village of Kluti Kaah (Copper Center)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7SL.label: Indic languages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7SL.definition: Indic languages are a group of languages spoken in the Indian subcontinent, including Hindi, Bengali, Punjabi, and Gujarati, among others.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7SN.label: Motion to Assign Case to Prior Panel
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7SN.definition: A Motion to Assign Case to Prior Panel is a formal request made in appellate courts to assign a case to a previously assigned panel of judges.
english_labels: Motion to Assign Case to Prior Panel

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7SN.label: Baltic languages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7SN.definition: Baltic languages refer to a group of languages spoken in the Baltic region, including Lithuanian and Latvian.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7SZ.label: Type 2 Diabetes
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7SZ.definition: Type 2 diabetes is a chronic condition characterized by insulin resistance and impaired insulin production, leading to elevated blood glucose levels. It is commonly associated with obesity and a sedentary lifestyle and requires management through lifestyle changes, oral medications, and sometimes insulin therapy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Sa.label: Immigration Violation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Sa.definition: The concept of "Immigration Violation" refers to a breach of immigration laws or regulations, which may result in penalties or legal consequences.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Sd.label: Trial Motions
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Sd.definition: Trial Motions are requests made by parties during a trial to the judge for a specific action or ruling, such as a Motion for Judgment Notwithstanding the Verdict (JNOV) or a Motion for Mistrial.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Sf.label: Net Revenue
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Sf.definition: Net revenue is gross revenue minus returns, allowances, and discounts. Net revenue provides a more accurate picture of the actual income a business has available for operating expenses, since it accounts for deductions that reduce the total income.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Sj.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Crawford County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Sj.definition: The Indiana Circuit Court - Crawford County is a specific court within the Indiana Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Crawford County, Indiana.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Sr.label: Civil Sexual Battery
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Sr.definition: Civil Sexual Battery: A type of civil battery that involves the intentional and unwanted sexual touching of another person, without their consent.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Sr.label: Mandatory Mediation Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Sr.definition: A mandatory mediation clause is a provision in a contract that requires the parties to attempt to resolve any disputes through mediation before pursuing legal action.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Sz.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Cumberland County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Sz.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Cumberland County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering civil and criminal proceedings at the county level in Pennsylvania.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Cumberland County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Sz.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Luzerne County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Sz.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court in Luzerne County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court system that handles minor criminal offenses, traffic violations, and civil cases involving amounts up to $12,000.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Luzerne County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7T7.label: Notice to Appear
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7T7.definition: A charging document in the context of immigration is a formal document issued by the country's agency (e.g., U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS)) that initiates removal proceedings against a noncitizen. It outlines the specific grounds for removal, such as violations of immigration laws or criminal convictions, and serves as the basis for the government's case in immigration court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TB.label: Legal Research
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TB.definition: Legal Research: The process of gathering and analyzing information related to legal issues, cases, and regulations in order to provide guidance and support for legal decision-making.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TD.label: LINE_ITEM_ADJUSTMENT_AMOUNT
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TD.definition: The LINE_ITEM_ADJUSTMENT_AMOUNT is a specific element within the LEDES98BI V5 Format Rev 1-2020 standard that represents the amount of adjustment made to a line item.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TD.label: Child Support Enforcement Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TD.definition: A Child Support Enforcement Claim is a legal action taken by a party to enforce a child support claim against a non-paying parent.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TE.label: Guardianship of Adult
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TE.definition: The concept of Guardianship of Adult refers to the legal arrangement where a court appoints a guardian to make decisions for an adult who is unable to make decisions for themselves due to mental or physical incapacity.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TE.label: Signature Page Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TE.definition: A Signature Page Clause is a specific type of clause found within a contractual agreement that outlines the location and manner in which the parties involved will sign the document.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TH.label: Hypoglycemia
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TH.definition: Hypoglycemia is an abnormally low level of blood glucose, which can result from diabetes management or other conditions. Symptoms can be recognized and reversed by consuming glucose-containing substances, though some individuals may not recognize the symptoms due to hypoglycemia unawareness. Severe cases can lead to complications like seizures or loss of consciousness.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TL.label: Military Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TL.definition: A Military Court is a specialized court within the jurisdiction of the military that has the authority to hear and decide cases involving military personnel and offenses related to military service.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TM.label: Legislative Drafting Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TM.definition: Legislative drafting practice involves the creation of legal texts that are intended to become laws, typically performed by specialized legal experts or legislative counsel. This practice requires a deep understanding of legal principles, legislative processes, and the ability to write clearly and unambiguously, with the goal of producing enforceable and effective laws.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TM.label: Devisee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TM.definition: A devisee is an individual or entity designated in a will to receive real property from the estate of the deceased. The term specifically refers to beneficiaries of real estate, distinguishing them from legatees who inherit personal property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TP.label: Pregnancy and Maternal Healthcare Coverage
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TP.definition: This specialized form of healthcare coverage provides medical services related to pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum care. Many standard health insurance plans offer this coverage as a part of their package, and specialized plans may offer more comprehensive benefits.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TP.label: Motion to Reschedule Oral Argument
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TP.definition: A Motion to Reschedule Oral Argument is a formal request made to a court to change the date or time of a hearing that was previously scheduled for oral argument.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TQ.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Wayne County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TQ.definition: Indiana Circuit Court - Wayne County: A court of general jurisdiction in Indiana that hears civil and criminal cases within Wayne County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TU.label: Design Defect
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TU.definition: A design defect is a legal concept within strict product liability that refers to a flaw in the design of a product that makes it unreasonably dangerous for its intended use.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TW.label: Quality Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TW.definition: A Quality Agreement is a document that defines the quality-related roles and responsibilities of parties involved in contract manufacturing or a similar arrangement. It ensures both parties understand quality standards, specifications, and processes required for the product or service in question.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TX.label: Alternative Legal Services Provider
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7TX.definition: An Alternative Legal Services Provider (ALSP) is an entity that delivers legal or legal-related services outside the conventional law firm model.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ta.label: Tigre
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ta.definition: Tigre is a language that belongs to the Afro-Asiatic family and is spoken in Eritrea and Sudan.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Td.label: Wildlife Trafficking
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Td.definition: Wildlife Trafficking is the illegal trade, smuggling, or movement of wildlife and wildlife products across borders. This activity contributes to the decline of species and biodiversity, violating national and international laws.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Tg.label: Labor Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Tg.definition: Law relating to the relationship between trade unions, employers, and the government.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Th.label: Constitutions
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Th.definition: A written instrument embodying the (usually foundational) rules of a political or social organization.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ti.label: Administrative and Support Services Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ti.definition: Industries in the Administrative and Support Services subsector group establishments engaged in activities that support the day-to-day operations of other organizations. The processes employed in this sector (e.g., general management, personnel administration, clerical activities, cleaning activities) are often integral parts of the activities of establishments found in all sectors of the economy. The establishments classified in this subsector have specialization in one or more of these activities and can, therefore, provide services to clients in a variety of industries and, in some cases, to households. The individual industries of this subsector are defined on the basis of the particular process that they are engaged in and the particular services they provide. Many of the activities in this subsector are ongoing routine support functions that businesses and organizations perform in-house. However, it is common to contract or purchase services from businesses that specialize in such activities and can, therefore, provide the services more efficiently. The industries in this subsector cannot be viewed as strictly "support." The Travel Arrangement and Reservation Services industry group includes travel agents, tour operators, and providers of other travel arrangement services, such as hotel and restaurant reservations and arranging the purchase of tickets, serving many types of clients, including individual consumers. This group was placed in this subsector because the services are often of the "support" nature (e.g., travel arrangement) to businesses and other organizations that purchase such services. The administrative and management activities performed by establishments in this sector are typically on a contract or fee basis. These activities may also be performed by establishments that are part of the company or enterprise. However, establishments involved in administering, overseeing, and managing other establishments of the company or enterprise are classified in Sector 55, Management of Companies and Enterprises. Establishments in Sector 55, Management of Companies and Enterprises, normally undertake the strategic and organizational planning and decision-making role of the company or enterprise. Government establishments engaged in administering, overseeing, and managing governmental programs are classified in Sector 92, Public Administration.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ti.label: Chuukese
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ti.definition: Chuukese (Language) is a structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary specific to the Chuukese people and culture.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Tk.label: Motion to Avoid Lien on Household Goods
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Tk.definition: A Motion to Avoid Lien on Household Goods is a legal request to remove a lien on personal property that is essential for daily living, such as furniture and appliances.
english_labels: Motion to Avoid Lien on Household Goods

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Tl.label: Matter Final Bill
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Tl.definition: A "Matter Final Bill" is a detailed record of the final charges for legal services provided in a specific matter, and is a subcategory of the broader concept of "Engagement Fee Detail".

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Tl.label: Asset Sale
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Tl.definition: The concept of Asset Sale refers to the transfer of ownership of assets for a regulatory purpose (e.g., selling bankrupt or financially distressed company's assets to another party in order to raise funds and pay off creditors; e.g., to increase public benefits).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Tm.label: Leukemia
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Tm.definition: Leukemia is a type of cancer that affects the blood and bone marrow, characterized by the overproduction of abnormal white blood cells. This disease can be acute or chronic and often requires treatments such as chemotherapy, radiation therapy, or stem cell transplantation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Tp.label: Indiana Circuit Court - LaPorte County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Tp.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Indiana that hears civil and criminal cases within LaPorte County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Tq.label: Freedom of Thought and Conscience
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Tq.definition: Freedom of thought, conscience, and religion refers to the basic human right that protects an individual's ability to hold and change beliefs, practice a religion, or exercise non-religious ethical views without coercion or penalty. This right is often enshrined in international human rights law, such as the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, and is considered fundamental to the dignity and freedom of individuals

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Tt.label: Charitable Organization Liable for Wrongdoing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Tt.definition: A Charitable Organization Liable for Wrongdoing is a legal concept that holds a charitable organization responsible for any wrongful actions or misconduct committed by its agents or representatives.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Tt.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Shelby County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Tt.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Shelby County refers to a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Shelby County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Tt.label: Murder
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Tt.definition: The intentional killing of another person, with malice aforethought, which is a criminal offense and can be classified as second-degree murder, first-degree murder, or felony murder.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Tx.label: Redemption Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Tx.definition: A redemption clause is a provision in a contract that allows one party to buy back or reclaim something, such as property or shares of stock, from the other party under certain conditions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Tz.label: Third-Party Defendant
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Tz.definition: A party who was not initially sued but is brought into a civil action by another defendant.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7U0.label: Breach of Loan Contract
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7U0.definition: A Loan Default occurs when a borrower fails to meet the legal obligations or conditions of a loan agreement, typically involving missed payments or breach of other terms. This default triggers legal consequences and can lead to actions such as foreclosure, repossession, or litigation.
