https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7U1.label: Medical Treatment Statement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7U1.definition: A Medical Treatment Statement is a hearsay exception that allows the admission of statements made for purposes of medical diagnosis or treatment. This exception is based on the belief that statements made to medical professionals are likely to be truthful because the declarant has a strong motivation to provide accurate information to receive proper care.
english_labels: Statement for Purposes of Medical Diagnosis or Treatment

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7U1.label: Poverty Line
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7U1.definition: The Poverty Line is a predetermined income threshold used to define the minimum level of income required for an individual or family to meet their basic living expenses. It serves as a reference point to identify individuals or households living in poverty and often influences social welfare policies and programs.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7UE.label: LAW_FIRM_COUNTRY
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7UE.definition: A country where a law firm is located, as defined by the LEDES98BI V5 Format Rev 1-2020 standard.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7UF.label: Fundamental Representations and Warranties
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7UF.definition: A Fundamental Representation and Warranty is a legally binding statement made by one party to another in a contract, which guarantees the accuracy and completeness of certain information or facts that are fundamental to the agreement, and which cannot be waived or modified without the consent of both parties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7UI.label: Au Pair Visa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7UI.definition: An Au Pair visa permits a foreign national to temporarily live with a host family in the host country, providing child care services in exchange for a cultural exchange experience. This visa is typically part of larger exchange visitor programs aimed at promoting mutual understanding through educational and cultural exchanges.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7UJ.label: Stocks - Assets
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7UJ.definition: A stock (also known as "shares" or "equity") is a type of security that signifies proportionate ownership in the issuing corporation. This entitles the stockholder to that proportion of the corporation's assets and earnings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7UL.label: Brand Value
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7UL.definition: Brand Value in accounting refers to the intangible asset that represents the additional value a business gains due to the favorable reputation or recognition associated with its brand name. It is often calculated as the present value of the estimated future cash flows attributable to the brand and is considered during mergers, acquisitions, or company valuation

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7UN.label: Millet
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7UN.definition: Millet is a group of small-seeded cereal crops belonging to the Poaceae family, known for their resilience to harsh growing conditions and nutritional benefits. These grains are staple foods in many parts of Asia and Africa, providing essential nutrients such as carbohydrates, proteins, and minerals.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7UO.label: Rheumatology Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7UO.definition: Negligent or wrongful conduct by a healthcare provider in the field of rheumatology, resulting in harm or injury to a patient.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7UY.label: Refugee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7UY.definition: In the context of immigration law, a "Refugee" is someone who has been forced to flee their home country due to a well-founded fear of persecution. That fear is often based on race, religion, nationality, political opinion, or membership in a particular social group.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ue.label: Notice of Continued Hearing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ue.definition: A Notice of Continued Hearing is a written communication that informs parties involved in a legal proceeding that a previously scheduled hearing has been postponed to a later date.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Uh.label: Florida Circuit Court - Gilchrist County - 8th Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Uh.definition: A court located in Gilchrist County, Florida that is part of the larger Florida Circuit Court system, which handles civil and criminal cases within its jurisdiction.
english_labels: Florida Circuit Court - Gilchrist County - 8th Circuit Court

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ui.label: Amendment Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ui.definition: An Amendment Clause is a provision in a contract that allows for changes or modifications to be made to the original agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ul.label: Rollover Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ul.definition: A Rollover Agreement refers to an arrangement where an investor transfers the proceeds from a mature security into a new issue of the same or a similar security. It can also pertain to the transfer of assets from one retirement plan to another without incurring tax penalties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Uo.label: Estimate of Exposure Amount
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Uo.definition: Estimate by the client and/or provider as to the amount of potential exposure.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ur.label: National Lower House Legislator
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ur.definition: A National Lower House Legislator is an elected official who serves as a member of the lower chamber in a bicameral national legislature. This individual is typically responsible for initiating legislation, representing local constituencies, and providing democratic accountability through more frequent elections compared to the upper house.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7V6.label: Failure to Return Tenant's Security Deposit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7V6.definition: The failure of a landlord to return a tenant's security deposit, which is a type of claim that falls under the broader category of disputes between landlords and tenants.
english_labels: Failure to Return Tenant's Security Deposit

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7V9.label: Crimes Against the Government
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7V9.definition: Crimes Against the Government refer to illegal acts committed against the state or its institutions, including but not limited to terrorism, perjury, counterfeiting, sabotage, tax evasion, insurrection, obstruction of justice, campaign finance violation, bribery, illegal re-entry, rescue of prisoner, treason, sedition, escape from correctional facility, subornation of perjury, and espionage.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7VH.label: Bankruptcy - Initial Case Filings
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7VH.definition: Bankruptcy - Initial Case Filings: The legal documents and forms required to initiate a bankruptcy case, including the Statement of Financial Affairs, Bankruptcy First Day Motions, Bankruptcy Initial Routine Motions, Bankruptcy Second Day Motions, Bankruptcy Schedules, and Bankruptcy Petition.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7VR.label: Regulatory Filing Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7VR.definition: Regulatory Filing Management refers to the process of managing and submitting required documents and information to regulatory authorities in order to comply with legal and regulatory requirements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7VS.label: Settlement Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7VS.definition: A settlement clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the terms and conditions for resolving disputes between parties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7VS.label: Condominium Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7VS.definition: Condominium Law refers to the legal rules and regulations that govern the ownership, management, and use of condominium properties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7VT.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Bond County (3rd Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Bond County (3rd Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7VV.label: New Jersey Superior Court - Warren County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7VV.definition: The New Jersey Superior Court - Warren County is a specific court within the New Jersey Superior Court Appellate Division, which is responsible for hearing appeals from lower courts in Warren County, New Jersey.
english_labels: New Jersey Superior Court - Warren County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7VZ.label: E106 Online research
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7VZ.definition: Online research expenses incurred by a party in a legal matter, including costs associated with accessing and utilizing electronic legal research databases and resources.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Vd.label: Material Change Report
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Vd.definition: A Material Change Report, also known as a Current Report, is a document filed with securities regulators that discloses significant events or changes affecting a company. This could include changes in management, mergers, or other events that could impact the stock price.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ve.label: AAA International Dispute Resolution Procedures
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ve.definition: AAA International Dispute Resolution Procedures refer to the specific rules and procedures established by the American Arbitration Association for resolving international disputes through arbitration.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Vl.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Buchanan County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Vl.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Buchanan County: A specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Buchanan County, Missouri.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Vm.label: Nanny Visa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Vm.definition: A Nanny Visa authorizes a foreign national to enter and work in a host country as a live-in or live-out caregiver, primarily for children of certain non-immigrant workers.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Vn.label: Mosaic Down Syndrome
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Vn.definition: Mosaic Down syndrome is a genetic condition in which an individual has a mixture of cells, some with the usual two copies of chromosome 21 and others with three copies (trisomy 21). This results in a mosaic pattern of normal and abnormal cells.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Vo.label: Analysis of Employee Retention
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Vo.definition: Analysis of Employee Retention refers to the examination and evaluation of the factors that influence an organization's ability to retain its employees, including but not limited to compensation and benefits packages.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Vo.label: Georgia District Court - Charlton County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Vo.definition: Georgia District Court - Charlton County: A specific court within the Georgia District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Charlton County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Vs.label: Motion for Relief due to Newly Discovered Evidence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Vs.definition: A Motion for Relief due to Newly Discovered Evidence is a legal request made to the court to reconsider a previous decision or judgment based on new evidence that was not available at the time of the original decision.
english_labels: Motion for Relief due to Newly Discovered Evidence

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7W4.label: Bankruptcy Chapter 13 Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7W4.definition: A Bankruptcy Chapter 13 Claim is a type of claim made in a bankruptcy case that allows individuals with regular income to develop a plan to repay all or part of their debts over a period of time.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7WD.label: Strongarm powers
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7WD.definition: Trustee as lien creditor and as successor to certain creditors and purchasers

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7WF.label: Matter Net Expenses
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7WF.definition: Matter Net Expenses refers to the costs incurred by a law firm in providing legal services to a client, which are then passed on to the client as part of the engagement fee.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7WG.label: Edisto Natchez-Kusso Tribe of South Carolina (Natchez Indian Tribe)
english_labels: Edisto Natchez-Kusso Tribe of South Carolina (Natchez Indian Tribe)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7WG.label: Balloon Payment Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7WG.definition: A balloon payment clause is a provision in a contract that requires the borrower to make a large payment at the end of the loan term, often used in mortgage agreements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7WJ.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Peoria County (10th Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Peoria County (10th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7WK.label: Contact State or Province
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7WK.definition: Contact State or Province refers to the geographic location of a person or entity's contact information, such as their address, within a specific state or province.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7WO.label: Texas District Court - Collin County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7WO.definition: A Texas District Court located in Collin County, which has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7WU.label: Material Contracts Representation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7WU.definition: Material Contracts Representation refers to a clause in merger and acquisition agreements where the selling party provides assurance about the status, validity, and enforceability of significant contracts to which the target entity is a party. It seeks to ensure that these critical contracts are in good standing and there are no hidden liabilities or issues that might adversely affect their value or enforceability.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Wd.label: Indiana Superior Court - Vigo County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Wd.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Indiana that has the power to hear and decide a wide range of legal cases within Vigo County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7We.label: Indiana Superior Court - Boone County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7We.definition: Indiana Superior Court - Boone County refers to a specific court within the Indiana Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Boone County, Indiana.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Wp.label: Amount in Controversy - expressed as "exceeding"
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Wp.definition: The minimum amount in controversy, where the actual amount in dispute exceeds that minimum. Example: U.S. federal courts deciding a state-law matter (e.g., breach of contract) require an amount of controversy exceeding a certain amount (in 2022, that amount was $75,000).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Wr.label: Public Housing Benefit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Wr.definition: Housing public benefit programs refer to government initiatives that provide assistance to individuals or families in obtaining affordable and safe housing. These programs often include subsidies, vouchers, or direct assistance to help low-income or vulnerable populations access housing that meets their needs. The specific eligibility criteria, types of assistance, and regulations governing such programs can vary widely by jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ws.label: inv_end_date
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ws.definition: "The ending date for the billing period. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ws.label: M&A Deal Size
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Ws.definition: The M&A Deal Size refers to the monetary value of a merger or acquisition transaction, which is a specific objective within the broader category of Mergers and Acquisitions (M&A) Objectives.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Wt.label: Notice of Voluntary Conversion - Chapter 13 to 7
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Wt.definition: A Notice of Voluntary Conversion - Chapter 13 to 7 is a written statement informing the court and creditors of a debtor's decision to convert their bankruptcy case from Chapter 13 to Chapter 7.
english_labels: Notice of Voluntary Conversion - Chapter 13 to 7

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Wv.label: Maithili
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Wv.definition: Maithili is a written or spoken structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary, and is a specific language within the context of legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7X4.label: Personal Jurisdiction Bases
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7X4.definition: Personal Jurisdiction Bases refer to the various legal grounds or criteria that a court may use to establish its authority over a person or entity in a legal matter, such as through property ownership, physical presence, or consent.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7X6.label: UTBMS MD00 Ancillary Documents
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7X6.definition: UTBMS MD00 Ancillary Documents: Documents that are not considered part of the main agreement in a merger or acquisition, but are related and necessary for the transaction, as classified under the UTBMS Mergers and Acquisitions code set.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7XB.label: New York City Court - Lackawanna
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7XB.definition: A court located in Lackawanna, New York, which is a subdivision of the New York City Court system.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7XC.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Elkhart County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7XC.definition: A court located in Elkhart County, Indiana that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographic area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7XE.label: Construction Defect Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7XE.definition: A construction defect claim is a legal action brought against a party for damages resulting from faulty construction work.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7XE.label: Cahto Indian Tribe of the Laytonville Rancheria
english_labels: Cahto Indian Tribe of the Laytonville Rancheria

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7XI.label: Patent-Agent Privilege
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7XI.definition: The Patent-Agent Privilege is a legal protection that allows communications between a patent agent and their client to remain confidential and not be disclosed in court, similar to attorney-client privilege.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7XZ.label: New York Supreme Court - Niagara County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7XZ.definition: The New York Supreme Court - Niagara County is a court of general jurisdiction located in Niagara County, New York, which is a subdivision of the New York Supreme Court.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - Niagara County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Xc.label: Inside
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Xc.definition: Actor attribute designating an internal role (e.g., Inside Counsel, In-house Counsel, Internal Expert).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Xg.label: Lack of Contractual Capacity Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Xg.definition: A Lack of Contractual Capacity Claim asserts that a party to a contract did not have the legal ability or competence to enter into the agreement, rendering the contract voidable. This claim typically arises due to factors such as minority, mental incapacity, or intoxication.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Xg.label: Right of Publicity
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Xg.definition: The Right of Publicity is a legal concept that protects an individual's right to control the commercial use of their name, image, likeness, or other identifiable aspects of their persona, and prohibits others from using them without permission.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Xj.label: Disinheritance
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Xj.definition: Disinheritance is the legal act of deliberately excluding an heir from receiving property or assets from a deceased person's estate, typically through the terms specified in a will or trust. This action can be taken for various personal, financial, or relational reasons, and must comply with legal statutes to be effective.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Xj.label: South Carolina Bar - Ethics Advisory Committee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Xj.definition: A committee established by the South Carolina Bar to provide guidance on ethical issues related to the practice of law.
english_labels: South Carolina Bar - Ethics Advisory Committee

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Xj.label: Illegal Gambling
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Xj.definition: To unlawfully bet or wager money or something else of value; assist, promote, or operate a game of chance for money or some other stake; possess or transmit wagering information; manufacture, sell, purchase, possess, or transport gambling equipment, devices or goods; or tamper with the outcome of a sporting event or contest to gain a gambling advantage.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Xk.label: Material Witness
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Xk.definition: A person who prosecutors believe has evidence of a material fact in a criminal investigation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Xl.label: Family Liability
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Xl.definition: Family Liability refers to the legal responsibility of family members for the actions or debts of other family members, including spousal and parent-child liability, as well as agency and vicarious liability.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Xn.label: Reasonable Act or Omission to Correct
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Xn.definition: A "Reasonable Act or Omission to Correct" refers to a legal concept within the larger framework of "Governmental Immunity for Condition of Public Property," which allows a government entity to avoid liability for injuries caused by a dangerous condition on public property if they can show that they acted reasonably in attempting to correct the condition or that their decision not to correct the condition was also reasonable.
english_labels: Reasonable Act or Omission to Correct

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Xp.label: Corporal Punishment Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Xp.definition: A claim made against an educational institution or its staff for the use of physical discipline on a student, falling under the category of Education Liability and specifically related to Corporal Punishment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Xy.label: Existing Mental, Emotional, Physical Condition
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Xy.definition: Existing Mental, Emotional, or Physical Condition is a hearsay exception that allows the admission of statements that describe the declarant's then-existing state of mind, feeling, sensation, or bodily health. This exception is based on the belief that such statements are reliable because they are made in the moment and are unlikely to be fabricated.
english_labels: Present State of Mind or Body
Then-Existing Mental, Emotional, or Physical Condition

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Y2.label: U.S. Tax Court Rules of Practice and Procedure
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Y2.definition: Procedural rules promulgated by the U.S. Tax Court.
english_labels: U.S. Tax Court Rules of Practice and Procedure

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Y2.label: E119 Experts
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Y2.definition: E119 Experts refer to the expenses incurred for hiring professionals with specialized knowledge or skills to provide expert testimony or advice in legal proceedings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7YH.label: Legal Work Location - Locality
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7YH.definition: Locality where the legal services work is being performed.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7YQ.label: Special Appendix
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7YQ.definition: A Special Appendix is a specific type of appendix that contains unique or exceptional information and is distinct from other types of appendices.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7YS.label: Economic Loss Doctrine
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7YS.definition: The Economic Loss Doctrine is a legal principle that limits recovery in negligence claims to only economic losses, such as lost profits or property damage, and excludes recovery for personal injury or other non-economic losses.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7YT.label: Second-Degree Murder
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7YT.definition: The concept of Second-Degree Murder, also known as Depraved Heart Murder, refers to the intentional killing of another person with malice aforethought, but without premeditation or deliberation, and with a reckless disregard for human life.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7YV.label: Non Waiver Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7YV.definition: A non-waiver clause is a contractual provision that states that the failure to enforce a right or remedy under the contract does not constitute a waiver of that right or remedy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7YX.label: Manufacturing Defect
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7YX.definition: A manufacturing defect is a type of product defect that occurs when a product is not made according to its intended design, resulting in a dangerous or defective product.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7YZ.label: Single Asset Real Estate Debtor
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7YZ.definition: A Single Asset Real Estate Debtor (SARE Debtor) refers to a specific classification in bankruptcy proceedings for debtors whose primary business involves a single real estate property. This classification impacts how bankruptcy cases are handled, particularly by expediting the process and applying unique rules concerning automatic stays and reorganization plans.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7YZ.label: Contact Name Suffix - J.D. (Juris Doctor)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7YZ.definition: The suffix "J.D." stands for "Juris Doctor" and is used after a person's name to signify that they have earned the professional graduate degree in law. This designation indicates the individual's qualifications to practice law in a particular jurisdiction, provided they have passed the bar exam, and is commonly used in legal settings, academic environments, and formal documents.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Yc.label: "Intervening Event" Thresholds
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Yc.definition: Intervening Event Thresholds refer to specific criteria or conditions that must be met in order for an event to be considered an intervening event, which is an event that occurs after the signing of a legal agreement and may affect its performance or outcome.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Yf.label: Indiana Superior Court - Marion County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Yf.definition: A court located in Marion County, Indiana that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Yq.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Floyd County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Yq.definition: Indiana Circuit Court - Floyd County: A court of general jurisdiction in Indiana that hears civil and criminal cases within Floyd County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Yr.label: Indiana Town Court - Marion County, Franklin Twp.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Yr.definition: A court located in Marion County, Franklin Township, Indiana that has limited jurisdiction over minor criminal offenses, traffic violations, and small claims disputes.
english_labels: Indiana Town Court - Marion County, Franklin Twp.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Z3.label: Per Diem Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Z3.definition: A per diem clause is a provision in a contract that specifies a daily allowance or rate of payment for expenses incurred by one party while performing duties for the other party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ZI.label: Kikuyu; Gikuyu
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ZI.definition: A Bantu language spoken primarily in Kenya by the Kikuyu people, characterized by its use of prefixes and suffixes to indicate tense, mood, and subject.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ZR.label: JI20 Pre Trial Review (UK J-CODE)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ZR.definition: Work in preparing for and attending any Pre Trial Review (excluding Costs Management).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ZU.label: Fiduciary Relationship
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ZU.definition: A fiduciary relationship is a legal relationship in which one party is entrusted with the care and management of another party's assets or interests, and is obligated to act in the best interests of the other party, with loyalty, honesty, and good faith.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ZX.label: payable_by_cl_name
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ZX.definition: "The name of the party paying the invoice. May not be the same party that is paying VAT on the invoice. The legal name of the party paying the invoice may also be different from the CLIENT.cl_name, the INVOICE tax_invoice_cl_name and the INVOICE.bill_to_cl_name. In some jurisdictions it may be required by law to provide this information. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Za.label: Information Management Risk
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Za.definition: The threats and opportunities associated with an organization's capacity and sustainability of information management procedures and practices — including the potential for negative outcomes resulting from an organization's inability to effectively collect, store, process, and protect its data and information assets. This can stem from poor data quality, outdated systems, inadequate data security measures, or noncompliance with data protection regulations, potentially leading to data breaches, or legal liabilities, ultimately affecting the organization's performance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Zb.label: Expungement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Zb.definition: Expungement is the legal process through which an arrest or conviction is removed from an individual's criminal record, effectively sealing or erasing it from public view. Once expunged, the individual typically does not need to disclose the arrest or conviction in most situations, such as during employment background checks, and it is as though the event never occurred in the eyes of the law.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Zb.label: Medical Negligence Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Zb.definition: Medical Negligence Claims refer to legal claims made by individuals who have suffered harm or injury due to the failure of medical professionals to provide an appropriate standard of care.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Zf.label: Motion to Introduce Evidence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Zf.definition: A Motion to Introduce Evidence is a formal request made to a court to allow the presentation of evidence during a trial or hearing.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Zf.label: Full-Time Employee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Zf.definition: A Full-Time Employee is an individual who works a minimum number of hours specified by their employer or by labor laws, often at least 35 to 40 hours per week. This classification usually comes with benefits such as health insurance, paid time off, and retirement plans, which may not be available to part-time or contract workers

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Zi.label: Notice of Bankruptcy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Zi.definition: A Notice of Bankruptcy is a formal written communication that informs creditors and other interested parties that an individual or entity has filed for bankruptcy protection.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Zk.label: Crohn's Disease
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Zk.definition: Crohn's disease is a chronic inflammatory condition of the gastrointestinal (GI) tract, which can affect any part from the mouth to the anus, though it most commonly impacts the small intestine and colon. The disease is characterized by transmural inflammation, which can lead to complications such as strictures, fistulas, and abscesses, and typically requires ongoing medical management and sometimes surgical intervention.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Zl.label: Nature of Work Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Zl.definition: A Nature of Work Clause is a provision in a contract that defines the type of work that will be performed by one or both parties involved in the agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Zq.label: Note-Related Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Zq.definition: A "Note-Related Agreement" is a supplementary or associated contract that clarifies, modifies, or elaborates upon the terms of a primary promissory note or similar debt instrument. This document may cover issues such as security interests, covenants, or guaranties that are not detailed in the main note but are critical to the lending arrangement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Zr.label: Judicial Finding of Fact
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Zr.definition: Finding of fact as adopted by a decisionmaker (e.g., judge, magistrate, arbitrator).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Zw.label: Entertainment Visa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Zw.definition: The Entertainment Visa (in the U.S., P-1B Visa), is designed for members of internationally recognized entertainment groups that wish to perform in the destination country (e.g., U.S.). In the United States, this non-immigrant visa allows the entertainers to stay for the duration of the event, competition, or performance, with an initial period of up to one year, which can be extended in increments of up to one year for continued performances or events

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Zx.label: Motions for Bail
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Zx.definition: A Motion for Bail is a formal request made to a court by a defendant or their attorney, asking for the release of the defendant from custody pending trial or appeal.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Zy.label: credit_note
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7Zy.definition: "In the European Union (and possibly in other areas of the world) it is required to indicate whether an instrument is a Credit Note if it corrects a Tax Invoice. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7a5.label: 450 Commerce (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7a5.definition: Action filed under the Interstate Commerce Acts 49:1 et seq., 49:301

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7a6.label: Transcript Appendix
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7a6.definition: A transcript appendix is a supplementary section of a document that includes a written or recorded record of spoken words, typically used in legal proceedings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7aB.label: New York District Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7aB.definition: The New York District Court is a trial court within the New York State Courts system, with jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases in a specific geographic area within the state.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7aF.label: Deportation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7aF.definition: The forced removal of a person from a country by the government as a consequence of violating immigration laws or committing a crime.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7aH.label: Disinterested
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7aH.definition: The attribute "disinterested" refers to parties, often trustees or professionals, who have no personal interest in the outcome of the proceedings and no prior relationship with the debtor or creditors. Disinterested parties ensure unbiased administration and decision-making, fostering fairness and integrity in the process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7aO.label: Expired Parking Violation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7aO.definition: This occurs when a vehicle is parked in a regulated space beyond the time limit indicated on a parking meter or permit. The violation is typically enforced through a citation and fine issued by parking enforcement officers.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7aP.label: Meal Break
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7aP.definition: A "Meal Break" is a period of time during the workday, typically lasting 30 minutes to an hour, in which employees are allowed to stop working and have a meal. This break is often unpaid and is intended to provide employees with the opportunity to eat and recharge.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7aS.label: Conflict of Interest Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7aS.definition: A Conflict of Interest Clause is a provision in a contract that requires the parties involved to disclose any potential conflicts of interest that may arise during the course of their relationship.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7aT.label: School Liability Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7aT.definition: School Liability Claims: Legal claims brought against educational institutions for damages or injuries caused by the institution's negligence or failure to provide a safe environment for students.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7aZ.label: Claim Construction Brief
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7aZ.definition: A Claim Construction (Markman) Brief is a written document submitted to a court that provides an interpretation of the language used in patent claims, specifically for the purpose of determining the scope of the patent.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ad.label: Bronchiectasis
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ad.definition: Bronchiectasis is a chronic respiratory condition characterized by abnormal and permanent dilation of the bronchial tubes, leading to impaired mucus clearance, chronic cough, and frequent respiratory infections. This condition results from damage to the airway walls, which can be caused by a variety of factors, including infections, genetic disorders, and autoimmune diseases.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7af.label: Negative Commerce Clause Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7af.definition: A Negative Commerce Clause claim is a legal argument asserting that a state law or regulation violates the United States Constitution by unduly burdening or discriminating against interstate commerce, even in the absence of federal legislation. This claim is based on the interpretation that the Negative Commerce Clause prohibits states from imposing unreasonable barriers on interstate trade and commerce, thereby ensuring a free and fair flow of goods and services between states.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ah.label: Blacklisting Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ah.definition: A blacklisting claim refers to a legal action taken by an individual or entity who alleges they have been unfairly prevented from obtaining employment, services, or opportunities due to being placed on a "blacklist." A blacklist is an unofficial list of persons or entities that are deemed undesirable or untrustworthy, resulting in exclusion from certain opportunities or associations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7al.label: Forfeiture Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7al.definition: A forfeiture clause is a provision in a contract that allows one party to forfeit or lose their right to something, such as a deposit, if they fail to meet certain obligations outlined in the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7at.label: Jury Selection / Voire Dire Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7at.definition: Jury Selection / Voire Dire Practice refers to the process of selecting a jury for a trial, which involves questioning potential jurors to determine their suitability for serving on the jury.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7at.label: Medical Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7at.definition: Medical Malpractice: Negligence or breach of duty by a healthcare professional that results in harm or injury to a patient.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7aw.label: Motion for Leave to Appeal
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7aw.definition: A Motion for Leave to Appeal is a formal request made by a non-party filer in a bankruptcy case to seek permission from the court to appeal a decision made by a lower court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7az.label: Presumption of Innocence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7az.definition: The presumption of innocence is a fundamental principle of criminal law that assumes an accused person is innocent until proven guilty. This cornerstone of the justice system places the burden of proof on the prosecution, requiring them to present sufficient evidence to convince a judge or jury of the defendant's guilt, and helps ensure that individuals are not unfairly convicted without proper evidence or due process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7bP.label: Criminal Claim Degree
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7bP.definition: The Criminal Claim Degree (Severity) refers to the level of seriousness of a criminal offense, such as a felony, misdemeanor, or infraction, within the context of a legal claim or litigation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7bR.label: Georgia District Court - Bryan County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7bR.definition: Georgia District Court - Bryan County: A court of law in the state of Georgia that has jurisdiction over legal cases and disputes specifically within Bryan County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7bU.label: Hair Evidence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7bU.definition: Hair evidence includes strands or fragments of hair found at crime scenes or on objects. Through microscopic examination and DNA analysis, hair can reveal information about its origin, potentially linking individuals to a particular location or event.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7bZ.label: Entrapment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7bZ.definition: Entrapment is a defense in criminal law where the defendant argues that law enforcement induced them to commit a crime they would not have otherwise committed. This defense is used to prevent the conviction of individuals who were coerced into illegal activities by police or government agents.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7bd.label: Exclusive Agreement Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7bd.definition: An exclusive agreement clause is a provision in a contract that restricts one or both parties from entering into similar agreements with other parties during the term of the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7bg.label: Lovelock Paiute Tribe of the Lovelock Indian Colony, Nevada
english_labels: Lovelock Paiute Tribe of the Lovelock Indian Colony, Nevada

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7bi.label: INVOICE_CURRENCY
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7bi.definition: The concept of INVOICE_CURRENCY refers to the specific currency used in a legal invoice, as defined by the LEDES98BI V5 Format Rev 1-2020 standard.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7bn.label: Employee Re-Hire Event
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7bn.definition: An Employee Re-Hire Event refers to the occasion when a former employee is formally rehired and rejoins the same organization. This event often involves the signing of a new employment contract and may necessitate another round of onboarding, while also potentially impacting seniority, benefits, and other employment conditions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7bn.label: Collateral Estoppel
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7bn.definition: Collateral Estoppel is a legal doctrine that prevents a party from relitigating an issue that has already been decided in a previous case, even if the parties and legal theories are different.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7bp.label: Contact City
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7bp.definition: Contact City refers to the city where a person or entity can be reached and is a subcategory of Contact Information in the context of Engagement Terms for providing legal services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7bt.label: Dependent Personality Disorder
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7bt.definition: Dependent Personality Disorder is characterized by a pervasive and excessive need to be taken care of, leading to submissive and clinging behaviors and fears of separation. Individuals with this disorder have difficulty making independent decisions and rely heavily on others for emotional and practical support.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7bv.label: A111 Other
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7bv.definition: A111 Other refers to an unspecified activity within the legal domain that does not fit into any other predefined category.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7bw.label: Prisoner Reentry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7bw.definition: Prisoner reentry refers to the process of individuals reintegrating into society after serving time in prison. It involves addressing various challenges such as employment, housing, and support services to reduce the likelihood of recidivism and help former prisoners successfully transition back into their communities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7bx.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Crawford County (2nd Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Crawford County (2nd Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7bz.label: Employment Misclassification Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7bz.definition: An employment misclassification claim is a legal action initiated by an employee who alleges that their employer has improperly classified them as an independent contractor, rather than an employee. The claim typically arises when an employer misclassifies an employee to avoid providing benefits or complying with certain employment laws, such as minimum wage and overtime requirements. Employees who are misclassified may be entitled to back wages, benefits, and other compensation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7c1.label: 446 Americans With Disabilities - Other (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7c1.definition: Action of discrimination against an individual with disabilities in areas other than employment, filed under 42 U.S.C. § 12133 (exclusion or discrimination in provision of services, programs or activities of a public entity) or 42 U.S.C. § 12188 (public accommodations)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7c1.label: Some Evidence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7c1.definition: Some Evidence refers to any type of proof or information presented in a legal case that supports one party's argument or position, and falls under the burden of proof required in litigation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7c3.label: White Mountain Apache Tribe of the Fort Apache Reservation, Arizona
english_labels: White Mountain Apache Tribe of the Fort Apache Reservation, Arizona

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7c3.label: Employment Mandatory Training
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7c3.definition: Employment Mandatory Training is a compulsory educational program required by an employer to address specific skills, knowledge gaps, or compliance issues among employees. This training aims to improve performance, ensure adherence to company policies, or meet legal and regulatory requirements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7c5.label: Wildlife Crimes
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7c5.definition: Wildlife Crimes involve illegal activities that harm wildlife species, including poaching, trafficking, and illegal trade. These crimes violate national and international laws aimed at protecting endangered and protected species.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7c5.label: New York Civil Court - New York County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7c5.definition: A court located in New York County that handles civil legal matters.
english_labels: New York Civil Court - New York County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7cF.label: Assignment of Contract Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7cF.definition: The Assignment of Contract Clause is a provision in a contract that allows one party to transfer their rights and obligations to another party, typically for consideration.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7cG.label: Indiana Superior Court - Jay County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7cG.definition: The Indiana Superior Court - Jay County is a specific court within the Indiana Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over cases within Jay County, Indiana.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7cH.label: Standard of Performance Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7cH.definition: A Standard of Performance Clause is a provision in a contract that sets a specific level of performance or quality that must be met by one or both parties involved in the agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7cI.label: Security Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7cI.definition: A "Security Agreement" is a legal contract between a debtor and a secured party that outlines the collateral provided by the debtor to secure a loan or other obligation. The agreement defines the terms under which the secured party can take possession of the collateral in the event the debtor defaults.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7cJ.label: Tuition Reimbursement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7cJ.definition: Tuition reimbursement refers to a company benefit in which an employer pays back employees for the costs associated with furthering their education, typically for courses or degree programs that are relevant to their current or potential future roles within the company. This benefit often has specific terms, such as grade requirements or staying with the company for a certain period after course completion.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7cJ.label: Failure to Provide Notice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7cJ.definition: The failure of a party to provide proper notification or warning as required by law or contract, which may be used as a defense in civil litigation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7cL.label: oasis:role collection
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7cL.definition: A collection of roles defined by the Organization for the Advancement of Structured Information Standards (OASIS), which is a subset of a larger collection.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7cN.label: Telephone Consumer Protection Act Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7cN.definition: A Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA) Claim is a legal claim made under the TCPA statute, which prohibits certain telemarketing practices and provides consumers with certain rights related to unwanted phone calls and text messages.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7cY.label: Outperformance Certificate
english_labels: An Outperformance Certificate, also known as a Leveraged ETF, is a financial instrument that allows disproportionate participation in the positive performance of the underlying asset(s) above a certain strike level. These certificates reflect the underlying price movements 1:1, adjusted by the conversion ratio and any related fees, offering a risk profile comparable to direct investment in the underlying asset(s) but with enhanced potential returns in favorable market conditions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7cf.label: Joint and Several Liability
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7cf.definition: Joint and Several Liability is a legal concept where multiple parties can be held responsible for the same damages or debt, and each party can be held liable for the entire amount.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7cl.label: Motion to Hear Case with Other Case
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7cl.definition: A Motion to Hear Case with Other Case is a formal request made in appellate courts to consolidate two or more cases for hearing together.
english_labels: Motion to Hear Case with Other Case

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7cl.label: Livestock Farmland
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7cl.definition: Livestock Farmland pertains to designated agricultural areas used for rearing animals. Legal issues often concern animal welfare laws, property rights, leasing agreements, and related environmental regulations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7co.label: Failure to Accommodate
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7co.definition: A claim of failure to accommodate is a legal action taken by an individual, often an employee, alleging that their employer has not made reasonable adjustments or provided necessary support to allow them to perform their job effectively despite having a known disability, religious belief, or other protected characteristic. Employers are required by law, such as the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, to provide reasonable accommodations for employees with disabilities or religious beliefs, as long as doing so does not cause undue hardship to the employer.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7cs.label: Student's Dependent Visa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7cs.definition: A Student's Dependent Visa is a specialized visa category that allows the spouse and dependent children of a student visa holder to accompany them to the host country while they pursue their studies. Depending on the country's immigration policies, dependents may be allowed to work or study to a limited extent, but the primary purpose of their stay is to reside with the student visa holder.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7cw.label: Secrecy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7cw.definition: The concept of Secrecy refers to the legal defense strategy of withholding information or evidence from the opposing party in a legal matter, typically to protect confidential or privileged information.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7d4.label: Bladder Cancer
english_labels: Bladder cancer is a type of cancer that starts in the cells of the bladder, the organ responsible for storing urine. It often presents with symptoms such as blood in the urine and requires treatments including surgery, chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and immunotherapy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7d5.label: oasis:Right
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7d5.definition: A right, as defined in the OASIS ontology, is a type of deontic specification.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7d6.label: Rules of the Judicial Panel on Multidistrict Litigation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7d6.definition: U.S. federal courts' body of procedural rules governing Multidistrict Litigation (MDLs).
english_labels: Rules of the Judicial Panel on Multidistrict Litigation

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7d6.label: Annelids
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7d6.definition: Annelids are a phylum of invertebrate animals known as Annelida, characterized by their segmented bodies and a true coelom, which acts as a hydrostatic skeleton. This group includes earthworms, leeches, and polychaetes, and they play vital roles in soil aeration and aquatic ecosystems.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7d6.label: Common Carrier
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7d6.definition: A common carrier is an individual or business that advertises to the public to transport people, offer goods, or provide services to the public. Common carriers are legally obligated to provide services to any paying customer without discrimination.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7d7.label: Viejas (Baron Long) Group of the Capitan Grande Band
english_labels: Viejas (Baron Long) Group of the Capitan Grande Band

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7d7.label: Georgia Magistrate Court - Lowndes County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7d7.definition: A court in Lowndes County, Georgia that has limited jurisdiction over certain civil and criminal cases.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7d8.label: NATO-3 Visa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7d8.definition: A NATO-3 visa is issued to official clerical staff accompanying a NATO-1 visa holder, allowing them to enter the U.S. to perform their duties. This visa category includes support staff essential for the operation of NATO-1 personnel.
english_labels: International Military Alliance Clerical Staff Visa

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7dE.label: Visa for Temporary Non-Agricultural Workers
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7dE.definition: A Temporary Non-Agricultural Workers Visa, such as the U.S. H-2B Visa, is a category of visa that permits foreign nationals to work temporarily in non-agricultural sectors of a host country. This type of visa is often used to fill temporary labor shortages in industries such as hospitality, construction, landscaping, or seasonal businesses.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7dI.label: Adjustment of Status Pending
english_labels: In immigration law, "Adjustment of Status Pending" refers to the interim period during which an individual's application to adjust their immigration status, often from a non-immigrant to an immigrant status (permanent resident), is under review by the immigration authorities (e.g., U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS)). During this time, the applicant is generally authorized to remain in the destination country (e.g., U.S.) and may be eligible for work authorization and other interim benefits while awaiting a final decision

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7dM.label: Unlimited Ruleset
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7dM.definition: A set of rules that applies to all cases within a particular jurisdiction, without any limitations or exceptions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7dU.label: Warehousing and Storage Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7dU.definition: Industries in this group are primarily engaged in operating warehousing and storage facilities for general merchandise, refrigerated goods, and other warehouse products. These establishments provide facilities to store goods. They do not sell the goods they handle. These establishments take responsibility for storing the goods and keeping them secure. They may also provide a range of services, often referred to as logistics services, related to the distribution of goods. Logistics services can include labeling, breaking bulk, inventory control and management, light assembly, order entry and fulfillment, packaging, pick and pack, price marking and ticketing, and transportation arrangement. However, establishments in this industry group always provide warehousing or storage services in addition to any logistic services. Furthermore, the warehousing or storage of goods must be more than incidental to the performance of services, such as price marking.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7dU.label: Standalone Material Adverse Effect Closing Condition
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7dU.definition: A Standalone Material Adverse Effect (MAE) Closing Condition, also known as MAE, is a specific language used in legal agreements that outlines the circumstances under which a party can terminate the agreement due to a significant negative change in the financial or operational condition of the other party.
english_labels: Standalone Material Adverse Effect Closing Condition

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7da.label: Human Resources Management Risk
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7da.definition: The threats and opportunities associated with staff/management turnover; employment/work culture; recruitment, retention and staffing processes and practices; succession planning and talent management; and employee development, training, and capacity building. It also includes the potential for negative consequences arising from an organization's ineffective or inefficient handling of its workforce-related policies, practices, and processes. This can result from poor recruitment, inadequate training, weak retention strategies, or insufficient attention to employee satisfaction and development, potentially leading to reduced productivity, and increased turnover, ultimately impacting the organization's overall performance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7da.label: Foster Care Negligence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7da.definition: Negligent actions or omissions by parents that result in harm or injury to a child who has been placed in foster care.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7dc.label: California Family Rights Act Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7dc.definition: A California Family Rights Act (CFRA) claim is a legal action initiated by an employee against their employer for not complying with the CFRA, which provides eligible employees with up to 12 weeks of unpaid leave in a 12-month period for certain family or medical reasons, such as the birth or adoption of a child, the employee's own serious health condition, or to care for a seriously ill family member. The claim typically arises when an employer denies an employee's request for CFRA leave or interferes with an employee's right to take CFRA leave, or retaliates against an employee for exercising their right to CFRA leave. Employers can face liability for violating the CFRA, which can result in significant damages for the affected employee.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7dd.label: Debt Supplemental Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7dd.definition: A Debt Supplemental Agreement is an addendum or modification to an existing debt agreement or indenture. It serves to amend, clarify, or add new terms and conditions to the original contract, such as changing the interest rate, extending the repayment schedule, or adding covenants, without altering the fundamental nature of the initial agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7df.label: Remote Synchronous Communication
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7df.definition: A communication that occurs synchronously and remotely, such as a telephone call or videoconference (e.g., Zoom, Teams, Meet).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7df.label: Hidden Assets Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7df.definition: A Hidden Assets Claim is a legal action taken during divorce proceedings when one spouse suspects that the other spouse is concealing or not fully disclosing assets or financial information. This claim seeks to uncover any undisclosed or hidden assets, which could include bank accounts, investments, real estate, or other valuable property, to ensure a fair and accurate division of marital property during the divorce process. Discovery methods and legal processes are used to identify and reveal any concealed assets.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7dq.label: Probate Reason of Financial Exploitation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7dq.definition: Probate Reason of Financial Exploitation: A legal cause for initiating a probate filing due to the suspected or proven financial exploitation of a deceased person.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7dr.label: Florida Circuit Court - Bay County - 14th Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7dr.definition: A court located in Bay County, Florida that is part of the larger Florida Circuit Court system.
english_labels: Florida Circuit Court - Bay County - 14th Circuit Court

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7dw.label: Air Quality Rights
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7dw.definition: Air Quality Rights refer to the legal entitlements and standards established to ensure the purity and safety of the air we breathe. This encompasses the right of individuals and communities to access clean and unpolluted air and places regulatory obligations on governments and industries to limit emissions, control pollutants, and maintain air quality standards to safeguard public health and the environment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7dz.label: Data Privacy Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7dz.definition: A Data Privacy Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the obligations and rights of parties with respect to the collection, use, and protection of personal data.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7e0.label: Caudal Regression Syndrome
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7e0.definition: Caudal Regression Syndrome (CRS) is a rare congenital disorder that results from abnormal development of the lower spine and structures. It affects the development of the caudal (tail) region of the embryo, leading to a spectrum of anomalies involving the lower spinal cord, pelvis, and lower limbs.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7e5.label: United Nations
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7e5.definition: The United Nations (UN) is an international organization founded in 1945 to promote peace, security, and cooperation among member states. It aims to address global challenges such as poverty, climate change, and conflict, and provides a forum for countries to engage in diplomatic relations and collective decision-making.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7e6.label: Public Intoxication
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7e6.definition: To drink alcoholic beverages to the extent that one’s mental faculties and physical coordination are substantially impaired.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7e7.label: Hedge Fund
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7e7.definition: A hedge fund is a type of investment vehicle that pools capital from accredited individuals or institutional investors and invests in a variety of assets, often using complex strategies with the goal of generating high returns. Unlike mutual funds, hedge funds are subject to fewer regulations and often employ more aggressive strategies, including short selling, leverage, and derivatives.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7eA.label: "Material Adverse Effect" Definition - Exceptions - Failure to Meet Projections
english_labels: "Material Adverse Effect" Definition - Exceptions - Failure to Meet Projections

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7eA.label: Stakeholders and Partnerships Risk
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7eA.definition: The threats and opportunities associated with an organization's partners and stakeholder demographics, characteristics, and activities. This includes the potential for negative consequences arising from an organization's inability to effectively manage relationships with key stakeholders, such as customers, suppliers, investors, or partners. Causes can include poor communication, misaligned expectations, or unaddressed concerns, potentially leading to diminished trust, reduced collaboration, or loss of support, ultimately impacting the organization's overall performance, reputation, and growth opportunities

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7eC.label: Intentional Interference with Prospective Economic Advantage
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7eC.definition: Intentional Interference with Prospective Economic Advantage refers to a tort where a third party intentionally disrupts a business relationship or contract between two parties, causing economic harm to one of the parties.
english_labels: Intentional Interference with Prospective Economic Advantage

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7eK.label: "Material Adverse Effect" Definition - Exceptions - Acts of War
english_labels: "Material Adverse Effect" Definition - Exceptions - Acts of War

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7eN.label: Limited Liability Partnership
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7eN.definition: A limited liability partnership (LLP) is a partnership in which some or all partners (depending on the jurisdiction) have limited liabilities. It therefore can exhibit elements of partnerships and corporations. In a LLP, each partner is not responsible or liable for another partner's misconduct or negligence.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7eR.label: Georgia Superior Court - Henry County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7eR.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Henry County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Henry County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7eS.label: Georgia Superior Court - Colquitt County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7eS.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Colquitt County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7eV.label: Board of Directors
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7eV.definition: The board of directors for a legal entity (e.g., corporation, nonprofit).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7eW.label: Fee Objection Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7eW.definition: Fee Objection Practice (Bankruptcy) refers to the legal practice area that deals with objections to fees charged by professionals in bankruptcy cases.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ea.label: Bankruptcy Budgeting Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ea.definition: Developing strategy for — and preparing — a debtor's Operating Reports (e.g., Budget Preparation, Budget Updates).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7eb.label: Estoppel Letters Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7eb.definition: A clause in a contract that prevents a party from denying certain facts or legal rights that have already been established or agreed upon in a previous communication.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ek.label: Drivers Privacy Protection Act Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ek.definition: A Drivers Privacy Protection Act Claim is a legal claim that arises from the violation of the federal law that regulates the disclosure of personal information contained in motor vehicle records.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7en.label: Melanoma
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7en.definition: Melanoma is a type of skin cancer that develops from the pigment-producing cells known as melanocytes. It is considered the most dangerous form of skin cancer due to its ability to spread to other parts of the body if not detected early, requiring treatments such as surgery, immunotherapy, chemotherapy, and radiation therapy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ep.label: Investigation Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ep.definition: An investigation, search, or examination with an intention to discover facts and their relationship to law.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ep.label: Generic Matter Narrative
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ep.definition: A generic version of a matter narrative. Usually used to further describe a category of matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7et.label: Assisted Suicide
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7et.definition: Assisted Suicide: The act of intentionally helping another person end their life, typically in cases where the person is suffering from a terminal illness or severe pain, and where the person has expressed a desire to die.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7eu.label: Kansas District Court - Woodson County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7eu.definition: A court located in Woodson County, Kansas that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ew.label: Georgia Superior Court - Marion County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ew.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Marion County is a specific court within the Georgia Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Marion County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7f6.label: Sales and Consumption Tax Payment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7f6.definition: Sales and Consumption Tax Payment (aka Tax payment on production, sale, transfer, leasing and delivery of goods and rendering of services) consists of all taxes, levied on transactions in goods and services on the basis of their intrinsic characteristics (e.g., value, weight of tobacco, strength of alcohol, and so on) as distinct from taxes imposed on the use of goods, or permission to use goods or perform activities.
english_labels: Tax payment on production, sale, transfer, leasing and delivery of goods and rendering of services

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7f8.label: Eviction (Event)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7f8.definition: Eviction is a legal process by which a landlord forces a tenant to leave a rented property, typically due to nonpayment of rent, lease violations, or other breaches of the rental agreement. The process involves court proceedings, notice requirements, and, if ordered by the court, law enforcement intervention to remove the tenant from the property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fB.label: Lemons
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fB.definition: Lemons are small, yellow citrus fruits from the Citrus limon species, known for their tart, acidic juice and aromatic zest. They are widely used in culinary applications, beverages, and as a natural cleaning agent, valued for their high vitamin C content and refreshing flavor.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fC.label: Identification of Documents Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fC.definition: Identification of Documents Practice refers to the process of locating and selecting relevant documents for a legal matter, which is a subset of the broader Document Collection and Production Practice.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fC.label: Inappropriate Content
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fC.definition: Inappropriate Content refers to claim regarding material that is deemed offensive, objectionable, or unsuitable for certain audiences, often violating societal norms or legal standards. This can include offensive language, explicit material, or any content that is considered harmful or inappropriate for public display or consumption.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fE.label: Citation to Legal Authority
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fE.definition: A document's citations to legal authorities (e.g., cases, statutes, regulations).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fF.label: Voter Fraud Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fF.definition: A Voter Fraud Claim refers to an allegation that illegal actions were taken to manipulate the outcome of an election, including activities such as voting more than once, casting ballots under false identities, tampering with vote counts, or falsifying voter registrations. These claims question the integrity of the voting process and require investigation to ensure electoral fairness.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fG.label: Hospice Negligence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fG.definition: Hospice Negligence refers to a legal claim for damages resulting from the failure of a hospice provider to provide adequate care and treatment to a patient who is terminally ill or in need of end-of-life care.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fG.label: Collection Limitation Principle
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fG.definition: Collection Limitation is the privacy principle that there should be limits to the collection of personal data and any such data should be obtained by lawful and fair means and, where appropriate, with the knowledge or consent of the data subject

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fH.label: First Amendment Defense
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fH.definition: A First Amendment Defense is a legal strategy used in both criminal and civil litigation to protect an individual's right to free speech, religion, press, assembly, and petition as guaranteed by the First Amendment of the United States Constitution.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fL.label: Stop Sign Violation Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fL.definition: A Stop Sign Violation Claim involves a legal allegation that a driver has failed to make a complete stop at a stop sign as required by traffic regulations, potentially leading to administrative or legal penalties. Such claims are integral to traffic law enforcement and often necessitate evidence review and legal proceedings to resolve.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fT.label: Petition for Visa for Dependent of Intended Spouse of Citizen
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fT.definition: In the United States, a "Petition for Alien Fiancé(e)" refers to Form I-129F in the United States, which is used by U.S. citizens to petition for their foreign fiancé(e) to enter the U.S. for the purpose of getting married. This form initiates the K-1 visa process, allowing the foreign fiancé(e) to travel to the U.S. and marry the U.S. citizen petitioner within 90 days of arrival
english_labels: Petition for Visa for Dependent of Intended Spouse of Citizen

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fe.label: Reletting Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fe.definition: A reletting clause is a provision in a contract that allows the landlord to lease the property to a new tenant if the original tenant breaches the lease agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fg.label: Business Unit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fg.definition: A Business Unit is a distinct division or department within an organization that operates with specific objectives and a degree of autonomy. It is often responsible for its own profit and loss, strategy, and operations, allowing it to be evaluated independently for performance and contribution to the overall corporate goals

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fk.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Henry County 2
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fk.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Henry County, Indiana, with the authority to hear and decide a wide range of legal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fq.label: Mississippi Ethics Opinions
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fq.definition: Mississippi Ethics Opinions are official statements issued by the Mississippi State Courts that provide guidance on ethical issues faced by attorneys and judges in the state of Mississippi.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fw.label: Persian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7fw.definition: Persian (Language) is a structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary, and is a member of the Language class, used in legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7g2.label: Non-current Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7g2.definition: The previously effective law currently appears to have no legal efficacy, having been displaced (e.g., overruled, reversed, vacated, superseded).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7g2.label: Normal Rate Dividend Payment
