https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7g2.definition: Normal Rate Income refers to a type of dividend income where shareholders receive the same dividends as common or ordinary shareholders but have additional privileges, such as preferential treatment in the distribution of assets upon the company's dissolution. These shareholders benefit from regular dividend payments while retaining certain priority rights in specific circumstances.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7g5.label: Crimean Tatar; Crimean Turkish
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7g5.definition: A language spoken by the Crimean Tatar people, primarily in Crimea and Turkey.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7g6.label: Litigation Support Vendors Expense
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7g6.definition: Expenses incurred by vendors who provide support services to parties involved in a legal dispute, such as document management, e-discovery, and trial presentation services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7g7.label: Organic Products Market Segment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7g7.definition: The organic foods market segment refers to a division of the market that is specifically targeted towards consumers who are interested in foods that are produced using methods that do not involve synthetic pesticides, fertilizers, genetically modified organisms (GMOs), or irradiation. This segment encompasses products and marketing strategies that are designed to cater to the needs, preferences, and interests of individuals who seek natural, environmentally friendly, and health-conscious food options.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gB.label: Grandparent
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gB.definition: A Grandparent is an individual who is the parent of one's mother or father. They are one generation removed from the primary familial lineage, and their children are typically referred to as the aunts or uncles of the subsequent generation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gE.label: Arawak
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gE.definition: Arawak (Language) is a structured system of communication spoken by the Arawak people, characterized by its own grammar and vocabulary, and is a subcategory of the Language top-level class.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gF.label: Pension Account
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gF.definition: A pension account is a financial arrangement where an individual or employee contributes funds during their working years to build a retirement fund. The accumulated funds are invested, and upon retirement, the account provides regular payments or a lump sum to support the retiree's financial needs.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gK.label: Oregon Circuit Court - Sherman County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gK.definition: Oregon Circuit Court - Sherman County: A specific court within the Oregon Circuit Court system located in Sherman County, with jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gP.label: Post-Trial Submission Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gP.definition: Post-Trial Submission Practice refers to the legal activities and procedures that take place after a trial has concluded, such as filing motions, briefs, and other documents with the court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gV.label: "Credit Agreement"/"Credit Facility" Definition - Bond Indenture
english_labels: Credit Agreement/Credit Facility Definition - Bond Indenture

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gb.label: Minnesota District Court - Stevens County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gb.definition: Minnesota District Court - Stevens County: A specific court within the Minnesota District Court system located in Stevens County, Minnesota.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gd.label: ICC Arbitration Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gd.definition: An ICC Arbitration Clause is a specific type of contractual clause that designates the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) as the arbitrator in the event of a dispute between parties to the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ge.label: New Jersey Superior Court - Middlesex County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ge.definition: The New Jersey Superior Court - Middlesex County is a specific court within the New Jersey Superior Court Appellate Division that has jurisdiction over cases in Middlesex County.
english_labels: New Jersey Superior Court - Middlesex County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gi.label: Analysis of Student Loan Obligations
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gi.definition: An Analysis of Student Loan Obligations involves the review and assessment of student loan agreements and payment histories to determine their current status and implications for debtors, particularly in contexts like bankruptcy or repayment plan negotiations. This analysis helps determine the enforceability, priority, and potential for discharge or restructuring of student loan debts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gm.label: Oregon Circuit Court - Baker County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gm.definition: Oregon Circuit Court - Baker County: A specific court within the Oregon Circuit Court system located in Baker County, with jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7go.label: California Court of Appeal - 6th Dist.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7go.definition: The California Court of Appeal - 6th Dist. is a specific division of the California Court of Appeal that hears appeals from trial courts in the 6th district of California.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gq.label: Analysis of Utilities Considerations
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gq.definition: Analysis of Utilities Considerations refers to the evaluation and assessment of the various utility factors involved in an obligation analysis.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gr.label: Guardian Ad Litem Attorney
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gr.definition: A Guardian Ad Litem (GAL) Attorney is a type of lawyer who is appointed by the court to represent the best interests of a child or incapacitated adult in a legal proceeding.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gs.label: Flax
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gs.definition: Flax is a fiber crop cultivated for its strong and durable fibers, used primarily to produce linen fabric. In addition to its textile applications, flax seeds are used to extract oil, known as linseed oil, which is utilized in various industrial and culinary applications.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gt.label: Grazing Rights
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gt.definition: These grant an individual or entity the right to allow their livestock to feed (or graze) on specific areas of land. Often, these rights are leased or licensed by landowners or governmental entities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gv.label: Motion to Extend Time to Appeal
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gv.definition: A Motion to Extend Time to Appeal is a request made to a higher court to allow additional time beyond the deadline for filing an appeal, typically made by a party who missed the original deadline due to circumstances beyond their control.
english_labels: Motion to Extend Time to Appeal

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gx.label: Liver Transplantation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gx.definition: Liver transplantation is a surgical procedure in which a diseased liver is replaced with a healthy donor liver to restore normal liver function. This procedure is typically performed for patients with end-stage liver disease, acute liver failure, or certain liver cancers, and requires lifelong immunosuppressive therapy to prevent organ rejection.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gz.label: Mortgage Foreclosure
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7gz.definition: The concept of Mortgage Foreclosure refers to the legal process by which a lender takes possession of a property when the borrower fails to make mortgage payments, and sells it to recover the outstanding debt.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7h0.label: Reseller Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7h0.definition: A Reseller Agreement is a legal contract between a manufacturer or wholesaler and a reseller, outlining the terms and conditions of the resale of goods or services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7h1.label: New York City Court - Little Falls
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7h1.definition: A court located in Little Falls, New York that operates under the jurisdiction of the New York City Court system.
english_labels: New York City Court - Little Falls

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hA.label: Motion to Strike Expert Reports
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hA.definition: A Motion to Strike Expert Reports is a legal request to exclude or remove expert reports from being presented as evidence in a trial or hearing.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hB.label: Other Recurrent Use and Permission Tax Payment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hB.definition: Other Recurrent Use and Permission Tax Payment covers taxes levied on a recurring basis for business and professional licenses required to carry on particular types of businesses or professions. This includes licenses such as those for taxis and casinos, as well as dog licenses and recurrent general licenses for hunting, shooting, and fishing. Broadcast license fees are included when the payer cannot opt out from making payments for public broadcasting, even if they do not consume such services. Specific exemptions do not alter the compulsory nature of these payments.
english_labels: Other Recurrent Use and Permission Tax Payment

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hD.label: Non-criminal Traffic Violation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hD.definition: A non-criminal traffic violation is a type of traffic violation claim that does not involve criminal charges or penalties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hE.label: Dating Market Segment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hE.definition: The dating market refers to a division of the market that is specifically targeted towards individuals who are seeking romantic relationships. This segment encompasses products and services that facilitate the process of finding and connecting with potential partners, such as dating apps, matchmaking services, and social events.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hI.label: Texas District Court - Medina County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hI.definition: A Texas District Court located in Medina County, which has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hP.label: Khotanese; Sakan
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hP.definition: Khotanese and Sakan are languages that belong to the Language class and are used in legal matters as a means of communication.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hR.label: JC20 Legal investigation (UK J-CODE)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hR.definition: Includes identification of the legal issues raised by the case facts and developing the strategy for the case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hS.label: Debt Mutual Fund
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hS.definition: A Debt Mutual Fund is an investment vehicle that pools money from various investors to purchase a diversified portfolio of debt securities such as bonds, corporate debentures, and government securities. The fund aims to generate returns through interest income and capital appreciation, and it is generally considered lower risk compared to equity mutual funds.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hY.label: Massachusetts Superior Court - Plymouth County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hY.definition: The Massachusetts Superior Court - Plymouth County is a court of general jurisdiction in Massachusetts that hears civil and criminal cases within Plymouth County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hY.label: Request for Information
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hY.definition: Document where a buyer collects written information about the capabilities of various legal service providers, normally in a format that can be used to compare providers. In the context of immigration, an RFI refers to a formal communication from immigration authorities to an applicant, seeking additional documentation, clarification, or details to further assess the application.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hZ.label: Service of Process Event
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hZ.definition: The Service of Process Event is a specific type of event within the context of litigation, which involves the delivery of legal documents to a party in a case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ha.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Cameron County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ha.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court in Cameron County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court system that has jurisdiction over minor criminal offenses and civil cases within its geographical area.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Cameron County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hc.label: Common Law Copyright Infringement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hc.definition: The unauthorized use or reproduction of a creative work protected under common law, which violates the exclusive rights of the owner and may result in legal action for damages or injunctions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hc.label: Psychotherapist-Patient Privilege
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hc.definition: A legal protection that allows a patient to keep confidential any communications made during psychotherapy sessions with their therapist.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hf.label: Motion to Dissolve Temporary Restraining Order
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hf.definition: A Motion to Dissolve Temporary Restraining Order is a formal request made to the court to lift a temporary order that prohibits a party from taking certain actions until a hearing can be held to determine whether a permanent order should be issued.
english_labels: Motion to Dissolve Temporary Restraining Order

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hf.label: Backup Certificate
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hf.definition: A Backup Certificate is a document certifying the accuracy and completeness of Legal Opinion's facts. Authors might include clients, law firms, or third parties. Backup certificates serve as a reassurance that the facts in the Legal Opinion are valid.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hg.label: Substantive Unconscionability Permitting Contract Rescission
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hg.definition: A legal concept that refers to the presence of unfair or oppressive terms in a contract that allow for the contract to be cancelled or rescinded.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hg.label: Analysis of Securities Reporting Considerations
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hg.definition: Analysis of Securities Reporting Considerations refers to the process of examining and evaluating the legal obligations and requirements related to the reporting of securities, including financial statements and other disclosures, in order to ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hh.label: Motion to Exclude Document
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hh.definition: A Motion to Exclude Document is a legal request made by a party in a case to prevent a specific document or evidence from being presented in court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ho.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Perry County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ho.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Perry County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering legal proceedings in Perry County, Pennsylvania.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Perry County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hr.label: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hr.definition: The Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services subsector groups establishments that provide computing infrastructure, data processing services, Web hosting services (except software publishing), and related services, including streaming support services (except streaming distribution services).
english_labels: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services Industry

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hs.label: Motion for Relief due to Clerical Error
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hs.definition: A Motion for Relief due to Clerical Error is a legal request to correct a mistake made by the court or court clerk in a previous order or judgment.
english_labels: Motion for Relief due to Clerical Error

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hs.label: Total Amount - Expense
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hs.definition: Total, cumulative amount paid in expenses.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hv.label: New York Supreme Court - Bronx County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hv.definition: The New York Supreme Court - Bronx County is a court of general jurisdiction located in the Bronx borough of New York City.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - Bronx County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hw.label: School-Based Public Benefit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7hw.definition: A school-based public benefit refers to programs or services provided in educational institutions to support the well-being and education of students, particularly those from low-income backgrounds. Examples include school breakfast and lunch programs, as well as initiatives aimed at improving the educational opportunities and outcomes for disadvantaged students.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7i0.label: Lease Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7i0.definition: A contract by which one party (landlord, or lessor) gives to another (tenant, or lessee) the use and possession of lands, buildings, property, etc. for a specified time and for fixed payments.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7i2.label: Creek
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7i2.definition: A Native American language spoken by the Creek people, primarily in the southeastern United States.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7i3.label: Sisal
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7i3.definition: Sisal is a strong, durable natural fiber obtained from the leaves of the Agave sisalana plant, primarily used in the production of ropes, twines, and matting. Its resilience and versatility make it a preferred choice for agricultural, marine, and industrial applications.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7i4.label: Kansas District Court - Dickinson County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7i4.definition: Kansas District Court - Dickinson County refers to a specific court within the Kansas District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Dickinson County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7i4.label: LAW_FIRM_ADDRESS_1
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7i4.definition: The concept LAW_FIRM_ADDRESS_1 refers to the first line of the address of a law firm and is a component of the LEDES98BI V5 Format Rev 1-2020 standard for electronic legal invoicing.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7i8.label: Negligent Hiring
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7i8.definition: Negligent Hiring: A legal claim that arises when an employer fails to exercise reasonable care in hiring an employee, resulting in harm to a third party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7iA.label: JB30 Budgeting - between the parties (UK J-CODE)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7iA.definition: Work on budgeting between the parties following initial completion of the first budget, including the monitoring of costs incurred against the budget and any applications for variation of a budget.
english_labels: JB30 Budgeting - between the parties (UK J-CODE)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7iD.label: Responses to Requests for Admission
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7iD.definition: Responses to Requests for Admission are written statements made in response to a request for admission, which is a type of discovery document used in legal proceedings to establish the truth of certain facts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7iM.label: Consent in Lieu of Meeting Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7iM.definition: A Consent in Lieu of Meeting Clause is a provision in a contract that allows parties to give their consent to a proposed action without the need for a formal meeting.
english_labels: Consent in Lieu of Meeting Clause

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7iR.label: AI Governance
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7iR.definition: AI Governance refers to the frameworks, policies, and practices that guide the ethical development, deployment, and oversight of artificial intelligence systems. It encompasses the establishment of standards and regulations to ensure AI systems are transparent, accountable, and aligned with societal values and ethical principles

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7iS.label: Freedom from War and Armed Conflict
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7iS.definition: Freedom from war and armed conflict is a human aspiration often reflected in international humanitarian law, which seeks to limit the effects of armed conflict on people and communities. While not always explicitly defined as a "right," various international treaties like the Geneva Conventions aim to protect civilians, prisoners of war, and combatants from unnecessary suffering and violence during times of conflict.
english_labels: Freedom from War and Armed Conflict

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7iU.label: Computer Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7iU.definition: Computer Malpractice refers to a type of malpractice claim that arises from the failure of a professional to use reasonable care in the use of computer technology, resulting in harm to a client or patient.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7iU.label: oasis:Expression
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7iU.definition: A type of metadata that describes a work of art or literature, including its author, title, and other identifying information.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7iV.label: Diversity Jurisdiction
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7iV.definition: The concept of Diversity Jurisdiction refers to the authority of a federal court to hear a case between parties from different states or countries, where the amount in controversy exceeds a certain threshold.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7iX.label: Neurology Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7iX.definition: Negligent or wrongful conduct by a medical professional in the field of neurology, resulting in harm or injury to a patient.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ia.label: Peripheral Arterial Disease
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ia.definition: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is a condition characterized by the narrowing or blockage of peripheral arteries, typically in the legs, due to atherosclerosis or other vascular issues. PAD can cause symptoms such as claudication (pain during walking), decreased limb perfusion, and can lead to severe complications including ulcers or gangrene if untreated.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ib.label: Judicial Order
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ib.definition: A judicial order is a written directive issued by a court, typically in response to a motion or petition, that directs a party to take or refrain from taking a particular action.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ig.label: Secret
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ig.definition: Secret is a security classification level used for information that requires significant protection because its unauthorized disclosure could cause serious damage to the organization (e.g., company, nonprofit, nation). Access to secret information is restricted to individuals with the appropriate security clearance and a demonstrated need to know.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ih.label: Notice of Related Cases
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ih.definition: A Notice of Related Cases is a written communication informing parties involved in a legal case of other cases that may have a bearing on the current case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7il.label: Idaho Juvenile Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7il.definition: Idaho Juvenile Court refers to a specialized court within the Idaho State Courts system that deals with cases involving minors.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7in.label: End-to-End Transaction Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7in.definition: End-to-End Transaction Management refers to the complete process of managing legal transactions from start to finish, including all necessary steps and parties involved.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7in.label: Grand Jury Proceeding
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7in.definition: A Grand Jury Proceeding is a legal process where a group of citizens is convened to determine whether there is enough evidence to bring criminal charges against a person or entity.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7io.label: Arkansas District Court - Independence Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7io.definition: Arkansas District Court - Independence Cty. is a specific court within the Arkansas District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Independence County, Arkansas.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ir.label: Employer Retaliation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ir.definition: The act of an employer taking adverse action against an employee in response to the employee engaging in protected activity, such as reporting illegal conduct or filing a workers' compensation claim.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7iz.label: Motion to Add Creditors
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7iz.definition: A Motion to Add Creditors is a formal request filed in a bankruptcy case by the debtor to include additional creditors not originally listed in the initial bankruptcy schedules. This motion ensures that all relevant parties are notified of the bankruptcy proceedings and can participate in the distribution of assets or discharge of debts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7iz.label: Business Trust
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7iz.definition: A business trust is a form of business organization which is similar to a corporation, in which investors receive transferable certificates of beneficial interest.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7j2.label: New Mexico Metropolitan Court - Bernalillo County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7j2.definition: The New Mexico Metropolitan Court - Bernalillo County is a specific court within the New Mexico Metropolitan Court system that handles cases within Bernalillo County.
english_labels: New Mexico Metropolitan Court - Bernalillo County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7j2.label: False Designation of Origin
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7j2.definition: A False Designation of Origin claim may be filed when an entity falsely represents the origin of their goods or services, misleading consumers and potentially causing damage to the business or reputation of the rightful owner of the trademark. In the United States, this type of claim is typically brought under the Lanham Act.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7jR.label: Pechanga Band of Luiseno Mission Indians
english_labels: Pechanga Band of Luiseno Mission Indians

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7jZ.label: Payment Defense
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7jZ.definition: A Payment Defense is a legal argument or strategy used by a defendant in a civil litigation case to refute or deny the plaintiff's claim for payment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7jZ.label: L200 Pre-Trial Pleadings and Motions
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7jZ.definition: L200 Pre-Trial Pleadings and Motions refer to the initial legal documents and requests filed by parties in a lawsuit before the trial phase, including complaints, answers, and motions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7jf.label: Engagement Arrangements
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7jf.definition: Ancillary engagement terms and features that the Provider may provide the Buyer, which may or may not involve remuneration.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7jt.label: Output VAT Payment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7jt.definition: Output VAT Payment refers to the Value Added Tax that a business collects on its sales of goods and services. This tax is remitted to the government after offsetting any Input VAT, ensuring businesses pay VAT only on the value they add to the products or services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ju.label: Shoshone-Bannock Tribes of the Fort Hall Reservation
english_labels: Shoshone-Bannock Tribes of the Fort Hall Reservation

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ju.label: Zoning Text Amendments
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ju.definition: Zoning Text Amendments refer to the changes made to the written regulations and ordinances that define how the land within different zones can be used. These changes can clarify ambiguities, address new development challenges, or enact new policies, and typically require legal review, public hearings, and governmental approvals.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7jz.label: Appellate Letter
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7jz.definition: An appellate letter is a written communication submitted to a higher court requesting review of a lower court's decision, and is a type of correspondence and form used in the appellate filing process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7k5.label: Business Division
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7k5.definition: A Business Division is a large organizational unit within a company that operates somewhat independently, often with its own profit and loss responsibility. It typically focuses on a distinct product line or market segment and may contain multiple departments or business units to support its specific objectives and operations

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7k6.label: Motion for Judgment on the Pleadings
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7k6.definition: A Motion for Judgment on the Pleadings is a type of dispositive motion that asks the court to make a decision based solely on the pleadings and without the need for a trial.
english_labels: Motion for Judgment on the Pleadings

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kA.label: INVOICE_TAX_TOTAL
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kA.definition: The concept of INVOICE_TAX_TOTAL refers to the total amount of taxes charged on an invoice, as defined in the LEDES98BI V5 Format Rev 1-2020 standard.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kD.label: Transaction Negotiation Dynamics
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kD.definition: Transaction negotiation dynamics refer to the processes and interactions involved in negotiating the terms and conditions of a business transaction between parties. These dynamics encompass various strategies, styles, and behaviors that influence the negotiation's outcome, including the degree of cooperation, conflict, and communication between the parties involved.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kE.label: Bankruptcy Schedule - Expenses
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kE.definition: Bankruptcy Schedule - Expenses, also known as Schedule J, requires the debtor to list all monthly living expenses, including housing, utilities, food, transportation, and other necessary costs. This schedule provides a detailed account of the debtor's expenditure, helping the court and creditors understand the debtor's financial obligations and capacity for debt repayment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kH.label: Visa for Specialty Occupation Workers from Australia
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kH.definition: The visa for Specialty Occupation Workers from Australia, commonly known as the E-3 visa in the United States, is a special work visa category that allows Australian nationals to work in a "specialty occupation" in the U.S. A "specialty occupation" is generally defined as a role requiring a bachelor's degree or higher in a specific field, and the visa is subject to annual numerical limitations.
english_labels: Visa for Specialty Occupation Workers from Australia

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kI.label: Employment Geographic Location
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kI.definition: Employment Geographic Location refers to the physical or virtual place where an employee performs their job duties, which can range from a specific city, state, or country to a remote setting. This location often has implications for taxation, labor laws, and eligibility for location-based benefits or allowances.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kN.label: Buyer Consent Not Unreasonably Withheld
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kN.definition: The concept of "Buyer Consent Not Unreasonably Withheld" refers to the requirement that a buyer's consent must be obtained before a certain action can be taken, but the buyer cannot unreasonably withhold their consent.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kQ.label: New York Civil Court - Queens County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kQ.definition: A court located in Queens County, New York that handles civil legal disputes within its jurisdiction.
english_labels: New York Civil Court - Queens County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kT.label: Interference with Contractual Right
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kT.definition: The concept of Interference with Contractual Right refers to the intentional and unjustified interference with a contractual relationship between two parties by a third party, causing harm or damages to one of the parties involved.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kU.label: Information Security Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kU.definition: Law regulating the protection of information and information systems from unauthorized access

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kY.label: Expert Witness Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kY.definition: Expert Witness Management refers to the process of managing and coordinating the selection, retention, and preparation of expert witnesses for use in legal proceedings, within the broader context of Litigation Management.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kd.label: Zapotec
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kd.definition: Zapotec (Language) is a structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary specific to the Zapotec people and culture.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kh.label: Matter Discount or Credit Category
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kh.definition: A Matter Discount or Credit Category is a subcategory of Discounts and Credits that pertains specifically to the reduction of fees or costs associated with a particular legal matter.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kj.label: Wrongful Conviction
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kj.definition: A wrongful conviction is a legal concept that refers to the conviction of an innocent person due to errors or misconduct by the government, resulting in damages for which the government may be held liable under the legal theory of governmental tort liability.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kk.label: Seller
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kk.definition: A seller is a person, company or entity who sells a thing or property in exchange for other property (often money). One who disposes of a thing in consideration of money.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kl.label: Order for Remote Hearing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kl.definition: An Order for Telephonic Hearing is a written document that directs a court proceeding to be conducted via telephone, videoconference, or other remote means, and is typically used in bankruptcy and restructuring cases.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7km.label: Criminal Battery
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7km.definition: The intentional and unlawful use of force against another person, resulting in harmful or offensive contact, without that person's consent.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kn.label: Civil Legal Determination
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kn.definition: A "civil legal determination" refers to the decision or verdict made by a court in a civil case. It includes outcomes such as finding a party liable or not liable for a particular claim or issue. This determination often leads to remedies or judgments, such as monetary awards or injunctive relief, to resolve the dispute between the parties involved in the civil litigation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ko.label: "'Reasonably likely/expected breach' of fiduciary duties" Language
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ko.definition: The concept of "'Reasonably likely/expected breach' of fiduciary duties" refers to the language used in legal documents to describe a situation where a fiduciary is expected to violate their duties, and the legal standards that apply in such a scenario.
english_labels: "'Reasonably likely/expected breach' of fiduciary duties" Language

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kt.label: Last Clear Chance Doctrine
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kt.definition: The Last Clear Chance Doctrine is a legal principle in tort law that allows a plaintiff to recover damages even if they were partially at fault, provided the defendant had the final opportunity to avoid the accident but failed to do so. This doctrine mitigates the harshness of contributory negligence by shifting the focus to the defendant's ability to prevent the harm.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kx.label: New York City Court - Amsterdam
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kx.definition: New York City Court - Amsterdam is a specific court within the New York City Court system located in Amsterdam, NY.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kz.label: JH20 Other Party's expert evidence (UK J-CODE)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kz.definition: Considering Other Party(s)' expert evidence, preparing and asking questions of their experts, considering replies, reviewing case in light of such evidence.
english_labels: JH20 Other Party's expert evidence (UK J-CODE)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kz.label: Kansas District Court - Bourbon County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7kz.definition: A court located in Bourbon County, Kansas that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7l0.label: Georgia Superior Court - Baker County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7l0.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Baker County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Baker County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7l1.label: New Mexico Magistrate Court - Hidalgo County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7l1.definition: A court located in Hidalgo County, New Mexico that has limited jurisdiction over certain types of cases.
english_labels: New Mexico Magistrate Court - Hidalgo County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7l1.label: Missouri Circuit Court - DeKalb County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7l1.definition: A Missouri Circuit Court in DeKalb County is a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within DeKalb County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7l1.label: Expert Report
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7l1.definition: An Expert Report is a written document that provides an opinion or analysis on a specific subject matter by an individual with specialized knowledge or experience, often used as evidence in legal proceedings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7l4.label: Litigation Civil Legal Theories
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7l4.definition: Litigation Civil Legal Theories refer to the various legal arguments and principles that are used in civil litigation cases, such as the doctrine of collateral estoppel or comparative negligence, to support a party's claim or defense.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7l5.label: Court Reporter
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7l5.definition: Person who provides verbatim recordings of each session of the court and every other proceeding by shorthand, mechanical means, electronic sound recording, or any other method. See 28 U.S. Code § 753

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7l8.label: Procurement Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7l8.definition: Procurement Management refers to the process of acquiring goods and services for a business or organization, and involves activities such as identifying needs, selecting vendors, negotiating contracts, and managing supplier relationships.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lC.label: units
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lC.definition: "Actual number of hours billed to this line item, e.g. ""3.40"". If FEE.charge_type = ""F"", enter the number of units that will be multiplied by the rate necessary to equal the FEE.base_amount charged for this line item. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lC.label: Systemic Sclerosis
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lC.definition: Systemic sclerosis (also known as scleroderma) constitutes a spectrum of disease in which thickening of the skin is the clinical hallmark. Raynaud's phenomenon, often medically severe and progressive, is present frequently and may be the peripheral manifestation of a vasospastic abnormality in the heart, lungs, and kidneys. The CREST syndrome (calcinosis, Raynaud's phenomenon, esophageal dysmotility, sclerodactyly, and telangiectasia) is a variant that may slowly progress over years to the generalized process, systemic sclerosis.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lG.label: Failure of Consideration
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lG.definition: Failure of Consideration is a legal defense that asserts that one party did not receive the agreed-upon consideration or value in exchange for their performance or promise, which renders the contract or agreement unenforceable.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lH.label: Tai languages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lH.definition: The Tai languages are a group of related languages spoken in Southeast Asia, including Thai, Lao, and Shan.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lM.label: Maximum Exposure Amount
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lM.definition: The Maximum Exposure Amount is the highest possible monetary value that is at stake in a legal dispute, which is determined by the amount in controversy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lR.label: New York Children's Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lR.definition: A specialized court within the New York State Courts system that handles cases involving children, such as abuse and neglect, delinquency, and adoption.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lT.label: tx_id
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lT.definition: A unique identifier associated with the tax/rate/jurisdiction, assigned by the law firm.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lV.label: Statistical Summary of Certain Liabilities
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lV.definition: A Statistical Summary of Certain Liabilities is a type of information presented in a Bankruptcy and Restructuring Document that provides a numerical representation of certain debts or obligations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lZ.label: Fact Witness
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lZ.definition: A nonparty who testifies to things that person has perceived.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7la.label: Proceeding Transferred to Problem-Solving Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7la.definition: The concept "Case Transferred to Problem-Solving Court" refers to the act of moving a legal case from a traditional court to a specialized court that focuses on addressing underlying issues that may have contributed to the legal matter, such as substance abuse or mental health problems.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lb.label: Automobile Damaged at Parking Facility
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lb.definition: An Automobile Damaged at Parking Facility refers to a legal claim related to property damage caused to a vehicle while parked in a designated parking area, and falls under the broader categories of Property and Premises Liability Claims.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lb.label: Testifying Expert Witness
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lb.definition: An expert whom a party retains for consultation, where that expert provides oral testimony and/or a written report.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lf.label: Simple Agreement for Future Equity
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lf.definition: A Simple Agreement for Future Equity (SAFE) is a contractual agreement between an investor and a company wherein the investor provides capital to the company in exchange for the rights to receive equity at a later date. The equity is usually issued during a subsequent financing round, at which point the SAFE converts based on the terms set forth in the agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lj.label: Scènes à Faire
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lj.definition: Scènes à Faire in copyright law refers to scenes, elements, or themes that are standard, necessary, or customary to a particular genre and are therefore not protectable due to their lack of originality. This doctrine acknowledges that certain expressions are indispensable or typical for certain topics or settings and are therefore free for use by all.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ln.label: Equal Pay Act Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ln.definition: An Gender Pay Equality Claim is a legal action alleging violation of a law requiring that men and women in the same workplace be given equal pay for equal work. The claim typically involves issues of gender-based wage discrimination.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lt.label: AAA Commercial Arbitration Rules and Mediation Procedures
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lt.definition: The AAA Commercial Arbitration Rules and Mediation Procedures are a set of guidelines and procedures established by the American Arbitration Association for resolving commercial disputes through arbitration and mediation.
english_labels: AAA Commercial Arbitration Rules and Mediation Procedures

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lw.label: Change of Recommendation Covenant
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lw.definition: A Change of Recommendation Covenant is a provision in a deal protection agreement that requires a target company's board to recommend a new offer to its shareholders, even if it is less favorable than a previous offer, in exchange for certain protections for the acquirer.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lx.label: ENT Negligence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7lx.definition: Failure of a healthcare provider to exercise reasonable care, skill, or diligence in the treatment of a patient resulting in harm or injury.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7m1.label: Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7m1.definition: A WARN Act claim is a legal action initiated by an employee against their employer for not complying with the Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) Act. The WARN Act is a federal law that requires certain employers to provide advance notice of significant layoffs or plant closings to affected employees, as well as to state and local government officials. The claim typically arises when an employer does not comply with the WARN Act's notice requirements, which can result in employees losing their jobs without sufficient notice or time to find alternative employment.
english_labels: Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act Claim

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7m3.label: Reinsurance Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7m3.definition: A Reinsurance Agreement is a contract where an insurer transfers a portion of its risks to another insurer, known as the reinsurer. This helps the primary insurer manage its risk exposure and maintain solvency by spreading potential large losses.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7m3.label: Genderqueer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7m3.definition: Genderqueer is a gender identity that falls outside the conventional binary of male or female and may encompass a range of identities that are not exclusively masculine or feminine. Legally, genderqueer individuals may seek recognition and protection under laws pertaining to gender discrimination, harassment, and equality, similar to other non-binary or gender non-conforming identities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7m7.label: Motorcyclist
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7m7.definition: A motorcycle driver is an individual who operates a motorcycle, controlling its mechanisms to navigate roads and other environments. This role entails a distinct set of skills and adherence to specific traffic laws to ensure the safety of the driver and other road users.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mB.label: CLIENT_NAME
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mB.definition: The term CLIENT_NAME refers to a specific data element within the LEDES98BI V5 Format Rev 1-2020 standard, which is used to identify the name of a client in legal billing and invoicing processes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mL.label: Senior Subordinated Credit Ranking
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mL.definition: Senior Subordinated Credit Ranking refers to the priority status of senior subordinated debts, which are ranked above junior and junior subordinated debts but below senior debts in the event of liquidation. This ranking ensures that senior subordinated creditors are paid before junior creditors from the proceeds of the liquidated assets, providing them with a moderate level of security and reduced risk compared to junior debts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mL.label: Judgment Lien
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mL.definition: A judgment lien is a type of lien that is created when a court grants a judgment in favor of a creditor, giving them the right to place a lien on the debtor's property in order to secure payment of the debt.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mM.label: Copyright Work Types
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mM.definition: Copyright Work Types encompass various forms of creative works such as Derivative Work, Collective Work, and Joint Work, each with unique characteristics and legal implications. Derivative Works are based on pre-existing works, Collective Works involve the assembly of independent works into a single publication, and Joint Works are created by collaboration with merged contributions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mP.label: Key Performance Indicator
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mP.definition: A Key Performance Indicator (KPI) is a quantifiable measure used to evaluate the success of an organization, employee, or process in achieving specific objectives. KPIs are essential for assessing performance, guiding strategic decisions, and improving efficiency across various sectors.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mR.label: New York Supreme Court - Nassau County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mR.definition: The New York Supreme Court - Nassau County is a court of general jurisdiction located in Nassau County, New York, with authority to hear and decide a wide range of civil and criminal cases.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - Nassau County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mS.label: Motion to Admit Involuntarily
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mS.definition: A Motion to Admit Involuntarily is a request made in a trial court to allow evidence that was obtained without the consent of the person from whom it was taken.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mT.label: Force Majeure Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mT.definition: A Force Majeure Clause is a contractual provision that can modify (e.g., terminate, excuse, extend) the party's performance of its obligations under the contract when unforeseeable events beyond the control of the parties, such as natural disasters or acts of war, make performance impracticable or impossible.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mV.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Pike County (8th Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Pike County (8th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mV.label: Insurance Adjuster
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mV.definition: An insurance adjuster is a professional who works for an insurance company and investigates and evaluates insurance claims made by policyholders.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mW.label: Nilo-Saharan languages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mW.definition: Nilo-Saharan languages are a group of languages spoken in parts of Africa, including Sudan, Chad, and Ethiopia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mZ.label: U.S. Personnel Appeals Board
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mZ.definition: The U.S. Personnel Appeals Board (PAB) is a specific administrative proceeding venue within the U.S. Government Accountability Office that handles appeals related to personnel actions taken by federal agencies.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ma.label: Inchoate Criminal Offenses
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ma.definition: Inchoate Criminal Offenses are incomplete or anticipatory criminal acts that have not yet been fully carried out, but are still punishable by law.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7md.label: Uncontested Adoption
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7md.definition: An Uncontested Adoption is when all relevant parties agree on the adoption of a child without any opposition. Typically, the biological parents have either voluntarily relinquished their parental rights or have had them legally terminated, allowing the adoption process to proceed smoothly and without legal disputes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7me.label: Banking Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7me.definition: Law that governs how banks and other financial institutions conduct business.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mg.label: Motion to File Oversized Brief
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mg.definition: A Motion to File Oversized Brief is a legal request to submit a brief that exceeds the standard page limit set by the court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mg.label: Property Rights and Transactions Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mg.definition: Law relating to the acquisition and transfer of real property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mh.label: Ewondo
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mh.definition: A language spoken in Cameroon, primarily in the central and southern regions, belonging to the Bantu language family.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mi.label: Outstanding Fees Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mi.definition: An Outstanding Fees Clause is a provision in a contract that requires one party to pay any unpaid fees or charges to the other party before the contract can be terminated or enforced.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mj.label: Promise to Pay Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mj.definition: A Promise to Pay Clause is a specific type of contractual clause that obligates one party to pay a specified amount of money to another party at a designated time or upon the occurrence of a certain event.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mq.label: UK National Health Service
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mq.definition: The UK National Health Service (NHS) is a publicly funded healthcare system in the United Kingdom, providing comprehensive medical services to residents. Established to offer free at the point of use healthcare, the NHS administers services including hospitals, general practitioners, dental care, and specialized treatments, ensuring accessible health care across the country.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ms.label: Argumentative Objection
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ms.definition: An Argumentative Objection is raised when a party in a legal proceeding believes that a question posed by the opposing counsel is designed to provoke an argument rather than elicit factual information. This objection seeks to maintain the proceeding's decorum, ensuring that questions are neutral and focused on obtaining relevant evidence.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mu.label: Commander in Chief Clause Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7mu.definition: A Commander in Chief Clause claim refers to a legal argument challenging the constitutionality of an action taken by the President or executive branch of government based on the powers and limitations outlined in the Commander in Chief Clause of the United States Constitution. This claim asserts that a particular action exceeds the President's authority as the Commander in Chief of the armed forces, potentially rendering it unconstitutional. The Commander in Chief Clause grants the President the power to command and control the military forces of the nation but is subject to checks and balances established by other constitutional provisions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7n4.label: Lessor’s Breach of Express Warranty on Goods
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7n4.definition: The Lessor's Breach of Express Warranty on Goods refers to the failure of the party leasing goods to fulfill a specific promise or guarantee made about the quality or condition of the goods, resulting in legal claims by the lessee.
english_labels: Lessor’s Breach of Express Warranty on Goods

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7n6.label: Consumer Contract Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7n6.definition: Consumer Contract Claims are legal claims made by a party in a contract with a consumer, including claims related to billing errors, unlawful provisions, unconscionable circumstances, and improper actions by loan brokers.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7n9.label: Blasphemous Material
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7n9.definition: Blasphemous Material refers to content that shows disrespect or irreverence toward religious beliefs, figures, deities, or sacred symbols. This type of material often leads to significant controversy and legal actions in jurisdictions where blasphemy laws are enforced.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7nC.label: Political Party
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7nC.definition: A political party is an organized group of individuals who share similar political beliefs and goals, seeking to influence public policy and gain control of government through the electoral process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7nE.label: Securities Purchase Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7nE.definition: Securities Purchase Agreement is a legal contract detailing the sale and purchase of securities, either equity or debt. It includes terms such as the purchase price, representations, warranties, and covenants of the parties involved.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7nF.label: Bankruptcy Plan Consummation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7nF.definition: Bankruptcy Plan Consummation refers to the completion of the necessary actions outlined in a bankruptcy plan, leading to its implementation. It marks the point at which the bankruptcy proceedings are consummated, and the plan's terms are effectuated.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7nI.label: Minnesota District Court - Kandiyohi County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7nI.definition: Minnesota District Court - Kandiyohi County: A specific court within the Minnesota District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Kandiyohi County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7nI.label: Intranet Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7nI.definition: Intranet Management refers to the process of organizing and controlling the internal network of an organization, including the management of content, access, and security.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7nJ.label: Chemical Patent
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7nJ.definition: A chemical patent is a legal protection granted to inventors of new and useful chemical compounds, compositions, processes, or improvements thereof.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7nL.label: Closing Event
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7nL.definition: The Closing Event is a specific type of event that occurs during a merger and acquisition or transaction, marking the completion of the deal.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7nR.label: Motion to Disqualify Counsel
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7nR.definition: A Motion to Disqualify Counsel is a legal request to remove an attorney from a case due to a conflict of interest or other ethical violation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7nS.label: Motion to File Supplemental Briefing for Petition for Rehearing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7nS.definition: A Motion to File Supplemental Briefing for Petition for Rehearing is a formal request to submit additional written arguments or evidence to support a request for a new hearing, after a decision has already been made, in order to address new or relevant information that was not available at the time of the original hearing.
english_labels: Motion to File Supplemental Briefing for Petition for Rehearing

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7nY.label: Hit and Run
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7nY.definition: The concept of Hit and Run refers to a criminal offense where a person involved in an accident fails to stop and provide information, such as their name and contact details, to the other party involved.
english_labels: Failure to Stop and Give Information

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7nc.label: Fixed Rate Interest Payment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7nc.definition: A Fixed Rate Interest Payment is a type of interest payment structure where the interest rate remains constant throughout the life of the debt instrument. Under this arrangement, the borrower pays a predetermined interest rate at regular intervals, typically annually or semi-annually, which is established at the time of issuance and does not change regardless of market fluctuations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ng.label: Immigration Arrival in Country
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ng.definition: Arrival In Country refers to the act of entering a nation, commonly documented and regulated through immigration control points like airports, seaports, and land borders. The process usually involves inspection and verification of travel documents, visas, and other entry requirements, after which the individual is granted or denied permission to enter the country.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ni.label: Primary Care Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ni.definition: Primary Care Malpractice: Negligence or wrongdoing by a healthcare provider who is responsible for the initial diagnosis and treatment of a patient, resulting in harm or injury to the patient.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7nn.label: Oil and Gas Extraction Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7nn.definition: Industries in this group operate and/or develop oil and gas field properties. Such activities may include exploration for crude petroleum and natural gas; drilling, completing, and equipping wells; operating separators, emulsion breakers, desilting equipment, and field gathering lines for crude petroleum and natural gas; and all other activities in the preparation of oil and gas up to the point of shipment from the producing property. This subsector includes the production of crude petroleum, the mining and extraction of oil from oil shale and oil sands, and the production of natural gas, sulfur recovery from natural gas, and recovery of hydrocarbon liquids.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7nq.label: Negligence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7nq.definition: Negligence is a legal concept that refers to the failure to exercise reasonable care, resulting in harm or injury to another person or property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ns.label: Pumpkins
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ns.definition: Pumpkins are a type of winter squash from the Cucurbita genus, characterized by their round shape, ribbed skin, and vibrant orange color. They are widely cultivated for their edible flesh and seeds and are valued for their nutritional content, including vitamins A and C, fiber, and antioxidants, as well as their use in decorative and cultural traditions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7o4.label: Construction and Development Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7o4.definition: Law dealing with matters relating to building construction, engineering, and related fields.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7o6.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Bureau County (13th Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Bureau County (13th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7o7.label: Welsh
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7o7.definition: Welsh (Language) is a structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary, and is spoken in Wales and some parts of the United Kingdom.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7o9.label: Indiana Superior Court - Greene County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7o9.definition: Indiana Superior Court - Greene County refers to a specific court within the Indiana Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Greene County, Indiana.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oA.label: Legislative Immunity
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oA.definition: Legislative Immunity refers to the legal protection granted to legislators from being held liable for their actions or statements made in the course of their legislative duties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oB.label: Entity
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oB.definition: A legal entity is a legal construct through which the law allows a group of natural persons to act as if they were a single person for certain purposes. The most common purposes are lawsuits, property ownership, and contracts. Some examples of legal entities include companies, cooperatives (co-ops), corporations, municipalities, political parties, sovereigns, states, temples, trade unions, and ships or vessels.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oD.label: work_location_locality
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oD.definition: The location where the work associated with the fee item was performed, to support the taxes appearing in the for example, in canada appropriate values would be the province; if city or other local tax is charged would be city or locality. use accepted abbreviations for state or province mandated by the country's postal service.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oI.label: Dyscalculia
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oI.definition: Dyscalculia is a specific learning disability that affects an individual's ability to understand, remember, and manipulate numbers and mathematical concepts. This condition leads to difficulties in performing arithmetic operations, understanding numerical relationships, and grasping abstract math concepts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oJ.label: Non-fundamental Representations and Warranties
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oJ.definition: Non-fundamental representations and warranties are the less essential or non-core statements made by a party in a contract, typically pertaining to the condition of a business, assets, or the accuracy of certain information. While important, these representations and warranties are generally considered less critical to the overall transaction than fundamental representations and warranties, which relate to crucial aspects such as the seller's ownership, authority, and the validity of the contract itself.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oJ.label: Georgia Superior Court - Cobb County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oJ.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Cobb County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Cobb County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oJ.label: Sponsorship Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oJ.definition: A Sponsorship Agreement is a legally binding contract between two parties that outlines the terms and conditions of a sponsorship arrangement, typically involving the exchange of goods, services, or financial support in exchange for advertising or promotional opportunities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oM.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Dearborn County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oM.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Indiana that hears civil and criminal cases within Dearborn County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oN.label: Common Benefit Fee Methodology
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oN.definition: A Common Benefit Fee Methodology is a method of calculating attorney fees in a legal matter where the outcome of the case provides a benefit to a group of individuals, and the fees are divided among the group based on their proportionate share of the benefit received.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oO.label: Privileges & Immunities Clause Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oO.definition: A Privileges & Immunities Clause claim refers to a legal argument based on the Privileges and Immunities Clause of the United States Constitution, asserting that states cannot discriminate against citizens of other states by denying them fundamental rights and privileges. It aims to protect the rights and equal treatment of individuals traveling or residing in different states within the United States.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oP.label: Customs and Import Controls Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oP.definition: Customs and Import Controls Practice encompasses the legal frameworks and regulations governing the importation of goods into a country. This practice area includes compliance with customs laws, import duties, tariffs, import restrictions, and procedures for resolving disputes related to customs and import controls.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oW.label: Private Right of Action
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oW.definition: A private right of action refers to the legal authority granted to an individual or private party to file a lawsuit for violations of law that have affected them. Essentially, it enables citizens to enforce statutes or regulations by taking alleged violators to court, rather than relying solely on government agencies for enforcement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oZ.label: Dependent
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oZ.definition: A dependent is an individual who relies on another person, typically a family member, for financial support and is often eligible for specific tax benefits. In legal and insurance contexts, dependents may include spouses, children, and sometimes other relatives or individuals who live in the same household and rely on the primary earner for essential financial support.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oa.label: Member Liability in Joint Enterprise
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oa.definition: Member Liability in Joint Enterprise refers to the legal responsibility of individuals who are part of a joint enterprise, such as a partnership or corporation, for any liabilities incurred by the enterprise.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ob.label: Extranet Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ob.definition: Extranet Management refers to the management of a secure network that allows external parties to access and share information with an organization, and is a subset of Collaboration Management.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ob.label: Educational Benefits
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ob.definition: Educational benefits are perks provided to employees to support their educational goals and aspirations, including offerings such as courses, seminars, tuition reimbursement, and professional development opportunities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7og.label: DEPRECATED: Bankruptcy Plan Hearing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7og.definition: DEPRECATED: Bankruptcy Plan Hearing - A hearing held in a bankruptcy case to consider the confirmation of a plan of reorganization or liquidation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oh.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Massac County (1st Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Massac County (1st Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oh.label: Domestic Relations Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oh.definition: A Domestic Relations Claim is a legal action brought by a party in a family law or matrimonial matter, seeking relief related to issues such as divorce, child custody, child support, alimony, or property division.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oi.label: Strategic Buyer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oi.definition: A strategic buyer is a type of M&A buyer who acquires a company with the intention of achieving long-term goals, such as expanding their market share or diversifying their product offerings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oo.label: Turkeys
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7oo.definition: Turkeys are large domesticated birds belonging to the species Meleagris gallopavo, commonly raised for their meat. Known for their distinctive fan-shaped tail and wattled neck, turkeys are an important source of poultry, particularly in North America, where they play a central role in traditional meals like Thanksgiving.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ov.label: Debarment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ov.definition: Debarment refers to the exclusion of an individual or entity from participating in certain activities, particularly government contracting and subcontracting, due to violations of regulations, misconduct, or failure to comply with contractual obligations. This measure aims to protect public interest by preventing unreliable or unethical parties from engaging in government-related activities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ow.label: Indiana Superior Court - Decatur County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7ow.definition: Indiana Superior Court - Decatur County refers to a specific court within the Indiana Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Decatur County, Indiana.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7p3.label: Structured Finance Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7p3.definition: A Structured Finance Agreement pertains to complex financial transactions that pool and repackage financial assets, often for the purpose of risk diversification and enhanced returns. These agreements govern the terms, parties involved, and the structure of such transactions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7p5.label: New York Supreme Court - Tioga County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7p5.definition: The New York Supreme Court - Tioga County is a court of general jurisdiction located in Tioga County, New York, with authority to hear and decide a wide range of civil and criminal cases.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - Tioga County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7p5.label: Motion to Extend Time to File Brief
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7p5.definition: A Motion to Extend Time to File Brief is a formal request made to a court to allow additional time beyond the original deadline for submitting a written argument or statement in a legal case.
english_labels: Motion to Extend Time to File Brief

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7pB.label: Indiana Superior Court - Blackford County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7pB.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Indiana that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Blackford County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7pE.label: Association and Membership Liability
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7pE.definition: Association and Membership Liability refers to the legal responsibility of individuals or entities who are members or associated with a corporation or partnership for any claims or damages arising from the actions or decisions of the organization.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7pE.label: Unmarried
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7pE.definition: The concept of "Single (Marital Status)" refers to an individual who is not currently married or in a legally recognized partnership.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7pF.label: Employment Immigration Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7pF.definition: National statutes, and regulations governing employment-based immigration into and deportation from a country.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7pH.label: Clearly Erroneous
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7pH.definition: A legal standard of review used by appellate courts to determine if a lower court's decision was clearly incorrect or mistaken.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7pJ.label: inv_total_tax_other_iso
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7pJ.definition: "For mixed currency situations only where it is mandated that the total tax must also be reported in a different currency ISO. The sum of all MATTER.matter_tax_on_fees + MATTER.matter_tax_on_exp + the sum of all TAX_TIER_SUMMARY.tax_tier_total_amount for this inv_id in the ISO required by law as identified in INVOICE.inv_other_iso. This figure includes Withholding Taxes and Tiered Taxes applicable to this invoice.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7pN.label: JD20 Other Settlement Matters (UK J-CODE)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7pN.definition: Work that is directed to settlement including Part 36 and other offers and consequent negotiations (includes all forms of ADR other than mediation).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7pQ.label: Breach of Confidential Relationship
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7pQ.definition: The Breach of Confidential Relationship is the unauthorized disclosure of confidential information by a person who has a duty to keep it confidential, resulting in harm to the party who entrusted the information.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7pU.label: Florida Mediator Ethics Advisory Committee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R7pU.definition: The Florida Mediator Ethics Advisory Committee is a committee established by the Florida State Courts to provide guidance on ethical issues related to mediation in Florida.
