https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R872.label: Landlord
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R872.definition: One who lets land to another: the owner or holder of land or houses which he leases or rents to another. Seattle Hous. Auth. v. City of Seattle, 416 P.3d 1280 (Wash. App. 2018)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R876.label: Myelodysplastic Syndromes
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R876.definition: Myelodysplastic syndromes are a group of disorders caused by poorly formed or dysfunctional blood cells due to ineffective hematopoiesis in the bone marrow. Patients with MDS often present with anemia, increased risk of infections, and bleeding problems due to the production of abnormal or insufficient blood cells.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R877.label: Lac du Flambeau Band of Lake Superior Chippewa Indian
english_labels: Lac du Flambeau Band of Lake Superior Chippewa Indian

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R878.label: Investor Relations Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R878.definition: An Investor Relations Agreement is a contract between a company and an agency or individual who manages communication and relationships with the company's investors. This includes reporting financial results, addressing investor inquiries, and ensuring regulatory compliance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87D.label: Braga
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87D.definition: Braga is a city in Portugal.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87E.label: Eviction Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87E.definition: An eviction claim is a legal action initiated by a landlord against a tenant to seek the removal of the tenant from a rented property. This claim is typically based on the tenant's alleged violation of the lease agreement, such as nonpayment of rent, breach of lease terms, or other grounds defined by local landlord-tenant laws. The eviction process involves court proceedings where both the landlord and tenant present their arguments, and a judge makes a decision regarding the eviction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87I.label: Trial Preparation Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87I.definition: Trial Preparation Practice refers to the specific legal work performed by a Legal Services Provider in preparing for a trial, including but not limited to, gathering evidence, interviewing witnesses, and drafting trial briefs.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87I.label: Material Adverse Effect Definition - "Arising from/out of and Resulting From" Language
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87I.definition: A Material Adverse Effect (MAE) Definition - "Arising from/out of and Resulting From" Language refers to a clause in a contract that outlines the specific circumstances under which a party can terminate the agreement due to a significant negative change in the financial condition or business operations of the other party, which must be directly caused by a specific event or circumstance.
english_labels: Material Adverse Effect Definition - "Arising from/out of and Resulting From" Language

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87M.label: Prior Art Search Process
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87M.definition: The prior art search process is a methodical examination conducted to identify existing knowledge, inventions, or technologies relevant to a new invention or patent application. This process helps determine the novelty and non-obviousness of the invention by uncovering prior art that may impact its patentability.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87M.label: Informed Consent
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87M.definition: The concept of Informed Consent refers to the legal requirement for medical professionals to fully inform patients of the risks and benefits of a medical procedure or treatment, and to obtain the patient's voluntary agreement to undergo the procedure or treatment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87P.label: Savings and Loan Association
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87P.definition: A Savings and Loan Association (S&L) is a financial institution primarily focused on accepting savings deposits and making mortgage loans. S&Ls play a significant role in providing home financing, particularly for residential properties, by offering favorable mortgage terms to depositors.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87Q.label: Limited Company
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87Q.definition: A Limited Company (Ltd.) is a type of corporate structure where the shareholders' liability for debts and obligations of the company is limited to the amount of capital they have invested. This structure is prevalent globally and is characterized by the separation of ownership and management, promoting investment while mitigating personal financial risk for shareholders.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87T.label: Fort Belknap Indian Community of the Fort Belknap Reservation
english_labels: Fort Belknap Indian Community of the Fort Belknap Reservation

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87d.label: Motion to Reopen Adversary Proceeding
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87d.definition: A Motion to Reopen Adversary Proceeding is a request made in a bankruptcy case to reopen a previously closed legal dispute between parties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87e.label: Civil Conspiracy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87e.definition: A civil conspiracy is a wrongful agreement between two or more parties to commit an unlawful act or to achieve a lawful objective through unlawful means, resulting in harm to another party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87f.label: Scientific Research and Development Services Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87f.definition: This industry group comprises establishments engaged in conducting original investigation undertaken on a systematic basis to gain new knowledge (research) and/or the application of research findings or other scientific knowledge for the creation of new or significantly improved products or processes (experimental development). Techniques may include modeling and simulation. The industries within this industry group are defined on the basis of the domain of research; that is, on the scientific expertise of the establishment.
english_labels: Scientific Research and Development Services Industry

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87o.label: Adversary Proceeding Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87o.definition: Adversary Proceeding Practice (Bankruptcy) refers to the legal work performed by a Legal Services Provider in the course of a bankruptcy matter involving a dispute between parties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87o.label: Florida Circuit Court - Gadsden County - 2nd Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87o.definition: A court located in Gadsden County, Florida that is part of the larger Florida Circuit Court system.
english_labels: Florida Circuit Court - Gadsden County - 2nd Circuit Court

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87q.label: Vesting Schedule Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87q.definition: A Vesting Schedule Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the schedule for when an individual's ownership or entitlement to something, such as stock options or retirement benefits, becomes fully realized.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87t.label: Motion for New Trial - Evidentiary Issues
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87t.definition: A Motion for New Trial - Evidentiary Issues is a request made to a court to reconsider a previous decision based on issues related to the admissibility or sufficiency of evidence presented during the trial.
english_labels: Motion for New Trial - Evidentiary Issues

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87u.label: Military and Veterans Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87u.definition: Legal procedures and regulations specific to the military and veterans rights.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87v.label: Social Security Payments
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87v.definition: Social Security Payments are government-provided financial benefits designed to support individuals who are retired, disabled, or survivors of deceased workers. These payments are funded through payroll taxes and aim to provide a safety net for individuals and their families, ensuring a basic level of income.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87x.label: Minnesota District Court - Big Stone County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R87x.definition: Minnesota District Court - Big Stone County refers to a specific court within the Minnesota District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Big Stone County, Minnesota.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R881.definition: The United States Department of Education (ED or DoED) is a Cabinet-level department of the United States government. The primary functions of the Department of Education are to "establish policy for, administer and coordinate most federal assistance to education, collect data on US schools, and to enforce federal educational laws regarding privacy and civil rights."

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R883.definition: The National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) is an agency of the United States Department of Commerce that serves as the President's principal adviser on telecommunications policies pertaining to the United States' economic and technological advancement and to the regulation of the telecommunications industry.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R883.label: Economics and Statistics Administration
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R883.definition: The Economics and Statistics Administration (ESA) is an agency within the United States Department of Commerce (DOC) that analyzes, disseminates, and reports on national economic and demographic data.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R88K.definition: An Announcements Clause is a provision in a contract that requires one or both parties to provide notice to the other party before taking certain actions or making certain announcements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R88R.definition: An Insurance Application is a formal document that a prospective policyholder fills out to provide necessary information for an insurance provider to evaluate risk and underwrite a new insurance policy. https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R88V.label: Improperly Buying Securities During Corporate Takeover
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R88V.definition: The concept of "Improperly Buying Securities During Corporate Takeover" refers to the act of purchasing securities in a company during a takeover in a manner that violates securities laws or regulations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R88V.label: Faithless Servant Doctrine
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R88V.definition: The Faithless Servant Doctrine is a legal concept that holds an agent liable for any profits they wrongfully obtain while acting on behalf of their principal.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R88Z.definition: A Bicycle Lane Violation Claim involves allegations that a motorist or other road user has unlawfully used or obstructed a bicycle lane, violating regulations designed to ensure the safety and mobility of cyclists. Such claims typically lead to enforcement actions that may include fines or mandatory education on sharing the road responsibly.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R88i.label: Wage and Hour Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R88i.definition: Law that governs the wages rates an employer can pay its employees, the hours for which an employer must compensate its employees, child labor laws and meal and break laws.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R88m.label: Artificial Intelligence System Taxonomy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R88m.definition: Artificial Intelligence System Taxonomy is the hierarchical classification and organization of AI systems and related concepts. https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R88n.label: Non-Proposition Statement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R88n.definition: A Non-Proposition Statement is a statement that does not contain a factual assertion or proposition that can be proven true or false. These statements, such as questions, commands, or exclamations, are not considered hearsay because they are not offered to prove the truth of any content within the statement itself.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R88q.label: Prisoner Suicide
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R88q.definition: The concept of "Prisoner Suicide" refers to the act of intentionally taking one's own life by an individual who is incarcerated, and the legal claims related to the right to die in such circumstances.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R88v.label: Rye
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R88v.definition: Rye is a cereal crop belonging to the species Secale cereale, known for its hardiness and ability to grow in poor soils and cold climates. It is commonly used for making bread, whiskey, and animal feed, and provides essential nutrients such as carbohydrates, fiber, and vitamins.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R88z.label: DEPRECATED Creditor Claims Practice

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89D.label: Disparate Treatment Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89D.definition: A Disparate Treatment Claim is a legal claim that alleges an individual or group has been treated unfairly or differently based on a protected characteristic, such as race, gender, or age.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89K.label: Motion for Judgment Notwithstanding the Verdict
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89K.definition: A Motion for Judgment Notwithstanding the Verdict (JNOV) is a post-trial motion that asks the court to overturn a jury verdict and enter judgment in favor of the moving party.

Motion for Judgment Notwithstanding the Verdict

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89O.label: Ballot to Approve Bankruptcy Plan
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89O.definition: A Ballot to Approve Bankruptcy Plan is a voting document used by creditors to approve or reject a proposed bankruptcy plan.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89O.label: Termination of Parental Rights (Remedy)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89O.definition: The Termination of Parental Rights (TPR) is a legal process that permanently ends the legal relationship between a parent and their child, typically due to abuse, neglect, or abandonment, and allows for the child to be adopted or placed in a permanent home.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89P.label: Pre-Trial Statement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89P.definition: A pre-trial statement is a written document submitted by a party in a bankruptcy or restructuring case before the trial, outlining their position and evidence.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89S.definition: This phase includes all legal research tasks, including internal meetings and consultations with those with special expertise, and computer and on-line research.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89T.label: A.S. (Associate of Science)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89T.definition: An A.S. (Associate of Science) is a two-year degree commonly obtained from community colleges, focusing on science and mathematics courses. It serves as a starting point for further education or entry into science-related careers

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89U.label: Power and Authority Representation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89U.definition: A representation made by a party in a legal matter that they have the authority to act on behalf of another person or entity.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89c.label: Use Tax Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89c.definition: Use Tax Practice refers to the application, administration, and enforcement of taxes on the use, storage, or consumption of goods and services that were not subject to sales tax at the time of purchase. These taxes are designed to complement sales taxes and ensure that all taxable transactions are taxed appropriately, even if the purchase occurs out of state or through an online retailer.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89e.label: LINE_ITEM_TAX_RATE
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89e.definition: The LINE_ITEM_TAX_RATE concept refers to the tax rate applied to a specific line item in a legal invoice, as defined in the LEDES98BI V5 Format Rev 1-2020 standard.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89e.label: Unlawful Eviction of Tenant
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89e.definition: The Unlawful Eviction of Tenant is the act of a landlord removing a tenant from their rental property without following the proper legal procedures, such as obtaining a court order or providing proper notice.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89i.label: Corporate Representative Deposition
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89i.definition: A Corporate Representative Deposition is a legal proceeding where a company designates a representative to testify on its behalf in response to a subpoena or other legal request for information.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89l.label: Deal Stance
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89l.definition: Deal stance refers to the approach taken by an acquiring company when pursuing a takeover of another company. They include hostile takeovers, friendly takeovers, proxy contests, control positions, and minority stakes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89o.label: Notice of Voluntary Dismissal as of Right
english_labels: Notice of Voluntary Dismissal as of Right

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89o.label: Salivary Gland Cancer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89o.definition: Salivary gland cancer is a malignant neoplasm that originates in the salivary glands, which produce saliva to aid in digestion and maintain oral health. It includes various subtypes depending on the specific gland affected, such as parotid, submandibular, and sublingual glands, and can impact functions like swallowing and speaking.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89u.label: API and API Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89u.definition: API and API Management refers to the process of creating, publishing, and managing application programming interfaces (APIs) that allow different software applications to communicate with each other and share data.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89z.label: Security and Confidentiality Attributes
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R89z.definition: Security and Confidentiality Attributes refer to the various levels of protection and access controls applied to information to prevent unauthorized disclosure, modification, or destruction. These attributes include different classifications such as top secret, secret, confidential, and restricted, each defining the degree of security and the associated protocols for managing sensitive information within an organization (e.g., company, nonprofit, nation).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8A0.label: Yunnan
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8A0.definition: Yunnan is a province in China.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8A0.label: Mass Market Segment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8A0.definition: The mass market segment refers to a large, broad portion of the market that consists of a wide range of consumers with diverse preferences and needs. This segment targets the general population and is characterized by products and services that are designed for widespread appeal and accessibility, often with a focus on affordability and practicality

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8A2.label: Kardzhali
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8A2.definition: Kardzhali is a city located in the southern part of Bulgaria.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8A2.label: Asset Voting Attributes
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8A2.definition: Asset Voting Attributes encompass the various rights and limitations associated with voting entitlements linked to ownership of financial assets. These attributes include voting rights, non-voting rights, restricted voting rights, and enhanced voting rights, each defining the degree of influence a shareholder has in an organization's decision-making process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8A2.label: Petition for Treaty Trader Visa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8A2.definition: An E-1 petition refers to the application process for obtaining an E-1 Treaty Trader Visa in the United States. The E-1 visa is available to individuals from countries that have a qualifying treaty of commerce and navigation with the U.S. It allows foreign nationals who are involved in substantial trade between their home country and the U.S. to come to the U.S. to conduct business activities. The E-1 visa can be applied for by individuals, employees of the treaty trader, or the employer itself. The petition involves demonstrating the substantial nature of trade and meeting other eligibility requirements as outlined by U.S. immigration laws and regulations

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8A3.label: Education Liability
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8A3.definition: Education Liability refers to the legal responsibility and accountability of educational institutions and their staff for any harm or injury caused to students or their families, including civil claims related to privacy of school records, corporal punishment, compulsory education, and prayer in public school.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8A3.label: Motion to File Late Opposition
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8A3.definition: A Motion to File Late Opposition is a request to the court to allow a party to submit their opposition to a motion after the deadline has passed.
english_labels: Motion to File Motion and Opposition Together

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8A4.label: Mississippi State Courts
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8A4.definition: Mississippi State Courts: The judicial system of the state of Mississippi, consisting of various courts and administrative bodies responsible for interpreting and enforcing the laws of the state.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8A4.label: Remittitur
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8A4.definition: Remittitur refers to a court's power to reduce the amount of damages awarded by a jury if the judge finds the award excessive. This practice is used to prevent the need for a new trial by offering the plaintiff the option to accept a lower amount.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8AI.label: Coinage Clause Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8AI.definition: A Coinage Clause claim is a legal argument asserting that a law or action violates the authority granted to Congress by the Coinage Clause of the United States Constitution. This claim is based on the interpretation that the Coinage Clause empowers Congress to regulate and control the minting and issuance of currency, including coins, and prohibits states or other entities from engaging in their own coinage without proper authorization.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8AK.label: Right to a Speedy Trial
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8AK.definition: A Right to a Speedy Trial claim a claim under many constitutions, which guarantee defendants in criminal prosecutions the right to a speedy trial. This right aims to limit the amount of time an accused person has to endure the anxiety and publicity of a pending criminal trial, and to reduce the potential for impairing the defense.
english_labels: Right to Trial without Undue Delay

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8AL.label: Nondisparagement Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8AL.definition: A Nondisparagement Agreement is a legal contract in which parties agree not to make negative or critical comments about each other, often used in settlement agreements or employment contracts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8AR.label: Breach of Third-Party Beneficiary Contract
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8AR.definition: The Breach of Third-Party Beneficiary Contract refers to a situation where a party fails to fulfill their obligations under a contract, which was made for the benefit of a third party who is not a direct party to the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8AS.label: Incapacity Event
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8AS.definition: An Incapacity Event refers to a situation where an individual becomes unable to make or communicate specific decisions, typically due to illness, injury, or cognitive decline. In such cases, legal instruments like durable powers of attorney or advance directives can guide decision-making on behalf of the incapacitated individual.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8AU.label: Legal Determination
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8AU.definition: "Litigation determination" refers to the final outcome or verdict reached in a legal dispute or trial. It can include findings such as "guilty" in a criminal case or "liable" in a civil case when a party is held responsible, or "acquitted" when a defendant is found not guilty in a criminal trial. A single matter's legal determination can be split between claims (e.g., liable for one claim; not liable for another claim).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ah.label: Criminal Conspiracy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ah.definition: A criminal agreement between two or more people to commit a crime, even if the crime is never carried out, falls under the concept of Criminal Conspiracy in the field of Inchoate Criminal Offenses and Concert of Action Crimes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ah.label: Cash and Cash Equivalents
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ah.definition: Cash is legal tender – currency or coins – that can be used to exchange goods, debt, or services. This practice involves monitoring competitors' products, services, marketing strategies, financial performance, and other relevant factors, and helps organizations identify opportunities, threats, and best practices to enhance their market position and drive growth.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8BH.definition: Sex and Gender Discrimination refers to the unfair treatment of individuals based on their sex or gender, particularly in the workplace, which can include differences in pay, promotion opportunities, and job responsibilities.

These rights often stem from international treaties like the 1951 Refugee Convention and may include the right to seek asylum, non-refoulement, and access to basic services such as healthcare and education.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8C3.label: Parole Proceeding
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8C3.definition: A Parole Proceeding is a legal process that determines whether a prisoner who has served part of their sentence may be released from prison and supervised in the community for the remainder of their sentence.

Participants must be employed by, trained by, or participate in a cultural exchange program administered by the sponsoring organization

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8CP.label: Material Adverse Effect Definition - "Attributable to" Language
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8CP.definition: A Material Adverse Effect (MAE) Definition with "Attributable to" Language refers to a clause in a contract that outlines the specific circumstances under which a party can terminate the agreement due to a significant negative change in the financial condition or business operations of the other party, which can be directly attributed to a specific event or circumstance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8CQ.label: Proprietary Agreement Clause

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8CR.label: Corporate Law Department
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8CR.definition: A Corporate Law Department is a division within a business entity (e.g., corporation, LLC, partnership) responsible for handling legal matters and ensuring compliance with laws and regulations. It advises the entity on legal issues, drafts and reviews legal documents, and represents the corporation in legal proceedings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8CY.label: Taxing Authority
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8CY.definition: A Taxing Authority is a governmental entity responsible for collecting taxes, enforcing tax laws, and ensuring compliance with tax regulations. https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8DV.definition: A Motion to Disqualify Arbitrator is a legal request to remove an arbitrator from a case due to a conflict of interest or bias, made by one of the parties involved in the arbitration process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8DX.label: Confession
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8DX.definition: A confession is a formal statement made by an individual acknowledging their guilt for a specific crime or offense. It can be given voluntarily or as a result of interrogation, and its validity can be a subject of legal scrutiny, especially if there are concerns about the circumstances under which it was obtained, such as the possibility of coercion or violation of rights.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Db.label: Tourette Syndrome
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Db.definition: Tourette Syndrome (TS) is a neurological disorder characterized by repetitive, involuntary movements and vocalizations called tics. These tics can range from mild to severe and may involve motor tics, such as blinking or head jerking, and vocal tics, such as grunting or shouting, often impacting daily activities and social interactions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Dm.label: Atheism
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Dm.definition: Atheism is the belief or doctrine that asserts the non-existence of deities or a supreme being. In legal contexts, it may pertain to the protection of non-religious individuals' rights, ensuring freedom from religious impositions, or the recognition of atheism as a legitimate philosophical stance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Dn.label: Motion for Appointment of Ombudsman
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Dn.definition: A Motion for Appointment of Ombudsman is a request made in a bankruptcy case for the appointment of an independent third party to investigate and resolve disputes between the debtor and creditors.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Dq.label: tax_tier_number
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Dq.definition: "A unique identifier associated with the number of tiers applicable to the tiered_tax. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Du.label: Discounts and Credits
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Du.definition: Discounts and Credits refer to reductions in fees or expenses provided to clients as a result of various factors such as matter type, volume of work, or other negotiated terms, and can be applied to specific fees or expenses within an Engagement for providing legal services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Dx.label: Non-Profit Organization
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Dx.definition: A non-profit organization (NPO) is dedicated to furthering a particular social cause or advocating for a shared point of view. In economic terms, it is an organization that uses its surplus of the revenues to further achieve its ultimate objective, rather than distributing its income to the organization's shareholders, leaders, or members. Non-profits are tax-exempt or charitable, meaning they do not pay income tax on the money that they receive for their organization.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Dz.label: Motion in Limine to Exclude Report
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Dz.definition: A Motion in Limine to Exclude Report is a legal request to prevent a specific report from being presented as evidence in a trial or hearing.
english_labels: Motion in Limine to Exclude Report

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E0.label: Defense Criminal Investigative Service
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E0.definition: The Defense Criminal Investigative Service is the criminal investigative arm of the Office of the Inspector General, U.S. Department of Defense.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E1.label: Kidricevo
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E1.definition: Kidricevo is a town located in Slovenia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E1.label: Management Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E1.definition: A Management Agreement is a contract in which one entity entrusts another with the management of its operations or properties. It outlines the responsibilities, performance expectations, compensation, and other terms for the managing entity.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E1.label: Wales
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E1.definition: Wales is a country located in the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E1.label: Norrbottens lan
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E1.definition: Norrbottens lan is a county in the northernmost part of Sweden.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E3.label: City of Freeport
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E3.definition: A city located in the Bahamas, specifically known as the City of Freeport.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E3.label: International Trade Administration
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E3.definition: The International Trade Administration (ITA) is an agency in the United States Department of Commerce that promotes United States exports of nonagricultural U.S. services and goods.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E4.label: Kayes
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E4.definition: Kayes is a city located in Mali.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E4.label: U.S. Special Tribunals of Pennsylvania
english_labels: United States Special Tribunals of Pennsylvania

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E4.label: Niassa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E4.definition: Niassa is a region in Mozambique.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E4.label: North Darfur
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E4.definition: North Darfur is a region located in the northern part of Sudan.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E5.label: Guelmim-Es Semara
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E5.definition: Guelmim-Es Semara is a region in Morocco.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E5.label: United States Trustee Program
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E5.definition: The United States Trustee Program is a component of the United States Department of Justice that is responsible for overseeing the administration of bankruptcy cases and private trustees.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E6.label: Cost or Fee Awarded - Percentage Reduced
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E6.definition: A "Cost or Fee Awarded - Percentage Reduced" is a type of cost or fee shifting where the amount awarded to the prevailing party is reduced by a certain percentage.
english_labels: Cost or Fee Awarded - Percentage Reduced

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E6.label: Novgorodskaya oblast'
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E6.definition: Novgorodskaya oblast' is a region within the Russian Federation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E6.label: Markman Hearing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E6.definition: A Markman Hearing is a type of hearing in a patent infringement case where a judge interprets the claims of a patent to determine its scope and meaning.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E7.label: Bukwa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E7.definition: Bukwa is a location in Uganda.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E7.label: Product Inherently Unsafe
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E7.definition: A product that is inherently dangerous or hazardous, and therefore cannot be made safe even with reasonable care, which may be used as a defense in a product liability lawsuit.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E8.label: Bilecik
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8E8.definition: Bilecik is a city in Turkey.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8EA.label: U.S. Capitol Police
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8EA.definition: The United States Capitol Police (USCP) is a federal law enforcement agency charged with protecting the United States Congress within the District of Columbia and throughout the United States and its territories.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8EC.label: U.S. Bankruptcy Court - D. New Hampshire
english_labels: U.S. Bankruptcy Court - D. New Hampshire
United States Bankruptcy Court, D. New Hampshire

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8EC.label: Maracha
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8EC.definition: Maracha is a location in Uganda.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ED.label: Georgia Superior Court - Toombs County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ED.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Toombs County, Georgia, with authority over civil and criminal cases.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8EL.label: Employment Transactions Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8EL.definition: Employment Transactions Practice refers to the area of law that involves the structuring, negotiation, and documentation of agreements related to employment relationships. This includes contracts, compensation plans, and other legal frameworks governing the employee-employer dynamic.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8EM.label: Prevailing Party Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8EM.definition: A Prevailing Party Clause is a provision in a contract that specifies which party will be considered the prevailing party in the event of a dispute or litigation, and may entitle that party to recover attorney's fees and costs.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8EP.label: Catalogue
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8EP.definition: A Catalogue is a type of directory that systematically lists, describes, and often categorizes items or services, typically for the purpose of identification, reference, or purchase. Unlike a simple directory, a catalogue often includes additional information about the listed items, such as specifications, prices, or images.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8EQ.label: Dinka
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8EQ.definition: A language spoken by the Dinka people of South Sudan.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ES.label: Romanian; Moldavian; Moldovan
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ES.definition: A language spoken in Romania and Moldova, which is a member of the Romance language family.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8EV.label: Addendum
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8EV.definition: An addendum to a document filed in a legal proceeding.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ej.label: Anticipation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ej.definition: Anticipation is an emotion characterized by the expectation or foresight of a future event, often accompanied by excitement or anxiety.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ek.label: Brain Death
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ek.definition: Brain death is a medical and legal condition characterized by the irreversible cessation of all brain functions, including those of the brain stem. It can be legally recognized as the end of life, and it has significant implications for organ donation, end-of-life care, and the determination of the time of death.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ek.label: Right of First Offer to Purchase Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ek.definition: A Right of First Offer to Purchase Clause is a contractual provision that grants a party the right to purchase a property or asset before it is offered to others, typically in the context of a real estate or business transaction.
english_labels: Right of First Offer to Purchase Clause

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Eo.label: System Identifiers
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Eo.definition: Unique identifiers (e.g., IRIs, UUIDs, GUIDs) within the systems of stakeholders (e.g., vendors, sellers, buyers, courts).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ep.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Armstrong County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ep.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Armstrong County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering civil and criminal proceedings at the county level in Pennsylvania.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Armstrong County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Eq.label: Fraudulent Misrepresentation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Eq.definition: Fraudulent Misrepresentation is a type of misrepresentation where one party intentionally makes a false statement to another party, with the intention of inducing them to enter into a contract or take some other action, and the other party relies on that false statement to their detriment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Er.label: Regulatory Disclosure Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Er.definition: Regulatory Disclosure Practice involves the legal requirements and procedures for disclosing information to regulatory authorities. This practice area includes compliance with disclosure laws, reporting obligations, transparency standards, and the management of regulatory filings and communications.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ex.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Lawrence County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ex.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Lawrence County: A court of law in Missouri that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Lawrence County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8F0.label: Liege
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8F0.definition: A person who owes loyalty to a sovereign or government, specifically in the context of the city of Liege in Belgium.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8F2.label: Overijssel
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8F2.definition: Overijssel is a province in the eastern part of the Netherlands.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8F4.label: Plea Agreement Evidence Objection
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8F4.definition: A Plea Agreement Evidence Objection is raised when a party in a legal proceeding believes that evidence of a plea agreement or negotiation is being used inappropriately, such as to prove guilt or liability. This objection aims to protect the plea negotiations and agreements, ensuring that they are not used prejudicially.
english_labels: Objection to Evidence of Plea Discussions

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8F6.label: Employee Expert
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8F6.definition: An expert who is also the employee of an actor participating in litigation (e.g., a party).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8F7.label: Chickpeas
english_labels: Chickpeas, also known as garbanzo beans, are seeds from the Cicer arietinum species, belonging to the legume family (Fabaceae). They are widely consumed for their nutty flavor and high nutritional content, including protein, fiber, vitamins, and minerals, and are a staple ingredient in many cuisines worldwide.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8FA.label: Thanh Hoa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8FA.definition: Thanh Hoa is a province in Vietnam.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8FB.label: Eastern Province
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8FB.definition: Eastern Province is a region in Sri Lanka.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8FE.label: Adangme
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8FE.definition: Adangme is a structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary, and is a specific language within the context of legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8FE.label: Persuasive Precedent
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8FE.definition: Persuasive Precedent refers to a legal decision or ruling from another jurisdiction or a lower court that, while not binding, may influence a court’s decision in a current case due to its relevance, reasoning, or persuasive value. This type of precedent serves as a guiding tool rather than a compulsory authority.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8FK.label: Consumer Contract Containing Unlawful Provision
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8FK.definition: A Consumer Contract Containing Unlawful Provision is a type of claim related to contracts between consumers and businesses, where the contract includes a provision that is illegal or against public policy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8FL.label: Environmental Rights
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8FL.definition: Environmental rights refer to the entitlements related to the protection of the natural environment and the right to live in a healthy and sustainable environment. These rights may include access to clean water and air, protection against environmental degradation, and the ability to participate in decisions affecting the environment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8FP.label: Independent Consideration Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8FP.definition: An independent consideration clause is a clause in a contract that states that each party's consideration is separate and independent from the other party's consideration, and that the failure of one party to perform their obligations does not release the other party from their obligations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8FU.label: Ekajuk
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8FU.definition: Ekajuk is a structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary, and is a specific language within the context of legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8FZ.label: Filipino; Pilipino
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8FZ.definition: A language spoken in the Philippines and used in legal documents, proceedings, and other legal aspects.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Fa.label: Judicial Clerk
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Fa.definition: A Judicial Clerk is a legal professional, typically a recent law school graduate, who assists a judge with research, writing opinions, and other tasks essential to judicial proceedings. Judicial clerks play a critical role in the judicial process by providing detailed analysis and support for the judge's decision-making.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ff.label: Compensation Bonus
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ff.definition: A bonus is a supplemental payment given to employees in addition to their regular salary or wages, typically as a reward for exceptional performance, meeting certain targets, or achieving specific goals. Bonuses are intended to incentivize and recognize outstanding contributions to an organization.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Fj.label: Court Reporter Request
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Fj.definition: A court reporter request is a type of correspondence or form filed in appellate court proceedings to request the services of a court reporter to create a written record of the proceedings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Fl.label: Legislative Amendment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Fl.definition: A Legislative Amendment is a formal change or addition to existing legislation, enacted by a legislative body. It serves to update, clarify, or otherwise modify the existing legal framework, often in response to new developments or identified shortcomings in the law.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Fs.label: Big Pine Paiute Tribe of the Owens Valley
english_labels: Big Pine Paiute Tribe of the Owens Valley

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Fu.label: Appellate Page Proof Brief
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Fu.definition: A written legal argument submitted to an appellate court, which presents evidence and analysis in support of a party's position on a specific issue or set of issues.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Fw.label: Whole Loan
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Fw.definition: a Whole Loan (also known as a Nonsyndicated Loan) refers to a loan or financial arrangement that is provided by a single lender or investor, rather than a group of lenders or investors. This type of arrangement typically involves direct negotiations and agreements between the borrower and the lender.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8G0.label: Commercial Motor Vehicle Indicator
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8G0.definition: Y/N code identifying whether the incident occurred while the driver was operating a commercial vehicle.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8G5.label: Right to Seize Asset
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8G5.definition: The Right to Seize Asset refers to the legal authority given to a creditor to take possession of a debtor's property or asset used as collateral for a secured debt or obligation. This action usually occurs when the debtor defaults on the loan or violates the terms of the contractual agreement, and it is carried out according to procedures outlined in the governing law or contract

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8G7.label: Citation Check Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8G7.definition: Citation Check Management refers to the process of verifying the accuracy and validity of legal citations within a case or document, and ensuring that all necessary citations have been included.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8G8.label: Coir
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8G8.definition: Coir is a natural fiber extracted from the husk of coconuts, commonly used for making ropes, mats, brushes, and other products. It is known for its durability, water resistance, and eco-friendly properties, making it a sustainable material choice.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8GB.label: Work for Hire
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8GB.definition: Work for Hire in copyright law refers to a work created by an employee within the scope of their employment, or a work specially commissioned under certain conditions, where the employer or commissioner is considered the legal author. This principle assigns copyright ownership to the hiring or commissioning party, rather than the actual creator.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8GE.label: Georgia District Court - Evans County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8GE.definition: Georgia District Court - Evans County: A court of law in the state of Georgia that has jurisdiction over legal disputes and criminal cases within Evans County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8GK.label: Chuvash
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8GK.definition: Chuvash (Language) is a structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary specific to the Chuvash people and culture.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8GR.label: Lottery
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8GR.definition: A Lottery is a form of gambling where participants purchase tickets for a chance to win a prize, typically determined by a random draw. This type of gambling is often regulated by government authorities and can support public projects or charitable causes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8GW.label: Attempted Battery
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8GW.definition: Attempted Battery is a criminal offense that involves the intent to cause bodily harm to another person, but falls short of actual physical contact.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8GX.label: Employment-Based Immigration Request
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8GX.definition: An Employment-Based Immigration Request is a type of immigration application in which an individual seeks entry or residency in a destination country based on a job offer or employment opportunity. The sponsoring employer usually files petitions and necessary documents on behalf of the employee, and the process often involves labor certifications and other prerequisites to prove the employment need.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Gb.label: Senior Credit Ranking
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Gb.definition: Senior Credit Ranking refers to the priority status of senior debts, which are ranked above senior subordinated, junior, and junior subordinated debts in the event of liquidation. This ranking ensures that senior creditors are paid first from the proceeds of the liquidated assets, providing them with a higher level of security and reducing their risk exposure.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Gc.label: Opinion Memo Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Gc.definition: A memorandum of law is a written explanation, based on research and analysis, of the drafter's opinion regarding a legal problem.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Gd.label: Originating Country
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Gd.definition: Originating Country, in the context of immigration and customs, refers to the country from which an individual or goods have moved or are seeking to move from. In the immigration context, this move is often with the intention of settling in another country either temporarily or permanently. This term is important for customs and immigration processes and policies, as it can influence visa requirements, eligibility for asylum, and other legal considerations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Gn.label: Podcast
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Gn.definition: A Podcast is a digital audio recording series, often structured as episodes, that can cover various topics such as interviews, storytelling, discussions, or educational content.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Gq.label: Texas Court of Appeals - 7th
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Gq.definition: The Texas Court of Appeals - 7th is a specific intermediate appellate court in Texas that hears appeals from lower courts within its jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Gt.label: Contingent Financial Obligations
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Gt.definition: Contingent Financial Obligations, or Contingent Liabilities, are potential debts that may or may not become actual liabilities, depending on the outcome of a future event. These are not recorded on the balance sheet but may be disclosed in the financial statements' notes if the contingency is considered significant, such as pending lawsuits or financial guarantees.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Gu.label: Immigrant
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Gu.definition: An immigrant is an individual who moves to a country other than their country of origin with the intention of residing there permanently or for an extended period. The reasons for immigration can vary and may include seeking employment opportunities, better living conditions, or reunification with family.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Gv.label: tax_matter_disc_cred segment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Gv.definition: "The specific taxes relevant to the parent MATTER_DISC_CRED items. There will be 0 or more TAX_MATTER_DISC_CRED segments for each MATTER_DISC_CRED segment. Note that the EXTEND_HEADER option was purposely omitted from this segment. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Gy.label: Fraud Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Gy.definition: Fraud Claims refer to civil or tort claims that involve intentional misrepresentation or deceitful conduct by one party towards another, including fraudulent misrepresentation, legal fraud, fraudulent transfers, and other forms of fraudulent behavior.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Gy.label: Shoplifting Theft
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Gy.definition: The theft, by someone other than an employee of the victim, of goods or merchandise exposed for sale.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Gz.label: Nuisance
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Gz.definition: A nuisance is a legal claim that arises from the use of one's property or conduct that interferes with another's use or enjoyment of their property, resulting in harm or annoyance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8H0.label: New Jersey Superior Court - Gloucester County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8H0.definition: The New Jersey Superior Court - Gloucester County is a specific court within the New Jersey Superior Court Appellate Division that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases in Gloucester County, New Jersey.
english_labels: New Jersey Superior Court - Gloucester County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8H6.label: "Back-Door" Material Adverse Effect Closing Condition
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8H6.definition: A "Back-Door" Material Adverse Effect (MAE) Closing Condition is a provision in a legal agreement that allows a party to back out of the agreement if an adverse event occurs that was not specifically listed as a condition for termination.
english_labels: Back-Door" Material Adverse Effect Closing Condition

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8H8.label: DEPRECATED NODES
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8H8.definition: DEPRECATED NODES: A group of concepts within the ZZZ - SANDBOX: UNDER CONSTRUCTION parent class that have been replaced or are no longer in use.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8H9.label: Book
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8H9.definition: A Book is a substantial written or printed work typically covering a specific subject or narrative. Books can be in many formats, both paper and electronic.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8H9.label: Brillhart-Wilton Abstention
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8H9.definition: A legal doctrine known as Brillhart-Wilton Abstention, which falls under the category of abstention doctrines, allows a federal court to abstain from hearing a case that involves complex state law issues that are better suited for resolution in state court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8HA.label: Stipulation to Avoid Lien
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8HA.definition: A Stipulation to Avoid Lien is a legal agreement between parties that prevents a lien from being placed on a property or asset.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8HB.label: TIMEKEEPER_ID
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8HB.definition: A TIMEKEEPER_ID is a unique identifier assigned to a timekeeper in the LEDES98BI V5 Format Rev 1-2020 standard for electronic billing in legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8HK.label: Due Diligence Contingency Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8HK.definition: A due diligence contingency clause is a provision in a contract that allows a party to conduct an investigation or review of the subject matter before the contract becomes binding.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8HL.label: Knowledge Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8HL.definition: Knowledge Management: The process of creating, sharing, using and managing the knowledge and information of an organization, with a focus on improving efficiency and effectiveness.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8HQ.label: Trade Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8HQ.definition: Law, rules, and customs governing trade between countries including imports and exports.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8HS.label: Divorced
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8HS.definition: The concept of "Divorced (Marital Status)" refers to the legal status of a person who has ended their marriage through a legal process, and is no longer considered married under the law.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8HT.label: Joint Tenancy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8HT.definition: Joint Tenancy is a form of concurrent ownership where two or more individuals hold equal shares in a property with the right of survivorship. This means that upon the death of one joint tenant, their share automatically passes to the surviving joint tenants.
english_labels: Joint Ownership with Right of Survivorship

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8HU.label: Pennsylvania Special Tribunal
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8HU.definition: A Pennsylvania Special Tribunal is a court-like entity within the Pennsylvania State Courts that is established to handle specific legal matters or disputes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Hc.label: Search Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Hc.definition: Search Management refers to the process of organizing and retrieving information in a knowledge management system. It involves the use of tools and techniques to efficiently search and locate relevant information within a knowledge repository.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Hd.label: Motions on Briefing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Hd.definition: Motions on Briefing refer to various types of requests made by parties in appellate courts to file briefs that do not conform to the standard requirements or to supplement, correct, or substitute previously filed briefs.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8He.label: Repapering Management Services
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8He.definition: Repapering Management Services refers to the provision of alternative legal services that specifically involve managing the process of updating legal documents and contracts to comply with new regulations or requirements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Hi.label: Standard Warranty Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Hi.definition: A standard warranty clause is a specific type of warranty clause that outlines the terms and conditions of a warranty agreement in a standardized manner.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Hj.label: Juror
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Hj.definition: A person called for jury duty, including jury selection, and who may ultimately sit on a jury.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Hl.label: Virginia State Bar Disciplinary Board
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Hl.definition: The Virginia State Bar Disciplinary Board is a legal entity within the Virginia State Courts that oversees and enforces ethical standards for lawyers practicing in Virginia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Hq.label: Mistaken Payment on Draft Returned
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Hq.definition: A mistaken payment on draft returned is a legal concept within the realm of banking, commercial paper, and creditor claims, referring to a situation where a payment made on a draft is returned due to an error or mistake.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Hr.label: LINE_ITEM_NUMBER_OF_UNITS
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Hr.definition: The concept of "LINE_ITEM_NUMBER_OF_UNITS" refers to the quantity of a particular item or service that is being billed for, as defined within the LEDES98BI V5 Format Rev 1-2020 standard.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Hr.label: Inaja Band of Diegueno Mission Indians of the Inaja and Cosmit Reservation
english_labels: Inaja Band of Diegueno Mission Indians of the Inaja and Cosmit Reservation

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Hr.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Henderson County (9th Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Henderson County (9th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Hs.label: Duty of Care
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Hs.definition: Duty of care is a legal obligation requiring individuals and organizations to adhere to a standard of reasonable care while performing acts that could foreseeably harm others. This duty ensures that actions or omissions do not result in injury or damage to other parties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Hu.label: Pee Dee Indian Tribe of South Carolina
english_labels: Pee Dee Indian Tribe of South Carolina

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8I8.label: PrescriptiveStatement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8I8.definition: A Prescriptive Statement is a type of logical formula within the OASIS ontology that provides specific instructions or requirements for a particular situation or action.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8IA.label: Santa Ynez Band of Chumash Mission Indians
english_labels: Santa Ynez Band of Chumash Mission Indians

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ID.label: Expert Report Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ID.definition: Expert Report Practice refers to the specialized area of expertise within the broader field of Expert Practice, which involves the preparation and submission of expert reports in legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8IH.label: Revocable Trust
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8IH.definition: A Living Trust, also known as a revocable trust, is a legal entity created during the grantor's lifetime to hold and manage assets. It can be altered, amended, or revoked by the grantor at any time before their death, allowing flexibility in asset management and distribution.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8IH.label: Copyright Claims Board
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8IH.definition: A Copyright Claims Board (CCB) is a specialized administrative body within the United States Copyright Office that is responsible for resolving disputes related to copyright claims.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8IO.label: Ethical AI
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8IO.definition: Ethical AI refers to AI systems that demonstrate respect for and adherence to ethical principles and values. These systems are designed to operate in a manner consistent with moral standards, ensuring fairness, transparency, accountability, and respect for human rights and societal norms.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8IP.label: Project Management Objectives
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8IP.definition: A project's goals, both milestone goals and final goals.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8IQ.label: Data Breach Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8IQ.definition: A Data Breach Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the responsibilities and liabilities of parties in the event of a breach of data security.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8IU.label: Services Warranty Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8IU.definition: A Services Warranty Clause is a provision in a contract that guarantees the quality and performance of services provided by one party to another.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8IU.label: Payment from Government-Regulated Defined Contribution Account
english_labels: Payment from Government-Regulated Defined Contribution Account

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ic.label: Precis
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ic.definition: A precis is a concise summary of a longer document or text, typically used in legal proceedings, and is a type of trial court practice document.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ih.label: Scheduling Motion
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ih.definition: A scheduling motion in bankruptcy refers to a request made by a debtor or trustee to set a hearing or deadline for a specific matter related to the bankruptcy case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ij.label: Hypothetical Question Objection
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ij.definition: A Hypothetical Question Objection is raised when an attorney asks a witness to speculate about a situation that is not based on facts in evidence or the witness's personal knowledge. This objection is used to prevent the witness from providing an opinion based on a hypothetical scenario that may not be relevant or accurate.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8It.label: Criminal Incarceration
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8It.definition: The concept of Criminal Incarceration refers to the punishment of a person who has been convicted of a crime by being confined to a prison or jail for a specified period of time, as a penalty for their wrongdoing.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Iu.label: Citation to Regulation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Iu.definition: A document's citations to a regulation (e.g., Code of Federal Regulations).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ix.label: Tunica Biloxi Indian Tribe of Louisiana
english_labels: Tunica Biloxi Indian Tribe of Louisiana

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8J1.label: Retaliatory Discharge
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8J1.definition: The concept of Retaliatory Discharge refers to the act of an employer firing an employee in response to the employee engaging in a protected activity, such as reporting discrimination or harassment, in violation of employment laws.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8J2.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Franklin County (2nd Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Franklin County (2nd Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8J5.label: Dutch, Middle
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8J5.definition: Middle Dutch is a historical language spoken in the Netherlands and Belgium between the years 1050 and 1350.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8J6.label: Reasonable Indications
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8J6.definition: Reasonable Indications refer to the level of evidence required to shift the burden of proof in a legal matter, specifically in litigation, where the party with the burden of proof must provide evidence to support their claim.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8J9.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Bollinger County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8J9.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Bollinger County: A specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Bollinger County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8JA.label: Commercial Property Foreclosure
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8JA.definition: Commercial Property Foreclosure is the legal procedure through which a lender seizes a commercial property, such as an office building or retail space, due to the borrower's failure to meet financial obligations specified in the mortgage contract. The property is then sold, usually through a public auction, to recoup the unpaid loan amount and any additional costs incurred during the foreclosure process

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8JM.label: Multiple Sclerosis
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8JM.definition: Multiple Sclerosis (MS) is a chronic autoimmune disease that affects the central nervous system (CNS), leading to the destruction of the protective myelin sheath covering nerve fibers. This demyelination disrupts nerve signals, resulting in symptoms such as muscle weakness, coordination problems, visual disturbances, and cognitive impairments.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8JQ.label: Employment Written Warning
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8JQ.definition: An Employment Written Warning is a formal document issued by an employer to an employee, outlining specific instances of misconduct or performance issues. It serves as an official notice that continued violations may result in further disciplinary action, including termination.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8JV.label: Patent Assessment Process
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8JV.definition: The patent assessment process is a systematic investigation conducted to ascertain the novelty and non-obviousness of an invention by examining existing patents and other relevant technical literature. This process is crucial for determining the likelihood of obtaining a patent and avoiding infringement of existing patents.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8JW.label: Champerty and Maintenance
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8JW.definition: The concept of Champerty and Maintenance refers to the illegal practice of a third party funding a lawsuit in exchange for a share of the proceeds, which can lead to an abuse of the legal system.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Jf.label: Damages Expert
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Jf.definition: An expert who opines on prospective or actual damages.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Jf.label: Underpayment of Public Benefit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Jf.definition: Underpayment of public benefit refers to the situation in which an individual or family receives less financial assistance or services than they are entitled to under a specific public benefit program. This can occur due to administrative errors, incomplete information, or misapplication of eligibility criteria, and may require corrective action to adjust the benefit amount and deliver the owed resources to the recipient.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Jg.label: Fon
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Jg.definition: African language spoken primarily in Benin, Togo, and Nigeria.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Jh.label: Oil and Gas Real Estate Asset
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Jh.definition: An oil and gas real estate asset refers to a property that contains or is believed to contain deposits of oil or natural gas. This asset is important in the context of property law, energy law, and environmental law, as it involves the rights to explore, extract, and sell these natural resources.
english_labels: Oil and Gas Real Estate Asset

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Jk.label: Unilateral Mistake in Contract
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Jk.definition: A unilateral mistake in contract is a legal concept that occurs when only one party to a contract is mistaken about a material fact, which can lead to the contract being voidable or unenforceable.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Jt.label: Arkansas District Court - Crittenden Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Jt.definition: The Arkansas District Court - Crittenden Cty. is a specific court within the Arkansas District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Crittenden County, Arkansas.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ju.label: DUPE Joint Administration Motion
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ju.definition: A DUPE Joint Administration Motion (Bankruptcy) is a legal request made in a bankruptcy case for the consolidation of multiple related cases into a single proceeding.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Jz.label: Rhode Island Supreme Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Jz.definition: The Rhode Island Supreme Court is the highest court in the state of Rhode Island and is responsible for hearing appeals from lower state courts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8K0.label: payable_by _cl_id
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8K0.definition: "The tax id number for the INVOICE.payable_by_cl_name. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8K5.label: Motion to Determine Mortgage Fees and Expenses
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8K5.definition: A Motion to Determine Mortgage Fees and Expenses is a legal request made in a bankruptcy case to determine the amount of fees and expenses associated with a mortgage.
english_labels: Motion to Determine Mortgage Fees and Expenses

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8K6.label: Summary Judgment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8K6.definition: A Summary Judgment is a legal decision made by a judge based on the evidence and facts presented in a case, without the need for a trial.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8K7.label: Market Risk
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8K7.definition: Risk of losses due to movements in market variables like interest rates, foreign exchange rates, equity and commodity prices.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KA.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Parke County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KA.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Parke County, Indiana, with the power to hear and decide a wide range of legal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KF.label: Motion for Declaratory Judgment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KF.definition: A Motion for Declaratory Judgment is a legal request made to a court to issue a formal declaration on the rights, duties, or obligations of parties involved in a legal dispute, without ordering any specific action or awarding damages.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KG.label: Repudiatory Breach of Contract
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KG.definition: A Repudiatory Breach of Contract Claim is a legal action asserting that one party has committed a breach so fundamental that it effectively nullifies the contract, allowing the innocent party to terminate the agreement. This type of claim alleges that the breach goes to the root of the contract, depriving the innocent party of substantially the whole benefit they were intended to derive from it.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KI.label: DEPRECATED - Material Adverse Effect Definition - Applies to Both Target and Subsidiaries
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KI.definition: SUPERCEDED BY ACQUIROR AND ACQUIREE TAGS. A Material Adverse Effect (MAE) is a significant negative change or event that impacts both the target and its subsidiaries, as defined in a legal agreement.
english_labels: DEPRECATED - Material Adverse Effect Definition - Applies to Both Target and Subsidiaries
Material Adverse Effect Definition - Applies to Both Target and Subsidiaries

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KM.label: Livestock
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KM.definition: Livestock refers to domesticated animals raised in an agricultural setting that are considered tangible assets for economic purposes. These animals hold monetary value and can be used as collateral in financial transactions or counted as part of an individual's or entity's assets.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KO.label: Internal Medicine Negligence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KO.definition: Negligence in the practice of internal medicine, which involves a breach of duty of care by a medical professional resulting in harm or injury to a patient.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KO.label: Georgia Superior Court - White County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KO.definition: Georgia Superior Court - White County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within White County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KP.label: Indiana Town Court - Marion County, Pike Twp.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KP.definition: A court located in Marion County, Pike Township, Indiana that has limited jurisdiction over minor criminal offenses, traffic violations, and small claims cases.
english_labels: Indiana Town Court - Marion County, Pike Twp.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KQ.label: Flat Covenant
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KQ.definition: A Flat Covenant (No Efforts Standard) is a type of covenant that does not require any specific effort or action to be taken by the party bound by the covenant.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KQ.label: Firm Equity Partner
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KQ.definition: A Firm Equity Partner is a partner in a law firm who holds an ownership interest in the firm, typically through the purchase of shares, and is entitled to a share of the firm's profits.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KR.label: Expenses
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KR.definition: Expenses refer to the various costs incurred during a legal matter, including but not limited to word processing, deposition transcripts, litigation support vendors, meals, copying, experts, trial exhibits, delivery services/messengers, witness fees, local counsel, postage, other professionals, online research, arbitrators/mediators, travel, trial transcripts, other, subpoena fees, outside printing, private investigators, facsimile, and court fees.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KR.label: Comparative Fault of Plaintiff
