https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KR.definition: The concept of "Comparative Fault of Plaintiff" refers to the legal principle that allows a plaintiff's recovery to be reduced in proportion to their own degree of fault or negligence in causing their own injuries, as compared to the fault of the defendant.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KT.label: Motion to File Opposition
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KT.definition: A Motion to File Opposition is a formal request made to a court or administrative agency seeking permission to submit a written response opposing a previous motion or request filed by another party in a legal proceeding.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KV.label: Novation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KV.definition: The concept of Novation refers to the substitution of a new contract or obligation for an existing one, with the mutual agreement of all parties involved, resulting in the discharge of the original obligation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KW.label: Repurchase Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8KW.definition: Often referred to as a "repo," a Repurchase Agreement is a short-term borrowing mechanism where one party sells a security with an agreement to repurchase it at a later date at a specified price. It's effectively a secured loan.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Kc.label: Motion to Stay Proceedings Pending Covered Business Method Review
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Kc.definition: A Motion to Stay Proceedings Pending Covered Business Method (CBM) Review is a request to pause legal proceedings while a review of a specific type of business method patent is conducted.
english_labels: Motion to Stay Proceedings Pending CBM Review
Motion to Stay Proceedings Pending Covered Business Method Review

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ke.label: Future Injury from Present Tortious Personal Injury
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ke.definition: Future Injury from Present Tortious Personal Injury: A claim for damages resulting from a personal injury that has not yet manifested, but is likely to occur in the future as a direct result of the initial injury.
english_labels: Future Injury from Present Tortious Personal Injury

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Kf.label: Carveout for Pandemic Response Language
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Kf.definition: A carveout for pandemic response language is a provision in a legal agreement that exempts certain obligations or requirements during a pandemic or other public health emergency.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Kh.label: HIV / AIDS
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Kh.definition: HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus) is a virus that attacks the body's immune system, specifically the CD4 cells (T cells), leading to a weakened immune response. If not treated, HIV can progress to AIDS (Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome), the final stage of HIV infection, where the immune system is severely damaged, and the body becomes vulnerable to opportunistic infections and cancers.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Kj.label: Military Draft
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Kj.definition: "Military Draft," also known as "Conscription," refers to the compulsory enlistment of individuals, typically within a specific age range, into the national armed forces. Governments enact conscription during times of war or when they anticipate potential military threats, requiring eligible citizens to serve for a specified period.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Kl.label: Minnesota District Court - Olmsted County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Kl.definition: A court located in Olmsted County, Minnesota that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ko.label: Disorderly Conduct
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ko.definition: Any behavior that tends to disturb the public or decorum, scandalize the community, or shock the public sense of morality.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ks.label: Claims Agent
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ks.definition: A claims agent is a person who acts on behalf of an individual or organization to manage and process insurance claims.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ky.label: Nondisclosure Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ky.definition: A Nondisclosure Agreement (NDA) is a legal contract between two or more parties that outlines confidential material, knowledge, or information that the parties wish to share with one another for certain purposes, but wish to restrict access to or by third parties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Kz.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Rock Island County (14th Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Rock Island County (14th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Kz.label: Carrots
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Kz.definition: Carrots are root vegetables belonging to the Daucus carota species, typically characterized by their elongated, tapering shape and orange color, although other colors exist. They are cultivated for their edible taproot, which is rich in beta-carotene and other nutrients, and are widely used in culinary applications and as animal feed.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8L0.label: Administrative Mandate
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8L0.definition: An Administrative Mandate is a court order that compels a government agency or official to perform a specific duty or act that is required by law.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8L8.label: California Superior Court - Santa Barbara Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8L8.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Santa Barbara County, California, with the power to hear and decide a wide range of legal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.
english_labels: California Superior Court - Santa Barbara Cty.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8LG.label: Indiana City Court - Vigo County, Terre Haute City
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8LG.definition: A court located in Vigo County, Terre Haute City, Indiana that has jurisdiction over cases within its geographical boundaries.
english_labels: Indiana City Court - Vigo County, Terre Haute City

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8LN.label: Notice to Individual Consumer Debtor
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8LN.definition: A Notice to Individual Consumer Debtor is a written communication directed to a specific consumer debtor, informing them of their legal rights and obligations in relation to a debt.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8LS.label: Ohio Court of Appeals - Montgomery County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8LS.definition: Ohio Court of Appeals - Montgomery County: A court of appeals located in Montgomery County, Ohio that hears appeals from lower courts within its jurisdiction.
english_labels: Ohio Court of Appeals - Montgomery County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8LT.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Lawrence County (2nd Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Lawrence County (2nd Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Lb.label: Agender
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Lb.definition: Agender refers to a gender identity where an individual identifies as having no gender, or a gender that is neutral or undefined. This term falls within the broader spectrum of gender identities and is often acknowledged in legal discussions surrounding gender discrimination, rights, and protections

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Lc.label: Relocation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Lc.definition: The concept of Relocation refers to the legal process of moving a child from one geographical location to another, typically in the context of a matrimonial emergency application.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Lf.label: L500 Appeal
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Lf.definition: An L500 Appeal is a type of litigation activity within the UTBMS framework that involves presenting arguments and evidence to a higher court in order to challenge a lower court's decision.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Lj.label: Peas
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Lj.definition: Peas are small, spherical seeds from the Pisum sativum species, belonging to the legume family (Fabaceae). Known for their sweet flavor and high nutritional content, peas are consumed fresh, dried, or processed and are valued for their protein, fiber, vitamins, and minerals, including vitamins A, C, and K, as well as iron and potassium.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ll.label: LINE_ITEM_ACTIVITY_CODE
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ll.definition: A LINE_ITEM_ACTIVITY_CODE is a code used in the LEDES98BI V5 Format Rev 1-2020 standard to identify a specific activity or task associated with a line item in a legal invoice.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ll.label: Motion to Amend Findings
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ll.definition: A Motion to Amend Findings is a legal request made after a trial asking the court to modify or correct its previous factual findings in the case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Lp.label: Pro Bono
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Lp.definition: A Pro Bono (Engagement Fee Model) is a type of Engagement Fee Model where legal services are provided for free or at a reduced cost to clients who cannot afford to pay for them.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Lt.label: Georgia Superior Court - Schley County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Lt.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Schley County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Lt.label: Consulting Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Lt.definition: A Consulting Agreement is a legally binding contract between two parties that outlines the terms and conditions of a consulting arrangement, including the scope of work, compensation, and confidentiality provisions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Lt.label: Arbitration Forum
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Lt.definition: An Arbitration Forum is a specific type of Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) Forum where disputes are resolved outside of the court system by a neutral third party or panel of experts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Lt.label: Incident Reconstruction Expert
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Lt.definition: An expert who inspects an accident scene, examining evidence and applying the laws of physics to determine the accident's cause. Cruso v. Greater Lakeside Corp., 425 So.2d 953 (La. App. 1983)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Lx.label: Congenital Disorders that Affect Multiple Body Systems
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Lx.definition: Congenital disorders that affect multiple body systems are conditions present from birth that impact several organ systems. These disorders often lead to a range of physical and developmental abnormalities affecting the functioning of multiple systems in the body.
english_labels: Congenital Disorders that Affect Multiple Body Systems

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8M0.label: Condition of Use Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8M0.definition: A Condition of Use Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the terms and conditions under which a product or service may be used.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8M0.label: Estate Planning Objectives
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8M0.definition: Estate Planning Objectives refer to the goals and purposes that individuals aim to achieve when organizing their assets, properties, and financial affairs for the future distribution upon their death. These objectives ensure the proper management and transfer of wealth, fulfillment of personal wishes, and minimization of taxes and legal complications.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8M1.label: Duress Permitting Contract Rescission
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8M1.definition: Duress Permitting Contract Rescission refers to a legal concept where a contract can be cancelled or rescinded due to the presence of duress, which is a situation where one party is forced to enter into a contract against their will.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8M2.label: Bengali
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8M2.definition: Bengali (Language) is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary, used in legal matters as the language of a document, artifact, evidence, testimony, proceeding, or any other legal aspect, specifically referring to the Bengali language.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8M3.label: Mezzanine Loan
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8M3.definition: A Mezzanine Loan is a hybrid form of financing that combines debt and equity features, typically used in acquisitions or expansions. It is subordinated to senior debt but ranks higher than equity, often allowing lenders to convert debt into equity if the loan is not repaid on time.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8M4.label: Duty of Loyalty
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8M4.definition: Duty of loyalty is a legal obligation that requires fiduciaries to act in the best interests of their beneficiaries or principals, avoiding conflicts of interest and self-dealing. This duty ensures that fiduciaries prioritize the interests of those they serve above their own personal gain.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8M6.label: Plastic Surgery Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8M6.definition: Plastic Surgery Malpractice refers to a type of medical malpractice claim that arises from a plastic surgery procedure that was performed negligently or incompetently, resulting in harm to the patient.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8M6.label: taxing_jurisdiction_locality
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8M6.definition: "The locality of the taxing jurisdiction. Use accepted abbreviations for state or province mandated by the country's postal service. For Canadian PST, taxing_jurisdiction_locality for Ontario would be ""ON""; for Local tax in New York City, taxing_jurisdiction_locality would be ""New York, NY""; for state tax in Georgia (USA), taxing_jurisdiction_locality would be ""GA""; for VAT tax in France, taxing_jurisdiction_locality would be null. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8MA.label: Mortgage Right
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8MA.definition: Mortgage Right refers to the secured interest a lender holds in a property as collateral for a loan extended to a borrower. This legal right grants the lender the authority to seize and sell the property through foreclosure if the borrower defaults on the loan, subject to specific procedures and regulations set forth by law

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8MA.label: Computer Systems Design and Related Services Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8MA.definition: This sector comprises establishments primarily engaged in activities in which human capital is the major input. These establishments make available the knowledge and skills of their employees, often on an assignment basis. The individual industries of this sector are defined on the basis of the particular expertise and training of the service provider.
english_labels: Computer Systems Design and Related Services Industry

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8MH.label: Opportunity to Cure Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8MH.definition: An Opportunity to Cure Clause is a provision in a contract that allows a party to remedy a breach or default before the other party can terminate the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8MP.label: Asset Valuation Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8MP.definition: Asset Valuation Practice refers to the specialized area of Asset Analysis that involves determining the monetary value of a particular asset or group of assets.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8MQ.label: CCRS Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8MQ.definition: A CCRS Clause is a specific type of contractual clause that pertains to the Canadian Common Reporting Standard (CCRS) and outlines the obligations and responsibilities of the parties involved in the exchange of financial information.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8MR.label: Foreign Exchange Risk
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8MR.definition: The risk that changes in exchange rates will negatively affect the value of an investment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8MR.label: Deposition Recording
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8MR.definition: A Deposition Recording is a type of transcript or recording that captures the testimony of a witness or party under oath, typically used in legal proceedings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8MR.label: Contract Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8MR.definition: Contract Management refers to the process of overseeing and administering contracts from creation to execution, including tasks such as review, negotiation, e-signatures, smart contracts, intake, notarization, and automation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8MT.label: Pitches and Proposals Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8MT.definition: The management of pitches and proposals within a legal business context.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Mi.label: New York District Court - Nassau County - 4th District
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Mi.definition: New York District Court - Nassau County (4th Dist.) is a specific court within the New York District Court system, located in Nassau County and serving as a venue for legal proceedings in the Fourth Judicial District.
english_labels: New York District Court - Nassau County - 4th District

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Mk.label: "'Breach' of fiduciary duties" Language
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Mk.definition: The "Breach" of fiduciary duties refers to a violation or failure to fulfill the legal obligation of loyalty and care owed by a fiduciary to their beneficiary, often resulting in harm or loss to the beneficiary.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ml.label: Misclassification of Exempt Status Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ml.definition: A misclassification of exempt status claim is a legal assertion that an employer has incorrectly classified an employee as exempt from overtime pay and other protections under labor laws, when they should be classified as non-exempt. Such claims often seek compensation for unpaid overtime and other benefits wrongly denied due to the misclassification.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ml.label: Trauma- and Stressor-Related Disorders
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ml.definition: Trauma- and Stressor-Related Disorders are characterized by experiencing or witnessing a traumatic or stressful event, or learning of a traumatic event occurring to a close family member or close friend, and the psychological aftermath of clinically significant effects on functioning. Symptoms and signs may include, but are not limited to, distressing memories, dreams, and flashbacks related to the trauma or stressor; avoidant behavior; diminished interest or participation in significant activities; persistent negative emotional states (for example, fear, anger) or persistent inability to experience positive emotions (for example, satisfaction, affection); anxiety; irritability; aggression; exaggerated startle response; difficulty concentrating; and sleep disturbance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Mr.label: Installment Payment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Mr.definition: An installment payment is a financial arrangement where a debtor repays a debt in equal, periodic payments over a specified period, often including interest or fees. These regular payments make it easier for individuals or businesses to manage their financial obligations while gradually reducing the outstanding debt.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Mx.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Hardin County (2nd Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Hardin County (2nd Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8N4.label: Immigration Status
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8N4.definition: Immigration Status refers to the legal condition that defines an individual's right to reside, work, or study in a country other than their country of origin. This status can vary widely, including categories such as citizen, permanent resident, temporary worker, or undocumented immigrant, and dictates the individual's rights, obligations, and limitations within the host country.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8N5.label: Tax Tier Total Tax
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8N5.definition: The Tax Tier Total Tax is a subcategory of Tax Tier Detail and refers to the total amount of taxes owed.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8N7.label: Kinyarwanda
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8N7.definition: Kinyarwanda is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary, used in legal matters, that is specifically spoken in Rwanda and neighboring countries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8NC.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Williamson County (1st Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Williamson County (1st Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ND.label: Tax ID - Client
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ND.definition: A Tax ID - Client is a specific type of Tax Detail that refers to the unique identification number assigned to a client for tax purposes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8NL.label: Indenture
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8NL.definition: An Indenture is a formal legal document that sets forth the terms and conditions governing a relationship, usually involving debt securities such as bonds. It specifies the obligations of the issuer, the rights of the bondholders, and the responsibilities of the trustee, who acts as an intermediary between the two parties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8NO.label: Officer's Certificate
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8NO.definition: An Officer's Certificate is a formal document executed by a company officer attesting to the accuracy of certain facts or figures, often in relation to the company's financials or compliance status. It is commonly used to validate representations made in contracts or agreements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8NP.label: Explicit Agreement
english_labels: An Explicit Agreement is a contract or agreement where the terms and conditions are clearly stated and agreed upon by all parties involved, leaving no room for ambiguity. This type of agreement can be either oral or written, provided the terms are clearly articulated and mutually understood.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8NS.label: Forest Resources Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8NS.definition: Laws governing activities in designated forest lands, most commonly with respect to forest management and timber harvesting.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8NS.label: Business Intelligence Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8NS.definition: Business Intelligence Management refers to the systematic process of collecting, analyzing, and managing data to support strategic decision-making for a particular business. It involves the use of tools and techniques to transform raw data into meaningful insights that can inform business strategies and operations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8NU.label: Mandatory Arbitration Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8NU.definition: A mandatory arbitration clause is a provision in a contract that requires any disputes arising from the contract to be resolved through arbitration rather than through the court system.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8NX.label: Goodwill
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8NX.definition: Goodwill is an intangible asset that represents the value of a business beyond its tangible assets and liabilities. It arises when one company acquires another for a price higher than the fair market value of its net identifiable assets. It also represents elements like excellence of management, customer loyalty, brand recognition, favorable location, or quality of employees and overall business going concern value that are not separately identifiable but contribute to generating future economic benefits.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8NX.label: Monetary Inflow
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8NX.definition: External Actor pays Legal Services Buyer. Money flowing into the Legal Services Buyer. E.g., Litigation proceeds from plaintiff-side litigation. E.g., Legal Services Buyer hires Legal Services Provider to negotiate with a contractual counterparty, resulting in increased funds flowing to Legal Services Buyer. In Accounts Payable systems (e.g., Oracle), this is labeled "Profit Center."

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Na.label: Apparent Authority
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Na.definition: The concept of Apparent Authority refers to the legal principle that holds a principal liable for the actions of an agent who appears to have the authority to act on their behalf, even if the agent does not actually have such authority.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Nb.label: Disbursement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Nb.definition: The concept of Disbursement (Distribution) refers to the act of distributing funds or assets to the intended recipients, often as part of a larger event or phase.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Nc.label: Tsimshian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Nc.definition: A language spoken by the Tsimshian people, primarily in British Columbia and Alaska.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ne.label: Patent Infringement - Utility Patents
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ne.definition: The unauthorized use, manufacture, sale, or importation of a product or process that is protected by a utility patent.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Nf.label: Work Product Ownership Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Nf.definition: A Work Product Ownership Clause is a provision in a contract that specifies the ownership rights of the work product created under the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ng.label: Common Law Lien
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ng.definition: A Common Law Lien is a type of lien that arises from the common law rather than from a statute, and allows a creditor to retain possession of a debtor's property until the debt is paid.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Nh.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Clarion County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Nh.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court in Clarion County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court system that handles minor criminal offenses, traffic violations, and civil cases involving amounts up to $12,000.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Clarion County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Nk.label: Freedom of Association
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Nk.definition: A freedom of association claim is a legal action initiated by an individual or group alleging that their right to freedom of association, as protected by the First Amendment of the United States Constitution, has been violated by the government or a government actor. The First Amendment guarantees the right to associate with others for the expression of ideas, beliefs, and collective action, including the right to form and join groups and organizations. A freedom of association claim may arise in various contexts, such as when a government body enacts a law or regulation that unduly restricts the right to associate or form organizations, when a government actor interferes with the right to join or participate in a group or organization, or when an individual or group is discriminated against or punished based on their association with a particular group or organization.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Nl.label: Georgia Superior Court - Worth County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Nl.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Worth County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Worth County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Nv.label: False Arrest and Imprisonment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Nv.definition: The concept of False Arrest and Imprisonment refers to the unlawful detention or confinement of an individual without legal justification or consent, resulting in a violation of their personal liberty and freedom of movement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Nv.label: Lost Profits Damages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Nv.definition: Lost Profits Damages refer to the financial harm suffered by a party as a result of a breach of contract or other wrongful act, where the damages are calculated based on the profits that the party would have earned if the breach or wrongful act had not occurred.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Nw.label: Transfer of Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Nw.definition: The Transfer of Claim is a legal document that allows a creditor to transfer their right to receive payment from a debtor to another party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8O1.label: Subtenant
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8O1.definition: A person or entity who subleases property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8O1.label: Spinach
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8O1.definition: Spinach is a leafy green vegetable from the Spinacia oleracea species, known for its tender leaves and mild, slightly earthy flavor. It is consumed raw or cooked and is valued for its high nutritional content, including vitamins A, C, and K, iron, calcium, and antioxidants.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8O1.label: Army
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8O1.definition: An Army is the land-based military branch of a nation's armed forces, primarily responsible for ground warfare and territorial defense. This organization consists of trained soldiers, support personnel, and various types of land-based military equipment, structured to conduct large-scale ground operations and maintain national security.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8O3.label: Copyright Concept Objectives
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8O3.definition: Copyright Concept Objectives refer to the criteria that a work must meet to be eligible for copyright protection. These objectives can include originality, expression in a tangible medium, and creativity, ensuring the work is a unique creation of the author.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8O7.label: tax_point_date
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8O7.definition: "The tax point is generally the invoice date. In instances where the tax point date is different from the invoice date, the tax point date indicates the financial period in which the tax applies. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8OG.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Tioga County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8OG.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court in Tioga County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court system that has jurisdiction over minor criminal offenses and civil cases.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Tioga County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8OH.label: Motion to Reopen Chapter 15 Case
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8OH.definition: A Motion to Reopen Chapter 15 Case is a request made to the court to reopen a previously closed Chapter 15 bankruptcy case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8OK.label: 140 Negotiable Instrument (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8OK.definition: Action relating to an agreement to pay a specific amount of money, including promissory notes, loan agreements and checks.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8OM.label: Non-Billable
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8OM.definition: The term "Non-Billable" refers to time spent or tasks performed by a legal service provider that cannot be charged to the client. These activities are typically considered necessary for practice operations but do not directly contribute to client work.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ON.label: Failure to Mitigate Damages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ON.definition: The failure of a plaintiff to take reasonable steps to minimize their losses or damages after an injury or breach of contract has occurred, which may limit the amount of damages they can recover in a lawsuit.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ON.label: Matter Narrative Format
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ON.definition: The file format containing the narrative description of a matter.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ON.label: Mechanical Patent
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ON.definition: A mechanical patent is a legal protection granted to inventors of new and useful machines, mechanical devices, or improvements thereof.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8OS.label: New York City Court - Glen Cove
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8OS.definition: A court located in Glen Cove, New York, which is a subdivision of the New York City Court system.
english_labels: New York City Court - Glen Cove

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8OX.label: Settlement Motions
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8OX.definition: Settlement Motions are motions filed in trial courts related to the settlement of a legal dispute, including motions to stay proceedings pending settlement, approve settlement, enforce settlement, postpone settlement conference, adjourn settlement conference, settle, and enforce agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8OY.label: Contract Reformation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8OY.definition: The concept of Contract Reformation refers to the legal remedy of modifying or changing the terms of a contract in order to correct a mistake or address an unfair situation, and is a type of equitable relief.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8OY.label: Kansas District Court - Crawford County, Girard
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8OY.definition: The Kansas District Court - Crawford County, Girard is a specific court within the Kansas District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Crawford County and is located in the city of Girard.
english_labels: Kansas District Court - Crawford County, Girard

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Oa.label: Marine Corps
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Oa.definition: A Marine Corps is an amphibious warfare branch of a nation's armed forces, specializing in projecting military power from the sea onto hostile or potentially hostile shores. This force is trained to operate in maritime, littoral, and land environments, often serving as a rapid response force for expeditionary operations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Oc.label: Tax on Tax ID
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Oc.definition: A tax imposed on a unique identification number assigned to an individual or entity for tax purposes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Oe.label: Local Governmental Leader
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Oe.definition: A Local Governmental Leader is an elected or appointed official who holds a position of authority in a municipal or regional government body. This individual is responsible for making decisions, implementing policies, and representing the interests of their constituents within a specific geographic area smaller than a state or province.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Oh.label: Motion for Mistrial
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Oh.definition: A Motion for Mistrial is a request made by a party during a trial asking the judge to declare the trial invalid and start over due to a significant error or misconduct that has occurred during the proceedings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ok.label: Laboratories - Real Estate Asset
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ok.definition: A laboratory is a type of real estate asset, which is a property that is owned or controlled by a person, business, or economic entity and is specifically designed and equipped for scientific research and experimentation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ol.label: Work Allocation Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ol.definition: Work Allocation Management refers to the process of assigning and distributing tasks and responsibilities among legal professionals within a law firm or legal department, as part of the overall management of legal operations and business activities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Om.label: Natural Language Processing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Om.definition: Natural Language Processing (NLP) is the field of artificial intelligence focused on enabling machines to process, analyze, and generate human language in its spoken, written, or signed forms. NLP involves a range of techniques to understand, interpret, and produce human language in a way that is both meaningful and useful.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8On.label: Unauthorized Practice of Medicine
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8On.definition: The Unauthorized Practice of Medicine occurs when an individual or entity engages in medical activities, such as diagnosis, treatment, or offering medical advice, without the necessary medical qualifications, licensure, or authorization in a particular jurisdiction. This practice poses significant risks to public health and safety, as it involves providing medical care without the required expertise and credentials.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Oo.label: Theft Locations
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Oo.definition: Theft Locations refer to specific places or settings where theft occurs, such as buildings, motor vehicles, or coin-operated machines, and are a subcategory of Criminal Theft.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Oq.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Montour County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Oq.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Montour County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering legal proceedings in Montour County, Pennsylvania.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Montour County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Os.label: Res Judicata
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Os.definition: Res Judicata refers to the legal principle that a matter that has been adjudicated by a competent court and a final judgment has been rendered, cannot be litigated again between the same parties or their privies.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ov.label: Personal Information
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ov.definition: Personal Information refers to any data that relates to an identified or identifiable individual. This includes both sensitive personal information, which requires greater protection due to its potential to cause harm if disclosed, and personally identifiable information (PII), which can be used to identify, contact, or locate a specific individual.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ow.label: Norwegian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ow.definition: Norwegian (Language) is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary used in Norway and other Norwegian-speaking regions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8P1.label: Bill and Hold Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8P1.definition: A Bill and Hold Clause is a provision in a contract that allows a seller to bill a buyer for goods that have not yet been delivered, but are being held by the seller for the buyer's future delivery instructions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8P3.label: Corporate Issuer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8P3.definition: A Corporate Issuer refers to a corporation that issues debt or equity securities to raise capital for various purposes, such as expanding operations, financing acquisitions, or refinancing existing debt. These securities can include corporate bonds, stocks, and commercial paper, and are sold to investors in the capital markets.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8P4.label: Nauru
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8P4.definition: Nauru (Language) refers to the structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary used in the Pacific island nation of Nauru.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8P6.label: Asset Appreciation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8P6.definition: Asset Appreciation is the increase in the value of an asset over time. This growth in worth can occur due to various factors such as market demand, scarcity, improvements, or economic conditions, and represents a gain in the asset's potential sale price or intrinsic value.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8P7.label: Application to Extend or Change Nonimmigrant Status
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8P7.definition: The "Application to Extend or Change Nonimmigrant Status" refers to Form I-539 in the United States, which is used by individuals in certain non-immigrant visa categories to request an extension of their stay or a change to a different non-immigrant status. This form is commonly used by individuals who want to prolong their stay or switch to a different visa category while remaining in the U.S.
english_labels: Application to Extend or Change Nonimmigrant Status

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8P8.label: Possession of a Controlled Substance
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8P8.definition: The unlawful cultivation, manufacture, distribution, sale, purchase, use, possession, transportation, or importation of any controlled drug or narcotic substance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8PC.label: Dollar-Based Antitrust Standard
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8PC.definition: A Dollar-Based Antitrust Standard is a legal concept that sets a monetary threshold for determining whether a business practice violates antitrust laws, with the aim of preventing anticompetitive behavior while also allowing for efficient business operations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8PM.label: INVOICE_NET_TOTAL
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8PM.definition: The INVOICE_NET_TOTAL concept refers to the total amount of money owed on an invoice, as defined within the LEDES98BI V5 Format Rev 1-2020 standard.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8PR.label: Response to Show Cause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8PR.definition: A response to show cause is a legal document filed in response to a court order requiring a party to explain why a certain action should not be taken against them.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8PR.label: Wrongful Incarceration
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8PR.definition: The concept of Wrongful Incarceration refers to the unlawful detention of an individual by the government, which results in the deprivation of their liberty and freedom.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8PS.label: New York City Court - Corning
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8PS.definition: A court located in Corning, New York that operates under the jurisdiction of the New York City Court system.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8PT.label: New York Village Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8PT.definition: New York Village Court is a local court in New York State that has jurisdiction over minor criminal and civil matters within its geographical area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8PX.label: regulation_heading
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8PX.definition: "The citation of the statute or regulation associated with the information provided in the next field. E-Billing vendors and clients are requested to provide instruction on how data is to be recorded in this field. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8PY.label: Down Payment Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8PY.definition: A Down Payment Clause is a provision in a contract that requires a specified amount of money to be paid upfront by one party to the other as a condition for entering into the agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Pk.label: Minnesota District Court - Houston County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Pk.definition: Minnesota District Court - Houston County: A specific court within the Minnesota District Court system located in Houston County, responsible for administering legal proceedings within its jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Pl.label: Texas District Court - Dallas County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Pl.definition: A Texas District Court located in Dallas County, which has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Pr.label: Common Share
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Pr.definition: Common Shares, also known as Ordinary Shares, represent a basic unit of equity ownership in a company, granting shareholders voting rights and a share in the company's profits through dividends. These shares typically entitle the holder to one vote per share and are the most prevalent type of stock issued by companies.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Pt.label: Trademark Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Pt.definition: Trademark Management refers to the process of overseeing and protecting a company's registered trademarks, including monitoring for infringement and taking legal action when necessary.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Pv.label: Due Diligence Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Pv.definition: Due Diligence Management refers to the process of conducting a thorough investigation and analysis of a legal transaction to ensure that all relevant information is disclosed and risks are identified and mitigated.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Q3.label: Investment Services Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Q3.definition: An Investment Services Agreement is a contract between an investor and a service provider detailing the scope of investment-related services to be offered. It outlines fees, responsibilities, and terms of the relationship.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Q8.label: Motion to Strike Complaint
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Q8.definition: A Motion to Strike Complaint is a legal document filed by a party in a lawsuit requesting the court to remove or strike certain allegations or claims made by the opposing party in their complaint.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Q9.label: Fees of Court Clerk or Marshal
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Q9.definition: The Fees of Court Clerk or Marshal refer to the charges imposed by the court clerk or marshal for their services rendered in a legal matter, which are included in the overall Court Costs.
english_labels: Fees of Court Clerk or Marshal

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QA.label: Physical Asset Delivery
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QA.definition: Physical Asset Delivery refers to the settlement of a contract, financial instruments, or assets through the receipt or delivery of the actual underlying instruments instead of cash. This method is common in derivative contracts, where fulfilling the settlement obligation involves the transfer of the physical underlying asset.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QA.label: Mediation Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QA.definition: A Mediation Agreement is a contract that parties enter into, agreeing to resolve their disputes through mediation: a process where a neutral third-party mediator assists the parties in reaching a voluntary settlement. The agreement outlines the terms of the mediation process and any resultant decisions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QB.label: Contact Information
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QB.definition: Contact Information refers to the details of an individual or entity that can be used to communicate with them, including their name, address, phone number, email, and other relevant information.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QG.label: Minnesota District Court - Clay County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QG.definition: Minnesota District Court - Clay County: A specific court within the Minnesota District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Clay County, Minnesota.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QI.label: Motion for Temporary Restraining Order
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QI.definition: A Motion for Temporary Restraining Order (TRO) is a legal request for a court order that would prevent a party from taking a certain action until a hearing can be held to determine whether a preliminary injunction should be issued.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QJ.label: UTBMS Litigation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QJ.definition: UTBMS Litigation refers to the standardized codes used to categorize legal activities and expenses related to the litigation process, including discovery, pre-trial pleadings and motions, trial preparation and trial, and appeal.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QK.label: Listed Asset
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QK.definition: Listed Assets refer to debt securities and other financial instruments that are registered and traded on a recognized stock exchange or regulated market. These assets include corporate bonds, government bonds, and other debt instruments, providing liquidity and transparency to investors.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QN.label: Waste Management and Remediation Services Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QN.definition: Industries in this group are engaged in the collection, treatment, and disposal of waste materials. This includes establishments engaged in local hauling of waste materials; operating materials recovery facilities (i.e., those that sort recyclable materials from the trash stream); providing remediation services (i.e., those that provide for the cleanup of contaminated buildings, mine sites, soil, or ground water); and providing septic pumping and other miscellaneous waste management services. There are three industry groups within the subsector that separate these activities into waste collection, waste treatment and disposal, and remediation and other waste management.
english_labels: Waste Management and Remediation Services Industry

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QO.label: E105 Telephone
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QO.definition: A telephone expense incurred in the course of business operations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QQ.label: Motion for Injunction Pending Appeal
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QQ.definition: A Motion for Injunction Pending Appeal is a legal request made to a higher court to temporarily stop a lower court's decision from being enforced until the appeal process is completed.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QR.label: Antitrust - Market Allocation Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QR.definition: Antitrust - Market Allocation Claims: A legal claim alleging that competitors in a market have colluded to divide the market among themselves, thereby reducing competition and harming consumers.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QT.label: Preamble Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QT.definition: A preamble clause is a type of contractual clause that serves as an introductory statement to a legal document, outlining the purpose and context of the agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QU.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Cameron County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QU.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Cameron County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering legal proceedings in Cameron County, Pennsylvania.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Cameron County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QW.label: Motion to Reopen Chapter 7 Case
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QW.definition: A Motion to Reopen Chapter 7 Case is a request made to the court to reopen a previously closed bankruptcy case under Chapter 7 of the Bankruptcy Code.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QX.label: Blin; Bilin
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8QX.definition: A language spoken by the Blin and Bilin people, primarily in Eritrea and Ethiopia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Qa.label: Magahi
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Qa.definition: Magahi is a language that belongs to the Indo-Aryan language family and is primarily spoken in the Bihar state of India.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Qd.label: Intervening Event - Reasonable Foreseeable at Signing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Qd.definition: An "Intervening Event - Reasonable Foreseeable at Signing" refers to a circumstance that occurs after the signing of a legal agreement, which was reasonably foreseeable at the time of signing and may affect the terms of the agreement.
english_labels: Intervening Event - Reasonable Foreseeable at Signing

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Qj.label: Blood Test
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Qj.definition: A Blood Test is a medical procedure where a sample of blood is taken from an individual's body, typically from a vein in the arm, to be analyzed for various purposes. These purposes can range from assessing general health, detecting diseases and infections, to evaluating organ function or checking for specific conditions like anemia or diabetes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ql.label: Public Information
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ql.definition: Public Information refers to information that is openly available to anyone and does not require any form of authorization or clearance for access. This type of information is intended for widespread dissemination and does not necessarily pose a risk of harm to the organization (e.g., company, nonprofit, nation) if disclosed.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Qp.label: Gifts Causa Mortis
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Qp.definition: A gift causa mortis is a transfer of property made by a person who is anticipating their imminent death, and is made with the expectation that the gift will only take effect if the donor dies from the illness or peril that they are facing.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Qt.label: Lack of Competency Objection
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Qt.definition: A Lack of Competency Objection is raised when a party in a legal proceeding believes that a witness does not possess the necessary qualifications, knowledge, or mental capacity to provide reliable testimony. This objection aims to ensure that testimony is provided only by individuals who are deemed competent to testify under the law.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8R1.label: Design Immunity
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8R1.definition: Design Immunity is an affirmative defense to a claim of dangerous condition of public property and should be considered where the design of the subject area is at issue.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8R2.label: Child’s Right to Rescind Contract
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8R2.definition: The Child's Right to Rescind Contract refers to the legal right of a minor to cancel or void a contract they entered into before reaching the age of majority. This concept falls under the broader category of Contract & Quasi-Contract Claims within the legal framework.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8R7.label: Unfair Prejudice Objection
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8R7.definition: An Unfair Prejudice Objection is raised when a party in a legal proceeding believes that evidence being presented is more likely to cause bias or unfair harm to one side than to contribute meaningfully to the resolution of the case. In other words, the evidence's probative value doesn't outweigh its unfairly prejudicial impact. This objection seeks to prevent evidence that might unfairly influence the decision-maker's judgment, ensuring that the trial remains fair and impartial.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8R9.label: Firm Knowledge Manager
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8R9.definition: A Firm Knowledge Manager is a non-timekeeper level provider who manages the knowledge and information within a law firm.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8RA.label: Notice of Settlement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8RA.definition: A Notice of Settlement is a written communication that informs parties involved in a legal dispute that an agreement has been reached and the case will not proceed to trial.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8RE.label: Gasoline Stations and Fuel Dealers Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8RE.definition: Industries in the Gasoline Stations and Fuel Dealers subsector retail automotive fuels (e.g., gasoline, diesel fuel, gasohol, alternative fuels) and automotive oils, without or in combination with convenience store items; or retail heating oil, liquefied petroleum (LP) gas, and other fuels via direct selling (i.e., home delivery). Gasoline stations have specialized equipment for storing and dispensing automotive fuels.
english_labels: Gasoline Stations and Fuel Dealers Industry

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8RG.label: Pre-petition Payroll Motion
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8RG.definition: A Pre-petition Payroll Motion is a request made in a bankruptcy case by the debtor to pay its employees for work done prior to the bankruptcy filing.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8RG.label: Consideration - Intellectual Property Assets
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8RG.definition: Intellectual property (IP) consideration refers to the valuation and transfer of intangible assets, such as patents, trademarks, copyrights, and trade secrets, from the seller to the buyer as part of the deal.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8RH.label: Prospectus
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8RH.definition: A Prospectus is a formal document filed with securities regulators that provides details about an investment offering for sale to the public. It usually includes the terms of the offering, risks, and financial statements among other critical information.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8RH.label: Mohawk
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8RH.definition: A Native American language spoken by the Mohawk people, characterized by its complex grammar and unique phonetics.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8RH.label: Siksika
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8RH.definition: Siksika (Language) refers to the structured system of communication used by the Siksika people, which consists of grammar and vocabulary specific to their culture and traditions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8RJ.label: Food Services and Drinking Places Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8RJ.definition: Industries in this froup prepare meals, snacks, and beverages to customer order for immediate on-premises and off-premises consumption. There is a wide range of establishments in these industries. Some provide food and drink only; while others provide various combinations of seating space, waiter/waitress services and incidental amenities, such as limited entertainment. The group includes special food services, such as food service contractors, caterers, and mobile food services; drinking places; and restaurants and other eating places.
english_labels: Food Services and Drinking Places Industry

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8RL.label: Esophagus Cancer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8RL.definition: Esophagus cancer is a malignant tumor that originates in the esophagus, the muscular tube that connects the throat to the stomach. This cancer can significantly impact swallowing and digestion and often requires a combination of treatments, including surgery, chemotherapy, and radiation therapy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8RL.label: Arkansas Circuit Court - Scott Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8RL.definition: The Arkansas Circuit Court - Scott County is a specific court within the Arkansas Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Scott County, Arkansas.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8RO.label: Invoice Due Date
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8RO.definition: The "Invoice Due Date" is a specific detail within the broader concept of "Fee Invoice Detail" and refers to the date by which payment for legal services must be made.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8RW.label: TR110 Fact Investigation and Development
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8RW.definition: All actions to investigate and understand the facts of a matter that are not included under another trademark task code below. Covers initial meeting to discuss new matter, interview of client personnel and potential witnesses, review of documents to learn the facts of a potential case, work with an investigator, and all related communications and correspondence.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8RZ.label: Directive
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8RZ.definition: A Directive is an official or authoritative instruction or guideline issued by a governing body or regulatory authority, often aiming to manage or direct specific actions within its jurisdiction. It typically outlines procedures, sets standards, or provides guidance for compliance with laws and regulations

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ra.label: Invalidity Analysis Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ra.definition: Invalidity Analysis Practice is a legal service that involves investigating and developing facts related to the invalidity of a legal matter.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Rb.label: Statutory Immunity
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Rb.definition: Statutory Immunity is a legal concept that provides protection from legal action to government officials or entities who are acting within the scope of their duties as defined by a specific statute.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Rf.label: Lease
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Rf.definition: A Lease Agreement is a binding contract between a lessor (the owner) and a lessee (the renter) that stipulates the terms and conditions for renting out an asset, such as real estate property or an automobile. The agreement outlines details like the rental amount, lease duration, responsibilities of each party, and other specific provisions related to the rented asset.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Rg.label: Pancreatic Cancer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Rg.definition: Pancreatic cancer is a type of cancer that originates in the tissues of the pancreas, an organ responsible for aiding digestion and regulating blood sugar. It is often diagnosed at an advanced stage and typically requires treatments such as surgery, chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and targeted therapy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Rj.label: Joint Work
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Rj.definition: Joint Work in copyright law refers to a work produced by the collaboration of two or more authors where their contributions are not separate from each other. This concept is characterized by the intent of the authors to merge their contributions into inseparable or interdependent parts of a unitary whole.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Rn.label: Insurance Deductible Amount
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Rn.definition: An insurance deductible amount, in the context of legal matters, is the portion of a covered loss that the insured party is responsible for paying before the insurance company's coverage begins.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ro.label: Motion for Judgment on Partial Findings
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ro.definition: A Motion for Judgment on Partial Findings is a legal request made by a party in a case asking the court to rule in their favor on specific issues that have already been decided during the trial.
english_labels: Motion for Judgment on Partial Findings

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Rp.label: tax_authority_ref
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Rp.definition: In some countries tax invoices must be routed, approved and in some cases even delivered to the customers by a platform controlled and/or imposed by the tax authority. This platform normally returns an approval code/identifier to the invoice issuer for audit trail purposes. Such code/identifier may need to be communicated to the customer as a reference depending on the jurisdiction. Use this field to specify the approval code/identifier if required in your country.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ru.label: Aymara
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Ru.definition: Aymara is a language that belongs to the Language top-level class and is spoken in the Andes region of South America, particularly in Bolivia, Peru, and Chile.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Rz.label: Voluntary Employment Termination Event
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Rz.definition: Voluntary employment termination event refers to the act of an employee willingly leaving their job, either through resignation or retirement. This is distinct from involuntary termination, where the employer initiates the separation due to reasons like downsizing, performance issues, or misconduct.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8S1.label: Incorporation of Recitals Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8S1.definition: The Incorporation of Recitals Clause is a specific clause within a contract that references and includes the introductory statements or background information (recitals) of the agreement into the body of the contract itself.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8S6.label: Deal Protection and Related Provisions
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8S6.definition: Deal Protection and Related Provisions refer to a set of contractual clauses and agreements that are designed to safeguard a merger or acquisition deal from external threats and ensure its successful completion, including provisions such as no-shop covenants, breakup fee triggers, and fiduciary termination rights.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8S6.label: Breach of Express Warranty
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8S6.definition: The Breach of Express Warranty is a legal concept that occurs when a seller fails to fulfill a specific promise or guarantee made to a buyer regarding the quality or performance of a product, resulting in harm or damages to the buyer.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8S7.label: IP Rights Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8S7.definition: IP Rights Management refers to the process of managing and protecting the legal rights associated with intellectual property assets, such as patents, trademarks, and copyrights.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8S9.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Franklin County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8S9.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Franklin County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering legal proceedings in the state of Pennsylvania.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Franklin County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8S9.label: Indiana Town Court - Marion County, Decatur Twp.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8S9.definition: A court located in Marion County, Decatur Township, Indiana that has limited jurisdiction over certain types of cases within its geographical area.
english_labels: Indiana Town Court - Marion County, Decatur Twp.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8SB.label: Salary Deferral Agreement Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8SB.definition: A Salary Deferral Agreement Clause is a provision in a contract that allows an employee to defer a portion of their salary to a later date, typically for retirement savings purposes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8SC.label: Increase of Public Benefit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8SC.definition: Increase of public benefit refers to the action of raising the amount or level of financial assistance or services granted to an individual or family under a specific public benefit program. This can occur due to changes in a recipient's circumstances, such as increased financial hardship, or modifications to eligibility criteria, and usually involves an administrative process for reevaluation and approval.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8SK.label: Lac Vieux Desert Band of Lake Superior Chippewa Indians
english_labels: Lac Vieux Desert Band of Lake Superior Chippewa Indians

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8SL.label: Legal Operations Consulting Services
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8SL.definition: Legal Operations Consulting Services refers to professional advice and guidance provided by experts in the field of legal operations management, including strategic planning, process improvement, and technology implementation, to help law firms and legal departments optimize their operations and achieve their business objectives.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8SL.label: European Parliament
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8SL.definition: The European Parliament is one of the legislative bodies of the European Union, composed of members elected by citizens of the member states. It shares the power to legislate, supervise, and budget with the Council of the European Union, representing the interests of EU citizens.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8SQ.label: Outstanding Professor or Researcher Immigrant Petition
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8SQ.definition: An Outstanding Professor or Researcher Immigrant Petition (in the U.S., I-140 EB-1) allows universities or private employers to sponsor foreign nationals who are internationally recognized as outstanding in their academic field. Applicants must demonstrate at least three years of experience in teaching or research and show evidence of significant achievements. Applicants must demonstrate international recognition for your outstanding achievements in a particular academic field, have at least three years of experience in teaching or research in that academic area, and be entering the United States to pursue tenure or a tenure-track teaching position or a comparable research position at a university, institution of higher education, or private employer.
english_labels: Outstanding Professor or Researcher Immigrant Petition

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8SU.label: L430 Written Motions and Submissions
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8SU.definition: A written request or argument submitted to a court or other legal authority during the trial preparation and trial phases of a legal case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8SW.label: DUPLICATIVE: Attempt
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8SW.definition: An attempt to duplicate something that is no longer in use.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8SX.label: Employee Stock Ownership Plans Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8SX.definition: Employee Stock Ownership Plans Law refers to the legal framework governing the establishment, management, and regulation of Employee Stock Ownership Plans (ESOPs), which allow employees to acquire ownership interests in their employer. This body of law includes statutes, regulations, and case law that ensure ESOPs are operated in the best interest of the employees and comply with tax and labor laws.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Sc.label: Likelihood of Adverse Result
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Sc.definition: Likelihood of an adverse result (e.g., client liability, client convicted) — sometimes expressed as a percentage, and sometimes expressed as a classification (e.g., Very High, High, Medium, Low)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Sm.label: 440 Other Civil Rights (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Sm.definition: Action alleging a civil rights violation other than the specific civil rights categories listed below or a violation related to prison. Example: Action alleging excessive force by police incident to an arrest. (Excludes claims against corrections officials)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Sv.label: Statutory Claim of Venue
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Sv.definition: A Statutory Claim of Venue is a legal argument made by a party in a case that asserts a specific location where the case should be heard, based on a specific statute or law.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Sz.label: Careless Contractual Work
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Sz.definition: Careless Contractual Work refers to a breach of contract claim that arises when a party fails to exercise reasonable care in the performance of their contractual obligations, resulting in harm or damages to the other party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8T3.label: UTBMS MK00 Deal Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8T3.definition: UTBMS MK00 Deal Management refers to the specific code used in the Uniform Task-Based Management System to categorize legal tasks related to managing deals, such as mergers and acquisitions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8T3.label: New York County Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8T3.definition: New York County Court is a court of general jurisdiction located in New York County, New York, which hears both civil and criminal cases.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8T5.label: Indemnification of Employee Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8T5.definition: A provision in a contract that requires one party to compensate and protect an employee of the other party from any legal claims or losses arising from their work or actions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8T6.label: Immigration Extension
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8T6.definition: "Immigration Extension" is the process of applying to prolong the duration of an individual's current immigration status, such as a visa or permit, allowing them to stay in the destination country beyond the original expiration date, typically requiring documentation and approval from immigration authorities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8TD.label: Washington Superior Court - Kittitas County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8TD.definition: Washington Superior Court - Kittitas County: A specific court within the Washington Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Kittitas County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8TE.label: Trust Formation Document
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8TE.definition: A Trust Formation Document is a legal instrument used to establish a trust, specifying the terms under which assets are held by a trustee for the benefit of beneficiaries. This document outlines the purpose of the trust, the parties involved, and the legal framework governing the trust's operations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8TG.label: New Jersey District Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8TG.definition: The New Jersey District Court is a court within the New Jersey State Courts system that has jurisdiction over certain types of cases within a specific geographic area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8TH.label: Inflammatory Bowel Disease
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8TH.definition: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) refers to a group of chronic conditions characterized by inflammation of the gastrointestinal (GI) tract. The primary forms of IBD are Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, both of which can cause symptoms such as abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss, and may require ongoing medical management and, in severe cases, surgical intervention.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8TM.label: Chicken Ranch Rancheria of Me-Wuk Indians
english_labels: Chicken Ranch Rancheria of Me-Wuk Indians

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8TW.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Knox County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8TW.definition: The Indiana Circuit Court - Knox County is a specific court within the Indiana Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Knox County, Indiana.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8TY.label: Georgia Superior Court - McIntosh County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8TY.definition: Georgia Superior Court - McIntosh County refers to a specific court within the Georgia Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within McIntosh County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Tc.label: Right of Sepulcher
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Tc.definition: The Right of Sepulcher is a legal claim that grants a person the right to control the burial and funeral arrangements of a deceased loved one.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Td.label: Not Guilty
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Td.definition: "Not guilty" is a legal determination made by a court in a criminal case when the defendant has been acquitted or found not responsible for the charges brought against them. It indicates that the prosecution failed to prove the defendant's guilt, and as a result, the defendant is not subject to criminal penalties or convictions for the alleged crime.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Td.label: Stipulated Judgment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Td.definition: A stipulated judgment is a legal decision agreed upon by both parties involved in a case, which is then approved by a judge.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Tg.label: New Jersey Superior Court - Cumberland County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Tg.definition: The New Jersey Superior Court - Cumberland County is a trial court within the New Jersey court system that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases in Cumberland County.
english_labels: New Jersey Superior Court - Cumberland County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Tk.label: Psychographic Market Segment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Tk.definition: Psychographic market segment refers to divisions of the market that are categorized based on what consumers think about and value, as well as how they live their lives, including consumers' specific interests, preferences, and passions. This category includes consumers who share a common interest or enthusiasm for particular products, services, activities, or priorities. These segments include areas like health-conscious, tech segment, sustainability segment, and others.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Tl.label: Project Requirement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Tl.definition: The customer's requirements necessary to ensure a successful outcome.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Tm.label: Pension and Benefits Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8Tm.definition: Pension and benefits claims are legal actions initiated by an employee against their employer for not complying with applicable laws or the terms of an employment agreement regarding retirement and other benefits. These claims can involve issues such as the mismanagement or mishandling of employee pension or retirement accounts, denial or reduction of employee benefits, or failure to provide required benefits such as health insurance or disability coverage.
