https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8e6.definition: A Resource Lease is an agreement granting rights to extract natural resources (like minerals, timber, or oil) from a property in exchange for payments, typically royalties based on the amount extracted.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8e7.label: Proprietary Information and Confidentiality Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8e7.definition: A Proprietary Information and Confidentiality Clause is a legal provision that restricts the disclosure of confidential information and trade secrets belonging to a company or individual, and is typically included in contracts or agreements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8eL.label: Experts Expense
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8eL.definition: The cost incurred by a party in a legal matter for the services of a professional with specialized knowledge or skills, such as a consultant or witness.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8eM.label: Petition for Visa for Temporary Non-Agricultural Workers
english_labels: Petition for Visa for Temporary Non-Agricultural Workers

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8eQ.label: Dying Declaration
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8eQ.definition: A Dying Declaration is a hearsay exception that allows the admission of statements made by a declarant while believing that their death was imminent, concerning the cause or circumstances of what the declarant believed to be their impending death. This exception is based on the rationale that a person facing imminent death is unlikely to lie, giving their statement a guarantee of trustworthiness.
english_labels: Statement Under Belief of Impending Death

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8eT.label: Role in Document
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8eT.definition: A "Role in Document" is a specific position or responsibility held by an individual, such as a Filer, Editor, or Author, in relation to a legal document or matter.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8eU.label: Motion to Stay Proceedings Pending Settlement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8eU.definition: A Motion to Stay Proceedings Pending Settlement is a legal request to temporarily halt a case until the parties involved can reach a settlement agreement.
english_labels: Motion to Stay Proceedings Pending Settlement

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8eY.label: Joinder
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8eY.definition: The concept of Joinder refers to the legal process of combining two or more legal cases or parties into a single action, typically to promote efficiency and avoid inconsistent outcomes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ed.label: Echinoderms
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ed.definition: Echinoderms are a phylum of marine invertebrates known as Echinodermata, characterized by their radial symmetry, a water vascular system, and a calcareous endoskeleton. This group includes starfish, sea urchins, sand dollars, and sea cucumbers, and they play vital roles in marine ecosystems.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ef.label: CLIENT_STATEorREGION
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ef.definition: A geographical location or state where a client is located, as defined in the LEDES98BI V5 Format Rev 1-2020 standard for legal electronic data exchange.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ei.label: Homeless
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ei.definition: A homeless individual is someone who lacks a fixed, regular, and adequate place to live. Homelessness can result from various factors, including economic hardship, housing affordability issues, mental health challenges, substance abuse, or other circumstances that leave individuals or families without stable housing. Efforts by governments and organizations aim to address homelessness by providing shelter, support services, and housing options to help homeless individuals and families secure stable living arrangements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8es.label: Motion for Reaffirmation Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8es.definition: A Motion for Reaffirmation Agreement is a legal request made in a bankruptcy case to reaffirm a debt that would otherwise be discharged, allowing the debtor to continue making payments on the debt.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8et.label: Earnout Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8et.definition: An earnout clause is a provision in a contract that allows for additional payments to be made based on the performance of the subject of the contract, typically a business or asset.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ev.label: Compensation for Damages Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ev.definition: A Compensation for Damages Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the terms and conditions for payment to be made in the event of a breach or violation of the agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ex.label: Indiana Superior Court - Wells County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ex.definition: Indiana Superior Court - Wells County refers to a specific court within the Indiana Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Wells County, Indiana.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ey.label: Sweeping Clause Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ey.definition: A Sweeping Clause claim is a legal argument asserting that a law or action exceeds the authority granted by a broad clause in a constitution or statute, contending that it goes beyond what is expressly stated or implied. The claim challenges the constitutionality or validity of the law or action based on the interpretation that it exceeds the scope of the sweeping clause.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ez.label: Transactional Deliverables
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ez.definition: Transactional Deliverables: The specific items or outputs that are expected to be produced or provided as part of a transactional engagement scope.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8f0.label: Employment Discrimination Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8f0.definition: Law relating to protected class employment discrimination including retaliation and harassment

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8f0.label: M.A. (Master of Arts)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8f0.definition: An M.A. (Master of Arts) is an advanced academic degree typically requiring one to two years of study beyond a bachelor's degree, often focused on humanities or social sciences. It signifies expertise and specialization in a particular field

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8f4.label: Industry and Market
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8f4.definition: Industry and markets refer to the collective sectors and segments within an economy that produce, distribute, and sell goods and services. This encompasses various industries such as agriculture, technology, and finance, as well as different market segments like luxury goods, budget services, and regional businesses

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8f5.label: UTBMS MF20 Data Security / Privacy / Data Protection / Cyber Security
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8f5.definition: UTBMS MF20 Data Security / Privacy / Data Protection / Cyber Security refers to the classification of legal services related to the protection of data and information in the context of mergers and acquisitions.
english_labels: UTBMS MF20 Data Security / Privacy / Data Protection / Cyber Security

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8f7.label: Compensatory Damages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8f7.definition: Compensatory Damages are a type of monetary damages awarded to a plaintiff in a legal case to compensate for the actual losses or harm suffered as a result of the defendant's actions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8f8.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Lancaster County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8f8.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court in Lancaster County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court system that handles minor criminal offenses, traffic violations, and civil cases involving amounts up to $12,000.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Lancaster County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8f9.label: Subsidiaries Representation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8f9.definition: A subsidiary representation is a statement made by a party in a legal matter regarding the ownership, control, or financial status of a subsidiary company, which is supported by legal or other professional frameworks and is subject to certain warranties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fF.label: Sentence Type
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fF.definition: A Sentence Type refers to the specific form of punishment or rehabilitation imposed by a court upon a convicted offender. This category encompasses various approaches to criminal sentencing, each designed to address the nature of the offense, the circumstances of the offender, and the goals of the justice system.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fI.label: Surveyor
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fI.definition: A person who is licensed to practice land surveying. See Cal. Bus. and Prof. § 8701.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fO.label: Haitian; Haitian Creole
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fO.definition: A language spoken in Haiti and its creole variant.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fR.label: Tenant Equitable Relief for Renewal Options
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fR.definition: Tenant Equitable Relief for Renewal Options: A legal claim made by a tenant seeking a court order to enforce a renewal option in a lease agreement, based on principles of fairness and justice.
english_labels: Tenant Equitable Relief for Renewal Options

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fS.label: Publisher
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fS.definition: A publisher is an individual, group, or organization responsible for producing and distributing printed or digital content, such as books, newspapers, magazines, or software. Publishers oversee the editorial, production, and marketing processes to bring a work from manuscript or concept to a finished, available product

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fa.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Lackawanna County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fa.definition: The Lackawanna County branch of the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas is a specific court within the Pennsylvania state court system that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within Lackawanna County.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Lackawanna County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fb.label: Lease Assignment and Consent to Lease Assignment
english_labels: Lease Assignment and Consent to Lease Assignment

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fc.label: Rape
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fc.definition: The carnal knowledge of a person, forcibly and/or against that person’s will or not forcibly or against the person’s will in instances where the victim is incapable of giving consent because of his/her temporary or permanent mental or physical incapacity.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fe.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Porter County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fe.definition: Indiana Circuit Court - Porter County refers to a specific court within the Indiana Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Porter County, Indiana.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ff.label: Motion for Relief from Order or Judgment
english_labels: Motion for Relief from Order or Judgment

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fn.label: NATO-5 Visa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fn.definition: A NATO-5 visa is issued to experts other than NATO officials who are entering the U.S. to perform duties on behalf of NATO, along with their immediate family members. This category includes consultants, advisors, and specialists providing expert services to NATO.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fo.label: Minnesota District Court - Redwood County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fo.definition: Minnesota District Court - Redwood County refers to a specific court within the Minnesota District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Redwood County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fq.label: Price Escalation Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fq.definition: A price escalation clause is a provision in a contract that allows for an increase in the price of goods or services based on certain predetermined conditions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fq.label: Florida County Court - Hernando County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fq.definition: A court located in Hernando County, Florida that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fr.label: New Jersey Superior Court - Cape May County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fr.definition: The New Jersey Superior Court - Cape May County is a specific court within the New Jersey Superior Court Appellate Division that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Cape May County.
english_labels: New Jersey Superior Court - Cape May County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fs.label: Deed of Variation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fs.definition: A Deed of Variation is a legal document that allows beneficiaries to alter the distribution of assets from a deceased person's estate after their death. It enables changes to be made to a will or the rules of intestacy within two years of the death, provided all affected beneficiaries agree.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fu.label: Trial Exhibits Expense
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fu.definition: The Trial Exhibits Expense is a type of expense incurred during a legal proceeding for the purpose of presenting evidence or information to the court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fz.label: Contaminant Cleanup Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8fz.definition: Law governing the removal of pollution or contaminants from environmental media such as soil, sediment, surface water, or groundwater.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8g6.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Bradford County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8g6.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Bradford County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering legal proceedings in the state of Pennsylvania.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Bradford County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8g9.label: Bankruptcy, Insolvency, and Restructuring Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8g9.definition: Laws relating to insolvent individuals and companies.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gA.label: Chapter 12 Bankruptcy Plan
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gA.definition: A Chapter 12 Bankruptcy Plan is a legal document that outlines how a family farmer or fisherman will repay their debts and reorganize their finances under Chapter 12 of the Bankruptcy Code.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gB.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Winnebago County (17th Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Winnebago County (17th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gB.label: Swaps - Assets
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gB.definition: Swaps are derivative contracts through which two parties exchange financial instruments, typically cash flows or other financial assets, based on predetermined conditions. Common types include interest rate swaps, currency swaps, and commodity swaps, each designed to manage risk or achieve specific financial objectives.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gE.label: Equitable Indemnification
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gE.definition: Equitable indemnification is a legal concept that allows a party who has paid damages to another party to seek reimbursement from a third party who is also responsible for the damages.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gG.label: inv_total_tax
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gG.definition: "The sum of all MATTER.matter_tax_on_fees + MATTER.matter_tax_on_exp for this inv_id + the sum of all TAX_TIER_SUMMARY.tax_tier_total_taxable_amount for this inv_id. This figure includes Withholding Taxes and Tiered Taxes applicable to this invoice. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gG.label: Ido
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gG.definition: Ido is a constructed language that is based on Esperanto and aims to be more regular and easier to learn.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gL.label: Fee Payee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gL.definition: A "Fee Payee" is a party who is entitled to receive payment for legal services rendered under the terms of an engagement agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gP.label: Transit Visa for Government Officials and Entourage
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gP.definition: A transit visa for government officials and their entourage is a specialized type of visa that allows high-ranking government representatives and their accompanying staff to pass through a foreign country en route to another destination for official duties. This visa is generally valid for a limited period and may come with certain privileges or immunities, depending on the diplomatic agreements between the countries involved.
english_labels: Transit Visa for Government Officials and Entourage

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gQ.label: JE00 Issue / Statements of Case (UK J-CODE)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gQ.definition: Covers issue and acknowledgment of proceedings, Statements of Case and Further Information requests/responses. Includes taking instructions, making inquiries and searches, researching, drafting, editing, filing and all meetings and communications for the purpose of such documents.
english_labels: JE00 Issue / Statements of Case (UK J-CODE)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gS.label: Assignment of Rents Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gS.definition: An Assignment of Rents Clause is a provision in a contract that allows a lender to collect rent from a property if the borrower defaults on the loan.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gU.label: Nondisturbance Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gU.definition: A Nondisturbance Clause is a provision in a contract that ensures that a tenant's rights to occupy a property will not be disturbed by a third party, such as a landlord's lender or a buyer of the property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gV.label: Liquidated Damages Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gV.definition: A liquidated damages clause is a provision in a contract that specifies the amount of damages that will be paid in the event of a breach of contract, where the actual damages are difficult to determine.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gf.label: Proof of Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gf.definition: Proof of Claim: A document filed in a bankruptcy case by a creditor or claimant asserting a right to payment from the debtor's assets.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gh.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Whiteside County (14th Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Whiteside County (14th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gj.label: M&A Remedies
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gj.definition: M&A Remedies refer to the legal actions or provisions that are put in place to address issues that arise during or after a merger or acquisition, such as breaches of contract or failure to meet agreed-upon terms.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gm.label: English, Old
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gm.definition: Old English is the language spoken in England from around 450 to 1100 AD.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gp.label: De Minimis
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gp.definition: De minimis refers to a legal principle asserting that trivial matters are not subject to legal scrutiny. This principle operates under the premise that the law does not concern itself with trifles.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gu.label: Georgia Superior Court - Lumpkin County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gu.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Lumpkin County is a specific court within the Georgia Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases in Lumpkin County, Georgia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gv.label: Volunteer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8gv.definition: A volunteer is an individual who offers services or time without the expectation of monetary compensation. Volunteers typically work for charitable, nonprofit, or public organizations to support causes or communities they care about.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8h2.label: Attorney Deceit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8h2.definition: The intentional misrepresentation or concealment of facts by an attorney to their client or the court, which constitutes a breach of the attorney's duty of loyalty and candor.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8h7.label: Materiality Scrapes
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8h7.definition: Materiality Scrapes (aka Material Adverse Effect (MAE) Qualification) refers to a provision in a contract that allows a party to back out of the agreement if certain negative events or changes occur that would significantly impact the value or profitability of the subject matter of the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8h9.label: Guardianship of Mentally Retarded or Developmentally Disabled
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8h9.definition: The Guardianship of Mentally Retarded or Developmentally Disabled refers to the legal process of appointing a guardian to make decisions on behalf of an individual who is unable to make decisions for themselves due to mental or developmental disabilities.
english_labels: Guardianship of Mentally Retarded or Developmentally Disabled

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hC.label: National Health Service Coverage
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hC.definition: Under a National Health Service model, healthcare services are funded by general taxation and are provided by government-run facilities. An example is the National Health Service (NHS) in the United Kingdom, which provides healthcare services free at the point of use for residents.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hJ.label: Privacy Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hJ.definition: Laws regulating the storing, and using of personally identifiable information of individuals.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hJ.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Putnam County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hJ.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Putnam County, Indiana, with the power to hear and decide a wide range of legal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hJ.label: Massachusetts Superior Court - Nantucket County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hJ.definition: A court located in Nantucket County that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hL.label: Law Enforcement Incident Tracking Number
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hL.definition: The unique tracking number associated with the incident that initiated the case; distinct from the arrest tracking number.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hM.label: Service Provider Indemnity Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hM.definition: A Service Provider Indemnity Clause is a provision in a contract that requires one party to compensate the other party for any losses or damages resulting from the service provider's actions or omissions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hR.label: lf_vendor_id
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hR.definition: A value that uniquely identifies the vendor. Depending on the location of the vendor, this value could be the vendor's tax id number, the vendor's VAT registration number, the vendor's DUNS number, the vendor's business registration number, or any other number or used by the vendor to uniquely identify itself, preferably to its local taxing or governmental authority.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hT.label: Furniture, Home Furnishings, Electronics, and Appliance Retailers Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hT.definition: Industries in the Furniture, Home Furnishings, Electronics, and Appliance Retailers subsector retail new furniture, home furnishings, electronics, and appliances. Establishments in this subsector with fixed point-of-sale locations may operate from showrooms or other locations that have substantial areas for the presentation or demonstration of their products. Establishments in this subsector may provide incidental services, including interior decorating, product assembly, installation, or repair services.
english_labels: Furniture, Home Furnishings, Electronics, and Appliance Retailers Industry

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hV.label: Military Reserves
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hV.definition: Reserves are a component of the armed forces consisting of individuals who maintain civilian careers but are trained to be called upon in times of need to supplement the active-duty military. This force provides additional manpower and specialized skills to support national defense and respond to emergencies or large-scale military operations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hV.label: Motion for Ongoing Royalty
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hV.definition: A Motion for Ongoing Royalty is a legal request made to a court to continue the payment of royalties beyond a certain period of time.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hW.label: Investor
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hW.definition: An investor is a person, company or entity that qualifies under the Securities Act of 1933 and related Securities and Exchange Commission regulations as one having sufficient knowledge and expertise in financial matters to weigh the value and risks of an investment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hX.label: Judgment Notwithstanding the Verdict
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hX.definition: JNOV or Judgment Notwithstanding the Verdict is a legal concept that allows a judge to overturn a jury's verdict if it is deemed unreasonable or unsupported by the evidence presented at trial.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ha.label: Provincial Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ha.definition: Provincial Court refers to a court of law that has jurisdiction over cases within a specific province or territory, and is a type of court forum within the legal system.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hb.label: Sales Tax Payment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hb.definition: Sales Tax Payment refers to general taxes levied on the sale of goods and services at a single stage in the supply chain, which could be at the manufacturing, production, wholesale, or retail stage. These taxes are typically collected by the seller at the point of sale and remitted to the government.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hd.label: New York City Court - Mechanicville
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hd.definition: A court located in Mechanicville, New York City that has jurisdiction over legal disputes and cases related to mechanics.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hd.label: Trial Type: Bench or Jury
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hd.definition: Trial Type is a subcategory of Trial Events and refers to the type of trial, which can be either Bench or Jury.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hg.label: Right to be Forgotten
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hg.definition: The "Right to be Forgotten" refers to an individual's legal ability to request the removal of personal information from digital platforms or search engine results. Originating in the European Union, this right aims to allow people to control their digital footprint by deleting or delisting information that is outdated, irrelevant, or no longer applicable.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hj.label: Lead Warning Statement Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hj.definition: A Lead Warning Statement Clause is a provision in a contract that requires the disclosure of the presence of lead in a product or property, in order to protect individuals from potential health hazards.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hk.label: Reply to Opposition
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hk.definition: A Reply to Opposition is a legal document filed in response to an opposition brief, typically in an appellate court, that addresses and refutes the arguments made by the opposing party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hn.label: Technical Report
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hn.definition: A Technical Report is a document that outlines the results, methodology, and conclusions of a scientific or engineering research project. It serves as a detailed record of the research performed and is often used to disseminate findings to specialists in the field.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hr.label: Dental Insurance Benefits
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hr.definition: Dental insurance benefits are a specialized form of health insurance offered to employees that covers part or all of the costs associated with dental care, such as routine check-ups, cleanings, and certain dental procedures.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ht.label: Termination by Mutual Agreement Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ht.definition: A Termination by Mutual Agreement Clause is a provision in a contract that allows both parties to end the agreement by mutual consent.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hx.label: Employment Application Process
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hx.definition: The Employment Application Process (Bankruptcy) refers to the legal procedures and requirements involved in filing for bankruptcy as it relates to employment of bankruptcy professionals.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hy.label: Source of Business
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hy.definition: The entity or process through which a law firm first acquired a client or a legal engagement. This source may be external, such as referrals from other lawyers, internal firm efforts like marketing, or direct client outreach.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hy.label: Warranty Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hy.definition: A Warranty Clause is a contractual provision in which one party guarantees the truth of certain facts or promises to perform certain obligations and assumes liability for any breach of such guarantees or promises.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hy.label: Conservator
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8hy.definition: A guardian, protector, or preserver - the modern equivalent of guardian. Collins v. Mnuchin, 938 F.3d 553 (5th Cir. 2019)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8i3.label: Mortgage Exacting Illegal Points and Prepayments Fees
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8i3.definition: The concept of Mortgage Exacting Illegal Points and Prepayments Fees refers to the practice of charging borrowers excessive fees for paying off their mortgage early or for points that were not properly disclosed, which is prohibited by law.
english_labels: Mortgage Exacting Illegal Points and Prepayments Fees

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8i3.label: Objection to Homestead Exemption
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8i3.definition: An objection made by a creditor or trustee in a bankruptcy case to challenge a debtor's claim of exemption for their homestead property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8i5.label: Payee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8i5.definition: A person legally entitled to payment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8i5.label: Process Mapping Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8i5.definition: Process Mapping Management refers to the systematic documentation, analysis, and improvement of legal processes in order to increase efficiency and effectiveness, and reduce costs and errors.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8i9.label: Domesticated Animal
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8i9.definition: A Domesticated Animal is a species that has been bred and adapted over generations to live in close association with humans, often providing companionship, labor, or products such as milk, eggs, and wool. These animals are typically dependent on humans for food, shelter, and care.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8iN.label: Georgia Superior Court - Seminole County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8iN.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over legal disputes and criminal cases within Seminole County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8iQ.label: New York Supreme Court - Schuyler County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8iQ.definition: The New York Supreme Court - Schuyler County is a court of general jurisdiction in the state of New York, with authority over civil and criminal cases within Schuyler County.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - Schuyler County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8iR.label: Motion to Compel Attendance
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8iR.definition: A Motion to Compel Attendance is a legal request made by one party to a lawsuit asking the court to order another party to attend a deposition or other legal proceeding.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8iS.label: Pharmaceutical Negligence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8iS.definition: Pharmaceutical Negligence refers to the failure of a medical professional or institution to provide adequate care and treatment in the prescription, dispensing, or administration of medication, resulting in harm or injury to the patient.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8iW.label: Universal Life Insurance
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8iW.definition: Universal life insurance is a type of permanent life insurance that offers both a death benefit and a cash value component, similar to whole life insurance. However, it differs in its flexibility, allowing policyholders to adjust the premiums and death benefit within certain limits, and it often has an investment element where the cash value can be invested for potential growth.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8iX.label: Equity Distribution Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8iX.definition: Equity Distribution Agreement is an agreement between a company and a distribution agent detailing the terms and conditions under which the company's equity securities may be sold or distributed to the public or private investors.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8iZ.label: 340 Marine (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8iZ.definition: Action (Admiralty and Maritime) alleging personal injury or death from an accident involving a water vessel or harbor/dock facilities, including suits brought under the Jones Act and the Limitation of Liability Act. (Excludes marine product liability claims)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ia.label: Fee Tail Estate
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ia.definition: A Fee Tail Estate is a form of property ownership in which land is granted to an individual and the heirs of their body, limiting inheritance to direct descendants and preventing the property from being sold or transferred outside the family line. This archaic legal concept was designed to keep estates within families for generations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ib.label: Correctional Facility - Real Estate Asset
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ib.definition: A Correctional Facility includes properties specifically designed, constructed, and operated to confine individuals who have been arrested, are awaiting trial, or have been convicted of crimes. These assets encompass a range of facilities, including prisons, jails, detention centers, and penitentiaries, and are critical components of the criminal justice system.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ie.label: Georgia Superior Court - Washington County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ie.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Washington County is a specific court within the Georgia Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Washington County, Georgia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8if.label: Chief of Police
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8if.definition: A Chief of Police is the highest-ranking law enforcement officer within a police department or municipal law enforcement agency. This individual is responsible for overseeing all aspects of police operations, including personnel management, policy implementation, and ensuring public safety within their jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ik.label: E104 Facsimile
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ik.definition: A facsimile, which falls under the category of expenses, refers to a document that is transmitted electronically and appears as a copy of the original document.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8il.label: Fabric Impressions
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8il.definition: Fabric impressions are patterns left by fabrics, often clothing, on surfaces or objects. Analysis of these impressions can reveal the type, weave, or specific characteristics of the fabric, aiding in identifying or corroborating details related to a crime scene.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8io.label: Motion for Claim Construction
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8io.definition: A Motion for Claim Construction is a formal request made in a trial court to interpret the meaning of specific language used in a patent claim.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8iq.label: Concert of Action Crimes
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8iq.definition: Concert of Action Crimes refer to a group of criminal offenses where two or more individuals work together to commit a crime, and each member of the group is held responsible for the actions of the others.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8is.label: Prima Facie Tort
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8is.definition: Prima Facie Tort is a civil claim that allows a plaintiff to seek damages for intentional harm caused by the defendant, without the need to prove any specific legal duty or relationship between the parties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8iw.label: Waste Management Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8iw.definition: Law governing the transport, treatment, storage, and disposal of all manner of waste, including municipal solid waste, hazardous waste, and nuclear waste.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8iw.label: Individual Rights Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8iw.definition: Individual rights such as privacy and the freedom of thought, speech, religion, press, assembly, and movement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8iy.label: Company Rules and Regulations Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8iy.definition: A Company Rules and Regulations Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the specific policies and procedures that govern the behavior and actions of employees within a company.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8j2.label: Triple Net Lease Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8j2.definition: A Triple Net Lease Clause is a provision in a contract that requires the tenant to pay for all expenses related to the property, including taxes, insurance, and maintenance costs.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8j2.label: Right to Food and Water
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8j2.definition: The right to food and water refers to the human entitlement to access adequate food and clean water necessary for survival and well-being. This right is often recognized under international law, such as the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, and aims to prevent malnutrition, starvation, and water-borne diseases by ensuring equitable distribution of essential resources.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8j6.label: Bini; Edo
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8j6.definition: A language spoken in Nigeria, specifically in the Edo State, by the Bini people.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jG.label: No-Fault Divorce
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jG.definition: A type of divorce where neither party is required to prove fault or wrongdoing in order to obtain a divorce, but rather the marriage is dissolved due to irreconcilable differences or other specified reasons.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jI.label: Tax Credits Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jI.definition: Tax Credits Law focuses on the rules, regulations, and application of tax credits within tax systems. It encompasses the interpretation and implementation of laws that allow taxpayers to reduce their tax liability directly through credits for various activities or circumstances deemed beneficial by the government.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jI.label: Improper Opinion Objection
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jI.definition: An Improper Opinion Objection is raised when a party in a legal proceeding believes that a witness is offering an opinion or conclusion that is not based on their expertise or is not permissible under the rules of evidence. This objection aims to ensure that opinions presented in court are relevant, based on proper expertise, and allowed by law.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jM.label: Age
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jM.definition: Age refers to the length of time that has elapsed since an individual's birth, typically measured in years, months, or days. In various contexts, age can be a factor in determining discrimination claims, legal rights, responsibilities, and eligibility for certain benefits or programs, such as voting, obtaining a driver's license, accessing healthcare, or participating in educational and employment opportunities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jM.label: Motions for Preliminary or Provisional Remedies
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jM.definition: A Motion for Preliminary or Provisional Remedies is a request made to a court in the early stages of a legal case seeking temporary relief or protection until a final decision can be made.
english_labels: Motions for Preliminary or Provisional Remedies

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jP.label: Receipt of Verdict
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jP.definition: Receipt of Verdict: The formal acceptance and recording of the decision made by a judge or jury at the end of a trial.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jY.label: Civil Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jY.definition: Civil Claims are legal actions brought by one party against another for a non-criminal matter, such as a breach of contract or personal injury, and seek monetary damages or other relief.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jc.label: Borda Count Electoral System
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jc.definition: The Borda count electoral system is a voting method where voters rank candidates in order of preference, and points are assigned based on the position in which each candidate is ranked. The candidate with the highest total points across all ballots wins the election, promoting a consensus-based selection rather than a simple majority.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jh.label: Assumption of Liability Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jh.definition: An Assumption of Liability Clause is a provision in a contract where one party agrees to take on the responsibility for any potential legal claims or damages that may arise from the actions of another party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ji.label: Antitrust - Vertical Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ji.definition: Antitrust - Vertical Claims refer to legal claims related to antitrust violations that involve vertical relationships between parties, such as price fixing, market allocation, and tying arrangements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jj.label: Reasonable Act or Omission
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jj.definition: An act or failure to act that a reasonable person would or would not do, which is used as a standard to determine liability in cases involving the condition of public property and governmental immunity.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jk.label: L310 Written Discovery
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jk.definition: L310 Written Discovery refers to the process of obtaining information from the opposing party through written requests, such as interrogatories, requests for admission, and requests for production of documents, as part of the broader legal process of discovery.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jl.label: 460 Deportation (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jl.definition: Action filed under the Immigration Acts (Habeas Corpus & Review) 8:1101/18:1546

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jm.label: Money Market Fund
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jm.definition: A Money Market Fund is an investment fund that aims to provide investors with a safe place to invest easily accessible, liquid assets. These funds typically invest in short-term debt securities like Treasury bills and commercial paper, and they are considered low-risk, offering relatively stable returns compared to other investment vehicles.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jm.label: Southern Common Market
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jm.definition: Mercosur (Southern Common Market): A South American trade bloc established to promote free trade and the fluid movement of goods, people, and currency.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jp.label: Choice of Law Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jp.definition: A Choice of Law Clause is a provision in a contract that specifies which jurisdiction's laws will govern the interpretation and enforcement of the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jq.label: Good Samaritan Liability
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jq.definition: The concept of Good Samaritan Liability refers to the legal responsibility of an individual who fails to provide or properly provide emergency aid to someone in need, despite having the ability to do so, and may be held liable for any resulting harm.
english_labels: Emergency Aid Not Given or Not Properly Given

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8jr.label: Red Lake Band of Chippewa Indians
english_labels: Red Lake Band of Chippewa Indians

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ju.label: Temporary Religious Worker Visa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ju.definition: This visa (in the U.S., R-1 visa) is a non-immigrant visa designated for religious workers who are coming to the destination country (e.g., U.S.) to work in a religious capacity. The initial period of stay can be up to 30 months, with the possibility of extending for an additional 30 months, for a maximum total stay of 60 months

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8k0.label: Manipuri
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8k0.definition: Manipuri is a structured system of communication, belonging to the Language top-level class, that is spoken in the Manipur state of India and neighboring areas.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8k1.label: L390 Other Discovery
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8k1.definition: L390 Other Discovery refers to the process of obtaining information through means other than formal discovery methods, such as through informal interviews or public records requests.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8k2.label: Contract Period Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8k2.definition: A Contract Period Clause is a provision in a contract that specifies the duration of the agreement between the parties involved.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8k6.label: Herero
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8k6.definition: A language spoken by the Herero people, primarily in Namibia and Botswana.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8k7.label: Employment Title
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8k7.definition: Employment Title refers to the formal designation given to a specific job position within an organization, such as "Software Engineer," "Marketing Manager," or "Legal Counsel." The title is often used to signify the roles and responsibilities of the position, and may also indicate the employee's rank or level within the organizational hierarchy

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8kJ.label: Publication Date
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8kJ.definition: Publication Date refers to the date on which a document, typically a legal or official one, is formally made available to the public. This date is critical for determining the beginning of time periods for legal actions, such as appeals or filings, and for establishing when information becomes part of the public domain.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8kJ.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Pulaski County (1st Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Pulaski County (1st Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8kK.label: Joint Enterprise Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8kK.definition: A Joint Enterprise Claim is a legal claim that holds multiple parties responsible for a wrongful act or omission committed in the course of a joint venture or enterprise, and is a type of Corporate and Partnership Liability Claim.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8kO.label: Power Press Exception
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8kO.definition: An employee can sue an employer for injury caused by the employer's willful failure to install or willful removal of a point of operation guard on a "power press" machine.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8kO.label: Auction
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8kO.definition: An auction is a legal event where goods or property are sold to the highest bidder, typically as part of a bankruptcy or restructuring process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8kP.label: Witness to Injury Suffering Emotional Distress
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8kP.definition: The concept of "Witness to Injury Suffering Emotional Distress" refers to a person who has observed another individual experiencing physical harm or emotional suffering, and as a result, has suffered emotional distress themselves.
english_labels: Witness to Injury Suffering Emotional Distress

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8kR.label: Sasak
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8kR.definition: A language spoken by the Sasak people of Lombok Island, Indonesia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8kZ.label: Curfew
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8kZ.definition: A curfew is a specific condition imposed as part of a criminal disposition, which requires an individual to be indoors or in a designated location during certain hours of the day or night.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8kc.label: Deonitic Modality
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8kc.definition: Deontic Modality refers to the linguistic expression of obligation, permission, or prohibition in legal language.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ke.label: Affirmed Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ke.definition: The legal authority (e.g., judicial opinion, statute, regulation) has been affirmed by some decisionmaker (e.g., judge, regulator).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8kf.label: Kara-Kalpak
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8kf.definition: Kara-Kalpak is a language that belongs to the Turkic language family and is spoken primarily in Uzbekistan.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8kj.label: Termination of Employment Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8kj.definition: A Termination of Employment Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the conditions under which an employer may end the employment relationship with an employee.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8kk.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Allegheny County, Civil Division
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8kk.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Allegheny County, Civil Division is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system that handles civil cases in Allegheny County.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Allegheny County, Civil Division

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8km.label: Mortgage Contingency Loan Exacting Illegal Commission
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8km.definition: A Mortgage Contingency Loan Exacting Illegal Commission is a type of loan in which the lender charges an illegal commission to the borrower, and the loan is contingent upon the borrower obtaining a mortgage.
english_labels: Mortgage Contingency Loan Exacting Illegal Commission

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8km.label: Signing Bonus Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8km.definition: A signing bonus clause is a provision in a contract that provides for an additional payment to be made to an individual upon signing the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ks.label: Death
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ks.definition: Death, in a legal context, marks the end of a person's life, as well as the termination of an individual's legal rights and duties. It initiates the probate process, where a deceased's estate is settled, debts are paid, and assets are distributed to heirs or beneficiaries according to a will or intestate laws.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8kt.label: expense segment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8kt.definition: Expense segment refers to a specific component within the LEDES XML E-Billing Ver. 2.2 standard, which includes information such as charge date, units, work location, expense code, and total amount for billing purposes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ku.label: Georgia Superior Court - Long County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ku.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Long County: A specific court within the Georgia Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases in Long County, Georgia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8kx.label: Travel Document Issued Date
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8kx.definition: The Travel Document Issued Date is the specific date on which a travel document like a passport or visa was officially issued by the relevant authority. This date is important for determining the document's validity period and is often required when applying for visas or entering foreign countries

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8kz.label: Defending Deposition
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8kz.definition: Defending Deposition refers to the legal process of representing a party in a deposition and protecting their interests, typically in response to a legal dispute or claim.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8l6.label: Credit Issuer Dishonoring or Repudiating
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8l6.definition: The concept of "Credit Issuer Dishonoring or Repudiating" refers to the act of a bank or other entity failing to honor or refusing to acknowledge a debt or obligation owed to a creditor, typically involving commercial paper or other financial instruments.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lG.label: Regulatory Exemption
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lG.definition: Regulatory exemption refers to a provision that allows an individual, business, or activity to be excused from complying with certain rules or requirements typically imposed by a regulatory authority. Exemptions are usually granted to promote specific policy objectives or because the standard regulations are deemed unnecessary or overly burdensome in particular cases.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lH.label: Absentee Shawnee Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma
english_labels: Absentee Shawnee Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lI.label: Plant Patent Registration
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lI.definition: The concept of Plant Patent Registration refers to the legal process of obtaining exclusive rights to a new and distinct variety of plant, as granted by the United States Patent and Trademark Office.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lJ.label: Breach of No-Shop Covenant
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lJ.definition: The Breach of No-Shop Covenant refers to the violation of a contractual agreement between parties involved in a business transaction, where one party agrees not to solicit or entertain offers from other potential buyers for a specified period of time.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lL.label: Retroactive Effectiveness Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lL.definition: A Retroactive Effectiveness Clause is a provision in a contract that makes it effective from a date before it was actually signed.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lS.label: Lease Assumption Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lS.definition: A Lease Assumption Agreement is a legal contract that allows a new tenant to take over the lease of a property from the original tenant, with the consent of the landlord, and outlines the terms and conditions of the transfer.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lU.label: Motion for Misjoinder of Parties
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lU.definition: A Motion for Misjoinder of Parties is a legal document filed by a party in response to a complaint, requesting the court to dismiss the case due to improper joinder of parties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lZ.label: Louisiana Department of Labor - Office of Workers' Compensation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lZ.definition: The Louisiana Department of Labor - Office of Workers' Compensation is a government agency responsible for administering workers' compensation proceedings in Louisiana State Courts.
english_labels: Louisiana Department of Labor - Office of Workers' Compensation

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8la.label: Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8la.definition: An Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD) Claim refers to a legal action or regulatory complaint arising from the alleged breach or non-compliance with the AIFMD, which regulates managers of alternative investment funds (AIFs) in the European Union. These claims often involve issues related to investor protection, transparency, and the marketing and management of AIFs.
english_labels: Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive Claim
Alternative Investment Fund Managers Regulation Claim

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lb.label: Supremacy Clause Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lb.definition: A Supremacy Clause claim refers to a legal argument based on the Supremacy Clause of the United States Constitution, asserting that federal law prevails over conflicting state or local laws when they are in direct conflict. It establishes the principle that the Constitution, federal laws, and treaties take precedence over inconsistent state laws, ensuring a consistent and unified legal framework throughout the United States.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ld.label: Trade Dress Dilution
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ld.definition: The concept of Trade Dress Dilution refers to a legal claim that protects the distinctiveness and uniqueness of a company's product or service design from being weakened or diluted by similar designs used by competitors, which may cause confusion among consumers.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ld.label: Crimes Against Property
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ld.definition: To willfully or maliciously destroy, damage, deface, or otherwise injure real or personal property without the consent of the owner or the person having custody or control of it.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lg.label: New York City Court - Lockport
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lg.definition: A court located in Lockport, New York that operates under the jurisdiction of the New York City Court system.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lh.label: Trusts and Estate Planning Event
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lh.definition: Trusts and Estate Planning Events refer to significant occurrences, like death, funeral, or incapacity, that trigger the provisions and directives outlined in estate planning documents. Such events necessitate actions like asset distribution, trust activation, or execution of end-of-life directives to ensure the deceased or incapacitated individual's wishes are honored.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lj.label: Cow Creek Band of Umpqua Tribe of Indians
english_labels: Cow Creek Band of Umpqua Tribe of Indians

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lj.label: Sole Shareholder Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lj.definition: A Sole Shareholder Clause is a provision in a contract that specifies the rights and obligations of a shareholder who owns all of the outstanding shares of a corporation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lk.label: Lease Termination Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lk.definition: A lease termination clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the conditions under which a lease agreement can be ended before its natural expiration date.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lm.label: Collective Bargaining Event
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lm.definition: A formal negotiation process between an employer (or group of employers) and a group of employees (or their representatives, usually a union) aimed at reaching agreements on employment conditions. This event typically involves discussions on wages, working hours, benefits, and other terms of employment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lm.label: Multi-District Litigation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lm.definition: Multi-District Litigation (MDL) refers to a legal procedure where multiple related cases from different jurisdictions are consolidated and transferred to a single court for pretrial proceedings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ln.label: By Time with Standard Rates
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ln.definition: A method of billing for legal services based on the amount of time spent on a task using standard rates.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lp.label: Health and Personal Care Retailers Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lp.definition: Industries in the Health and Personal Care Retailers subsector retail health and personal care merchandise. Establishments in this subsector are characterized principally by the products they retail, and some health and personal care retailers have specialized staff including pharmacists, opticians, and other professionals engaged in retailing, advising customers, and/or fitting the product sold to the customer's needs.
english_labels: Health and Personal Care Retailers Industry
Health and Personal Care Store Industry

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lq.label: Hassanamisco Band of the Nipmuc Nation
english_labels: Hassanamisco Band of the Nipmuc Nation

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lq.label: Personal Property Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lq.definition: Matters relating to personal property — not real property — such as damage to vehicles, ownership of valuables (e.g., jewelry), trespass to chattels, etc.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lt.label: Japanese
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lt.definition: Japanese (Language) is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary, used in legal matters as a means of document, artifact, evidence, testimony, proceeding, or any other legal aspect, and is a subcategory of the Language top-level class.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lu.label: Motion to File Noncomforming Brief
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lu.definition: A Motion to File Nonconforming Brief is a request made to the court to allow a party to file a brief that does not comply with the court's rules or standards.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ly.label: Depressive, Bipolar and Related Disorders
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ly.definition: Depressive, Bipolar, and Related Disorders encompass a range of mental health conditions characterized by significant mood disturbances. These disorders are characterized by an irritable, depressed, elevated, or expansive mood, or by a loss of interest or pleasure in all or almost all activities, causing a clinically significant decline in functioning. Symptoms and signs may include, but are not limited to, feelings of hopelessness or guilt, suicidal ideation, a clinically significant change in body weight or appetite, sleep disturbances, an increase or decrease in energy, psychomotor abnormalities, disturbed concentration, pressured speech, grandiosity, reduced impulse control, sadness, euphoria, and social withdrawal.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lz.label: Holdover Eviction Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8lz.definition: A holdover eviction claim is a legal action initiated by a landlord against a tenant who remains in a rented property after the lease or rental agreement has expired. In such cases, the tenant is often referred to as a "holdover tenant." The claim seeks the tenant's removal from the property due to their continued occupancy without a valid lease or rental agreement. The eviction process typically involves court proceedings to resolve the dispute.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8m3.label: Waiver of Presentment Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8m3.definition: A Waiver of Presentment Clause is a provision in a legal document that waives the requirement for a party to present a document or instrument for payment or acceptance before taking legal action.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8m7.label: Mandamus
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8m7.definition: A writ of mandamus is a civil remedy sought to compel a public official or entity to perform a duty that they are legally obligated to perform.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mB.label: Warden
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mB.definition: A Warden is the chief administrative officer of a correctional facility, responsible for overseeing all aspects of the facility's operations, including security, inmate management, staff supervision, and compliance with regulations. The Warden ensures the effective and humane treatment of inmates while maintaining order and safety within the institution.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mC.label: Broadcast
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mC.definition: A Broadcast is the transmission of audio and/or video content to a dispersed audience via electronic mass communication mediums such as radio, television, or internet streaming. Broadcasts can include news, entertainment, educational programs, and advertisements, reaching audiences in real-time or through scheduled programming.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mC.label: Interest Payment in Kind
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mC.definition: Interest Payment in Kind (PIK) is a method of paying interest on debt obligations using additional securities or other non-cash assets instead of cash. This payment structure allows the issuer to defer cash outlays by increasing the principal amount of the debt or by issuing additional securities, typically used in situations where the issuer wants to conserve cash or lacks immediate liquidity.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mF.label: Manzanita Band of Diegueno Mission Indians
english_labels: Manzanita Band of Diegueno Mission Indians

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mH.label: Early Termination Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mH.definition: An Early Termination Clause is a provision in a contract that allows one or both parties to end the agreement before its natural expiration date.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mI.label: New Mexico Magistrate Court - Santa Fe County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mI.definition: A court located in Santa Fe County, New Mexico that has limited jurisdiction over certain types of cases, such as traffic violations and misdemeanors.
english_labels: New Mexico Magistrate Court - Santa Fe County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mK.label: Utilities Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mK.definition: A Utilities Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the rights and obligations of the parties with respect to the provision and use of utilities, such as electricity, gas, water, and telecommunications services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mP.label: Minnesota District Court - Rice County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mP.definition: Minnesota District Court - Rice County refers to a specific court within the Minnesota District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Rice County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mR.label: Litigation Criminal Defenses
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mR.definition: A criminal defense used in a legal proceeding to protect an individual accused of a crime from prosecution or punishment, specifically in the context of litigation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mR.label: Indiana Superior Court - Jennings County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mR.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Indiana that has the authority to hear and decide a wide range of legal cases within Jennings County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mU.label: Texas District Court - Gillespie County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mU.definition: A Texas District Court in Gillespie County is a specific court within the Texas District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Gillespie County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mV.label: Slovenian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mV.definition: Slovenian (Language) refers to the written or spoken structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary specific to the Slovenian language, which is used in legal matters such as documents, artifacts, evidence, testimony, proceedings, or any other legal aspect.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ma.label: Institutional Investment Manager Holdings Report
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8ma.definition: Institutional Investment Manager Holdings Report is a report filed by institutional investment managers with the financial regulator (e.g., U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)) to disclose the investment manager's holdings in "in country" traded equities (e.g., within U.S.), options, and other securities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mc.label: Occitan
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mc.definition: Occitan (post 1500) is a language that developed after the year 1500 and is part of the Language top-level class.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mc.label: Software as a Service Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mc.definition: A SaaS Agreement governs the provision and use of cloud-based software services. It typically covers aspects like subscription terms, data handling, service levels, and terms of use.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mc.label: South American Indian languages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mc.definition: South American Indian languages are a group of structured systems of communication spoken by indigenous peoples in South America.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8md.label: Spin-off
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8md.definition: A spin-off divestiture is a corporate action in which a company separates a business unit, division, or subsidiary into a standalone, independent entity. In this process, shares of the new company are often distributed to existing shareholders of the parent company on a pro-rata basis. Spin-off divestitures are often undertaken to allow the separated entity to focus on its core competencies, unlock shareholder value, or comply with regulatory requirements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mg.label: Georgia Superior Court - Dougherty County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mg.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Dougherty County, Georgia, with authority to hear and decide a wide range of legal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mh.label: Synchronous Communication
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mh.definition: A communication that occurs synchronously (at the same time), such as an in-person meeting, telephone call, or videoconference.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mh.label: Constructive Eviction of Tenant
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mh.definition: The Constructive Eviction of Tenant is a legal concept that occurs when a landlord's actions or omissions make a rental property uninhabitable, forcing the tenant to move out, and is considered a form of Unlawful Eviction of Tenant.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mi.label: AIDS
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mi.definition: AIDS (Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome) is the advanced stage of HIV infection, characterized by a severely weakened immune system due to the significant loss of CD4 cells. This condition makes the body highly susceptible to opportunistic infections and certain cancers, requiring intensive medical treatment and supportive care.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mm.label: Physical Elder Abuse
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mm.definition: Physical Elder Abuse: The intentional use of force against an elderly person that results in physical pain, injury, or impairment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mo.label: Product Liability Representation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mo.definition: Product Liability Representation is a clause in merger and acquisition agreements where the selling party attests to the absence of product defects or claims arising from sold or distributed products of the target company. It serves to protect the buyer from potential undisclosed liabilities or claims related to product malfunctions, damages, or injuries that may arise after the acquisition.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mv.label: Employee Benefits Motion
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mv.definition: A request made by a debtor in a bankruptcy case seeking authorization to continue providing employee benefits, such as health insurance and retirement plans, to its employees.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mw.label: Freedom from Discrimination
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mw.definition: Freedom from discrimination is a fundamental human right that entails the equal treatment of all individuals, regardless of race, gender, religion, nationality, disability, or other characteristics. This right is upheld by various international treaties and national laws, aiming to prevent unjust or prejudicial treatment based on a person's inherent traits or beliefs.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mx.label: Notice of Status Conference
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mx.definition: A Notice of Status Conference is a written communication that informs parties involved in a legal case of a scheduled meeting with the judge to discuss the current status of the case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mz.label: Subsidized Healthcare Coverage Policy for Low-Income Groups
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8mz.definition: Subsidized healthcare programs like Medicaid in the U.S. provide medical coverage to low-income individuals and families. These programs are often funded by both state and federal governments, and eligibility criteria can vary by jurisdiction.
english_labels: Subsidized Healthcare Coverage Policy for Low-Income Groups

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8n4.label: Non-Testifying Expert
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8n4.definition: An expert whom a party retains for consultation, but the expert does not provide oral testimony or a written report.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8n7.label: Motion to Cancel Meeting of Creditors
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8n7.definition: A Motion to Cancel Meeting of Creditors is a request made in a bankruptcy case to cancel the scheduled meeting of creditors, which is a meeting where the debtor is required to appear and answer questions under oath about their financial affairs.
english_labels: Motion to Cancel Meeting of Creditors

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8nA.label: Indiana Superior Court - Morgan County, Superior Court2
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8nA.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Morgan County, Indiana, with authority over civil and criminal cases.
english_labels: Indiana Superior Court - Morgan County, Superior Court2

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8nD.label: Signed During Tail Period
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8nD.definition: A contract or agreement that is executed during the final stage of an acquisition proposal, typically after the main terms have been agreed upon and before the deal is closed.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8nI.label: Judicial Chambers Meeting
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8nI.definition: "Judicial chambers meeting" pertains to private discussions and exchanges of information among judges and their clerks or staff members within a court's administrative office or chambers. These communications can involve case-related matters, administrative issues, or legal research and are typically not part of the public record of court proceedings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8nJ.label: WC130 Experts/Consultants
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8nJ.definition: Identify medical experts and vocational experts, developing/reviewing Expert/Consultant Reports, communication with expert /consultants adjuster/employer/ nurse case manager regarding expert opinions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8nK.label: AI Accuracy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8nK.definition: AI Accuracy is a metric within AI measurement that quantifies an AI system's proportion of correct (intended) predictions, compared to the total number of predictions. It serves as an indicator of how well an AI system performs in making accurate predictions, based on Ground Truth, encompassing both precision and recall, providing a comprehensive assessment of model performance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8nL.label: Post-Judgment Interest
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8nL.definition: Post-Judgment Interest refers to the interest that accrues on a monetary award after a judgment has been entered by a court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8nN.label: Married
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8nN.definition: The concept of "Married (Marital Status)" refers to the legal status of being married, indicating that an individual has entered into a legally recognized union with another person.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8nP.label: Air Quality Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8nP.definition: Law governing the emission of air pollutants into the atmosphere.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8nR.label: Misappropriation of Name
