https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xg.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Reynolds County: A court of law in Missouri that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Reynolds County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xg.label: Successor Probate
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xg.definition: Successor Probate is a type of probate filing where a new executor is appointed to administer the estate of a deceased person when the original executor is unable or unwilling to fulfill their duties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xg.label: Contact ID
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xg.definition: Contact ID refers to a unique identifier assigned to a specific contact within a system or database, typically used for tracking and organizing contact information.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xh.label: Perjury
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xh.definition: The intentional act of lying or giving false testimony under oath in a legal proceeding, which is considered a crime against the government and can result in judicial and procedural tort claims.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xh.label: Settlement Offer Evidentiary Objection
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xh.definition: A Settlement Offer Evidentiary Objection, also known as an Offers of Compromise Objection, is raised when a party in a legal proceeding believes that evidence of a settlement offer or negotiation is being used to prove liability or the validity of a claim. This objection aims to protect the confidentiality of settlement discussions and encourage parties to negotiate without fear of their offers being used against them in court.
english_labels: Objection to Evidence of Negotiated Settlements

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xi.label: Texas District Court - Travis County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xi.definition: A Texas District Court located in Travis County, which has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xk.label: Proration Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xk.definition: A proration clause is a provision in a contract that allocates costs or benefits between parties based on a specific formula or method.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xo.label: Entity Groups
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xo.definition: Entity Groups are a subset of Legal Entities and refer to groups of individuals or organizations that come together for a specific purpose, such as a Board of Directors or Joint Defense Group.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xp.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Allegheny County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xp.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court located in Allegheny County, responsible for administering legal proceedings within its jurisdiction.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Allegheny County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xq.label: Sex Trafficking
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xq.definition: Sex trafficking involves the recruitment, harboring, transportation, provision, or obtaining of a person for the purpose of a commercial sex act, usually through force, fraud, or coercion. This is a serious criminal offense and is subject to severe penalties under various international and national laws.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xq.label: Municipal Corporation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xq.definition: A municipal corporation is the legal term for a local governing body, including (but not necessarily limited to) cities, counties, towns, townships, charter townships, villages, and boroughs. The term can also be used to describe municipally owned corporations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xr.label: Swan Creek Black River Confederate Tribe
english_labels: Swan Creek Black River Confederate Tribe

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xr.label: Texas District Court - Comal County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xr.definition: A Texas District Court located in Comal County, which has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xr.label: Public Benefits
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xr.definition: Public benefits are government programs designed to provide financial or material aid to individuals or families who meet certain eligibility criteria, usually based on need or income. These benefits can include healthcare, food assistance, housing subsidies, and unemployment compensation, among others, and are intended to improve the well-being and stability of a society

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xs.label: Increased Risk of Harm
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xs.definition: Increased Risk of Harm: A legal concept that refers to the likelihood of harm or injury occurring in the future as a result of a defendant's actions or negligence, even if the harm has not yet occurred.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xs.label: False Light
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xs.definition: False Light is a type of privacy claim where a person is portrayed in a misleading or false manner that would be highly offensive to a reasonable person.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xw.label: Wrongful Foreclosure Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xw.definition: A wrongful foreclosure claim is a legal action brought by a borrower against a lender or creditor alleging that the foreclosure of their property was conducted improperly or unlawfully.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xw.label: Country Risk
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xw.definition: The risk that a foreign government will default on its bonds or other financial commitments. Country risk also refers to the broader notion of the stability of the country's financial system.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xw.label: Communication Accessibility Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xw.definition: This claim pertains to barriers that prevent individuals with disabilities from receiving or conveying information effectively. Examples include lack of sign language interpreters, inaccessible formats for the visually impaired, or lack of captioning for audio content.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xy.label: Nondispositive Stipulation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xy.definition: A Nondispositive Stipulation is an agreement between parties in a legal case that does not determine the outcome of the case, but rather sets forth certain facts or procedural matters that are not in dispute.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xz.label: Copyright Infringement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8xz.definition: The unauthorized use or reproduction of a copyrighted work, without the permission of the owner, which may include copying, distributing, displaying, or performing the work.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8y6.label: Motion for Relief due to Satisfaction, Release, or Discharge
english_labels: Motion for Relief due to Satisfaction, Release, or Discharge

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yA.label: Creoles and pidgins
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yA.definition: A creole or pidgin language is a simplified language that develops as a means of communication between groups who do not share a common language.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yB.label: Lessors of Nonfinancial Intangible Assets (except Copyrighted Works) Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yB.definition: Industries in the Lessors of Nonfinancial Intangible Assets (except Copyrighted Works) subsector include establishments primarily engaged in assigning rights to assets, such as patents, trademarks, brand names, and/or franchise agreements, for which a royalty payment or licensing fee is paid to the asset holder. Establishments in this subsector own the patents, trademarks, and/or franchise agreements that they allow others to use or reproduce for a fee and may or may not have created those assets. Establishments that allow franchisees the use of the franchise name, contingent on the franchisee buying products or services from the franchisor, are classified elsewhere. Excluded from this subsector are establishments primarily engaged in leasing real property and establishments primarily engaged in leasing tangible assets, such as automobiles, computers, consumer goods, and industrial machinery and equipment. These establishments are classified in Subsector 531, Real Estate, and Subsector 532, Rental and Leasing Services, respectively.
english_labels: Lessors of Non-financial Intangible Assets Industry
Lessors of Nonfinancial Intangible Assets (except Copyrighted Works) Industry

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yC.label: Indiana Superior Court - Hendricks County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yC.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Indiana that hears civil and criminal cases within Hendricks County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yJ.label: Denial
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yJ.definition: Denial is a response to a claim where the defendant asserts that the allegations made against them are false or invalid.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yK.label: Medical Payment Evidentiary Objection
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yK.definition: A Medical Payment Evidentiary Objection is raised when a party in a legal proceeding believes that evidence of payments made for medical expenses is being used to prove liability or fault. This objection aims to prevent the prejudicial impact of such evidence, as the payment of medical bills does not necessarily indicate an admission of liability.
english_labels: Objection to Evidence of Medical Expense Payments

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yL.label: Full Payment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yL.definition: Full Payment refers to a financial transaction where the total amount due has been paid in its entirety. This status indicates that the current financial obligation has been completely satisfied, leaving no outstanding balance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yM.label: California Superior Court - Kern Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yM.definition: A California Superior Court - Kern Cty. is a specific court within the California Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Kern County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yM.label: Balinese
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yM.definition: Balinese (Language) is a structured system of communication spoken in Bali, Indonesia, consisting of its own unique grammar and vocabulary.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yN.label: Freedom of Information Act Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yN.definition: A Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) Claim is a legal claim made under the FOIA statute, which allows individuals to request access to federal agency records and information.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yP.label: Procedural Motions - Trial Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yP.definition: A Procedural Motion in Trial Court refers to a formal request made by a party to the court during a trial, seeking a specific action or decision from the court, such as a request for sanctions or attorney fees.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yR.label: Personal Care Products
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yR.definition: In the context of bankruptcies and monthly spending budgets, Personal Care Products refer to non-medical goods purchased for hygiene or beautification, such as toiletries, cosmetics, and grooming supplies. These are generally considered non-discretionary expenses, but their allocation may be scrutinized during a bankruptcy process to determine reasonable living expenses for the debtor

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yT.label: LGB+
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yT.definition: LGBTQIA+ is an acronym that stands for Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Queer or Questioning, Intersex, and Asexual, with the plus sign indicating the inclusion of other sexual orientations, gender identities, and expressions. The term serves as an umbrella for various communities that do not conform to heteronormative definitions of gender and sexuality.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yY.label: Public Disclosure of Acquisition Disclosure
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yY.definition: The Public Disclosure of Acquisition Disclosure refers to the requirement of disclosing information related to the acquisition of a company or its assets to the public, triggered by a specific event or condition, such as the Tail Period Fee.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yo.label: Swahili
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yo.definition: Swahili is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary, used in legal matters, that is specifically identified as the language of Swahili.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yq.label: General Business Liability Insurance Policy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yq.definition: General Business Liability Insurance, also known simply as general liability insurance, provides coverage for common business risks, including bodily injury and property damage that occur at the business premises or as a result of business operations. It also often covers legal costs related to these risks. This type of insurance is foundational for most businesses.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yw.label: Collecting Bank Late Objection to Negotiable Instrument
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8yw.definition: A Collecting Bank Late Objection to Negotiable Instrument is a claim made by a bank that collected a negotiable instrument after the deadline for objections has passed, and is related to banking, commercial paper, and creditor claims.
english_labels: Collecting Bank Late Objection to Negotiable Instrument

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8z4.label: Licensor
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8z4.definition: A licensor is person or entity with exclusive legal rights over a thing or, acting as agent for the owner, gives, sells or otherwise surrenders to another a limited right to use that thing.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8z6.label: Opt Out Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8z6.definition: An opt-out clause is a provision in a contract that allows one or more parties to withdraw from the agreement under certain circumstances.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8z8.label: Catalan; Valencian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8z8.definition: A language spoken in Catalonia and Valencia, which has its own unique grammar and vocabulary.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8z9.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Rush County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8z9.definition: Indiana Circuit Court - Rush County refers to a specific court within the Indiana Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Rush County, Indiana.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zA.label: Prompt
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zA.definition: A Prompt is an input to a generative AI system that specifies the task to be performed or the information the system should generate in response. Prompts guide the AI's behavior, directing it toward producing desired outputs based on the given instructions or queries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zB.label: disc_cred_amount
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zB.definition: "The total amount discounted/credited against or additional charges incurred for this disc_cred. If EXP_ITEM_DISC_CRED.increase_decrease equals ""increase"", then this value is a positive number; if EXP_ITEM_DISC_CRED.increase_decrease equals ""decrease"", then this value is a negative number. Discounts or reductions should be a negative number; credits should be a positive number. I.e. ""-150.0000"" reflects a $150 decrease/reduction/write-down on the expense item, ""150.0000"" reflects a $150 increase/charge/write-up on the expense item. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zB.label: Immigration Amendment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zB.definition: "Immigration Amendment" involves requesting changes to specific details of an existing immigration application or status, often to correct errors or update information, requiring submission of appropriate documentation and approval from immigration authorities

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zF.label: Royalty Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zF.definition: A Royalty Agreement is a contract between two parties where one party agrees to pay the other for the use of intellectual property or physical assets. The payment, often a percentage of revenues from using the asset, is termed as royalty.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zG.label: Arthropods
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zG.definition: Arthropods are a diverse phylum of invertebrate animals known as Arthropoda, characterized by their exoskeleton, segmented bodies, and jointed appendages. This group includes insects, arachnids, crustaceans, and myriapods, and they are found in virtually every habitat on Earth, playing crucial ecological roles.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zI.label: Right of Integrity
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zI.definition: The Right of Integrity, a key aspect of moral rights in copyright law, allows the creator to object to any modification of their work that could harm their reputation or honor. This right protects the personal connection between the creator and their work, ensuring that their artistic vision remains unaltered without their consent.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zM.label: Breach of Implied Warranty of Title
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zM.definition: The Breach of Implied Warranty of Title is a legal concept that occurs when a seller of property fails to transfer clear and marketable title to the buyer, despite not making any express warranties about the title.
english_labels: Breach of Implied Warranty of Title

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zN.label: Minnesota District Court - Nicollet County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zN.definition: Minnesota District Court - Nicollet County: A specific court within the Minnesota District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Nicollet County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zT.label: Georgia District Court - Liberty County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zT.definition: Georgia District Court - Liberty County: A specific court within the Georgia District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Liberty County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zV.label: Lessor’s Default on Lease of Goods
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zV.definition: The Lessor's Default on Lease of Goods refers to the failure of the party who owns the leased property to fulfill their obligations under the lease agreement, resulting in a breach of contract and potential legal action by the lessee.
english_labels: Lessor’s Default on Lease of Goods

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zV.label: Prisoners' Rights
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zV.definition: Prisoners' rights are legal protections afforded to individuals who are incarcerated, ensuring that they are treated with dignity and have access to basic human rights while serving their sentences. These rights include access to medical care, protection from cruel and unusual punishment, and the ability to challenge their confinement through legal processes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zc.label: Graffiti
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zc.definition: A Graffiti Claim is a criminal misdemeanor charge alleging that an individual has defaced property by painting, marking, or inscribing surfaces without the owner's consent. This legal action asserts that the accused has engaged in vandalism through the unauthorized application of graffiti, potentially causing property damage and public nuisance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zf.label: Minnesota District Court - Brown County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zf.definition: Minnesota District Court - Brown County is a specific court within the Minnesota District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Brown County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zg.label: Warehouseman or Carrier Lien on Goods
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zg.definition: A Warehouseman or Carrier Lien on Goods is a legal concept that allows a person or entity who stores or transports goods to have a legal claim on those goods until they receive payment for their services.
english_labels: Warehouseman or Carrier Lien on Goods

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zg.label: Georgia Superior Court - Emanuel County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zg.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Emanuel County refers to a specific court within the Georgia Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Emanuel County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zi.label: Bankruptcy and Restructuring Document
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zi.definition: A Bankruptcy and Restructuring Document is a written or recorded representation of information related to bankruptcy and restructuring proceedings, including forms, statements, and motions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zl.label: 550 Civil Rights (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zl.definition: Action by current or former prisoner alleging a civil rights violation by corrections officials that is not related to a condition of prison life.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zr.label: Contact Name
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zr.definition: Contact Name refers to the name of an individual, business, or organization. This name is used for communication and documentation purposes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zw.label: Motions in Trial Courts
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zw.definition: Motions in Trial Courts are requests made by parties in a legal case to the judge for a specific action or ruling during the trial process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zx.label: Stipulation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zx.definition: A stipulation is a legal document that outlines an agreement between parties involved in a court case, often used in trial court practice and bankruptcy and restructuring proceedings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zz.label: Waiver of Sovereign Immunity Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R8zz.definition: A Waiver of Sovereign Immunity Clause is a provision in a legal agreement where a government entity agrees to be subject to the jurisdiction of a court or tribunal, thereby waiving its immunity from legal action.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R900.label: GDPR Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R900.definition: A GDPR Clause is a specific provision within a Data Privacy Clause that outlines the requirements and obligations for the processing and protection of personal data under the General Data Protection Regulation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R901.label: Seeking Advisory Judicial Opinion
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R901.definition: Seeking an advisory judicial opinion involves requesting a court's guidance on a legal question, usually without the existence of an actual case or controversy. Such opinions are generally non-binding and are more common in some legal systems than others; for example, U.S. federal courts generally do not issue advisory opinions due to the "case or controversy" requirement under Article III of the Constitution.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R902.label: Kisoro
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R902.definition: Kisoro is a town located in Uganda.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R903.label: Tete
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R903.definition: Tete is a location in Mozambique.

english_labels: Ma-Chis Lower Creek Indian Tribe of Alabama

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R905.label: Jowzjan
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R905.definition: Jowzjan is a province in Afghanistan.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R905.label: Minnesota District Court - Rock County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R905.definition: Minnesota District Court - Rock County: A specific court within the Minnesota District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Rock County, Minnesota.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R906.label: Entire Agreement Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R906.definition: An Entire Agreement Clause, also known as an Entire Contract Clause, is a provision in a contract that declares that the written agreement is the complete and final expression of the parties' agreement, and supersedes all prior negotiations and understandings between them.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R909.label: Helicopter
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R909.definition: A Helicopter is a type of rotorcraft that achieves flight through the use of horizontally spinning rotors, allowing it to take off, land vertically, hover, and fly in various directions. This aircraft is widely used for its versatility in reaching remote areas, providing air ambulance services, and performing aerial surveillance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90A.label: Dissolution for Deadlock
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90A.definition: The concept of "Dissolution for Deadlock" refers to a legal claim made by a corporation or partnership when the entity is unable to make decisions due to a deadlock among its members, resulting in the need for the entity to be dissolved.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90A.label: Trelawny
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90A.definition: Trelawny is a geographic location in Jamaica, which is a political subdivision of the country.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90B.label: Chukotskiy avtonomnyy okrug
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90B.definition: Chukotskiy avtonomnyy okrug is a region in the Russian Federation with the status of an autonomous okrug.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90B.label: Polzela
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90B.definition: Polzela is a town located in Slovenia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90C.label: New York Community Justice Center - Harlem
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90C.definition: A court program located in Harlem that aims to provide alternative sentencing options and community-based services to reduce recidivism and improve public safety.
english_labels: New York Community Justice Center - Harlem

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90C.label: Federal Highway Administration
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90C.definition: The Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) is a division of the United States Department of Transportation that specializes in highway transportation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90D.label: Lyantonde
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90D.definition: Lyantonde is a district in Uganda.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90D.label: Zurich
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90D.definition: Zurich is a city in Switzerland.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90E.label: Gumushane
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90E.definition: Gumushane is a city in Turkey, located in the TR+29 region.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90E.label: Namur
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90E.definition: Namur is a city in Belgium.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90E.definition: Dokolo is a location in Uganda.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90E.label: Sikasso
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90E.definition: Sikasso is a city in Mali.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90E.label: Georgia Superior Court - Hart County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90E.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Hart County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Hart County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90F.label: Extradition Clause Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90F.definition: An Extradition Clause claim refers to a legal argument based on the Extradition Clause of the United States Constitution, asserting that a person accused of a crime in one state can be legally transferred or surrendered to another state for prosecution. It provides a framework for the extradition process between states, ensuring cooperation in apprehending and returning fugitives to face trial.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90N.label: Reaffirmation Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90N.definition: A Reaffirmation Agreement is a legal agreement made in the context of bankruptcy proceedings, in which a debtor agrees to repay a debt that would otherwise be discharged in bankruptcy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90T.label: Uruguay Peso en Unidades Indexadas - URUIURUI Funds Code
english_labels: Uruguay Peso en Unidades Indexadas - URUIURUI Funds Code

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90V.label: Minnesota District Court - Fillmore County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90V.definition: Minnesota District Court - Fillmore County: A specific court within the Minnesota District Court system located in Fillmore County, responsible for administering legal proceedings within its jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90W.label: Intervention
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90W.definition: An Intervention is a legal action taken by a third party to become involved in a lawsuit between two other parties, typically to protect their own interests or rights.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90a.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Ray County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R90c.label: Motion to Enforce Judgment

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R91u.label: Adjustment of Status Application
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R91u.definition: The Adjustment of Status application, commonly referred to as Form I-485 in the United States, is used by eligible individuals who are already present in the U.S. on a non-immigrant visa and wish to apply for lawful permanent resident status (green card) without leaving the country. This process allows the applicant to transition from a temporary visa holder to a permanent resident without the need to undergo consular processing outside the U.S. The I-485 application requires various supporting documents and fees, and its approval results in the issuance of a green card, granting the applicant the right to live and work permanently in the U.S.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R94e.label: Inflammatory Arthritis

Clinically, inflammation of major joints in an upper or lower extremity may be the dominant manifestation causing difficulties with walking or fine and gross movements; there may be joint pain, swelling, and tenderness. The arthritis may affect other joints, or cause less limitation in walking or fine and gross movements. However, in combination with extra-articular features, including constitutional symptoms or signs (severe fatigue, fever, malaise and involuntary weight loss), inflammatory arthritis may result in an extreme limitation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R98N.label: Prostitution

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R98P.label: Covered Warrant
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R98P.definition: A Covered Warrant is a financial instrument issued by a third party that is not the issuer of the underlying securities to which the warrant refers. https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R98u.label: GED (General Educational Development)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R98u.definition: A GED (General Educational Development) is a high school equivalency credential earned by passing a series of exams. It signifies the attainment of knowledge and skills comparable to a high school graduate.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R99M.definition: Loss of visual efficiency, or visual impairment, in the better eye is characterized by a severe reduction in visual performance after the best possible correction has been applied. This ranking ensures that junior subordinated creditors are the last to be paid from the proceeds of the liquidated assets, providing them with the lowest level of security and the highest risk compared to other creditors.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R99y.label: Estoppel in Pais

The agreement outlines the terms under which financial products or services, such as insurance, mutual funds, or loans, will be marketed and distributed.

In mental health care and special education law, it emphasizes placing individuals in the least confining setting or using the least intrusive means necessary to meet their needs or ensure safety, balancing individual rights with societal concerns.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9C8.definition: Asset Sales Practice refers to the legal practice area that deals with the sale of assets, such as property or businesses, typically in the context of bankruptcy or restructuring proceedings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CA.definition: Noord-Holland: A province in the Netherlands, located in the northwestern part of the country.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CB.label: Waiver
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CB.definition: A waiver is a voluntary relinquishment or surrender of some known right, claim, or privilege, often documented in a formal, written statement. A waiver can also be a legal defense that can be used in civil litigation where a party intentionally relinquishes a known right or privilege. A waver is usually prospective (forward-looking), where a Release is usually retrospective (backward-looking).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CC.label: Interpreter
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CC.definition: A translator. Taniguchi v. Kan Pac. Saipan, Ltd., 566 U.S. 560 (2012)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CD.definition: The Office of Tax Policy is an agency of the United States Department of the Treasury headed by the Assistant Secretary of the Treasury for Tax Policy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CE.label: ERISA Advisory Council
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CE.definition: The duties of the ERISA Advisory Council are to advise the Secretary and submit recommendations regarding the Secretary's functions under ERISA.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CF.label: Georgia District Court - Treutlen County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CF.definition: A court located in Treutlen County, Georgia that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CF.label: Employee Rights Campaigns Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CF.definition: Employee Rights Campaigns Practice involves strategic efforts by labor unions and other worker advocacy groups to influence corporate behavior and policy, often through public relations, media, legal, and political pressure. These campaigns aim to improve working conditions, secure collective bargaining rights, and address labor-related grievances within corporations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CH.label: tax_summary segment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CH.definition: "Summarizes the taxes charged on this matter/invoice. There will be 0 or more TAX_SUMMARY segments per MATTER segment. Note that the EXTEND_HEADER option was purposely omitted from this segment. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CI.label: Contact Country
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CI.definition: Contact Country refers to the country where a person or entity is located or resides, and is a subcategory of Contact Information in the context of legal services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CP.label: Not Work Authorized
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CP.definition: In the context of immigration law, "Not Work Authorized" refers to an individual who does not have the legal permission to be employed in a specific country. Under U.S. law, individuals in certain visa categories or those without legal status are considered "not work authorized," and employers could face penalties for employing such individuals.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CP.label: Michigan Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CP.definition: The Michigan Circuit Court is a court of general jurisdiction in the state of Michigan that hears civil and criminal cases at the trial level.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CP.label: Audiobook
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CP.definition: An Audiobook is a spoken word recording of a book or other written material, narrated and often enhanced with sound effects or music, intended for playback on digital devices, CDs, or other media. Protected under copyright law, audiobooks grant the narrators and producers exclusive rights to reproduce, distribute, and publicly perform the recorded content.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CP.label: Motion to Compel Response
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CP.definition: A Motion to Compel Response is a formal request made to a court to require the opposing party to provide a response to a discovery request that has been previously made and not answered.
english_labels: Motion to Compel Response to Disclosure Request
Motion to Compel Response to Discovery

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CV.label: Interjurisdictional Child Custody and Jurisdiction Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CV.definition: An Interjurisdictional Child Custody and Jurisdiction Claim pertains to legal proceedings in cases involving child custody and which state's court has authority to make custody decisions. When parents live in different states, jurisdictional rules defined by the Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement Act (UCCJEA) or other relevant laws determine which state's court can handle the custody case. These claims are essential in ensuring that custody disputes are resolved appropriately and in compliance with interstate legal frameworks.
english_labels: Interjurisdictional Child Custody and Jurisdiction Claim
Interstate Child Custody and Jurisdiction Claim

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CV.label: Motion to Dismiss for Lack of Jurisdiction
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CV.definition: A Motion to Dismiss for Lack of Jurisdiction is a formal request made to a court to dismiss a case due to the court lacking the authority to hear and decide the matter at hand.
english_labels: Motion to Dismiss for Lack of Jurisdiction

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CZ.label: Engagement Identification
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9CZ.definition: Engagement Identification refers to the specific identification of a legal service engagement, including its name, description, invoice type, start date, and matter ID.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Cb.label: Firm Pricing Personnel
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Cb.definition: Firm Pricing Personnel refers to individuals within a legal service provider who are responsible for determining the pricing of services offered by the firm, and who are not involved in the direct provision of legal services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Cd.label: Deed of Trust
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Cd.definition: A Deed of Trust is a legal agreement that transfers the title of real property to a trustee as security for a loan between a borrower and a lender.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Cf.label: inv_id
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Cf.definition: "The law firm assigned invoice number or code. Multiple inv_id's can be billed in the same LEDES e-billing file. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Cj.label: Entrepreneurial Buyer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Cj.definition: An entrepreneurial buyer is an individual or entity that engages in mergers and acquisitions with the primary goal of acquiring a business to actively manage and grow. These buyers often possess industry-specific knowledge, skills, or experience that enable them to identify opportunities and add value to the target company. Unlike financially driven buyers who focus mainly on generating financial returns, entrepreneurial buyers are more likely to take a hands-on approach, seeking to build and develop the acquired business for the long term, often driven by a strategic vision or passion for the industry.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Cj.label: New York City Court - Yonkers
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Cj.definition: A court located in Yonkers, New York that operates under the jurisdiction of the New York City Court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Ck.label: Travel Document Number
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Ck.definition: A Travel Document Number refers to a unique identifier assigned to a travel document, such as a visa or refugee travel document, by the issuing authority. This number is used for verification and identification purposes during international travel and border crossings, and it is required for various legal and administrative processes related to travel.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Cn.label: Foreign Corporation Financial Disclosure
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Cn.definition: A Foreign Corporation Financial Disclosure, known in the U.S. as a Form 20-F, is an annual report submitted to the governmental entity (e.g., Securities and Exchange Commission) by foreign private issuers with securities listed on domestic (e.g., U.S.) exchanges. In the United States, the 20-F provides a comprehensive overview of the company's financial position and business operations, including audited financial statements, executive compensation, major shareholders, material risks, and other information required by the SEC.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Cp.label: Hodgkin Lymphoma
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Cp.definition: Hodgkin lymphoma is a type of cancer that originates in the lymphatic system, characterized by the presence of Reed-Sternberg cells. It typically begins in the lymph nodes and can spread to other organs, requiring specific treatment approaches distinct from those for non-Hodgkin lymphomas.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Cq.label: Probate Reason of Restoration
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Cq.definition: Probate Reason of Restoration refers to the legal basis for filing a subsequent probate case to restore a previously revoked or invalidated will or trust.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Cs.label: New Mexico Magistrate Court - Eddy County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Cs.definition: A court located in Eddy County, New Mexico that has limited jurisdiction over certain types of cases.
english_labels: New Mexico Magistrate Court - Eddy County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Cv.label: Non-Hearsay Document Objective
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Cv.definition: The non-hearsay document objective is the legal principle that certain documents are admissible as evidence in court without being considered hearsay, due to their inherent reliability. These documents, such as business records, public records, and learned treatises, are deemed trustworthy because they are created and maintained in the regular course of activities and are used for important purposes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Cw.label: Presentment Clause Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Cw.definition: A Presentment Clause claim refers to a legal argument challenging the constitutionality of a law based on the requirements outlined in the Presentment Clause of the United States Constitution. This claim asserts that a law is invalid because it was not properly presented to the President for signature or veto, violating the constitutional process for enacting legislation and potentially rendering it unconstitutional.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Cy.label: Friedreich’s Ataxia
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Cy.definition: Friedreich’s ataxia is a rare, inherited degenerative disorder that primarily affects the nervous system and the spinal cord. It is characterized by progressive loss of coordination, muscle weakness, and gait disturbances due to the degeneration of spinal cord pathways and cerebellum.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9D0.label: Corporate President
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9D0.definition: A Corporate President is a senior executive often responsible for overseeing the day-to-day operations of a company and implementing strategic initiatives set by the board of directors. The President often acts as the second-highest-ranking officer in a company, reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) or, in some cases, the board.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9D2.label: Assignability Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9D2.definition: An Assignability Clause is a provision in a contract that allows one party to transfer their rights and obligations to another party without the consent of the other party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9DC.label: Gender-Based Market Segment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9DC.definition: Gender-based market segments refer to divisions of the market that are categorized based on the gender of consumers. These segments allow businesses to tailor their products, services, and marketing strategies to cater to the specific needs, preferences, and behaviors of different gender groups, such as men, women, and non-binary individuals.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9DD.label: Loss Function
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9DD.definition: A Loss Function, also known as a Cost Function, is a mathematical function that provides a single metric to evaluate the performance of an AI model by quantifying the difference between predicted and actual values. The primary goal of training an AI system is to minimize the total loss over a set of validation examples, thereby improving the model's accuracy and effectiveness.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9DI.definition: Dakota (Language) is a specific written or spoken structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary, used in legal matters, and is a subcategory of the Language class.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9DJ.label: Contact Prior First Name
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9DJ.definition: Contact Prior First Name refers to the first name that an individual used before it was legally changed. This could be due to various reasons such as personal choice, religious conversion, or gender transition. When relevant, the prior first name may be included in formal documents or databases for identification or historical records.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Dv.label: 7th Amendment Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Dv.definition: A Seventh Amendment claim is a legal argument asserting that an individual's constitutional right to a trial by jury in civil cases, as guaranteed by the Seventh Amendment of the United States Constitution, has been violated.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Dx.label: Armed Services
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Dx.definition: Armed Services, or a Military Body, refers to the organized, trained, and equipped forces maintained by a state for national defense, security, and military operations. These forces are typically divided into distinct branches, each specializing in different domains of warfare and national security.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Dz.label: Virtual Data Room Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Dz.definition: Virtual Data Room Management refers to the process of securely managing and sharing confidential legal documents and information in a virtual environment, typically used in legal transactions and collaborations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9E2.label: "Hell or High Water" Antitrust Standard
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9E2.definition: The "Hell or High Water" Antitrust Standard is a legal concept that sets a high bar for proving antitrust violations, requiring evidence that the defendant engaged in conduct that would have been undertaken only in the face of an extreme, non-economic threat.
english_labels: Hell or High Water Antitrust Standard

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9E3.label: Zangilan
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9E3.definition: Zangilan is a geographic location in Azerbaijan.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9E6.label: Afrihili
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9E6.definition: Afrihili is a structured system of communication, belonging to the Language top-level class, that consists of grammar and vocabulary and is used in legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9E7.label: Money Had and Received
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9E7.definition: Money Had and Received is a legal claim that arises when one party has received money that rightfully belongs to another party, either through a contract or a quasi-contractual relationship.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9E7.label: Georgia District Court - Brooks County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9E7.definition: Georgia District Court - Brooks County: A court of law in the state of Georgia that has jurisdiction over legal cases within Brooks County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9E9.definition: Borsod-Abauj-Zemplen is a region in Hungary.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9E9.label: Zoning Map Amendments
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9E9.definition: Zoning Map Amendments involve the modification of an official zoning map, which visually represents land-use classifications within a jurisdiction. These changes can shift boundaries, reclassify areas, or add new zones and are generally subjected to public hearings, environmental reviews, and regulatory approvals.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9EA.label: Baja Verapaz
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9EA.definition: Baja Verapaz is a region in Guatemala.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9EB.definition: "An optional field assigned by the law firm to identify the firm. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9EE.label: Munda languages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9EE.definition: Munda languages are a group of languages that belong to the Austroasiatic language family and are spoken in parts of India and Bangladesh.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9EE.label: Emotional State of Patient Doctrine
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9EE.definition: Defendant does not have to provide information about risks where the information will so seriously upset the patient that the patient will be unable to reasonably consider the risks of refusing the procedure.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9EF.definition: Lai Chau is a province in Vietnam.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9EL.label: Minnesota District Court - Goodhue County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9EL.definition: The Minnesota District Court - Goodhue County is a specific court within the Minnesota District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Goodhue County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9EM.label: Conflict of Laws Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9EM.definition: A Conflict of Laws Clause is a provision in a contract that determines which jurisdiction's laws will apply in the event of a legal dispute between the parties involved.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9EN.label: Georgia District Court - Ware County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9EN.definition: Georgia District Court - Ware County: A specific court within the Georgia District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Ware County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9EO.label: Parent
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9EO.definition: A mother or father of a child. Lanier v. Traub, 934 F.2d 287 (11th Cir. 1991)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9EP.label: Credit Card Payment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9EP.definition: Credit Card Payment is a method of transferring funds through a credit card network, wherein the credit card holder authorizes the payment to a merchant. This form of payment is unsecured and reliant on the holder's credit limit.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9EP.label: Right to Counsel
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9EP.definition: The right to counsel refers to a fundamental legal principle that ensures individuals have access to legal representation, particularly during criminal proceedings. In the United States, this right is enshrined in the Sixth Amendment of the United States Constitution and guarantees that defendants facing criminal charges have the opportunity to be represented by an attorney, either privately retained or provided by the state if they cannot afford one, to protect their rights and ensure a fair trial.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9EP.label: Yoruba
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9EP.definition: A language spoken in Nigeria and Benin, belonging to the Niger-Congo language family.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9ER.label: At Will Employment Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9ER.definition: An "At Will Employment Clause" is a provision in a contract that allows either the employer or employee to terminate the employment relationship at any time, without cause or notice.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9EU.label: Consulting Services and Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9EU.definition: Consulting Services and Management refers to a range of professional services provided to legal organizations to improve their operations, processes, and technology, and to help them achieve their business goals.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9EV.label: Right to Privacy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9EV.definition: The right to privacy refers to the legal and ethical entitlement to personal autonomy and the protection of personal information from unauthorized access or disclosure. This right is often protected by international human rights law and national constitutions, and can extend to various domains including personal communications, medical records, and online activity.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Ec.label: Opposition / Reply
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Ec.definition: A written response to an argument or claim made by the opposing party in a legal case, typically filed in court and presented as evidence.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Ec.label: Sovereign Immunity
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Ec.definition: Sovereign immunity is a legal doctrine that protects governments and their agencies from being sued or held legally liable for their actions, without their consent. In the United States, this principle is rooted in the Eleventh Amendment of the Constitution, which provides states with immunity from certain types of lawsuits in federal courts, and is also applied to the federal government under the principle of federal sovereign immunity.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Ed.label: Arkansas Circuit Court - Jackson Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Ed.definition: The Arkansas Circuit Court - Jackson Cty. is a specific court within the Arkansas Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Jackson County, Arkansas.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Ee.definition: A court located in Duval County, Florida that is part of the Florida Circuit Court system and serves as a venue for legal proceedings within the 4th Circuit.
english_labels: Florida Circuit Court - Duval County - 4th Circuit Court

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Ek.label: Motion for Exemption from Financial Management Course
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Ek.definition: A Motion for Exemption from Financial Management Course is a request made in a bankruptcy case to be excused from completing a financial management course as required by law.
english_labels: Motion for Exemption from Financial Management Course

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9El.label: Georgia Superior Court - Franklin County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9El.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Franklin County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Franklin County.

english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Cass County (8th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Eq.label: Texas District Court - Tom Green County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Eq.definition: A court located in Tom Green County, Texas that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical boundaries.
english_labels: Texas District Court - Tom Green County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Es.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Jasper County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Es.definition: Indiana Circuit Court - Jasper County refers to a specific court within the Indiana Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Jasper County, Indiana.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Es.label: 310 Airplane (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Es.definition: Action alleging personal injury or wrongful death from an air crash or other occurrence involving an airplane. (Excludes airplane product liability claims)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Et.label: Buriat
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Et.definition: Buriat is a language spoken by the Buriat people in Russia and Mongolia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Ex.label: New York Supreme Court - Lewis County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Ex.definition: The New York Supreme Court - Lewis County is a court of general jurisdiction located in Lewis County, New York, which is a subdivision of the New York Supreme Court.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - Lewis County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Ey.label: General Terms and Conditions Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Ey.definition: A General Terms and Conditions Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the overall terms and conditions of the agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Ey.label: Florida Circuit Court - Polk County - 10th Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Ey.definition: A Florida Circuit Court located in Polk County that operates within the 10th Circuit Court jurisdiction.
english_labels: Florida Circuit Court - Polk County - 10th Circuit Court

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9F2.label: U.S. District Court - D. New Hampshire
english_labels: U.S. District Court - D. New Hampshire

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9F3.label: Souss-Massa-Draa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9F3.definition: Souss-Massa-Draa is a region in Morocco.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9F6.label: Sofia
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9F6.definition: Sofia (stolitsa) is the capital city of Bulgaria.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9F6.label: Superior Offer - Minimum Necessary Amount of Stock
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9F6.definition: A "Superior Offer - Minimum Necessary Amount of Stock" is a threshold concept in a legal matter that refers to the minimum amount of stock required for an offer to be considered superior to another offer.
english_labels: Superior Offer - Minimum Necessary Amount of Stock

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9F7.label: Fryslan
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9F7.definition: Fryslan is a region in the Netherlands.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9F8.label: Diyarbakir
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9F8.definition: Diyarbakir is a city in Turkey.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9F9.label: Executive, Legislative, and Other General Government Support Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9F9.definition: The Executive, Legislative, and Other General Government Support subsector groups offices of government executives, legislative bodies, public finance, and general government support.
english_labels: Executive, Legislative, and Other General Government Support Industry

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9FA.label: Ile-de-France
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9FA.definition: Ile-de-France is a region in France, located in the north-central part of the country.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9FA.label: Hhohho
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9FA.definition: Hhohho is a region in Swaziland, located in the northern part of the country.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9FB.label: Oplotnica
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9FB.definition: Oplotnica is a town located in Slovenia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9FB.label: Zardab
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9FB.definition: Zardab is a location in Azerbaijan.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9FC.label: Ayeyarwady
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9FC.definition: Ayeyarwady is a region in Myanmar.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9FD.label: Negotiable Instrument Signed for Accommodation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9FD.definition: A negotiable instrument signed for accommodation is a type of commercial paper that is endorsed by a third party as a favor to the borrower, and is used as a means of obtaining credit or financing.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9FE.label: Tovuz
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9FE.definition: Tovuz is a district in Azerbaijan.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9FL.label: Reduced Life Expectancy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9FL.definition: Reduced Life Expectancy: A type of non-economic damages in a legal matter where the plaintiff's life expectancy is shortened due to the defendant's actions or negligence.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9FM.label: Fractional Ownership Assets
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9FM.definition: Fractional Ownership Assets, such as timeshares, are assets that are owned by multiple individuals or entities, each holding a fraction of the ownership and entitled to use or benefit from the asset for a specific period. In the case of timeshares, owners typically have the right to use a vacation property for a set number of weeks each year, while sharing the costs and responsibilities of ownership and maintenance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9FN.label: De Facto Taking
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9FN.definition: The concept of De Facto Taking refers to a situation where the government takes private property without following the proper legal procedures for eminent domain or taking, resulting in the property owner being deprived of their rights without compensation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9FZ.label: Bankruptcy Chapter 9 Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9FZ.definition: A Bankruptcy Chapter 9 Claim is a type of claim made in a bankruptcy case filed under Chapter 9 of the Bankruptcy Code, which allows for the reorganization of municipalities and other governmental entities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9FZ.label: Florida Circuit Court - Putnam County - 7th Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9FZ.definition: A court located in Putnam County, Florida that operates within the jurisdiction of the 7th Circuit Court.
english_labels: Florida Circuit Court - Putnam County - 7th Circuit Court

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Fc.label: Indiana City Court - Elkhart County, Goshen City
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Fc.definition: A court located in Goshen City, Elkhart County, Indiana that has jurisdiction over cases within its geographical boundaries.
english_labels: Indiana City Court - Elkhart County, Goshen City

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Fh.label: Civilian Board of Contract Appeals
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Fh.definition: The Civilian Board of Contract Appeals (CBCA) is a specific administrative venue that resolves disputes between government contractors and agencies related to contract claims and disputes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Fi.label: Exclusive Use Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Fi.definition: An Exclusive Use Clause is a provision in a contract that grants one party the sole right to use a particular property or asset, prohibiting others from using it for a specified period of time.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Fj.label: Positive Advertisement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Fj.definition: A Positive Advertisement is a type of advertising that focuses on promoting the strengths, benefits, and positive attributes of a product, service, individual, or idea. These advertisements aim to build a favorable image, encourage consumer engagement, and highlight the desirable aspects of what is being advertised.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Fl.label: Notice Provision Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Fl.definition: A Notice Provision Clause is a specific type of Contractual Clause that requires one party to provide written notification to the other party in the event of certain circumstances, such as a breach of contract or termination of the agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Fo.label: Separation from Bed and Board
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Fo.definition: A legal concept falling under Family Law and Matrimonial Claims, Separation from Bed and Board refers to a court-ordered separation of a married couple where they live apart but remain legally married.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Fu.label: Texas District Court - Smith County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Fu.definition: A Texas District Court located in Smith County, which is a trial court of general jurisdiction in Texas, responsible for hearing civil and criminal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Fy.label: Fiduciary's Misappropriation of Funds
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Fy.definition: The wrongful taking or misuse of funds by a person who has a legal or ethical duty to manage and protect those funds, such as a trustee or executor.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9G2.label: Proposed Conclusions of Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9G2.definition: Proposed Conclusions of Law refer to the legal arguments and opinions presented by parties in a court case, outlining their interpretation of the law and how it applies to the facts of the case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9G3.label: LGBTQ+ Market Segment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9G3.definition: The gay lifestyle market refers to a division of the market that is specifically targeted towards the LGBTQ+ community, focusing on products and services that cater to the needs, preferences, and interests of gay individuals and couples. This segment encompasses a wide range of offerings, from community events to specialized products, all designed to support and celebrate the gay lifestyle.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9G5.label: Patent Infringement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9G5.definition: The unauthorized use, manufacture, sale, or importation of a patented invention or process, which is protected by law and owned by someone else.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9G7.label: Credit and Loan Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9G7.definition: A Credit and Loan Agreement is a legally binding contract between a lender and a borrower that outlines the terms and conditions for the provision of credit or a loan. The agreement specifies key details such as the amount borrowed, interest rate, repayment schedule, and any collateral required, among other terms.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9GC.label: Tire Tread Evidence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9GC.definition: Tire tread evidence encompasses the patterns and impressions left by vehicle tires on surfaces. By analyzing these marks, forensic experts can determine the type, brand, and sometimes specific wear characteristics of the tire, potentially linking a vehicle to a crime scene.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9GE.label: Tax Point Date
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9GE.definition: Tax Point Date refers to the specific date on which a taxable event occurs for the purpose of calculating taxes, and is a subcategory of Fee Invoice Detail within the context of Engagement Terms.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9GG.label: Government Guarantee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9GG.definition: A Government Guarantee is a formal assurance provided by a governmental entity to support the fulfillment of financial obligations associated with a debt instrument or investment. This guarantee serves as a pledge that the government will assume responsibility for repayment if the primary obligor defaults, thereby enhancing the security and creditworthiness of the guaranteed instrument.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9GH.label: Aphonia
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9GH.definition: Aphonia is the complete loss of voice resulting from the inability to produce vocal sounds through the vocal cords, resulting in the inability to produce speech that can be heard, understood, or sustained. This condition can be caused by various factors, including severe laryngitis, vocal cord paralysis, trauma to the larynx, or neurological disorders.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9GM.label: JH10 Own expert evidence (UK J-CODE)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9GM.definition: Identifying and interviewing experts and consultants (testifying or non-testifying), working with them, and developing expert reports. Reviewing case in the light of such evidence. Considering questions asked by Other Party(s) of own experts and experts' responses. Arranging experts' discussions. Considering reports of experts' discussions. Includes all communications or other work with counsel, and all communications with Other Party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9GO.label: DEPRECATED Debtor Claims Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9GO.definition: A debtor claims practice is a deprecated concept related to the legal process of making claims against a debtor.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9GQ.label: Construction Site Negligence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9GQ.definition: Construction Site Negligence refers to the failure of a construction company or its employees to exercise reasonable care in maintaining a safe work environment, resulting in harm or injury to workers or others on the construction site.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9GR.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Gibson County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9GR.definition: Indiana Circuit Court - Gibson County refers to a specific court within the Indiana Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Gibson County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9GW.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Jefferson County (2nd Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Jefferson County (2nd Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Ga.label: Castle Doctrine Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Ga.definition: A Castle Doctrine Claim refers to a legal principle that allows a person to use force, including deadly force, in defense of their home or dwelling without the duty to retreat. This doctrine is based on the premise that one's home is their castle, and they have the right to protect it and its occupants from intruders or attackers.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Gg.label: Paraplegia
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Gg.definition: Paraplegia is a type of mobility disability characterized by the partial or complete paralysis of the lower half of the body, including both legs. This condition typically results from spinal cord injuries or diseases affecting the thoracic, lumbar, or sacral regions of the spine, leading to loss of motor and sensory function below the level of injury.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Gg.label: Motion to File Oversized Petition for Rehearing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Gg.definition: A Motion to File Oversized Petition for Rehearing is a request to submit a petition for rehearing that exceeds the standard size limit set by the court, typically due to the complexity of the case or the amount of evidence presented.
english_labels: Motion to File Oversized Petition for Rehearing

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Gh.label: International Annual Report
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Gh.definition: An International Annual Report is an annual report of a foreign company listed on a domestic stock exchange. In the United States, Form 40-F is an annual report filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission by Canadian issuers to register securities under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. The 40-F serves as a combined annual report and registration statement, providing key financial statements, management discussion and analysis, and detailed business information. It helps meet SEC disclosure requirements for foreign private issuers accessing U.S. capital markets.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Gi.label: Trademark Renewal Process
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Gi.definition: The trademark renewal process is a legal procedure that allows the owner of a registered trademark to extend the protection of the trademark beyond its initial term. This process typically involves submitting a renewal application and paying the required fees before the expiration of the current registration period.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Gi.label: Georgia District Court - Walker County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Gi.definition: Georgia District Court - Walker County: A specific court within the Georgia District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Walker County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Gl.label: Limited Conservatorship of Adult
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Gl.definition: A Limited Conservatorship of Adult is a legal arrangement in which a conservator is appointed to manage the personal and/or financial affairs of an adult with developmental disabilities who is unable to fully care for themselves, but only to the extent necessary to provide for their basic needs and protect them from harm.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Gq.label: Primary Metal Manufacturing Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Gq.definition: Industries in the Primary Metal Manufacturing subsector smelt and/or refine ferrous and nonferrous metals from ore, pig, or scrap, using electrometallurgical and other process metallurgical techniques. Establishments in this subsector also manufacture metal alloys and superalloys by introducing other chemical elements to pure metals. The output of smelting and refining, usually in ingot form, is used in rolling, drawing, and extruding operations to make sheet, strip, bar, rod, or wire, and in molten form to make castings and other basic metal products. Primary manufacturing of ferrous and nonferrous metals begins with ore or concentrate as the primary input. Establishments manufacturing primary metals from ore and/or concentrate remain classified in the primary smelting, primary refining, or iron and steel mill industries regardless of the form of their output. Establishments primarily engaged in secondary smelting and/or secondary refining recover ferrous and nonferrous metals from scrap and/or dross. The output of the secondary smelting and/or secondary refining industries is limited to shapes such as ingot or billet that will be further processed. Recovery of metals from scrap often occurs in establishments that are primarily engaged in activities, such as rolling, drawing, extruding, or similar processes. Excluded from the Primary Metal Manufacturing subsector are establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing ferrous and nonferrous forgings (except ferrous forgings made in steel mills) and stampings. Although forging, stamping, and casting are all methods used to make metal shapes, forging and stamping do not use molten metals and are included in Subsector 332, Fabricated Metal Product Manufacturing. Establishments primarily engaged in operating coke ovens are classified in Industry 32419, Other Petroleum and Coal Products Manufacturing.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Gr.label: Dead
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Gr.definition: Dead refers to the state of an individual who has ceased to live and has no vital signs or brain activity.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Gy.label: Investor Questionnaire
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Gy.definition: An Investor Questionnaire in a legal and financial context is a structured document consisting of a series of questions designed to gather specific information from the respondent. It is often used for due diligence purposes, like in Bad Actor Questionnaires to assess regulatory compliance, or FINRA Questionnaires to evaluate suitability for financial industry roles.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Gz.label: Employer's Failure to Obtain Workers' Compensation Insurance Policy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9Gz.definition: The failure of an employer to obtain an insurance policy that provides benefits to employees who suffer work-related injuries or illnesses.
english_labels: Employer's Failure to Obtain Workers' Compensation Insurance Policy

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9H0.label: Multi-National Governmental Body
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9H0.definition: A Multi-National Governmental Body refers to an organization formed by a coalition of multiple nations, primarily to address collective concerns, facilitate diplomatic relations, or coordinate actions in various fields. These entities operate based on treaties or agreements and often have a governing structure, legal personality, and set jurisdictions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9H2.label: U.S. Code of Federal Regulations
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9H2.definition: Rules or orders issued by a United States governmental regulatory agency and having the force of law.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9H4.label: Penalty Proceeding
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9H4.definition: A penalty proceeding is a legal process that deals specifically with the determination and imposition of punishment for a criminal offense.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9H8.label: Broadcast Timing Attributes
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9H8.definition: Broadcast Timing Attributes refer to the characteristics that define the timing of broadcast transmissions, distinguishing between content that is delivered in real-time and content that is pre-recorded and scheduled for later playback. These attributes categorize broadcasts into synchronous (live) and asynchronous (pre-recorded) transmissions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9H9.label: Separated
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9H9.definition: Separated (Marital Status) refers to the legal status of a married couple who are no longer living together but have not yet obtained a divorce.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9H9.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Clay County (4th Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Clay County (4th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9HB.label: Failure to Mediate
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9HB.definition: The concept of Failure to Mediate refers to a civil defense in litigation where one party fails to participate in mediation, which is a process of resolving disputes outside of court with the help of a neutral third party.
