https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9lZ.definition: A bill of costs is a detailed statement of expenses incurred during a legal case, including court fees, witness fees, and other costs, which is submitted to the court for reimbursement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9le.label: Jute
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9le.definition: Jute is a long, soft, and shiny vegetable fiber that can be spun into coarse, strong threads, widely used for making burlap, hessian, and other packaging materials. Known for its eco-friendly properties, jute is one of the most affordable natural fibers and is predominantly grown in regions with warm and humid climates.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9lf.label: Market Intelligence Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9lf.definition: Market Intelligence Management is the process of gathering and analyzing information about a specific market or industry, with the goal of making informed business decisions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9li.label: Project Schedule
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9li.definition: The timing of activities necessary to complete the deliverables.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9li.label: Motion to Continue Hearing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9li.definition: A Motion to Continue Hearing is a formal request made to a court to postpone a scheduled hearing or trial to a later date.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9ll.label: Texas District Court - Grayson County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9ll.definition: A Texas District Court located in Grayson County, which is a trial court of general jurisdiction in Texas, handling civil and criminal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9lu.label: Child Neglect Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9lu.definition: A Child Neglect Claim is a legal action brought against a parent or guardian for failing to provide adequate care and support for a child, falling under the broader category of Dependency Claims.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9m5.label: 720 Labor/Management Relations (Union) (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9m5.definition: Action relating to disputes between labor unions and employers as well as all petitions regarding actions of the Nation Labor Relations Board (NLRB)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9m7.label: Action to Quiet Title
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9m7.definition: An Action to Quiet Title is a legal claim brought to establish clear and undisputed ownership of a property, and to remove any clouds or challenges to the title.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9m8.label: Discovery and Evidentiary Defenses
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9m8.definition: Discovery and Evidentiary Defenses: Legal arguments and strategies used by a party in a civil litigation case to challenge the admissibility or relevance of evidence obtained through the discovery process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9mA.label: Federal Trade Commission Act Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9mA.definition: A Federal Trade Commission Act Claim is a legal claim that alleges a violation of the laws and regulations enforced by the Federal Trade Commission, which is responsible for protecting consumers from unfair or deceptive business practices.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9mB.label: Charges Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9mB.definition: A charges clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the fees or costs that one party may charge the other party for specific services or actions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9mC.label: Custodial Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9mC.definition: A Custodial Agreement is a contract where a financial institution, often a bank, agrees to hold and safeguard an individual's or entity's financial assets. The custodian may also provide additional services like account administration, transaction settlements, and tax support.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9mE.label: Client Passport Number
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9mE.definition: Client Passport Number refers to the unique identification number assigned to an individual's passport by the issuing government. This number is used to verify the passport's authenticity and can be required for various legal, travel, or identification purposes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9mQ.label: Mapudungun; Mapuche
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9mQ.definition: A language spoken by the Mapuche people in Chile and Argentina, characterized by its unique grammar and vocabulary.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9mR.label: Sami languages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9mR.definition: Sami languages are a group of languages that are spoken by the Sami people in northern Europe, including Norway, Sweden, Finland, and Russia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9mS.label: Pornography and Obscene Material
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9mS.definition: The violation of laws or ordinances prohibiting the manufacture, publishing, sale, purchase, or possession of sexually explicit material, e.g., literature, photographs, etc.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9mV.label: North Atlantic Treaty Organization
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9mV.definition: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) is a military alliance established in 1949, consisting of North American and European countries, formed to ensure mutual defense and security against external threats. NATO operates under a system of collective defense, whereby an attack against one member is considered an attack against all members, as outlined in Article 5 of the NATO treaty.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9mZ.label: Motion to Extend Exclusivity Period
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9mZ.definition: A Motion to Extend Exclusivity Period is a request made in a bankruptcy case to prolong the time during which a debtor has the exclusive right to propose a reorganization plan, thereby preventing competing plans from being proposed.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9md.label: Interested Party
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9md.definition: A person or entity who is interested in a legal proceeding - without necessarily being a party to that legal proceeding. https://www.ca11.uscourts.gov/e-filing/notices-cases-interest

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9mf.label: Bail Payment Event
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9mf.definition: A Bail Payment is the financial transaction made to secure the temporary release of an accused individual from custody, usually in the form of cash, bond, or property, which is pledged to guarantee their appearance at future court dates. This payment acts as a surety that the defendant will return for trial and may be forfeited if the individual fails to appear in court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9mh.label: Mortgagee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9mh.definition: A Mortgagee is the lender in a mortgage transaction, typically a bank or financial institution, that provides funds for the borrower (mortgagor) to purchase property. The mortgagee holds a lien on the property as security for the loan repayment and can foreclose on the property if the borrower fails to meet the terms of the mortgage.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9mm.label: Arkansas Circuit Court - Independence Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9mm.definition: Arkansas Circuit Court - Independence County is a specific court within the Arkansas Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Independence County, Arkansas.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9mm.label: Billable
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9mm.definition: The term "Billable" refers to whether a legal service provider can charge a client for time spent or tasks completed on the client's behalf. This concept encompasses activities that are directly related to delivering legal services and are eligible for invoicing.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9mz.label: Failure to Obtain Auto Insurance
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9mz.definition: The failure of an individual to obtain automobile insurance as required by law.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9n7.label: Good Faith Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9n7.definition: A Good Faith Clause is a provision in a contract that requires the parties to act honestly and fairly towards each other in their dealings, and to refrain from taking advantage of one another.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9n8.label: Kumyk
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9n8.definition: Kumyk is a language that belongs to the Turkic language family and is spoken primarily in the Dagestan Republic of Russia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9n8.label: Commutation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9n8.definition: Commutation is the reduction of a punishment or sentence for a crime, usually from a more severe form to a lesser one, without negating the underlying conviction. Unlike a pardon, which absolves the individual of the crime, a commutation typically pertains to reducing the length of a prison sentence or changing the type of punishment, but the conviction remains on the individual's record.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9nB.label: Anorexia Nervosa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9nB.definition: Anorexia Nervosa is an eating disorder characterized by an intense fear of gaining weight and a distorted body image leading to severe food restriction and extreme weight loss. Individuals with this disorder may also engage in excessive exercise, purging, or other behaviors to prevent weight gain.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9nJ.label: Indiana Superior Court - Morgan County, Superior Court1
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9nJ.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Morgan County, Indiana, with authority to hear and decide a wide range of legal disputes and cases.
english_labels: Indiana Superior Court - Morgan County, Superior Court1

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9nK.label: Judgment As a Matter of Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9nK.definition: Judgment As a Matter of Law (JAML) is a legal decision made by a judge based on the evidence presented in a case, rather than being left to the jury to decide.
english_labels: Judgment As a Matter of Law

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9nM.label: Analysis of Dischargeability Issues
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9nM.definition: The Analysis of Dischargeability Issues is the examination and evaluation of whether a particular debt can be eliminated through bankruptcy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9nN.label: Collective Bargaining Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9nN.definition: A Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) is a legally binding contract negotiated between a labor union or employee association and an employer or group of employers. It outlines the terms and conditions of employment for the represented workers, covering aspects such as wages, working hours, benefits, workplace conditions, and dispute resolution procedures.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9nO.label: Klingon; tlhIngan-Hol
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9nO.definition: A constructed language created for the Star Trek franchise, spoken by the fictional Klingon species and used in various media and fan communities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9nO.label: Option to Extend Lease Term Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9nO.definition: An Option to Extend Lease Term Clause is a provision in a contract that grants one or both parties the right to extend the lease agreement for a specified period of time beyond the original lease term.
english_labels: Option to Extend Lease Term Clause

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9nO.label: Legal Management Consulting Services
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9nO.definition: Legal Management Consulting Services refers to the provision of expert advice and guidance to legal organizations and professionals on matters related to business management and strategy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9nQ.label: Washington Superior Court - King County District Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9nQ.definition: A court located in King County, Washington that has jurisdiction over certain types of cases within its district.
english_labels: Washington Superior Court - King County District Court

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9nS.label: Effective Date of Resignation Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9nS.definition: An Effective Date of Resignation Clause is a provision in a contract that specifies the date on which a resignation will become effective.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9nT.label: Thai
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9nT.definition: Thai (Language) is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary used in Thailand and by Thai speakers worldwide.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9nb.label: Blind and Shade Manufacturing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9nb.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing one or more of the following: venetian blinds, other window blinds, and shades; curtain and drapery rods and poles; and/or curtain and drapery fixtures. The blinds and shades may be made on a stock or custom basis and may be made of any material.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9nj.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Taney County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9nj.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Taney County is a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Taney County, Missouri.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9nn.label: Motion for Relief Because No Longer Equitable
english_labels: Motion for Relief Because No Longer Equitable

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9no.label: Real Right of Pledge
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9no.definition: The Real Right of Pledge is a security interest that allows a creditor to hold a tangible asset or property as collateral to secure a debt or obligation from the debtor. In the event of default, the creditor has the right to seize and potentially sell the pledged property to satisfy the debt, subject to the rules and procedures outlined in the governing law.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9o0.label: U.S. Executive Branch
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9o0.definition: The U.S. Executive Branch is the division of the federal government responsible for enforcing laws and administering public policy, headed by the President of the United States. It comprises the President, Vice President, Cabinet members, and federal agencies and departments.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9o2.label: Personal Goods
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9o2.definition: Often considered in Bankruptcy Proceedings, Personal Goods are movable, tangible objects owned by an individual and primarily used for personal, household, or everyday living purposes. They are distinct from real property (real estate) and intellectual property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9o4.label: New York Supreme Court - Orleans County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9o4.definition: The New York Supreme Court - Orleans County is a court of general jurisdiction located in Orleans County, New York, with authority to hear and decide a wide range of legal disputes within its geographic jurisdiction.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - Orleans County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9o6.label: Release from Active Duty
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9o6.definition: The concept of "Release from Active Duty" refers to the legal objective of obtaining a discharge from military service, and the associated legal and professional frameworks that support this goal within the context of bankruptcy and restructuring.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9o6.label: Motion to Sever
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9o6.definition: Seeks to sever claims and/or parties into separate proceedings

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9o8.label: Active Investor Disclosure
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9o8.definition: An Active Investor Disclosure is a document filed by investors who hold a significant stake in a company and intend to actively influence or control its management or operations. This disclosure is required by regulatory authorities to ensure transparency about the intentions of major shareholders and to monitor their potential impact on the company's governance and strategic direction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9oK.label: Cooperation Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9oK.definition: A Cooperation Agreement is a legally binding document that outlines the terms and conditions of a collaborative effort between two or more parties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9oT.label: Partner
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9oT.definition: A partner is an individual who is a member of a partnership - an entity formed when at least two or more individuals agree to go into business with one another.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9oT.label: Housing Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9oT.definition: A Housing Court is a specialized court forum that has jurisdiction over cases related to housing disputes and issues.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9oT.label: Agreement in Principle Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9oT.definition: An Agreement in Principle Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the basic terms and conditions of an agreement that has not yet been finalized.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9oa.label: Fingerprint Evidence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9oa.definition: Fingerprint evidence involves the collection, analysis, and comparison of the unique patterns found on human fingers. Because every individual has a unique set of fingerprints, they can serve as a reliable means of identification. When fingerprints are recovered from a crime scene, they can be compared to known prints in a database or from suspects to establish a match. The accuracy and reliability of fingerprint evidence have made it a fundamental tool in criminal investigations and forensic science for over a century.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9on.label: Utility Patent Assets
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9on.definition: Utility Patent Assets are a specific type of patent asset that refers to the exclusive rights granted to an inventor or assignee for a specific period of time to make, use, and sell an invention.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9oq.label: Vacation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9oq.definition: A Vacation, or Holiday, is a period of time taken off from work or regular activities for rest, relaxation, or travel. This planned absence from routine duties is typically paid time off for employees, allowing for leisure activities, personal pursuits, or extended breaks from professional responsibilities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9oz.label: Indemnification Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9oz.definition: An Indemnification Clause is a provision in a contract that requires one party to compensate the other for any losses or damages incurred as a result of the contract or a related transaction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9p1.label: Prompt Engineering
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9p1.definition: Prompt Engineering is the process of designing and crafting prompts for AI models to elicit desired outputs. It involves understanding the capabilities of the model and tailoring the prompt to guide the model effectively toward generating relevant, informative, and creative responses.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9p2.label: Vexatious Litigant
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9p2.definition: A party who has abused the court system by filing too many frivolous lawsuits may be prohibited from filing another suit or matter.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9p2.label: Forward-looking MAE Application - "Adverse impact on ability to consummate" Language
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9p2.definition: The "Adverse impact on ability to consummate" Language refers to a provision in a legal agreement that outlines the potential negative effects on the ability to complete a transaction, and is part of the Forward-looking Material Adverse Effect (MAE) Standard.
english_labels: "Adverse impact on ability to consummate" Language
Forward-looking MAE Application - "Adverse impact on ability to consummate" Language

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9p3.label: account_type
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9p3.definition: "An identifier indicating whether an invoice is ""own account"" (""O""), or ""third party"" (""T""). "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9p9.label: Advisory Service
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9p9.definition: Any process that provides advice to a single party without adversarial event.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pC.label: Negligent Manslaughter
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pC.definition: The killing of another person through negligence.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pD.label: Mergers and Acquisitions Documents
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pD.definition: Mergers and Acquisitions Documents are written or recorded representations of agreements and disclosures related to the purchase or merger of companies.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pJ.label: Repair and Maintenance Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pJ.definition: Industries in the Repair and Maintenance industry group restore machinery, equipment, and other products to working order. These establishments also typically provide general or routine maintenance (i.e., servicing) on such products to ensure they work efficiently and to prevent breakdown and unnecessary repairs.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pQ.label: Enforcement of Judgment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pQ.definition: The enforcement of judgment refers to the legal process of ensuring that a court's decision is carried out, often through methods such as seizing assets or placing liens on property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pV.label: Codicil
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pV.definition: A Codicil is a legal document that amends, rather than replaces, a previously executed will. It allows an individual to make changes or additions to their existing will without drafting an entirely new one, ensuring that certain provisions are updated or altered while the remainder of the will stays intact.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pW.label: Term of Agreement Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pW.definition: A Term of Agreement Clause is a provision in a contract that specifies the duration of the agreement and the conditions under which it can be terminated.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pW.label: Washington Superior Court - King County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pW.definition: Washington Superior Court - King County is a specific court within the Washington Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within King County, Washington.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pc.label: Space Force
english_labels: A Space Force is a military branch dedicated to space warfare and space operations, responsible for developing, maintaining, and operating space-based assets for national security and military purposes. This organization focuses on protecting a nation's interests in space, supporting other military branches with space-based capabilities, and potentially conducting offensive and defensive operations in the space domain.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pd.label: Callable Asset
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pd.definition: A Callable Asset is a financial instrument that can be redeemed or repaid by the issuer before its specified maturity date, at the issuer's discretion. This feature allows the issuer to take advantage of favorable interest rate movements or other financial conditions, often resulting in the repayment of the principal and cessation of interest payments prior to the original maturity date.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pj.label: Right to Indemnification Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pj.definition: A Right to Indemnification Clause is a provision in a contract that requires one party to compensate and defend the other party against any losses or damages incurred as a result of the contract, even if the losses or damages were caused by the indemnified party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pm.label: Energy Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pm.definition: Law concerned with creating, enforcing and challenging laws that regulate energy use.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pr.label: PO_NUMBER
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pr.definition: A PO_NUMBER is a unique identifier assigned to a purchase order within the LEDES98BI V5 Format Rev 1-2020 standard.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9ps.label: Commercial Paper
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9ps.definition: Commercial paper is an unsecured, short-term debt instrument issued by a corporation, typically for the financing of accounts payable and inventories and meeting short-term liabilities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pt.label: Buyout Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pt.definition: A buyout clause is a provision in a contract that allows one party to purchase the rights or assets of another party under certain conditions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pu.label: Orthopedic Surgery Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pu.definition: Negligent or improper conduct by a medical professional specializing in orthopedic surgery, resulting in harm or injury to the patient.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pv.label: INVOICE_DATE
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pv.definition: The INVOICE_DATE concept refers to the specific date on which an invoice was issued, as defined within the LEDES98BI V5 Format Rev 1-2020 standard.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pw.label: Jury
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pw.definition: A body of persons (jurors) temporarily selected from a jurisdiction's citizenry that is invested with power to present or indict a person for a public offense or to try a question of fact.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pz.label: Motion to Extend Time to File Amended Complaint
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9pz.definition: A Motion to Extend Time to File Amended Complaint is a request made to the court to allow a party to have more time to submit a revised version of their initial complaint.
english_labels: Motion to Extend Time to File Amended Complaint

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9q0.label: Insurance Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9q0.definition: Insurance Claims: A legal demand made by an insured party to an insurance company for compensation or coverage for a loss or damage that is covered by the insurance policy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9q2.label: 376 Qui Tam (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9q2.definition: Action brought under the False Claims Act by private persons (also known as "whistleblowers") on their own behalf and on behalf of the United States to recover damages against another person or entity that acted fraudulently in receiving payments or property from, or avoiding debts owed to, the United States Government, 31 U.S.C. § 3730

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9q3.label: Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9q3.definition: OSCE (Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe): The world's largest security-oriented intergovernmental organization, whose mandate includes issues such as arms control and the promotion of human rights, freedom of the press, and fair elections.
english_labels: Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9q4.label: Operating Report
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9q4.definition: An Operating Report is a type of Report that is specifically related to Bankruptcy and Restructuring Document, providing information on the financial and operational status of a company during the bankruptcy process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9q6.label: Par
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9q6.definition: Par refers to the face value of a financial instrument, such as a bond or loan, at the time of issuance or redemption. It is the nominal value that does not account for interest rates or market fluctuations

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9q6.label: Indiana Superior Court - Lawrence County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9q6.definition: Indiana Superior Court - Lawrence County: A court of general jurisdiction in Indiana that has the authority to hear and decide a wide range of legal cases within Lawrence County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9q7.label: Litigation Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9q7.definition: Demand or assertion seeking money, property, or enforcement of another right as provided by law.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qK.label: New York Supreme Court - Cortland County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qK.definition: The New York Supreme Court - Cortland County is a court of general jurisdiction in the state of New York, with authority to hear and decide a wide range of legal disputes within its geographic jurisdiction.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - Cortland County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qN.label: Inactive Employment Status
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qN.definition: Inactive Employment refers to a temporary or prolonged period during which an employee remains on the payroll but is not actively performing job duties. This can occur for various reasons such as medical leave, furlough, or sabbatical, and usually entails a change in benefits or compensation during the inactive period.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qP.label: Petitioning Creditor
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qP.definition: A creditor who initiates an involuntary bankruptcy by filing an involuntary petition, which can be filed against an individual or business. 11 US Code § 303

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qS.label: Data Protection Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qS.definition: A Data Protection Agreement is a contract that outlines the terms and conditions under which personal data will be processed, stored, and protected. It's especially relevant in jurisdictions with strict data protection laws, ensuring that both parties are aware of and comply with their obligations to protect personal data from breaches and unauthorized access.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qW.label: Gifts Inter Vivos
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qW.definition: Gifts Inter Vivos: A legal term referring to gifts made during the lifetime of the donor, which are irrevocable and are not subject to probate upon the donor's death, and are often used as a means of reducing estate taxes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qW.label: Mutual Indemnification Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qW.definition: A Mutual Indemnification Clause is a provision in a contract where both parties agree to protect and compensate each other against any losses, damages, or liabilities that may arise from the agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qW.label: Asset-Based Lending Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qW.definition: Asset-Based Lending Practice involves legal work related to providing loans secured by a borrower's assets, such as inventory, accounts receivable, or equipment. This practice includes drafting and negotiating loan agreements, conducting due diligence on collateral, and ensuring compliance with relevant laws and regulations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qY.label: Right to Nationality
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qY.definition: The right to nationality is a fundamental human right that ensures individuals have a legal membership in a sovereign state, often signified by citizenship. This right is protected by international treaties like the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and aims to prevent statelessness, which can result in the loss of basic rights and protections.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qZ.label: Project Management Risk
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qZ.definition: The threats and opportunities associated with an organization's process and practice of developing and managing major projects in support of its overall mandate, as well as risks associated with specific projects that may require ongoing management. This includes negative outcomes stemming from an organization's inability to effectively plan, execute, and control its projects or initiatives. Causes can include poor project planning, inadequate resource allocation, scope creep, or ineffective communication. And this risk can potentially lead to delays, cost overruns, unmet objectives, or diminished quality, ultimately impacting the organization's overall performance, reputation, and success.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qc.label: Coptic
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qc.definition: A language that was spoken in Egypt from the 2nd to the 17th century AD, characterized by its use of the Coptic alphabet derived from the Greek alphabet.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qe.label: Retail Real Estate Asset
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qe.definition: Real estate retail properties including malls, stores, and restaurants.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qh.label: Rule of Construction Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qh.definition: A Rule of Construction Clause is a provision in a contract that helps interpret the meaning of other clauses within the same contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qh.label: Idea-Expression Distinction
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qh.definition: The Idea-Expression Dichotomy in copyright law distinguishes between ideas, which are free for all to use, and the expression of those ideas, which may be protected. This principle asserts that copyright does not extend to ideas, procedures, concepts, or methods of operation, but only to their particular expression.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qi.label: Possessing Stolen Property
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qi.definition: The concept of Possessing Stolen Property refers to the criminal offense of knowingly having control over property that has been unlawfully taken from another person, without the owner's consent.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qi.label: Reorganization Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qi.definition: Reorganization Agreement is a contract detailing the terms and conditions of a corporate reorganization, including mergers, acquisitions, or other structural changes. This agreement outlines the rights of stakeholders and procedures for the reorganization.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qj.label: Transportation Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qj.definition: Law involving transportation infrastructure and all forms of road, railway, water and air transport.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qo.label: New York City Court - Tonawanda
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qo.definition: A court located in Tonawanda, New York, which is a subdivision of the New York City Court system.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qp.label: Santali
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qp.definition: Santali is a language that belongs to the Language top-level class and is spoken by a significant number of people in India, Bangladesh, and Nepal.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qt.label: Organizational Board Roles
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9qt.definition: Organizational Board Roles refer to the positions and responsibilities assigned to individuals on a board of directors, including governance, oversight, and strategic planning functions. These roles are designed to ensure effective leadership, compliance, and decision-making within an organization.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9r2.label: Spoken Word Recording
english_labels: A Spoken Word Recording is an audio capture of spoken performances, such as speeches, poetry, audiobooks, or podcasts, stored in a medium that can be played back.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9r6.label: Strict Confidentiality Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9r6.definition: A strict confidentiality clause is a provision in a contract that requires the parties involved to keep certain information confidential and not disclose it to third parties without prior consent.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9r6.label: Georgia District Court - Thomas County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9r6.definition: A court located in Thomas County, Georgia that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9r7.label: Disgust
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9r7.definition: Disgust is a strong emotion of revulsion or profound disapproval aroused by something unpleasant or offensive.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rA.label: Document Version
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rA.definition: Attributes of a document's version (e.g., version 2, version modified date, version description, version title).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rC.label: Bring-down of Representations and Warranties
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rC.definition: Representations and Warranties are statements made by a party in a legal matter regarding the accuracy and completeness of certain facts or conditions, which are relied upon by the other party, and may be subject to legal remedies if found to be untrue.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rC.label: Russian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rC.definition: Russian (Language) is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary used in legal matters, including documents, artifacts, evidence, testimony, proceedings, or any other legal aspect.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rC.label: Insolvent Buyer Having Bought Goods
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rC.definition: An Insolvent Buyer Having Bought Goods refers to a legal claim arising from a situation where a buyer who is unable to pay for goods purchased becomes insolvent, and the seller seeks to recover the value of the goods sold.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rE.label: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rE.definition: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a neurological disorder characterized by persistent patterns of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity that interfere with functioning or development. ADHD affects both children and adults, leading to challenges in academic, occupational, and social settings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rE.label: Cost Shifting and Fee Shifting
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rE.definition: Cost Shifting and Fee Shifting refers to the legal practice of transferring the responsibility of paying litigation costs or attorney fees from one party to another, typically as a result of a court order or settlement agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rH.label: Exchange Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rH.definition: An Exchange Agreement is a contract in which parties agree to exchange assets, securities, or other items of value. These agreements often detail the specific items being exchanged, their values, and any terms or conditions pertinent to the exchange process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rI.label: JB20 Budgeting - Precedent H (UK J-CODE)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rI.definition: Initially completing Precedent H - This task is confined to preparing and compiling the first budget required by the court in the form of Precedent H.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rN.label: Arkansas Circuit Court - Bradley Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rN.definition: A court located in Bradley County, Arkansas that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its designated geographical area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rO.label: Newco
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rO.definition: A new company that results after a merger or acquisition.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rQ.label: Motion to Appoint Examiner
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rQ.definition: A Motion to Appoint Examiner is a request made in a bankruptcy case for the appointment of an independent third-party examiner to investigate and report on certain aspects of the debtor's financial affairs.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rQ.label: Debtor's Rebuttal of Presumption of Abuse
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rQ.definition: A Debtor's Rebuttal of Presumption of Abuse is a legal document filed in bankruptcy cases that challenges the presumption that the debtor's income is too high to qualify for Chapter 7 bankruptcy.
english_labels: Debtor's Rebuttal of Presumption of Abuse

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rR.label: Fort Mojave Indian Tribe of Arizona, California, and Nevada
english_labels: Fort Mojave Indian Tribe of Arizona, California, and Nevada

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rX.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Centre County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rX.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Centre County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering civil and criminal proceedings at the county level in Pennsylvania.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Centre County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rY.label: Claim for Falling on Spill
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rY.definition: A claim for falling on spill is a legal action brought by a plaintiff who has suffered injuries as a result of slipping and falling on a spill, and is based on the legal theory of negligence.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rb.label: Access Easement Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rb.definition: An Access Easement Clause is a provision in a legal document that grants the right to use a specific portion of land for access purposes, such as for ingress and egress, to a person or entity who does not own the land.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rd.label: Tax Tier Detail
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rd.definition: Tax Tier Detail refers to the specific details and breakdown of taxes applied to a taxable amount, including the tax percentage, maximum and minimum amounts, and the total tax amount for each tier.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rh.label: Injunction
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rh.definition: A court order that requires a party to do or refrain from doing a specific act, typically issued to prevent irreparable harm or to enforce a legal right.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9ri.label: Lender Liability Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9ri.definition: Law which holds lender liable for a borrower's financial losses that are directly or indirectly related to the lender's actions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rn.label: Exclusive Use and Occupancy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rn.definition: The concept of Exclusive Use and Occupancy refers to a legal remedy sought by one spouse in a matrimonial emergency application, which allows them to have sole possession and control of the matrimonial home, excluding the other spouse.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rn.label: Bankruptcy Schedules
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rn.definition: Bankruptcy Schedules refer to the required documentation filed by a debtor in a bankruptcy case, detailing their assets, liabilities, income, and expenses.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9ro.label: Expert System
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9ro.definition: An Expert System is an automated system encoded with the knowledge of human experts, typically utilizing knowledge representation techniques. These systems are focused on narrow tasks and employ automated decision-making based on "if-then" rules to simulate the expertise of human specialists in specific domains.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9ro.label: Overruled Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9ro.definition: The previously effective law has been overruled by some authority (e.g., appellate court, judge, regulator).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9ro.label: A.A. (Associate of Arts)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9ro.definition: An A.A. (Associate of Arts) is a two-year degree typically earned at community colleges, emphasizing general education and liberal arts courses. It provides a foundation for further academic pursuits or entry-level positions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rq.label: Motion to Approve Sale
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rq.definition: A Motion to Approve Sale is a formal request made in a trial court seeking approval for the sale of a property or asset.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rt.label: Podiatry Negligence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rt.definition: Podiatry Negligence refers to a legal claim of medical malpractice specifically related to the field of podiatry.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rx.label: Hebrew
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rx.definition: Hebrew (Language) is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary, used in legal matters as a language of documents, artifacts, evidence, testimony, proceedings, or any other legal aspect, and is a subcategory of the Language top-level class.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9ry.label: Vocational Expert
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9ry.definition: An expert in the areas of vocational rehabilitation, earning capacity, lost earnings, cost of replacement labor, and loss of being able to perform household services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rz.label: bill_to_cl_name
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9rz.definition: "The name of the party being billed on the invoice. The legal name of the party being billed may be different from the CLIENT.cl_name, and the INVOICE.tax_invoice_cl_name. In some jurisdictions it may be required by law to provide this information. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9s5.label: Compulsory Education Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9s5.definition: A claim made by parents regarding their legal responsibility to provide compulsory education to their children.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9s6.label: Communications Risk
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9s6.definition: Communications Risk is the potential for negative consequences arising from miscommunication, misinformation, or inadequate communication within an organization or with external stakeholders. This can result from unclear messaging, lack of transparency, or the spread of false information, potentially leading to misunderstandings, damaged reputations, legal liabilities, or missed opportunities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sH.label: Plant Patent Assets
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sH.definition: Plant Patent Assets are a type of patent asset that refers specifically to plants that have been patented.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sH.label: Pali
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sH.definition: A language used primarily in the Theravada Buddhist scriptures and teachings, originating from ancient India and still used in some Southeast Asian countries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sI.label: Limited Guardianship of Juvenile
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sI.definition: A Limited Guardianship of Juvenile is a legal arrangement where a guardian is appointed to care for a minor child, but the guardian's authority is limited to specific areas, such as education or medical decisions, while the parents retain their rights and responsibilities in other areas.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sT.label: Cash
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sT.definition: Cash is legal tender – currency or coins – that can be used to exchange goods, debt, or services. Sometimes it also includes the value of assets that can be easily converted into cash immediately, as reported by a company.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sW.label: New York Supreme Court - Seneca County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sW.definition: The New York Supreme Court - Seneca County is a court of general jurisdiction located in Seneca County, New York, with authority to hear and decide a wide range of legal disputes within its geographic jurisdiction.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - Seneca County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sW.label: Cruise Ship Negligence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sW.definition: Cruise Ship Negligence refers to the legal concept of a cruise ship operator's failure to exercise reasonable care in ensuring the safety of its passengers, resulting in harm or injury to those passengers.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sY.label: Federal Rules of Evidence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sY.definition: U.S. federal courts' procedural rules governing the use of evidence.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sb.label: Court Forum Jurisdiction Types
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sb.definition: Court Forum Jurisdiction Types are specific types of courts that have the authority to hear and decide legal cases within a particular area of law or geographic region.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sc.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Mercer County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sc.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Mercer County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering civil and criminal proceedings at the county level in Pennsylvania.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Mercer County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sd.label: Payment Event
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sd.definition: A Payment Event refers to the specific occurrence when a payment is executed. This has legal implications for accounting and financial planning, as it impacts cash flow and may have implications for interest calculations, late fees, or contractual obligations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9se.label: False Advertising
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9se.definition: False Advertising: A type of business tort or product liability claim that involves the dissemination of misleading or deceptive information about a product or service in order to induce consumers to purchase it.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9se.label: Reasonable Best Efforts Antitrust Standard
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9se.definition: The Reasonable Best Efforts Antitrust Standard is a legal provision that requires parties to make a good faith effort to achieve a particular goal or outcome in an antitrust matter, without imposing an absolute obligation to succeed.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sj.label: D.C. Office of the Corporation Counsel
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sj.definition: The D.C. Office of the Corporation Counsel is a government entity within the District of Columbia Courts that provides legal representation and advice to the District government.
english_labels: D.C. Office of the Corporation Counsel

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9so.label: Balance
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9so.definition: In the context of a balance sheet, "balance" refers to the value assigned to an asset, liability, or equity account at a specific point in time. The balance sheet itself is based on the accounting equation "Assets = Liabilities + Equity," and individual balances should sum up to satisfy this equation. This is related to several legal areas (e.g., Tax Law, Bankruptcy Law).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sp.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Venango County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sp.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court in Venango County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court system that has jurisdiction over minor criminal offenses and civil cases.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Venango County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sr.label: Local Travel Expense
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sr.definition: Expenses incurred by an individual for transportation, lodging, and meals during a business trip within a specific geographic area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sw.label: Wasting Another's Property or Inheritance
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sw.definition: The concept of "Wasting Another's Property or Inheritance" refers to the intentional or negligent destruction, depletion, or misuse of assets or inheritance that belong to someone else, which can result in legal claims within the context of trusts and estates.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sx.label: Property Right of Habitation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sx.definition: In civil law jurisdictions, the Right of Property Habitation refers to a real right that allows an individual to reside in a dwelling for life or a specified period, without owning the property outright. This right is personal in nature and typically cannot be transferred, leased, or inherited, distinguishing it from more complete forms of ownership like fee simple or leasehold

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sy.label: Notices Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sy.definition: A notices clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the requirements for providing formal communication between parties, such as the method and timing of delivering notices.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sz.label: Litigation Costs
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9sz.definition: Litigation Costs: The expenses incurred by parties in a legal dispute, including attorney fees, court fees, and other related expenses.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9t3.label: Longshore and Harbor Workers’ Compensation Act Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9t3.definition: A claim made under the Longshore and Harbor Workers’ Compensation Act (LHWCA), which provides benefits to certain maritime workers who are injured or become ill while working on navigable waters or in adjoining areas used for loading, unloading, repairing, or building a vessel.
english_labels: Longshore and Harbor Workers’ Compensation Act Claim

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9t8.label: Petition for Skilled Worker and Specialty Occupation Visa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9t8.definition: The "Petition for Specialty Occupation Visa" generally refers to the H-1B visa petition in the United States. The H-1B visa is a non-immigrant visa category that allows U.S. employers to hire foreign workers in specialty occupations that require specialized knowledge and skills. The employer must file a Form I-129 petition with U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), demonstrating that the position meets the criteria of a specialty occupation and that the beneficiary (the foreign worker) has the necessary qualifications. If approved, the beneficiary can work in the U.S. for the sponsoring employer for a specified period, typically up to three years with the possibility of extension
english_labels: Petition for Skilled Worker and Specialty Occupation Visa

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9t9.label: Motion to Waive Fee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9t9.definition: A Motion to Waive Fee is a request made in a bankruptcy case to waive the filing fee due to the petitioner's inability to pay.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tA.label: Immigration Service
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tA.definition: Immigration legal service refers to the range of legal assistance provided to individuals seeking to navigate immigration laws, regulations, and procedures. This can include help with visa applications, asylum requests, deportation defense, and naturalization processes, among other immigration-related matters, and is usually provided by specialized immigration attorneys or legal firms

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tC.label: Georgia Superior Court - Wheeler County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tC.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Wheeler County is a specific court within the Georgia Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Wheeler County, Georgia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tI.label: Lawyer's Bar Identifier
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tI.definition: A Lawyer Identifier is a unique number or code assigned to a lawyer upon admission to practice law in a specific jurisdiction, such as a Bar Admission Number.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tK.label: Economic Interest Defense
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tK.definition: A legal defense used in civil litigation that argues that the actions taken by a party were in the best interest of their economic well-being.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tP.label: Wheat
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tP.definition: Wheat is a cereal crop belonging to the genus Triticum, known for its edible grain that is a staple food worldwide. It is a key ingredient in many food products, including bread, pasta, and pastries, and provides essential nutrients such as carbohydrates, proteins, and vitamins.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tU.label: Temporary Child Support
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tU.definition: Temporary Child Support refers to the financial assistance provided by one parent to the other during the pendency of a matrimonial emergency application, for the purpose of supporting their child/children.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tW.label: Georgia Superior Court - Whitfield County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tW.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Whitfield County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Whitfield County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tX.label: APAC Market Region
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tX.definition: The APAC Market Region encompasses the geographical area of Asia and the Pacific, including East Asia, South Asia, Southeast Asia, and Oceania, known for its economic dynamism, technological innovation, and diverse consumer bases. This region is a focal point for global businesses due to its rapid economic growth, significant market opportunities, and varied regulatory environments.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tX.label: Objector
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tX.definition: A person, usually a nonparty, who objects to an aspect of the litigation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tZ.label: Witness
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tZ.definition: A witness or non-party is a person or entity called upon to produce documents or provide testimony or other information in connection with a dispute or proceeding (and not a party to the dispute or proceeding).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tZ.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Jefferson County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tZ.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Jefferson County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering civil and criminal proceedings at the county level in Pennsylvania.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Jefferson County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tc.label: AI Bias
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tc.definition: Bias in an AI system refers to the differential treatment of different groups and concepts, which may arise from implicit systems of meaning, norms, and values. Bias can lead to unfair or discriminatory outcomes, impacting the effectiveness and ethical alignment of AI systems.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tk.label: Indiana Superior Court - Miami County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tk.definition: Indiana Superior Court - Miami County refers to a specific court within the Indiana Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Miami County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tu.label: Firm Accounting Personnel
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tu.definition: Firm Accounting Personnel refers to non-timekeeping staff members of a legal service provider who are responsible for financial management and accounting tasks.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tw.label: Endorsement Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tw.definition: An Endorsement Agreement is a legally binding contract between parties that outlines the terms and conditions of an endorsement deal, typically involving a celebrity or public figure promoting a product or service.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tw.label: Treatise
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tw.definition: A treatise is a comprehensive and systematic written work that provides an in-depth analysis of a particular legal subject or area of law. It is often used as a reference by legal professionals and scholars to gain a deeper understanding of legal principles, case law, and statutory interpretations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tx.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Spencer County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9tx.definition: Indiana Circuit Court - Spencer County: A court of general jurisdiction in Indiana that hears civil and criminal cases within Spencer County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9ty.label: Plaintiff
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9ty.definition: A plaintiff, complainant, or claimant is a person who brings a civil or criminal action against another person or entity in a dispute.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9ty.label: Seasonal Worker
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9ty.definition: A Seasonal Employee is hired for a specific period that coincides with a season, event, or holiday, often in industries like retail, tourism, and agriculture. Unlike full-time or part-time employees, seasonal employees are usually not eligible for long-term company benefits and are laid off at the end of the season.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9u1.label: Motion to Transfer Appeal to Other Circuit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9u1.definition: A Motion to Transfer Appeal to Other Circuit is a formal request made in an appellate court to move a case to a different circuit for review.
english_labels: Motion to Transfer Appeal to Other Circuit

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9u4.label: Restrictive Covenant Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9u4.definition: A "Restrictive Covenant Agreement" is a contractual document that imposes certain limitations or obligations on one or more parties, commonly in the context of employment, real estate, or business transactions. The agreement specifies the scope, duration, and geographic extent of restrictions such as non-compete, non-solicitation, or land use limitations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9uT.label: Insurance Policy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9uT.definition: An insurance policy is a contract between an insurance provider and a policyholder that outlines the terms and conditions under which the insurer will provide coverage and financial compensation for specific risks, events, or damages. The policy specifies the premiums to be paid by the policyholder, the coverage limits, and the obligations of each party in the event of a claim.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9uT.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Macoupin County (7th Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Macoupin County (7th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9uZ.label: Application for Entry of Final Decree
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9uZ.definition: An Application for Entry of Final Decree is a formal request submitted to a court by a debtor in a bankruptcy case, asking for the court's approval of the final order that will close the case.
english_labels: Application for Entry of Final Decree

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9ui.label: Sodomy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9ui.definition: Oral or anal sexual intercourse with another person, forcibly and/or against that person’s will or not forcibly or against the person’s will in instances where the victim is incapable of giving consent because of his/her youth or because of his/her temporary or permanent mental or physical incapacity.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9ul.label: Dower
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9ul.definition: A dower is a claim made by a widow to a portion of her deceased husband's estate, typically one-third, as a form of support and security.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9uo.label: Civil Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9uo.definition: A Civil Court is a type of court forum that has jurisdiction over non-criminal cases involving private disputes between individuals or organizations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9ur.label: Conservatorship of Juvenile
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9ur.definition: A conservatorship of juvenile is a legal arrangement where a court appoints a responsible adult to care for a minor's personal and financial needs when the minor's parents are unable to do so.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9ur.label: Georgia District Court - Fulton County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9ur.definition: Georgia District Court - Fulton County: A specific court within the Georgia District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Fulton County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9uz.label: Special Purpose Acquisition Company
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9uz.definition: A Special Purpose Acquisition Company (SPAC) is a shell corporation specifically created to raise capital through an initial public offering (IPO) for the purpose of acquiring an existing company. Once the funds are raised, the SPAC identifies a target company to acquire, and if the acquisition is successful, the SPAC effectively takes the acquired company public.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9v1.label: Dispute Venue
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9v1.definition: A Dispute Venue is a specific type of Forum or Venue that is responsible for administering legal proceedings related to disputes, including Courts, Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) Venues, Legislative Proceedings, and Administrative Proceeding Venues.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9v1.label: Liquidity Risk
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9v1.definition: The risk that a party will be unable to buy or sell an asset quickly enough to prevent or minimize a loss.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9v2.label: Failure to Prevent Discrimination
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9v2.definition: Failure to prevent discrimination refers to a situation in which an employer, organization, or entity neglects to take appropriate steps to address and deter discriminatory actions or practices within their environment. This may include not establishing and enforcing clear policies, failing to provide training or education on discrimination and harassment, or neglecting to investigate and remedy complaints of discrimination.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9v3.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Lincoln County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9v3.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Lincoln County refers to a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Lincoln County, Missouri.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9v4.label: Escrow Provisions Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9v4.definition: An Escrow Provisions Clause is a legal provision within an Escrow Clause that outlines the specific terms and conditions for holding funds or property in a neutral third-party account until certain conditions are met.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9v4.label: Florida Court of Appeals - 3d District
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9v4.definition: The Florida Court of Appeals - 3d District is a specific court within the Florida District Court of Appeals that hears appeals from lower courts in the third district of Florida.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9v8.label: Motion to File Claim After Claims Bar Date
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9v8.definition: A Motion to File Claim After Claims Bar Date is a request made in a bankruptcy case to allow a creditor to file a claim after the deadline for filing claims has passed.
english_labels: Motion to File Claim After Claims Bar Date

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9v9.label: Custody Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9v9.definition: Custody Law refers to the legal rules and regulations that govern the care, control, and maintenance of children in cases of separation or divorce.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9vD.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Howard County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9vD.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Howard County refers to a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Howard County, Missouri.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9vG.label: Right to Use Common Areas
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9vG.definition: The Right to Use Common Areas refers to the legal entitlement of property owners or tenants within a multi-unit building or complex to access and utilize shared spaces, such as hallways, lobbies, parking lots, and recreational facilities. This right is usually governed by rules set forth in property agreements or by a homeowners' association, and may be subject to certain limitations and responsibilities

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9vH.label: Equitable Tolling
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9vH.definition: Equitable Tolling is a legal doctrine that allows for the extension of a statute of limitations in certain circumstances to prevent unfair forfeitures of rights, provided that the defendant is not prejudiced by the delay.
english_labels: Equitable tolling is designed to prevent unjust and technical forfeitures of rights and may delay the running of the statute of limitations in certain circumstances if a lack of prejudice to the defendant can be shown.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9vJ.label: Putable Asset
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9vJ.definition: A Putable Asset is a financial instrument that grants the holder the right to sell the asset back to the issuer at a specified price before its maturity date. This feature provides investors with the flexibility to exit the investment under certain conditions, often mitigating potential losses and reducing risk.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9vN.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Adair County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9vN.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Adair County refers to a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Adair County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9vX.label: Litigation Case - Long Name
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9vX.definition: A litigation case with a longer name, which is a subcategory of a litigation case name.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9va.label: Disclaimer of Damages Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9va.definition: A disclaimer of damages clause is a provision in a contract that limits or eliminates the liability of one party for any damages incurred by the other party, even if the first party is at fault.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9vh.label: Bankruptcy Schedule - Exempt Property
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9vh.definition: Bankruptcy Schedule - Exempt Property requires the debtor to list property they claim as exempt from the bankruptcy estate, protecting it from liquidation to satisfy creditor claims. This schedule identifies assets the debtor is allowed to retain under federal or state exemption laws, such as certain amounts of equity in a home, vehicle, or personal items.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9vl.label: Rescue Doctrine
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9vl.definition: The Rescue Doctrine is a legal concept that allows a person who voluntarily attempts to rescue another person in danger to potentially recover damages if they are injured due to the negligence of another party.
english_labels: Voluntary Rescuer Injured by Negligence of Other

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9vp.label: Academic Paper
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9vp.definition: An academic paper is a scholarly piece of writing that is based on original research or analysis and contributes to the existing body of knowledge on a particular subject. In legal academia, these papers are often published in law reviews or journals, and they adhere to a stringent set of formatting and citation standards, providing a rigorous examination of legal theories, case law, or legislative issues.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9vs.label: 740 Railway Labor Act (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9vs.definition: Action relating to disputes filed under the Railway Labor Act, 45 U.S.C. § 151 including labor disputes, individual claims, and response to sanctions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9vw.label: Videoconference
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9vw.definition: A communication that occurs via videoconference (e.g., Zoom, Teams, Meet).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9vz.label: Admission Pro Hac Vice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9vz.definition: Admission Pro Hac Vice is a legal term that refers to the permission granted to an out-of-state lawyer to practice law in a particular jurisdiction for a specific case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9vz.label: Insider Trading
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9vz.definition: The act of buying or selling securities based on material, non-public information obtained from a company or its insiders, in violation of a duty to keep such information confidential.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9w6.label: Bite Mark Evidence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9w6.definition: Bite mark evidence involves the study of patterns left by teeth on various materials, often skin. Forensic odontologists analyze these marks to identify unique dental characteristics, potentially linking a suspect to an injury or crime scene.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9w8.label: Georgia Superior Court - Wilkinson County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9w8.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Wilkinson County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over legal matters within Wilkinson County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9wJ.label: Statutory Appeal
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9wJ.definition: A statutory appeal is a type of appeal that is specifically authorized by a statute or law, and allows a party to challenge a decision made by a lower court or administrative agency.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9wM.label: Unlawful Detainer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9wM.definition: An unlawful detainer is a summary proceeding for a landlord to recover possession of a leased premises from a tenant wrongfully withholding or "detaining" the property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9wO.label: Cancer of Unknown Primary Site
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9wO.definition: Cancer where the primary site is unknown after appropriate search refers to a malignant neoplasm for which the origin remains unidentified despite comprehensive diagnostic testing. This condition, also known as carcinoma of unknown primary (CUP), requires tailored treatment approaches due to the uncertainty of its origin and may involve symptoms affecting various organs or systems.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9wO.label: Hematology Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9wO.definition: Medical negligence related to the diagnosis, treatment, or management of blood disorders or diseases.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9wQ.label: Spokane Tribe of The Spokane Reservation
english_labels: Spokane Tribe of The Spokane Reservation

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9wT.label: New York City Court - Poughkeepsie
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9wT.definition: A court located in Poughkeepsie, New York that operates under the jurisdiction of the New York City Court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9wT.label: Kurukh
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9wT.definition: Kurukh (Language) is a specific written or spoken structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary, and is a member of the Language top-level class.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9wT.label: Motion for Summary Adjudication
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9wT.definition: A Motion for Summary Adjudication is a legal request made by a party in a bankruptcy or civil case, asking the court to rule in their favor without a trial, based on the evidence presented in the motion.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9wU.label: Binding Precedent
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9wU.definition: Binding Precedent is a legal principle established in a previous case that must be followed by all lower courts in the same jurisdiction when deciding subsequent cases with similar facts or legal issues. It is a fundamental aspect of common law legal systems and ensures consistency and predictability in the application of law.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9wU.label: Arkansas Circuit Court - Saline Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9wU.definition: A court located in Saline County, Arkansas that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its designated area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9wW.label: Mi'kmaq; Micmac
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9wW.definition: A Native American language spoken by the Mi'kmaq people in Eastern Canada and Northeastern United States.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9wX.label: Drug Testing Policy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9wX.definition: A drug testing policy is a formal document established by an organization that outlines the procedures, guidelines, and consequences related to the testing of employees for the presence of drugs and/or alcohol. It generally seeks to ensure a safe and productive work environment by preventing substance abuse and its associated risks.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9wf.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Boone County (17th Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Boone County (17th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9wi.label: Exhibits Attached Hereto Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9wi.definition: A provision in a contract that specifies the inclusion of physical or digital items as evidence or proof of the agreement, which are attached to the contract itself.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/R9wj.label: Wrongful Seduction
