https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBDx.definition: The Employment Objection Process (Bankruptcy) refers to the legal procedure in bankruptcy cases where an objection is raised regarding the employment of a professional, such as an attorney or accountant, by the debtor.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBE3.label: firm_URL
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBE3.definition: "The law firm's website URL. Should always begin ""http://www. …"" "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBE3.label: Probate due to Disability
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBE3.definition: Probate due to Disability refers to the legal process of managing the assets and affairs of a person who is unable to do so themselves due to a physical or mental disability.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBE3.label: U.S. Bankruptcy Court - N.D. Alabama
english_labels: United States Bankruptcy Court, N.D. Alabama

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBE3.label: Kalmykiya, Respublika
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBE3.definition: Kalmykiya, Respublika is a region within the Russian Federation with the official name of the Republic of Kalmykia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBE4.label: Guidimaka
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBE4.definition: Guidimaka is a region in Mauritania.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBE6.label: Federal Bureau of Investigation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBE6.definition: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is the domestic intelligence and security service of the United States, and its principal federal law enforcement agency.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBE7.label: Intimidation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBE7.definition: To unlawfully place another person in reasonable fear of bodily harm through the use of threatening words and/or other conduct, but without displaying a weapon or subjecting the victim to actual physical attack.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBE7.label: Georgia Superior Court - Gilmer County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBE7.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Gilmer County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBE9.label: Dakhlet Nouadhibou
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBE9.definition: Dakhlet Nouadhibou is a coastal city located in Mauritania.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEE.label: Gorgol
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEE.definition: Gorgol is a region in Mauritania.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEF.label: Pskovskaya oblast'
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEF.definition: Pskovskaya oblast' is a region in the Russian Federation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEJ.label: Ladino
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEJ.definition: A language derived from medieval Spanish and spoken by Sephardic Jews, primarily in Israel, Turkey, and the Balkans.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEK.label: JL20 Support of advocates (UK J-CODE)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEK.definition: Work by lawyers other than advocates relating to the above matters and all attendances at court on trial days including conferences or meetings before or after court and travel and waiting. Where there is a substantial gap between trial days, work should be allocated to whichever is the more appropriate of the Trial Preparation and Trial phases.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEL.label: New York City Court - Binghamton
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEL.definition: A court located in Binghamton, New York that operates under the jurisdiction of the New York City Court system.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEL.label: Shelf Takedown
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEL.definition: Shelf Takedown refers to the process of issuing and selling securities from an existing shelf registration. This method allows companies to quickly and efficiently raise capital by taking down portions of the previously registered securities when market conditions are favorable.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEM.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Hamilton County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEM.definition: Indiana Circuit Court - Hamilton County refers to a specific court within the Indiana Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Hamilton County, Indiana.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEN.label: Texas District Court - Johnson County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEN.definition: A Texas District Court located in Johnson County is a specific court within the Texas District Court system that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEP.label: LAW_FIRM_ID
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEP.definition: A unique identifier assigned to a law firm, as defined in the LEDES98BI V5 Format Rev 1-2020 standard.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBET.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Monroe County Circuit 6
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBET.definition: The Indiana Circuit Court - Monroe County Circuit 6 is a specific court within the Indiana Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Monroe County.
english_labels: Indiana Circuit Court - Monroe County Circuit 6

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEV.label: Rehabilitation Center Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEV.definition: Negligent or wrongful actions or omissions committed by a rehabilitation center or its staff, resulting in harm or injury to a patient, and giving rise to a legal claim for damages.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEf.label: Financial Advisor
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEf.definition: A professional adviser offering financial counsel, sometimes charging fees and/or earning commissions. Rockhill v. William M. Jeude & Univest, Inc. (W.D. Wash. 2012)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEh.label: Choice of Venue Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEh.definition: A Choice of Venue Clause is a provision in a contract that specifies the location or jurisdiction where any disputes arising from the contract will be resolved.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEh.label: UK Serious Fraud Office
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEh.definition: The UK Serious Fraud Office is a governmental department responsible for investigating and prosecuting serious or complex fraud, bribery, and corruption. Operating independently, the SFO combines the functions of police and prosecutor to tackle high-level economic crimes affecting the United Kingdom.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEi.label: Management, Scientific, and Technical Consulting Services Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEi.definition: This industry group comprises establishments primarily engaged in providing advice and assistance to businesses and other organizations on management, environmental, scientific, and technical issues.
english_labels: Management, Scientific, and Technical Consulting Services Industry

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEl.label: Co-Authoring Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEl.definition: Co-Authoring Management refers to the process of managing the collaboration and contribution of multiple authors to a document, within the context of Document Management.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEn.label: Georgia Superior Court - Cook County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEn.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Cook County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEp.label: Visa for Staff of Diplomats and Government Officials
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEp.definition: A visa for staff of diplomats and government officials is a specialized visa category that allows personal employees, domestic workers, aides, attendants, or personal staff to accompany and work for diplomats or government officials while they are stationed in a foreign country. These visas are usually subject to specific conditions and may require the sponsoring diplomat or official to assume certain responsibilities for the employee's welfare and legal status in the host country.
english_labels: Visa for Staff of Diplomats and Government Officials

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEs.label: Residual Hearsay Exception
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEs.definition: The residual hearsay exception is a legal provision that allows hearsay evidence to be admitted in court if it meets certain criteria, even if it does not fall under any other specific hearsay exception. These criteria include the statement being offered as evidence of a material fact, no other more probative evidence exists, its admission serves the interests of justice, and the offering party provides prior notice to the opposing counsel.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEt.label: Good Faith Deposit Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEt.definition: A Good Faith Deposit Clause is a provision in a contract that requires one party to provide a deposit as a demonstration of good faith in fulfilling their obligations under the agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEy.label: Georgia Superior Court - Jefferson County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEy.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Jefferson County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Jefferson County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBEz.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Jo Daviess County (15th Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Jo Daviess County (15th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBF1.label: Thessalia
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBF1.definition: Thessalia is a region in Greece.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBF1.label: Threatened
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBF1.definition: A modifier of a criminal claim indicating that harm or danger has been communicated or perceived, and that action may be taken to prevent it.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBF5.label: Consumer Goods Leased Under Unconscionable Circumstances
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBF5.definition: Consumer Goods Leased Under Unconscionable Circumstances refers to the situation where a consumer leases goods from a party who has taken advantage of the consumer's vulnerability, lack of bargaining power, or inability to understand the terms of the lease agreement, resulting in an unfair and unreasonable contract.
english_labels: Consumer Goods Leased Under Unconscionable Circumstances

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBF5.label: Florida County Court - Union County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBF5.definition: Florida County Court - Union County: A court of limited jurisdiction in Florida that handles civil and criminal cases within the geographical boundaries of Union County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBF5.label: L420 Expert Witnesses
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBF5.definition: An L420 Expert Witness is a professional who possesses specialized knowledge or skills in a particular field and is called upon to provide testimony in a legal proceeding related to that field.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBF8.label: Limited Ruleset
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBF8.definition: A Limited Ruleset is a specific type of rule that has a restricted scope or application.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBF8.label: Motion to File Answer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBF8.definition: A Motion to File Answer is a formal request made to a court by a defendant in a legal case, seeking permission to submit their response to the plaintiff's complaint.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBF8.label: Cervical Cancer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBF8.definition: Cervical cancer is a type of cancer that originates in the cells of the cervix, the lower part of the uterus that connects to the vagina. It is often caused by persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) and requires treatments such as surgery, radiation therapy, and chemotherapy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBF8.label: No Liens Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBF8.definition: A No Liens Clause is a provision in a contract that states that the property or assets involved in the agreement are free from any claims or encumbrances by third parties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBF9.label: Acquaviva
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBF9.definition: Acquaviva is a location in San Marino.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBF9.label: Kachin
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBF9.definition: Kachin refers to an ethnic group and their language in Myanmar.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFA.label: Bale
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFA.definition: A bale is a unit of measurement used to quantify goods such as cotton or hay, typically weighing between 100 and 500 pounds.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFA.label: Utilities Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFA.definition: This group comprises establishments engaged in the provision of the following utility services: electric power, natural gas, steam supply, and water supply. Within this sector, the specific activities associated with the utility services provided vary by utility: electric power includes generation, transmission, and distribution; natural gas includes distribution; steam supply includes provision and/or distribution; water supply includes treatment and distribution.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFB.label: Hung Yen
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFB.definition: Hung Yen is a province in Vietnam.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFB.label: Federal Rules of Criminal Procedure
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFB.definition: U.S. federal courts' body of procedural rules governing criminal actions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFF.label: IRS Tax Exempt and Government Entities Division
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFF.definition: The IRS Tax Exempt and Governments Entities Division of the IRS provides administrative guidance to their examiners to ensure consistent tax administration and on matters relating to internal operations. The administrative guidance can be in the form of interim guidance or directives; they don't establish the IRS's position on legal issues and are not legal guidance.
english_labels: IRS Tax Exempt and Government Entities Division

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFF.label: Visa for Nurses and Medical Professionals
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFF.definition: A visa for nurses and medical professionals is a specialized visa category that may be offered by certain countries to healthcare workers who wish to enter for the purpose of employment in the medical field. These visas often have specific requirements, including proof of qualifications, job offers from recognized healthcare institutions, and sometimes a need to address shortages of medical professionals in the host country.
english_labels: Visa for Nurses and Medical Professionals

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFH.label: Appellate Filings - Nonparty Filing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFH.definition: A non-party filing made in an appellate court, such as a motion to appear pro hac vice, motion for leave to appeal, motion to intervene, motion for leave to file as amicus, or notice of appearance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFL.label: Objection to Application for Professional Employment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFL.definition: An objection made specifically in response to an application for professional employment.
english_labels: Objection to Application for Professional Employment

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFL.label: Professional Services Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFL.definition: The Professional Services industry group comprises establishments that specialize in performing professional, scientific, and technical activities for others. These activities require a high degree of expertise and training.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFO.label: Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFO.definition: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) is a diverse group of blood cancers that originate in the lymphatic system, which is part of the body's immune system. It includes various subtypes that differ in their aggressiveness and treatment protocols, commonly requiring chemotherapy, radiation therapy, immunotherapy, or stem cell transplantation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFQ.label: Non-Profit Formation Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFQ.definition: Nonprofit formation practice refers to the legal service where lawyers assist in establishing nonprofit organizations, guiding clients through aspects like drafting bylaws, filing for tax-exempt status, and ensuring compliance with state and federal laws. This specialized legal service aims to create a compliant and effective organizational structure that meets the client's charitable, educational, or social objectives.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFS.label: Color Blindness
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFS.definition: Color Blindness is a visual impairment that affects an individual's ability to perceive colors accurately, typically due to a deficiency or absence of certain color-sensitive photoreceptors in the retina. This condition can range from difficulty distinguishing between specific colors to complete inability to see any colors.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFS.label: Chattels
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFS.definition: Chattels are personal property items that are movable and do not include land or interests in land. This legal term encompasses tangible and intangible assets that a person owns, which can be physically relocated or transferred from one place to another, as opposed to real property or immovable assets.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFV.label: Involuntary Debtor
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFV.definition: An involuntary debtor is an individual or entity against whom creditors initiate bankruptcy proceedings, often because the debtor has failed to meet financial obligations. The involuntary bankruptcy process is initiated by the filing of a petition by the creditors, rather than the debtor themselves

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFZ.label: Additional Provisions Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFZ.definition: An Additional Provisions Clause is a specific clause within a contract that outlines additional terms and conditions beyond those already stated in the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFg.label: Personal and Family Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFg.definition: Law that deals with family matters and domestic relations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFl.label: Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians
english_labels: Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFp.label: Georgia District Court - Miller County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFp.definition: Georgia District Court - Miller County: A specific court within the Georgia District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Miller County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFu.label: Traffic Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFu.definition: Traffic Court is a specialized court that deals with traffic violations and related offenses.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFu.label: Intrusion
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFu.definition: The concept of Intrusion refers to a type of privacy claim that involves intentional and offensive interference with an individual's solitude or private affairs, which would be highly offensive to a reasonable person.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFv.label: Court Administrator
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFv.definition: A person who serves a clerical, administrative function for a court. In some jurisdictions, this can include the Clerk of Court, and in other jurisdictions these roles are distinct.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFv.label: Right of First Refusal to Lease Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFv.definition: A Right of First Refusal to Lease Clause is a provision in a contract that gives a party the opportunity to lease a property before it is offered to others, if the owner decides to lease it.
english_labels: Right of First Refusal to Lease Clause

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFz.label: Amendment Fee Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBFz.definition: An Amendment Fee Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the fees associated with making changes or modifications to the agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBG3.label: Appellate Page Proof Reply Brief
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBG3.definition: An Appellate Page Proof Reply Brief is a written document submitted to a higher court in response to an opposing party's arguments, which includes evidence and legal reasoning to support the appellant's position.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBG9.label: Condominium Right
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBG9.definition: Condominium Right, also known as Horizontal Property Right, refers to the legal structure that allows individual ownership of a unit within a multi-unit building, along with a shared ownership interest in common areas like hallways, elevators, and amenities. This right enables the individual unit owner to sell, lease, or mortgage their unit independently, while being subject to the rules and governance of a homeowners' association or similar entity.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGC.label: Billing and Payment Terms Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGC.definition: A Billing and Payment Terms Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the terms and conditions for payment and billing between parties involved in the agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGO.label: Inupiaq
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGO.definition: A language spoken by the Inupiaq people, primarily in Alaska and Canada.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGP.label: Admiralty Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGP.definition: Admiralty Court refers to a specialized court that has jurisdiction over maritime disputes and offenses, including those related to shipping, navigation, and marine commerce.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGX.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Wabash County (2nd Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Wabash County (2nd Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGY.label: Texas District Court - Hays County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGY.definition: A Texas District Court located in Hays County, which has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGa.label: Corporate Insolvency Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGa.definition: Law relating to insolvency or reorganization of corporations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGa.label: Preservation of Documents Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGa.definition: Preservation of Documents Practice refers to the legal practice of ensuring that relevant documents are protected and maintained in their original form during a legal matter, in order to prevent their destruction or alteration.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGb.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Northampton County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGb.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Northampton County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering legal proceedings in Northampton County, Pennsylvania.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Northampton County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGd.label: Asset-Backed Securities
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGd.definition: Asset-Backed Securities (ABS) are financial instruments backed by a pool of assets, typically loans or receivables, that generate cash flows to pay interest and principal to investors. ABS allow lenders to transfer the risk of the underlying assets to investors and are commonly used to improve liquidity and raise capital.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGg.label: New York City - Municipal Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGg.definition: New York City Municipal Court is a court of limited jurisdiction that hears cases involving minor criminal offenses, civil cases involving amounts up to $25,000, and small claims cases involving amounts up to $5,000 in New York City.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGj.label: Lease Renewal and Extension Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGj.definition: A Lease Renewal & Extension Agreement allows a tenant to renew or extend their lease for an additional period, often under the same terms and conditions as the original lease.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGk.label: Injunctive Relief Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGk.definition: An Injunctive Relief Clause is a provision in a contract that allows a party to seek a court order to prevent the other party from taking certain actions or to compel them to perform certain obligations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGm.label: Motion in Limine to Exclude Document
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGm.definition: A Motion in Limine to Exclude Document is a legal request made by a party to prevent the opposing party from introducing a specific piece of evidence, such as a written or recorded representation, during a trial or hearing.
english_labels: Motion in Limine to Exclude Document

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGn.label: Book of Authorities Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGn.definition: Book of Authorities Management refers to the process of organizing and maintaining a collection of legal authorities cited in a litigation case, including cases, statutes, and regulations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGq.label: Consumer Price Index Escalation Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGq.definition: A Consumer Price Index (CPI) Escalation Clause, also known as CPI, is a clause in a contract that allows for adjustments to be made to payments or prices based on changes in the CPI, which measures the average change in prices over time for goods and services consumed by households.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGq.label: Artificial languages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGq.definition: Artificial languages are a subset of language that are created by humans for specific purposes, such as programming languages or constructed languages like Esperanto.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGw.label: Investment Companies Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBGw.definition: Regulations on companies that engage primarily in investing, reinvesting, and trading in securities, and whose own securities are offered to the investing public.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBH1.label: Insurance Fraud
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBH1.definition: The concept of Insurance Fraud refers to the intentional deception or misrepresentation made by an individual or entity to an insurance company for the purpose of obtaining benefits or compensation to which they are not entitled, including the fraudulent acquisition of life or health insurance policies.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBH5.label: Assignee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBH5.definition: An assignee is a person, company or entity who receives the transfer of property, title or rights from a contract. The assignee receives the transfer from the assignor.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBH5.label: Minnesota District Court - Martin County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBH5.definition: Minnesota District Court - Martin County: A specific court within the Minnesota District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Martin County, Minnesota.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBH6.label: Elements of Civil Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBH6.definition: The Elements of Civil Claim are the specific components that must be present in a legal claim brought in civil court, including facts, legal theories, and damages sought.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBH9.label: New Jersey Superior Court - Bergen County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBH9.definition: The New Jersey Superior Court - Bergen County is a specific court within the New Jersey Superior Court Appellate Division that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases in Bergen County, New Jersey.
english_labels: New Jersey Superior Court - Bergen County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBH9.label: Acceleration of Rent Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBH9.definition: An acceleration of rent clause is a provision in a contract that allows the landlord to demand the full amount of rent owed for the remainder of the lease term if the tenant breaches the lease agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHB.label: Witness Statement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHB.definition: A witness statement is a written or recorded account of an individual's observations or knowledge of an event, provided as evidence in a legal proceeding.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHC.label: Peer Reviewed
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHC.definition: Peer Reviewed indicates that a document has undergone a formal evaluation by experts in the same field to assess its validity, significance, and originality. This characteristic is often considered a marker of academic rigor and credibility.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHH.label: Motion to Recall Mandate
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHH.definition: A Motion to Recall Mandate is a legal request made in an appellate court to withdraw or cancel a previously issued mandate.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHI.label: Valuation Metrics
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHI.definition: Valuation Metrics are quantifiable measures and methodologies used to assess the economic worth of an asset, business, or investment. These metrics serve as the basis for informed decision-making in activities such as acquisitions, investments, and financial reporting

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHI.label: Visa for Dependents of Exchange Visitors
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHI.definition: This non-immigrant visa for dependents of exchange visitors (in the U.S., a J-2 Visa) allows spouses and minor children of exchange visitors (in the U.S., J-1 Visa holders) to accompany them during their stay in the destination country (e.g., U.S.).
english_labels: Visa for Dependents of Exchange Visitors

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHM.label: AI Lifecycle Systems
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHM.definition: AI Lifecycle Systems encompass the processes and methodologies involved in the development, deployment, and maintenance of artificial intelligence systems. These systems include various stages such as data collection, model training, evaluation, and continuous improvement to ensure effective and ethical AI performance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHM.label: Negligent Advice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHM.definition: Negligent Advice refers to a claim of professional negligence where a legal professional fails to provide competent advice or guidance to a client, resulting in harm or damages.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHM.label: Project Statement of Work
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHM.definition: An agreement between the customer and the project team on success criteria, requirements, budget, and timeline.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHP.label: Private Offering
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHP.definition: Private Debt Offering refers to the sale of debt securities directly to a small group of private investors, typically without the need for public registration or regulatory approval. This method is often used by companies seeking to raise capital more quickly and with greater confidentiality than through public offerings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHW.label: Voter Intimidation and Coercion Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHW.definition: Voter Intimidation and Coercion Claims refer to allegations that individuals were threatened, harassed, or pressured to influence their vote or deter them from voting. These claims can include physical threats, verbal harassment, misleading information, or coercive tactics designed to interfere with the free exercise of voting rights.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHc.label: Bearer Securities
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHc.definition: Bearer Securities are financial instruments where the owner's identity is not recorded on the books of the issuer or the registrar. These securities can be transferred by mere possession, making them highly negotiable and anonymous.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHh.label: Lemon Law Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHh.definition: A Lemon Law Claim is a legal action taken by a consumer against a motor vehicle dealership or manufacturer for selling a defective vehicle that fails to meet the standards of quality and performance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHh.label: tax_tier_tax_percent
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHh.definition: "The tax rate percentage for this tax tier, i.e. 7.2516% tax_rate_percent would be represented as ""0.072516"". "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHi.label: New Jersey Supreme Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHi.definition: The New Jersey Supreme Court is the highest court in the state of New Jersey, with the authority to hear appeals from lower courts and to make final decisions on legal disputes within the state.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHi.label: Position Posting
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHi.definition: A Position Posting is a public or internal announcement made by an organization to advertise a job vacancy. It typically outlines the job description, qualifications required, and instructions for application.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHl.label: Words Negligently Spoken
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHl.definition: Words Negligently Spoken refers to a legal concept under Defamation where a statement is made without proper care and caution, resulting in harm to the reputation of the subject.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHs.label: Guaranty Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHs.definition: A guaranty claim is a cause of action over a legal promise made by one party to be responsible for the debt or obligation of another party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHs.label: Regulatory Risk
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHs.definition: Regulatory Risk refers to the potential for negative consequences arising from an organization's noncompliance with laws, regulations, or industry standards that govern its operations, products, or services. These risks can stem from various sources, such as changes in regulatory requirements, lack of clarity on compliance obligations, or failure to implement adequate controls, potentially leading to legal penalties, reputational damage, or operational disruptions, ultimately impacting the organization's overall performance and sustainability.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHx.label: Progressive Bulbar Palsy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHx.definition: Progressive bulbar palsy (PBP) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by the progressive degeneration of motor neurons in the brainstem, leading to progressive weakness and atrophy of the muscles involved in speech, swallowing, and breathing. This condition often overlaps with Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) but primarily affects the bulbar muscles.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHx.label: Fair Debt Collection Act Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHx.definition: A Fair Debt Collection Act Claim is a legal claim made by a consumer against a debt collector for violating the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, which sets standards for debt collection activities and prohibits certain abusive and deceptive practices.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHz.label: Trade Safeguards Dispute
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBHz.definition: Trade Safeguards Disputes involve legal proceedings related to the application of safeguard measures, which are temporary restrictions on imports to protect domestic industries from serious injury caused by increased imports. This practice includes representing clients in disputes before international trade bodies and ensuring compliance with international trade agreements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBI1.label: Statutory Rape
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBI1.definition: Nonforcible sexual intercourse with a person who is under the statutory age of consent.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBI4.label: Tort Claimants Committee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBI4.definition: A Tort Claimants Committee is typically established within bankruptcy proceedings or large-scale litigation contexts to represent the interests of individuals who have tort claims against the debtor or defendant. This committee works to ensure that the rights and recovery opportunities of tort claimants are protected and maximized during the legal process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBI5.label: Bankruptcy and Restructuring Events
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBI5.definition: Bankruptcy and Restructuring Events: The various legal proceedings and actions that occur during the process of bankruptcy and restructuring, including confirmation of a bankruptcy plan, asset sales, installment payments, joinder, auctions, creditor voting, initial meetings, disbursements, automatic stays, and financial management courses.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBIA.label: Federated Learning
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBIA.definition: Federated learning is an approach to machine learning that addresses data governance and privacy concerns by enabling the collaborative training of algorithms without transferring data to a central location. In this model, each device trains on data locally and shares its local model parameters instead of sharing the training data, and different federated learning systems have various topologies for parameter sharing.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBIF.label: L440 Other Trial Preparation and Support
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBIF.definition: The concept of L440 Other Trial Preparation and Support refers to activities and tasks related to trial preparation and support that do not fall under any other specific category within the broader concept of trial preparation and trial.
english_labels: L440 Other Trial Preparation and Support

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBIM.label: Harmful Bias
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBIM.definition: Harmful bias in an AI system refers to biases that create negative impacts, such as unfair or discriminatory outcomes. These biases can emerge from various factors, including human or system decisions across the AI lifecycle, pre-existing cultural and social biases in training data, technical limitations like non-representative data, or the use of AI systems in unanticipated contexts

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBIQ.label: Fijian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBIQ.definition: A language spoken in Fiji, which is a member of the Austronesian language family and is the official language of the country.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBIU.label: Objection to Professional Fees
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBIU.definition: An objection raised by a party to challenge the amount or reasonableness of fees charged by a professional for services rendered.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBIV.label: Watercraft
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBIV.definition: A Watercraft is a vehicle designed for travel on or in water, including boats, ships, submarines, and personal watercraft. These vessels are used for various purposes such as transportation, recreation, military operations, and commercial activities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBIX.label: Foreign Private Issuer Report
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBIX.definition: A Foreign Private Issuer Report is a document filed by foreign companies listed on U.S. exchanges, summarizing financial and operational data. It is a U.S.-specific requirement aimed at standardizing information for U.S. investors.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBIc.label: Florida County Court - Duval County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBIc.definition: A court located in Duval County, Florida that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographic area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBId.label: Product Liability Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBId.definition: Law relating to liability for injuries caused by defective or unsafe products.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBId.label: Negligent Entrustment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBId.definition: Negligent Entrustment is a legal claim that arises when a person allows someone else to use their property, such as a vehicle, knowing that the person is likely to cause harm due to their incompetence or recklessness.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBIg.label: Goods and Services Tax Payment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBIg.definition: Goods and Services Tax Payment encompasses all taxes and duties levied on the production, extraction, sale, transfer, leasing, or delivery of goods, as well as the rendering of services. This also includes taxes on the use of goods or permissions to use goods or perform activities, ensuring comprehensive taxation of economic activities related to goods and services.
english_labels: Payment of Tax on Goods and Services

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBIj.label: Expiration Date
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBIj.definition: For a legal proceeding or regulatory filing (e.g., patent registration, trademark registration) that filing's expiration date refers to the expiration date of a specific status, benefit, or action, as indicated in official documents such as visas, permits, or contracts. This date marks the end of the authorized period for a particular activity, residency, or employment, as determined by the relevant regulatory authority

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBIm.label: Motion to Convert
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBIm.definition: A Motion to Convert is a request made in a bankruptcy case to change the type of bankruptcy being filed, typically from Chapter 13 to Chapter 7.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBIn.label: Separation Agreement Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBIn.definition: Separation or dissolution of a legal entity or legal relationship (such as employment).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBIp.label: Standing Rock Sioux Tribe of North & South Dakota
english_labels: Standing Rock Sioux Tribe of North & South Dakota

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJ0.label: Immune System Disorders
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJ0.definition: Immune system disorders are conditions that result from abnormalities in the immune system, leading to improper immune responses. These disorders include a wide range of diseases, such as autoimmune diseases, immune deficiency disorders, and hypersensitivity reactions, which can cause significant impairment in the body's ability to fight infections and maintain homeostasis.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJ4.label: Transactional Document
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJ4.definition: A Transactional Document is a written or recorded representation of a legal agreement or transaction, such as a contract or deed, that memorializes the terms and conditions of the agreement between parties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJ5.label: Origination Clause Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJ5.definition: An Origination Clause claim refers to a legal argument challenging the constitutionality of a bill or law based on the requirement in the United States Constitution that revenue-raising bills must originate in the House of Representatives. This claim asserts that a particular law violates the Origination Clause by originating in the wrong legislative chamber, potentially rendering it invalid or unconstitutional.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJ8.label: New York City Court - Jamestown
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJ8.definition: A court located in Jamestown, New York that operates under the jurisdiction of the New York City Court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJ9.label: Non-metallic Mineral Rights
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJ9.definition: These pertain to the ownership and extraction of non-metallic minerals, such as coal, limestone, and gravel, from specific plots of land. As with metallic minerals, these rights can be leased, sold, or transferred.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJH.label: Georgia Superior Court - Telfair County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJH.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Telfair County, Georgia, with authority over civil and criminal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJH.label: Excited Utterance
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJH.definition: An Excited Utterance is a statement relating to a startling event or condition made while the declarant was under the stress of excitement caused by the event or condition. This hearsay exception is based on the idea that statements made under the influence of excitement or shock are unlikely to be fabricated due to the lack of time for reflection or deliberation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJK.label: Avoidance Action Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJK.definition: Avoidance Action Claims refer to legal claims made in bankruptcy and restructuring cases that seek to recover property or assets that were transferred or paid out in a way that is considered fraudulent or preferential, and may include actions such as turnover of property, setoff, and avoidance of statutory liens.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJN.label: Assignment of Case
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJN.definition: The concept of "Assignment of Case" refers to the act of designating a specific case to a particular individual or group for handling.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJV.label: oasis:Prohibition
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJV.definition: A prohibition is a type of deontic specification in the OASIS ontology, indicating that an action or behavior is not allowed or prohibited.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJW.label: Data Tampering
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJW.definition: Data tampering involves the unauthorized alteration of data, often to mislead or commit fraud. It can compromise the integrity of the data and lead to incorrect or false conclusions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJX.label: Cargo
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJX.definition: Cargo refers to goods or merchandise conveyed in a vessel, airplane, or vehicle. It encompasses all types of freight, excluding passengers' baggage, transported for commercial gain or military purposes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJY.label: Order Granting in Part, Denying in Part
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJY.definition: An "Order Granting in Part, Denying in Part" is a legal decision issued by a court that approves some requests made by a party and denies others.
english_labels: Order Granting in Part, Denying in Part

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJd.label: JF10 Preparation of the disclosure report and the disclosure proposal (UK J-CODE)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJd.definition: Preparation of the disclosure report and the disclosure proposal to comply with obligations that came in on 1-April-2013 (applicable to both manual and e-disclosure). All Disclosure related work required for the CMC. Additionally, this task encompasses work such as determining the location of documents, letters to client re disclosure obligations and setting up client based disclosure teams.
english_labels: JF10 Preparation of the disclosure report and the disclosure proposal (UK J-CODE)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJl.label: Civil Rights
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJl.definition: Civil rights are the rights of individuals to receive equal treatment and protection under the law, typically focusing on issues such as discrimination, freedom of speech, and the right to vote. These rights are enshrined in national laws and constitutions and are designed to protect individuals from unfair treatment or discrimination by the government or private organizations

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJp.label: Flat Antitrust Efforts Standard
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJp.definition: A Flat Antitrust Efforts Standard is a provision within antitrust efforts that requires a company to make a consistent effort to comply with antitrust laws, without any specific benchmarks or goals to meet.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJu.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Elk County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJu.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Elk County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering legal proceedings in Elk County, Pennsylvania.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Elk County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJy.label: Practice Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJy.definition: Practice Management refers to the administration and organization of a law firm's operations, including financial management, client relations, and human resources, within the context of the broader legal industry.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBJy.label: Miccosukee Tribe of Indians of Florida
english_labels: Miccosukee Tribe of Indians of Florida

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBK3.label: Examiner Investigation Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBK3.definition: Examiner Investigation Practice refers to the process of analyzing and evaluating assets by an examiner in order to investigate and gather information related to a legal matter.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBK4.label: Florida Circuit Court - Hillsborough County - 13th Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBK4.definition: The Florida Circuit Court - Hillsborough County (13th Circuit Court) is a specific court within the Florida Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Hillsborough County.
english_labels: Florida Circuit Court - Hillsborough County - 13th Circuit Court

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBK5.label: oasis:Associable
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBK5.definition: A legal concept within the LegalXML OASIS SCHEMA that pertains to the ability to associate or link information with other data based on a temporal characteristic.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBK6.label: Central Bank
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBK6.definition: A central bank is a national financial institution responsible for managing a country's monetary policy, issuing currency, and regulating the banking sector to ensure financial stability. Central banks play a crucial role in controlling inflation, setting interest rates, and serving as a lender of last resort to commercial banks during financial crises.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBK6.label: DEPRECATED SANDBOX VERSION: Contractual Clause Types
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBK6.definition: This concept refers to types of clauses that are commonly found in contracts, but this version is no longer in use and has been replaced by newer versions.
english_labels: DEPRECATED SANDBOX VERSION: Contractual Clause Types

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKA.label: Incitement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKA.definition: Incitement is the act of encouraging or persuading another person to commit a crime or unlawful act. It involves speech or conduct that is intended to provoke imminent illegal action.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKA.label: Stand Your Ground Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKA.definition: Stand Your Ground Law is a type of legislation that permits individuals to use force, including deadly force, to defend themselves without any obligation to retreat or flee if they believe they are in imminent danger of serious harm or death.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKB.label: Lacks Personal Knowledge Objection
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKB.definition: A Lacks Personal Knowledge Objection is raised when a party in a legal proceeding believes that a witness is testifying about matters beyond their direct experience or observation. This objection aims to ensure that testimony is based on firsthand knowledge and is reliable.
english_labels: Objection to Testimony Without Personal Experience

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKD.label: Texas District Court - Wood County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKD.definition: Texas District Court - Wood County: A court of law in Texas that has jurisdiction over legal cases within Wood County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKD.label: Ewe
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKD.definition: A language spoken by the Ewe people, primarily in Ghana and Togo.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKL.label: Employee Misconduct Event
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKL.definition: Employee misconduct event refers to an action or behavior by an employee that violates a company's policies, codes of conduct, or legal statutes. Such events can result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination, and may also have legal repercussions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKQ.label: Sac and Fox Tribe of the Mississippi in Iowa
english_labels: Sac and Fox Tribe of the Mississippi in Iowa

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKS.label: Chapter 15 Service List
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKS.definition: A Chapter 15 Service List is a specific type of document related to bankruptcy and restructuring proceedings that contains a list of parties who have been served with notice of the proceedings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKT.label: Appellate Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKT.definition: Any service before a court oflaw that is empowered to hear an appeal of a trial court or other lower tribunal.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKT.label: Workers' Compensation Discrimination Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKT.definition: A workers' compensation discrimination claim is a legal action brought by an employee who alleges that they have been subjected to unfair treatment, retaliation, or adverse actions by their employer due to filing a workers' compensation claim or exercising their rights under workers' compensation laws. Workers' compensation is a system designed to provide medical benefits and wage replacement for employees who suffer work-related injuries or illnesses. Employers are generally prohibited from discriminating or retaliating against employees who seek workers' compensation benefits.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKT.label: Mother and Child Health Public Benefit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKT.definition: Mother and Child Health Public Benefit refers to specialized government programs aimed at providing healthcare services or financial assistance specifically for mothers and their children. These may cover prenatal care, childbirth, postnatal care, and pediatric services to ensure the health and well-being of both mother and child. In the United States, one such program is the Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP).
english_labels: Mother and Child Health Public Benefit

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKX.label: Consideration
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKX.definition: Consideration refers to the value given in exchange for a promise or performance in a legal contract, often involving the transfer of money, property, or services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKX.label: Material Contracts
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKX.definition: Material Contracts are key contracts that a company is obligated to disclose because they significantly affect the company's operations, financial condition, or liquidity. These are typically included as exhibits in regulatory filings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKZ.label: Georgia District Court - Jackson County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKZ.definition: Georgia District Court - Jackson County: A specific court within the Georgia District Court system located in Jackson County, responsible for administering legal proceedings within its jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKb.label: Eastern Shoshone Tribe of the Wind River Reservation, Wyoming
english_labels: Eastern Shoshone Tribe of the Wind River Reservation, Wyoming

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKd.label: Insolvency Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKd.definition: Insolvency Practice encompasses the legal processes and procedures involved in handling the financial distress and liquidation of individuals and businesses unable to meet their debt obligations. It includes bankruptcy filings, debt restructuring, and the administration of insolvent estates. In the United Kingdom, insolvency is distinct from the U.S. concept of Bankruptcy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKh.label: Contribution Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKh.definition: A Contribution Claim is a legal claim made by a defendant seeking to recover a portion of damages paid to a plaintiff from another party who is also responsible for the same harm.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKm.label: Tax Invoice Client Name
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKm.definition: A tax invoice client name is a specific detail included in a fee invoice that identifies the client for whom legal services were provided and for which taxes are being invoiced.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKn.label: Arizona Superior Court - Mohave Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKn.definition: Arizona Superior Court - Mohave Cty. is a specific court located in Mohave County, Arizona that operates under the jurisdiction of the Arizona Superior Court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKp.label: Banking, Commercial Paper, and Creditor Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKp.definition: Banking, Commercial Paper, and Creditor Claims refer to legal claims and disputes related to banking transactions, commercial paper, and creditor rights, including issues such as dishonored checks, wrongful foreclosures, and fraudulent transfers.
english_labels: Banking, Commercial Paper, and Creditor Claims

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKs.label: Regulator
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBKs.definition: A regulator is an entity, typically a government agency or authority, responsible for overseeing and enforcing specific regulations within a particular industry or sector. Regulators ensure compliance with laws, standards, and guidelines to protect public interests, such as consumer safety, environmental protection, and market fairness.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBL1.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Menard County (8th Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Menard County (8th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBL2.label: Detainer Proceeding
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBL2.definition: A Detainer Proceeding is a legal process used to hold a person in custody until they can be transferred to another jurisdiction to face criminal charges.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBL4.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Pope County (1st Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Pope County (1st Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBL4.label: Interference with the Custody of Children
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBL4.definition: The concept of "Interference with the Custody of Children" refers to the act of intentionally taking, withholding, or concealing a child from their legal guardian or custodian without permission, which is considered a crime against individuals under the law.
english_labels: Interference with the Custody of Children

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBL7.label: New York District Court - Suffolk County - 1st District
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBL7.definition: A court located in Suffolk County, New York that is part of the larger New York District Court system.
english_labels: New York District Court - Suffolk County - 1st District

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBLA.label: Autism Spectrum Disorder
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBLA.definition: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by persistent difficulties in social communication and interaction, along with restricted, repetitive patterns of behavior, interests, or activities. The severity and manifestations of symptoms vary widely among individuals, making it a spectrum disorder.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBLI.label: "Confidential Information" Definition - Exceptions - Known Prior to Agreement
english_labels: "Confidential Information" Definition - Exceptions - Known Prior to Agreement

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBLO.label: Governance Risk
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBLO.definition: Governance Risk refers to the potential for negative consequences arising from an organization's ineffective or inadequate leadership, decision-making processes, and oversight structures. This can result from poor corporate governance practices, lack of transparency, or weak accountability mechanisms, ultimately leading to reputational damage, legal liabilities, and decreased stakeholder trust, which can impact the organization's performance and sustainability.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBLP.label: Georgia Superior Court - Jasper County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBLP.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Jasper County is a specific court within the Georgia Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Jasper County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBLT.label: Adultery
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBLT.definition: Voluntary sexual intercourse between a married person and someone who is not their spouse, which is considered as a ground for divorce.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBLV.label: Generalized Anxiety Disorder
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBLV.definition: Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) is a mental health condition characterized by persistent and excessive worry about various aspects of life, such as work, health, and social interactions, that is difficult to control. This anxiety is often accompanied by physical symptoms such as restlessness, fatigue, difficulty concentrating, irritability, muscle tension, and sleep disturbances.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBLV.label: Setoff
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBLV.definition: A setoff in bankruptcy refers to the right of a creditor to offset a debt owed to them by the debtor against a debt owed by the creditor to the debtor, thereby reducing the amount owed by the creditor to the debtor.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBLW.label: Data Architecture Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBLW.definition: Data Architecture Management involves organizing the data extraction, planning, design, and implementation of policies, structures, and processes that govern the organization, storage, and accessibility of data within an enterprise, ensuring data integrity, consistency, and efficient use across various applications and systems.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBLY.label: Regulatory Applicant
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBLY.definition: A Regulatory Applicant is an individual or entity that applies for authorization, licensing, or compliance approval from a regulatory authority. This role relates to sectors where operations are subject to legal and regulatory standards, ensuring adherence to established laws, guidelines, and norms.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBLZ.label: Clause Bank Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBLZ.definition: Clause Bank Management refers to the process of organizing and maintaining a repository of standardized legal clauses for efficient retrieval and use in legal documents.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBLo.label: Commission
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBLo.definition: A commission is an authoritative body formed by a government or other organization to oversee, manage, and regulate specific activities or issues. Commissions can vary widely in scope, such as city commissions for local governance, the European Commission for regional policy and law, or commissions on human rights to oversee and promote human rights protections.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBLs.label: Motion for Relief due to Fraud, Misrepresentation, or Other Misconduct
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBLs.definition: A Motion for Relief due to Fraud, Misrepresentation, or Other Misconduct is a legal request made to a court to set aside a previous order or judgment based on the opposing party's fraudulent, misleading, or wrongful actions.
english_labels: Motion for Relief due to Fraud, Misrepresentation, or Other Misconduct

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBLt.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Lawrence County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBLt.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Lawrence County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering legal proceedings in Lawrence County, Pennsylvania.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Lawrence County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBLz.label: Disability
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBLz.definition: Disability refers to a physical, mental, or sensory impairment that significantly limits one or more major life activities, such as walking, speaking, learning, or working. Disabilities can be congenital or acquired, temporary or permanent, and vary in severity. Various laws, such as the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) in the United States, protect individuals with disabilities from discrimination and ensure they have equal access to opportunities, services, and accommodations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBM2.label: Advice & Consent Clause Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBM2.definition: An Advice & Consent Clause claim is a legal argument asserting that a particular appointment or nomination made by a government official violates the Advice and Consent Clause of the United States Constitution. This claim contends that the appointment or nomination was made without obtaining the necessary advice and consent of a legislative body, typically the Senate, as required by the constitutional provision.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBM3.label: Intercreditor Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBM3.definition: An "Intercreditor Agreement" is a contract between two or more creditors that establishes the hierarchy and relationship of their claims against a common debtor. The agreement sets forth the rules and procedures for the distribution of assets and proceeds in the event of the debtor's default, bankruptcy, or insolvency.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMJ.label: Data Management and Strategy Services
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMJ.definition: Data Management and Strategy Services refers to the provision of expert advice and support in the planning, implementation, and maintenance of effective data management practices, including the development of strategies and policies, data governance, and data quality management.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBML.label: Car Renter Liable for Injury
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBML.definition: A legal principle that holds a person who rents a car responsible for any injuries or damages caused by the car while it is in their possession.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMM.label: Web Search Portals, Libraries, Archives, and Other Information Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMM.definition: Industries in the Web Search Portals, Libraries, Archives, and Other Information Services subsector group establishments supplying information, storing and providing access to information, searching and retrieving information, and operating Web sites that use search engines to allow for searching information on the Internet. The main components of the subsector are libraries, archives, and Web search portals.
english_labels: Web Search Portals, Libraries, Archives, and Other Information Industry

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMN.label: Motion Picture and Sound Recording Industries
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMN.definition: Industries in the Motion Picture and Sound Recording Industries subsector group establishments involved in the production and distribution of motion pictures and sound recordings. While producers and distributors of motion pictures and sound recordings issue works for sale as traditional publishers do, the processes are sufficiently different to warrant placing establishments engaged in these activities in a separate subsector. Production is typically a complex process that involves several distinct types of establishments that are engaged in activities, such as contracting with performers, creating the film or sound content, and providing technical postproduction services. Film distribution is often to exhibitors, such as theaters and broadcasters, rather than through the wholesale and retail distribution chain. When the product is in a mass-produced form, NAICS treats production and distribution as the major economic activity as it does in the Publishing Industries subsector, rather than as a subsidiary activity to the manufacture of such products. This subsector does not include establishments primarily engaged in the wholesale distribution of video and sound recordings, such as compact discs and audio tapes; these establishments are included in the Wholesale Trade sector. Reproduction of video and sound recordings that is carried out separately from establishments engaged in production and distribution is treated in NAICS as a manufacturing activity. Establishments that primarily acquire the rights to distribute video and sound recordings to the public via television or radio broadcast or streaming distribution services are classified in Subsector 516, Broadcasting and Content Providers. Establishments using facilities and infrastructure that they operate to distribute cable and satellite television subscription programming are included in Subsector 517, Telecommunications.
english_labels: Motion Picture and Sound Recording Industries
Motion Picture and Sound Recording Industry

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMN.label: Innocence Commission
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMN.definition: An Innocence Commission, often inspired by or affiliated with initiatives like the Innocence Project, is an organized body that investigates claims of wrongful convictions with the aim of exonerating individuals who have been unjustly imprisoned. These commissions often utilize new evidence, such as DNA testing, to re-examine cases where there might have been miscarriages of justice, and they advocate for legal reforms to prevent future wrongful convictions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMO.label: Sukuma
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMO.definition: Sukuma is a language spoken in Tanzania, characterized by its unique grammar and vocabulary.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMP.label: Waiver of Jury Trial Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMP.definition: A Waiver of Jury Trial Clause is a provision in a contract where parties agree to give up their right to a trial by jury in the event of a dispute, and instead have the dispute resolved by a judge or arbitrator.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMS.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Wells County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMS.definition: The Indiana Circuit Court - Wells County is a specific court within the Indiana Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Wells County, Indiana.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMU.label: Nursing Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMU.definition: Nursing Malpractice refers to a legal claim against a nurse for failing to provide the appropriate standard of care, resulting in harm or injury to a patient.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMa.label: Tenancy by the Entirety
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMa.definition: Tenancy by the Entirety is a form of concurrent property ownership available only to married couples, where both spouses hold equal and undivided interest in the property with the right of survivorship. This type of ownership ensures that upon the death of one spouse, the surviving spouse automatically inherits the entire property, and the property cannot be sold or encumbered without the consent of both parties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMc.label: Disaster Relief
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMc.definition: Disaster relief refers to the provision of immediate and coordinated assistance, including legal resources and services, to individuals and communities affected by natural or human-made catastrophes. The aim is to alleviate suffering, minimize further damage, and provide legal support for recovery and rebuilding efforts. Particular services might include helping obtain benefits and assistance, clearing title to property, and dealing with insurance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMf.label: Oregon Circuit Court - Polk County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMf.definition: The Oregon Circuit Court - Polk County is a specific court within the Oregon Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Polk County, Oregon.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMh.label: Persian, Old
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMh.definition: Old Persian (ca.600-400 B.C.) is an ancient language used in legal documents, artifacts, evidence, testimony, proceedings, or any other legal aspect during the mentioned time period.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMj.label: Data Poisoning
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMj.definition: Data Poisoning is a type of adversarial attack where malicious actors intentionally alter or manipulate the training data of a machine learning model to compromise its integrity and performance. This can lead to the model learning incorrect patterns or making erroneous predictions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMl.label: Objections to Cross Examination
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMl.definition: Objections to Cross-Examination are formal challenges raised by a party in a legal proceeding, questioning the propriety, relevance, or admissibility of questions or evidence presented during the cross-examination of a witness. These objections aim to ensure the integrity and fairness of the examination process and protect the witness from unfair or improper questioning.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMm.label: Summary of Schedules
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMm.definition: A Summary of Schedules is a document that provides a condensed overview of a debtor's assets, liabilities, and other financial information, and is typically filed as part of a bankruptcy or restructuring proceeding.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMr.label: Financial Services Commission
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMr.definition: A commission for financial services refers to a fee or percentage-based compensation that financial professionals, such as investment advisors or brokers, receive for providing financial services to clients. This compensation can be earned for services such as managing investments, providing financial advice, executing trades, or facilitating financial transactions

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMu.label: Excessive Force Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMu.definition: A claim made against a government entity or its agents for the use of unnecessary or unreasonable physical force in the course of their duties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMv.label: International Organization Visa - Representatives and Their Families
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMv.definition: An International Organization Visa for representatives and their families is a specialized visa category that permits individuals who represent their country at international organizations to enter and reside in a host country for the duration of their assignment. This visa often extends to the immediate family members of the representatives as well. It typically comes with certain diplomatic privileges and immunities to facilitate their work and official duties.
english_labels: International Organization Visa - Representatives and Their Families

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMv.label: Invoice Total Net Due Other ISO
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMv.definition: A legal billing term that refers to the total amount due on an invoice after deducting any applicable taxes or discounts, and expressed in a currency code specified by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO).
english_labels: Invoice Total Net Due Other ISO

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMw.label: Illinois Circuit Court - St. Clair County (20th Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - St. Clair County (20th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMw.label: Florida Circuit Court - Franklin County - 2nd Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMw.definition: A court located in Franklin County, Florida that is part of the larger Florida Circuit Court system.
english_labels: Florida Circuit Court - Franklin County - 2nd Circuit Court

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMy.label: Georgia Superior Court - Pierce County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMy.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Pierce County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Pierce County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMz.label: Minnesota District Court - Hubbard County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBMz.definition: Minnesota District Court - Hubbard County: A specific district court located in Hubbard County, Minnesota, responsible for administering legal proceedings within its jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBN7.label: Affiliate Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBN7.definition: An affiliate agreement is a legally binding contract between two parties, where one party agrees to promote or sell the products or services of the other party in exchange for a commission or other compensation.
