https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBN9.label: Cryptocurrency Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBN9.definition: Cryptocurrency law encompasses the legal rules and regulations governing the use, creation, and exchange of digital currencies, such as Bitcoin and Ethereum. It addresses issues related to security, taxation, and compliance with financial regulations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNA.label: Minority Stake
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNA.definition: A Minority Stake refers to ownership of less than 50% of a company's shares, which does not provide control over the company but can still offer significant influence. Minority stakeholders often rely on shareholder agreements and other mechanisms to protect their interests.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNF.label: Severance Pay
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNF.definition: Severance pay is a monetary compensation provided to employees upon termination of their employment, typically when they are laid off or made redundant. The amount and terms of severance pay can vary based on factors such as the duration of employment, contractual agreements, company policy, and legal regulations in the jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNI.label: Written Discovery Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNI.definition: Written Discovery Practice refers to the process of obtaining information from the opposing party in a legal matter through written requests, such as requests for documents or answers to written questions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNJ.label: Loan Participation Interest
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNJ.definition: Participations refer to the fractional interests in a loan or pool of loans sold by the original lender to other investors in the secondary market. These investors, known as participants, acquire the rights to receive payments and share in the risks associated with the underlying loans.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNK.label: Litigation Privilege
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNK.definition: A legal protection that allows parties involved in a lawsuit to keep certain communications and documents confidential from disclosure to the opposing party or in court proceedings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNL.label: Approval of Project Document
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNL.definition: The Approval of Project Document is a specific type of Project Management Document that signifies the authorized acceptance or agreement of a particular project document by a designated individual or group.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNL.label: Sale of Premises Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNL.definition: A Sale of Premises Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the terms and conditions for the sale of a property or real estate.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNL.label: Preferred Shares
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNL.definition: Preferred Shares represent a class of ownership in a company that confers preferential treatment regarding dividend payments and asset distribution in the event of liquidation. These shares typically do not carry voting rights but offer a fixed dividend that must be paid before any dividends are distributed to common shareholders.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNN.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Dubois County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNN.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Dubois County, Indiana, with the power to hear and decide a wide range of legal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNQ.label: North American Indian languages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNQ.definition: North American Indian languages are a group of structured systems of communication used by indigenous peoples of North America, consisting of unique grammar and vocabulary.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNT.label: Public Benefit Document
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNT.definition: A public benefit document is an official form, notification, or record associated with a government-provided public assistance program. These documents may include applications, eligibility criteria, award letters, or notices of changes to benefits, and serve as the legal foundation for the provision and management of public benefits to individuals or families.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNW.label: Court Order Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNW.definition: A Court Order Clause is a provision in a contract that requires one or both parties to comply with a court order or judgment related to the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNY.label: Banda languages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNY.definition: The Banda languages are a group of structured systems of communication that consist of grammar and vocabulary, and are a subset of the larger category of languages.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNZ.label: Purchase Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNZ.definition: A Purchase Agreement is a legally binding contract between two or more parties that outlines the terms and conditions of a transaction involving the sale of goods or services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNc.label: Insurance Policy Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNc.definition: A claim made by an individual or entity to an insurance company for compensation or reimbursement for a loss or damage covered by an insurance policy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNg.label: Corsican
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNg.definition: Corsican (Language) is a structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary, and is spoken in Corsica and parts of Italy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNm.label: Tracker Certificate
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNm.definition: A Tracker Certificate is a financial instrument that allows participation in the development of the underlying asset(s). These certificates reflect the underlying price movements 1:1, adjusted by the conversion ratio and any related fees, offering a risk profile comparable to direct investment in the underlying asset(s).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNm.label: Bailments
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNm.definition: A bailment is a legal relationship in which one party (the bailee) holds personal property belonging to another party (the bailor) for a specific purpose, with the understanding that the property will be returned or disposed of according to the bailor's instructions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNu.label: Deposition Subpoena
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNu.definition: A deposition subpoena is a legal document that requires a witness to appear and give testimony in a deposition, which is a pre-trial questioning under oath.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNz.label: Vandalism
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNz.definition: DEFINITION OF Destruction/Damage/Vandalism of Property — To willfully or maliciously destroy, damage, deface, or otherwise injure real or personal property without the consent of the owner or the person having custody or control of it.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNz.label: Management's Discussion and Analysis
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBNz.definition: MD&A, or Management's Discussion and Analysis, is a section often included in annual and quarterly reports that provides an overview of the company's financial condition and operational performance. It is presented from the perspective of management and aims to offer insights into past performance, future plans, and material risks.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBO0.label: Contact Name Suffix - IV (Fourth)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBO0.definition: The suffix "IV" stands for "Fourth" and is used after a person's full name to indicate that they are the fourth generation in their family to bear that name. This suffix is used to differentiate among family members in formal, legal, or financial contexts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBO1.label: Arkansas Circuit Court - Clark Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBO1.definition: The Arkansas Circuit Court - Clark Cty. is a specific court within the Arkansas Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Clark County, Arkansas.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBO5.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Bradford County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBO5.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court in Bradford County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court system that handles minor criminal offenses, traffic violations, and civil cases involving amounts up to $12,000.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Bradford County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOB.label: Schizophrenia Spectrum and Psychotic Disorders
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOB.definition: Psychiatric Disability, also known as Psychotic Disorder, refers to a wide range of mental health conditions that significantly impair an individual's cognitive, emotional, and social functioning. These disorders are characterized by delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, or grossly disorganized or catatonic behavior, causing a clinically significant decline in functioning. Symptoms and signs may include, but are not limited to, inability to initiate and persist in goal-directed activities, social withdrawal, flat or inappropriate affect, poverty of thought and speech, loss of interest or pleasure, disturbances of mood, odd beliefs and mannerisms, and paranoia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOO.label: Oath or Affirmation Clause Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOO.definition: An Oath or Affirmation Clause claim refers to a legal argument based on the Oath or Affirmation Clause found in various legal contexts, including the United States Constitution, asserting that individuals are required to take an oath or affirm their commitment to uphold certain obligations, duties, or principles. It ensures that individuals solemnly affirm their allegiance, honesty, and adherence to specific requirements or standards, such as those related to public office, testimony in court, or membership in an organization.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOT.label: Aromanian; Arumanian; Macedo-Romanian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOT.definition: Aromanian, also known as Arumanian or Macedo-Romanian, is a language that belongs to the Language top-level class and is spoken in certain regions of the Balkans.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOW.label: Engagement Location - Locality
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOW.definition: Locality where the engagement was originated (e.g., client location).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOX.label: New York City Court - Newburgh
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOX.definition: A court located in Newburgh, New York that operates under the jurisdiction of the New York City Court system.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOY.label: Voluntary Bankruptcy Petition
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOY.definition: A voluntary bankruptcy petition is a legal document filed by an individual or business seeking relief from their debts through the bankruptcy process, done willingly and without coercion.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOc.label: Georgia Superior Court - Clarke County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOc.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Clarke County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Clarke County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOc.label: Remedies in Family Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOc.definition: Ancillary Relief refers to additional financial orders made by a court in the context of divorce or separation proceedings, including maintenance payments, division of assets, and financial support. These orders are intended to ensure fair financial arrangements between the parties involved.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOd.label: Indiana Superior Court - Johnson County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOd.definition: Indiana Superior Court - Johnson County: A court of general jurisdiction in Indiana that hears civil and criminal cases within Johnson County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOh.label: Client Internal Counsel
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOh.definition: Internal counsel for a client -- for a particular matter.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOh.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Northampton County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOh.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court located in Northampton County, responsible for administering legal proceedings within its jurisdiction.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Northampton County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOj.label: Midwife Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOj.definition: Negligent or improper actions or omissions by a midwife during the course of providing medical care, resulting in harm or injury to the patient.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOj.label: Manufacturing Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOj.definition: The Manufacturing industry group comprises establishments engaged in the mechanical, physical, or chemical transformation of materials, substances, or components into new products. The assembling of component parts of manufactured products is considered manufacturing. This industry group does not include construction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOj.label: Acceptance in International Trade
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOj.definition: An acceptance is a contractual agreement by an importer to pay the amount due for receiving goods at a specified date in the future. Documents are presented for acceptance in international trade.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOm.label: Public Comment Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOm.definition: Public comment in the context of rulemaking refers to the procedure that allows individuals, organizations, or other stakeholders to submit their views and concerns on proposed regulations before they are finalized. This practice is often mandated by law in democratic systems and aims to enhance transparency, public participation, and the quality of the regulatory process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOt.label: 04_1 Civil Rights (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOt.definition: 04_1 Civil Rights (PACER NoS) refers to a specific category of civil rights cases in the PACER system, including cases related to employment, voting, disabilities, education, housing, and other civil rights issues.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOu.label: Actor Expert
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOu.definition: Actor or party in the litigation who is also an expert in the field at issue.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOu.label: Application for Administrative Expenses
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOu.definition: An Application for Administrative Expenses is a request made in a bankruptcy case for reimbursement of expenses incurred in administering the bankruptcy estate, such as fees for attorneys or accountants.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOw.label: Child Support Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOw.definition: A Child Support Claim is a legal action taken by a parent to seek financial support from the other parent for the upbringing and care of their child, which falls under the broader category of Custody and Visitation Claims.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOz.label: Medical Record
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBOz.definition: A medical record is a comprehensive and confidential document that contains a patient's medical history, including information about their medical conditions, diagnoses, treatments, prescriptions, and interactions with healthcare providers. These records are typically maintained by healthcare institutions and practitioners to track and manage a patient's health and treatment over time, and they are essential for providing continuity of care and ensuring accurate medical documentation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBP1.label: Empty Chair
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBP1.definition: The Empty Chair is a legal defense strategy in civil litigation where the defendant is absent from the trial and is not represented by counsel.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBP4.label: Bosnian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBP4.definition: Bosnian (Language) is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary used in Bosnia and Herzegovina and other regions, and is a subcategory of the Language class.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBP6.label: Water Quality Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBP6.definition: Law governing the release of pollutants into water resources.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPB.label: Attorney Work Product Protection
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPB.definition: Attorney Work Product Protection is a legal privilege that shields materials prepared by an attorney or their team in anticipation of litigation from discovery by opposing parties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPD.label: Medical Form
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPD.definition: A Medical Form is a standardized document used within healthcare settings for collecting, storing, or conveying information related to a patient's medical history, condition, or treatment. Examples include consent forms, referral forms, and records release forms.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPE.label: Continuation Coverage Plan
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPE.definition: Continuation coverage plans, such as the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act (COBRA) in the U.S., allow former employees to continue their employer-sponsored health insurance for a limited period after employment ends. The individual is generally responsible for the full premium cost plus an administrative fee.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPM.label: Adaptive Learning
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPM.definition: Adaptive Learning, or Adaptiveness, is the characteristic of some AI systems that allows them to change their behavior while in use based on interactions with input and data. This adaptation may involve changes in the model's weights or its internal structure, enabling the system to produce different results for the same inputs compared to its previous state.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPN.label: New York Style Closing Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPN.definition: A New York Style Closing Clause is a specific type of contractual clause used in legal agreements that outlines the procedures and requirements for the finalization of the agreement, typically including the location and governing law of the agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPN.label: Non Solicitation Agreement Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPN.definition: A Non-Solicitation Agreement Clause is a provision in a contract that prohibits one party from soliciting or hiring employees or clients of the other party for a specified period of time after the termination of the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPP.label: Tuvinian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPP.definition: Tuvinian is a language that belongs to the Language class and is spoken in the Tuva Republic of Russia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPQ.label: Contract Formation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPQ.definition: Contract Formation is the event when a contract is formed and fully executed, meeting all legal requirements necessary for it to be binding and enforceable. This includes the elements of offer, acceptance, consideration, mutual assent, and legality of purpose.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPX.label: Debt Collection Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPX.definition: Debt Collection Practice encompasses the methods and procedures employed by creditors and collection agencies to recover overdue debts from borrowers. These practices must comply with relevant laws and regulations to ensure ethical and legal collection efforts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPZ.label: Forum Non Conveniens
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPZ.definition: A legal doctrine that allows a court to dismiss a case if it determines that another court, with jurisdiction over the case, is a more appropriate forum for the case to be heard.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPe.label: Ambassador
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPe.definition: An ambassador is a diplomatic representative who serves as the highest-ranking official of their home country's government in a foreign nation. The ambassador is responsible for managing diplomatic relations, representing their country's interests, and overseeing the activities of their nation's embassy or consulate in the host country.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPe.label: Guilty
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPe.definition: In a criminal context, "guilty" is a legal determination made by a court or jury when the defendant has been found responsible or culpable for the charges brought against them. It signifies that the defendant has been proven to have committed the alleged crime and may face penalties or sentencing as a result of the guilty verdict.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPp.label: Fiscal Year
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPp.definition: A fiscal year is a 12-month period used by governments, businesses, and organizations for accounting and financial reporting purposes. It may differ from the calendar year and is set according to the specific financial and operational needs of the entity.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPw.label: tax_tier_detail segment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPw.definition: "There will be 0 or more TAX_TIER_DETAIL segments per file. If no TAX.tax_tiers is defined, no TAX_TIER_DETAIL section would be included in the file. This segment must fully define each of the tiers involved in the tax calculation, even if the invoice total is less than the tax tier. This segment defines the tax tiers specified in TAX.tax_tiers and tallies the amount of tax at each tier for this invoice. Unlike regular taxes, Tiered Taxes roll up to the invoice level whereas regular taxes roll up to the matter/invoice level. A Tiered Tax is one where the tax rate can vary depending on the total of the file. As compared to other kinds of taxes where a flat tax rate applies to the taxable item total, multiple tax rates apply. All tiers associated with the Tiered Tax as set forth by the tax authority must be represented in this segment, even if the tier exceeds the total of taxable items in the file. Illustration: Let's say there is a Tiered Tax where the tax rate is 10% for $0 to $25,000, 12.5% for $25,000 to $50,000, 15% for $50,000 to $100,000, 17.5% for $100,000 to $200,000, and 20% for amounts above that amount. Let's also say that an invoice includes $125,000 in taxable items subject to the Tiered Tax. For $125,000 in taxable detail, the TAX_TIER_DETAIL segment would include 5 lines for each of the 5 defined tiers as follows: tier 1 ($0 >= $25,000) = $25,000.00 * 10% = $2,500.00 tax due tier 2 ($25,000.01 >= $50,000) = $25,000.00 * 12.5% = $3,125.00 tax tier 3 ($50,000.01 >= $100,000) = $50,000.00 * 15% = $7,500.00 tax due tier 4 ($100,000.01 >= $200,000) = $25,000.00 * 17.5% = $4,375,00 tax due tier 5 ($200,000.01 and above) = $0 * 20% = $0.00 tax due Every tier must be defined in the file regardless of whether it exceeds the amount of taxable items. Using the example above, the TAX_TIER_DETAIL segment must include a representation for tier 5. The total tax due on this tiered tx_id then is $17,500.00 (the sum of the amounts above in blue). "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPy.label: Sichuan Yi; Nuosu
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBPy.definition: Sichuan Yi; Nuosu (Language) is a written or spoken structured system of communication used by the Yi people in Sichuan Province, China, and is a subcategory of the Language class.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQ5.label: Motion for Supplemental Information
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQ5.definition: A Motion for Supplemental Information is a formal request made by a party in a trial court seeking additional evidence or information to support their case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQA.label: "Material Adverse Effect" Definition - Exceptions - Changes in Law
english_labels: "Material Adverse Effect" Definition - Exceptions - Changes in Law

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQC.label: Trademark Infringement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQC.definition: The unauthorized use of a trademark or service mark, including the trafficking of counterfeit marks, which violates the rights of the owner and may result in legal action under unfair competition or intellectual property claims.
english_labels: Trafficking Counterfeit Trade or Service Marks

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQD.label: People Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQD.definition: The concept of People Management refers to the legal use cases related to managing employees, including temporary placement, recruiting, appraisals, and professional development.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQD.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Forest County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQD.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court located in Forest County, which is responsible for administering justice in minor criminal and civil matters within its jurisdiction.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Forest County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQG.label: Governmental Body
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQG.definition: Administrative entities of government or state agency or appointed commission, as a permanent or semi-permanent governmental organization that oversees or administers specific governmental functions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQG.label: zip_postal_code
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQG.definition: "The postal code of parent. Required except in countries without an equivalent address component. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQJ.label: Climate Stability Rights
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQJ.definition: Climate Stability Rights pertain to the legal entitlements and principles recognizing the fundamental right of present and future generations to a stable and healthy climate. This concept underscores the obligation of governments, industries, and other entities to take proactive measures to mitigate climate change, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and preserve the planet's ecological balance. These rights emphasize the importance of intergenerational equity, sustainable development, and global cooperation to ensure a habitable environment for all.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQN.label: Florida Circuit Court - Okaloosa County - 1st Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQN.definition: Florida Circuit Court - Okaloosa County (1st Circuit Court) is a specific court within the Florida Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Okaloosa County.
english_labels: Florida Circuit Court - Okaloosa County - 1st Circuit Court

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQR.label: Right to a Fair Trial
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQR.definition: The right to a fair trial is a fundamental legal principle that ensures individuals facing legal proceedings are treated impartially, justly, and in accordance with established legal procedures. This right, which is protected by various international human rights instruments and national constitutions, includes elements such as the presumption of innocence, the right to counsel, the right to a speedy and public trial, the right to an impartial judge or jury, and the right to confront witnesses and present evidence

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQU.label: American Call Option Style
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQU.definition: An American Call Option Style is an option contract that grants the holder the right to purchase the underlying asset at a specified strike price at any time between the purchase date and the expiration date. This flexibility allows the holder to benefit from favorable price movements in the underlying asset at any point during the option's life.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQX.label: UK Electoral Commission
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQX.definition: The UK Electoral Commission is an independent regulatory body responsible for overseeing and ensuring the integrity and fairness of elections and referendums in the United Kingdom. It regulates political party funding, monitors compliance with electoral laws, provides guidance and support for voters and electoral administrators, and conducts public awareness campaigns to promote democratic participation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQX.label: Bankruptcy Plan Vote
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQX.definition: A Bankruptcy Plan Vote (Event) is a specific type of event within the broader category of Bankruptcy and Restructuring Events, where stakeholders vote on a proposed plan for the distribution of assets and liabilities in a bankruptcy case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQZ.label: Theft of Motor Vehicle Parts/Accessories
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQZ.definition: Theft of Motor Vehicle Parts/Accessories: The act of taking or removing parts or accessories from a motor vehicle without the owner's consent, with the intention of permanently depriving the owner of their property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQa.label: Activist Shareholder
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQa.definition: An Activist Shareholder is an investor who uses their equity stake in a corporation to push for changes within the company. These changes can include modifications in management, corporate policies, strategic direction, and overall governance to increase shareholder value or address specific concerns.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQd.label: L450 Trial and Hearing Attendance
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQd.definition: The concept of L450 Trial and Hearing Attendance refers to the act of physically being present at a trial or hearing, and is a subcategory of the broader concept of trial preparation and trial.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQd.label: Investment Fund Unit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQd.definition: Investment Fund Unit refers to ownership interests in certain types of investment funds or pooled investment vehicles, such as mutual funds, ETFs, and REITs. Unlike traditional shares in a corporation, units represent a proportional stake in the collective assets of the fund, providing investors with a share of profits, losses, and distributions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQh.label: California Superior Court - San Diego Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQh.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in San Diego County, California, with the power to hear and decide a wide range of legal cases.
english_labels: California Superior Court - San Diego Cty.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQi.label: Debt Collection Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQi.definition: Debt Collection Law (also known as Debt Recovery Law) refers to the legal processes and actions taken to collect outstanding debts owed by individuals or businesses. It involves methods such as negotiation, litigation, and enforcement of judgments to ensure creditors receive payment. The legal practices and regulations related to the collection of debts by creditors or third-party agencies seek to ensure fair treatment of debtors and compliance with statutory procedures during the collection process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQj.label: contact_info segment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQj.definition: "This is not an actual segment of the file, per se, like the rest of the segments listed above. This segment contains a list of fields that will be used to represent contact information. When a contact is requested in a segment, that element will be listed and all fields in this segment will be the children of that element. The EXTEND_HEADER segment was purposely omitted from this segment. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQn.label: Credit Counseling Waiver
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQn.definition: A Credit Counseling Waiver is a legal document that allows an individual to waive the requirement of credit counseling before filing for bankruptcy or restructuring.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQq.label: Client ID
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQq.definition: The provider's code for the buyer.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQq.label: International Trade Tax Payment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQq.definition: International Trade Tax Payment covers revenue received by the government from the purchase and sale of foreign exchange at different rates, when the government exercises monopoly powers to extract a margin between the purchase and sales price, other than to cover administrative costs. This revenue constitutes a compulsory levy exacted from both purchasers and sellers of foreign exchange and is equivalent to import and export duties in a single exchange rate system. It also includes profits of export or import monopolies and other taxes specifically levied on international trade or transactions.
english_labels: Other taxes on international trade and transactions

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQr.label: Accountant-Client Privilege
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQr.definition: A legal protection that allows communication between an accountant and their client to remain confidential and not be disclosed in court without the client's consent.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQs.label: Visa for Dependent of Intermittent Intra-Company Transferee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQs.definition: The visa for dependents of intermittent intra-company transferees (in the U.S., the L-2 visa) allows spouses and minor children of intra-company transferees (e.g., L-1 visa holders), including intermittent transferees, to accompany them during their stay in the destination country (e.g., U.S.) Spouses holding an L-2 visa may also apply for work authorization
english_labels: Visa for Dependent of Intermittent Intra-Company Transferee

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQs.label: Statement of Services Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQs.definition: A Statement of Services Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the specific services that will be provided by one party to another.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQt.label: Votic
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQt.definition: Votic is a language that belongs to the Language top-level class and is spoken by the Votic people in Estonia and Russia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQw.label: Invoice Terms
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBQw.definition: Invoice terms refers to the specific information related to billing and payment for legal services provided within the context of an engagement agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBR1.label: Advanced Health Care Directive
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBR1.definition: An Advanced Health Care Directive is a legal document that allows an individual to specify their medical treatment preferences and appoint a healthcare agent to make decisions on their behalf if they become unable to do so.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBR3.label: Visitation Rights of Sibling
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBR3.definition: The Visitation Rights of Sibling refer to the legal entitlement of a brother or sister to spend time with their sibling who is under the custody of one or both parents, and the legal procedures and rights involved in such visitation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBR4.label: Motion for New Trial - Newly Discovered Evidence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBR4.definition: A Motion for New Trial - Newly Discovered Evidence is a legal request made by a party to a case asking the court to grant a new trial based on evidence that was not available during the original trial and could have changed the outcome.
english_labels: Motion for New Trial - Newly Discovered Evidence

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBR4.label: Feticide
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBR4.definition: The intentional killing of a fetus, typically committed by a third party, which is considered a criminal offense under the category of criminal homicide.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRE.label: Governmental Tort Liability
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRE.definition: Governmental Tort Liability refers to the legal responsibility of a government entity for harm caused by its employees or agents while acting within the scope of their employment or authority.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRF.label: Post-Grant Review
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRF.definition: A Post-Grant Review (PGR) is a type of administrative dispute proceeding practice conducted by the U.S. Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB) to review the validity of a granted patent.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRJ.label: Buy Back Option Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRJ.definition: A buy back option clause is a provision in a contract that allows one party to repurchase property or assets from the other party at a predetermined price and time.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRN.label: Lack of Insurance Coverage
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRN.definition: Lack of insurance coverage refers to a situation where an individual or entity does not have an insurance policy, or the existing policy does not cover a specific risk, loss, or event. This can result in financial liability for the uninsured party, who must bear the cost of any damages or losses incurred.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRP.label: Residential Real Estate Asset
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRP.definition: A Residential Real Estate Asset is a property designated for residential use, including houses, townhouses, condominiums, and mobile homes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRS.label: Death of A Limited Partner Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRS.definition: A Death of A Limited Partner Clause is a provision in a partnership agreement that outlines the procedures to be followed in the event of the death of a limited partner.
english_labels: Death of A Limited Partner Clause

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRT.label: Health Care Provider
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRT.definition: A Health Care Provider is a professional or institution licensed to provide medical services, treatment, or advice to individuals seeking health care. This term encompasses a wide range of practitioners and organizations responsible for diagnosing, treating, and preventing illness, injury, and other physical and mental impairments in human beings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRX.label: Motion for Permanent Injunction
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRX.definition: A Motion for Permanent Injunction is a legal request to prohibit a party from engaging in certain activities permanently, as opposed to temporarily, in order to prevent harm or damage.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRZ.label: Article 5 Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRZ.definition: An Article V claim pertains to a legal argument based on Article V of the U.S. Constitution, which sets out the process for amending the Constitution. Such a claim might arise in disputes over the interpretation or application of the amendment process, including the proposal and ratification of amendments.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRb.label: Occupational License
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRb.definition: An occupational license is a permit or certification issued by a governmental or professional body that authorizes an individual to practice a specific profession or trade. This type of license is generally required for professions that have an impact on public health, safety, or welfare, such as healthcare providers, lawyers, and contractors.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRc.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Ozark County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRc.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Ozark County refers to a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Ozark County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRe.label: Certificate of No Objection
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRe.definition: A Certificate of No Objection is a legal document that certifies that there are no objections or hindrances to a particular action or transaction, typically in the context of bankruptcy and restructuring.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRf.label: Amendment to Operating Agreement Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRf.definition: An Amendment to Operating Agreement Clause is a provision added to an operating agreement that modifies or alters a previous clause in the agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRj.label: Passport Valid From
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRj.definition: Passport Valid From refers to the specific day, month, and year from which an individual's passport becomes valid. This date marks the beginning of the passport's period of validity and is used for identification and verification purposes during travel and various legal procedures.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRk.label: Agency Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRk.definition: An agency agreement is a type of agreement between two parties where one party (the agent) is authorized to act on behalf of the other party (the principal) in certain matters, such as making contracts or managing finances.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRl.label: No Smoking Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRl.definition: A No Smoking Clause is a provision in a contract that prohibits smoking in a certain area or premises.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRl.label: Employee Matters Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRl.definition: A provision in a contract that pertains to the rights, obligations, and responsibilities of employees, including but not limited to compensation, benefits, and termination.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRm.label: Deceit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRm.definition: Deceit is a type of fraudulent claim that involves intentionally misleading or tricking someone in order to gain an advantage or cause harm.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRo.label: Unrestricted Asset Ownership
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRo.definition: Unrestricted Asset Ownership indicates the absence of limitations or special conditions on the ownership, transfer, or sale of securities. This attribute allows free and unencumbered transferability and ownership of financial assets without regulatory or contractual constraints.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRo.label: Breach of Implied Warranty of Habitability
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRo.definition: The Breach of Implied Warranty of Habitability refers to a legal claim that arises when a landlord fails to provide a tenant with a safe and habitable living environment, which is implied in every lease agreement.
english_labels: Breach of Implied Warranty of Habitability

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRp.label: Oregon Circuit Court - Clackamas County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRp.definition: The Oregon Circuit Court - Clackamas County is a specific court within the Oregon Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Clackamas County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRr.label: New York City Court - Peekskill
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRr.definition: A court located in Peekskill, New York that operates under the jurisdiction of the New York City Court system.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRt.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - York County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRt.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court in York County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court system that handles minor criminal offenses, traffic violations, and civil cases involving amounts up to $12,000.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - York County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRx.label: Cruel and Unusual Punishment Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBRx.definition: A cruel and unusual punishment claim is a legal action initiated by an individual alleging that their Eighth Amendment right to be free from cruel and unusual punishment has been violated by the government or a government actor. The Eighth Amendment prohibits the government from imposing punishments that are excessive, torturous, or barbaric. A cruel and unusual punishment claim may arise in various contexts, such as when a person is subjected to excessive physical or mental pain, suffering, or humiliation during the course of their punishment, when a person is punished for a non-violent offense in a way that is disproportionate to the crime, or when a person is denied necessary medical treatment while in custody.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBS7.label: New Jersey Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBS7.definition: The New Jersey Circuit Court is a court within the New Jersey State Courts system that has jurisdiction over certain types of cases and operates within a specific geographic area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSF.label: 430 Banks and Banking (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSF.definition: Action filed under the Federal Home Loan Bank Act 12:1421-1449, Home Owners Loan Act 12:1461 or Federal Reserve Acts 12:142 et seq.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSK.label: Florida County Court - Dixie County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSK.definition: A court located in Dixie County, Florida that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSO.label: Unjust Enrichment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSO.definition: Unjust Enrichment refers to a legal claim that arises when one party has been enriched at the expense of another party, without any legal justification or basis for such enrichment, and the enriched party should therefore be required to make restitution to the other party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSP.label: Nepali
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSP.definition: Nepali (Language) is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary used in Nepal and some parts of India.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSQ.label: News Source Privilege
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSQ.definition: News source privilege is a legal principle that allows journalists to refuse to disclose the identities of confidential sources or unpublished information obtained during the newsgathering process. This privilege is grounded in the First Amendment's freedom of the press and is intended to protect the flow of information to the public by ensuring the confidentiality of sources.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSS.label: New York City Court - Fulton
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSS.definition: New York City Court - Fulton is a specific court located in New York City that operates under the jurisdiction of the larger New York City Court system.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSV.label: Foreign Investments in US Real Property Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSV.definition: A Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA) claim involves legal action taken against individuals or entities for failing to comply with the disclosure and registration requirements mandated by FARA. Such claims seek to enforce transparency and accountability regarding foreign influence on U.S. political and public processes.
english_labels: Foreign Investments in US Real Property Claim
Foreign Real Estate Investment Tax Claim

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSX.label: Georgia Superior Court - Gordon County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSX.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Gordon County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Gordon County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSa.label: Hemophilia
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSa.definition: Hemophilia is a genetic disorder characterized by the inability of blood to clot properly, leading to excessive bleeding from minor injuries or spontaneous bleeding without apparent cause. The condition is due to a deficiency or dysfunction in specific clotting factors necessary for normal blood coagulation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSe.label: Bad Check Crime
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSe.definition: Knowingly and intentionally writing and/or negotiating checks drawn against insufficient or nonexistent funds.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSf.label: Territorial Market Segment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSf.definition: A territorial market segment refers to a group of consumers or businesses categorized based on the geographical boundaries or territories within which they operate. This segmentation allows companies to tailor their marketing strategies and product offerings to the specific characteristics and needs of different countries, regions, or localities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSh.label: Georgia Superior Court - Haralson County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSh.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia, located in Haralson County and presided over by a judge.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSi.label: Georgia Superior Court - Fannin County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSi.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Fannin County, Georgia, with authority over civil and criminal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSm.label: Official Committee of Creditors
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSm.definition: In U.S. bankruptcy law under chapter 11, the United States Trustee may appoint an official committee of unsecured creditors. The purpose of this committee is to represent the overall interests of all unsecured creditors.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSt.label: Angel Investor
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSt.definition: High-net-worth individuals who provide capital for startups, often in exchange for equity or convertible debt.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSy.label: Business Judgment Rule
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSy.definition: The Business Judgment Rule is a legal principle that shields corporate directors and officers from liability for decisions made in good faith and with reasonable care in the best interests of the company, even if those decisions ultimately result in negative consequences.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSy.label: Ethics Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBSy.definition: An ethics claim is a formal allegation that an individual or organization has violated ethical standards or principles within a specific profession or field. These claims can arise in various contexts, such as legal ethics, medical ethics, or government ethics, and often lead to investigations and disciplinary actions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBT0.label: Direct Patent Infringement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBT0.definition: The unauthorized making, using, selling, or importing of a patented invention by a party without the permission of the patent owner.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBT0.label: No Subletting Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBT0.definition: A "No Subletting Clause" is a provision in a contract that prohibits the tenant from subleasing the property to another party without the landlord's prior written consent.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBTD.label: Motion for New Trial - Format and Tactics
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBTD.definition: A Motion for New Trial - Format and Tactics is a specific type of legal document filed by a party after a trial, requesting the court to set aside the verdict and order a new trial based on specific grounds and strategies.
english_labels: Motion for New Trial - Format and Tactics

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBTF.label: Chickens
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBTF.definition: Chickens are domesticated birds belonging to the species Gallus gallus domesticus, commonly raised for their meat, eggs, and feathers. They are one of the most widespread and important sources of protein in agriculture, with numerous breeds adapted for specific purposes such as egg-laying or meat production.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBTG.label: Digital Transformation Services
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBTG.definition: Digital Transformation Services refer to consulting and management services that help organizations adopt and integrate digital technologies and processes to improve their business operations and customer experiences.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBTH.label: O-3 Visa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBTH.definition: An O-3 visa is issued to the immediate family members of O-1 and O-2 visa holders, allowing them to accompany or join the primary visa holder in the U.S. This visa category includes spouses and unmarried children under the age of 21.
english_labels: Family Visa For Extraordinary Talent Holders

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBTL.label: New York Appellate Division - 3d Dept.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBTL.definition: The New York Appellate Division - 3d Dept. is a specific court within the New York Supreme Court - Appellate Division that hears appeals from lower courts in the third department of New York State.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBTM.label: Changes in Target's Industry Language
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBTM.definition: Changes in Target's Industry Language refers to modifications in the terminology and language used in the industry of the target company, which may have an impact on the Material Adverse Effect (MAE) definition and carveouts in a legal agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBTR.label: Break Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBTR.definition: A break clause is a provision in a contract that allows one or both parties to terminate the agreement before the end of its term.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBTR.label: Assumption Agreement Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBTR.definition: An Assumption Agreement Clause is a provision in a contract that requires one party to take on the obligations and liabilities of another party in a specific situation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBTS.label: Sycuan Band of the Kumeyaay Nation
english_labels: Sycuan Band of the Kumeyaay Nation

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBTf.label: Anticipatory Breach of Contract
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBTf.definition: Anticipatory Breach of Contract refers to a situation where one party to a contract indicates, before the time for performance, that they will not perform their obligations under the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBTh.label: Prakrit languages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBTh.definition: Prakrit languages are a group of ancient Indian languages that were spoken in the Indian subcontinent before the emergence of Sanskrit.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBTn.label: Indiana Superior Court - Ripley County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBTn.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Indiana that has the authority to hear and decide a wide range of legal cases within Ripley County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBTv.label: Debt Investment Assets
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBTv.definition: Debt investment assets are financial instruments where an investor lends money to an entity with the expectation of receiving periodic interest payments and the return of the principal amount at a specified maturity date. Examples include bonds, certificates of deposit, and promissory notes

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBU0.label: Limburgan; Limburger; Limburgish
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBU0.definition: A regional language spoken in the Limburg province of the Netherlands, Belgium, and Germany, characterized by its distinct grammar and vocabulary.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBU1.label: European Court of Justice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBU1.definition: The European Court of Justice (ECJ) is the highest court in the European Union, tasked with interpreting EU law and ensuring its uniform application across all member states. It has the authority to settle legal disputes between EU institutions, member states, businesses, and individuals.
english_labels: Court of Justice of the European Union

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBU1.label: Confidential
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBU1.definition: Confidential is a security classification level used for information that requires protection because its unauthorized disclosure could cause damage to the organization (e.g., company, nation). Access to confidential information is restricted to individuals with the appropriate security clearance and a demonstrated need to know.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBU1.label: Undeveloped - Real Estate Asset
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBU1.definition: An "Undeveloped Real Estate Asset" refers to parcels of land that have not yet been altered or improved for specific use. The associated legal matters typically involve zoning laws, land use rights, environmental assessments, and property taxation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBU9.label: Neurodevelopmental Disorders
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBU9.definition: Neurodevelopmental Disorders are characterized by onset during the developmental period, that is, during childhood or adolescence, although sometimes they are not diagnosed until adulthood. Symptoms and signs may include, but are not limited to, underlying abnormalities in cognitive processing (for example, deficits in learning and applying verbal or nonverbal information, visual perception, memory, or a combination of these); deficits in attention or impulse control; low frustration tolerance; excessive or poorly planned motor activity; difficulty with organizing (time, space, materials, or tasks); repeated accidental injury; and deficits in social skills. Symptoms and signs specific to tic disorders include sudden, rapid, recurrent, non-rhythmic, motor movement or vocalization.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUB.label: Intellectual Property Assets
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUB.definition: Intellectual property is a broad categorical description for the set of intangibles owned and legally protected by a company from outside use or implementation without consent. Intellectual property can consist of patents, trade secrets, copyrights, franchises, and trademarks or simply ideas.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUI.label: Minnesota District Court - Morrison County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUI.definition: Minnesota District Court - Morrison County: A specific court within the Minnesota District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Morrison County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUL.label: Old Age Public Benefits
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUL.definition: Old Age Public Benefits refer to government programs designed to provide financial assistance, healthcare, and other forms of support to individuals who have reached retirement age. These programs aim to ensure a reasonable standard of living and access to necessary services for elderly citizens.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUL.label: Foul Ball Liability Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUL.definition: A foul ball liability claim is a legal claim for damages resulting from a personal injury caused by a foul ball at a sporting event.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUL.label: Redeeming Shares in Company Merger or Sale
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUL.definition: The concept of "Redeeming Shares in Company Merger or Sale" refers to the legal process of exchanging shares in a company for cash or other assets during a merger or sale, which may result in liability claims against the corporation or partnership.
english_labels: Redeeming Shares in Company Merger or Sale

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUL.label: Residence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUL.definition: Residence refers to a specific place where an individual or entity lives or operates. It can include a personal residence where someone lives, or a business residence where a company operates its activities. This aspect is important for several legal analyses (e.g., personal jurisdiction, bankruptcy law, tax law). Residence refers to a person's fixed, permanent, and principal home, often with legal implications and the intention to remain for an extended period, in contrast to "occupancy," which refers to the physical act of living in or using a property, which can be temporary or intermittent,

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUP.label: Currently Operative Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUP.definition: The law appears to have legal efficacy, operating effectively.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUS.label: Sabotage
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUS.definition: The intentional destruction or damage of property or equipment belonging to the government or its citizens, with the aim of hindering or disrupting government operations or activities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUW.label: Georgia Superior Court - Jenkins County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUW.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Jenkins County refers to a specific court within the Georgia Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Jenkins County, Georgia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUc.label: Operating Supplies Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUc.definition: An Operating Supplies Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the terms and conditions related to the provision and use of supplies necessary for the operation of a business or organization.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUe.label: Disability and Medical Condition Discrimination
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUe.definition: Discrimination based on a person's disability or medical condition, which is prohibited by law and can be the basis for a legal claim.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUi.label: Disavowed Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUi.definition: The previously effective law has been disavowed by some authority (e.g., appellate court, judge).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUn.label: Waiver of Subrogation Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUn.definition: A Waiver of Subrogation Clause is a provision in a contract where one party agrees to waive their right to seek reimbursement from another party's insurance company for damages covered by the insurance policy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUo.label: Emphysema
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUo.definition: Emphysema is a chronic respiratory condition characterized by the progressive destruction of the alveoli (air sacs) in the lungs, leading to reduced gas exchange and difficulty in breathing. This destruction results in the enlargement of the air spaces and loss of elastic tissue, causing symptoms such as shortness of breath, chronic cough, and wheezing.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUr.label: Statement of Current Monthly Income
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUr.definition: A Statement of Current Monthly Income is a document required in bankruptcy and restructuring proceedings that provides a detailed account of an individual's income and expenses for the current month.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUt.label: Purchase Price Adjustment Mechanism
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUt.definition: A Purchase Price Adjustment Mechanism is a contractual provision in M&A transactions that allows for changes to the initial purchase price based on the target company's financial performance or position as of the closing date. It ensures that the final price reflects the actual value of the target, protecting the interests of both buyer and seller.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUu.label: Release of Obligations Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUu.definition: A Release of Obligations Clause is a provision in a contract that relieves one party from fulfilling certain obligations or liabilities specified in the agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUw.label: House
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUw.definition: A House is a residential building designed to provide living space for individuals or families, typically featuring multiple rooms, including bedrooms, a kitchen, a bathroom, and common living areas. Houses vary in size, style, and structure, ranging from single-story bungalows to multi-story mansions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUw.label: Manchester Band of Pomo Indians of the Manchester Rancheria, California
english_labels: Manchester Band of Pomo Indians of the Manchester Rancheria, California

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUx.label: Awadhi
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUx.definition: Awadhi is a language that belongs to the Hindi branch of the Indo-Aryan language family and is primarily spoken in the Awadh region of Uttar Pradesh and other parts of India.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUz.label: No Tax Advice Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBUz.definition: A "No Tax Advice Clause" is a provision in a contract that states that no tax advice has been given by one party to the other, and that each party is responsible for obtaining their own tax advice.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBV1.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Moniteau County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBV1.definition: A Missouri Circuit Court in Moniteau County is a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Moniteau County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBV3.label: Criminal Proceedings
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBV3.definition: Criminal Proceedings refer to the legal process of prosecuting and punishing individuals who have been accused of committing a crime, including all related proceedings such as indictment, grand jury, sentencing, and parole.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBV6.label: Illness Anxiety Disorder
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBV6.definition: Illness Anxiety Disorder involves an excessive preoccupation with having or acquiring a serious medical condition, despite having no or only mild symptoms. The preoccupation leads to significant distress or impairment in daily functioning, and is not better explained by another mental disorder.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBV7.label: 19th Amendment Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBV7.definition: A 19th Amendment claim is a legal assertion related to the Nineteenth Amendment of the United States Constitution, which grants citizens the right to vote regardless of sex, effectively giving women the right to vote.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBV7.label: Kansas District Court - Linn County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBV7.definition: Kansas District Court - Linn County is a specific court within the Kansas District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Linn County, Kansas.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVC.label: Property Tax Payment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVC.definition: A Property Tax Payment refers to the payment made by property owners to local government authorities, based on the assessed value of their property. This payment is used to fund various public services such as education, infrastructure, and emergency services within the community.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVG.label: Settlement Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVG.definition: A Settlement Agreement is a legal document that outlines the terms and conditions agreed upon by parties to resolve a dispute or legal matter outside of court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVI.label: Florida County Court - Lafayette County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVI.definition: Florida County Court - Lafayette County: A court of limited jurisdiction in Florida that handles civil and criminal cases within the geographical boundaries of Lafayette County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVQ.label: Investment Assets
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVQ.definition: Investment assets are financial instruments or physical assets acquired with the expectation that they will generate returns or appreciate in value over time. These can include stocks, bonds, real estate, mutual funds, and other forms of financial or tangible properties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVU.label: Georgia Superior Court - Bacon County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVU.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Bacon County refers to a specific court within the Georgia Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Bacon County, Georgia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVU.label: Tuition Reimbursement Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVU.definition: A tuition reimbursement clause is a provision in a contract that requires one party to pay for the educational expenses of another party, typically an employee, in exchange for certain conditions being met.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVX.label: Visas for Dependents and Families
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVX.definition: Visas for dependents and families typically allow the spouses, minor children, and sometimes other family members to accompany or join the principal visa holder in the host country. In the United States, for example, these visas often take the form of derivative visas such as F-2, J-2, H-4, and L-2, which correspond to the principal visa categories like F-1, J-1, H-1B, and L-1, respectively

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVh.label: Contact Name Suffix - Sr. (Senior)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVh.definition: The suffix "Sr." stands for "Senior" and is used after a person's full name to distinguish a father from his son when they share the same name. The usage is particularly helpful in legal, formal, or financial documents to clearly identify which individual is being referred to.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVj.label: US Chapter 15 Bankruptcy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVj.definition: Chapter 15 bankruptcy provides a way of dealing with cases that involve more than one country. The main goal of chapter 15 is to provide cooperation between a foreign debtor, foreign courts and the U.S. bankruptcy courts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVp.label: Justifiable Homicide
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVp.definition: The killing of a perpetrator of a serious criminal offense by a peace officer in the line of duty, or the killing, during the commission of a serious criminal offense, of the perpetrator by a private individual.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVq.label: Putative Parent
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVq.definition: An alleged parent whose legal status as a parent has not yet been resolved.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVs.label: Arizona Superior Court - Yavapai Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVs.definition: Arizona Superior Court - Yavapai Cty. is a specific court within the Arizona Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Yavapai County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVu.label: General Practitioner Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVu.definition: Negligent or wrongful conduct by a general practitioner in the medical field, resulting in harm or injury to a patient, which may lead to a legal claim for compensation or damages.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVv.label: Arkansas District Court - Desha Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVv.definition: A court located in Desha County, Arkansas that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVz.label: Delaware Court of General Sessions
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBVz.definition: The Delaware Court of General Sessions is a court within the Delaware State Courts system that has jurisdiction over criminal and civil cases.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBW2.label: Television Series
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBW2.definition: A Television Series is a set of episodic content produced for television broadcast, typically following a consistent narrative or theme across multiple episodes and seasons. Television series can range from dramas and comedies to documentaries and reality shows, engaging viewers with recurring characters and storylines.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBW7.label: Industrial and Logistics - Real Estate Asset
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBW7.definition: Real estate industrial property including factories, logistic centers, and warehouses.
english_labels: Industrial and Logistics - Real Estate Asset

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBW9.label: Securities Lending Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBW9.definition: A Securities Lending Agreement allows the temporary transfer of securities, typically stocks or bonds, from an initial holder to another party in return for collateral, which could be cash or other securities. The agreement also outlines terms for the return of the lent securities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBW9.label: Treaties
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBW9.definition: A signed agreement or arrangement made by negotiation between by two political authorities (usually states or sovereign governments), and usually ratified by the states' lawmaking authorities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBWA.label: Florida County Court - Nassau County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBWA.definition: A court located in Nassau County, Florida that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBWE.label: Joint Guarantee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBWE.definition: A Joint Guarantee is a financial arrangement where an entity other than the issuer, typically a corporation, provides an assurance to fulfill the obligations of a debt instrument if the primary obligor defaults. This type of guarantee creates a shared responsibility for the debt, with both the issuer and the guarantor being jointly liable for the repayment, thus enhancing the creditworthiness of the instrument.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBWF.label: L340 Expert Discovery
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBWF.definition: The concept of L340 Expert Discovery refers to the process of eliciting evidence from individuals with specialized knowledge or skills to provide testimony or consultation in a legal case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBWJ.label: Holdover Tenant
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBWJ.definition: A holdover tenant is an individual who remains in a rented property after the expiration of their lease or rental agreement. In such cases, the tenant continues to occupy the property without formal authorization or a renewed agreement with the landlord. Holdover tenancy situations often lead to legal actions, such as eviction proceedings, as the landlord seeks to regain possession of the property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBWK.label: Oregon Circuit Court - Crook County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBWK.definition: Oregon Circuit Court - Crook County: A court of law in Oregon that has jurisdiction over cases within Crook County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBWM.label: International Organization Visa - Unrecognized or Non-Member Governments
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBWM.definition: An International Organization Visa for representatives of unrecognized or non-member governments is a specialized visa category that allows individuals from entities not officially recognized as states, or from governments not currently members of specific international organizations, to attend meetings or engage in activities at those organizations. The issuance of this visa is often a sensitive diplomatic matter and may be subject to specific conditions and limitations set by the host country.
english_labels: International Organization Visa - Unrecognized or Non-Member Governments

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBWP.label: Release and Indemnity Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBWP.definition: A Release and Indemnity Clause is a legal provision that absolves one party from liability for damages or injuries suffered by another party, and requires the other party to indemnify and hold harmless the first party from any claims or losses arising from the agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBWT.label: Securities Law Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBWT.definition: Securities Law Claims refer to legal claims arising from violations of laws and regulations related to securities, such as buying securities improperly during a corporate takeover or committing securities fraud.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBWW.label: Letter of Credit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBWW.definition: A Letter of Credit is a written agreement between a buyer and a seller, typically used in international trade, in which a bank guarantees payment to the seller upon receipt of certain documents.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBWY.label: Public Comment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBWY.definition: A Public Comment Document is a written submission made by an individual, organization, or other stakeholder to express views, provide data, or raise concerns about a proposed rule or regulation during the public comment period. These documents become part of the administrative record and are considered by the regulating agency before finalizing the new rule, serving to inform and potentially influence the final regulation

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBWY.label: Commercially Reasonable Efforts Antitrust Standard
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBWY.definition: The Commercially Reasonable Efforts Antitrust Standard is a provision within antitrust efforts that requires parties to make a good faith effort to achieve a particular goal or outcome, while taking into account the costs and benefits of such efforts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBWa.label: Texas Court of Appeals - 11th
