https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBfw.definition: A dealer is a person, company, or entity that buys and sells securities for his or her or its own account and not for others.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBg5.label: Conditional Use Permit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBg5.definition: A Conditional Use Permit is a type of land use authorization that allows a property owner to engage in activities not typically permitted within a specific zoning classification, subject to meeting predetermined conditions. This permit is granted by a local governing body after a review process, often involving public hearings and assessments.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBg7.label: Domestication Action
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBg7.definition: Domestication Action refers to the legal process of making a foreign judgment enforceable in a jurisdiction different from where it was originally issued. This involves registering or recognizing the judgment in the new jurisdiction to allow for its enforcement, including collections.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBg7.label: Law Review Article
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBg7.definition: A Law Review Article is a scholarly piece of writing published in a law review, which is a type of academic journal focused on legal and jurisprudential topics. These articles are written by legal scholars, practitioners, or law students, and they provide in-depth analysis, critique, or novel perspectives on legal theories, case law, statutes, or societal legal issues, often influencing legal thought and occasionally, policy or judicial decisions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgA.label: Cyberbullying
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgA.definition: Cyberbullying is a form of criminal harassment that involves the use of electronic communication to repeatedly intimidate, threaten, or harm another person.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgB.label: Habeas Corpus
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgB.definition: A legal concept that allows a person who is detained or imprisoned to challenge the legality of their detention and seek release.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgD.label: Idaho Magistrate Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgD.definition: Idaho Magistrate Court is a lower court in the Idaho State Court system that handles minor criminal and civil cases.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgK.label: In Witness Whereof Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgK.definition: An "In Witness Whereof Clause" is a clause in a contract that identifies the parties who have signed the contract and the date of execution.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgK.label: Feature Engineering
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgK.definition: Feature Engineering is the process of selecting, transforming, and creating input features from raw data to improve the performance and accuracy of machine learning models. This involves extracting meaningful attributes that capture essential patterns within the data, thereby enhancing the model's ability to make accurate predictions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgK.label: Elements of Criminal Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgK.definition: The Elements of Criminal Claim refer to the specific components that must be proven in a criminal case, including the harm caused, the intent of the accused, and the causal link between the two.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgV.label: Clinical Trial
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgV.definition: A Clinical Trial is a research study conducted with human participants to evaluate the safety, efficacy, and side effects of new medical treatments, drugs, or interventions. These trials are essential for determining whether new therapies should be approved for use in the general population.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgX.label: Arkansas Circuit Court - Randolph Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgX.definition: A court located in Randolph County, Arkansas that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its designated geographical area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgY.label: Trial Court Procedural Documents
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgY.definition: Trial Court Procedural Documents are written materials that are filed with a court during the course of a trial, such as motions, pleadings, and orders, which outline the procedural steps taken by the parties involved in the case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBga.label: Accident Benefits Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBga.definition: Accident Benefits Law refers to the legal area of study and practice that deals with the compensation and benefits provided to individuals who have been injured in an accident, typically related to automobile insurance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgb.label: Demonstrative Bequest
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgb.definition: A Demonstrative Bequest is a provision in a will or trust that designates a specific monetary amount or asset to be paid or distributed from a particular source within the estate. This type of bequest combines elements of both specific and general bequests, specifying the source while also ensuring a fixed amount is given to the beneficiary.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgc.label: Resolution Date Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgc.definition: A Resolution Date Clause is a provision in a contract that specifies the date by which any disputes or issues arising from the contract must be resolved.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgi.label: Autism Spectrum Disorder with Language Impairment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgi.definition: Autism Spectrum Disorder with Language Impairment is characterized by deficits in social communication and interaction, alongside restricted, repetitive patterns of behavior or interests. Individuals with this condition exhibit significant difficulties with language development and usage, impacting their ability to communicate effectively and engage in social interactions.
english_labels: Autism Spectrum Disorder with Language Impairment
Autistic Spectrum Disorder with Communication Impairment

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgl.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Mifflin County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgl.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Mifflin County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering legal proceedings in Mifflin County, Pennsylvania.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Mifflin County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgn.label: Georgia Superior Court - Butts County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgn.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Butts County, Georgia, with authority to hear and decide a wide range of legal cases.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgu.label: Luxury Market Segment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgu.definition: The luxury segment refers to a specific portion of the market that is characterized by consumers who seek high-end, premium products and services. This segment is associated with luxury goods that offer exclusivity, superior quality, and a high level of craftsmanship, catering to consumers who are willing to pay a premium for these attributes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgw.label: Greek, Modern
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgw.definition: Greek, Modern (1453-) is a form of language that emerged after the fall of the Byzantine Empire and is still in use today.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgy.label: Health Public Benefit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgy.definition: Health public benefit refers to government programs designed to provide medical services or financial assistance for healthcare needs to eligible individuals. This can include programs like Medicaid in the United States, which offers healthcare coverage to low-income families and individuals.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgy.label: Non-economic Damages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgy.definition: Non-economic damages refer to compensation awarded in a legal matter for harm or loss that cannot be quantified in monetary terms, such as pain and suffering, emotional distress, disfigurement, and loss of consortium.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgy.label: Bankrupt’s Voiding of Preferential Transfer of Property
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgy.definition: The Bankrupt's Voiding of Preferential Transfer of Property refers to the legal concept where a bankrupt individual or entity is allowed to cancel or undo any transfer of property made to a creditor within a certain time period before filing for bankruptcy, in order to ensure fair distribution of assets among all creditors.
english_labels: Bankrupt’s Voiding of Preferential Transfer of Property

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgz.label: Trial Court Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgz.definition: Trial Court Practice refers to the legal work performed by a Legal Services Provider in the course of a legal matter that involves presenting evidence and arguments before a judge or jury in a trial court, including procedures and rules specific to district courts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgz.label: Scienter
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBgz.definition: The concept of Scienter refers to the knowledge or intent of wrongdoing by a defendant in a legal claim, which is an essential element of the plaintiff's case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBh0.label: Mixed-Member Proportional Representation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBh0.definition: Mixed-Member Proportional Representation (MMP) is an electoral system that combines elements of first-past-the-post and proportional representation. Voters typically have two votes: one for a candidate to represent their local constituency and another for a party list, with the overall composition of the legislature reflecting the proportion of party list votes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBh2.label: Afar
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBh2.definition: Afar (Language) is a structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary, and is a member of the Language class.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBh4.label: Dyslexia
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBh4.definition: Dyslexia is a specific learning disability that affects an individual's ability to read, spell, write, and sometimes speak, due to difficulties in recognizing and processing written words and symbols. It is a neurological condition that is often hereditary and varies in severity, requiring tailored educational strategies and interventions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBh8.label: Motion to Waive Credit Counseling
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBh8.definition: A Motion to Waive Credit Counseling is a formal request submitted by a debtor to a bankruptcy court to exempt them from the mandatory credit counseling requirement. This requirement is typically necessary before filing for bankruptcy, but the motion may be granted under special circumstances, such as exigency or incapacity.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhE.label: Landlord Insurance Policy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhE.definition: Landlord insurance is designed to provide coverage for property owners who rent out one or more residential homes, apartments, or condos. It generally covers the building structure, and it may also provide coverage for loss of rental income and liability protection. It typically does not cover the personal belongings of the tenants.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhG.label: Negative Pledge
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhG.definition: A Negative Pledge is a covenant in a loan agreement where the borrower agrees not to pledge any assets as collateral if doing so would result in less security for the agreement's bondholders. This provision aims to protect the interests of the bondholders by ensuring that the borrower does not take actions that would dilute the security or increase the risk associated with the debt.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhO.label: Regional Market Segment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhO.definition: The regional segment refers to a portion of the market that is focused on consumers and businesses for a geographical region within a country. This segment tailors its products, services, and marketing strategies to meet the needs and preferences of the regional population, often considering local culture, language, and economic conditions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhS.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Bucks County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhS.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court located in Bucks County, responsible for administering proceedings related to minor criminal offenses, traffic violations, and civil disputes within its jurisdiction.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Bucks County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhS.label: Closed During Tail Period
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhS.definition: The concept of "Closed During Tail Period" refers to a specific timing of the acquisition proposal closing, where the target company is not allowed to consider any other offers during a certain period after the initial offer has been made.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhX.label: Rest Break
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhX.definition: A "Rest Break" is a shorter break during the workday, during which employees can briefly pause from work to rest, stretch, or relax. These breaks are usually paid and are designed to improve productivity and well-being.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhf.label: Proceeding Removed
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhf.definition: Case Removed refers to a legal matter that has been transferred from one court to another, resulting in the case being removed from the original court's jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhg.label: Hospital Negligence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhg.definition: Hospital Negligence refers to a legal claim against a medical facility for failing to provide adequate care or treatment to a patient, resulting in harm or injury.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhi.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Washington County (20th Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Washington County (20th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhk.label: Small Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhk.definition: A type of civil claim that involves disputes of a relatively low monetary value and is resolved through a simplified and informal process known as conciliation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhk.label: Drug Equipment Violation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhk.definition: The unlawful manufacture, sale, purchase, possession, or transportation of equipment or devices utilized in preparing and/or using drugs or narcotics.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhk.label: Whistleblower's Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhk.definition: A Whistleblower's Claim is a legal action brought by an individual who reports illegal or unethical activities within an organization, seeking protection from retaliation and potentially receiving a portion of any resulting financial penalties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhl.label: JA10 Funding (UK J-CODE)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhl.definition: All work relating to reviewing funding options and securing funding.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhm.label: Remedies Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhm.definition: A Remedies Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the available legal remedies in the event of a breach of the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhm.label: Concealed Handgun License
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhm.definition: A concealed handgun license (CHL), also known as a concealed carry permit or license, is an official authorization granted by a governing authority that permits an individual to carry a concealed firearm, typically a handgun, on their person in public areas. The process to obtain a CHL usually includes a background check, firearms training, and demonstration of proficiency, though specific requirements vary by jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhm.label: Voidable Release
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhm.definition: A voidable release is a legal agreement that can be cancelled or made invalid by one of the parties involved due to certain circumstances, such as fraud or duress.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhn.label: Joint Filing Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhn.definition: A Joint Filing Agreement is an agreement between parties that allows them to file certain documents jointly, especially with regulatory agencies. Often seen in securities law, it signifies that the filers have collaborated on the document but may not agree on all points or share the same views.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhp.label: Guaranteed Maximum Price Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhp.definition: A Guaranteed Maximum Price Clause is a provision in a contract that sets a limit on the amount that a party will be required to pay for a project, ensuring that the cost will not exceed a certain amount.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhq.label: As Is Purchase Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhq.definition: A provision in a contract that states the buyer accepts the property in its current condition, without any warranties or guarantees from the seller.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhv.label: Interim Trustee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhv.definition: A trustee appointed temporarily, usually until the appointment of a permanent trustee.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhy.label: Visa for Intermittent Intra-Company Transferee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBhy.definition: Visas for intermittent intra-company transferees (in the United States, L-1A Visa) is designed for managers, executives, or specialized knowledge employees who need to travel back and forth between affiliated companies in their home country and the destination country (e.g., U.S.). In the United States, the intermittent L-1 allows the individual to stay in the U.S. for shorter periods without affecting the maximum allowable period of stay, which is typically seven years for L-1A visas and five years for L-1B visas

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBi3.label: Lessee’s Default on Lease of Goods
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBi3.definition: The Lessee's Default on Lease of Goods refers to the situation where the lessee fails to fulfill their obligations under a lease agreement for goods, resulting in a breach of contract and potential legal action by the lessor or creditor.
english_labels: Lessee’s Default on Lease of Goods

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBi5.label: Leave-Related Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBi5.definition: Leave-related claims are legal actions initiated by an employee against their employer for not complying with applicable laws or the terms of an employment agreement regarding various types of leave, such as medical leave, family leave, or military leave. These claims can involve issues such as denial of leave, interference with the employee's right to take leave, or retaliation against the employee for taking leave. Employees may also bring leave-related claims if their employer fails to provide required notice or fails to provide benefits or protections required by law during the leave period.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBi5.label: Motion to Bifurcate
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBi5.definition: A Motion to Bifurcate is a legal request to separate a trial into two parts, typically to address liability and damages separately.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBi8.label: DEPRECATED Attorney-Client Discussions
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBi8.definition: Deprecated Attorney-Client Discussions refer to the communication between a lawyer and their client that is no longer in use or recommended. It falls under the broader category of Deprecated Budgeting and Project Management.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBiA.label: Matter Accumulated Fees
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBiA.definition: Matter Accumulated Fees: Fees accumulated for a specific legal matter within an engagement for providing legal services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBiB.label: Georgia Superior Court - Paulding County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBiB.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia, located in Paulding County and presided over by a judge.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBiK.label: Qui Tam Whistleblower Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBiK.definition: A Qui Tam Whistleblower Claim is a legal action brought by an individual who reports fraud against the government and seeks to recover damages on behalf of the government.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBiM.label: Visa for Foreign Government Employees on Official Business
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBiM.definition: Visa for full-time foreign government employees who will conduct official business of the foreign country at an embassy, consulate, mission or military base.
english_labels: Visa for Foreign Government Employees on Official Business

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBiN.label: Court Filings Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBiN.definition: Court Filings Management refers to the process of organizing and maintaining legal documents and pleadings submitted to a court, as a part of the broader Litigation Management process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBiZ.label: Classes of Goods and Services
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBiZ.definition: When filing for trademark registration, the classes of goods or services that the trademark covers (e.g., clothing, electronics, musical groups), as defined by the regulatory agency (e.g., U.S. Patent & Trademark Office).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBib.label: Disclosure Statement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBib.definition: A Disclosure Statement is a document filed in a bankruptcy case that provides information about the debtor's financial affairs, including assets, liabilities, income, and expenses, and is intended to assist creditors in making informed decisions about the debtor's proposed plan of reorganization.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBib.label: Strategic Communications Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBib.definition: Strategic Communications Practice involves providing legal advice and services related to the management and dissemination of information to the public, media, and stakeholders, particularly in situations requiring public relations and crisis management. This legal practice ensures that communications are legally compliant, strategically effective, and aligned with the client’s objectives.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBif.label: Minnesota District Court - Sibley County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBif.definition: Minnesota District Court - Sibley County: A specific court within the Minnesota District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Sibley County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBii.label: Ponca Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma
english_labels: Ponca Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBik.label: Proxy Contest
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBik.definition: A proxy contest is a struggle for control of a company where opposing factions of shareholders seek to gather enough proxy votes to win a corporate election or effect significant corporate decisions. This often occurs during annual meetings when shareholders vote on the election of directors or other major corporate issues.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBil.label: Employment Events
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBil.definition: Employment Events refer to specific milestones in an employee's work history with an organization, such as the date of hiring, date of termination, and date of re-hiring. These events are important for both administrative record-keeping and compliance with employment laws and regulations

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBio.label: Special Nonimmigrant Visa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBio.definition: This special non-immigrant visa classification is a rarely used.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBio.label: Mineral Resources Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBio.definition: Laws covering the ownership of the mineral resource and who can work them.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBis.label: Paroled Refugee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBis.definition: A Paroled Refugee is an individual who has been allowed entry into a country on a temporary basis for urgent humanitarian reasons or significant public benefit, even though they do not meet the regular admission requirements for refugees. This status provides temporary legal presence in the host country while the individual’s case is reviewed or until more permanent arrangements can be made.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBix.label: Breach of Fiduciary Duty by Trustee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBix.definition: The breach of fiduciary duty by trustee refers to a situation where a trustee fails to act in the best interest of the beneficiaries of a trust, violating their legal obligation to manage the trust assets and affairs with loyalty, honesty, and good faith.
english_labels: Breach of Fiduciary Duty by Trustee

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBiz.label: Forcible Fondling
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBiz.definition: The touching of the private body parts of another person for the purpose of sexual gratification, forcibly and/or against that person’s will or not forcibly or against the person’s will in instances where the victim is incapable of giving consent because of his/her youth or because of his/her temporary or permanent mental or physical incapacity.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBj5.label: X304 Discovery/eDiscovery Review and Analysis
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBj5.definition: Any costs associated with the inspection, review, consideration and analysis of documents and/or evidence, relevance issues, quality assurance and control when billed as an expense instead of a service. Excludes creation of privilege log (X305).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjD.label: Junior Credit Ranking
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjD.definition: Junior Credit Ranking refers to the priority status of junior debts, which are ranked above junior subordinated debts but below senior and senior subordinated debts in the event of liquidation. This ranking ensures that junior creditors are paid before junior subordinated creditors from the proceeds of the liquidated assets, providing them with a lower level of security compared to senior debts but higher than junior subordinated debts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjG.label: Collision Auto Insurance Coverage Policy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjG.definition: Collision auto insurance covers damage to the insured's own vehicle resulting from a collision with another vehicle or object, or from flipping over. It is generally an optional coverage but may be required if the vehicle is leased or financed. A deductible usually applies.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjG.label: Indiana Superior Court - Vanderburgh County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjG.definition: A court located in Vanderburgh County, Indiana that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjH.label: Borderline Personality Disorder
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjH.definition: Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD) is a mental health condition characterized by pervasive instability in moods, behavior, self-image, and functioning. Individuals with BPD often experience intense episodes of anger, depression, and anxiety that can last from a few hours to days, leading to impulsive actions and unstable relationships.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjH.label: Forums and Venues
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjH.definition: Forums and Venues refer to organizational or governmental entities where proceedings occur, either as disputes or as transactions. For disputes, the term "Forum" describes the jurisdiction or court type, while "Venue" refers to the actual location, such as the courthouse, jurisdiction, or judicial district. For equities and securities, this category also includes Stock Exchanges.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjI.label: Neonatology Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjI.definition: Negligent or wrongful conduct by a healthcare provider in the field of neonatology, resulting in harm or injury to a newborn or infant.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjO.label: Kansas District Court - Anderson County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjO.definition: A court located in Anderson County, Kansas that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjP.label: Gastrointestinal Hemorrhaging
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjP.definition: Gastrointestinal hemorrhaging refers to bleeding that occurs within the gastrointestinal (GI) tract, which includes the esophagus, stomach, intestines, and rectum. This condition can manifest as either upper GI bleeding (e.g., from ulcers or varices) or lower GI bleeding (e.g., from hemorrhoids or colorectal cancer) and may require urgent medical attention and treatment to manage blood loss and address underlying causes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjR.label: Shoshone-Paiute Tribes of the Duck Valley Reservation
english_labels: Shoshone-Paiute Tribes of the Duck Valley Reservation

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjR.label: Claims Objection Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjR.definition: Claims Objection Practice (Bankruptcy) refers to the legal practice of objecting to claims made by creditors in a bankruptcy case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjT.label: Turnover of property to the estate
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjT.definition: The turnover of property to the estate refers to the legal process of transferring ownership or possession of assets to a bankruptcy estate, typically as a result of an avoidance action claim.
english_labels: Turnover of property to the estate

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjY.label: Landlord Tenant Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjY.definition: Law that details the rights and duties of landlords and tenants

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjY.label: Assignee of Member
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjY.definition: An assignee of a member (e.g., member of an LLC) is a person or entity to whom a member transfers their membership interest, either partially or wholly. The assignee typically acquires the economic rights associated with the membership interest but may not automatically gain the right to participate in the management or voting of the organization unless the other members consent.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjb.label: Motion to Stay Permanent Injunction
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjb.definition: A Motion to Stay Permanent Injunction is a request made to a court to temporarily suspend the enforcement of a permanent injunction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjc.label: Cure of Residential Judgment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjc.definition: The "Cure of Residential Judgment" refers to a legal document related to bankruptcy and restructuring that outlines the process of bringing a delinquent mortgage current and avoiding foreclosure on a residential property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjc.label: Phlebotomy Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjc.definition: Phlebotomy Malpractice refers to a type of medical malpractice claim that arises from errors or negligence committed during the process of drawing blood from a patient.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjn.label: Kansas District Court - Neosho County, Chanute
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjn.definition: A court located in Neosho County, Chanute, Kansas that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical area.
english_labels: Kansas District Court - Neosho County, Chanute

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjo.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Orange County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjo.definition: Indiana Circuit Court - Orange County is a specific court within the Indiana Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Orange County, Indiana.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjs.label: Indiana Town Court - Marion County, Wayne Twp.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjs.definition: A court located in Marion County, Wayne Township, Indiana that has limited jurisdiction over minor criminal offenses, traffic violations, and small claims cases.
english_labels: Indiana Town Court - Marion County, Wayne Twp.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjs.label: Real Estate Broker's Liability for Injury at Open House
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjs.definition: Real Estate Broker's Liability for Injury at Open House: The legal responsibility of a real estate broker for injuries sustained by a person who was invited to an open house hosted by the broker.
english_labels: Real Estate Broker's Liability for Injury at Open House

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjs.label: Goats
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjs.definition: Goats are domesticated ruminant animals belonging to the species Capra aegagrus hircus, commonly raised for their milk, meat, fiber (such as cashmere and mohair), and hides. Known for their agility and ability to graze on various types of vegetation, goats are valuable in agricultural practices and can thrive in diverse environments.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjt.label: Acoli
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjt.definition: Acoli is a structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary, and is a specific language within the context of legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjv.label: Oral Surgery Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBjv.definition: Oral Surgery Malpractice refers to a type of medical malpractice claim that arises from negligent or improper treatment during oral surgery procedures.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBk0.label: U.S. Board of Tax Appeals
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBk0.definition: The U.S. Board of Tax Appeals is a specialized court that hears and decides disputes related to tax matters, operating under the jurisdiction of the U.S. Tax Court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBk6.label: Guardianship of Juvenile
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBk6.definition: The concept of Guardianship of Juvenile refers to the legal arrangement where a court appoints a guardian to take care of a minor's personal and financial affairs when the parents are unable to do so.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBk9.label: Court Calendaring Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBk9.definition: Court Calendaring Management refers to the process of scheduling and managing court hearings and events, including the allocation of resources and coordination of participants, within the context of Litigation Management.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBk9.label: Kawi
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBk9.definition: Kawi is a language that belongs to the Language top-level class and is used in legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBk9.label: Texas Court of Appeals - 6th
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBk9.definition: The Texas Court of Appeals - 6th is a specific intermediate appellate court in Texas that hears appeals from lower courts within its jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBkF.label: LINE_ITEM_TAX_TYPE
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBkF.definition: A LINE_ITEM_TAX_TYPE is a specific type of tax applied to a line item in a legal invoice, as defined in the LEDES98BI V5 Format Rev 1-2020 standard.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBkG.label: Joint and Several Liability Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBkG.definition: A joint and several liability clause is a provision in a contract that holds multiple parties responsible for fulfilling the obligations of the contract, either individually or collectively.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBkG.label: Minnesota District Court - Carver County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBkG.definition: Minnesota District Court - Carver County: A specific court within the Minnesota District Court system located in Carver County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBkH.label: English
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBkH.definition: English (Language) is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary, used in legal matters as the language of a document, artifact, evidence, testimony, proceeding, or any other legal aspect.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBkI.label: Compliance Risk
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBkI.definition: Risk in the way that an entity might comply (or potentially fail to comply) with applicable laws and/or regulations. This risk can arise from an organization's failure to adhere to internal policies, industry standards, or legal and regulatory requirements. Causes can include inadequate controls, lack of training, or noncompliance with ethical or governance standards, potentially leading to legal penalties, reputational damage, or loss of stakeholder trust, ultimately impacting the organization's overall performance and sustainability.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBkP.label: Breach of Meeting Covenant
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBkP.definition: The Breach of Meeting Covenant refers to the violation of an agreement between parties to meet and discuss a specific matter, which may result in the triggering of a breakup fee.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBkY.label: Settlement Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBkY.definition: Settlement Practice refers to the legal process of negotiating and reaching an agreement between parties involved in a legal dispute, often involving a demand for compensation or other remedy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBkg.label: Estimate of Recoverable Amount
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBkg.definition: Estimate by the client and/or provider as to the amount of potential recovery

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBki.label: Bulimia Nervosa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBki.definition: Bulimia Nervosa is an eating disorder characterized by recurrent episodes of binge eating followed by compensatory behaviors such as vomiting, excessive exercise, or misuse of laxatives to prevent weight gain. Individuals with this disorder often have a preoccupation with body image and weight, leading to a cycle of bingeing and purging.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBks.label: Transportation Company Negligence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBks.definition: Transportation Company Negligence refers to the failure of a common carrier to exercise reasonable care in the transportation of goods or passengers, resulting in harm or injury to those goods or passengers.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBku.label: Advance Directive
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBku.definition: This is a broad term that refers to any document in which a person specifies what actions should be taken for their health if they are no longer able to make decisions for themselves because of illness or incapacity. An advance directive can include a variety of instructions about future medical care and can encompass several types of directives, including the living will and durable power of attorney for health care

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBkx.label: Durable Power of Attorney Document
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBkx.definition: A Durable Power of Attorney Document is a legal instrument that grants a designated person, called an agent or attorney-in-fact, the authority to act on behalf of the principal in financial and other matters. Unlike a standard power of attorney, its durability ensures the agent's authority persists even if the principal becomes incapacitated.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBkz.label: Religious Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBkz.definition: Religious Law is a system of law based on religious texts and traditions, governing the conduct of adherents of a particular faith or belief.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBl0.label: L140 Document/File Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBl0.definition: The concept of L140 Document/File Management refers to the organization, storage, and retrieval of legal documents and files within a case, as a part of the overall case assessment, development, and administration process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBl1.label: Moment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBl1.definition: In legal terms, a Moment (Point in Time) refers to a precise, specific point on the timeline, often critical in determining the applicability, initiation, or cessation of legal rights, duties, or conditions. It is essential in contexts such as the execution of contracts, occurrence of events triggering legal consequences, or the effective date of legislation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBl1.label: Motion for Leave to File as Amicus
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBl1.definition: A Motion for Leave to File as Amicus is a legal document filed by a non-party to a case, seeking permission from the court to submit a brief or argument in support of one of the parties.
english_labels: Motion for Leave to File as Amicus

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBl2.label: Insurer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBl2.definition: One that insures, usually an insurance underwriter.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBl5.label: New York Supreme Court - Otsego County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBl5.definition: The New York Supreme Court - Otsego County is a court of general jurisdiction located in Otsego County, New York, with authority to hear and decide legal disputes within its geographical jurisdiction.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - Otsego County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlH.label: Document ID
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlH.definition: Identifier (e.g., IRIs, UUIDs, GUIDs) of the particular document stored in the systems of stakeholders (e.g., vendors, sellers, buyers, courts).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlJ.label: Arkansas District Court - Van Buren Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlJ.definition: Arkansas District Court - Van Buren Cty. is a specific court within the Arkansas District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Van Buren County, Arkansas.
english_labels: Arkansas District Court - Van Buren Cty.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlP.label: Cash Asset Delivery
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlP.definition: Cash Asset Delivery refers to the settlement of a contract through the payment or receipt of a net cash amount instead of the actual delivery of the underlying assets. This method is commonly used in financial instruments and derivatives to simplify the settlement process and avoid the logistics of transferring physical assets.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlQ.label: Missouri Circuit Court - New Madrid County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlQ.definition: A Missouri Circuit Court in New Madrid County is a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases in that county.
english_labels: Missouri Circuit Court - New Madrid County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlR.label: DEPRECATED Status - Inactive
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlR.definition: DEPRECATED in favor of Proceeding Inactive

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlR.label: Probate Reason of Abuse
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlR.definition: Probate Reason of Abuse refers to a specific reason for filing a subsequent probate, which involves the abuse of power or mistreatment of an individual by the executor or administrator of an estate.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlW.label: Debt Collection Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlW.definition: Debt Collection Claims refer to legal actions initiated by creditors to recover unpaid debts from borrowers. These claims encompass various legal grounds and causes of action used to pursue debt recovery through the courts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlW.label: 6th Amendment Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlW.definition: A Sixth Amendment claim is a legal assertion made by a defendant in a criminal case, arguing that their constitutional right to a fair trial, as guaranteed by the Sixth Amendment of the United States Constitution, has been violated. Such a claim may involve issues related to the right to counsel, the right to a speedy and public trial, the right to an impartial jury, or the right to be informed of the nature and cause of the accusation, among others.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlZ.label: Bhojpuri
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlZ.definition: Bhojpuri is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary, used in legal matters as a language of a document, artifact, evidence, testimony, proceeding, or any other legal aspect.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBld.label: Trampoline Liability Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBld.definition: A claim made against a manufacturer or seller of trampolines for injuries or damages caused by a defect in the product.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBle.label: Date Modified
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBle.definition: Date Modified refers to the specific time and date when a Document Component was last changed or updated.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlg.label: Florida County Court - Putnam County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlg.definition: A court located in Putnam County, Florida that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBln.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Scotland County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBln.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Scotland County refers to a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Scotland County, Missouri.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlt.label: L530 Oral Argument
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlt.definition: The concept of L530 Oral Argument refers to the presentation of arguments and responses by parties in a legal case before an appellate court, as part of the appeal process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlt.label: Stipulation to Assume
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlt.definition: A Stipulation to Assume is a legal agreement between parties where one party agrees to take on the responsibility or liability for a particular matter or issue.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlu.label: Duty to Defend
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlu.definition: A duty imposed on an insurer to provide legal defense to its insured against claims or lawsuits brought by third parties, as specified in the insurance policy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlx.label: Maryland State Bar Association Ethics Opinions
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlx.definition: The Maryland State Bar Association Ethics Opinions are official statements issued by the Maryland State Bar Association regarding the ethical responsibilities of lawyers in Maryland.
english_labels: Maryland State Bar Association Ethics Opinions

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlx.label: Georgia District Court - Jenkins County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBlx.definition: Georgia District Court - Jenkins County: A specific court within the Georgia District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Jenkins County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBm2.label: Florida County Court - Gulf County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBm2.definition: Florida County Court - Gulf County refers to the specific court located in Gulf County, Florida that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBm2.label: payee_name
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBm2.definition: The name of the payee for the expense item. If a payee name is indicated, the item is a disbursement paid to a third party and not a firm expense or soft cost.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBm3.label: Community Service Penalty
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBm3.definition: A community service penalty is a type of criminal penalty that requires an offender to perform unpaid work for the benefit of the community, as a form of punishment for their offense.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBm4.label: Fragile X Syndrome
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBm4.definition: Fragile X Syndrome is a genetic disorder caused by a mutation on the FMR1 gene located on the X chromosome. This mutation leads to a lack of the fragile X mental retardation protein (FMRP), which is crucial for normal brain development.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBm5.label: Emergency Medical Assistance Coverage
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBm5.definition: This refers to immediate healthcare services provided in urgent or life-threatening situations. Coverage for emergency medical assistance is often a component of general health insurance policies and is also commonly included in travel insurance plans.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBm5.label: Chichewa; Chewa; Nyanja
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBm5.definition: A Bantu language spoken in Malawi, Zambia, and Mozambique, among other countries, belonging to the Niger-Congo language family and falling under the Language top-level class.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBm7.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Phelps County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBm7.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Phelps County refers to a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Phelps County, Missouri.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmC.label: Intuitu Personae Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmC.definition: An Intuitu Personae Clause is a contractual clause that requires the performance of a specific obligation by a particular person, based on their personal characteristics or qualifications, rather than allowing for a substitute to perform the obligation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmE.label: Sale of Goods Breached by Seller
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmE.definition: The Sale of Goods Breached by Seller refers to a legal concept where the seller fails to fulfill their obligations under a contract for the sale of goods, resulting in a breach of contract.
english_labels: Sale of Goods Breached by Seller

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmJ.label: Assignment by Buyer Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmJ.definition: An Assignment by Buyer Clause is a provision in a contract that allows the buyer to transfer their rights and obligations to a third party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmM.label: Engagement Scope
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmM.definition: Engagement Scope refers to the specific boundaries and limitations of a project or task that a party has agreed to undertake, as defined within the context of project management objectives.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmT.label: "Materiality" Based Antitrust Standard
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmT.definition: A "Materiality" Based Antitrust Standard is a legal concept that sets a threshold for determining whether certain conduct or information is significant enough to be considered in antitrust analysis, and only conduct or information that meets this threshold will be taken into account.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmV.label: Confidentiality Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmV.definition: A Confidentiality Agreement is a legal contract between parties that outlines the terms and conditions for keeping certain information confidential and not disclosing it to third parties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmW.label: Choctaw
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmW.definition: A Native American language spoken primarily in the southeastern United States, particularly in Oklahoma and Mississippi, and belonging to the Muskogean language family.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmY.label: Promise to Make a Will
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmY.definition: A Promise to Make a Will is a legal concept within Trust and Estate Claims that refers to a commitment made by one party to another to create a will in the future.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmd.label: Indiana Superior Court - Cass County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmd.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Indiana that has the power to hear and decide a wide range of legal cases within Cass County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmd.label: Motor Vehicle Manufacturing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmd.definition: This industry group comprises establishments primarily engaged in (1) manufacturing complete automobiles, light duty motor vehicles, and heavy duty trucks (i.e., body and chassis or unibody) or (2) manufacturing motor vehicle chassis only.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBme.label: Extradition
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBme.definition: The concept of Extradition refers to the legal process of transferring an individual who has been accused or convicted of a crime from one jurisdiction to another for the purpose of facing trial or punishment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmg.label: Florida County Court - Highlands County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmg.definition: A court located in Highlands County, Florida that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmj.label: Analysis of Critical Vendor Status
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmj.definition: Analysis of Critical Vendor Status refers to the evaluation and assessment of vendors that are essential to the operation of a business, with a focus on identifying potential risks and developing strategies to mitigate them.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmm.label: Nephrology Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmm.definition: Negligent or wrongful conduct by a medical professional in the field of nephrology, resulting in harm or injury to a patient.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmt.label: Armenian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmt.definition: Armenian (Language) refers to the written or spoken structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary specific to the Armenian language.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmv.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Blair County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmv.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court in Blair County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court system that handles minor criminal offenses, traffic violations, and civil cases involving amounts up to $12,000.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Blair County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmv.label: Militia Clause Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmv.definition: A Militia Clause claim is a legal argument asserting that a law or action violates the authority granted to Congress by the Militia Clause of the United States Constitution. This claim is based on the interpretation that the Militia Clause empowers Congress to regulate and organize the militia, and prohibits states or other entities from taking actions that infringe upon this federal authority or interfere with the proper functioning of the militia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmz.label: Contact Name Suffix - V (Fifth)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBmz.definition: The suffix "V" stands for "Fifth" and is used after a person's full name to indicate that they are the fifth generation in their family to bear that name. This convention helps to distinguish individuals in formal, legal, or financial documents.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBn0.label: Confession of Judgment Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBn0.definition: A Confession of Judgment Clause is a contractual provision that allows one party to confess to a judgment in favor of the other party without the need for a trial or hearing.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBn1.label: Offset Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBn1.definition: An offset clause is a provision in a contract that requires one party to purchase goods or services from the other party in order to balance out payments owed.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBn4.label: New York City Court - Geneva
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBn4.definition: New York City Court - Geneva is a specific court located in New York City that operates under the jurisdiction of the New York City Court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBn4.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Fulton County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBn4.definition: Indiana Circuit Court - Fulton County: A court of general jurisdiction in Indiana that hears civil and criminal cases within the geographical boundaries of Fulton County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBn4.label: Paternity Acknowledgement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBn4.definition: Paternity acknowledgement is a legal document or process by which a man formally recognizes and claims himself to be the biological father of a child born outside of marriage. Signing this acknowledgement typically grants the father certain rights and responsibilities related to the child, such as custody or support, and establishes the child's legal relationship to the father.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBn5.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Starke County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBn5.definition: A court located in Starke County, Indiana that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographic area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBn6.label: Claim for Falling on Ice and Snow
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBn6.definition: A claim for falling on ice and snow is a legal action brought by a plaintiff who has suffered injuries due to slipping and falling on ice or snow, and seeks compensation for damages from the defendant who may be held liable for negligence.
english_labels: Claim for Falling on Ice and Snow

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBn8.label: Director Compensation and Governance Policy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBn8.definition: The Director Compensation and Governance Policy outlines the rules and guidelines for how board members are compensated and how governance activities are conducted within an organization. This policy ensures alignment with organizational goals and compliance with relevant laws and regulations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBn8.label: Fang
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBn8.definition: A language spoken by the Fang people, primarily in Central Africa.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnB.label: Radiology Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnB.definition: Radiology Malpractice refers to a type of medical malpractice claim that arises from errors or negligence in the interpretation of medical images or the performance of radiological procedures.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnF.label: Fernandeno Tataviam Band of Mission Indians
english_labels: Fernandeno Tataviam Band of Mission Indians

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnS.label: Debt Repayment Plan Bankruptcy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnS.definition: Debt Repayment Plan Bankruptcy allows individuals with a regular income to develop a plan to repay all or part of their debts over a period of time. This form of bankruptcy can provide the debtor with an opportunity to save their home from foreclosure, reschedule secured debts, and consolidate their obligations into a single payment plan overseen by a bankruptcy trustee.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnT.label: Ossetian; Ossetic
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnT.definition: A language spoken by the Ossetian people, primarily in the Caucasus region, which belongs to the Language top-level class in legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnW.label: 445 Americans With Disabilities - Employment (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnW.definition: Action of discrimination against an employee with disabilities of any type in the work place, filed under 42 U.S.C. § 12117

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnW.label: Publishing Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnW.definition: A "Publishing Agreement" is a legal contract between an author or content creator and a publisher, outlining the terms under which the publisher will produce, distribute, and often market the author's work. The agreement specifies rights, royalties, deadlines, and other conditions pertaining to the publication of the work.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnW.label: Trust Formation Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnW.definition: Trust Formation (Service) refers to the legal work performed by a Legal Services Provider in creating a trust, which is a legal arrangement where a trustee holds and manages assets for the benefit of a beneficiary.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnc.label: P100 Project Administration
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnc.definition: Focuses on administrative aspects of the assignment, including planning, budgeting, and maintenance of documents. Covers developing, negotiating, and revising the administrative plan and the budget for a matter. Also includes developing and communicating project status reports. Time coded here is to be distinguished from strategizing about the project, which is included in the P300 code.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnc.label: Analysis and Strategy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnc.definition: Analysis (Strategy) refers to the process of evaluating and developing a plan of action to achieve a desired outcome in a legal matter, including identifying strengths and weaknesses of a case and determining the best course of action to pursue.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBne.label: L320 Document Production
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBne.definition: The concept of L320 Document Production refers to the process of producing documents during the discovery phase

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnh.label: Expedited Processing Objective
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnh.definition: Expedited processing objective refers to a procedural goal within a regulatory or administrative system to accelerate the review and decision-making process for certain applications, often for an additional fee or under special circumstances. This is commonly employed in scenarios such as visa applications, permit requests, or public benefit claims, where quicker processing is desirable for the applicant and meets certain criteria set by the authority

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBni.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Madison County 5
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBni.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Madison County, Indiana, with the authority to hear civil and criminal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnn.label: Conversion Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnn.definition: A Conversion Claim (Civil Theft) is a civil claim that arises when someone intentionally takes another person's property without permission, and then uses or sells it as their own.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnn.label: New Mexico Magistrate Court - San Miguel County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnn.definition: A court located in San Miguel County, New Mexico that has limited jurisdiction over certain types of cases.
english_labels: New Mexico Magistrate Court - San Miguel County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBns.label: Pretrial Release Revocation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBns.definition: The concept of Pretrial Release Revocation refers to the legal event of revoking a defendant's release from custody before trial, typically due to a violation of the conditions of their release.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnu.label: Tax Dispute Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnu.definition: Tax Dispute Practice, also known as a Tax Controversy Practice, involves representing and advising clients in disputes with tax authorities over tax liabilities, assessments, and compliance issues. This practice includes resolving controversies through negotiation, administrative proceedings, litigation, and alternative dispute resolution methods.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnv.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Beaver County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnv.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court in Beaver County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court system that handles minor criminal offenses, traffic violations, and civil cases involving amounts up to $12,000.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Beaver County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnz.label: Privacy Policy - Externally Facing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnz.definition: An externally facing privacy policy is a public document that outlines how a company or organization collects, uses, stores, and protects the personal information of its customers, users, or visitors. This policy serves to inform individuals about their rights regarding their personal data and to ensure the organization's compliance with applicable data protection laws and regulations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnz.label: New York Supreme Court - Montgomery County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBnz.definition: The New York Supreme Court - Montgomery County is a court of general jurisdiction located in Montgomery County, New York, with authority to hear and decide a wide range of legal disputes within its geographic jurisdiction.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - Montgomery County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoD.label: Lunda
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoD.definition: Lunda is a structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary, and is a specific language within the context of legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoD.label: Beyond a Reasonable Doubt
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoD.definition: The concept of "Beyond a Reasonable Doubt" refers to the highest standard of proof required in a criminal trial, where the evidence presented must be so convincing that there is no reasonable doubt in the mind of a reasonable person that the defendant committed the crime.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoG.label: New Jersey Superior Court - Monmouth County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoG.definition: The New Jersey Superior Court - Monmouth County is a specific court within the New Jersey Superior Court Appellate Division that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases in Monmouth County, New Jersey.
english_labels: New Jersey Superior Court - Monmouth County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoI.label: Land Conservation Rights
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoI.definition: Land Conservation Rights involve the legal entitlements and mechanisms to protect, preserve, and sustainably manage land and its natural resources. This can include the right of individuals, communities, or organizations to conserve land for ecological, historical, recreational, or cultural significance. Additionally, these rights can manifest through tools like conservation easements, land trusts, and zoning regulations, which aim to prevent degradation, limit development, and ensure the long-term protection of the land's intrinsic values.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoJ.label: HSSE Standards Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoJ.definition: A HSSE Standards Clause is a specific provision within a contract that outlines the health, safety, security, and environmental standards that must be adhered to by the parties involved.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoJ.label: Missouri Circuit Court - St. Charles County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoJ.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - St. Charles County: A specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within St. Charles County.
english_labels: Missouri Circuit Court - St. Charles County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoM.label: Consideration - Stock
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoM.definition: The concept of "Consideration - Stock" refers to the exchange of stocks as the form of payment in a legal agreement, where both parties agree to the transfer of ownership of the stocks in exchange for the fulfillment of obligations or promises.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoN.label: City of Birth
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoN.definition: City of Birth refers to the specific city or locality where an individual was born. This detail is often used for identification purposes and may be required for various legal, medical, or governmental activities. It is commonly recorded on birth certificates and sometimes in passports.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoN.label: matter_perc_shar_fees
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoN.definition: "MATTER_DISC_CRED.disc_cred_percent where MATTER_DISC_CRED.disc_credit_type equals ""Percent"" and MATTER_DISC_CRED.disc_credit_category equals ""Fee"" and MATTER_DISC_CRED.disc_cred equals ""MISF"" "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoO.label: Severance Pay Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoO.definition: A Severance Pay Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the compensation an employee will receive upon termination of employment, typically due to layoffs or restructuring.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoT.label: Contract Amendment Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoT.definition: A contract amendment clause is a provision added to a contract that allows for changes to be made to the original agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoW.label: Criminal Intent
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoW.definition: The mental state of a person when they commit a crime, including the intention to commit the act and knowledge of its wrongfulness.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoe.label: Commodity Investor
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoe.definition: Investors who invest in physical substances like gold, oil, or agricultural products.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoh.label: Crustaceans
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoh.definition: Crustaceans are a large class of arthropods within the subphylum Crustacea, characterized by a hard exoskeleton, jointed limbs, and typically two pairs of antennae. This diverse group includes crabs, lobsters, shrimp, and barnacles, and they are primarily aquatic, inhabiting marine and freshwater environments.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoq.label: Firm Non-Equity Partner
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoq.definition: A Firm Non-Equity Partner is a member of a law firm who is not a shareholder but has a partnership-like role in the firm.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBos.label: Collection of Documents Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBos.definition: Collection of Documents Practice refers to the legal practice of gathering and organizing relevant documents for a legal matter, typically in preparation for litigation or discovery.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBos.label: Mergers and Acquisitions Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBos.definition: The purchase of one company by another (an acquisition), or the blending of two companies into a new entity (a merger). A merger is a process by which two companies join and one new company continues to exist.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBox.label: Kamba
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBox.definition: Kamba is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary, and is a specific language within the context of legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoy.label: Article 6 Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoy.definition: An Article VI claim refers to a legal argument grounded in Article VI of the U.S. Constitution, which includes the Supremacy Clause, declaring federal laws and treaties to be the supreme law of the land. Such a claim may arise in disputes involving the precedence of federal law over state law, or the constitutionality of treaties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoz.label: Minnesota District Court - Itasca County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBoz.definition: Minnesota District Court - Itasca County is a specific court within the Minnesota District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Itasca County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBp1.label: oasis:Permission
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBp1.definition: A permission in the context of OASIS refers to a deontic specification that grants authorization or consent for a particular action or behavior.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBp1.label: Institutional Debt Offering
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBp1.definition: Institutional Debt Offering refers to the sale of debt securities primarily to institutional investors, such as banks, insurance companies, pension funds, and mutual funds. This method of distribution typically involves larger issuance amounts, more complex underwriting processes, and higher denominations compared to retail debt placements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBp4.label: Nonassertive Conduct
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBp4.definition: Nonassertive Conduct refers to actions, behaviors, or gestures that are not intended by the actor to communicate or assert the matter to be proven. This type of conduct is not considered hearsay because the actor does not intend to make a statement or assertion, and therefore, the reliability of the evidence is not dependent on the credibility of the actor.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBp6.label: Debtor Lying to Creditor About Assets
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBp6.definition: The concept of "Debtor Lying to Creditor About Assets" refers to the act of a debtor intentionally providing false information to a creditor regarding their assets in order to deceive them and avoid paying their debts.
english_labels: Debtor Lying to Creditor About Assets

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBp8.label: Ndebele, South; South Ndebele
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBp8.definition: A dialect of the Nguni language spoken in South Africa and Zimbabwe.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBp9.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Clark County (5th Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Clark County (5th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBp9.label: Sound Recording
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBp9.definition: A Sound Recording is a captured audio performance of sounds, whether musical, spoken, or otherwise, stored in a medium that can be played back, such as digital files, CDs, or vinyl records.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBpG.label: Public Finance Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBpG.definition: Law including legislation and regulations relating to the financial activities of government or public sector organizations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBpH.label: Georgia Superior Court - Warren County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBpH.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Warren County refers to a specific court within the Georgia Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Warren County, Georgia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBpH.label: 153 Recovery of Overpayment of Veterans' Benefits (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBpH.definition: Action relating to payments of veterans’ benefits, primarily including actions to recover overpayments.
english_labels: 153 Recovery of Overpayment of Veterans' Benefits (PACER NoS)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBpL.label: Consequential Damages Waiver Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBpL.definition: A Consequential Damages Waiver Clause is a provision in a contract that limits the liability of one party for indirect or consequential damages resulting from a breach of the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBpP.label: Value Added Tax Payment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBpP.definition: Value Added Tax (VAT) Payment encompasses all general consumption taxes charged on the value added to goods and services, irrespective of the method of deduction and the stages at which the taxes are levied. Typically, VAT allows for the immediate deduction of taxes on purchases by all entities except the final consumer and is imposed at all stages of production and distribution. In some countries, this category may include taxes on financial and insurance activities due to the difficulty in separating these receipts from general VAT collections or because they are considered integral to the VAT system.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBpS.label: Criminal Theft
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBpS.definition: The unlawful taking, carrying, leading, or riding away of property from the possession, or constructive possession, of another person.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBpS.label: Postal Service Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RBpS.definition: The Postal Service subsector includes the activities of the National Post Office and its subcontractors operating under a universal service obligation to provide mail services, and using the infrastructure required to fulfill that obligation. These services include delivering letters and small parcels. These articles can be described as those that can be handled by one person without using special equipment. This allows the collection, pick-up, and delivery operations to be done with limited labor costs and minimal equipment. Sorting and transportation activities, where necessary, are generally mechanized. The restriction to small parcels distinguishes these establishments from those in the transportation industries. These establishments may also provide express delivery services using the infrastructure established for provision of basic mail services.
