https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCCD.definition: United States Strategic Command (USSTRATCOM), is one of ten unified commands in the United States Department of Defense. It is responsible for strategic deterrence, global strike, and operating the Defense Department's Global Information Grid.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCCE.label: Anambra
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCCE.definition: Anambra is a state in Nigeria.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCCS.label: Agnosticism
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCCS.definition: Agnosticism is a philosophical position that asserts the uncertainty or impossibility of knowing the existence or non-existence of deities or other metaphysical entities. In legal contexts, it may refer to a neutral stance regarding religious beliefs or practices in matters such as oaths, testimonies, or religious accommodations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCCY.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Cooper County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCCY.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Cooper County: A court of law in Missouri that has jurisdiction over legal cases within Cooper County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCCb.label: Eggplants
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCCb.definition: Eggplants, also known as aubergines, are fruit vegetables from the Solanum melongena species, characterized by their glossy purple skin and spongy texture. They are widely used in cooking for their ability to absorb flavors and are valued for their fiber content, vitamins, and antioxidants.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCCe.label: Right to Alter Structure
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCCe.definition: The Right to Alter Structure refers to the legal permission an owner or lessee has to modify a building or other structure on a property. This right is often subject to local building codes, zoning laws, and potentially restrictive covenants or lease agreements, and may require permits or approval from governing bodies

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCCf.label: Recurrent Taxes on Property
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCCf.definition: Recurrent Taxes on Property are regular, ongoing taxes imposed on specific types of property or goods, typically assessed annually. Although rare in OECD member countries, these taxes can include levies on cattle, jewelry, windows, and other visible signs of wealth.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCCl.label: Multiple languages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCCl.definition: Multiple languages refer to the use of two or more distinct languages in a legal context.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCCo.label: Material Breach Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCCo.definition: A Material Breach Clause is a specific type of clause found in a contract that outlines the conditions under which a party's failure to perform a significant obligation will be considered a breach of the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCCr.label: Welfare Clause Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCCr.definition: A Welfare Clause claim refers to a legal argument challenging the constitutionality of a law or government action based on the interpretation and application of the Welfare Clause found in a particular jurisdiction's constitution. This claim asserts that the law or action exceeds the scope of the government's authority by not promoting the welfare of the people, as mandated by the clause, and therefore may be unconstitutional. The specific provisions and scope of the Welfare Clause can vary depending on the jurisdiction in question.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCCu.definition: Private investigators are individuals who are hired to conduct investigations and gather information on behalf of private clients.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCCv.label: Damages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCCv.definition: Monetary compensation sought or awarded by a party as a result of harm or loss caused by another party, which is a specific element of a legal claim.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDA.label: Cumulative Voting System
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDA.definition: The cumulative voting system is an electoral method where voters have multiple votes that they can distribute among one or more candidates as they choose. This system allows for greater representation of minority groups by enabling voters to concentrate their votes on a single candidate or spread them across several candidates.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDC.label: Georgia Superior Court - Harris County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDF.label: Right of Withdrawal
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDF.definition: The Right of Withdrawal, an element of moral rights in copyright law, empowers the creator to retract their work from the public domain under certain conditions. It reflects the creator's ongoing personal and emotional connection to their work, allowing them to change their mind about publication based on personal or ethical grounds.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDF.label: Brodsko-posavska zupanija
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDF.definition: Brodsko-posavska zupanija is a region in Croatia, which is a political subdivision of the country.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDN.label: Louisiana Supreme Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDN.definition: The Louisiana Supreme Court is the highest court in the state of Louisiana, with the authority to hear appeals from lower state courts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDS.label: Homeowners' Association
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDS.definition: A homeowners' association (HOA) is an organization formed by residents in a planned community or housing development, such as a neighborhood of single-family homes or a condominium complex. The HOA is responsible for managing and maintaining common areas, enforcing community rules and regulations, and collecting dues or assessments from homeowners to fund these activities. Homeowners' associations help ensure the upkeep and overall quality of life in the community but may also impose restrictions and guidelines on property use and appearance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDS.label: Insurrection
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDS.definition: An insurrection is a type of crime against the government that involves a violent uprising or rebellion against the established authority.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDS.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Wyoming County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDS.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Wyoming County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering legal proceedings at the county level in Pennsylvania.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDT.label: Elementary and Secondary Schools Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDT.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in furnishing academic courses and associated course work that comprise a basic preparatory education. A basic preparatory education ordinarily constitutes kindergarten through 12th grade. Examples include: Parochial schools, elementary or secondary, High schools, Primary schools, Kindergartens, Schools for the physically disabled, elementary or secondary, and Military academies, elementary or secondary

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDW.label: Contempt
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDW.definition: Contempt refers to the intentional disobedience or disregard of a court order or authority, which can result in criminal or civil penalties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDa.label: Breakup Fee Triggers
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDa.definition: Breakup Fee Triggers are provisions in a merger or acquisition agreement that specify the circumstances under which a termination fee will be paid by one party to the other.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDg.label: Charitable Trust
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDg.definition: A Charitable Trust is a legal arrangement where assets are held and managed by a trustee for charitable purposes, benefiting the public or a specific community. This trust operates under specific regulations to ensure that the trust's funds are used solely for the stated charitable objectives.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDp.label: Plurality-at-Large Electoral System
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDp.definition: The plurality-at-large electoral system, also known as block voting or plurality block voting, is a multi-winner voting method where each voter can cast as many votes as there are seats to be filled, and the candidates with the highest number of votes win. This system is often used in local elections and can result in the overrepresentation of the majority group.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDr.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Tipton County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDr.definition: A court located in Tipton County, Indiana that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographic area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDw.definition: Objectives related to regulatory filings (e.g., trademark application, patent applications, copyright registrations).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDw.label: Minimum Wage
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDw.definition: Minimum Wage is the legally mandated lowest hourly wage that employers are required to pay their employees. It is typically set by government authorities and is intended to establish a baseline income level for workers.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDz.label: Letter of Credit Obligation Breached
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCDz.definition: A Letter of Credit Obligation Breached refers to a situation where a party fails to fulfill their obligation to pay under a letter of credit, which is a document issued by a bank guaranteeing payment to a seller of goods or services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCE0.label: Statement Against Interest
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCE0.definition: A Statement Against Interest is a hearsay exception that allows the admission of statements that, at the time they were made, were contrary to the declarant's pecuniary, proprietary, or penal interest, or subjected the declarant to civil or criminal liability. This exception is based on the assumption that a person is unlikely to make a statement that goes against their own interests unless they believe it to be true.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCE0.label: Koulikoro
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCE0.definition: Koulikoro is a city in Mali.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCE0.label: At Will Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCE0.definition: An at-will clause is a provision in a contract that allows either party to terminate the agreement at any time without cause or penalty.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCE1.label: Requests for Admission Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCE1.definition: Requests for Admission Practice refers to the legal practice of using written requests to ask the opposing party to admit or deny certain facts in a legal matter, typically used in the discovery phase of litigation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCE1.label: Antitrust - Predatory Pricing Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCE1.definition: Antitrust - Predatory Pricing Claims refer to allegations of anti-competitive behavior by a company that sets prices below cost with the intention of driving competitors out of the market.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCE2.label: Office of the Whistleblower Protection Program
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCE2.definition: OSHA's whistleblower statutes protect whistleblowers from retaliation. An employer cannot retaliate by taking "adverse action" against workers who report injuries, safety concerns, or other protected activity.
english_labels: Office of the Whistleblower Protection Program

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCE5.label: Subsidy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCE5.definition: A Subsidy is a financial assistance provided by the government to individuals, businesses, or industries to support economic activities deemed beneficial for the public or to reduce the cost of goods and services. Subsidies can take various forms, including direct cash payments, tax breaks, or reduced interest loans, aimed at promoting economic growth, sustainability, and social welfare.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCE5.label: GSA Office of the Inspector General
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCE5.definition: The GSA Office of Inspector General (GSAOIG) was established by the Inspector General Act of 1978 (Public Law 95-452) as an independent unit responsible for promoting economy, efficiency, and effectiveness and detecting and preventing fraud, waste, and mismanagement in the General Services Administration's (GSA) programs and operations.
english_labels: GSA Office of the Inspector General

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCE6.label: Bureau of Justice Statistics
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCE6.definition: The United States Bureau of Justice Statistics (BJS) is a federal government agency belonging to the U.S. Department of Justice and a principal agency of the U.S. Federal Statistical System.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCE6.label: Dialysis Treatment Negligence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCE6.definition: Negligent provision of dialysis treatment by a medical professional, resulting in harm or injury to the patient.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCE8.definition: Nigde is a city located in Turkey.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEA.definition: Aklan is a province in the Philippines.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEA.definition: Goycay is a town located in Azerbaijan.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEC.label: Cash Flow Statement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEC.definition: A Cash Flow Statement is a financial document that shows the inflow and outflow of cash in a company over a specific period of time, and is typically used in bankruptcy and restructuring proceedings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCED.label: Role in Matter
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCED.definition: An individual or entity's role, responsibility, or function in executing the legal matter.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEE.label: Hardap
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEE.definition: Hardap is a region in Namibia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEE.label: Motels
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEE.definition: Motels are a type of real estate asset within the hospitality industry that provide temporary lodging accommodations for travelers.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEE.label: Civil Contempt
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEE.definition: Civil contempt refers to the willful disobedience of a court order or judgment that is intended to enforce a private right, and can result in sanctions or penalties imposed by the court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEE.label: Andorra
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEE.definition: A country located in the Pyrenees mountains between France and Spain.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEF.label: Dalarnas lan
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEF.definition: Dalarnas lan is a county in Sweden.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEP.label: Indiana Superior Court - Marion County, Probate Division
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEP.definition: A division of the Indiana Superior Court located in Marion County that handles legal matters related to the estates of deceased individuals.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCER.label: Human Resources Business Partner Manager
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCER.definition: An HRBP Manager, or Human Resources Business Partner Manager, is a managerial role within the Human Resources department focused on aligning business objectives with employees and management. They serve as a consultant to the management team on HR-related issues and work to develop integrated solutions that optimize employee performance, engagement, and retention

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEW.label: Arkansas Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEW.definition: The Arkansas Circuit Court is a court of general jurisdiction in the state of Arkansas that hears civil and criminal cases within its designated geographic area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEZ.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Clinton County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering civil and criminal proceedings at the county level in Pennsylvania.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEc.label: Temporary Child Custody
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEc.definition: Temporary Custody refers to the legal arrangement where a child is placed in the care of a guardian or custodian for a limited period of time, typically during the pendency of a matrimonial emergency application filed by the parents.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEe.label: Insane Party Rescinding Contract
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEe.definition: The concept of "Insane Party Rescinding Contract" refers to the legal action of canceling a contract by a party who was not mentally competent at the time of entering into the agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEe.label: Noticing Agent
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEe.definition: A Noticing Agent is an individual or entity who is authorized to provide legal notice to parties involved in a legal matter.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEg.label: Mandar

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEl.label: Copyright Registration Process
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEl.definition: The Copyright Registration Process involves submitting an application to a copyright office, such as the U.S. Copyright Office, along with a copy of the work to be registered and the required fee. Once the application is reviewed and approved, a Copyright Registration Document is issued, serving as public record and prima facie evidence of copyright ownership, which can be advantageous in legal disputes over infringement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEr.label: Urology Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEr.definition: Urology Malpractice refers to a type of medical malpractice claim that arises from the negligent or improper treatment of urological conditions by a healthcare provider.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEv.label: Indemnification by Service Provider Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEv.definition: A provision in a contract where a service provider agrees to compensate the other party for any losses or damages incurred as a result of the service provider's actions or omissions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEv.definition: "Knowledge Limited to Identified Persons" Language refers to a clause in a legal agreement that limits the scope of knowledge to only those individuals who have been identified in the agreement, and defines the circumstances under which a material adverse effect can occur.
english_labels: "Constructive Knowledge - Knowledge Limited to Identified Persons" Language
Material Adverse Effect Definition - "Knowledge Limited to Identified Persons" Language

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEw.label: Deal Collaboration Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEw.definition: Deal Collaboration Management refers to the process of coordinating and managing the collaboration between parties involved in a legal transaction. It falls under the broader category of Legal Transaction Management.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEx.label: Foundation and Competency Objections
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEx.definition: Foundation and Competency Objections are raised when a party in a legal proceeding believes that evidence lacks the necessary groundwork for admissibility (foundation) or when a witness lacks the qualifications to provide reliable testimony (competency). These objections aim to ensure that evidence and testimony meet legal standards for relevance, reliability, and expertise.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEx.label: Prisoner
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEx.definition: A person who is jailed or incarcerated.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEy.label: Terms of Sale
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCEy.definition: Terms of Sale specify the conditions under which a sale is transacted. These terms outline payment methods, delivery timelines, transfer of ownership, return policies, and other conditions and obligations relevant to the sale of goods or services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCF0.label: Securities and Financial Instruments Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCF0.definition: Law covering transactions and other dealings with securities including both federal- and state-level regulation by purely governmental regulatory agencies, listing requirements of exchanges, and rules of self-regulatory organizations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCF1.label: Fes-Boulemane
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCF1.definition: Fes-Boulemane refers to a region in Morocco with the code MA+05.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCF1.label: Bauchi
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCF1.definition: Bauchi is a city in Nigeria.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCF2.label: Colorado State Courts
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCF2.definition: Colorado State Courts are the judicial branch of the Colorado state government, responsible for interpreting and enforcing state laws and resolving legal disputes within the state.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCF2.label: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCF2.definition: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is a province in Pakistan.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCF5.label: Georgia District Court - Tift County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCF5.definition: A court located in Tift County, Georgia that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCF6.label: Sjelland
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCF6.definition: Sjelland is a region in Denmark.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCF8.label: Tunceli
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCF8.definition: Tunceli is a city located in Turkey.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCF8.label: U.S. District Court - D. New York
english_labels: U.S. District Court - D. New York

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCF8.label: Mehedinti
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCF8.definition: Mehedinti is a region or administrative subdivision located in Romania.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCF8.label: Oberosterreich
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCF8.definition: Oberosterreich is a region in Austria.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCF9.label: Susu
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCF9.definition: A language spoken primarily in Guinea, Sierra Leone, and Liberia, belonging to the Mande branch of the Niger-Congo language family.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFA.label: Defense Logistics Agency
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFA.definition: The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) is a combat support agency in the United States Department of Defense, with more than 26,000 civilian and military personnel throughout the world.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFB.label: Mariy El, Respublika
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFB.definition: A region within the Russian Federation, located in the eastern part of Europe.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFD.label: Sarawak
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFD.definition: Sarawak is a state located in Malaysia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFD.label: Misamis Oriental
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFD.definition: Misamis Oriental is a province in the Philippines.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFE.label: L410 Fact Witnesses
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFE.definition: A fact witness is a person who provides testimony in a trial based on their personal knowledge of the events or facts in question.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFE.label: Alba
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFE.definition: Alba is a region in Romania.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFF.label: U.S. Bankruptcy Court - W.D. North Carolina
english_labels: U.S. Bankruptcy Court - W.D. North Carolina
United States Bankruptcy Court, W.D. North Carolina

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFN.label: Maltese
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFN.definition: Maltese is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary, used in legal matters, that is specific to the Maltese islands and spoken by the Maltese people.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFO.label: DEPRECATED: Two-Step Tender Offer Followed by Merger
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFO.definition: A Two-Step Tender Offer Followed by Merger is a type of M&A Deal Structure where the acquiring company first makes a tender offer to the target company's shareholders, and then proceeds with a merger if a certain threshold of shares is acquired.
english_labels: DEPRECATED: Two-Step Tender Offer Followed by Merger
Two-Step Tender Offer Followed by Merger

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFP.label: Antitrust Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFP.definition: Antitrust Claims refer to legal claims made against individuals or companies for engaging in anti-competitive behavior, such as market allocation, vertical or horizontal agreements, pricing, or conspiracy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFT.label: Spendthrift Provision Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFT.definition: A spendthrift provision clause is a type of contractual clause that restricts a beneficiary's ability to transfer or assign their interest in a trust or estate, in order to protect the beneficiary's assets from creditors or other third parties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFa.label: Notice of Trial
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFa.definition: A Notice of Trial is a written communication that informs parties involved in a legal proceeding of the date and time of the trial.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFd.label: Left a Location
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFd.definition: "Left a Location" refers to the act of a person or object exiting a specific geographic area, often to establish presence or conduct activities elsewhere. Examples include a person leaving a state for tax purposes, an immigrant departing their country of origin, or a product being exported from its originating country for trade. Such events usually have legal, tax, or regulatory consequences.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFe.label: Safety Experts
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFe.definition: An expert in the area of safety, including someone who implements, manages and monitors safety programs, policies, and procedures that meet governmental safety standards (e.g., OSHA).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFg.label: Application to Pay Filing Fees in Installments
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFg.definition: An Application to Pay Filing Fees in Installments is a request made in a bankruptcy application to pay the required fees in installments rather than in a lump sum.
english_labels: Application to Pay Filing Fees in Installments

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFg.label: Litigant
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFg.definition: A party to litigation or court matter (e.g., criminal matter).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFj.label: Nyankole
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFj.definition: Nyankole is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary, and is a language within the context of legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFm.label: Indiana Superior Court - Clinton County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFm.definition: Indiana Superior Court - Clinton County refers to a specific court within the Indiana Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Clinton County, Indiana.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFs.label: Interference with Contracts and Business Relationships
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFs.definition: Interference with Contracts and Business Relationships refers to the intentional and unjustified interference with a contractual or business relationship between two parties, resulting in economic harm to one or both parties.
english_labels: Interference with Contracts and Business Relationships

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFu.label: Injurious Falsehood
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCFu.definition: A false statement made about a person or entity that causes harm to their reputation or business interests.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCG4.label: Freedom of Speech
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCG4.definition: A freedom of speech claim is a legal action initiated by an individual or entity alleging that their right to freedom of speech, as protected by the law (e.g., First Amendment of the United States Constitution), has been violated by the government or a government actor. The freedom of speech guarantees that the government shall not abridge the freedom of speech, which includes the right to express opinions, ideas, and beliefs without censorship or restraint. A freedom of speech claim may arise in various contexts, such as when a government body enacts a law or regulation that unduly restricts speech, when a public employee is disciplined for exercising their speech rights, or when a public forum is improperly restricted.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCG9.label: Ombudsman Report
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCG9.definition: An Ombudsman Report is a written document created by an independent mediator who investigates complaints and disputes, particularly in the context of bankruptcy and restructuring.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCGC.label: Inflation Risk
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCGC.definition: The risk that the value of assets or income will decrease as inflation shrinks the purchasing power of a currency.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCGE.label: Website
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCGE.definition: A Website is a collection of interconnected web pages hosted on the internet, accessible via a web browser, that provides information, services, or content to users. Protected under copyright law, websites grant the creators exclusive rights to reproduce, distribute, and display the content.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCGF.label: Florida Circuit Court - Hardee County - 10th Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCGF.definition: A Florida Circuit Court located in Hardee County within the 10th Circuit Court, responsible for administering legal proceedings within its jurisdiction.
english_labels: Florida Circuit Court - Hardee County - 10th Circuit Court

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCGU.label: Piedmont American Indian Association - Lower Eastern Cherokee NAtion SC (PAIA)
english_labels: Piedmont American Indian Association - Lower Eastern Cherokee NAtion SC (PAIA)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCGW.label: Principal-Agent Liability
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCGW.definition: Principal-Agent Liability is a legal concept that holds a principal responsible for the actions of their agent, who acts on their behalf, and can be held liable for any harm caused by the agent's actions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCGl.label: eSignatures Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCGl.definition: eSignatures Management refers to the process of creating, verifying, and managing electronic signatures within the context of contract and document management.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCGp.label: Florida Circuit Court - Columbia County - 3rd Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCGp.definition: A court located in Columbia County, Florida that is part of the larger Florida Circuit Court system.
english_labels: Florida Circuit Court - Columbia County - 3rd Circuit Court

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCGq.label: Involuntary Commitment to a Mental Health Facility
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCGq.definition: Involuntary commitment to a mental health facility is a legal process where an individual is mandated to be admitted to a psychiatric hospital or clinic against their will. This typically occurs when the individual poses a significant risk to themselves or others due to a mental disorder, and the decision is often based on medical evaluations and established legal criteria.
english_labels: Involuntary Commitment to a Mental Health Facility

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCGs.label: Arkansas Circuit Court - Garland Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCGs.definition: The Arkansas Circuit Court - Garland Cty. is a specific court within the Arkansas Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Garland County, Arkansas.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCGy.label: Intellectual Asset Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCGy.definition: Intellectual Asset Management refers to the process of identifying, protecting, and maximizing the value of a company's intellectual property assets, such as patents, trademarks, and copyrights, through strategic planning and legal management.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCGz.label: Voluntary Commitment to a Mental Health Facility
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCGz.definition: Voluntary commitment to a mental health facility occurs when an individual willingly and knowingly agrees to be admitted to a psychiatric hospital or clinic for treatment. This decision is made without external coercion, and the individual retains the right to request discharge, though there might be conditions or procedures to follow before release.
english_labels: Voluntary Commitment to a Mental Health Facility

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCH1.label: Metadata Scrubbing Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCH1.definition: Metadata Scrubbing Management refers to the process of removing sensitive or identifying information from electronic documents and files.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCH1.label: Mutual Fund
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCH1.definition: A Mutual Fund is an investment vehicle that pools money from various investors to purchase a diversified portfolio of assets, which can include stocks, bonds, money market instruments, or other securities. Managed by professional portfolio managers, the fund aims to generate returns for its investors according to its stated investment objectives, while spreading risk across a range of assets.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCH2.label: Technology Procurement Services
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCH2.definition: Technology Procurement Services refers to the process of acquiring technology products and services for an organization, typically involving consulting and management services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCH6.label: Recognition of Foreign Insolvency
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCH6.definition: Recognition of foreign insolvency involves a domestic court acknowledging and giving effect to an insolvency proceeding initiated in another country. This legal process facilitates cooperation between jurisdictions, enabling efficient administration and resolution of cross-border insolvency cases.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCH9.label: Business License
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCH9.definition: A business license is a permit or certification issued by a governmental authority that allows an individual or company to operate a business within a specific jurisdiction. The license serves as proof of compliance with local, state, or federal regulations and is often required for tax purposes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHD.label: Equity Security Holders List
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHD.definition: A list of individuals or entities who hold equity securities in a company, typically used in bankruptcy and restructuring proceedings to determine the distribution of assets.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHE.label: Right to Confront Witnesses
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHE.definition: The right to confront witnesses is a fundamental aspect of a fair trial, ensuring that a defendant in a criminal case has the opportunity to question or cross-examine the witnesses testifying against them. Protected by the Sixth Amendment of the United States Constitution, this right enables the defense to challenge the credibility, accuracy, and reliability of the witnesses' testimony, and helps ensure that the trial process is transparent and adversarial.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHF.label: Mississippi County Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHF.definition: Mississippi County Court refers to a court of law that operates within the jurisdiction of a specific county in Mississippi and is responsible for hearing and deciding cases related to civil and criminal matters within that county.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHG.label: Lushai
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHG.definition: Lushai is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary, belonging to the family of languages under the Language top-level class.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHI.label: Requests for Admission
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHI.definition: Requests for Admission are a type of discovery document used in legal proceedings where one party requests that the other party admit or deny certain facts or allegations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHK.label: Junior Colleges Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHK.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in furnishing academic, or academic and technical, courses and granting associate degrees, certificates, or diplomas below the baccalaureate level. The requirement for admission to an associate or equivalent degree program is at least a high school diploma or equivalent general academic training.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHK.label: New York City Court - Troy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHK.definition: A court located in Troy, New York that operates under the jurisdiction of the New York City Court system.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHO.label: Motion to Transfer Venue for Convenience
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHO.definition: A Motion to Transfer Venue for Convenience is a legal request to move a case from one court to another based on the convenience of the parties or witnesses involved, rather than the location of the incident or the jurisdiction of the court.
english_labels: Motion to Transfer Venue for Convenience

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHQ.label: Business Operations Risk
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHQ.definition: Business Operations Risk refers to the potential for losses or disruptions that may occur in a company's daily activities, processes, or systems. These risks can stem from various sources, such as technology failures, human errors, or supply chain disruptions, ultimately impacting the organization's overall performance and profitability.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHR.label: Name Change
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHR.definition: A name change refers to the legal act of altering one's official given name, surname, or both. The process typically requires the submission of a petition to a court and, upon approval, results in a legal decree formally recognizing the new name

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHR.label: Kimbundu
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHR.definition: Kimbundu (Language) is a structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary, specifically referring to the language spoken by the Kimbundu people in Angola.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHY.label: Specific Learning Disorder
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHY.definition: Specific Learning Disorder is a neurodevelopmental condition characterized by persistent difficulties in learning and using academic skills. These difficulties manifest in areas such as reading, writing, or mathematics, and are not attributable to intellectual disabilities, sensory impairments, or inadequate educational opportunities. It affects an individual's ability to process and comprehend information, leading to difficulties in reading, writing, math, or other cognitive skills essential for academic performance. These disabilities are lifelong conditions that can vary in severity and often require specialized teaching methods and accommodations to support learning.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHb.label: Governmental Immunity for Condition of Public Property
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHb.definition: Governmental Immunity for Condition of Public Property: A legal concept that shields government entities from liability for injuries or damages caused by the condition of public property, unless the government entity failed to take reasonable steps to correct the dangerous condition.
english_labels: Governmental Immunity for Condition of Public Property

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHb.label: Pituitary Gland Disorders
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHb.definition: Pituitary gland disorders involve conditions affecting the pituitary gland, an endocrine organ responsible for regulating various bodily functions through hormone production. These disorders can lead to hormonal imbalances and impact growth, metabolism, and reproductive functions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHb.label: Berry Creek Rancheria of Maidu Indians
english_labels: Berry Creek Rancheria of Maidu Indians

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHd.label: Olives
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHd.definition: Olives are small, oval fruits from the Olea europaea tree, known for their culinary and oil-producing uses. They are consumed as table olives or processed into olive oil, valued for their rich flavor, healthy fats, and nutritional benefits, including antioxidants and vitamins.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHe.label: Insurance Policy Terminated Without Notice to Insured
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHe.definition: An insurance policy terminated without notice to the insured refers to the situation where an insurance policy is cancelled by the insurer without informing the policyholder, resulting in the termination of coverage and potential legal disputes.
english_labels: Insurance Policy Terminated Without Notice to Insured

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHg.label: Tswana
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHg.definition: A Bantu language spoken in Botswana, South Africa, and Namibia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHj.label: Statutory Fraud
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHj.definition: The concept of Statutory Fraud refers to a type of fraud that involves a violation of a specific statute or regulation, and is often used in legal claims related to fraudulent activities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHj.label: EMEA Market Region
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHj.definition: The EMEA Market Region refers to the geographical area encompassing Europe, the Middle East, and Africa, recognized for its economic diversity, varied consumer markets, and complex regulatory frameworks. Businesses often consider this region strategically important due to its significant economic potential and cultural diversity.
english_labels: Europe, Middle East, and Africa Market Region

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHj.label: Medical Provider Liability to Third Parties
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHj.definition: The legal responsibility of a medical provider to compensate third parties for harm caused by their actions or omissions, including situations where the provider is not directly at fault but may be held liable under agency or vicarious liability principles.
english_labels: Medical Provider Liability to Third Parties

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHj.label: Elapsed Time Method Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHj.definition: An Elapsed Time Method Clause is a provision in a contract that specifies the amount of time that must pass before a certain action or event can occur, and is a subcategory of a Contractual Clause.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHr.label: Florida County Court - Miami-Dade County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHr.definition: A court located in Miami-Dade County, Florida that handles civil and criminal cases within its jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHs.label: Oklahoma Court on the Judiciary - Appellate Division
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCHs.definition: The Oklahoma Court on the Judiciary - Appellate Division is a specific court within the Oklahoma State Courts system that hears appeals.
english_labels: Oklahoma Court on the Judiciary - Appellate Division

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCI1.label: Motion to Amend Default Judgment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCI1.definition: A Motion to Amend Default Judgment is a formal request made to a court to modify or change a judgment that was entered against a party who failed to appear or respond to the original lawsuit.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCI3.label: Bounced Check Causing Damage
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCI3.definition: A bounced check causing damage refers to a situation where a check is returned unpaid by a bank, resulting in harm or loss to the recipient of the check.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCI7.label: Central Visual Acuity Loss
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCI7.definition: Central visual acuity loss is a condition where the best-corrected vision in the better eye measures 20/200 or less, indicating severe impairment in the central vision. This level of acuity loss signifies significant visual impairment that cannot be corrected to a level better than 20/200, typically requiring adaptive measures for daily living.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCI8.label: Motion to Withdraw as Counsel
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCI8.definition: A Motion to Withdraw as Counsel is a formal request made by an attorney to be removed from representing a client in a legal matter.
english_labels: Motion to be Relieved As Counsel

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCI9.label: Concealing Stolen Property
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCI9.definition: The act of hiding or keeping stolen property secret, with the intention of preventing its discovery or recovery by the rightful owner or authorities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCI9.label: Participating Dividend Payment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCI9.definition: Participating Dividend Payment refers to a type of dividend income where preferred shareholders, in addition to receiving their fixed rate of prior dividend, also share in further dividend distributions and capital distributions with common shareholders. This feature allows preferred shareholders to benefit from the company's profitability beyond the fixed dividend rate.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIB.label: Privatization
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIB.definition: Privatization is the process of transferring ownership and management of a business, enterprise, or public service from the government to private individuals or entities. This often aims to improve efficiency, foster competition, and reduce public sector burden.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIG.label: Taking Deposition
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIG.definition: The act of taking a deposition involves questioning a witness under oath outside of court proceedings, typically done in a seated position.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIG.label: French, Old
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIG.definition: Old French (842-ca.1400) is a historical language that was spoken in France during the period from 842 to around 1400.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIP.label: Contract Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIP.definition: The General Theory of Contracts is an umbrella term used in civil law jurisdictions, like Spain and Latin America, that refers to the body of law that governs contracts. In the U.S. and other common law jurisdictions, the equivalent would simply be Contract Law or Law of Contracts. They both concern principles and rules that regulate agreements made between parties, detailing how contracts are formed, executed, and potentially breached, and what remedies are available.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIQ.label: Arraignment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIQ.definition: Arraignment is a legal event that involves the defendant being brought before a court to hear the charges against them and to enter a plea.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIQ.label: Provider Timekeeper Level
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIQ.definition: Provider Timekeeper Level refers to the classification of legal service providers based on their level of expertise and experience, including paralegals, lawyers, and limited license legal technicians (LLLTs).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIS.label: Subcontractors Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIS.definition: A Subcontractors Clause is a provision in a contract that allows the primary contractor to hire other individuals or companies to perform some or all of the work required under the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIV.label: Cisgender
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIV.definition: Cisgender describes an individual whose gender identity aligns with the sex they were assigned at birth. It is used to differentiate from transgender individuals, whose gender identity does not align with their assigned sex.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIZ.label: Bisexual
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIZ.definition: Bisexual refers to an individual who is attracted to both men and women, although not necessarily to the same degree or in the same way. It is a sexual orientation that is part of the LGBTQIA+ spectrum, and like other orientations, the experience of being bisexual can vary among individuals.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIc.label: Trial Testimony Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIc.definition: Trial Testimony Practice refers to the specific legal work performed by a Legal Services Provider during a trial, which involves presenting evidence and testimony to support a client's case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIc.label: Minnesota District Court - Freeborn County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIc.definition: A Minnesota District Court located in Freeborn County, which is a trial court of general jurisdiction in Minnesota, handling civil and criminal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCId.label: DEPRECATED: Fee Charge
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCId.definition: Deprecated in favor of Base Amount

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIk.label: Subordinated Creditor
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIk.definition: A Subordinated Creditor holds a claim or loan against a debtor that ranks below other debts in terms of repayment priority, often arising when creditors agree to lesser priority in exchange for potential higher returns. In bankruptcy, these creditors are paid only after senior debts have been settled, making their recovery prospects less certain.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIs.label: Georgia Superior Court - Echols County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIs.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Echols County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIs.label: Multiple Question Objection
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIs.definition: A Multiple Question Objection, also known as a Compound Objection, is raised when a party in a legal proceeding believes that a question posed by the opposing counsel contains two or more distinct inquiries. This objection aims to ensure that each question is addressed separately, allowing for clear and focused responses.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIv.label: Fruit Vegetables
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIv.definition: Fruit vegetables are a category of vegetables that develop from the flowering part of the plant and contain seeds, technically classifying them as fruits. They are consumed in savory dishes and valued for their diverse flavors, textures, and nutritional content, including vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIv.label: Motion in Limine to Exclude Fact Witness
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIv.definition: A Motion in Limine to Exclude Fact Witness is a legal request made by one party to prevent a specific witness from testifying at trial, based on the argument that their testimony would be irrelevant, prejudicial, or inadmissible.
english_labels: Motion in Limine to Exclude Fact Witness

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIw.label: Asset Type
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCIw.definition: Type of resource that is owned or controlled by a person, business, or economic entity

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJ0.label: Limited Conservatorship of Juvenile
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJ0.definition: A Limited Conservatorship of Juvenile is a legal arrangement where a conservator is appointed to care for a minor who has a developmental disability and is unable to fully care for themselves, but still has some ability to make decisions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJ2.label: Lifecycle of an AI System
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJ2.definition: The Lifecycle of an AI System encompasses the series of phases involved in the development, deployment, and maintenance of an AI system. These phases include planning and design, data collection and processing, model building, testing, evaluation, verification, validation, deployment, and operation and monitoring, often occurring iteratively, rather than sequentially.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJ5.label: Locked Box Pricing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJ5.definition: Locked Box is a pricing mechanism in M&A transactions where the purchase price is based on the target company's financial statements at a specified historical date, known as the locked box date. From this date to the closing date, the seller is prohibited from extracting value from the company, ensuring price certainty and protecting the buyer against financial deterioration.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJA.label: New Jersey Municipal Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJA.definition: New Jersey Municipal Court is a court of limited jurisdiction in New Jersey that handles minor criminal offenses, traffic violations, and small claims cases.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJA.label: Sardinian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJA.definition: A dialect of the Romance language spoken in Sardinia, Italy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJB.label: Retainer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJB.definition: A recurring amount agreed to be billed.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJC.label: Food and Beverage Retailers Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJC.definition: Industries in the Food and Beverage Retailers subsector primarily retail general or specialized lines of food and beverage products. Establishments in this subsector with fixed point-of-sale locations have special equipment (e.g., freezers, refrigerated display cases, refrigerators) for displaying food and beverage products and have staff trained in the processing of food products to guarantee the proper storage and sanitary conditions required by regulatory authority. Vending machine operators are also included in this subsector.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJE.label: Pancreatic Gland Disorders
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJE.definition: Pancreatic gland disorders disrupt the production of hormones, including insulin, affecting metabolism and digestion. These disorders can lead to conditions such as diabetes mellitus and digestive enzyme insufficiency.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJE.label: Violation of Probation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJE.definition: The violation of probation is a breach of the terms and conditions set forth by a court order that requires an individual to comply with certain rules and regulations as a result of a prior criminal misdemeanor offense.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJG.label: Failure to Repair or Remedy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJG.definition: The Failure to Repair or Remedy is a legal concept within Landlord-Tenant Claims that refers to the landlord's failure to fix or address issues with the rental property that they are responsible for maintaining.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJK.label: Motion to Amend Petition
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJK.definition: A Motion to Amend Petition is a formal request to modify or change a legal document submitted to a court or other authority, typically made during the pre-trial phase of a case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJQ.label: Motion to File Amendment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJQ.definition: A Motion to File Amendment is a formal request to submit a revised version of a document or pleading to a court or other legal authority.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJW.label: Secured Transaction
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJW.definition: A secured transaction is a legal agreement where a borrower pledges collateral to a lender to secure a loan or other obligation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJY.label: Basa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJY.definition: Basa (Language) is a specific written or spoken structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary, and is a subcategory of Language in the context of legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJZ.label: Motion to Disqualify Judge on Due Process Grounds
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJZ.definition: A Motion to Disqualify Judge on Due Process Grounds is a legal request to remove a judge from a case based on a violation of the defendant's right to a fair trial.
english_labels: Motion to Disqualify Judge on Due Process Grounds

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJn.label: Accommodation Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJn.definition: Industries in the Accommodation subsector provide lodging or short-term accommodations for travelers, vacationers, and others. There is a wide range of establishments in these industries. Some provide lodging only, while others provide meals, laundry services, and recreational facilities, as well as lodging. Lodging establishments are classified in this subsector even if the provision of complementary services generates more revenue. The types of complementary services provided vary from establishment to establishment. The subsector is organized into three groups: (1) traveler accommodation, (2) recreational accommodation, and (3) rooming and boarding houses, dormitories, and workers' camps. The Traveler Accommodation industry group includes establishments that primarily provide traditional types of lodging services. This group includes hotels, motels, and bed-and-breakfast inns. In addition to lodging, these establishments may provide a range of other services to their guests. The RV (Recreational Vehicle) Parks and Recreational Camps industry group includes establishments that operate lodging facilities primarily designed to accommodate outdoor enthusiasts. Included are travel trailer campsites, recreational vehicle parks, and outdoor adventure retreats. The Rooming and Boarding Houses, Dormitories, and Workers' Camps industry group includes establishments providing temporary or longer-term accommodations, that for the period of occupancy, may serve as a principal residence. Board (i.e., meals) may be provided but is not essential. Establishments that manage short-stay accommodation establishments (e.g., hotels and motels) on a contractual basis are classified in this subsector if they both manage the operation and provide the operating staff. Such establishments are classified based on the type of facility managed and operated.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJn.label: Breach of Contract for Failure of Consideration
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJn.definition: The Breach of Contract for Failure of Consideration refers to a situation where one party fails to fulfill their contractual obligations due to a lack of consideration from the other party.
english_labels: Breach of Contract for Failure of Consideration

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJp.label: Endangered Species Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJp.definition: An Endangered Species Claim is a legal assertion made to protect a species at risk of extinction due to environmental changes, habitat loss, or human activities. This claim seeks to enforce conservation measures and legal protections under national or international laws.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJp.label: Family Health Public Benefit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJp.definition: Family Health Public Benefit refers to government programs specifically designed to provide healthcare coverage or financial assistance for medical needs to families. These programs aim to ensure that both adults and children within a family unit have access to necessary healthcare services

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJp.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Monroe County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJp.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Monroe County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering legal proceedings in Monroe County, Pennsylvania.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Monroe County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJq.label: Statement of Executive Compensation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJq.definition: A Statement of Executive Compensation is a disclosure detailing the remuneration packages of a company's key executives and directors. It is usually included in annual proxy statements and is required by securities regulators.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJy.label: Florida Circuit Court - Bradford County - 8th Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCJy.definition: A court located in Bradford County, Florida that is part of the 8th Circuit Court system.
english_labels: Florida Circuit Court - Bradford County - 8th Circuit Court

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCK2.label: Motion to Extend Time to File Bill of Costs
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCK2.definition: A Motion to Extend Time to File Bill of Costs is a request made to the appellate court to allow additional time beyond the original deadline for a party to submit a statement of costs incurred during the legal proceedings.
english_labels: Motion to Extend Time to File Bill of Costs

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCK3.label: Hemp
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCK3.definition: Hemp is a versatile plant species cultivated for its strong and durable fibers, seeds, and oil, with applications ranging from textiles and construction to food and personal care products. Known for its environmental benefits, hemp is also used in bioplastics, paper, and as a sustainable alternative to traditional raw materials.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKA.label: Oregon Land Use Board of Appeals
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKA.definition: The Oregon Land Use Board of Appeals is a specialized court within the Oregon State Courts system that hears appeals related to land use decisions made by local governments.
english_labels: Oregon Land Use Board of Appeals

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKE.label: Playbook
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKE.definition: Document containing a matter type's variations and preferred practices.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKG.label: Te-Moak Tribes of Western Shoshone Indians of Nevada
english_labels: Te-Moak Tribes of Western Shoshone Indians of Nevada

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKG.label: expense_code
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKG.definition: "Expense code for this line item, e.g. ""E101"". Only one code per line item. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKH.label: Natural Gas Distribution Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKH.definition: This industry comprises: (1) establishments primarily engaged in operating gas distribution systems (e.g., mains, meters); (2) establishments known as gas marketers that buy gas from the well and sell it to a distribution system; (3) establishments known as gas brokers or agents that arrange the sale of gas over gas distribution systems operated by others; and (4) establishments primarily engaged in transmitting and distributing gas to final consumers.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKM.label: Absentee Ballot
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKM.definition: An Absentee Vote is a voting method that allows a person to cast a ballot without being physically present at a designated polling station on election day. This mechanism enables voters who cannot attend in person due to various reasons such as illness, travel, or military service to participate in the electoral process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKM.label: Domestic Servitude Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKM.definition: A domestic servitude claim is a legal allegation that a person is being forced to work in a household setting against their will, often through manipulation or coercion. This is a form of human trafficking and is considered a violation of labor laws and human rights.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKO.label: Unearned Income
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKO.definition: Unearned income refers to money received by an individual from sources other than employment, such as interest, dividends, rental income, or certain government benefits. Unlike earned income, which results from active work, unearned income comes from investments, inheritances, or other passive sources.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKT.label: Informational Advertisement
english_labels: An Informational Advertisement, also known as a Public Service Announcement (PSA), is a type of advertising aimed at raising awareness, educating the public, or promoting beneficial behaviors and social issues. These advertisements are typically sponsored by government agencies, non-profit organizations, or public health groups and focus on delivering important messages to the community.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKT.label: Dismissal
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKT.definition: Dismissal is a type of trial court created document that terminates a case without a decision on the merits, and can be either voluntary or involuntary, with or without prejudice, and for various reasons such as violation of rules or failure to prosecute.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKV.label: Arrival / Departure Record
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKV.definition: Arrival / Departure Record (in the U.S., I-94 form) is a document used by the national immigration agency (e.g., U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP)) to track the arrival and departure dates of foreign visitors entering and leaving the destination country (e.g, United States). It contains information such as the visitor's name, birth date, country of citizenship, visa classification, and the authorized period of stay.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKc.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Greene County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKc.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Greene County refers to a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Greene County, Missouri.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKh.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Pemiscot County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKh.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Pemiscot County: A court of law in the state of Missouri that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Pemiscot County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKj.label: Escort
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKj.definition: In legal terms, an escort may refer to an individual who provides companionship or social accompaniment for a fee. The distinction between an escort and a prostitute often hinges on whether sexual services are explicitly offered or advertised, as this can have significant legal implications.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKk.label: 08_1 Intellectual Property Rights (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKk.definition: Intellectual Property Rights (PACER NoS) refers to a category of legal cases related to the protection of creative works and inventions, including patents, trademarks, copyrights, and trade secrets, as classified under the PACER Nature of Suit (NoS) Codes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKo.label: Fee Adjustment Note
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKo.definition: A Fee Adjustment (Credit or Discount) Note is a document that records a reduction in the amount charged for legal services provided, either as a credit or discount, and is a subcategory of Discounts and Credits and Engagement Fee Detail.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKr.label: Licenses and Permits
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKr.definition: A license is a legal authorization granted by a governing body or entity, permitting an individual or organization to engage in certain activities, such as operating a business or practicing a profession. Licenses are generally subject to regulations and can be revoked if the licensee fails to comply with specified conditions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKw.label: Mental Health Expert
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKw.definition: An expert in the field of mental health.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKy.label: Economic Rights
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCKy.definition: Economic rights refer to the entitlements that enable individuals to achieve a basic standard of living, such as the rights to work, receive a fair wage, and have access to essential social services like healthcare and education. These rights are often articulated in international treaties and may be protected to varying degrees by national laws.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCL4.label: OCIJ Immigration Court Practice Manual
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCL4.definition: Rules promulgated by the Office of the Chief Immigration Judge (OCIJ) regarding practice in U.S. immigration courts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCL4.label: Minnesota District Court - Dakota County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCL4.definition: Minnesota District Court - Dakota County: A specific court within the Minnesota District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Dakota County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCL6.label: Failure to Provide Wage Records Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCL6.definition: A failure to provide wage records claim is a legal action brought by an employee against their employer for not complying with the legal obligation to furnish access to or copies of the employee's wage-related documents. Wage records may include payroll records, pay stubs, and timekeeping data, and the claim typically arises when an employer either refuses or neglects to provide the requested information within the specified time frame mandated by applicable laws.
english_labels: Failure to Provide Wage Records Claim

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCL9.label: Defamation Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCL9.definition: The action of damaging the good reputation of someone; slander or libel.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLF.label: Structured Finance Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLF.definition: Law surrounding securitization and asset-backed securities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLG.label: Fiduciary Termination Right
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLG.definition: The Fiduciary Termination Right is a provision in a legal agreement that allows a fiduciary to terminate the agreement if they believe it is in the best interest of their client, and is typically included in deal protection provisions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLH.label: Georgia Superior Court - Richmond County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLH.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Richmond County is a specific court within the Georgia Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Richmond County, Georgia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLH.label: Sunset Provision Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLH.definition: A sunset provision clause is a type of contractual clause that specifies the expiration date or termination conditions of an agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLP.label: Republican Form Clause Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLP.definition: A Republican Form Clause claim refers to a legal argument based on the Republican Form Clause of the United States Constitution, asserting that the federal government must ensure that each state is governed by a republican form of government. It aims to prevent the establishment of monarchies or other non-republican forms of government within the states, promoting representative democracy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLQ.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Washington County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLQ.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Washington County, Indiana, with the power to hear and decide a wide range of legal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLa.label: Complex Ruleset
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLa.definition: A complex ruleset is a type of rule that is characterized by having a large number of interdependent and intricate provisions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLh.label: Extraordinary Ability Immigrant Petition
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLh.definition: An Extraordinary Ability Immigrant Petition (in the U.S., the I-140 EB-1) allows individuals with extraordinary abilities in the sciences, arts, education, business, or athletics to apply for permanent residency in the United States. Applicants must demonstrate sustained national or international acclaim and recognition in their field of expertise. Applicants must be able to demonstrate extraordinary ability in the sciences, arts, education, business, or athletics through sustained national or international acclaim.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLh.label: Filing Fee Waived
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLh.definition: Filing Fee Waived: A status within a legal dispute indicating that the fee required to file the case has been waived.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLh.label: Conservatorship of Adult
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLh.definition: A conservatorship of adult is a legal arrangement where a court appoints a responsible person or organization to care for an adult who is unable to care for themselves due to physical or mental limitations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLm.label: Code of Conduct
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLm.definition: A Code of Conduct is a set of written guidelines or rules outlining the ethical principles, responsibilities, and proper practices expected of individuals within a particular organization or community. It serves as a standard for behavior and decision-making, often enforced through disciplinary action.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLn.label: Arkansas Circuit Court - Howard Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLn.definition: A court located in Howard County, Arkansas that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLo.label: Uncured Default Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLo.definition: An Uncured Default Clause is a provision in a contract that allows one party to declare a default by the other party if they fail to cure the breach within a specified time period.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLo.label: Trial Court Judge
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLo.definition: A judge in a trial court, which is a lower-level court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLp.label: Arizona Superior Court - Greenlee Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLp.definition: Arizona Superior Court - Greenlee Cty. is a specific court within the Arizona Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Greenlee County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLs.label: Requirement to Litigate
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLs.definition: Provision stating that if a legal proceeding is commenced to restrict the consummation of the Transaction, one or more parties are required to litigate against those efforts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLu.label: Massachusetts Superior Court - Hampden County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLu.definition: The Massachusetts Superior Court - Hampden County is a court of general jurisdiction in Massachusetts that hears civil and criminal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLx.label: 09 Other Statutes (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLx.definition: 09 Other Statutes (PACER NoS) refers to a category of legal cases filed in the PACER system that involve violations of statutes not covered by other specific categories.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLz.label: Article
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLz.definition: A article that discusses a legal topic. Articles are usually published or otherwise distributed (e.g., website, blog). Authors are usually lawyers, law firms, academics, or academic institutions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLz.label: Matters Listed on Disclosure Schedules Language
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCLz.definition: A description of specific language used in disclosure schedules that list exceptions to the definition of Material Adverse Effect (MAE) in a legal agreement.
english_labels: Matters Listed on Disclosure Schedules Language

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCM3.label: Engagement Invoice Type
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCM3.definition: An identifier indicating whether an invoice is ""own account"" (""O""), or ""third party"" (""T"").

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCM3.label: total_amount
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCM3.definition: "The final billed value of the fee item after application of all FEE_ITEM_DISC_CRED.disc_cred_amounts. Does not include MATTER_DISC_CRED.disc_cred_amounts or taxes on the fee item. FEE.total_amount = FEE.base_amount + FEE.item_disc_cred_amount "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCM3.label: Unlawful Gaming and Lotteries
