https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCM3.definition: Unlawful Gaming and Lotteries refers to the illegal act of participating in games of chance or lotteries that are not authorized by law, and is considered a crime against the public.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCM9.label: Appeals Under Court Rule
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCM9.definition: Appeals Under Court Rule refers to the process of challenging a lower court's decision by filing a request for review with a higher court, as governed by the specific procedural rules established by that court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMB.label: Palm Oil
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMB.definition: Palm oil is a vegetable oil extracted from the fruit of the oil palm tree, primarily the species Elaeis guineensis. Known for its versatility, palm oil is widely used in food production, cosmetics, and industrial applications, and is valued for its high yield and economic importance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMC.label: Apples
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMC.definition: Apples are a type of fruit crop from the Malus domestica tree, known for their crisp texture and sweet to tart flavor. They are consumed fresh, cooked, or processed into products such as juices, ciders, sauces, and baked goods, contributing significantly to human nutrition with their fiber and vitamin content.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMC.label: Relinquishment Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMC.definition: A relinquishment clause is a provision in a contract that allows one party to give up or surrender their rights or claims to something specified in the agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMC.label: Ownership Type Attributes
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMC.definition: Ownership Type Attributes refer to the specific characteristics and categories of shares that represent ownership in a company. These attributes include distinctions such as common shares, ordinary shares, and preferred shares, each with unique rights, privileges, and obligations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMD.label: Assessment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMD.definition: Assessment refers to the process of evaluating or appraising a situation or circumstance, typically within the context of a legal dispute or litigation event.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMD.label: Warrant Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMD.definition: Warrant Agreement is a document that outlines the terms of a warrant, which is a derivative giving the holder the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an underlying asset at a specific price within a certain period. Warrant agreements detail the exercise price, expiration date, and other terms.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMI.label: Motion for Sanctions
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMI.definition: A Motion for Sanctions is a formal request made to a court asking for punishment or penalties to be imposed on a party for failing to comply with discovery or other procedural rules during a legal proceeding.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMK.label: tk_id
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMK.definition: "Unique ID of a person billing on this matter. The same tk_id may appear multiple times if the timekeeper's name, level or rate changes during the billing period. This value is assigned by the firm and should remain the same for a biller across all work done by the biller within the firm (could be biller initials if the biller initials will be unique across that firm) "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMS.label: Florida County Court - Walton County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMS.definition: Florida County Court - Walton County is a specific court located in Walton County, Florida that handles civil and criminal cases within its jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMZ.label: Party-List Proportional Representation System
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMZ.definition: The Party-List Proportional Representation System is an electoral method where voters cast their ballots for a party rather than individual candidates, and seats are allocated to each party in proportion to the number of votes received. The party then fills its allocated seats with candidates from a pre-determined list.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMb.label: Business Executive
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMb.definition: A business executive is someone holding a senior management position within a company or organization, responsible for making strategic decisions and overseeing the implementation of the company's policies and objectives. Executives typically include roles such as Chief Executive Officer (CEO), Chief Information Officer (CIO), Senior Vice President (SVP), and Vice President (VP), among others.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMe.label: Texas District Court - Fort Bend County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMe.definition: A Texas District Court located in Fort Bend County, which has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical boundaries.
english_labels: Texas District Court - Fort Bend County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMe.label: Boating DUI/BUI
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMe.definition: Operating a boat or watercraft while under the influence of drugs or alcohol, which is classified as a criminal misdemeanor offense.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMg.label: Pauma Band of Luiseno Mission Indians
english_labels: Pauma Band of Luiseno Mission Indians

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMj.label: Enforcement of Security Interest Delegating Seller’s Performance
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMj.definition: The Enforcement of Security Interest Delegating Seller's Performance refers to the legal process of ensuring that a seller who has delegated their performance to a third party is still held responsible for fulfilling their obligations to a creditor who has a security interest in the property being sold.
english_labels: Enforcement of Security Interest Delegating Seller’s Performance

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMo.label: Trover
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMo.definition: A legal claim for the recovery of damages resulting from the conversion of personal property by another party, falling under the categories of property and premises liability claims.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMt.label: Honorable Discharge
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCMt.definition: An "Honorable Discharge" from the military signifies that a service member has met or exceeded the conduct and performance standards of the armed forces throughout their service period. It indicates that the individual has served honorably, fulfilling their commitments effectively and without any significant disciplinary infractions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCN2.label: Employment Offer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCN2.definition: A job offer is a formal proposal made by an employer to a candidate selected for a position, detailing the terms and conditions of employment. This includes information about the role, salary, benefits, start date, and other pertinent details.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCN2.label: Legal Issue
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCN2.definition: A legal question where the author seeks and/or posits an answer.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCN3.label: Not Opposed During Tail Period
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCN3.definition: Not Opposed During Tail Period: A condition in the Timing of Acquisition Proposal Closing where the target company does not express opposition during the specified period after the proposal is made.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNA.label: BILLING_START_DATE
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNA.definition: The term BILLING_START_DATE refers to the date on which a billing period begins, as defined in the LEDES98BI V5 Format Rev 1-2020 standard for electronic legal invoicing.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNA.label: Total Operating Revenues Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNA.definition: A Total Operating Revenues Clause is a provision in a contract that specifies the total amount of revenue generated by a business during a certain period of time, which is used to calculate payments or other financial obligations under the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNA.label: Kidnapping
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNA.definition: The act of unlawfully taking or confining a person, typically for ransom or as a means of coercion, and is considered a crime against individuals.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNC.label: Obstruction of Justice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNC.definition: The intentional interference with the administration of law or justice, including but not limited to the tampering with or destruction of evidence, the intimidation of witnesses, or the giving of false testimony.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCND.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Clark County Circuit 2
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCND.definition: The Indiana Circuit Court - Clark County Circuit 2 is a court of general jurisdiction in Indiana that hears civil and criminal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.
english_labels: Indiana Circuit Court - Clark County Circuit 2

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNJ.label: Youth Arrival Immigrant
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNJ.definition: Youth Arrival Immigrants (in the U.S., DACA (Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals) immigrants) are individuals who were brought to a country as children and have lived there without legal status. DACA is a U.S. policy that provides temporary relief from deportation and work authorization to eligible individuals who meet certain age, educational, and background criteria

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNK.label: Penalty Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNK.definition: A penalty clause is a provision in a contract that specifies a predetermined amount of money or other penalty that one party will owe to the other if they breach the terms of the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNL.label: Online Research Expense
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNL.definition: An online research expense is a type of expense that is incurred by a party in a legal matter for conducting research on the internet or other online sources.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNN.label: Employment Harassment Based on Protected Characteristics
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNN.definition: Employment Harassment Based on Protected Characteristics refers to the mistreatment of an employee by a colleague or superior in the workplace due to their membership in a protected class, such as race, gender, or religion.
english_labels: Employment Harassment Based on Protected Characteristics

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNP.label: Texas District Court - Matagorda County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNP.definition: A Texas District Court located in Matagorda County, which has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNQ.label: Analysis of Employee Benefits/Pensions
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNQ.definition: The Analysis of Employee Benefits/Pensions is the examination and evaluation of the benefits and pension plans provided to employees by an employer, typically in the context of legal obligations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNS.label: Milestone Payment Schedule Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNS.definition: A Milestone Payment Schedule Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the specific dates or events that trigger payment obligations, typically tied to the completion of certain project milestones.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNV.label: Gift Tax Payment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNV.definition: Gift Tax Payment refers to the settlement of taxes imposed on the transfer of wealth or property during an individual's lifetime that exceeds certain thresholds. This tax is generally paid by the donor, not the recipient, and is intended to prevent the avoidance of estate and inheritance taxes through lifetime gifts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNV.label: 01 Contract (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNV.definition: A Contract (PACER NoS) is a legal agreement between two or more parties that creates an obligation to do or not do a particular thing, categorized under the PACER Nature of Suit (NoS) Codes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNX.label: Minnesota District Court - Chippewa County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNX.definition: The Minnesota District Court - Chippewa County is a specific court within the Minnesota District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Chippewa County, Minnesota.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNY.label: Stipulation to Allow Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNY.definition: A Stipulation to Allow Claims is a legal agreement between parties in a lawsuit that allows certain claims to be accepted without further dispute or litigation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNd.label: Governance Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNd.definition: A Governance Agreement is a document that outlines the framework, procedures, and policies guiding the management and oversight of an organization, ensuring alignment with its goals and objectives.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNd.label: JH30 Joint expert evidence (UK J-CODE)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNd.definition: As [JH10] (own expert evidence) with appropriate modifications.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNf.label: New York Supreme Court - Steuben County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNf.definition: The New York Supreme Court - Steuben County is a court of general jurisdiction located in Steuben County, New York, with authority to hear and decide a wide range of civil and criminal cases.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - Steuben County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNh.label: Fraudulent Transfers
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNh.definition: Fraudulent Transfers refer to the transfer of assets made with the intent to hinder, delay, or defraud creditors. This concept falls under the broader category of Fraud Claims, Avoidance Action Claims, Banking, Commercial Paper, and Creditor Claims.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNn.label: Alzheimer's Disease
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNn.definition: Alzheimer's disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by the gradual decline in cognitive functions, including memory, reasoning, and language skills. It is the most common cause of dementia, leading to significant impairment in daily activities and requiring comprehensive medical and supportive care.
english_labels: Senile Dementia of the Alzheimer Type

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNo.label: Dravidian languages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNo.definition: A group of languages spoken in southern India and parts of Sri Lanka, characterized by a distinct grammatical structure and vocabulary, and including Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, and Malayalam.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNo.label: California Superior Court - San Mateo Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNo.definition: California Superior Court - San Mateo Cty. is a specific court within the California Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within San Mateo County.
english_labels: California Superior Court - San Mateo Cty.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNu.label: Mine Safety and Health Administration Claim
english_labels: Mine Safety and Health Administration Claim

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNw.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Pettis County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCNw.definition: A Missouri Circuit Court in Pettis County is a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Pettis County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCO0.label: Rural Market Segment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCO0.definition: The rural market segment consists of consumers or businesses located in countryside areas or small towns, typically characterized by lower population density and distinct lifestyle and consumption patterns compared to urban areas. Businesses targeting this segment often adapt their products and marketing strategies to cater to the needs and preferences of rural consumers, who may have limited access to certain goods and services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCO3.label: Mutual Confidentiality Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCO3.definition: A mutual confidentiality clause is a provision in a contract that requires both parties to keep certain information confidential and not disclose it to third parties without consent.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCO4.label: Jury Deliberation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCO4.definition: Jury Deliberation refers to the process by which a group of jurors discuss and analyze evidence presented during a trial in order to reach a verdict.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCO5.label: Art
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCO5.definition: Art refers to the expression or application of human creative skill and imagination, typically in a visual form such as painting or sculpture, producing works to be appreciated primarily for their beauty or emotional power. It encompasses various mediums, techniques, and styles, which are often subject to cultural and historical context.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCO7.label: Malicious Civil Prosecution
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCO7.definition: The concept of Malicious Civil Prosecution refers to the intentional and wrongful initiation of a civil lawsuit without probable cause, for the purpose of harassing, injuring, or otherwise causing harm to the defendant.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCO8.label: Restrictive Covenant
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCO8.definition: A restrictive covenant, in property law, is a clause in a contract or deed that limits what the owner of the property can do with it, often to preserve the value and enjoyment of adjoining properties. In employment law, it refers to an agreement, typically between an employer and employee, that restricts the employee's actions post-employment, such as prohibiting competition or solicitation of clients.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCOE.label: Bullying
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCOE.definition: A bullying claim is a legal assertion that an individual has been subjected to repeated aggressive behavior, typically involving a real or perceived power imbalance. It can occur in various environments, including the workplace, schools, and online, and may involve physical, verbal, or psychological harassment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCOL.label: Moapa Band of Paiute Indians of the Moapa River Indian Reservation, Nevada
english_labels: Moapa Band of Paiute Indians of the Moapa River Indian Reservation, Nevada

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCOM.label: Bar Association
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCOM.definition: A Bar Association is a professional organization of lawyers that serves multiple functions, including regulating the legal profession, providing continuing legal education, and offering resources and support to its members. These organizations may also engage in advocacy, public service, and the setting of ethical standards for lawyers.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCOO.label: Document Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCOO.definition: Document Management: The process of organizing, storing, and retrieving electronic or physical documents in a systematic and efficient manner, often involving the use of software tools and workflows.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCOY.label: Contact Name Suffix
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCOY.definition: A "Contact Name Suffix" is a set of letters or abbreviations that follow an individual's last name to provide additional information about that person. These suffixes can indicate generational lineage (e.g., "Jr." or "Sr."), professional or academic qualifications (e.g., "Ph.D." or "M.D."), or other honors and titles

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCOZ.label: Massachusetts Superior Court - Essex County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCOZ.definition: The Massachusetts Superior Court - Essex County is a court of general jurisdiction in Massachusetts that hears civil and criminal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCOa.label: Kashubian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCOa.definition: Kashubian (Language) is a written or spoken structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary, and is a subcategory of Language, specifically referring to the Kashubian language.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCOc.label: Restricted Asset Ownership
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCOc.definition: Restricted Ownership refers to the limitations and special conditions imposed on the ownership, transfer, or sale of assets (e.g., securities). These restrictions can include country-specific regulations, legal requirements, and contractual obligations that govern who can own or transfer these assets and under what conditions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCOl.label: Outside
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCOl.definition: Actor attribute designating an external role (e.g., Outside Counsel, External Counsel, External Expert).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCOt.label: Motor Vehicle and Parts Dealers Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCOt.definition: Industries in the Motor Vehicle and Parts Dealers subsector retail motor vehicles and parts. Establishments in this subsector often operate from a showroom and/or an open lot where the vehicles are on display. The display of vehicles and the related parts require little by way of display equipment. The personnel generally include both the sales and sales support staff familiar with the requirements for registering and financing a vehicle as well as a staff of parts experts and mechanics trained to provide repair and maintenance services for the vehicles. Specific industries included in this subsector identify the type of vehicle being retailed. Sales of capital or durable nonconsumer goods, such as medium- and heavy-duty trucks, are always included in wholesale trade.
english_labels: Motor Vehicle and Parts Dealer Industry
Motor Vehicle and Parts Dealers Industry

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCOv.label: Environmental Indemnification Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCOv.definition: An Environmental Indemnification Clause is a provision in a contract that requires one party to compensate the other for any losses or damages resulting from environmental contamination or pollution caused by the first party's actions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCOz.label: Post-Trial Motions
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCOz.definition: Post-Trial Motions are requests made by a party after a trial has concluded, asking the court to take a specific action, such as granting a new trial or amending the findings, based on the evidence presented during the trial.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCP0.label: Insurer's Breach of Implied Covenant of Good Faith and Fair Dealing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCP0.definition: The Insurer's Breach of Implied Covenant of Good Faith and Fair Dealing refers to a violation by an insurance company of the obligation to act in good faith and deal fairly with its policyholders, which is implied in every insurance contract.
english_labels: Insurer's Breach of Implied Covenant of Good Faith and Fair Dealing

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCP4.label: Patent Reexamination Process
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCP4.definition: The Patent Reexamination Process allows the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) to re-evaluate the validity of an existing patent based on new evidence or prior art not considered during the original examination. This process can be requested by the patent owner or a third party and aims to confirm the patent's claims or cancel them if they are found to be invalid.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCP6.label: Florida Circuit Court - Marion County - 5th Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCP6.definition: A court located in Marion County, Florida that is part of the larger Florida Circuit Court system.
english_labels: Florida Circuit Court - Marion County - 5th Circuit Court

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCP7.label: Compensation Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCP7.definition: A Compensation Related Agreement is a legally binding contract that specifically focuses on the structure and details of an employee's compensation, including elements like base salary, bonuses, stock options, and other financial incentives. These agreements serve to outline how an employee's pay is determined, disbursed, and adjusted over time, ensuring clarity and fairness in compensation arrangements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCPG.label: Curtilage
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCPG.definition: Curtilage refers to the area immediately surrounding a dwelling, including associated buildings and structures, that is considered part of the home for legal purposes. This concept relates to property law and criminal law, particularly concerning privacy rights and search and seizure protections.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCPJ.label: Berber languages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCPJ.definition: Berber languages are a group of languages spoken by various ethnic groups in North Africa, characterized by their unique grammar and vocabulary.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCPQ.label: Taxonomy/Ontology Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCPQ.definition: Taxonomy/Ontology Management refers to the organization and management of knowledge structures and systems used to categorize and classify information related to a specific domain or subject matter, within the broader field of Knowledge Management.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCPR.label: Drug Possession
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCPR.definition: The possession of illegal or controlled substances, which is classified as a criminal offense that is less serious than a felony.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCPS.label: Other Miscellaneous Retailers
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCPS.definition: This industry group comprises establishments primarily engaged in retailing miscellaneous specialized lines of merchandise (except motor vehicle and parts dealers; building material and garden equipment and supplies dealers; food and beverage retailers; furniture, home furnishings, electronics, and appliance retailers; general merchandise retailers; health and personal care retailers; gasoline stations and fuel dealers; clothing, clothing accessories, shoe, and jewelry retailers; sporting goods, hobby, and musical instrument retailers; book retailers and news dealers; florists; office supplies, stationery, and gift retailers; and used merchandise retailers).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCPV.label: Capitan Grande Band of Diegueno Mission Indians
english_labels: Capitan Grande Band of Diegueno Mission Indians

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCPZ.label: Inari Sami
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCPZ.definition: A language spoken by the Inari Sami people, primarily in Finland and Russia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCPi.label: Peeping Tom Violation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCPi.definition: To secretly look through a window, doorway, keyhole, or other aperture for the purpose of voyeurism.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCPm.label: Imaging Facility Negligence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCPm.definition: Negligence by an imaging facility in the context of medical malpractice claims.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCPt.label: Commercial Transactions Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCPt.definition: Law related to business contracts and agreements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCPv.label: Ineffective Assistance of Counsel
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCPv.definition: Ineffective Assistance of Counsel refers to a claim made by a defendant that their attorney's performance during a criminal trial or appeal was so deficient that it deprived them of their constitutional right to a fair trial.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCPy.label: Georgia District Court - Washington County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCPy.definition: A court located in Washington County, Georgia that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its designated area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCPz.label: Agent’s Negligence Causing Harm to Others
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCPz.definition: Agent's Negligence Causing Harm to Others: The legal concept where an individual or entity is held responsible for causing harm or injury to another person or entity due to their failure to exercise reasonable care or caution.
english_labels: Agent’s Negligence Causing Harm to Others

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQ5.label: Reinforcement Learning
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQ5.definition: Reinforcement Learning (RL) is a subset of machine learning that enables an artificial system, or agent, to optimize its behavior in a given environment by learning from feedback signals, such as rewards or punishments. The goal is to maximize the cumulative reward received, which is determined by a reward function representing the system's objectives (e.g., answering legal questions, drafting legal documents).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQ5.label: ext_name
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQ5.definition: "Used to provide the name of the variable. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQ6.label: Jones Act Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQ6.definition: A Jones Act Claim is a legal claim made under the Jones Act, which provides compensation for seamen who are injured or killed while working on a vessel in navigable waters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQ6.label: Georgia Superior Court - Crawford County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQ6.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Crawford County refers to a specific court within the Georgia Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Crawford County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQ8.label: 210 Land Condemnation (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQ8.definition: Action by a governmental entity to take privately-owned real property (land or buildings) for public use for compensation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQ9.label: Bank Secrecy and Anti-Money Laundering Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQ9.definition: Law regulating financial institutions relating to money laundering.
english_labels: Bank Secrecy and Anti-Money Laundering Law

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQ9.label: Interlingua
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQ9.definition: Interlingua is a constructed language developed by the International Auxiliary Language Association for the purpose of facilitating communication between people of different linguistic backgrounds.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQC.label: Administrative Dispute Proceeding Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQC.definition: All or some part of a cause heard and determined by an Administrative Agency or governmental entity. Any legal step or action taken at the direction of, or by the agency or entity.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQE.label: New Jersey Superior Court - Union County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQE.definition: The New Jersey Superior Court - Union County is a trial court within the New Jersey court system that has jurisdiction over cases within Union County.
english_labels: New Jersey Superior Court - Union County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQF.label: Virginia Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQF.definition: The Virginia Circuit Court is a court of general jurisdiction in the state of Virginia that has the authority to hear a wide range of civil and criminal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQF.label: M&A F7 Securities Regulatory Matters Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQF.definition: A legal practice area that specializes in advising clients on securities regulatory matters related to mergers and acquisitions.
english_labels: M&A F7 Securities Regulatory Matters Practice

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQJ.label: Matrimonial Emergency Applications
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQJ.definition: Matrimonial Emergency Applications refer to legal requests made in family law and matrimonial claims for temporary relief, such as maintenance, child support, custody, and protection orders, to address urgent and pressing issues that require immediate attention.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQX.label: Electronic Fund Transfer Privacy or Safety Violation Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQX.definition: A law that governs the privacy and safety of electronic fund transfers, specifically in the context of banking, commercial paper, and creditor claims.
english_labels: Electronic Fund Transfer Privacy or Safety Violation Law

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQX.label: Campaign Finance Violation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQX.definition: A campaign finance violation is a type of crime against the government and a statutory or regulatory claim that involves breaking laws related to the financing of political campaigns.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQY.label: Construction Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQY.definition: The Construction industry group comprises establishments primarily engaged in the construction of buildings or engineering projects (e.g., highways and utility systems). Establishments primarily engaged in the preparation of sites for new construction and establishments primarily engaged in subdividing land for sale as building sites also are included in this sector.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQZ.label: Directory Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQZ.definition: Directory Management is the management of information resources that organize and provide access to a collection of data or documents, within the context of Knowledge Management.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQa.label: Georgia Superior Court - Charlton County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQa.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Charlton County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Charlton County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQu.label: Piercing the Corporate Veil
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQu.definition: Piercing the Corporate Veil is a legal concept that allows a court to disregard the limited liability protection of a corporation or partnership and hold its shareholders or partners personally liable for the entity's actions or debts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQu.label: Military Discharge
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQu.definition: Military Discharge is the formal release of a service member from their obligation to continue service in the armed forces. The discharge can occur for various reasons, such as the completion of a service term, medical reasons, or disciplinary actions, and may be classified as honorable, general, or other types, affecting future veteran benefits.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQz.label: Washington Superior Court - Chelan County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCQz.definition: Washington Superior Court - Chelan County is a specific court located in Chelan County, Washington that operates under the jurisdiction of the Washington Superior Court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCR0.label: Audiovisual Work
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCR0.definition: An Audiovisual Work is a creation that combines both visual and auditory elements, such as films, television shows, and videos, intended to be experienced simultaneously. Protected under copyright law, audiovisual works grant the creator exclusive rights to reproduce, distribute, and publicly display the content.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCR2.label: General Relief Benefit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCR2.definition: General Relief Benefit, also known as a general assistance program, refers to a form of public assistance provided by local or state governments to individuals or families who do not qualify for specialized aid programs, such as unemployment or disability benefits. The aim is to offer temporary financial support for basic needs like food, housing, and medical care.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCR7.label: Immunity and Privilege
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCR7.definition: Immunity and Privilege refers to legal defenses that protect individuals or entities from being held liable or from having to disclose certain information in a legal proceeding. These defenses can include governmental immunity, parental immunity, and various types of privileges such as attorney-client privilege or fair and true reporting privilege.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCR9.label: Negligence Per Se
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCR9.definition: Negligence Per Se is a legal concept that refers to a situation where an action or failure to act violates a law or regulation, and that violation automatically establishes a breach of duty in a negligence case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCR9.label: Unfair Import Investigation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCR9.definition: Adjudicatory investigations conducted under section 337 of the Tariff Act of 1930, frequently involving allegations of patent or trademark infringement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCRA.label: UTBMS MF80 Tax
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCRA.definition: A specific category within the UTBMS coding system used to classify legal services related to tax matters in the context of mergers and acquisitions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCRA.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Carbon County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCRA.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Carbon County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering legal proceedings in the Carbon County region of Pennsylvania.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Carbon County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCRK.label: cl_lf_id
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCRK.definition: "A vendor ID that uniquely identifies the law firm, as specified by the client. Could be the law firm's tax id number or other value used by the client to uniquely identify the law firm. Values required in this field may vary from client to client, but within a client's e-billing implementation only one such unique ID is allowed per law firm. Some client AP systems maintain multiple vendor IDs for a law firm that could be, for example, location dependent. It is not intended that multiple lf_vendor_ids for the same law firm would be supported by this field as they would be impossible to program into the law firm's time and billing software. Clients must choose only one unique identifier per law firm to be used in this field. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCRN.label: Western Frisian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCRN.definition: A language spoken in the northwestern region of the Netherlands, characterized by its use of the Frisian alphabet and grammar rules.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCRR.label: California Superior Court - Merced Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCRR.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Merced County, California, with the power to hear and decide a wide range of legal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCRS.label: Contact Middle Name
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCRS.definition: Contact Middle Name refers to the middle name of an individual serving as a point of contact in professional or business interactions. While not always used, when included, it helps to differentiate individuals with common first and last names and may appear in formal documentation or correspondence.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCRV.label: Post-Conviction Modification
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCRV.definition: Post-conviction modification refers to the legal processes available to an individual after a conviction to alter, reduce, or eliminate the consequences of that conviction. Examples include expungement, where the criminal record is sealed or erased; and pardon, where the individual is formally forgiven for the crime. These modifications can help restore rights and opportunities lost due to the initial conviction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCRd.label: Oil Rights
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCRd.definition: These rights pertain to the ownership and control of oil reserves located beneath a specific parcel of land. The owner of these rights can extract the oil or lease, sell, or transfer these rights to another party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCRh.label: Buyer Recovering Costs Due to Title Defect
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCRh.definition: The concept of "Buyer Recovering Costs Due to Title Defect" refers to the legal right of a purchaser of property to seek compensation for expenses incurred as a result of a defect in the title of the property, such as legal fees or costs associated with correcting the defect.
english_labels: Buyer Recovering Costs Due to Title Defect

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCRm.label: Protection of Property from Damage
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCRm.definition: The Protection of Property from Damage is a legal objective within the context of Bankruptcy and Restructuring, aimed at safeguarding assets from harm or destruction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCRm.label: Ship and Boat Building Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCRm.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in building boats.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCRt.label: Constructive Fraud in Contract
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCRt.definition: Constructive Fraud in Contract refers to a situation where one party to a contract misleads or deceives the other party, causing them to enter into the contract under false pretenses, without disclosing important information that would have affected their decision to enter into the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCRw.label: New York City Court - Buffalo Viol.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCRw.definition: A court located in Buffalo, New York that has jurisdiction over violations of the law within its geographical area.
english_labels: New York City Court - Buffalo Viol.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCS1.label: Fee Paid
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCS1.definition: Fee Paid refers to the specific amount of money that has been paid by the client to the lawyer or law firm for the legal services provided, and is a subcategory of Engagement Fee Detail.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCS5.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Newton County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCS5.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Newton County refers to a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Newton County, Missouri.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCS9.label: Accountant Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCS9.definition: Accountant Malpractice refers to a claim of professional negligence or misconduct by an accountant, which results in harm or damages to their client.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCS9.label: Slander of Title
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCS9.definition: The term "Slander of Title" refers to a false and malicious statement made about someone's property or ownership rights, which causes harm to their reputation and results in financial loss or damages.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSC.label: Guardian Ad Litem
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSC.definition: A Guardian Ad Litem (GAL) is a court-appointed individual, often an attorney or a trained professional, who represents and protects the best interests of a minor, an incapacitated person, or someone otherwise unable to represent themselves in legal proceedings. The GAL investigates the circumstances of the case, communicates with relevant parties, and provides an independent report and recommendations to the court, ensuring that the person they represent receives fair and unbiased consideration of their needs and rights

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSG.label: Health Care Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSG.definition: This industry group comprises establishments providing health care and social assistance for individuals. The sector includes both health care and social assistance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSG.label: Procedural Due Process Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSG.definition: A procedural due process claim is a legal action initiated by an individual or entity alleging that their right to procedural due process, as protected by the Fifth and Fourteenth Amendments of the United States Constitution, has been violated by the government or a government actor. Procedural due process requires the government to follow fair and established procedures before depriving an individual of their life, liberty, or property interests. A procedural due process claim may arise in various contexts, such as when the government fails to provide adequate notice, a fair and impartial hearing, or an opportunity to be heard before taking an action that impacts an individual's rights. Examples of procedural due process violations include the termination of public benefits without prior notice, the suspension of a student from a public school without a hearing, or the seizure of property without proper procedures.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSG.label: Freedom of Information Act Request
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSG.definition: A Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) Request is a formal request made under the FOIA law to obtain access to government records or information.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSG.label: PACER Nature of Suit Codes
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSG.definition: PACER Nature of Suit (NoS) Codes are a standardized set of codes used to categorize legal cases filed in the PACER system, with each code representing a specific type of legal claim or cause of action.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSO.label: Writ
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSO.definition: A writ is a formal written order issued by a body with administrative or judicial jurisdiction, often a court. Writs command the addressee to act or refrain from acting in some way, and they can take various forms such as writs of habeas corpus, mandamus, or certiorari.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSR.label: Negligent Infliction of Emotional Distress
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSR.definition: Negligent Infliction of Emotional Distress refers to a legal claim that arises when a person suffers emotional harm due to the negligent actions of another party, either as a direct victim or as a bystander.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSX.label: UTBMS MB00 Purchase / Merger Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSX.definition: A UTBMS MB00 Purchase/Merger Agreement is a legal document that outlines the terms and conditions of a purchase or merger between two companies, falling under the broader category of UTBMS Mergers and Acquisitions (M&A).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSa.label: Metlakatla Indian Community, Annette Indian Reserve
english_labels: Metlakatla Indian Community, Annette Indian Reserve

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSb.label: Oregon Circuit Court - Wallowa County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSb.definition: The Oregon Circuit Court - Wallowa County is a specific court within the Oregon Circuit Court system, located in Wallowa County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSd.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Harrison County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSd.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Harrison County is a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Harrison County, Missouri.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSe.label: Failure to Exhaust Contractual Remedy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSe.definition: The Failure to Exhaust Contractual Remedy is a defense in civil litigation where the defendant argues that the plaintiff did not fulfill the contractual obligations before filing a lawsuit.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSi.label: Prayer in Public School Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSi.definition: A claim made by parents alleging that the education system has violated their civil rights by allowing prayer in public schools.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSk.label: Javanese
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSk.definition: Javanese (Language) refers to the written or spoken structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary specific to the Javanese language, which is a member of the Austronesian language family and primarily spoken on the island of Java in Indonesia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSn.label: No Hire Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSn.definition: A "No Hire Clause" is a provision in a contract that prohibits one party from hiring or soliciting the employees of the other party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSp.label: Extraordinary Writ
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSp.definition: An extraordinary writ is a legal motion filed in an appellate court that seeks relief outside of the normal appeals process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSq.label: Chagatai
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSq.definition: Chagatai is a language that belongs to the Turkic language family and was once widely spoken in Central Asia and parts of Russia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSt.label: Washington Superior Court - Ferry County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSt.definition: Washington Superior Court - Ferry County refers to a specific court within the Washington Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Ferry County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSt.label: Committee Charter
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSt.definition: A Committee Charter is a formal document that outlines the purpose, authority, and responsibilities of a committee within an organization. It serves as a guiding framework for the committee's operations, defining its objectives, scope of work, membership, decision-making process, and reporting requirements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSt.label: Superseded Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSt.definition: The previously effective law has been superseded by some authority (e.g., statute).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSu.label: Minnesota District Court - Traverse County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSu.definition: Minnesota District Court - Traverse County: A specific court within the Minnesota District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Traverse County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSv.label: Email Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSv.definition: Email Management refers to the process of organizing, storing, and retrieving electronic messages in a business or legal setting.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSx.label: Asset Delivery Attribute
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSx.definition: The Asset Delivery Attribute indicates whether the settlement of an option, when exercised, is made in cash or involves the physical delivery of the underlying instruments. This attribute defines the method by which the option holder receives value upon exercising the option.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSz.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Fountain County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCSz.definition: Indiana Circuit Court - Fountain County refers to a specific court within the Indiana Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Fountain County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCT6.label: Transfer of Ownership Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCT6.definition: A Transfer of Ownership Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the conditions under which ownership of a particular asset or property is transferred from one party to another.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCT9.label: International Organization Visa - Diplomats
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCT9.definition: An International Organization Visa for diplomats refers to a specialized visa category that allows foreign diplomats representing their countries at international organizations to enter and reside in a host country for the duration of their diplomatic assignment. This visa comes with specific diplomatic privileges and immunities in accordance with international law to facilitate their diplomatic duties and interactions within the international organization's context.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTD.label: Mutual Limitation of Liability Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTD.definition: A mutual limitation of liability clause is a provision in a contract where both parties agree to limit their liability to a certain amount or exclude certain types of damages in case of breach or other legal claims.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTK.label: Motion to Expunge
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTK.definition: A Motion to Expunge is a legal request made in trial courts or bankruptcy proceedings to remove or erase a record or document from the court's official records.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTM.label: Flat Buyer Consent Requirement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTM.definition: A Flat Buyer Consent Requirement is a legal concept that refers to the specific requirement for a buyer's consent in a transaction, without any additional conditions or qualifications.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTO.label: Debt Security Offering Method
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTO.definition: Debt Security Offering Method refers to the various strategies and processes employed by issuers to sell debt securities to investors. These methods can vary based on the type of investors targeted, regulatory requirements, and the desired speed and confidentiality of the issuance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTQ.label: Motion to Stay Proceedings Pending ITC Investigation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTQ.definition: A Motion to Stay Proceedings Pending ITC Investigation is a legal request to pause a court case while an investigation is conducted by the International Trade Commission.
english_labels: Motion to Stay Proceedings Pending ITC Investigation

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTQ.label: Arbitrary and Capricious
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTQ.definition: A legal standard of review used by appellate courts to determine whether an agency's decision was made without any rational basis or in an unpredictable manner.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTV.label: Unsolicited Information Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTV.definition: An Unsolicited Information Clause is a provision in a contract that specifies the conditions under which unsolicited information provided by one party to the other will be treated as confidential and not used for any purpose other than the intended purpose.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTY.label: Zuni Tribe of the Zuni Reservation
english_labels: Zuni Tribe of the Zuni Reservation

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTZ.label: Reservation of Rights Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTZ.definition: A Reservation of Rights Clause is a provision in a contract that allows a party to retain certain rights or defenses even after entering into the agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTh.label: Articulation Disorder
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTh.definition: An Articulation Disorder is a speech disorder characterized by difficulties in correctly producing speech sounds, leading to mispronunciations that can affect intelligibility. This condition can result from various factors, including developmental delays, structural anomalies, neurological impairments, or hearing loss.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTi.label: New Jersey Special Statutory Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTi.definition: A New Jersey Special Statutory Court is a specialized court within the New Jersey State Courts system that is created by statute to handle specific types of cases.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTi.label: Fee Increase or Decrease
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTi.definition: A Fee Increase or Decrease is a type of discount or credit that modifies the original cost of legal services provided, resulting in either an increase or decrease in the overall fee charged.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTm.label: Georgia Superior Court - Walton County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTm.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Walton County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Walton County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTn.label: Employment Record
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTn.definition: An "Employment Record" is a structured historical record that documents an individual's employment-related information, including details about their work history, positions held, employers, dates of employment, and relevant achievements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTs.label: Current Policy Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTs.definition: A current policy clause is a provision in a contract that requires the parties to comply with the most up-to-date policies and regulations related to the subject matter of the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTy.label: Akkadian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTy.definition: Akkadian is an ancient language used in Mesopotamia, characterized by its cuneiform script and grammar, and is considered a predecessor to modern-day Semitic languages.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTy.label: Consideration - Real Estate Assets
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTy.definition: Consideration of real estate assets refer to the land, buildings, and other property-related resources that are transferred from the one party to another as part of the deal.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTz.label: Fetal Alcohol Syndrome
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCTz.definition: Fetal Alcohol Syndrome (FAS) is a severe form of Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorders (FASD) resulting from prenatal alcohol exposure. It is characterized by growth deficiencies, distinctive facial anomalies, and central nervous system dysfunction, leading to intellectual disabilities, behavioral problems, and learning difficulties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCU0.label: Perpetual Asset
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCU0.definition: A Perpetual Asset is a financial instrument that does not have a fixed maturity date, allowing it to exist indefinitely without a predetermined end. This attribute is common in certain types of equity and debt instruments, providing ongoing returns or obligations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCU0.label: Smart Contracts Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCU0.definition: Smart Contracts Management refers to the process of overseeing and administering the creation, execution, and enforcement of digital contracts that are self-executing and self-enforcing, utilizing blockchain technology and computer code to automate the performance of contractual obligations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCU0.label: Data Leakage
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCU0.definition: In the context of AI, data leakage refers to the introduction of information into the training data that the system is expected to infer but should not legitimately have access to during model training. This results in a model that appears to perform well during evaluation on the test set but demonstrates poor performance during deployment when evaluated on new data sets.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCU1.label: Gbaya
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCU1.definition: Gbaya is a structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary, and is a specific language within the context of legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCU2.label: Motion to Allow Payment Arrearages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCU2.definition: A Motion to Allow Payment Arrearages is a request made in a bankruptcy case to permit the debtor to pay off missed payments over time, rather than in a lump sum.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCU6.label: Overtime Pay
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCU6.definition: Overtime pay refers to the additional compensation provided to employees who work hours in excess of what is considered standard or regular for a given period, typically a workweek. The rate for overtime pay is often higher than the employee's regular hourly wage, commonly set at one and a half times the standard rate or more, depending on labor laws and employment contracts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCU6.label: Preparer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCU6.definition: A Preparer is an individual or entity responsible for completing and submitting documentation on behalf of someone else, typically for a specific legal or financial process. Examples include immigration preparers, who assist with immigration paperwork, and bankruptcy preparers, who help file bankruptcy documents, although their roles may be limited by law in providing legal advice.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCU7.label: Insurance Broker Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCU7.definition: Insurance Broker Malpractice refers to a type of malpractice claim that arises from the actions or omissions of an insurance broker in the course of providing insurance services to a client.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUA.label: Engagement Service Status
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUA.definition: The Service Status concept refers to the current state or condition of a particular legal service, such as whether it is open, closed/ended, or canceled.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUE.label: Necessary and Proper Clause Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUE.definition: A Necessary & Proper Clause claim is a legal argument asserting that a particular law or action exceeds the authority granted to Congress by the Necessary and Proper Clause of the United States Constitution. This claim is based on the interpretation that the Necessary and Proper Clause empowers Congress to pass laws that are necessary and proper for carrying out its enumerated powers, and that any law or action must be directly linked to an enumerated power in order to be constitutionally valid.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUI.label: Georgia Superior Court - Turner County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUI.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Turner County refers to a specific court within the Georgia Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Turner County, Georgia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUI.label: Local Ruleset
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUI.definition: A Local Ruleset is a specific set of rules that govern a particular jurisdiction or court, typically created by the court itself or a local governing body.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUK.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Philadelphia County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUK.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Philadelphia County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within Philadelphia County.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Philadelphia County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUP.label: Input VAT Payment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUP.definition: Input VAT Payment refers to the Value Added Tax paid on purchases of goods and services that a business can reclaim or offset against the VAT collected on sales. This mechanism ensures that VAT is ultimately paid only on the value added at each stage of production.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUP.label: Convertible Note
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUP.definition: A Convertible Note is a form of short-term debt that converts into equity, usually in conjunction with a future financing round. The investor lends money to a startup and instead of getting the money back with interest, the investor receives equity in the company. Each convertible note is usually an unsecured, short-term debt instrument that converts into equity — typically preferred shares — under specified conditions, such as a future funding round. The conversion to equity can be mandatory in some conditions or elective in others.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUS.label: Cash Public Benefit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUS.definition: Cash public benefit refers to government programs that provide direct financial assistance to individuals or families who meet certain eligibility criteria, such as income level or employment status. These cash benefits, which can include unemployment compensation, welfare payments, or emergency relief funds, are intended to help recipients meet basic living expenses like housing, utilities, and food.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUX.label: Dispute Resolution Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUX.definition: A Dispute Resolution Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the process for resolving any disagreements or conflicts that may arise between the parties involved, typically through negotiation, mediation, or arbitration.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUX.label: Family Law and Matrimonial Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUX.definition: Family Law and Matrimonial Claims refer to legal disputes and proceedings related to issues such as divorce, custody, adoption, and guardianship, among others, that arise within the context of family relationships.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUa.label: Title to Assets Representation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUa.definition: Title to Assets Representation is a clause in merger and acquisition agreements where the selling party certifies that the target company holds clear and unencumbered title to its assets. This representation assures the buyer that the assets being acquired are free from liens, claims, encumbrances, or disputes, and that the target company has the full right to transfer them as part of the transaction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUd.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Pike County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUd.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Pike County refers to a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Pike County, Missouri.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUj.label: Closing Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUj.definition: Closing Management refers to the process of managing the legal aspects of a transaction, specifically the final stages of completing the deal.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUj.label: Accord and Satisfaction
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUj.definition: An accord and satisfaction is a legal defense that arises when a debtor offers to pay a creditor a sum of money in exchange for the creditor releasing the debtor from further liability.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUm.label: Arkansas Circuit Court - Polk Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUm.definition: A court located in Polk County, Arkansas that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its designated geographic area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUp.label: Right to Exclusive Use
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUp.definition: The Right to Exclusive Use refers to the legal authority granted to an individual or entity to have sole access to a particular property, asset, or area for a specific purpose. This right may be conferred through a lease, contract, or other legal arrangement and usually means that no one else can use the asset or space for the duration of the agreement, subject to any conditions or limitations outlined therein.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUq.label: Interim Operations Provisions
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUq.definition: Interim Operations Provisions are legal clauses that are included in a contract to regulate the actions of parties during the period between the signing of the contract and its completion, often to protect the interests of one or more parties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUq.label: Notice of Disposition Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUq.definition: A Notice of Disposition Clause is a provision in a legal document that specifies how property or assets will be distributed or disposed of upon a certain event, such as death or termination of a contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUq.label: Clean Water Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUq.definition: A Clean Water Claim is a legal action brought under environmental law seeking to enforce or protect the right to clean water.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUs.label: oasis:Obligation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUs.definition: An "Obligation" is a type of deontic specification in the OASIS ontology, indicating a requirement or duty that must be fulfilled.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUs.label: Craniofacial Bone Cancer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUs.definition: Maxilla, orbit, or temporal fossa cancer refers to malignant tumors originating in the bones and surrounding structures of the upper jaw (maxilla), eye socket (orbit), and the temporal fossa, which is located at the side of the skull. These cancers can significantly impact functions such as vision, chewing, and facial symmetry and often require complex, multidisciplinary treatment approaches.
english_labels: Maxilla, Orbit, or Temporal Fossa Cancer

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUt.label: Fixed Maturity Asset
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUt.definition: A Fixed Maturity Asset is a financial instrument where the principal amount is repaid in full at a specified maturity date. This type of asset provides a predictable repayment schedule, offering investors assurance of receiving their principal investment at the end of the term.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUu.label: Integration Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCUu.definition: An integration clause is a contractual provision that declares that the written agreement is the final and complete expression of the parties' intentions, and that any prior or contemporaneous agreements or understandings are merged into the written agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCV4.label: Classifications of Representations and Warranties
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCV4.definition: "Classifications of Representations and Warranties" refer to the categorization of assertions made by one party to another in a contractual agreement regarding the state of affairs, facts, or promises.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCV6.label: First Right of Refusal Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCV6.definition: A First Right of Refusal Clause is a provision in a contract that grants a party the opportunity to purchase or lease property before it is offered to others.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCV8.label: Minnesota District Court - Ramsey County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCV8.definition: Minnesota District Court - Ramsey County: A specific court within the Minnesota District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Ramsey County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVF.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Atchison County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVF.definition: A Missouri Circuit Court located in Atchison County is a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system, responsible for administering legal proceedings within its jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVJ.label: Failure to Meet Projections Language
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVJ.definition: The Failure to Meet Projections Language refers to a clause in a contract that outlines the consequences if a party fails to meet the projected goals or expectations outlined in the agreement, specifically in relation to Material Adverse Effect (MAE) Definition - Carveouts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVK.label: Arbitrators/Mediators Expense
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVK.definition: The Arbitrators/Mediators Expense concept refers to the costs incurred by parties in a legal matter for the services of an impartial third party who facilitates negotiations and resolution of disputes outside of court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVL.label: Assonet Band of the Wampanoag Nation
english_labels: Assonet Band of the Wampanoag Nation

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVM.label: Absolute Privilege
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVM.definition: Absolute Privilege: A legal immunity that protects government officials from being held liable for statements made during official proceedings, even if those statements are defamatory or otherwise harmful.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVP.label: Asbestos Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVP.definition: Asbestos Claims refer to legal claims made by individuals who have suffered harm due to exposure to asbestos, seeking compensation for damages such as medical expenses, lost wages, and pain and suffering.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVP.label: Notice and Right to Cure Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVP.definition: A Notice and Right to Cure Clause is a provision in a legal agreement that requires a party to provide notice of a breach and an opportunity to cure the breach before taking legal action.
english_labels: Notice and Right to Cure Clause

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVP.label: Business Process Outsourcing Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVP.definition: A Business Process Outsourcing Agreement is a legal contract between a company and an external service provider, where the provider undertakes specific business tasks or processes on behalf of the company.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVS.label: Forensic Expert
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVS.definition: A forensic expert is a professional who specializes in the application of scientific methods and techniques to investigate and analyze evidence in legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVT.label: Pharmaceutical and Medicine Manufacturing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVT.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in one or more of the following: (1) manufacturing biological and medicinal products; (2) processing (i.e., grading, grinding, and milling) botanical drugs and herbs; (3) isolating active medicinal principals from botanical drugs and herbs; and (4) manufacturing pharmaceutical products intended for internal and external consumption in such forms as ampoules, tablets, capsules, vials, ointments, powders, solutions, and suspensions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVW.label: Pee Dee Indian Nation of Upper South Carolina
english_labels: Pee Dee Indian Nation of Upper South Carolina

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVY.label: Prime Minister
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVY.definition: A prime minister is the head of government in many parliamentary systems, responsible for running the country's day-to-day operations and leading the executive branch. Typically appointed from the majority party or coalition in the legislature, the prime minister sets government policy, oversees the cabinet, and represents the country domestically and internationally.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVc.label: Utility Patent Registration Document
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVc.definition: A utility patent registration document is a legal certificate issued by a patent office that grants the holder exclusive rights to a new and useful invention, such as a process, machine, manufacture, or composition of matter, for a certain period. It includes detailed information about the invention, its utility, and the scope of protection granted.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVd.label: Complaint
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVd.definition: A Complaint is a formal legal document filed by a plaintiff that sets forth the allegations and claims against a defendant in a civil lawsuit.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVd.label: Borderline Intellectual Functioning
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVd.definition: Borderline Intellectual Functioning is characterized by an IQ score that is above the range for intellectual disability but significantly below average. Individuals with this condition may experience difficulties with cognitive tasks and adaptive functioning, but their challenges are not severe enough to qualify as an intellectual disability.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVd.label: Motion to Amend
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVd.definition: A Motion to Amend is a formal request made to a court or tribunal to modify or change a previously filed document or pleading, such as a complaint, petition, or judgment, in order to correct errors or provide additional information.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVg.label: Ownership of Information Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVg.definition: A clause in a legal document that specifies who has the right to possess and control certain information.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVh.label: Utu Utu Gwaitu Paiute Tribe of the Benton Paiute Reservation, California
english_labels: Utu Utu Gwaitu Paiute Tribe of the Benton Paiute Reservation, California

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVm.label: Business Disparagement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVm.definition: The act of making false or misleading statements about a business or its products or services, with the intention of causing harm to its reputation or financial standing.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVn.label: Guardianship
