https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVn.definition: The legal concept of Guardianship refers to the legal authority granted to a person to make decisions on behalf of another individual who is unable to make decisions for themselves due to mental or physical incapacity, with specific application to family law and matrimonial claims.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVp.label: Public Record Document
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVp.definition: A public record document is an official record created, maintained, and accessible by a government agency or public body, which can be used as evidence in legal proceedings. These documents include a wide range of materials, such as birth certificates, property deeds, and court records, and are generally considered reliable and admissible under the public records exception to the hearsay rule.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVq.label: Motion to Incur Debt
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCVq.definition: A Motion to Incur Debt is a request made in a bankruptcy case seeking court approval to obtain new debt or credit.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCW4.label: Retaliatory Discrimination
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCW4.definition: Retaliatory Discrimination refers to the act of an employer taking adverse action against an employee in response to the employee's complaint or opposition to discriminatory practices in the workplace.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCW9.label: matter_final_bill
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCW9.definition: Field used to specify whether this is the final bill for the matter_id.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWB.label: Birth Details
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWB.definition: Birth Details refer to specific information about an individual's birth, commonly including Date of Birth, Country of Birth, and City of Birth. These details are often required in legal, medical, and governmental contexts for identification, verification of nationality, and eligibility for certain rights or benefits.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWB.label: Private Equity Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWB.definition: Private Equity refers to investments made in private companies that are not publicly traded, typically by institutional investors or high net worth individuals, with the goal of generating high returns through various strategies such as leveraged buyouts, growth capital, and venture capital.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWI.label: Texas Court of Appeals - 10th
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWI.definition: The Texas Court of Appeals - 10th is a specific intermediate appellate court in Texas that hears appeals from lower courts within its jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWP.label: Florida Circuit Court - Sarasota County - 12th Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWP.definition: The Florida Circuit Court - Sarasota County (12th Circuit Court) is a specific court within the Florida Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Sarasota County.
english_labels: Florida Circuit Court - Sarasota County - 12th Circuit Court

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWP.label: Contributory Patent Infringement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWP.definition: Contributory Patent Infringement refers to the act of knowingly aiding, abetting, inducing, or encouraging another party to infringe on a patent, with the knowledge that the actions being encouraged constitute patent infringement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWR.label: Lease Related Guaranty
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWR.definition: A Lease Related Guaranty is a promise by a third party (the guarantor) to fulfill the tenant's obligations under a lease if the tenant fails to do so.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWY.label: Texas District Court - El Paso County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWY.definition: A Texas District Court located in El Paso County, which has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical boundaries.
english_labels: Texas District Court - El Paso County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWc.label: Benchmarking Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWc.definition: A benchmarking clause is a provision in a contract that allows for the comparison of a company's performance or costs against those of other similar companies in the industry.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWi.label: Human Resources Document
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWi.definition: A Human Resources Document is any formal record, form, or piece of information related to the management of personnel within an organization. These documents can include employment contracts, performance evaluations, and company policies related to human resources.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWj.label: Brain Cancer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWj.definition: Brain cancer is a type of cancer that arises from the brain cells, tissues, or the meninges (the protective membranes surrounding the brain and spinal cord). It can be primary, originating in the brain, or secondary, resulting from the spread of cancer from other body parts, and requires treatments such as surgery, radiation therapy, and chemotherapy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWp.label: Burns
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWp.definition: Burns are injuries to the skin or other tissues caused by exposure to heat, chemicals, electricity, or radiation. They are categorized by severity into first, second, third, and fourth degrees based on the depth and extent of tissue damage.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWq.label: Georgia Superior Court - Wilkes County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWq.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Wilkes County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWv.label: Florida County Court - Gilchrist County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWv.definition: A court located in Gilchrist County, Florida that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWx.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Columbia County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWx.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Columbia County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering civil and criminal proceedings at the county level in Pennsylvania.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Columbia County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWz.label: Insuring Agreement Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCWz.definition: An Insuring Agreement Clause is a specific provision within a contract that outlines the terms and conditions of an insurance policy, including the scope of coverage and the obligations of the insurer.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCX3.label: Off-the-Clock Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCX3.definition: An off-the-clock claim is a legal action initiated by an employee who alleges that their employer required them to perform work-related tasks outside of their normal working hours without providing appropriate compensation, such as overtime pay. These tasks can include checking work emails or taking work-related phone calls outside of work hours, or completing work assignments after clocking out for the day. The claim typically arises when an employer does not comply with applicable wage and hour laws, which require employers to compensate employees for all hours worked, including overtime.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCX4.label: Appellee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCX4.definition: A party against whom an appeal is taken.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCX6.label: Georgia District Court - Pierce County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCX6.definition: Georgia District Court - Pierce County: A court of law in the state of Georgia that has jurisdiction over legal disputes and criminal cases within Pierce County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXB.label: Indiana Superior Court - Howard County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXB.definition: Indiana Superior Court - Howard County: A court of general jurisdiction in Indiana that has the authority to hear and decide a wide range of legal cases within Howard County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXB.label: tax_invoice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXB.definition: "In the European Union (and possibly in other areas of the world) it is required that an invoice contain the words, ""This is a Tax Invoice"" or ""This is not a Tax Invoice"". It would be possible for the law firm to submit an invoice containing all line items details and designated ""This is a Tax Invoice"" in this field, and for the receiving system to display a view of the invoice to the Client and Law Firm that satisfies the requirements for the Tax Invoice required by law in many countries. In this situation, the law firm may not need to send a separate tax invoice to the Client. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXE.label: Indiana Superior Court - Jasper County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXE.definition: Indiana Superior Court - Jasper County refers to a specific court within the Indiana Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Jasper County, Indiana.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXG.label: New York Supreme Court - Orange County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXG.definition: A court located in Orange County, New York that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical area.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - Orange County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXK.label: Foreign Agents Registration Act Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXK.definition: A Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA) claim involves legal action taken against individuals or entities for failing to comply with the disclosure and registration requirements mandated by FARA. Such claims seek to enforce transparency and accountability regarding foreign influence on U.S. political and public processes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXZ.label: Trisomy X Syndrome
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXZ.definition: Trisomy X Syndrome, also known as XXX Syndrome, is a genetic condition where a female has three X chromosomes instead of the usual two. This extra chromosome affects development and can lead to a range of physical, cognitive, and behavioral symptoms.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXe.label: Application for Renewal of Judgment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXe.definition: An Application for Renewal of Judgment is a legal document filed in bankruptcy proceedings seeking to extend the time period for collecting a debt that has already been reduced to a judgment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXh.label: Facsimile Signature Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXh.definition: A facsimile signature clause is a provision in a contract that allows for the use of a reproduced signature, typically in the form of a fax or scanned image, as a valid and binding signature.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXi.label: Admiralty and Maritime Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXi.definition: Law that governs nautical issues and private maritime disputes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXm.label: Interference with Prospective Relations
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXm.definition: The concept of Interference with Prospective Relations refers to the intentional and unjustified interference with a party's potential or anticipated business relationships or economic advantages, causing harm or loss to that party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXo.label: Environmental Risk
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXo.definition: Risk of financial loss due to environmental disasters or changes in environmental regulation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXo.label: Educational Quality Objective
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXo.definition: The Educational Quality Objective refers to the goal of ensuring a high standard of education for all students, irrespective of their socio-economic or cultural backgrounds. This objective emphasizes the delivery of comprehensive, well-rounded, and effective educational experiences, utilizing optimal resources, curriculum standards, teaching methodologies, and continuous assessment to promote student success and lifelong learning.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXo.label: Partnership Liability for Debts
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXo.definition: The concept of Partnership Liability for Debts refers to the legal responsibility of partners in a partnership to pay off any debts incurred by the partnership, even if it means using their personal assets to do so.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXr.label: Payment for Services Rendered Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXr.definition: A Payment for Services Rendered Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the terms and conditions for compensating a party for services provided.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXw.label: Transportation Accessibility Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCXw.definition: A claim of this type arises when transportation services, whether public or private, are not accessible to individuals with disabilities. This can range from buses not having accessible ramps to airports not providing appropriate assistance for passengers with mobility challenges.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCY2.label: Equipment Purchase Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCY2.definition: An Equipment Purchase Agreement is a legally binding contract between a buyer and a seller outlining the terms and conditions of the sale of specific equipment or machinery. It typically includes details such as the purchase price, payment terms, warranties, delivery arrangements, and any conditions or representations related to the equipment being sold.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCY7.label: Retainer Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCY7.definition: A retainer clause is a provision in a contract that requires a party to pay a fee in advance to secure the services of another party for a specified period of time.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCY7.label: Zuni
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCY7.definition: Zuni (Language) is a specific written or spoken structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary, and is a member of the Language top-level class.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCY8.label: Vehicular Manslaughter
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCY8.definition: The unlawful killing of a human being caused by the operation of a motor vehicle by a person who acted with gross negligence or recklessness.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCYA.label: No Prepayment Penalty Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCYA.definition: A "No Prepayment Penalty Clause" is a provision in a contract that prohibits the imposition of a fee or penalty for paying off a debt or obligation before its due date.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCYD.label: Oregon Attorney General Opinions
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCYD.definition: Oregon Attorney General Opinions are legal interpretations and advice provided by the Attorney General of Oregon, which are binding on state agencies and officials.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCYR.label: 510 Motions to Vacate Sentence (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCYR.definition: Action by a prisoner to vacate or modify a sentence imposed in federal court, other than a death sentence, under 28 U.S.C. § 2255.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCYW.label: Indemnification and Hold Harmless Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCYW.definition: An indemnification and hold harmless clause is a contractual provision in which one party agrees to protect and defend another party against any claims or losses arising from a particular transaction or relationship, and to assume all liability for any damages or costs incurred as a result.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCYf.label: New York Supreme Court - Jefferson County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCYf.definition: The New York Supreme Court - Jefferson County is a court of general jurisdiction located in Jefferson County, New York, with authority to hear and decide a wide range of legal disputes within its geographical jurisdiction.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - Jefferson County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCYh.label: Georgia District Court - Houston County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCYh.definition: Georgia District Court - Houston County: A specific court within the Georgia District Court system located in Houston County, responsible for hearing and deciding legal cases within its jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCYi.label: Pretrial Motion Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCYi.definition: The practice of filing and arguing motions before a trial, typically seeking to resolve issues or disputes before the trial begins.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCYk.label: Arizona Superior Court - Coconino Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCYk.definition: Arizona Superior Court - Coconino Cty. is a specific court within the Arizona Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Coconino County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCYl.label: Intangible Assets
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCYl.definition: Intangible assets are non-physical assets that an entity owns, which have value due to the rights or privileges they provide to the entity. Examples include patents, copyrights, trademarks, brand recognition, and goodwill, which can contribute to a company's long-term revenue but cannot be physically touched or seen.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCYo.label: Internet Broadcast
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCYo.definition: An Internet Broadcast is the transmission of audio, video, or multimedia content over the internet to reach a dispersed online audience. This form of broadcasting includes live streaming, on-demand videos, and internet radio, allowing users to access content via computers, smartphones, and other internet-enabled devices.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCYo.label: Lamba
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCYo.definition: A language spoken by the Lamba people, primarily in Zambia and Congo.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCYr.label: Legal Services Buyer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCYr.definition: A person or entity that is obtaining legal services from a legal service provider

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCYs.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Warren County (9th Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Warren County (9th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCYv.label: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCYv.definition: U.S. federal courts' body of procedural rules governing civil actions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCYw.label: San Juan Southern Paiute Tribe of Arizona
english_labels: San Juan Southern Paiute Tribe of Arizona

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZ0.label: Crop Production Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZ0.definition: Industries in this group grow crops mainly for food and fiber. The subsector comprises establishments, such as farms, orchards, groves, greenhouses, and nurseries, primarily engaged in growing crops, plants, vines, or trees and their seeds.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZ6.label: Direct Deposit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZ6.definition: Direct Deposit is an electronic method of transferring funds directly from one bank account to another, commonly used for payroll or benefit disbursements. It's a form of ACH transfer that allows money to be moved without the need for physical checks.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZ9.label: Swedish
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZ9.definition: Swedish (Language) refers to the written or spoken structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary specific to the Swedish language, which is a subset of the broader category of Language.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZ9.label: Taxes Motion
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZ9.definition: A Taxes Motion (Bankruptcy) is a request made by a debtor in bankruptcy court seeking permission to pay taxes owed by the debtor or the bankruptcy estate.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZC.label: Florida Circuit Court - Desoto County - 12th Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZC.definition: A court located in Desoto County, Florida that is part of the larger Florida Circuit Court system.
english_labels: Florida Circuit Court - Desoto County - 12th Circuit Court

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZC.label: Texas District Court - Henderson County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZC.definition: A Texas District Court located in Henderson County, which has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZC.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Kankakee County (21st Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Kankakee County (21st Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZK.label: Criminal Stalking
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZK.definition: Criminal Stalking is a criminal offense that involves a pattern of behavior that causes fear or distress to another person, including following, harassing, or threatening them.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZK.label: Acknowledgement and Acceptance Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZK.definition: An Acknowledgement and Acceptance Clause is a provision in a legal document where a party acknowledges and accepts the terms and conditions of the agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZM.label: Lower Sorbian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZM.definition: Lower Sorbian is a Slavic language spoken in eastern Germany, primarily in the state of Brandenburg.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZN.label: Tabletop Exercise Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZN.definition: A tabletop exercise practice involves legal work related to conducting simulated scenarios to test and evaluate the effectiveness of an organization’s plans and procedures for handling emergencies or specific situations, such as cybersecurity incidents or disaster recovery. Legal work related to these exercises typically involve discussion-based sessions where participants analyze hypothetical events and collaboratively develop response strategies, as well as the resultant legal implications.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZP.label: California Superior Court - Butte Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZP.definition: A California Superior Court in Butte County is a specific court within the California Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within Butte County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZQ.label: Massachusetts Trial Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZQ.definition: The Massachusetts Trial Court is a court system within the Massachusetts State Courts that handles cases related to housing, district, probate and family, juvenile, and land court matters, as well as the Boston Municipal Court and the Massachusetts Superior Court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZS.label: File Item Number
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZS.definition: File Item Number refers to a unique identifier assigned to a specific item or task within an invoice for legal services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZW.label: Density Credit Transactions
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZW.definition: Density Credit Transactions refer to the buying, selling, or transferring of development rights, allowing property owners to adjust the allowable density of development on their land. These transactions are typically facilitated through legal agreements and are overseen by regulatory agencies to ensure compliance with land use and zoning laws.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZc.label: Cash Payment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZc.definition: Cash Payment involves the physical transfer of paper money or coins between parties to settle a financial obligation. It is one of the oldest and simplest forms of payment, often used for in-person transactions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZd.label: Opacity
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZd.definition: Opacity in an AI system refers to the condition where one or more features, such as processes, the provenance of datasets, functions, output, or behavior, are unavailable or incomprehensible to all stakeholders. Opacity is usually considered an antonym for transparency and can hinder understanding, trust, and accountability in AI systems.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZe.label: Land Use and Zoning Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZe.definition: Law regulating the subdivision, use, and restriction of land.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZg.label: Florida Circuit Court - Monroe County - 16th Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZg.definition: The Florida Circuit Court - Monroe County (16th Circuit Court) is a specific court within the Florida Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Monroe County.
english_labels: Florida Circuit Court - Monroe County - 16th Circuit Court

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZh.label: Criminal Record
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZh.definition: A criminal record is an official compilation of an individual's past arrests, charges, convictions, and other interactions with the criminal justice system. This record can have implications for employment, housing, and other opportunities, as many entities conduct background checks. In some jurisdictions, certain convictions can be expunged or sealed, removing them from public view.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZh.label: Maximum Recoverable Amount
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZh.definition: The Maximum Recoverable Amount is the highest sum of money that can be awarded to a party in a legal dispute, based on the amount in controversy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZk.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Christian County (4th Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Christian County (4th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZm.label: Change of Recommendation Trigger
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZm.definition: Change of Recommendation Trigger refers to a provision in a fiduciary exemption to a change of recommendation covenant or a breakup fee trigger that allows for a change in the recommendation of a merger or acquisition based on certain events or circumstances.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZn.label: Creditor Matrix Motion
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZn.definition: A Creditor Matrix Motion (Bankruptcy) is a legal request made in a bankruptcy case to obtain approval for the debtor's list of creditors, which is used to determine the distribution of assets.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZq.label: Probate Filing Reason
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZq.definition: Probate Filing Reason refers to the specific cause or circumstance that led to the initiation of a probate filing, such as substance abuse, medical condition, disability, death/testamentary, abuse, neglect/abandonment, or financial exploitation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZs.label: Motion to Continue Trial
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZs.definition: A Motion to Continue Trial is a formal request made by one party in a legal case to postpone the scheduled trial date to a later time.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZv.label: M&A F3 Employment, Labor and Employee Benefits Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZv.definition: A legal practice area that focuses on employment, labor, and employee benefits issues related to mergers and acquisitions, including executive compensation matters.
english_labels: M&A F3 Employment, Labor and Employee Benefits Practice

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZw.label: Compliance
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZw.definition: Deontic compliance refers to the conformity in action, behavior, or attitude to a set of rules or standards, as prescribed by laws, regulations, or ethical principles.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZy.label: Policy Document
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZy.definition: A Policy Document is a written or presented representation of a set of principles or guidelines that provide direction for decision-making and action in a particular area, created with the intention of guiding behavior and achieving specific goals.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZz.label: California Superior Court - Kings Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCZz.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Kings County, California, with the power to hear and decide a wide range of legal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RC_n.label: X137 Experts, Consultants, Other Vendors and Professionals
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RC_n.definition: This code is a catch-all for any experts, consultants or other vendors used in a matter where the types of services provided by the vendor do not apply to any other code specified in this list
english_labels: X137 Experts, Consultants, Other Vendors and Professionals

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCa0.label: DUPLICATE Motion for Change of Venue
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCa0.definition: A "Duplicate Motion for Change of Venue" is a deprecated concept in legal knowledge management that refers to a motion requesting a change of location for a trial that has already been filed previously.
english_labels: DUPLICATE Motion for Change of Venue

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCa0.label: Asset Negotiability and Transmission
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCa0.definition: Asset Negotiability and Transmission refer to the characteristics and methods by which ownership of an asset can be transferred. This includes assets with registered ownership, where the owner's identity is recorded, and bearer assets, where ownership is transferred by possession without registration.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCa5.label: eBilling Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCa5.definition: eBilling Management refers to the process of managing electronic billing for legal services, including the creation, submission, and tracking of invoices and payments.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCaB.label: Gastroenterology Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCaB.definition: Negligent or wrongful conduct by a medical professional in the field of gastroenterology, resulting in harm or injury to a patient.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCaD.label: New York District Court - Suffolk County - 6th District
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCaD.definition: A court located in Suffolk County, New York that operates as a part of the larger New York District Court system.
english_labels: New York District Court - Suffolk County - 6th District

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCaJ.label: Contribution Disclosure
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCaJ.definition: Contribution Disclosure is a report detailing the contributions, often financial, made by a corporation to political campaigns, charitable organizations, or other external entities. It's usually filed with regulators or voluntarily disclosed.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCaL.label: Third-Party Employment Placement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCaL.definition: Third-Party Employment Placement refers to a work arrangement where an employee is hired through an external agency or organization but performs work for a different, client company. In this setup, the agency typically handles administrative tasks like payroll and benefits, while the employee works under the direction of the client company.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCaM.label: Financial Sponsor
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCaM.definition: <skos:definition>An M&A financially driven buyer is an individual or entity, such as a private equity firm or an investment fund, that pursues mergers and acquisitions with the primary goal of generating financial returns on their investment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCaU.label: Trespass to Personal Property or Chattel
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCaU.definition: The concept of Trespass to Personal Property or Chattel refers to the intentional interference with another person's lawful possession of their personal property or chattel, without their consent.
english_labels: Trespass to Personal Property or Chattel

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCaZ.label: Jury Instructions
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCaZ.definition: Jury Instructions are written directions given by a judge to a jury during a trial, explaining the law that applies to the case and how the jury should evaluate the evidence presented.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCae.label: Food Manufacturing Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCae.definition: Industries in the Food Manufacturing subsector transform livestock and agricultural products into products for intermediate or final consumption. The industry groups are distinguished by the raw materials (generally of animal or vegetable origin) processed into food products. The food products manufactured in these establishments are typically sold to wholesalers or retailers for distribution to consumers, but establishments primarily engaged in retailing bakery and candy products made on the premises not for immediate consumption are included. Establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing beverages are classified in Subsector 312, Beverage and Tobacco Product Manufacturing.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCaf.label: AI Trustworthiness
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCaf.definition: AI Trustworthiness refers to the degree of confidence that users and stakeholders can have in an AI system's ability to perform its intended functions reliably, safely, and ethically. It encompasses various attributes such as fairness, transparency, accountability, and robustness, ensuring that AI systems operate in a manner aligned with societal values and ethical standards.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCag.label: Scots
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCag.definition: Scots (Language) is a variety of Germanic language spoken in Scotland, characterized by its distinct grammar, vocabulary, and pronunciation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCaq.label: TIFF
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCaq.definition: A Tag Image File Format (TIFF) file.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCar.label: Legal Aid Attorney
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCar.definition: A legal aid attorney is a lawyer who provides free or low-cost legal assistance to individuals who cannot afford traditional legal services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCas.label: Inventive Step
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCas.definition: Inventive Step is a patentability requirement that an invention must not be obvious to a person skilled in the relevant field, based on the prior art. It is used to determine whether an invention has sufficient ingenuity to warrant a patent.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCat.label: Kosraean
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCat.definition: Kosraean is a language that belongs to the Austronesian language family and is spoken primarily in the Federated States of Micronesia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCat.label: Chemical Safety Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCat.definition: Law governing the use of chemicals in human activities, particularly man-made chemicals in modern industrial applications.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCau.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Fulton County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCau.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court in Fulton County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court system that has jurisdiction over minor criminal offenses and civil cases.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Fulton County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCax.label: Oregon Employee Relations Board
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCax.definition: The Oregon Employee Relations Board is a state agency responsible for administering and enforcing laws related to labor relations and collective bargaining in Oregon.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCb8.label: Breach of Implied Warranty of Good & Workmanlike Services - Home Construction
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCb8.definition: The Breach of Implied Warranty of Good & Workmanlike Services in Home Construction refers to a violation of the implied promise that a contractor will provide services that meet industry standards and are of a quality that a reasonable person would expect in the construction of a home.
english_labels: Breach of Implied Warranty of Good & Workmanlike Services - Home Construction

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbH.label: Unauthorized Practice Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbH.definition: Unauthorized Practice Claims refer to legal allegations or complaints asserting that an individual or entity has engaged in professional activities without the required licensure or authorization in a specific field. These claims are commonly associated with regulated professions such as law and medicine, where practicing without proper credentials can pose significant risks to the public.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbI.label: Coma
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbI.definition: A coma is a deep state of unconsciousness in which an individual cannot be awakened and fails to respond to external stimuli or internal needs. It is a medical condition that can result from various causes, including brain injury, stroke, or illness, and has significant legal implications for decision-making and guardianship.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbL.label: Substantial Performance of Contract Allowing Recovery
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbL.definition: The concept of "Substantial Performance of Contract Allowing Recovery" refers to a legal claim that allows a party to recover damages even if they have not fully performed their contractual obligations, as long as their performance was substantial and in good faith.
english_labels: Substantial Performance of Contract Allowing Recovery

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbO.label: Phlebotomy Negligence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbO.definition: Phlebotomy Negligence refers to a type of medical negligence claim that arises when a healthcare professional fails to perform a blood draw procedure with the appropriate standard of care, resulting in harm to the patient.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbQ.label: Invoice Total Tax Other ISO
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbQ.definition: The concept of "Invoice Total Tax Other ISO" refers to the additional taxes and fees included in the total amount charged on a legal services invoice, beyond the basic fee and itemized details.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbT.label: Diversion Rights
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbT.definition: Also known as "appropriative rights," diversion rights allow entities to divert water from its natural source for use in a different location. These rights are typically granted based on a "first in time, first in right" principle, meaning the earliest users have senior rights to the water source. This system is common in parts of the western United States.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbU.label: Closely Held Company
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbU.definition: A closely held company is a business entity in which a small group of shareholders controls the majority of shares. Typically, these shareholders are family members or close associates, and the company's shares are not publicly traded.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbW.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Sullivan County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbW.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court in Sullivan County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court system that has jurisdiction over minor criminal offenses and civil cases within Sullivan County.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Sullivan County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbX.label: Citation to Litigation Procedural Rules
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbX.definition: A document's citations to a court's procedural rules (e.g., Federal Rule of Civil Procedure, Federal Rules of Evidence).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbZ.label: Sequestration
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbZ.definition: The concept of Sequestration refers to the legal process of taking possession of property or assets by a court-appointed trustee in order to enforce a judgment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCba.label: Motions to Reduce Award
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCba.definition: A motion made by a party after a trial requesting the court to reduce the amount of damages awarded by the jury.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbb.label: Cardiac Surgery Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbb.definition: Negligence or wrongdoing by a medical professional during cardiac surgery, resulting in harm or injury to the patient, which may lead to a legal claim for compensation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbe.label: Arizona Superior Court - Yuma Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbe.definition: The Arizona Superior Court - Yuma County is a specific court within the Arizona Superior Court system, which is responsible for administering legal proceedings within Yuma County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbe.label: Unpaid
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbe.definition: Unpaid refers to a financial obligation or transaction for which no payment has been made. This status indicates that the total amount due remains outstanding and has not been fulfilled.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbn.label: Nulhegan Band of the Coosuk Abenaki Nation
english_labels: Nulhegan Band of the Coosuk Abenaki Nation

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbn.label: Tax Tier Minimum
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbn.definition: Tax Tier Minimum refers to the minimum amount of taxable income required to be eligible for a particular tax tier within a tax bracket.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbp.label: Bankruptcy Exit Financing
english_labels: Bankruptcy Exit Financing refers to the financial arrangements made to provide a debtor with the necessary capital to successfully emerge from bankruptcy proceedings. This type of financing is crucial for restructuring the debtor’s operations, settling outstanding debts, and ensuring the company’s post-bankruptcy viability.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbr.label: Board Secretary
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCbr.definition: A Board Secretary, also known as Secretary of the Board, is an officer responsible for managing the administrative tasks of a board of directors, including preparing agendas, recording meeting minutes, and maintaining corporate governance documents. The Secretary ensures compliance with legal and regulatory requirements and facilitates communication between the board and executive management.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCby.label: Entity Formation Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCby.definition: Formation of a legal entity such as a company, joint venture, fund, security, etc.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCc2.label: Excise Tax Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCc2.definition: Excise Tax Practice refers to the application, administration, and enforcement of taxes imposed on specific goods, services, or activities, such as alcohol, tobacco, fuel, and gambling. These taxes are typically levied at the point of production or sale and are often used to generate revenue and regulate consumption of certain products.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCc5.label: Product Liability Defenses
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCc5.definition: Product Liability Defenses refer to the legal arguments and strategies used by defendants in a product liability case to defend against claims of liability for harm caused by their product, including arguments related to the inherent safety of the product, the scope of its intended use, the knowledge and experience of the user, and the balance of risks and benefits associated with the product.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCc5.label: Assuming Facts Not in Evidence Objection
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCc5.definition: Assuming Facts Not in Evidence is an objection raised when a party in a legal proceeding believes that a question or statement implies the existence of facts that have not been formally introduced or established as evidence in the case. This objection aims to prevent the influence of unfounded assumptions on the proceedings.
english_labels: Assuming Facts Not in Evidence Objection

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCc7.label: Freedom from Torture
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCc7.definition: Freedom from torture is a fundamental human right that prohibits the use of torture and other cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment or punishment against individuals. This right is enshrined in various international treaties, such as the United Nations Convention Against Torture, and is considered a non-derogable right, meaning it cannot be suspended under any circumstances.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCc9.label: Ganda
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCc9.definition: Ganda (Language) is a structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary used in Uganda and surrounding regions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCcN.label: Quality Guarantee Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCcN.definition: A Quality Guarantee Clause is a specific type of clause found in a contract that ensures the quality of goods or services provided under the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCcO.label: Employee Disciplinary Event
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCcO.definition: An Employment Disciplinary Event refers to actions taken by an employer to address an employee's misconduct, performance issues, or violations of company policies, short of termination. These actions can include warnings, suspensions, mandatory training, or demotion.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCcO.label: Judicial Branch Monitoring Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCcO.definition: Judicial Branch Monitoring Practice involves the continuous observation, analysis, and reporting of activities and decisions within the judiciary, including court rulings, legal precedents, and judicial appointments. This practice helps stakeholders stay informed about judicial developments and assess their implications for the legal and regulatory environment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCcO.label: Trademark Registration Document
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCcO.definition: A Trademark Registration Document is the official certificate issued by a governmental authority, such as the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO), confirming the registration of a specific trademark. The document delineates the scope of protection, including the classes of goods or services for which the trademark is registered, and serves as prima facie evidence of the owner's exclusive right to use the trademark in commerce

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCcQ.label: Tortious Interference Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCcQ.definition: Tortious Interference Claims refer to legal claims made by a party against another for intentionally interfering with their contractual or business relationships, resulting in economic harm or loss.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCcT.label: Case Management Order
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCcT.definition: A Case Management Order is a legal directive issued by a court that outlines the procedures and deadlines for managing a specific case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCcT.label: Internist Negligence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCcT.definition: Negligence committed by an internist, which is a type of medical malpractice claim.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCcU.label: Foreign Corrupt Practices Act Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCcU.definition: A Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA) Claim arises when an individual or entity is accused of violating the FCPA, which prohibits bribery of foreign officials to obtain or retain business. This claim involves allegations of unlawful payments, gifts, or offers made to foreign officials to influence their actions or decisions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCcW.label: Visitor
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCcW.definition: A visitor is an individual who temporarily enters a specific location, such as a country, city, or residence, for various purposes. Visitors can include tourists, who travel for leisure and exploration; business visitors, who come for work-related activities; or guests invited to a residence for social or personal reasons. The nature of the visit and applicable regulations, such as visa requirements or entry permissions, can differ based on the visitor's purpose and destination.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCcZ.label: Schizoaffective Disorder
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCcZ.definition: Schizoaffective Disorder is a mental health condition characterized by the presence of both schizophrenia symptoms and mood disorder symptoms (either depressive or manic episodes). Individuals with this disorder experience significant disruptions in their mood and cognitive functioning, leading to impairments in daily life.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCci.label: Termination Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCci.definition: Law encompassing rules by which an employer may terminate an employee.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCcw.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Fulton County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCcw.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Fulton County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering legal proceedings at the county level in Pennsylvania.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Fulton County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCcx.label: JI30 Costs Management Conference (UK J-CODE)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCcx.definition: Work in preparing for and attending any Costs Management Conference / Hearing including the hearing of any applications to vary a budget.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCd2.label: Agreement Not to Sue Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCd2.definition: An Agreement Not to Sue Clause is a provision in a contract that prohibits one or more parties from pursuing legal action against each other in relation to the subject matter of the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCd7.label: Intermediate Representations and Warranties
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCd7.definition: Intermediate Representations and Warranties refer to the statements and assurances made by parties involved in a contract or agreement that fall between standard and extensive warranties. These representations often cover specific aspects of the transaction or product, providing a moderate level of protection and assurance for both parties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCd7.label: Minnesota District Court - Cass County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCd7.definition: Minnesota District Court - Cass County refers to a specific court within the Minnesota District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Cass County, Minnesota.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCdB.label: Bankruptcy Schedule - Creditors Holding Claims Secured by Property
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCdB.definition: Bankruptcy Schedule - Creditors Holding Claims Secured by Property, also known as Schedule D, requires the debtor to list all creditors who have claims secured by the debtor's property. This schedule provides details about each secured claim, including the creditor's name, the amount owed, the collateral securing the debt, and the value of that collateral.
english_labels: Bankruptcy Schedule - Creditors Holding Claims Secured by Property

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCdC.label: Federal Preemption
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCdC.definition: The concept of Federal Preemption refers to the legal principle that federal law takes precedence over state law in cases where there is a conflict between the two.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCdG.label: Motion for Protective Order
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCdG.definition: A Motion for Protective Order is a legal request made by a party in a bankruptcy or discovery case to limit or prevent the disclosure of certain information or evidence.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCdJ.label: matter segment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCdJ.definition: A matter segment is a component of LEDES XML E-Billing Ver. 2.2 that includes various details related to a legal matter, such as matter ID, description, billing type, associated line items, and contact information.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCdJ.label: Exception
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCdJ.definition: In a legal context, an exception refers to a situation or circumstance that deviates from the general rule or norm. Exceptions are typically invoked to address specific conditions or cases that require special consideration or treatment within a legal framework.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCdJ.label: Demand Amount
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCdJ.definition: The demand amount refers to the specific sum of money or compensation requested in a demand letter.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCdS.label: Capias Ad Respondendum
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCdS.definition: A "Capias Ad Respondendum" is a legal concept within the categories of Judicial and Procedural Tort Claims, which refers to a writ or order issued by a court to arrest and bring a defendant before the court to answer to a civil action or lawsuit.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCdT.label: Right of Offset Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCdT.definition: A Right of Offset Clause is a provision in a contract that allows one party to offset or deduct any amount owed to them by the other party from any amount owed by them, in order to settle the debt.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCdd.label: Analysis of Vendor Contracts
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCdd.definition: The concept of "Analysis of Vendor Contracts" refers to the examination and evaluation of agreements between a company and its suppliers or service providers, with a focus on identifying potential risks and ensuring compliance with legal and business requirements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCdj.label: Negative Pledge Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCdj.definition: A Negative Pledge Clause is a provision in a contract that prohibits a party from creating any new liens or encumbrances on their assets, which could negatively affect the other party's security interest.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCdq.label: Motion to Exclude Witness
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCdq.definition: A Motion to Exclude Witness is a formal request made to the court to prevent a particular witness from testifying in a trial or hearing.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCdu.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Owen County Circuit 2
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCdu.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Indiana that has the authority to hear a wide range of civil and criminal cases within Owen County.
english_labels: Indiana Circuit Court - Owen County Circuit 2

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCdu.label: New Jersey Superior Court - Morris County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCdu.definition: The New Jersey Superior Court - Morris County is a court of general jurisdiction within the New Jersey state court system, located in Morris County and serving the surrounding area.
english_labels: New Jersey Superior Court - Morris County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCe2.label: Georgia District Court - Toombs County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCe2.definition: A court located in Toombs County, Georgia that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCe7.label: Direct Debt Offering
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCe7.definition: A Direct Debt Offering refers to the issuance of debt securities by a borrower directly to investors, without the involvement of underwriters or intermediaries. This approach allows the issuer to raise capital efficiently, often at a lower cost, by bypassing traditional financial institutions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCeB.label: Tsonga
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCeB.definition: Tsonga is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary, and is a specific language within the context of legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCeE.label: Allied Legal Professional
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCeE.definition: An allied legal professional supports the delivery of legal services through specialized skills and knowledge. These professionals work in various roles, such as paralegals, law librarians, and legal marketing personnel, all enabling legal service providers (e.g., law firms) to deliver legal services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCeG.label: Supplementary Papers
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCeG.definition: Supplementary Papers refer to additional documents submitted to a court after the initial filing of an appeal, specifically in relation to requests for rehearing or further supplements to the original filing.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCeK.label: Political Questions
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCeK.definition: Political questions refer to issues that courts deem inappropriate for judicial review because they involve decisions best made by the legislative or executive branches of government. In such cases, the judiciary typically refrains from ruling, citing a lack of judicially manageable standards and the need to respect the separation of powers.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCeM.label: Roadway Dedication
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCeM.definition: Roadway Dedication is the legal process by which a private entity or individual transfers land to a public entity for the specific purpose of constructing or expanding a public road. This act typically requires formal documentation, legal agreements, and may involve negotiations between private and public parties to meet local planning and zoning requirements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCeR.label: Dry Creek Rancheria Band of Pomo Indians, California
english_labels: Dry Creek Rancheria Band of Pomo Indians, California

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCeW.label: Cybercrime Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCeW.definition: Crimes committed using a computer or directed at computers, data, or other information technology - piracy, hacking, etc.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCeX.label: Cross-Designation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCeX.definition: Cross-Designation refers to the act of designating a party or a document in a legal case with a different name or title than originally given, and it falls under the category of Appellate Filings - Correspondence and Forms.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCeY.label: Somatic Symptom Disorder
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCeY.definition: Somatic Symptom Disorder is characterized by one or more physical symptoms that cause significant distress or impairment in daily functioning, with excessive thoughts, feelings, or behaviors related to the symptoms. The physical symptoms cannot be fully explained by a medical condition, substance use, or another mental disorder.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCeZ.label: Manchu
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCeZ.definition: Manchu is a written or spoken structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary, and is a member of the Language top-level class.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCeb.label: Moksha
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCeb.definition: A language spoken by the Moksha people, who reside primarily in the Mordovia region of Russia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCed.label: Arkansas Circuit Court - Union Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCed.definition: A court located in Union County, Arkansas that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its designated geographical area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCei.label: Tay-Sachs Disease
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCei.definition: Tay-Sachs disease is a rare, inherited neurodegenerative disorder caused by a deficiency of the enzyme hexosaminidase A. This deficiency leads to the accumulation of GM2 gangliosides, which are toxic to nerve cells.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCei.label: Indiana Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCei.definition: The Indiana Circuit Court is a court of general jurisdiction in the state of Indiana that hears civil and criminal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCeq.label: Class Action Waiver Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCeq.definition: A Class Action Waiver Clause is a provision in a contract that prohibits a group of individuals from collectively bringing a legal claim against the other party, requiring each individual to pursue their claim individually.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCes.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Union County (1st Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Union County (1st Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfE.label: Subpoena
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfE.definition: A subpoena is a legal document that requires a person to appear in court or produce evidence for a case, and is a type of discovery document used in bankruptcy and restructuring proceedings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfI.label: tax_item_fee segment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfI.definition: A tax_item_fee segment is a component of the LEDES XML E-Billing Ver. 2.2 standard that includes information about a specific tax or fee charged in a legal matter, identified by a unique transaction ID and file item number.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfK.label: Divehi; Dhivehi; Maldivian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfK.definition: A language spoken in the Maldives, also known as Divehi or Dhivehi, which belongs to the top-level class of Language.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfM.label: New York Traffic Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfM.definition: New York Traffic Court is a specialized court within the New York State Courts system that handles traffic violations and related matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfM.label: Filing Receipt Number
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfM.definition: A Filing Receipt Number, such as an immigration filing receipt number or other regulatory filing receipt number, is a unique identifier assigned to an application or filing submitted to a government agency, indicating that the submission has been received and officially acknowledged. This number is used to track the progress of the filing and corresponds to the specific case for reference during the processing period.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfO.label: Eating Disorders
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfO.definition: Eating Disorders are characterized by disturbances in eating behavior and preoccupation with, and excessive self-evaluation of, body weight and shape. Symptoms and signs may include, but are not limited to, restriction of energy consumption when compared with individual requirements; recurrent episodes of binge eating or behavior intended to prevent weight gain, such as self-induced vomiting, excessive exercise, or misuse of laxatives; mood disturbances, social withdrawal, or irritability; amenorrhea; dental problems; abnormal laboratory findings; and cardiac abnormalities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfQ.label: Money Order Payment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfQ.definition: Money Order Payment involves the use of a money order, a pre-funded paper document resembling a check, to transfer funds between parties. Money orders are typically issued by financial institutions, post offices, or retail stores and offer a secure method of payment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfQ.label: Disinhibited Social Engagement Disorder
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfQ.definition: Disinhibited Social Engagement Disorder (DSED) is a condition in children characterized by overly familiar behavior with strangers and a lack of appropriate reticence in new social situations. It often arises from severe neglect or inconsistent caregiving during early childhood, leading to indiscriminate social interactions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfR.label: Manufacturing Expert
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfR.definition: An expert in the field of manufacturing, including managers and workers with experience in the manufacturing industry. 10 U.S.C. § 2197

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfS.label: Scotts Valley Band of Pomo Indians of California
english_labels: Scotts Valley Band of Pomo Indians of California

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfT.label: Heart Transplant
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfT.definition: A heart transplant is a surgical procedure in which a diseased or damaged heart is replaced with a healthy donor heart. It is a significant intervention for end-stage heart failure or severe coronary artery disease, and involves lifelong medical management to prevent rejection of the donor heart and to manage post-transplant complications.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfY.label: Washington Superior Court - Grant County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfY.definition: Washington Superior Court - Grant County refers to a specific court within the Washington Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Grant County, Washington.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfc.label: Ohio Board of Unauthorized Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfc.definition: The Ohio Board of Unauthorized Practice is a regulatory body established by the Ohio State Courts to oversee and prevent the unauthorized practice of law in Ohio.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfd.label: Bribery
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfd.definition: The offering, giving, receiving, or soliciting of anything of value (i.e., a bribe, gratuity, or kickback) to sway the judgment or action of a person in a position of trust or influence.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfe.label: task_activity
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfe.definition: "Activity code for this line item, e.g. ""A101"". Only one code per line item. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCff.label: Oregon Circuit Court - Deschutes County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCff.definition: The Oregon Circuit Court - Deschutes County is a specific court within the Oregon Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Deschutes County, Oregon.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfu.label: Negligence Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfu.definition: Negligence Claims refer to civil claims arising from a failure to exercise reasonable care, resulting in harm or injury to another person or property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfz.label: Residential Mortgage-Backed Securities
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCfz.definition: Residential Mortgage-Backed Securities (RMBS) are a type of mortgage-backed security that is backed by a pool of residential mortgages. RMBS offer investors the opportunity to receive payments from the interest and principal of the underlying home loans, providing exposure to the residential real estate market.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCg0.label: Pregnancy Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCg0.definition: Negligent or wrongful conduct by a medical professional during pregnancy or childbirth that results in harm to the mother or child.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCg1.label: Dissolution of Limited Liability Company
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCg1.definition: The Dissolution of Limited Liability Company refers to the legal process of ending the existence of a company that has been formed with limited liability, which may involve the distribution of assets, payment of debts, and termination of contracts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCg2.label: Motion for Relief from Void Judgment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCg2.definition: A Motion for Relief from Void Judgment is a legal request made to a court to set aside a judgment that is considered null and void due to a lack of jurisdiction or other fundamental defects.
english_labels: Motion for Relief from Void Judgment

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCg7.label: Class Action [Certified Class]
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCg7.definition: A Class Action is certified class consisting of a group of people who have suffered similar harm or injury, where the claims are too numerous or impractical to be brought individually.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCg8.label: D.D.S. (Doctor of Dental Surgery)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCg8.definition: The suffix "D.D.S." stands for "Doctor of Dental Surgery" and is used after a person's name to indicate that they have completed the necessary education and training to practice dentistry. This suffix signifies the individual's credentials in the field of dental care and is commonly used in medical settings, academic contexts, and formal documents

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgB.label: Boston Municipal Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgB.definition: Boston Municipal Court is a court within the Massachusetts Trial Court system that has jurisdiction over criminal and civil cases within the city of Boston.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgE.label: Registration Rights Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgE.definition: Registration Rights Agreement is a contractual agreement between the issuer of securities and the security holders that obligates the issuer to register the securities under relevant securities laws, allowing for public trading. Typically, it benefits investors by providing liquidity.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgH.label: Intellectual Property License Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgH.definition: An Intellectual Property License Agreement grants a party the right to use a specific intellectual property owned by another party under specified conditions. It doesn't transfer ownership but allows for certain usages, often in exchange for compensation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgL.label: Oregon Circuit Court - Morrow County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgL.definition: Oregon Circuit Court - Morrow County: A specific court within the Oregon Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Morrow County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgM.label: Canon Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgM.definition: Canon Law is the body of laws and regulations developed by the Catholic Church for its own governance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgO.label: Minnesota District Court - Steele County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgO.definition: Minnesota District Court - Steele County: A specific court within the Minnesota District Court system located in Steele County, responsible for administering legal proceedings within its jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgP.label: Original Writings Objection
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgP.definition: An Original Writings Objection, also known as the Best Evidence Rule Objection, is raised when a party attempts to introduce a copy or other secondary evidence of a document when the original document is available and required. This objection asserts that the party offering the evidence must provide the original document, as it is the best evidence of its content.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgT.label: No Third Party Beneficiary Rights Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgT.definition: A No Third Party Beneficiary Rights Clause is a provision in a contract that explicitly states that no third party, other than the parties involved in the contract, has any rights or benefits under the contract.
english_labels: No Third Party Beneficiary Rights Clause

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgU.label: Auditor
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgU.definition: A person who conducts audits and investigates accounting functions of a private or governmental entity.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgV.label: Negotiation Sequence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgV.definition: In the context of contract negotiations, a Contractual Turn refers to each sequential exchange or iteration in the negotiation process, typically involving the drafting, reviewing, and revising of the contract. For example, Turn 1 may involve Party A sending the initial draft of the agreement to Party B, and Turn 2 may involve Party B sending a marked-up draft back to Party A.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgW.label: Date Signed
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgW.definition: Date Signed refers to the specific calendar date on which a legal document or contract is executed by the involved parties. This date is crucial as it often marks the commencement of the document’s legal effect and the start of obligations or rights.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCga.label: Washington Superior Court - Skagit County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCga.definition: Washington Superior Court - Skagit County refers to a specific court within the Washington Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Skagit County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgh.label: Kansas District Court - Morris County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgh.definition: Kansas District Court - Morris County: A specific court within the Kansas District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Morris County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgl.label: Child Labor Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgl.definition: A child labor claim is a legal assertion that a minor has been employed in violation of labor laws that regulate the age, conditions, and hours of work for minors. Such claims often seek remedies for the exploitation or harm suffered by the child due to illegal employment practices.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgs.label: O-1A Visa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgs.definition: An O-1A visa is issued to individuals with extraordinary ability in the sciences, education, business, or athletics, demonstrated by sustained national or international acclaim. This visa allows them to enter the U.S. to work in their area of expertise.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgv.label: Due Diligence Period Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgv.definition: A Due Diligence Period Clause is a provision in a contract that allows a party a specified amount of time to conduct investigations and assessments to ensure that the terms of the contract are acceptable before finalizing the agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgx.label: Motion to File Substitute or Corrected Brief
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgx.definition: A Motion to File Substitute or Corrected Brief is a formal request made to a court to allow a party to replace or amend a previously filed brief with a new or corrected version.
english_labels: Motion to File Substitute or Corrected Brief

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCgx.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Scott County (7th Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Scott County (7th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCh0.label: Cebuano
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCh0.definition: A language spoken in the Philippines, specifically in the Central Visayas region and some parts of Mindanao.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCh6.label: Rules of Professional Conduct
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCh6.definition: The "Rules of Professional Conduct" are a set of ethical guidelines and standards that lawyers are required to adhere to in the course of their legal practice. These rules are designed to ensure lawyers act with integrity, competence, and loyalty to their clients while upholding the principles of justice and the legal profession. Violations of these rules can result in disciplinary actions by legal authorities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCh6.label: Intervening Event - Knowledge by Target Board
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCh6.definition: An intervening event in a legal matter that involves the knowledge possessed by the target board, which may affect the outcome of the case.
english_labels: Intervening Event - Knowledge by Target Board

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCh6.label: Breach of Implied Warranty of Good & Workmanlike Services
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCh6.definition: Breach of Implied Warranty of Good & Workmanlike Services is a legal concept that refers to a failure to provide services that meet the reasonable expectations of the parties involved, without any express agreement or promise.
english_labels: Breach of Implied Warranty of Good & Workmanlike Services

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RChA.label: Counterparts and Electronic Signatures Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RChA.definition: A Counterparts and Electronic Signatures Clause is a provision in a contract that allows for the execution of the contract through electronic means and permits the use of multiple counterparts, each signed by different parties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RChD.label: Pharmacist Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RChD.definition: Pharmacist Malpractice refers to a type of medical malpractice claim that involves negligence or wrongdoing by a pharmacist in dispensing medication or providing pharmaceutical care.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RChE.label: Washington Superior Court
