https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCrH.definition: Review of Documents Practice refers to the legal work performed by a Legal Services Provider in the course of a legal matter, specifically involving the examination and analysis of documents collected and produced during the case, and may include the identification of relevant information and potential evidence.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCrT.label: Criminal False Imprisonment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCrT.definition: The concept of Criminal False Imprisonment refers to the intentional and unlawful confinement or restraint of an individual against their will, without legal justification or authority, and with the knowledge that the confinement is unlawful.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCrV.label: New Jersey County Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCrV.definition: A New Jersey County Court is a court of law that has jurisdiction over cases within a specific county in New Jersey, and is a subcategory of the New Jersey State Courts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCrX.label: Ethics Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCrX.definition: An Ethics Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the ethical standards and principles that the parties agree to abide by during the course of their relationship.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCrY.label: JJ50 Applications relating to Costs alone (UK J-CODE)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCrY.definition: Includes applications for security for costs, costs capping and protective costs orders. Does not include budgeting or costs management orders which are dealt with at [JB40]. Does not include applications proceeding as to costs alone where a substantive application for some other relief has settled.
english_labels: JJ50 Applications relating to Costs alone (UK J-CODE)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCrc.label: Proxy Vote
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCrc.definition: A Proxy Vote is a form of voting in which a member of a decision-making body delegates their voting power to a representative to vote in their absence. This mechanism allows for continued representation and participation in the voting process when the original voter cannot be physically present or chooses not to attend a meeting or election.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCrc.label: Food and Cash Public Benefit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCrc.definition: Food and cash public benefit refers to government programs that provide financial assistance and food resources to individuals or families in need. Cash benefits, often delivered through electronic benefit transfer (EBT) cards or direct deposits, are intended to help cover basic living expenses, while food benefits, such as the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) in the United States, are designated for purchasing eligible food items.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCrk.label: Automobile Registration
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCrk.definition: "Automobile Registration" refers to the official process of recording essential information about an automobile, such as its make, model, and ownership, with a government authority. This registration, often represented by a certificate or license plate, is required for the vehicle to be legally driven on public roads.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCro.label: Concussion
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCro.definition: Mild traumatic brain injury (concussion) is a form of TBI resulting from a blow or jolt to the head that temporarily disrupts brain function. Symptoms can include headache, confusion, dizziness, and memory loss, and while typically short-term, they may require rest and medical monitoring.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCrs.label: Knowledge Qualifiers
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCrs.definition: Material Adverse Effect (MAE) Definition - "Knowledge" Qualifiers: A term used in legal agreements to describe a negative change or event that has occurred or is likely to occur, and which is known or should have been known by a party based on their level of knowledge or investigation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCs0.label: Kaibab Band of Paiute Indians of the Kaibab Indian Reservation
english_labels: Kaibab Band of Paiute Indians of the Kaibab Indian Reservation

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCs2.label: Exchange Debt for Debt
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCs2.definition: An asset exchange involving the replacement of one form of debt with another. This often aims to take advantage of better terms or to extend the maturity of the debt.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCs5.label: Structure Diagram Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCs5.definition: Structure Diagram Management refers to the management of diagrams that represent the structure of legal transactions and solutions, and is a subcategory of Legal Transaction Management and Legal Point Solutions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCs6.label: Business Visa Exception
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCs6.definition: A Business Visa Exemption refers to a special arrangement where nationals from certain countries are allowed to enter another country for short-term business activities without the need for a traditional business visa. This is often part of broader visa-free entry agreements or reciprocal arrangements between countries, and is generally time-limited

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCs6.label: Satellite Broadcast
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCs6.definition: A Satellite Broadcast is the transmission of television and radio signals via communication satellites, delivering content to a wide audience across vast geographical areas. This form of broadcasting provides access to various programming, including live events, news, entertainment, and educational shows, typically received through satellite dishes and decoders.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCsA.label: Appellate Argument Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCsA.definition: Appellate Argument Practice refers to the specialized legal practice of preparing and presenting arguments before an appellate court, with the aim of persuading the court to overturn or modify a lower court's decision.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCsH.label: Acceleration Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCsH.definition: An acceleration clause is a provision in a contract that allows the creditor to demand immediate payment of the entire outstanding balance if the debtor fails to meet certain obligations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCsM.label: Appraisal Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCsM.definition: Appraisal Management refers to the process of overseeing and coordinating the evaluation of an individual's performance or value, within the context of managing people.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCsR.label: Hearing Disability
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCsR.definition: A Hearing Disability is a partial or total inability to hear sounds in one or both ears, which can affect communication, social interaction, and daily activities. This condition can range from mild hearing loss to profound deafness and may require the use of hearing aids, cochlear implants, or other assistive devices.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCsS.label: Cooperative
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCsS.definition: A cooperative is a legal entity that is owned and operated by its members, who share in the profits and decision-making of the organization.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCsd.label: Walloon
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCsd.definition: A dialect of French spoken in Wallonia, Belgium.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCsg.label: Abbreviated New Drug Application Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCsg.definition: An Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA) Claim arises when there is a dispute or legal challenge related to the submission or approval of an ANDA, which allows for the marketing of a generic drug that demonstrates bioequivalence to an already approved brand-name drug. This claim can involve issues of patent infringement, exclusivity rights, or regulatory compliance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCsj.label: Declaration of Chapter 13 Income
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCsj.definition: A Declaration of Chapter 13 Income is a written statement that discloses the income of an individual who has filed for Chapter 13 bankruptcy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCsm.label: Notice of Lodging
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCsm.definition: Notice of filing physical items (e.g., thumb drives, videotapes) with the court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCss.label: Natural Resources Extraction Real Estate Asset
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCss.definition: A natural resources extraction real estate asset refers to a property that contains or is believed to contain natural resources such as minerals, oil, gas, or timber, which can be extracted for economic value. This asset is significant in the realms of property law, environmental law, and resource management, as it encompasses the rights and regulations related to the extraction and use of these resources.
english_labels: Natural Resources Extraction Real Estate Asset

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCsv.label: Interstitial Lung Disease
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCsv.definition: Interstitial lung disease (ILD) refers to a group of disorders characterized by inflammation and scarring of the interstitium (the tissue and space around the air sacs) in the lungs. This group of diseases leads to progressive lung damage, impaired gas exchange, and respiratory symptoms such as cough and shortness of breath.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCsx.label: Dismissal for Violation of Rules
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCsx.definition: Dismissal for Violation of Rules refers to the termination of employment due to an employee's failure to comply with company policies or regulations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCsz.label: Midwife Negligence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCsz.definition: Negligent actions or omissions by a midwife during the provision of care to a mother and/or baby, resulting in harm or injury, and giving rise to a legal claim for compensation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCt3.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Johnson County (1st Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Johnson County (1st Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCt4.label: Motion to Approve Settlement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCt4.definition: A Motion to Approve Settlement is a formal request made to a court to approve a proposed agreement between parties to a legal dispute.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCt5.label: Disclosure of Compensation of Attorney for Debtor
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCt5.definition: The Disclosure of Compensation of Attorney for Debtor refers to the requirement for a bankruptcy attorney to disclose their compensation to the court and other parties involved in the bankruptcy case.
english_labels: Disclosure of Compensation of Attorney for Debtor

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCt6.label: Consumer Loan Broker Acting Improperly
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCt6.definition: A Consumer Loan Broker Acting Improperly refers to a situation where a broker who arranges loans for consumers engages in unethical or illegal behavior, such as misrepresenting loan terms or charging excessive fees.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCtD.label: Cash Collateral Motion
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCtD.definition: A Cash Collateral Motion in Bankruptcy is a legal request made by a debtor to use cash or cash equivalents that are held as collateral by a creditor, in order to continue operating their business during the bankruptcy process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCtF.label: Mongolian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCtF.definition: Mongolian (Language) refers to the written or spoken structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary specific to the Mongolian language.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCtJ.label: Strawberries
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCtJ.definition: Strawberries are small, red, and fragrant aggregate fruits belonging to the Fragaria genus, known for their sweet flavor and juicy texture. They are widely consumed fresh or processed into jams, desserts, and beverages and are valued for their high vitamin C content, antioxidants, and dietary fiber.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCtL.label: Waiver of Liability Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCtL.definition: A waiver of liability clause is a provision in a legal document that releases a party from responsibility for any harm or injury that may occur as a result of participating in an activity or using a product, typically signed by the participant or user.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCtU.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Huntington County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCtU.definition: Indiana Circuit Court - Huntington County refers to a specific court within the Indiana Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Huntington County, Indiana.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCtU.label: Illinois Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCtU.definition: Illinois Circuit Court is a court of general jurisdiction in the state of Illinois that hears civil and criminal cases.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCtV.label: Post-Polio Syndrome
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCtV.definition: Post-Polio Syndrome (PPS) is a condition that affects polio survivors years after recovery from the initial poliomyelitis infection. It is characterized by new or worsening muscle weakness, fatigue, and pain, often developing 15 to 40 years after the original polio illness.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCtV.label: Insurance Document
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCtV.definition: An Insurance Document is a formal written record that encompasses all types of materials related to the underwriting, administration, and execution of insurance policies. Examples include insurance forms, policies, and reinsurance agreements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCtW.label: Incumbency Certificate
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCtW.definition: An Incumbency Certificate is a legal document issued by a corporation or organization, certifying the names and positions of its current officers, directors, and, in some cases, key employees. It serves as official evidence of the authority of specific individuals to act on behalf of the corporation or organization in legal and financial transactions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCtX.label: oasis:Collection
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCtX.definition: A collection in the LegalXML OASIS SCHEMA that includes figures, agents, roles, times, and temporal characteristics.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCtZ.label: Copyright Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCtZ.definition: Laws intended to encourage the creation of art and culture by rewarding authors and artists with a set of exclusive rights.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCta.label: Dogrib
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCta.definition: Dogrib is a structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary, and is a specific language within the context of legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCtb.label: DOC
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCtb.definition: A Microsoft Word document file from Microsoft Office 2003 or earlier.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCth.label: Employment Authorization Document
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCth.definition: Employment Authorization Documents (EADs) are permits granted by a country's immigration authority to allow foreign nationals to work legally within its borders. Types of EADs can include those for students, refugees or asylum seekers, dependents of primary visa holders, and individuals under special humanitarian or temporary protection programs.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCty.label: Employment Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCty.definition: Employment Claims refer to legal actions brought by employees against their employers for various reasons such as discrimination, wrongful termination, wage theft, and harassment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCty.label: Indiana Town Court - Marion County, Perry Twp.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCty.definition: A court located in Perry Township, Marion County, Indiana, with limited jurisdiction over minor criminal offenses, traffic violations, and small claims.
english_labels: Indiana Town Court - Marion County, Perry Twp.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCtz.label: Sports Competitor Visa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCtz.definition: This type of visa allows amateur or professional athletes to enter a country temporarily to participate in events where they may earn prize money. It does not permit employment beyond prize winnings and is typically subject to conditions and duration limits based on the specifics of the competition.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCu2.label: Effective Date Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCu2.definition: An Effective Date Clause is a provision in a contract that specifies the date on which the agreement becomes legally binding and enforceable.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCu2.label: Private Company
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCu2.definition: Company whose stock is not publicly available on a public stock exchange, as recognized by the relevant jurisdictions' authority — and is not required by relevant legal authorities to make public disclosures (e.g., operations, finance).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCu3.label: Magistrate Judge
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCu3.definition: A judicial officer who usually conducts proceedings that deal with minor or preliminary matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCu5.label: tax_id_number
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCu5.definition: "Tax ID Number for law firm or vendor associated with specific tax. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCu7.label: Probationary Period Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCu7.definition: A probationary period clause is a provision in a contract that outlines a trial period during which an employee's performance is evaluated before a permanent employment decision is made.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuC.label: Purchase Order Number
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuC.definition: A Purchase Order Number is a unique identifier assigned to a specific purchase order within an Engagement Fee Detail, used to track and manage the procurement of goods or services related to the engagement for providing legal services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuD.label: Charitable Donation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuD.definition: A Charitable Donation is a voluntary gift of money, goods, or services given to a non-profit organization or cause that serves the public interest. This type of donation is typically tax-deductible and is made with the intention of supporting philanthropic activities, addressing social needs, or promoting the welfare of others without expectation of direct personal benefit.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuE.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Cambria County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuE.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court in Cambria County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court system that has jurisdiction over minor criminal offenses and civil cases.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Cambria County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuJ.label: charge_type
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuJ.definition: """U"" unit price, ""F"" fixed charge. [Note: most line items will be unit price.] "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuL.label: Dogs
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuL.definition: Dogs are domesticated mammals belonging to the species Canis lupus familiaris, known for their loyalty, intelligence, and diverse roles in human society. They serve as companions, working animals, and service animals, and come in a wide variety of breeds with specific traits and purposes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuR.label: Massachusetts Superior Court - Franklin County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuR.definition: The Massachusetts Superior Court - Franklin County is a court of general jurisdiction in Massachusetts that hears civil and criminal cases within Franklin County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuT.label: Transit Visa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuT.definition: A transit visa is a short-term visa that allows travelers to pass through a foreign country en route to another destination. This type of visa is generally valid for a very limited period, often 24 to 72 hours, and does not permit the holder to engage in activities like tourism or business within the transit country.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuV.label: New York Supreme Court - Madison County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuV.definition: The New York Supreme Court - Madison County is a court of general jurisdiction located in Madison County, New York, with authority to hear and decide a wide range of legal disputes within its geographical jurisdiction.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - Madison County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuc.label: Cable Broadcast
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuc.definition: A Cable Broadcast is the transmission of television content through coaxial or fiber-optic cables to subscribers, providing access to a wide range of channels and programming. This form of broadcasting offers both live and on-demand content, including news, entertainment, sports, and educational shows, delivered to viewers via a cable television service.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuh.label: Willful Misconduct
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuh.definition: Intentional and reckless behavior that goes beyond mere negligence, often resulting in harm or injury to another person or property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuh.label: Cardiovascular Disorders
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuh.definition: Cardiovascular disorders encompass any condition that impairs the normal functioning of the heart or the circulatory system, including arteries, veins, capillaries, and lymphatic vessels. These disorders can be congenital, present from birth, or acquired, developing over time due to various factors such as lifestyle or disease.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCui.label: Payment Terms and Conditions Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCui.definition: A Payment Terms and Conditions Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the specific terms and conditions related to payment, including the amount, timing, and method of payment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuj.label: Kansas District Court - Osage County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuj.definition: A court located in Osage County, Kansas that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCul.label: Nepal Bhasa; Newari
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCul.definition: A language spoken in Nepal, also known as Newari.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCum.label: Executive Branch
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCum.definition: The executive branch is responsible for implementing, administering, and enforcing the laws enacted by the legislative branch. It is typically headed by a president, prime minister, or monarch, and includes various administrative agencies and departments.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCun.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Lewis County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCun.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Lewis County refers to a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Lewis County, Missouri.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuo.label: Deceptive Insurance Practices
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuo.definition: Deceptive Insurance Practices refer to any fraudulent or misleading actions taken by an insurance company or its representatives in order to deny or delay payment of a claim.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCup.label: Administration Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCup.definition: An Administration Agreement in the context of private fund administration refers to a contract where a third-party administrator is appointed to manage operational functions like accounting, reporting, and compliance for a private investment fund. This agreement delineates the scope of services, responsibilities, and fees related to the administration of the fund.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuq.label: Electrical Patent
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuq.definition: An electrical patent is a legal protection granted to inventors of new and useful electrical inventions, such as circuits, electrical devices, and systems.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCur.label: Business Acquisition Report
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCur.definition: A Business Acquisition Report is a disclosure document filed with securities regulators detailing the acquisition of another business. It typically includes financial statements and the rationale behind the acquisition.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCur.label: Permission
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCur.definition: Permission refers to the formal consent or authorization granted by an authority, allowing an individual or entity to perform a certain action that would otherwise be illegal or against the rules.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCur.label: Native American
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCur.definition: A Native American is a person who belongs to one of the indigenous peoples of North America, with a distinct cultural and historical heritage.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuu.label: Medical Malpractice Defenses
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuu.definition: Medical Malpractice Defenses are legal arguments or strategies used by defendants in a medical malpractice case to defend against the plaintiff's claims of negligence or wrongdoing.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuv.label: Akan
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCuv.definition: Akan is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary, primarily spoken in Ghana and Ivory Coast.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCv1.label: State-Provided Public Benefit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCv1.definition: State-provided public benefit refers to assistance programs that are administered and funded at the state or provincial level. These can include state-specific healthcare programs, housing assistance, and educational grants.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCv4.label: Oregon State Board of Nursing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCv4.definition: The Oregon State Board of Nursing is a government entity responsible for regulating and overseeing the practice of nursing within the state of Oregon.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCv6.label: COMI (Center of Main Interest)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCv6.definition: COMI, or Center of Main Interest, refers to the primary location where a debtor conducts its principal business operations and is recognized as the central point of its economic activities. This concept is crucial in cross-border insolvency cases to determine jurisdiction and the appropriate forum for the main insolvency proceeding.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCv7.label: Motion for Attorney Fees
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCv7.definition: A Motion for Attorney Fees is a request made by a party in a legal case to recover the costs of their attorney's services, which may include fees, interest, and other expenses incurred during the proceedings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCvC.label: Export Compliance Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCvC.definition: An Export Compliance Clause is a provision in a contract that requires the parties to comply with applicable laws and regulations related to the export of goods or technology.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCvE.label: Real Estate Tax Payment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCvE.definition: Payment of Recurrent Taxes on Immovable Property refers to the regular, often annual, tax payments made by property owners to local or national governments based on the assessed value of their real estate. These taxes fund public services such as education, infrastructure, and emergency services.
english_labels: Payment of Recurrent Taxes on Immovable Property

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCvI.label: Intellectual Property Ownership Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCvI.definition: A provision in a contract that establishes the ownership rights of intangible creations, such as inventions, literary and artistic works, and symbols.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCvN.label: Wrongful Birth Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCvN.definition: A wrongful birth claim is a type of personal injury claim brought by parents who allege that they were not properly informed by a medical professional of the risk of having a child with a genetic or congenital abnormality, resulting in the birth of a child with such abnormality.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCvQ.label: Wiretap Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCvQ.definition: A wiretap claim is a civil claim that alleges the illegal interception of electronic communications, such as phone calls or emails.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCvU.label: Legatee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCvU.definition: A legatee is an individual or entity named in a will to receive personal property or money from the estate of the deceased. This term differentiates from a devisee, who inherits real property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCvV.label: Regulatory Events
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCvV.definition: Events related to legal services surrounding regulations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCvf.label: Pharmacology Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCvf.definition: Pharmacology Malpractice refers to a type of medical malpractice claim that involves errors or negligence in the prescription, administration, or monitoring of medication by a healthcare professional.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCvi.label: Requests for Production
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCvi.definition: Requests for Production are a type of Discovery Document that require a party to provide specific documents or items for inspection and copying by the opposing party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCvk.label: Criminal Restitution
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCvk.definition: The concept of Criminal Restitution refers to the court-ordered payment made by a convicted criminal to their victim(s) as compensation for the harm caused by the criminal act.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCvm.label: Waray
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCvm.definition: Waray is a structured system of communication, both written and spoken, that belongs to the group of languages classified as "Language".

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCvx.label: On-View Arrest
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCvx.definition: An on-view arrest is a type of arrest made by a law enforcement officer without a warrant, based on their own observation of a crime being committed.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCw2.label: Conditional Bequest
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCw2.definition: A Conditional Bequest is a provision in a will or trust that designates the transfer of assets or property to a beneficiary only if certain specified conditions or criteria are met. This type of bequest allows the testator to impose requirements that must be fulfilled for the beneficiary to receive the inheritance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCw8.label: Attempted
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCw8.definition: An action taken with the intention of committing a crime, but which ultimately fails to achieve its intended result.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCw8.label: Adoption
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCw8.definition: The legal process by which a person or couple becomes the legal parent(s) of a child who is not biologically their own, often involving termination of the biological parents' rights and responsibilities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwB.label: End-to-end CLM Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwB.definition: End-to-end CLM Management refers to the comprehensive management of the entire contract lifecycle, from creation to execution and beyond, within the context of Contract Management.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwB.label: Illinois Circuit Court - DuPage County (18th Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - DuPage County (18th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwE.label: Accredited Investor
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwE.definition: Individuals or entities that meet certain requirements set by regulatory authorities, such as a specific net worth or income level.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwO.label: Impossibility of Performance
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwO.definition: The Impossibility of Performance is a legal defense in civil litigation that arises when a party is unable to fulfill their contractual obligations due to circumstances beyond their control, such as an act of God or a change in the law.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwP.label: Petition - Treaty Skilled Worker Visa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwP.definition: A Petition for Treaty Skilled Worker Visa (in the U.S., TN application) refers to the process of applying for a TN (Trade NAFTA) visa at the U.S.-Canada or U.S.-Mexico border. The TN visa is available to Canadian and Mexican citizens engaged in specific professional occupations. Applicants must meet the qualifications outlined in the NAFTA agreement and provide the necessary documentation to demonstrate eligibility. Upon approval, the TN visa allows individuals to work in the U.S. temporarily in qualifying professional roles

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwT.label: Wage Theft Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwT.definition: A wage theft claim is a legal action taken by an employee against an employer for the unlawful withholding of wages or benefits that the employee is entitled to receive.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwV.label: Motion for New Trial - Inadequate Damages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwV.definition: A Motion for New Trial - Inadequate Damages is a legal request made by a party to a lawsuit asking the court to set aside the previous verdict and order a new trial due to the damages awarded being insufficient.
english_labels: Motion for New Trial - Inadequate Damages

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwb.label: Little River Band of Ottawa Indians of Michigan
english_labels: Little River Band of Ottawa Indians of Michigan

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwd.label: Organizational Officer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwd.definition: A fiduciary with respect to the corporation and its shareholders. In re Long, 774 F.2d 875 (8th Cir. 1985)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwd.label: Anti-Corruption Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwd.definition: An Anti-Corruption Clause is a provision in a contract that prohibits bribery or other corrupt activities between the parties involved.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwe.label: Bond Assets
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwe.definition: A bond is a fixed income instrument that represents a loan made by an investor to a borrower (typically corporate or governmental). A bond could be thought of as an I.O.U. between the lender and borrower that includes the details of the loan and its payment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwf.label: Arkansas Circuit Court - Dallas Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwf.definition: A court located in Dallas County, Arkansas that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its designated geographical area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwh.label: Corporate Meeting Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwh.definition: Corporate Meeting Management refers to the process of organizing and managing meetings for corporations, including scheduling, logistics, and documentation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwl.label: Sworn Complaint
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwl.definition: A sworn complaint is a formal written statement made under oath by a person alleging wrongdoing by another party, typically used in legal proceedings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwl.label: Bankruptcy Plan's Substantial Consummation Objective
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwl.definition: A legal principle where a court can determine that a bankruptcy plan has been sufficiently executed, preventing parties from initiating new actions or modifications related to the plan. This principle provides legal finality and ensures the implementation of the plan's provisions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwr.label: Purchase Receipt
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwr.definition: A Purchase Receipt is a financial document provided by a seller to a buyer as proof of a completed transaction. It details the goods or services purchased, the amount paid, and often the method of payment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwx.label: Trespass
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwx.definition: The act of unlawfully entering or interfering with someone else's property, whether it be real property or personal property, resulting in potential liability for the trespasser.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwx.label: Collaboration Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCwx.definition: Collaboration Management refers to the process of coordinating and managing the sharing of information and resources among individuals or groups within a legal context, including the use of extranets, virtual data rooms, and collaboration platforms.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCx0.label: Evidence Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCx0.definition: Evidence Management refers to the process of collecting, organizing, and preserving evidence in a legal case, with the aim of ensuring its admissibility and reliability in court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCx3.label: No Liability Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCx3.definition: A no liability clause is a type of contractual clause that absolves one party from any legal responsibility or obligation for any damages or losses incurred by the other party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCx5.label: Automobile Insurance Policy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCx5.definition: An automobile insurance policy is a contract between a policyholder and an insurance company that provides financial protection against losses arising from accidents, theft, or other events affecting a motor vehicle. The policy specifies the types of coverage included, such as liability, collision, and comprehensive, and requires the payment of premiums to maintain this coverage.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCx6.label: Fraudulent Concealment by Fiduciary
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCx6.definition: The fraudulent concealment by fiduciary concept refers to the intentional act of a person in a position of trust or confidence, such as a trustee or executor, to hide or withhold material information from another party for personal gain or to cause harm.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCx9.label: Negligent Operation of Activity Requiring Franchise or License
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCx9.definition: Negligent Operation of Activity Requiring Franchise or License refers to a legal claim for damages resulting from the careless or reckless operation of a business or activity that requires a franchise or license to operate, such as a taxi service or a liquor store.
english_labels: Negligent Operation of Activity Requiring Franchise or License

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxE.label: Asset Turnover Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxE.definition: Asset Turnover Practice refers to the legal analysis and evaluation of a company's asset turnover ratio, which measures the efficiency of a company's use of its assets to generate revenue.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxF.label: Short-term Spousal Support
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxF.definition: Short-term Spousal Support, also known as temporary alimony or maintenance, is financial support paid by one spouse to the other for a limited and predefined duration. It is typically awarded during the divorce process to provide financial assistance to a lower-earning spouse until a final divorce settlement is reached or until they can achieve financial self-sufficiency. The duration and amount of short-term spousal support are determined by court orders or agreements between the parties and are designed to address immediate financial needs during the divorce proceedings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxI.label: Proceeding Status
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxI.definition: "Proceeding Status" refers to the current stage or status of a legal or regulatory process, whether it's a court proceeding or a regulatory proceeding. It signifies whether the proceeding is open, closed, consolidated, inactive, or has had filing fees waived.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxL.label: matter_disc_credit_exp
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxL.definition: "Sum of all MATTER_DISC_CRED.disc_credit_amount where MATTER_DISC_CRED.disc_credit_type equals ""EXP"" and (MATTER_DISC_CRED.disc_cred is not ""MISF"", ""MIDB"" or ""MIFA""). Excludes discounts or credits applied to expense line items as these are already part of matter_total_detail_exp. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxR.label: Motion for Substantive Consolidation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxR.definition: A Motion for Substantive Consolidation is a legal request made in a bankruptcy case to combine the assets and liabilities of two or more related entities into a single entity for the purpose of simplifying the administration of the bankruptcy proceedings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxR.label: Document Description
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxR.definition: Document Description refers to the specific information or details provided about a written, drawn, presented, or memorialized representation of thought or expression, including evidence such as recordings and other artifacts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxR.label: Motion for Rehearing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxR.definition: A Motion for Rehearing is a request made to a trial court to reconsider a decision or ruling that has already been made.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxR.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Stephenson County (15th Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Stephenson County (15th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxW.label: Arkansas Circuit Court - Crittenden Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxW.definition: The Arkansas Circuit Court - Crittenden Cty. is a specific court within the Arkansas Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Crittenden County, Arkansas.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxX.label: Specialty Rulesets
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxX.definition: Specialty Rulesets are a subset of Rule Type in legal knowledge management, consisting of specific sets of rules and regulations related to a particular area of law, such as Personal Injury or COVID.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxY.label: DEPRECATED - Material Adverse Effect Definition - Applies to Target and Subsidiaries as a Whole
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxY.definition: SUPERCEDED BY ACQUIROR AND ACQUIREE TAGS. A Material Adverse Effect (MAE) is a significant negative change or event that affects both the target company and its subsidiaries as a whole, as defined in a legal agreement.
english_labels: DEPRECATED - Material Adverse Effect Definition - Applies to Target and Subsidiaries as a Whole
Material Adverse Effect Definition - Applies to Target and Subsidiaries as a Whole

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxc.label: Auction Rate Dividend Payment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxc.definition: Auction Rate Income refers to a type of dividend income where the dividend rate is periodically adjusted through an auction process, such as a Dutch auction. This mechanism allows the dividend rate to be determined by investor demand, resulting in potentially variable payouts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxf.label: Real Estate Fraud
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxf.definition: Real Estate Fraud: A type of fraud claim that involves deceitful or dishonest practices related to the buying, selling, or leasing of real property, which may result in property or premises liability claims.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxi.label: Withdrawal Event
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxi.definition: A Withdrawal Event occurs when an individual voluntarily cancels or withdraws an application or request that was previously submitted to a regulatory authority, such as immigration authorities. This action signifies the individual's decision not to proceed with the application and may have implications for fees, future applications, and legal status

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxq.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Philadelphia County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxq.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court located in Philadelphia County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court system that has jurisdiction over minor criminal offenses and civil cases with limited monetary claims.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Philadelphia County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxr.label: Cotton
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxr.definition: Cotton is a natural fiber obtained from the seed hairs of the cotton plant, used extensively in the textile industry to produce clothing, linens, and other fabric-based goods. It is known for its softness, breathability, and versatility, making it one of the most widely cultivated and utilized fiber crops globally.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxu.label: Telecommunication Utilities Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxu.definition: Laws regulating telecommunications and broadcasting utilities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxv.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Bedford County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxv.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Bedford County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering civil and criminal proceedings at the county level in Pennsylvania.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Bedford County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxw.label: Serbian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCxw.definition: Serbian (Language) is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary used in Serbia and other parts of the Balkans.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCy1.label: Georgia Superior Court - Lanier County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCy1.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Lanier County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Lanier County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCy6.label: Employee Termination Event
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCy6.definition: Employee Termination refers to the formal end of an employment relationship between an employee and an employer. This can occur for various reasons, including but not limited to, voluntary resignation, layoffs, or dismissal for cause, and typically involves the completion of exit procedures and documentation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCy9.label: Detinue
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCy9.definition: Detinue is a legal claim that allows a person to recover wrongfully detained property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyE.label: App Development Services
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyE.definition: App Development Services refers to the provision of legal process improvement services related to the creation and maintenance of software applications for legal purposes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyM.label: National Origin
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyM.definition: National origin refers to an individual's country or region of birth, ancestry, or cultural heritage. In many jurisdictions, including the United States, it is unlawful to discriminate against someone based on their national origin in various contexts, such as employment, housing, and public services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyN.label: Vesting
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyN.definition: Vesting refers to the process by which an individual gains unconditional ownership or entitlement to certain assets or benefits over time, often subject to meeting specific conditions or remaining in employment for a predetermined period. In legal and financial contexts, it's a mechanism to incentivize loyalty and performance, typically applied to assets like stock options, retirement benefits, or property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyS.label: Juvenile Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyS.definition: Juvenile law and child protective proceedings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyU.label: E109 Local travel
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyU.definition: Local travel expenses incurred by an individual in a specific location, such as transportation costs for commuting or running errands, which are categorized under the broader category of expenses.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyU.label: Matter Total Detail Expenses
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyU.definition: Expenses related to the total details of a legal matter, including all costs incurred in providing legal services, such as fees, disbursements, and other expenses.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyU.label: Speeding Ticket
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyU.definition: A speeding ticket is a written notice issued by a law enforcement officer to a driver who is alleged to have exceeded the posted speed limit. The ticket serves as a formal accusation of the speeding violation and typically includes information about the offense, the fine amount, and the steps the driver must take to resolve the matter.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyX.label: Approval Event
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyX.definition: A Regulatory Approval Event refers to the occurrence of receiving official authorization or clearance from a regulatory authority for a particular action or request. In the context of immigration, this might involve obtaining approval for a visa, permit, or other immigration-related application, signifying the successful completion of the regulatory process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCya.label: Senior Housing - Real Estate Asset
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCya.definition: Senior Housing - Real Estate Asset refers to a type of real estate asset that is specifically designed and intended for senior citizens to reside in.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyf.label: Dispositive Power Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyf.definition: A dispositive power clause is a type of contractual clause that grants the holder the authority to make decisions or take actions that affect the rights and obligations of the parties involved in the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyi.label: California Court of Appeal - 2d Dist.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyi.definition: The California Court of Appeal - 2d Dist. is a specific division of the California Court of Appeal that hears appeals from trial courts in the second appellate district of California.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyj.label: Rarotongan; Cook Islands Maori
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyj.definition: A language spoken in the Cook Islands, including the Rarotongan dialect, used in legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCym.label: Party Admission
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCym.definition: A Party Admission is a statement made by a party to a legal proceeding that is offered as evidence against that party. Party admissions are considered non-hearsay and are admissible as an exception to the hearsay rule due to the inherent reliability and fairness of allowing a party's own statements to be used against them.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCym.label: Florida County Court - Santarosa County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCym.definition: A court located in Santa Rosa County, Florida that handles civil and criminal cases within its jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyo.label: Criminal Causation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyo.definition: The concept of Criminal Causation refers to the causal relationship between the defendant's actions and the resulting harm or injury, which is an essential element of a criminal claim.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCys.label: Monthly Recurring Revenue
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCys.definition: Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR) is a financial metric commonly used by subscription-based businesses to measure the total amount of revenue generated each month from recurring subscriptions. It does not include one-time payments or variable fees and is often used to assess business stability and growth potential.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyu.label: New York Supreme Court - Clinton County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyu.definition: The New York Supreme Court - Clinton County is a court of general jurisdiction located in Clinton County, New York, with authority to hear and decide a wide range of civil and criminal cases.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - Clinton County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyv.label: Tahitian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyv.definition: Tahitian (Language) is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary used in Tahiti and other French Polynesian islands.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyx.label: JH00 Expert reports (UK J-CODE)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyx.definition: Work that relates to the identification of potential experts and preparing their evidence for trial (excludes expert evidence in relation to interim applications).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyy.label: Irrelevant
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyy.definition: The concept of "Irrelevant" refers to evidence or information that is not related or connected to the legal matter at hand and therefore cannot be used to support or refute a party's arguments or claims.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyy.label: Tax Authority Reference
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyy.definition: Tax Authority Reference: A specific identifier assigned by a tax authority to a fee invoice detail.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyz.label: Accounts Payable
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCyz.definition: Accounts Payable is an accounting term that represents a company's obligation to pay off short-term debts to its creditors or suppliers within a specified period. It appears on the balance sheet as a current liability and indicates the amounts that a company owes for goods or services received but not yet paid for.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCz0.label: New York City Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCz0.definition: New York City Court is a court of law located in New York City that has jurisdiction over a variety of legal matters within its geographical area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCz1.label: Cross-Examination of Witness
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCz1.definition: The Cross-Examination of Witness is the questioning of a witness by the opposing party during a trial, aimed at testing the credibility and accuracy of their testimony.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCz2.label: Writ Appeal
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCz2.definition: A writ appeal is a legal action taken by a party who is dissatisfied with a lower court's decision, requesting a higher court to review and potentially overturn the decision.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCz6.label: Bikol
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCz6.definition: Bikol is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary, and is a specific language used in legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCz8.label: Admission
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCz8.definition: The concept of Admission refers to the act of acknowledging or accepting the truth or validity of a claim or allegation made by another party in a legal matter.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCz8.label: Caring for Collateral or Security
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCz8.definition: The concept of "Caring for Collateral or Security" refers to the legal responsibility of an agent to properly maintain and protect assets that have been pledged as security for a loan or other obligation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzD.label: Kidney Cancer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzD.definition: Kidney cancer is a type of cancer that originates in the kidneys, the two bean-shaped organs responsible for filtering blood and producing urine. The most common type is renal cell carcinoma, and treatments often include surgery, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, and, in some cases, radiation therapy.
english_labels: Kidney, Adrenal Gland, or Ureter Cancer

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzE.label: Minor in Possession of Alcohol
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzE.definition: A Minor in Possession of Alcohol refers to the illegal act of a person under the legal drinking age possessing or consuming alcohol, which falls under the category of Liquor Law Violations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzN.label: Bankruptcy Initiation Type
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzN.definition: Bankruptcy Initiation Type refers to the classification of bankruptcy proceedings based on who initiates the process. It includes subclasses Voluntary Bankruptcy, where the debtor voluntarily files for bankruptcy, and Involuntary Bankruptcy, where creditors force the debtor into bankruptcy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzQ.label: Water Rights
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzQ.definition: Water rights are legal entitlements allowing the holder to use water from a particular source (like a river, stream, or underground source). The allocation and usage of water rights can be complex and are often based on historic use, need, and regional laws.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzR.label: Electoral Petition
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzR.definition: A formal legal document filed with a court or tribunal in some jurisdictions, such as the United Kingdom, to challenge the validity or outcome of an election, often based on alleged irregularities, violations of election laws, or misconduct by candidates or election officials. Electoral petitions serve as a mechanism for aggrieved parties to seek legal redress and ensure the integrity of the electoral process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzS.label: Incorporation of Exhibits Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzS.definition: A clause in a contract that specifies the inclusion of exhibits, which are documents or other materials that are attached to and made a part of the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzU.label: Franchise Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzU.definition: Franchise Law refers to the legal rules and regulations that govern the relationship between a franchisor and a franchisee in a business arrangement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzV.label: Appellate Filings - Rehearing and Supplements
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzV.definition: Appellate Filings - Rehearing and Supplements refer to additional documents submitted to a higher court after a decision has been made, including petitions for a rehearing or en banc review, and supplementary papers.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzW.label: Iroquoian languages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzW.definition: A group of indigenous languages spoken by the Iroquois people in North America, including Mohawk, Oneida, Onondaga, Cayuga, Seneca, and Tuscarora.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzY.label: Unsecured Credit Arrangement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzY.definition: An Unsecured Credit Arrangement is a financial agreement where the borrower does not pledge any assets as collateral for the loan. This type of loan relies on the borrower's creditworthiness and often results in higher interest rates and stricter borrowing terms due to the increased risk for the lender.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzc.label: Proprietary Information Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzc.definition: A Proprietary Information Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the confidential information that belongs to one party and cannot be shared with others without permission.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzd.label: Mechoopda Indian Tribe of Chico Rancheria
english_labels: Mechoopda Indian Tribe of Chico Rancheria

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzj.label: Delaware
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzj.definition: Delaware (Language) refers to the specific written or spoken structured system of communication used in the state of Delaware, including its grammar and vocabulary, within the context of legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzl.label: Lumbar Stenosis with Cauda Equina Compromise
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzl.definition: Lumbar spinal stenosis resulting in compromise of the cauda equina is a condition where narrowing of the spinal canal in the lumbar region causes compression of the cauda equina, a bundle of nerve roots located at the end of the spinal cord. This compression can lead to severe symptoms such as lower back pain, numbness, weakness, and loss of bowel or bladder function.
english_labels: Lumbar Spinal Stenosis Resulting in Compromise of the Cauda Equina
Lumbar Stenosis with Cauda Equina Compromise

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzl.label: Texas District Court - Montgomery County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzl.definition: Texas District Court - Montgomery County: A court of law in Texas that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within Montgomery County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzq.label: JJ70 All other types of application not covered by the categories above (UK J-CODE)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzq.definition: All other types of application not covered by the categories above
english_labels: JJ70 All other types of application not covered by the categories above (UK J-CODE)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzr.label: Prior Inventions Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzr.definition: A Prior Inventions Clause is a contractual clause that requires an employee to disclose any inventions they have created prior to their employment with the company.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzs.label: Litigation Civil Defenses
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzs.definition: Litigation Civil Defenses are legal arguments and strategies used by a party in a civil lawsuit to defend against the claims made by the opposing party, including but not limited to, affirmative defenses, evidentiary defenses, and procedural defenses.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzv.label: Funds On Deposit Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzv.definition: A Funds On Deposit Clause is a provision in a contract that requires one party to deposit a certain amount of money with the other party as a form of security or collateral.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzv.label: Labor and Employment Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzv.definition: Law relating to the relationship between trade individuals, unions, employers and the government.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzx.label: Investment Funds
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzx.definition: Investment Funds are pooled investment vehicles that collect capital from multiple investors to invest in a diversified portfolio of assets. These funds include various types such as mutual funds, hedge funds, and real estate investment trusts (REITs), each with distinct investment strategies and regulatory structures.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RCzx.label: Gila River Indian Community of the Gila River Indian Reservation
english_labels: Gila River Indian Community of the Gila River Indian Reservation

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD01.label: Batak languages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD01.definition: The Batak languages are a group of languages that are spoken in Indonesia, primarily in the northern part of Sumatra.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD01.label: Tekirdag
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD01.definition: Tekirdag is a city in Turkey.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD03.label: Co-tenant's Share of Profits and Expenses
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD03.definition: The Co-tenant's Share of Profits and Expenses refers to the portion of profits and expenses that a co-tenant is entitled to receive or responsible for paying in relation to a property they share with others.
english_labels: Co-tenant's Share of Profits and Expenses

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD07.label: Jenin
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD07.definition: Jenin is a city located in the State of Palestine.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD07.label: Judicial Lien
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD07.definition: A judicial lien is a type of lien that is created by a court order to secure the payment of a debt or judgment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD08.label: Analysis of Cash Management Reports
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD08.definition: The concept of "Analysis of Cash Management Reports" refers to the examination and evaluation of financial reports related to the management of cash, typically performed in the context of a legal matter.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0A.label: Sliema
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0A.definition: Sliema is a locality in Malta.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0C.label: Micoud
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0C.definition: Micoud is a locality in Saint Lucia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0C.label: National Security Council
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0C.definition: A National Security Council (NSC) is usually an executive branch governmental body responsible for coordinating policy on national security issues and advising chief executives on matters related to national security.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0D.label: Rukungiri
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0D.definition: Rukungiri is a location in Uganda, which is a country in East Africa.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0E.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Union County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0E.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court in Union County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court system that has jurisdiction over minor criminal offenses and civil cases within Union County.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Union County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0F.label: Federal Housing Finance Agency
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0F.definition: The Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) is an independent federal agency created as the successor regulatory agency of the Federal Housing Finance Board (FHFB), the Office of Federal Housing Enterprise Oversight (OFHEO), and the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development government-sponsored enterprise mission team,[2] absorbing the powers and regulatory authority of both entities, with expanded legal and regulatory authority, including the ability to place government-sponsored enterprises (GSEs) into receivership or conservatorship.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0F.label: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0F.definition: The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) is a bureau of the United States Department of the Treasury that collects and analyzes information about financial transactions in order to combat domestic and international money laundering, terrorist financing, and other financial crimes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0F.label: Lao
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0F.definition: Lao (Language) refers to the written or spoken structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary specific to the Lao people and culture.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0N.label: Business Department
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0N.definition: A Business Department is a specialized functional area within an organization that focuses on specific tasks, roles, and objectives aligned with the company's broader mission. Unlike a business unit, a department usually doesn't have its own profit and loss responsibility but contributes to the overall goals and performance of the organization

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0Q.label: Formal Engagement Name
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0Q.definition: The matter name used by the actors in formal conversation or communications.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0R.label: Liability Cap Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0R.definition: A Liability Cap Clause is a provision in a contract that limits the amount of damages that can be recovered by one party from the other party in case of a breach of contract or other liability.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0S.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Wayne County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0S.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court in Wayne County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court system that handles minor criminal offenses, traffic violations, and civil cases involving amounts up to $12,000.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Wayne County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0S.label: 120 Marine (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0S.definition: Action (Admiralty or Maritime) based on service, employment, insurance or other contracts relating to maritime vessels and other maritime contractual matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0W.label: Type 1 Diabetes
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0W.definition: Type 1 diabetes is a chronic autoimmune condition where the body's immune system attacks and destroys the insulin-producing beta cells in the pancreas, leading to high blood glucose levels. It typically develops in children and young adults and requires lifelong insulin therapy for management.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0W.label: North Fork Rancheria of Mono Indians
english_labels: North Fork Rancheria of Mono Indians

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0a.label: inv_other_iso
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0a.definition: "For mixed currency situations only where it is mandated that the total tax must also be reported in a different currency ISO. This represents the ISO other than the currency used for this invoice and relates to the information provided in the fields INVOICE.inv_total_tax_other_iso and INVOICE.inv_total_net_due_other_iso. Use ISO 4217 currency codes set forth by International Standards Organization (www.iso.org.)"

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0a.label: Data Protection Regulation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0a.definition: Data Protection Regulation refers to laws and policies designed to safeguard personal and sensitive information from unauthorized access, use, disclosure, alteration, and destruction. These regulations ensure that organizations (e.g., companies, nonprofits, governments) implement appropriate measures to protect data privacy and security, complying with legal standards such as the GDPR, CCPA, and HIPAA.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0b.label: Sikh Religion
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0b.definition: The Sikh Religion, or Sikhism, is a monotheistic faith originating in the Punjab region of India in the 15th century, founded by Guru Nanak and continued by nine successive Gurus. In legal contexts, it often involves issues related to the protection of religious freedoms, the accommodation of Sikh practices such as wearing turbans and carrying kirpans, and the recognition of Sikh holidays and customs.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0e.label: Government Official
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0e.definition: A government official is an individual who holds a position of authority within a governmental organization, either elected or appointed. Their responsibilities vary widely depending on their role and the level of government they serve, but they are generally tasked with implementing laws, managing public services, and representing the interests of their constituents or the state.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0e.label: Saving Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0e.definition: A saving clause is a clause in a contract that preserves certain rights or obligations even if other parts of the contract are found to be invalid or unenforceable.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0f.label: Employee Hire Event
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0f.definition: An Employee Hire Event refers to the specific instance when an individual formally becomes an employee of a company, often marked by the signing of an employment contract and completion of onboarding processes. The official start date of employment may affect benefits, seniority, and other employment conditions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0g.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Fayette County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0g.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court in Fayette County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court system that handles minor criminal offenses, traffic violations, and civil cases involving amounts up to $12,000.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Fayette County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0k.label: Negative Pledge Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0k.definition: A "Negative Pledge Agreement" is a contractual clause or standalone agreement where a debtor promises not to encumber assets with liens, or offer them as collateral, without the consent of a specific creditor. This agreement aims to protect the unsecured creditor's interests by limiting the debtor's ability to further secure its assets to other creditors.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0o.label: Truck
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0o.definition: A truck is a motor vehicle designed to transport cargo, ranging from small pickups to large commercial trucks used for transporting goods.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0q.label: Regulation Heading
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0q.definition: Regulation Heading refers to a subcategory of Invoice Data that pertains to the specific regulations or laws that apply to the services provided and billed for in an engagement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0q.label: Mergers and Acquisitions Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0q.definition: Law dealing with companies that are purchasing and/or merging with other companies.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0r.label: Right to Encumber Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0r.definition: A Right to Encumber Clause is a provision in a contract that grants the right to create a lien or mortgage on the subject property as security for a debt or obligation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RD0u.label: Equitable Conversion Claim

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDAQ.label: Background Check
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDAQ.definition: A background check is a process through which an individual's personal, criminal, credit, and/or employment history is investigated and verified, typically by an employer, landlord, or other decision-maker. Background checks are often conducted to assess an individual's suitability for employment, housing, or other opportunities, as well as to ensure the safety and security of a workplace or community. Common elements of a background check may include verifying identity, checking criminal records, reviewing credit history, confirming education and employment history, and examining professional licenses or certifications. In many jurisdictions, background checks are regulated by laws such as the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA) to protect individual privacy and prevent discrimination.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDAU.label: Uniform Dispute Resolution Service Provider
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDAU.definition: A Uniform Dispute Resolution Service Provider (UDRSP) is an organization accredited by the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN) to administer dispute resolution proceedings for domain name disputes under the Uniform Domain-Name Dispute-Resolution Policy (UDRP). These providers facilitate the resolution of conflicts between domain name registrants and trademark owners over domain name registrations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDAV.label: E123 Other professionals

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDAe.label: Truancy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDAe.definition: Truancy refers to the act of a student intentionally and regularly missing school without a valid excuse or permission from their parents or guardians. Truancy can have legal consequences, and it is often seen as a concern because it can negatively impact a student's education and future prospects.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDAg.label: Authorization
