https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDAh.label: Meal Break Violation Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDAh.definition: A meal break violation claim is a legal action initiated by an employee against their employer for not complying with the legal requirement to provide a duty-free meal break of a certain duration during the workday. The claim typically arises when an employer either denies or interrupts the meal break, does not provide the break in accordance with applicable labor laws, or requires the employee to perform work duties during the meal break. In some cases, employers may also be liable for meal break violations if they do not compensate employees for certain types of work performed during meal breaks.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDAh.label: Appellate Filing Event
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDAh.definition: An Appellate Filing Event refers to the submission of documents or appeals to a higher court or regulatory body, challenging a lower entity's decision. In the legal realm, this involves presenting arguments and evidence to seek a review and potential reversal of the original court or regulatory body's ruling or judgment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDAq.label: Panic Disorder

These attacks are often accompanied by physical symptoms such as heart palpitations, sweating, trembling, shortness of breath, chest pain, and feelings of impending doom or loss of control.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDAt.label: Diabetes
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDAt.definition: Diabetes is a chronic health condition characterized by high levels of glucose in the blood due to the body's inability to produce or effectively use insulin. It requires ongoing management through lifestyle changes, medication, and regular monitoring to prevent complications.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDB0.label: United States Marshals Service
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDB0.definition: The United States Marshals Service (USMS) is a federal law enforcement agency within the U.S. Department of Justice. It is the oldest American federal law enforcement agency and was created by the Judiciary Act of 1789 during the presidency of George Washington as the Office of the United States Marshal. The USMS as it stands today was established in 1969 to provide guidance and assistance to Marshals throughout the federal judicial districts. USMS is an agency of the United States executive branch reporting to the United States Attorney General, but serves as the enforcement arm of the United States federal courts to ensure the effective operation of the judiciary and integrity of the Constitution.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDBx.label: Labor Management Relations Act Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDBx.definition: A Labor Management Relations Act (LMRA) claim is a legal action initiated by an employee, group of employees, or an employer, alleging that the opposing party has violated their rights or obligations under the LMRA, also known as the Taft-Hartley Act. The LMRA is a federal law enacted in 1947, amending the National Labor Relations Act (NLRA) to balance the rights and responsibilities of both employees and employers in the context of labor-management relations, and to address unfair labor practices committed by labor unions. An LMRA claim may involve issues such as union representation, collective bargaining, or the enforcement of labor contracts. These claims can be filed with the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) or pursued through the court system, depending on the nature of the alleged violation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDCX.label: Firm Business Development Personnel
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDCX.definition: Firm Business Development Personnel are professionals within a law firm or legal organization who focus on identifying and pursuing new business opportunities, expanding client relationships, and enhancing the firm's market position. They strategize and implement initiatives to attract new clients, retain existing ones, and increase the firm's revenue and growth potential.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDCa.label: Soft Tissue Cancer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDCa.definition: Soft tissue sarcoma refers to a group of malignant tumors that originate in the soft tissues of the body, including muscles, fat, blood vessels, nerves, tendons, and the lining of joints. These cancers can occur in any part of the body and often require complex treatment due to their aggressive nature and potential to spread.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDCb.label: Presentation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDCb.definition: A descriptive or persuasive account, usually made to a group (e.g., conference, committee).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDCb.label: Magazine
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDCb.definition: A Magazine is a periodical publication containing articles, stories, photographs, and advertisements, typically focusing on a particular subject or area of interest. Protected under copyright law, magazines grant publishers and contributors exclusive rights to reproduce, distribute, and display the content.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDCi.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Grant County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDCi.definition: The Indiana Circuit Court - Grant County is a specific court within the Indiana Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Grant County, Indiana.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDCk.label: Individual Person
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDCk.definition: An individual or natural person is a person that is an individual human being, as opposed to a legal person or entity, which may be a private or public organization.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDCq.label: Intervening Event - Occurs Before Signing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDCq.definition: An intervening event that occurs before signing refers to a circumstance or occurrence that takes place between the formation of a legal agreement and its execution.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDCr.label: Assignor
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDCr.definition: An assignor is a person, company or entity who transfers rights they hold to another entity. The assignor transfers to the assignee.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDD5.label: Twin-Win Certificate
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDD5.definition: A Twin-Win Certificate is a financial instrument that allows participation in the development of the underlying asset or assets, offering potential profits from both rising and falling asset values. If the underlying asset price falls but does not breach a specified barrier, it converts into profit; however, if the barrier is breached, the product converts into a tracker certificate. This instrument provides a minimum redemption equal to the nominal value, given the barrier remains intact, and with higher risk levels, multiple underlying assets (worst-of) can enable a higher bonus level or lower barrier, thereby reducing the risk compared to a direct investment in the underlying assets.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDDH.label: New York Supreme Court - Fulton County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDDN.label: Copyright Royalty Board

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDDR.label: Buyout Provisions Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDDR.definition: A Buyout Provisions Clause is a specific provision within a Buyout Clause in a legal agreement that outlines the terms and conditions for one party to buy out the other party's interest in a business or property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDDV.label: Work Capacity
english_labels: Work capacity refers to the maximum amount of work that a system, machine, or individual can handle over a specific period of time. It is often used to measure the productivity and efficiency of various aspects of a business, such as labor, machinery, or entire operational processes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDDV.label: Physician Assistant Negligence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDDV.definition: Physician Assistant Negligence refers to a legal claim of medical malpractice against a physician assistant, alleging that they failed to provide the appropriate standard of care to a patient.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDDa.label: Defined Terms Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDDa.definition: A Defined Terms Clause, also known as Definitions, is a contractual clause that provides specific meanings for terms used in a legal document.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDDb.label: Franchisor
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDDb.definition: A franchisor is a company or individual who grants a license to a third party for the conducting of a business under their brand, following a specific business model, usually in exchange for a fee or percentage of sales.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDDd.label: Complicated Fracture of an Upper Limb
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDDd.definition: A non-healing or complex fracture of an upper extremity refers to a severe fracture of the arm or shoulder that fails to heal properly or involves complicated breaks that hinder the normal healing process. Such fractures may require advanced medical treatment due to complications such as misalignment, infection, or insufficient bone regeneration.
english_labels: Complicated Fracture of an Upper Limb
Non-Healing or Complex Fracture of an Upper Extremity

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDDm.label: Duress
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDDm.definition: Duress is a legal defense that can be used in civil litigation to excuse or justify a party's actions when they were performed under the threat of harm or coercion.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDDo.label: Unlawful Restraint
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDDo.definition: The concept of Unlawful Restraint refers to the criminal offense of intentionally restricting someone's movement without their consent, and is classified as a misdemeanor offense.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDDq.label: Operational Metrics

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDDs.label: Timekeeping Management

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDEM.label: Kidney Transplant
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDEM.definition: A kidney transplant is a surgical procedure in which a healthy kidney from a donor is implanted into a patient whose kidneys have failed or are severely impaired. https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDEP.definition: An Employment Verbal Warning is an informal reprimand issued by an employer to an employee for minor misconduct or performance issues. https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDET.label: Incapacity
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDET.definition: Incapacity encompasses various conditions that hinder an individual's ability to perform tasks, make decisions, or engage in activities due to physical limitations, cognitive impairments, or emotional challenges. https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDEj.label: Voting Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDEj.definition: A Voting Agreement, also known as a Support Agreement, is a contract where shareholders agree to vote their shares in a particular manner, usually in favor of a proposed transaction or board member election. https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDEk.label: L190 Other Case Assessment, Development and Administration

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDEu.label: Regulatory Compliance

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDF2.definition: The Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) is a federally owned corporation in the United States created to provide navigation, flood control, electricity generation, fertilizer manufacturing, and economic development to the Tennessee Valley.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDF3.label: Cancer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDF3.definition: Cancer is a group of diseases characterized by the uncontrolled growth and spread of abnormal cells, which can invade and destroy healthy body tissue. https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFF.label: Liberty Clause Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFF.definition: A Liberty Clause claim is a legal assertion related to the Due Process Clauses of the Fifth and Fourteenth Amendments of the United States Constitution. These clauses prohibit the federal government (Fifth Amendment) and state governments (Fourteenth Amendment) from depriving any person of "life, liberty, or property" without due process of law. A claim involving the Liberty Clause might arise in situations where an individual argues that a government action has unduly restricted their personal freedoms without proper legal procedures or justification.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFL.label: Civil Law System
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFL.definition: Civil Law is a legal system that is primarily based on written codes and statutes, rather than case law. This system emphasizes comprehensive sets of laws that are codified and accessible, guiding judges in applying the law to individual cases.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFM.label: Travel Expense
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFM.definition: Travel Expense refers to the costs incurred by an individual or organization for transportation, lodging, meals, and other related expenses while traveling for business or other purposes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFR.label: Socialist Law System
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFR.definition: Socialist Law is a legal system that developed in communist states, primarily based on the principles of Marxism-Leninism. This system emphasizes state ownership of property, centralized planning, and the role of the state in enforcing laws that promote socialist values.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFR.label: Mortgage-Backed Securities
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFR.definition: Mortgage-Backed Securities (MBS) are investment vehicles that represent claims to the cash flows from pools of mortgage loans, primarily residential or commercial properties. Investors in MBS receive periodic payments derived from the principal and interest of the underlying mortgages, offering a means to invest in real estate without direct property ownership.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFS.label: Public Utility Liability
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFS.definition: Public Utility Liability is the legal responsibility of a utility company for any harm caused to the public due to their actions or negligence, and falls under the categories of agency and vicarious liability.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFV.label: Prisoner Trust Fund Account Statement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFV.definition: A Prisoner Trust Fund Account Statement is a financial record of an inmate's account that holds money earned or received while incarcerated, used for purchasing items from the prison commissary or for other approved expenses.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFZ.label: Arkansas Circuit Court - Lonoke Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFZ.definition: The Arkansas Circuit Court - Lonoke Cty. is a specific court within the Arkansas Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Lonoke County, Arkansas.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFa.label: Exculpatory Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFa.definition: An exculpatory clause is a type of contractual clause that releases one party from liability for certain actions or events, typically used in situations where one party is assuming a risk.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFd.label: Health Care Directive
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFd.definition: A Health Care Directive is a legal document that outlines an individual's wishes regarding medical treatment and end-of-life care in the event they become unable to make decisions for themselves.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFg.label: Mortgagee Failing to Cancel Redeemed Mortgage
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFg.definition: When a mortgagee fails to cancel a redeemed mortgage, it refers to the legal concept where a lender fails to release a borrower's property from the mortgage lien after the loan has been fully paid off, which can result in legal claims by the borrower against the lender.
english_labels: Mortgagee Failing to Cancel Redeemed Mortgage

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFg.label: 11th Amendment Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFg.definition: An Eleventh Amendment claim is a legal argument asserting that a lawsuit against a state government or its agencies violates the Eleventh Amendment of the United States Constitution, which provides states with sovereign immunity from certain types of lawsuits in federal courts. These claims typically involve disputes over whether a state has consented to be sued or if there are specific exceptions that permit the lawsuit to proceed despite the Eleventh Amendment's protections.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFh.label: Insurance Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFh.definition: Law surrounding insurance, including insurance policies and claims.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFh.label: Dispute Events
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFh.definition: Dispute Events refer to the various stages and actions that occur during a legal disagreement between parties, including but not limited to negotiations, mediations, and arbitrations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFl.label: Malignant Melanoma
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFl.definition: Malignant melanoma is an aggressive type of cancer that originates in melanocytes, the cells responsible for producing melanin, the pigment that gives skin its color. This cancer can develop in the skin, eyes (ocular melanoma), or mucosal surfaces (mucosal melanoma), and is known for its high potential to metastasize to other parts of the body.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFm.label: General Economic or Financial Conditions Language
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFm.definition: General Economic or Financial Conditions Language refers to a provision in a contract that outlines the impact of economic or financial conditions on the agreement, typically used as a carveout to a Material Adverse Effect definition.
english_labels: General Economic or Financial Conditions Language

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFn.label: Speculation Objection
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFn.definition: Speculation Objection is a legal objection raised when a question or testimony calls for an answer based on conjecture or guesswork rather than personal knowledge or facts. It is used to prevent witnesses from providing opinions or conclusions without a proper foundation

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFo.label: Appearance
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFo.definition: Appearance refers to a litigation event where a party or their representative appears before a court or tribunal.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFt.label: Motion for New Trial - Jury's Passion or Prejudice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFt.definition: A Motion for New Trial - Jury's Passion or Prejudice is a legal request made by a party to a case asking the court to grant a new trial due to the jury being influenced by emotions or biases rather than the evidence presented.
english_labels: Motion for New Trial - Jury's Passion or Prejudice

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFv.label: Limited Partnership
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFv.definition: A Limited Partnership is a business entity that consists of one or more General Partners and one or more Limited Partners. The General Partner may be an individual or an entity, such as a corporation. Typically, the General Partners are liable for any and all of the company's financial obligations, while the Limited Partners possess no liability for the company's debts, obligations or actions. General Partners usually possess all the rights and responsibilities of managing the business entity, including all of its activities and financial matters. They also hold general liability for the debts, obligations, and activities of the Limited Partnership.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFy.label: Railway Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDFy.definition: Law that concerns railways and associated legal and business concerns.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDG1.label: Experience Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDG1.definition: Experience Management is the process of capturing, sharing, and utilizing knowledge gained through practical application and personal involvement, within the broader context of Knowledge Management.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDG2.label: Release of Claims Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDG2.definition: A Release of Claims Clause is a legal provision that releases one party from any future claims or liabilities related to a specific matter, typically included in a contract or settlement agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDG5.label: Georgia District Court - Bacon County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDG5.definition: Georgia District Court - Bacon County: A court of law in the state of Georgia that has jurisdiction over legal cases within Bacon County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDG5.label: Civil Cover Sheet
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDG5.definition: A Civil Cover Sheet is a document used in trial court practice to provide basic information about a civil case, such as the parties involved and the nature of the case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDG7.label: Emotional Incapacity
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDG7.definition: Emotional incapacity refers to an individual's inability to manage or cope with their emotions effectively, often resulting in difficulty forming or maintaining relationships, making decisions, or participating in daily activities. Emotional incapacity may be considered in certain legal contexts, such as family law or mental health-related cases, to assess a person's competence or decision-making abilities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGD.label: UTBMS Codes
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGD.definition: A standardized set of codes used to classify legal services and expenses, with specific subcategories for litigation, mergers and acquisitions, and UK-based services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGE.label: New York Supreme Court - Queens County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGE.definition: The New York Supreme Court - Queens County is a court of general jurisdiction located in Queens County, New York, with authority to hear and decide a wide range of legal disputes.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - Queens County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGI.label: Bulgarian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGI.definition: Bulgarian (Language) is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary used in Bulgaria and by Bulgarian speakers worldwide.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGI.label: Individual Health Insurance Plan
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGI.definition: This is a health insurance policy purchased by an individual independently of an employer or government program. Coverage and costs vary widely depending on the plan chosen and the needs of the individual.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGL.label: Solicitation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGL.definition: The concept of Solicitation refers to the act of encouraging, requesting, or commanding another person to commit a crime, with the intent that the crime be committed.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGO.label: Inventory
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGO.definition: Inventory refers to the goods or materials that a business holds for the ultimate purpose of resale or production.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGR.label: Direct-Examination of Witness
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGR.definition: The Direct-Examination of Witness is a legal practice that involves questioning a witness by the party who called them to testify, in order to elicit testimony that supports their case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGU.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Perry County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGU.definition: The Indiana Circuit Court - Perry County is a specific court within the Indiana Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Perry County, Indiana.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGU.label: Professional Association
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGU.definition: A Professional Association is an organization founded and operated by professionals who share a common field of expertise or occupation. The association promotes standards, offers networking opportunities, and provides various professional development resources to its members.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGd.label: Tax Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGd.definition: Federal, State, and Local tax laws.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGf.label: Judeo-Arabic
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGf.definition: Judeo-Arabic is a language that combines elements of Arabic and Hebrew and is used primarily by Jewish communities in Arabic-speaking regions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGj.label: Podiatry Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGj.definition: Podiatry Malpractice refers to a type of medical malpractice claim that arises from the negligence or wrongdoing of a podiatrist in the treatment of a patient's foot or ankle.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGq.label: Technical Analysis
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGq.definition: Technical Analysis refers to the process of examining and evaluating technical data and information in order to draw conclusions and make recommendations in the context of a legal matter, and is a subcategory of Fact Investigation and Development.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGs.label: Direct Public Offering Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGs.definition: A Direct Public Offering (DPO) is a financial instrument that allows a company to offer its shares directly to the public, often without the need for intermediaries like underwriters or brokers. Unlike traditional Initial Public Offerings (IPOs), a DPO bypasses many of the costly fees and requirements, enabling smaller companies to raise capital more directly from individual investors.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGw.label: Reserved for local use
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGw.definition: Reserved for local use (Language): A term or label that is specific to a particular jurisdiction or organization and is not commonly used outside of that context, within the framework of language as a system of communication.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGx.label: Penis Cancer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGx.definition: Penis cancer is a malignant tumor originating in the tissues of the penis, typically starting in the skin cells or the internal structures of the penis. It can present with symptoms such as growths or sores on the penis, unusual discharge, and bleeding, often requiring treatments such as surgery, radiation therapy, and chemotherapy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGz.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Berks County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDGz.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court located in Berks County, responsible for administering proceedings related to minor criminal offenses, traffic violations, and civil disputes within its jurisdiction.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Berks County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDH4.label: Georgia Superior Court - Baldwin County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDH4.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Baldwin County is a specific court within the Georgia Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Baldwin County, Georgia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDH4.label: Out-Of-Town Travel Expense
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDH4.definition: Expenses incurred by an individual while traveling outside of their usual place of business, which may include transportation, lodging, meals, and other related costs.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDH6.label: Zoning Ordinance
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDH6.definition: A Zoning Ordinance is a set of legal regulations adopted by municipal or other local government bodies that specifies the types of land use permitted within certain geographic areas. The ordinance usually includes zoning maps and text detailing the land use regulations for different zones, such as residential, commercial, industrial, and other specialized categories.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDH9.label: Description of Assets in Controversy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDH9.definition: For a given dispute, a description of the assets that are potentially exposed or subject to recovery.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHJ.label: Originating Matter
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHJ.definition: An originating matter refers to a legal case or issue that originates or is initiated within a particular law firm or jurisdiction. This term is used to distinguish cases that are started by the firm from those that are transferred or referred from other sources.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHJ.label: New York Supreme Court - Delaware County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHJ.definition: The New York Supreme Court - Delaware County is a court of general jurisdiction located in Delaware County, New York, which is a subordinate court of the New York Supreme Court.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - Delaware County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHL.label: Tax Total Detail Fees
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHL.definition: Tax Total Detail Fees refers to the specific fees associated with tax details within an engagement for providing legal services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHO.label: Claim for Falling on Mopped Waxed Floor
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHO.definition: A claim for falling on a mopped waxed floor is a legal action brought by an individual who has suffered injury or harm as a result of slipping and falling on a floor that has been recently mopped and waxed.
english_labels: Claim for Falling on Mopped Waxed Floor

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHQ.label: Bankruptcy Petition
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHQ.definition: A Bankruptcy Petition is a formal request submitted to a court by an individual or entity seeking relief from their debts and financial obligations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHT.label: Masai
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHT.definition: A language spoken by the Masai people of East Africa, characterized by its use of clicks and traditionally used in oral storytelling and communication.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHU.label: South Carolina Executive Department - Office of the Governor
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHU.definition: The South Carolina Executive Department - Office of the Governor is a government entity responsible for administering the executive branch of the South Carolina state government.
english_labels: South Carolina Executive Department - Office of the Governor

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHU.label: Professional Development Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHU.definition: Professional Development Management refers to the process of planning, implementing, and evaluating activities that enhance the knowledge, skills, and abilities of individuals in a professional setting, specifically in the context of managing the development of employees.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHX.label: Oregon Circuit Court - Harney County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHX.definition: The Oregon Circuit Court - Harney County is a specific court within the Oregon Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Harney County, Oregon.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHX.label: Statement of Non-Opposition
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHX.definition: A Statement of Non-Opposition is a legal document filed in bankruptcy and restructuring cases indicating that a party does not object to a proposed action or motion.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHX.label: Trust (Emotion)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHX.definition: Trust is an emotion based on the belief in the reliability, truth, or ability of someone or something, often associated with a sense of security and confidence.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHY.label: Register of Deeds
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHY.definition: A public official who records deeds, mortgages, and other instruments affecting real property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHa.label: Notice of Loss
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHa.definition: In disputes, the date where a claimant gives notice of the claimant's loss.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHf.label: New York City Court - Canandaigua
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHf.definition: A court located in Canandaigua, New York that operates under the jurisdiction of the New York City Court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHf.label: Alternative Dispute Resolution Events
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHf.definition: Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) Events refer to the events or phases involved in resolving legal disputes outside of traditional litigation, including arbitration and mediation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHh.label: Liability Auto Insurance Coverage Policy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHh.definition: Liability auto insurance provides coverage for bodily injury and property damage inflicted on others in an accident for which the insured is at fault. It does not cover damages to the insured's own vehicle or medical expenses for the insured. This type of coverage is generally mandatory in most U.S. states.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHj.label: Malayalam
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHj.definition: Malayalam is a written or spoken structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary, and is a member of the Language top-level class.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHq.label: Client Administrator
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHq.definition: The law department's administrator for a given matter.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHv.label: Groundwater Contamination Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHv.definition: A groundwater contamination claim is a legal action seeking compensation for damages caused by the pollution of underground water sources, falling under the category of environmental law claims.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHx.label: New Mexico Magistrate Court - Sandoval County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHx.definition: A court located in Sandoval County, New Mexico that has limited jurisdiction over certain types of cases.
english_labels: New Mexico Magistrate Court - Sandoval County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHx.label: New York Supreme Court - Dutchess County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHx.definition: The New York Supreme Court - Dutchess County is a court of general jurisdiction located in Dutchess County, New York, with authority to hear and decide a wide range of legal disputes.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - Dutchess County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHx.label: Motion to Quash Subpoena
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHx.definition: A Motion to Quash Subpoena is a legal request to invalidate or nullify a subpoena that has been issued by a court or other legal authority, typically on the grounds that it is overly broad, unduly burdensome, or otherwise improper.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHy.label: Georgia Superior Court - Stewart County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHy.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Stewart County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Stewart County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHy.label: Arkansas Circuit Court - Hempstead Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDHy.definition: The Arkansas Circuit Court - Hempstead Cty. is a specific court within the Arkansas Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Hempstead County, Arkansas.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDI1.label: ODR - Human Facilitation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDI1.definition: ODR - Human Facilitation refers to the process of resolving disputes online with the assistance of a human facilitator, within the context of an Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) Forum.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDI3.label: Title to Property
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDI3.definition: Title to property refers to the legal ownership and right to use, possess, and transfer a particular piece of property, whether real estate or personal property. Holding the title signifies that the person or entity has recognized rights and interests in that property, often evidenced by a deed or similar document.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDI5.label: Misstatement of Evidence Objection
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDI5.definition: A Misstatement of Evidence Objection is raised when a party in a legal proceeding believes that the opposing counsel or a witness has inaccurately represented the evidence on record. This objection seeks to ensure that the evidence is accurately portrayed and understood by courts, factfinders, and decisionmakers.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDI9.label: Intentional Interference with Prospective Business Relationship
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDI9.definition: Intentional Interference with Prospective Business Relationship: A tort where a third party intentionally disrupts a business relationship that is likely to occur, causing economic harm to the plaintiff.
english_labels: Intentional Interference with Prospective Business Relationship

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDID.label: Bulletin
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDID.definition: A Bulletin, also known as a Newsletter, is a periodic publication distributed to a specific audience, providing news, updates, and information relevant to the readers.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDIE.label: Georgia District Court - McIntosh County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDIE.definition: A court located in McIntosh County, Georgia that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographic area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDIO.label: Santa Rosa Band of Cahuilla Indians
english_labels: Santa Rosa Band of Cahuilla Indians

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDIT.label: Antitrust - Vertical Price Fixing Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDIT.definition: An allegation of illegal collusion between parties at different levels of a supply chain to set prices for goods or services, in violation of antitrust laws.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDIT.label: Matter Total Detail Fees
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDIT.definition: Matter Total Detail Fees refers to the specific fees associated with a particular legal matter, including all costs and expenses incurred in providing legal services, as defined within the context of Engagement Terms.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDIT.label: Executor Plaintiff
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDIT.definition: An executor of an estate who is also the plaintiff in a legal matter.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDIc.label: Enforceability Representation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDIc.definition: Enforceability Representation: A statement made in a legal agreement that assures the parties involved that the terms of the agreement can be enforced by law.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDId.label: Georgia Superior Court - Decatur County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDId.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Decatur County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDIg.label: Unemployment Benefits Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDIg.definition: Unemployment benefits refer to those benefits given by the government to unemployed persons.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDIh.label: Compact Clause Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDIh.definition: A Compact Clause claim is a legal argument asserting that a particular agreement or compact between states or between a state and a foreign power violates the Compact Clause of the United States Constitution. This claim contends that the agreement or compact exceeds the scope of authority granted by the Compact Clause, which requires congressional approval for interstate compacts that impact the balance of power between states or have implications for federal supremacy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDIh.label: Motion for Appointment of Pro Bono Counsel
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDIh.definition: A Motion for Appointment of Pro Bono Counsel is a formal request made to the court by a party who cannot afford an attorney, asking the court to appoint a volunteer lawyer to represent them in the case.
english_labels: Motion for Appointment of Pro Bono Counsel

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDIn.label: Massachusetts Superior Court - Middlesex County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDIn.definition: The Massachusetts Superior Court - Middlesex County is a court of general jurisdiction in Massachusetts that hears civil and criminal cases within Middlesex County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDIu.label: Procedural Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDIu.definition: Procedural Claims are legal claims that relate to the process of a lawsuit, such as jurisdiction, venue, or intervention, rather than the substantive issues of the case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDIw.label: Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDIw.definition: An economic branch that produces a related set of raw materials, goods, or services (e.g., Agriculture Industry, Pharmaceuticals Industry).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJ5.label: Undersecured Creditor
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJ5.definition: An Undersecured Creditor is a lender whose collateral value securing a loan is less than the outstanding debt owed by the borrower. This situation often arises in bankruptcy contexts, affecting the creditor’s ability to fully recover the loan amount through collateral liquidation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJ9.label: Motion to Dismiss for Lack of Subject Matter Jurisdiction
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJ9.definition: A Motion to Dismiss for Lack of Subject Matter Jurisdiction is a legal request to terminate a case due to the court lacking the authority to hear and decide on the specific legal matter at hand.
english_labels: Motion to Dismiss for Lack of Subject Matter Jurisdiction

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJG.label: Official Immunity
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJG.definition: Official Immunity: Legal protection granted to government officials from being held personally liable for actions taken in the course of their official duties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJG.label: Kansas District Court - Labette County, Oswego
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJG.definition: A court located in Labette County, Oswego, Kansas that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical area.
english_labels: Kansas District Court - Labette County, Oswego

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJH.label: Travel Document Valid From
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJH.definition: The "Travel Document Valid From" date indicates the starting date from which a travel document such as a passport or visa becomes legally valid for use. This date may differ from the issued date and marks the beginning of the period during which the holder is authorized to travel under the conditions specified by the document

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJK.label: Post-Petition Transfer Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJK.definition: A post-petition transfer claim is a type of avoidance action claim in bankruptcy law that seeks to recover property or assets transferred by a debtor after the filing of a bankruptcy petition.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJM.label: Limitations
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJM.definition: The concept of Limitations refers to the legal time constraints that restrict the period within which a party can bring a claim or defense in a civil litigation matter, including statutes of repose, frauds, and limitations, equitable tolling, and laches.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJP.label: Airplane
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJP.definition: An Airplane is a powered fixed-wing aircraft that achieves flight through the use of forward thrust and aerodynamic lift. It typically has a fuselage, wings, and one or more engines, and is designed for transporting passengers, cargo, or both.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJU.label: Substantive Due Process Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJU.definition: A substantive due process claim is a legal action initiated by an individual or entity alleging that their fundamental rights, as protected by the Due Process Clauses of the Fifth and Fourteenth Amendments of the United States Constitution, have been violated by the government or a government actor. Substantive due process protects individuals from arbitrary or unreasonable government actions that infringe on fundamental rights, even if proper procedures were followed. A substantive due process claim may arise in various contexts, such as when a government body enacts a law or regulation that unduly restricts a fundamental right (e.g., the right to privacy, the right to marry, or the right to make decisions about family matters) or when a government actor takes an arbitrary or irrational action that infringes on an individual's rights.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJW.label: Georgia District Court - Dougherty County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJW.definition: A court located in Dougherty County, Georgia that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJW.label: Joy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJW.definition: Joy is an emotion of great pleasure or happiness, often resulting from success, good fortune, or a sense of well-being.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJY.label: Wrongful Discharge or Termination
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJY.definition: The concept of Wrongful Discharge or Termination refers to the illegal firing or dismissal of an employee by an employer, in violation of the law or employment contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJc.label: Supplemental Jurisdiction
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJc.definition: Supplemental Jurisdiction refers to the authority of a court to hear and decide on claims that are related to the original claim, but may not fall under the court's primary jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJc.label: Motion for Royalty
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJc.definition: A Motion for Royalty is a formal request made to a trial court for compensation or ongoing payment for the use of intellectual property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJd.label: Contact Full Name
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJd.definition: Contact Full Name refers to the complete legal name of an individual serving as a point of contact in professional or business interactions. This often includes the person's first name, middle name or initial, and last name, and is used for formal documentation and communication.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJg.label: Interactive Media
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJg.definition: Interactive Media refers to digital content that requires user interaction to deliver its content, such as video games, virtual reality experiences, and interactive websites. Protected under copyright law, interactive media grants the creators exclusive rights to reproduce, distribute, and display the content.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJp.label: Proceeding Transferred Into This Dispute Forum
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJp.definition: The concept of "Case Transferred Into This Dispute Forum" refers to a legal matter that has been moved from another forum to the current forum for resolution, and is currently open or pending.
english_labels: Case Transferred Into This Dispute Forum
Proceeding Transferred Into This Dispute Forum

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJq.label: Warranty
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJq.definition: A Warranty is a promise or guarantee provided by a manufacturer or seller to the buyer concerning the quality, condition, or functionality of a product for a specified period. If the product fails to meet the stipulated conditions during the warranty period, the manufacturer or seller is obliged to repair, replace, or refund the product.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJr.label: Minangkabau
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJr.definition: A language spoken in the Minangkabau region of Indonesia, characterized by its unique matrilineal culture and use of a modified Arabic script.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJr.label: D.C. Board on Professional Responsibility
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJr.definition: The D.C. Board on Professional Responsibility is a disciplinary body within the District of Columbia Courts that oversees the conduct of lawyers practicing in the District of Columbia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJs.label: Crewmember Visa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJs.definition: A Crewmember Visa is a specific type of visa issued to individuals who work on board a sea vessel or international airline, such as pilots, flight attendants, or ship crew members. This visa allows the holder to enter and stay in a foreign country for a limited period, strictly for the purpose of joining, working on, or disembarking from their vessel or aircraft.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJv.label: Failure to Yield to Pedestrian Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJv.definition: A Pedestrian Right-of-Way Violation Claim involves allegations that a driver has failed to yield the right-of-way to pedestrians under circumstances where pedestrians are legally prioritized, such as crosswalks or signals.
english_labels: Failure to Yield to Pedestrian Claim

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJw.label: Liquor Law Violations
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJw.definition: The violation of laws or ordinances prohibiting the manufacture, sale, purchase, transportation, possession, or use of alcoholic beverages.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJx.label: Impression Evidence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJx.definition: Impression evidence refers to marks, patterns, or imprints left on surfaces that can be studied and analyzed to derive information about the object or tool that made them. Examples include shoeprints, tire treads, and tool marks. Such evidence can be instrumental in criminal investigations, as it can link a particular object or individual to a crime scene. Detailed analysis of these impressions can reveal unique characteristics or wear patterns that can be matched to specific sources.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJy.label: Best Interest of the Child Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJy.definition: A Best Interest of the Child Claim is a legal argument presented in family court, typically during custody or visitation disputes, where one party asserts that a particular custody arrangement or decision serves the child's best interests. This claim focuses on the child's welfare and well-being, considering factors such as their emotional, physical, and educational needs, the stability of each parent's home, and their relationship with both parents. Courts prioritize the best interests of the child when making custody and visitation determinations to ensure their safety and well-being.
english_labels: Best Interest of the Child Claim

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJy.label: Enurement Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJy.definition: An Enurement Clause is a provision in a contract that ensures the benefits or obligations of the contract extend to third parties who were not originally parties to the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJy.label: Fixed Costs
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDJy.definition: Fixed costs are expenses that do not change regardless of the business's production levels or service levels. Examples include rent, salaries of permanent staff, and insurance premiums, and these costs are incurred even if the business has zero output.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDK0.label: Legislative Proceedings
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDK0.definition: Legislative Proceedings refer to the formal discussions and decision-making processes carried out by a governing body, such as a parliament or congress, in order to create or amend laws.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDK1.label: Application for Order Waiving Requirement for Business Evaluation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDK1.definition: An Application for Order Waiving Requirement for Business Evaluation is a legal document submitted in bankruptcy proceedings requesting exemption from the requirement to evaluate the debtor's business.
english_labels: Application for Order Waiving Requirement for Business Evaluation

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDK1.label: Service
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDK1.definition: The legal work performed, usually by a Legal Services Provider, in the course of a legal matter.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDK1.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Susquehanna County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDK1.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Susquehanna County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering legal proceedings in Susquehanna County, Pennsylvania.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Susquehanna County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDK3.label: Labor and Delivery Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDK3.definition: Negligent or improper medical care provided during the process of childbirth, resulting in harm or injury to the mother or child, falling under the category of medical malpractice claims.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDK3.label: Last Will and Testament
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDK3.definition: A Last Will and Testament is a legal document that outlines a person's wishes for the distribution of their property and assets after their death, and is a type of Trusts and Estate Planning Document.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDK6.label: Squash
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDK6.definition: Squash refers to a diverse group of fruit vegetables from the Cucurbitaceae family, known for their various shapes, sizes, and flavors. They are categorized into summer and winter types, and are valued for their culinary versatility, nutritional benefits, including vitamins A and C, fiber, and antioxidants.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDK6.label: Tax Law Regulatory Objectives
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDK6.definition: Tax law regulatory objectives encompass the fundamental principles and considerations surrounding taxation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDKA.label: Registered Securities
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDKA.definition: Registered Securities are financial instruments recorded in the name of the owner on the books of the issuer or the issuer's registrar. Normally, these securities can only be transferred to another owner when endorsed by the registered owner, ensuring a clear record of ownership.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDKB.label: Testimonial Evidence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDKB.definition: Testimonial Evidence is a type of evidence that is presented in the form of a witness's oral or written statement under oath, which is offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted. This evidence is based on the witness's personal knowledge or experience and is subject to cross-examination by the opposing party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDKG.label: Anxiety and Obsessive-Compulsive Disorders
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDKG.definition: Anxiety and Obsessive-Compulsive Disorders are characterized by excessive anxiety, worry, apprehension, and fear, or by avoidance of feelings, thoughts, activities, objects, places, or people. Symptoms and signs may include restlessness, difficulty concentrating, hyper-vigilance, muscle tension, sleep disturbance, fatigue, panic attacks, obsessions and compulsions, constant thoughts and fears about safety, and frequent physical complaints.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDKH.label: Foster Care
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDKH.definition: Foster care is a system in which a minor has been placed into a ward, group home, or private home of a state-certified caregiver, referred to as a "foster parent". This placement is often arranged through the government or a social service agency, usually due to the child's home environment being deemed unsafe or unsuitable.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDKJ.label: Statute of Limitations
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDKJ.definition: A Statute of Limitations is a legal defense that sets a specific time limit for bringing a lawsuit or criminal charges, after which the claim or charges cannot be pursued.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDKN.label: Motion for Turnover of Property
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDKN.definition: A Motion for Turnover of Property is a legal request made in a bankruptcy case, asking the court to order the transfer of specific property from the debtor to the trustee or creditor.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDKS.label: Domain Name Dispute Resolution Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDKS.definition: Domain Name Dispute Resolution Practice refers to the set of procedures and guidelines followed to resolve conflicts over domain name registrations. This practice typically involves arbitration or mediation processes under policies like the Uniform Domain-Name Dispute-Resolution Policy (UDRP) to address issues such as cybersquatting and trademark infringement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDKZ.label: Teen Market Segment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDKZ.definition: The teen market segment refers to a division of the market that is specifically targeted towards teenagers as consumers. This segment encompasses products, services, and marketing strategies that are designed to cater to the unique needs, preferences, and interests of teenagers, taking into account factors such as social trends, lifestyle choices, and identity exploration.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDKa.label: Oregon Circuit Court - Hood River County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDKa.definition: Oregon Circuit Court - Hood River County: A specific court within the Oregon Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Hood River County.
english_labels: Oregon Circuit Court - Hood River County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDKb.label: Adverse Co-Party
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDKb.definition: A co-party in a litigation or transactional matter who, although formally aligned on the same side (such as co-plaintiffs or co-defendants), is acting contrary to the interests of a specific client in the same proceeding or deal. This adverse action may involve conflicting positions, strategies, or goals within the shared matter.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDKk.label: Havasupai Tribe of the Havasupai Reservation
english_labels: Havasupai Tribe of the Havasupai Reservation

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDKm.label: Remedies in Property Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDKm.definition: Remedies in Property Law are legal actions or procedures used to enforce property rights and resolve disputes over property ownership or possession. Each remedy (e.g., foreclosure, seizure, attachment) serves to protect the interests of the property holder or creditor and is governed by specific laws and regulations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDKp.label: Georgia District Court - Fayette County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDKp.definition: Georgia District Court - Fayette County: A court of law in the state of Georgia with jurisdiction over legal cases within Fayette County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDL0.label: California Court of Appeal - 4th Dist.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDL0.definition: The California Court of Appeal - 4th Dist. is a specific division of the California Court of Appeal that hears appeals from trial courts in the fourth appellate district of California.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDL7.label: Large Language Model
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDL7.definition: A Large Language Model (LLM) is a class of language models that utilize deep learning algorithms and are trained on extensive textual datasets, often spanning multiple terabytes in size. While most LLMs can generate text, some are designed to form compressed representations of inputs for tasks like classification or question answering.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLA.label: Urdu
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLA.definition: Urdu (Language) is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary, primarily spoken in Pakistan and India.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLA.label: Motion to Extend Time to File Appellee Designation of Reporters Transcript
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLA.definition: A request made to the appellate court to allow additional time for the appellee to submit the designated reporters' transcript.
english_labels: Motion to Extend Time to File Appellee Designation of Reporters Transcript

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLA.label: Self-Defense
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLA.definition: Self-defense is a legal doctrine that allows an individual to use reasonable force to protect themselves or others from imminent physical harm or danger. It is generally considered a justifiable defense in criminal cases when a person believes they are facing a genuine threat and uses force in a proportionate and necessary manner to defend themselves.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLC.label: Altaic languages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLC.definition: A group of languages including Turkish, Mongolian, and Manchu, among others, that share certain grammatical and phonetic features and are primarily spoken in Central Asia and parts of Eastern Europe.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLE.label: URL of Legal Services Provider
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLE.definition: A URL of Legal Services Provider is a web address that identifies an organization providing legal services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLI.label: Auctioneer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLI.definition: A person who sells goods at a public auction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLJ.label: Frustration of Purpose Doctrine
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLJ.definition: The Frustration of Purpose Doctrine is a legal defense in civil litigation that allows a party to be excused from performing their contractual obligations when an unforeseen event occurs that completely undermines the purpose of the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLO.label: Attached Hereto Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLO.definition: A clause in a contract that specifies certain documents or items that are attached to and made a part of the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLP.label: Angika
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLP.definition: Angika is a language that is a member of the Language top-level class and is spoken in the Indian state of Bihar.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLQ.label: Georgia Superior Court - Jones County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLQ.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Jones County, Georgia, with authority over civil and criminal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLQ.label: Chapter 13 Bankruptcy Plan
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLQ.definition: A Chapter 13 Bankruptcy Plan is a legal document that outlines a debtor's proposed repayment plan to creditors under Chapter 13 bankruptcy, which allows individuals with regular income to reorganize their debts and keep their property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLS.label: Aleut
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLS.definition: Aleut (Language) is a structured system of communication spoken by the Aleut people, which belongs to the Language top-level class in the context of legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLT.label: 535 Death Penalty (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLT.definition: Action by a federal or state prisoner challenging a death sentence.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLX.label: Petition for Visa for Intermittent Intra-Company Transferee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLX.definition: The "Petition for Visa for Intermittent Intra-Company Transferee" typically refers to the L-1 visa category in the United States. This visa is used for employees who work in a managerial, executive, or specialized knowledge capacity and are being transferred within the same company from a foreign office to a U.S. office on an intermittent basis. The employer must file a Form I-129 petition with U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) to seek approval for the L-1 visa
english_labels: Petition for Visa for Intermittent Intra-Company Transferee

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLd.label: Chignik Bay Tribal Council (Native Village of Chignik)
english_labels: Chignik Bay Tribal Council (Native Village of Chignik)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLm.label: Insurance Representation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLm.definition: Insurance Representation is a provision in merger and acquisition agreements where the selling party confirms the existence, sufficiency, and status of insurance policies held by the target entity. This representation assures the buyer that the target has adequate insurance coverage in place to protect against potential liabilities or losses, and that there are no material lapses or issues with these policies.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLo.label: Co-Branding Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLo.definition: A co-branding agreement is a legal contract between two or more companies that outlines the terms and conditions of a joint marketing campaign or product collaboration.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLr.label: Debtor's Certification in Support of Discharge
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLr.definition: A Debtor's Certification in Support of Discharge is a document filed in a bankruptcy case by the debtor, attesting to the accuracy of the information provided in the bankruptcy petition and supporting documents.
english_labels: Debtor's Certification in Support of Discharge

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLu.label: UTBMS MC00 Due Diligence and Disclosure Schedules
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLu.definition: A category within the UTBMS Mergers and Acquisitions (M&A) class that pertains to the due diligence and disclosure schedules involved in such transactions.
english_labels: UTBMS MC00 Due Diligence and Disclosure Schedules

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDLw.label: Yankton Sioux Tribe of South Dakota
english_labels: Yankton Sioux Tribe of South Dakota

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDM0.label: Warehouseman or Carrier Liability for Goods
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDM0.definition: The legal responsibility of a warehouseman or carrier for the goods they are holding or transporting, which falls under the broader category of agent liability.
english_labels: Warehouseman or Carrier Liability for Goods

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDM1.label: Hungarian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDM1.definition: A language spoken in Hungary and by Hungarian communities worldwide.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDM2.label: Michigan District Court - Wayne County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDM2.definition: Michigan District Court - Wayne County: A court of limited jurisdiction in the state of Michigan that handles civil and criminal cases within Wayne County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDM4.label: Issuer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDM4.definition: An issuer is a legal entity that develops, registers and sells securities to finance its operations. Issuers may be corporations, investment trusts, or domestic or foreign governments.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDM5.label: Request for Evidence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDM5.definition: A Request for Evidence (RFE) in the context of immigration is a document issued by the government agency (e.g., United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS)) when an immigration application or petition lacks sufficient evidence or documentation. The RFE requests additional information or documentation from the applicant or petitioner to make a decision on the case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMC.label: Probate due to Neglect/Abandonment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMC.definition: Probate due to Neglect/Abandonment refers to the legal process of distributing the assets of a deceased person who died without a will or heirs due to neglect or abandonment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMD.label: General Representations and Warranties
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMD.definition: A General Representation and Warranty is a statement made by a party in a legal matter that asserts the truthfulness and accuracy of certain facts or conditions, without any specific limitations or exceptions, and which may be subject to a Material Adverse Effect (MAE) Qualification.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMH.label: Washington Superior Court - Wahkiakum County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMH.definition: Washington Superior Court - Wahkiakum County refers to a specific court within the Washington Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Wahkiakum County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMI.label: Mental Health Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMI.definition: Mental health claims involve legal processes related to an individual's psychological well-being, often concerning the need for treatment or intervention. Commitments to mental health facilities can be voluntary, where an individual willingly seeks treatment, or involuntary, where an individual is mandated to receive treatment due to potential harm to themselves or others, based on legal criteria and professional assessments.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMJ.label: Trespassing Livestock Causing Harm
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMJ.definition: The concept of Trespassing Livestock Causing Harm refers to the legal claim that arises when someone's animals enter another person's property without permission and cause damage or injury.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMN.label: Obscenity
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMN.definition: Obscenity refers to a criminal offense that involves the distribution or display of materials that are considered offensive or indecent according to community standards.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMS.label: Jaywalking Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMS.definition: A Jaywalking Claim involves allegations that a pedestrian has violated traffic regulations by crossing a street outside of designated crosswalks or against traffic signals, creating potential hazards for both themselves and motorists.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMT.label: Use of Premises Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMT.definition: The Use of Premises Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the permitted use of a specific property or space by the tenant or lessee.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMT.label: 861 HIA (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMT.definition: Action filed with regard to social security benefits associated with Health Insurance Part A Medicare

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMU.label: Ulcerative Colitis
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMU.definition: Ulcerative colitis is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease characterized by inflammation and ulceration of the lining of the colon and rectum. This condition primarily affects the mucosal layer, leading to symptoms such as abdominal pain, diarrhea with blood or pus, and weight loss, and may require ongoing medical treatment or surgical intervention, such as colectomy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMU.label: Motion to Exclude Testimony
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMU.definition: A Motion to Exclude Testimony is a formal request made to a court to prevent certain testimony from being presented as evidence during a trial or hearing.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMU.label: Lease Obligations
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMU.definition: Lease Obligations refer to the financial and contractual responsibilities that a lessee must fulfill as part of a lease agreement. These often include timely payment of rent, adherence to maintenance and use provisions, and compliance with any terms for lease termination or renewal

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMi.label: Buyer In Breach Liable for Real Estate Broker's Commission
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMi.definition: If a buyer fails to fulfill their obligations under a real estate contract, they may be held responsible for paying the commission owed to the broker who facilitated the sale.
english_labels: Buyer In Breach Liable for Real Estate Broker's Commission

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMl.label: Life Insurance Policy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMl.definition: A life insurance policy is a contract between an insurance company and a policyholder that provides a financial payout to designated beneficiaries upon the death of the insured individual. The policy often requires the payment of regular premiums in exchange for the death benefit, and may include other features like investment growth or cash value.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMl.label: Florida Circuit Court - Holmes County - 14th Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMl.definition: A court located in Holmes County, Florida that is part of the larger Florida Circuit Court system.
english_labels: Florida Circuit Court - Holmes County - 14th Circuit Court

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMm.label: Escrow Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMm.definition: An Escrow Agreement is a legal contract between two parties where a third party holds and manages assets or funds until the conditions of the agreement are met.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMm.label: Trustworthy AI
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMm.definition: Trustworthy AI is an AI system characterized by three main components: (1) it must be lawful, ensuring compliance with all applicable laws and regulations, (2) it should be ethical, demonstrating respect for and adherence to ethical principles and values, and (3) it should be robust, both technically and socially, to prevent unintentional harm. Trustworthy AI concerns the trustworthiness of the AI system itself and includes all processes and actors involved in the AI system's life cycle, emphasizing respect for human rights and democratic values.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMo.label: Current Financial Obligations
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMo.definition: Current Financial Obligations, also known as Current Liabilities, are debts or obligations that a company is expected to settle within one fiscal year or operating cycle, whichever is longer. These can include accounts payable, short-term loans, and other debts that are due within a short timeframe, and they are listed on a company's balance sheet.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMr.label: Florida Circuit Court - Pinellas County - 6th Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMr.definition: A court located in Pinellas County, Florida that is part of the larger Florida Circuit Court system.
english_labels: Florida Circuit Court - Pinellas County - 6th Circuit Court

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMv.label: Mootness
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDMv.definition: Mootness refers to a legal principle where a case is deemed irrelevant because it no longer presents an ongoing issue, or the parties involved no longer have a legally recognizable interest in the outcome. When a case becomes moot, courts generally dismiss it, as there is no longer a "live" controversy to resolve

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDN1.label: Forward-looking MAE Standard - "Could reasonably be expected to" Language
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDN1.definition: A Forward-looking MAE Standard with "Could reasonably be expected to" Language is a legal concept that refers to a standard used in contracts to determine whether a particular event or circumstance could reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on a party's business, financial condition, or operations.
english_labels: Forward-looking MAE Standard - "Could reasonably be expected to" Language

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDN7.label: Negligent Retention
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDN7.definition: The concept of Negligent Retention refers to a legal claim that an employer was negligent in retaining an employee who they knew or should have known posed a risk of harm to others.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDN7.label: Total Tax on Fees
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDN7.definition: The Total Tax on Fees is a subcategory of Tax Detail in the Engagement Terms ontology, referring to the complete amount of tax imposed on legal service fees.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDN8.label: Climate-Based Market Segment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDN8.definition: A climate-based market segment refers to a group of consumers or businesses categorized based on the climatic conditions of their geographical location. This segmentation helps businesses tailor their products, services, and marketing strategies to suit the specific needs and preferences of people living in areas with similar climatic characteristics

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNA.label: Umbundu
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNA.definition: A Bantu language spoken in Angola, characterized by its use of click consonants and other unique phonetic features.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNB.label: Breathalyzer Test
