https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNB.definition: A Breathalyzer test is a procedure that measures the concentration of alcohol in an individual's breath to determine their blood alcohol content (BAC). This test is commonly used by law enforcement agencies to assess if a driver is operating a vehicle under the influence of alcohol.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNC.label: Hiligaynon
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNC.definition: A language spoken in the Western Visayas region of the Philippines, specifically in the provinces of Iloilo, Guimaras, and Negros Occidental.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDND.label: Termination Without Cause by the Company Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDND.definition: A Termination Without Cause by the Company Clause is a provision in a contract that allows a company to end the agreement without providing a reason.
english_labels: Termination Without Cause by the Company Clause

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNJ.label: Virgin Islands Territorial Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNJ.definition: The Virgin Islands Territorial Court is a court system within the Virgin Islands Territory Courts that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters in the United States Virgin Islands.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNO.label: School Zone Violation Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNO.definition: A School Zone Violation Claim involves allegations that a driver has failed to adhere to specific traffic rules in a school zone, such as speed limits or stopping requirements, endangering the safety of children and other pedestrians.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNO.label: Living
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNO.definition: Living refers to the state of being alive and having the capacity to perform vital functions, such as breathing and circulating blood, as opposed to being deceased or non-living.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNW.label: Architectural, Engineering, and Related Services Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNW.definition: This industry group comprises establishments primarily engaged in architectural, engineering, and related services, such as drafting services, building inspection services, geophysical surveying and mapping services, surveying and mapping (except geophysical) services, and testing services.
english_labels: Architectural, Engineering, and Related Services Industry

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNa.label: Judicial Opinion
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNa.definition: A judicial opinion is a written statement by a judge or a panel of judges explaining the decision reached in a legal case, typically including the legal reasoning and principles applied to the case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNc.label: Georgia Superior Court - Tattnall County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNc.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over legal matters within Tattnall County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNo.label: Georgia Superior Court - Walker County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNo.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Walker County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Walker County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNr.label: General Partner
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNr.definition: A general partner is an owner of a partnership. Often, a general partner either plays an active role in the company's daily operations or is a managing partner. A general partner for a business can act on the company's behalf.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNs.label: Requirements for Public Benefits
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNs.definition: Requirements for public benefits refer to the conditions or activities that an individual or family must fulfill to qualify for or continue receiving financial assistance or services from a government program. These can include mandates for job searches, participation in educational or vocational training programs, or completion of specific plans aimed at improving self-sufficiency. Failure to meet these requirements may result in reduction, suspension, or termination of benefits.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNs.label: WC210 Pleadings
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNs.definition: Drafting/editing/filing all pleadings, reviewing opposing pleadings, counter-claims and third party complaints, research for pleadings, preparing/drafting/filing workers' compensation state forms and supporting Memorandum of Law, preparing affidavits/attorney affirmations, prepare communication with adjuster/employer regarding analysis/summary of pleadings/state forms

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNw.label: New York City Court - Syracuse
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNw.definition: A court located in Syracuse, New York that operates under the jurisdiction of the New York City Court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNy.label: Litigation Collaboration Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNy.definition: Litigation Collaboration Management refers to the process of managing and coordinating the efforts of multiple parties involved in a legal dispute, with the goal of achieving a successful outcome.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNz.label: Company Blanket Petition
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDNz.definition: The "Company Blanket Petition" refers to the L-1 Blanket Petition in the United States, which allows certain multinational companies to streamline the process of transferring employees to the U.S. under the L-1A or L-1B visa categories. With a blanket petition approval, the company can bypass the individual L-1 petition process for each employee and instead submit a simplified application to facilitate multiple employee transfers.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDO2.label: Motion to Delay Discharge
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDO2.definition: A Motion to Delay Discharge is a request made in a bankruptcy case to extend the time period before the debtor is released from their debts, typically to allow for completion of certain requirements or to address objections from creditors.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDO3.label: Wire Transfer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDO3.definition: "Wire Transfer" refers to the electronic transfer of funds from one financial institution or account to another, executed via a network of banking institutions or transfer service providers. This method of transferring money is commonly used for both domestic and international transactions and is generally considered secure and fast.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDO4.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Marion County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDO4.definition: The Indiana Circuit Court - Marion County is a specific court within the Indiana Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Marion County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOA.label: Grand Jury Privilege
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOA.definition: The Grand Jury Privilege is a legal protection that allows a grand jury to keep their proceedings and deliberations confidential, even from the court and the public.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOD.label: Blind
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOD.definition: Total Blindness, also referred to as Blindness, is a condition where an individual has complete loss of vision, with no perception of light or visual images. This severe form of visual impairment significantly impacts daily activities, communication, and mobility, requiring the use of adaptive strategies and assistive technologies.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOH.label: Breach of Insurance Contract
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOH.definition: The Breach of Insurance Contract is a legal claim that arises when an insurance company fails to fulfill its obligations under the terms of an insurance policy, resulting in harm or damages to the policyholder.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOJ.label: Arkansas Circuit Court - Searcy Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOJ.definition: The Arkansas Circuit Court - Searcy County is a specific court within the Arkansas Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Searcy County, Arkansas.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOQ.label: Human Trafficking
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOQ.definition: A "Human Trafficking Claim" pertains to the allegation or assertion that individuals have been recruited, transported, harbored, or received, often through force, coercion, or deception, for the purpose of exploitation. Such claims challenge violations of human rights and can encompass various forms of exploitation including, but not limited to, forced labor, sexual exploitation, and organ trafficking.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOR.label: Illinois Circuit Court - DeKalb County (23rd Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - DeKalb County (23rd Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOT.label: Judeo-Persian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOT.definition: Judeo-Persian is a language that combines elements of Persian and Hebrew and is used in legal documents, artifacts, evidence, testimony, proceedings, or any other legal aspect.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOV.label: Timekeeper ID
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOV.definition: A Timekeeper ID is a unique identifier assigned to an individual who provides legal services, indicating their role and responsibilities within a legal engagement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOW.label: Financial Statement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOW.definition: A Financial Statement is a formal record of the financial activities and position of a business, organization, or individual, typically presented in structured manner for a specific time period. Common types of financial statements include income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow statements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOb.label: Oncology Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOb.definition: Negligent or wrongful actions or omissions by a medical professional in the field of oncology, resulting in harm or injury to a patient.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOc.label: Rundi
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOc.definition: Rundi is a structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary, and is a member of the language family.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOf.label: Family Petition For Intracompany Transferees
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOf.definition: An L-2 Petition allows the immediate family members of L-1 visa holders, specifically their spouses and unmarried children under 21, to accompany or join the primary visa holder in the U.S. This petition facilitates the entry and stay of dependents of L-1 visa holders.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOf.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Kane County (16th Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Kane County (16th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOg.label: Motions and Filings to Disqualify Decisionmaker
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOg.definition: A Motion or Filing to Disqualify Decisionmaker is a legal request made by a party to remove a judge, arbitrator, or other decisionmaker from a case due to a perceived conflict of interest or bias.
english_labels: Motions and Filings to Disqualify Decisionmaker

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOm.label: Work Utilization
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOm.definition: Utilization is a metric often used in service industries to measure the percentage of a professional's working hours that are engaged in revenue-generating activities (billable). It is calculated by dividing the billable hours by the total available working hours. Utilization it usually expressed as a percentage, used to assess individual, team, or workforce efficiency and capacity utilization.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOo.label: State Government Representative
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOo.definition: A State Government Representative is an elected or appointed official who serves in the government of a state, province, or similar sub-national administrative division. This individual is responsible for participating in the creation, debate, or implementation of state-level laws, policies, and programs, as well as representing the interests of their constituents within the state governmental structure.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOp.label: Fair and True Reporting Privilege
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOp.definition: The Fair and True Reporting Privilege is a legal immunity and privilege that protects journalists and media outlets from being sued for defamation when reporting on matters of public interest, as long as they report accurately and in good faith.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOq.label: Confidentiality Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOq.definition: A confidentiality clause is a provision in a contract that requires one or more parties to keep certain information confidential and not disclose it to others.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOs.label: PA550 Continuing Application Preparation - International
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOs.definition: All actions associated with completing a continuing patent application (claiming priority to an earlier-filed application in the same country, but without adding new disclosure) that are to be filed outside the ('domestic') home country or region of the applicant, including translations, review of any invention disclosure materials or parent applications, drafting of application including pre-filing revision of any parent applications, preparation and execution of formal documents (such as assignments, declarations, information disclosure statements, transmittals, and biological deposits) filing of application, and reporting to the client. Also includes PCT National Phase entry where the parent PCT International Application was previously filed in another country. For PCT National Phase entry in the applicant's home country, use PA300. Note that (so-called "continuation-in-part") patent applications extending the scope of the disclosure (or so-called "new matter" in the U.S.) in an earlier-filed application are included under PA520- PA540. Also that government fees and other external expenses are included under E100

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOt.label: Common-Law Marriage Creation Event
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOt.definition: Common-law marriage refers to a type of informal marriage where two individuals cohabit and present themselves as a married couple without having undergone a formal legal marriage ceremony. For a common-law marriage to be recognized, certain conditions, which vary by jurisdiction, must be met, including cohabitation for a specified period and a mutual intent to be regarded as husband and wife.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOv.label: Language
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOv.definition: Written or spoken structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary; in the context of legal matters, the language of a document, artifact, evidence, testimony, proceeding, or any other legal aspect (e.g., English, Spanish, German, French, Russian, Chinese).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOv.label: Indiana City Court - Hamilton County, Fishers City
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOv.definition: A court located in Hamilton County, Fishers City, Indiana that has jurisdiction over cases within its geographical boundaries.
english_labels: Indiana City Court - Hamilton County, Fishers City

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOz.label: Reverse Mortgage Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDOz.definition: A Reverse Mortgage Agreement is a financial contract that allows homeowners, usually seniors, to convert part of their home equity into cash while retaining ownership of their home. Unlike a traditional mortgage, borrowers do not make monthly payments to the lender; instead, the loan amount, along with interest and fees, is repaid when the homeowner sells the property, moves out permanently, or passes away.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDP2.label: Rescission
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDP2.definition: Rescission is the act of canceling or voiding a contract, typically due to factors such as duress, unconscionability, or fraud, and is a type of equitable relief available in contract and quasi-contract claims.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDP3.label: Banking Operations Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDP3.definition: Law governing routine banking operations including bank capital requirements, risk management, etc.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDP4.label: Sicilian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDP4.definition: Sicilian (Language) refers to a written or spoken structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary specific to the Sicilian region of Italy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDP5.label: Hmong; Mong
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDP5.definition: A language spoken by the Hmong people, also known as Mong, which belongs to the top-level class of Language in the context of legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDP6.label: Breach of Joint Venture Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDP6.definition: The violation of a legally binding agreement between two or more parties to work together on a specific business venture.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDPA.label: NATO-6 Visa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDPA.definition: A NATO-6 visa is issued to members of a civilian component attached to NATO armed forces, allowing them to enter the U.S. to perform their duties. This visa category includes civilian employees and contractors working directly with NATO military operations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDPD.label: Trademark Cancellation Process
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDPD.definition: A trademark cancellation proceeding is a legal process in which a party seeks to remove an existing trademark registration from the official register. This proceeding can be initiated if the trademark is believed to be improperly registered or if it conflicts with a prior trademark.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDPG.label: Motion to Exclude
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDPG.definition: A Motion to Exclude is a legal request made by a party in a trial to prevent certain evidence, documents, reports, witnesses, or testimony from being presented or considered by the court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDPL.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Jersey County (7th Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Jersey County (7th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDPO.label: Takeover Statutes Representation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDPO.definition: A representation within a legal agreement that specifically pertains to the statutes and regulations related to the acquisition of a company.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDPS.label: Board of Members
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDPS.definition: A Board of Members refers to a collective group within an organization, typically composed of individuals who are elected or appointed to oversee the organization’s strategic direction, governance, and policy-making. This body sets long-term goals, approves plans and budgets, and ensures organizational adherence to its mission and legal requirements. Different from a Board of Directors, "Board of Members" can be used in specific organizational contexts where the board is composed entirely of members from within the organization, such as in some cooperatives, membership organizations, or clubs. The term might emphasize that the directors are also members of the organization, highlighting their dual roles as both members and directors, or it may refer to a governing body in a less formal or less structured setting than what is typically governed by a board of directors.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDPU.label: Foreign National Identifier
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDPU.definition: Foreign National Identifier refers to a unique identification number or code assigned to non-citizens by a country's immigration or governmental agency. In the United States, this is commonly known as the Alien Number or A-Number, which is used to track immigration cases and statuses. These identifiers appear on official documents such as green cards, visas, and employment authorization documents.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDPb.definition: The Indiana Superior Court - Scott County is a specific court within the Indiana Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Scott County, Indiana.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQ4.definition: A Seed Investor provides initial capital to a startup or early-stage business in exchange for equity or convertible debt, often taking significant risks with the expectation of high returns. This funding typically supports product development, market research, and initial operations before larger investments are secured.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQ4.label: Parol Evidence Rule

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQ7.definition: A court located in Jeff Davis County, Georgia that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQ8.label: Shona
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQ8.definition: Shona is a structured system of communication, consisting of grammar and vocabulary, used in legal matters as a language of documents, artifacts, evidence, testimonies, proceedings, or any other legal aspect.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQ8.label: Freedom of Assembly
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQ8.definition: A freedom of assembly claim is a legal action initiated by an individual or group alleging that their right to freedom of assembly, as protected by the First Amendment of the United States Constitution, has been violated by the government or a government actor. The First Amendment guarantees that the government shall not abridge the freedom of assembly, which includes the right to peacefully gather, protest, or associate with others for the expression of ideas, beliefs, and collective action. A freedom of assembly claim may arise in various contexts, such as when a government body enacts a law or regulation that unduly restricts assembly, when a permit for a peaceful protest or gathering is unfairly denied, or when an assembly is disbanded or interfered with by law enforcement without just cause.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQK.label: Employment Discrimination Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQK.definition: A claim made by an employee alleging unfair treatment or disparate impact based on a protected characteristic such as race, gender, age, or disability in the workplace.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQM.label: Motion to Review Fees
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQM.definition: A Motion to Review Fees is a request made in a bankruptcy case to examine and potentially adjust the fees charged by a professional, such as an attorney or accountant, for services rendered during the bankruptcy proceedings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQO.definition: The Indiana Circuit Court - Johnson County is a specific court within the Indiana Circuit Court system, located in Johnson County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQT.label: California Superior Court - Orange Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQT.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Orange County, California, with the power to hear and decide a wide range of legal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQT.definition: A Company Registration for Investors or Traders Petition, in the United States, the company's first E-2 application, allows a company to qualify for the Treaty Investor or Trader category by demonstrating that the company meets the necessary requirements for the status. https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQW.definition: A court located in Mahnomen County, Minnesota that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQa.label: EEA Market Region
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQa.definition: The EEA Market Region refers to the European Economic Area, which includes the member countries of the European Union (EU) and the European Free Trade Association (EFTA), except Switzerland. This region is characterized by the free movement of goods, services, capital, and people, facilitating a single market for businesses and consumers.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQa.label: Costs and Settlement Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQa.definition: Costs and Settlement Management refers to the process of managing and resolving financial aspects of a legal case, including expenses, fees, and settlements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQc.label: Statement of Personal or Family History
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQc.definition: A Statement of Personal or Family History is a hearsay exception that allows the admission of statements concerning the declarant's own birth, adoption, marriage, divorce, legitimacy, relationship by blood or marriage, ancestry, or other similar facts of personal or family history. This exception also includes statements concerning the same facts about another person, if the declarant was related to that person by blood, adoption, or marriage.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQf.label: Employer Fault Set-off
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQf.definition: Employer fault set-off diminishes the amount of damages a defendant is liable for based on the comparative fault of a plaintiff's employer and/or co-employees, as well as a certain set-off from the Workers' Compensation benefits paid to date.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQh.label: Furniture and Related Product Manufacturing Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQh.definition: Industries in the Furniture and Related Product Manufacturing subsector make furniture and related articles, such as mattresses, window blinds, cabinets, and fixtures. The processes used in the manufacture of furniture include the cutting, bending, molding, laminating, and assembly of such materials as wood, metal, glass, plastics, and rattan. However, the production process for furniture is not solely bending metal, cutting and shaping wood, or extruding and molding plastics. Design and fashion trends play an important part in the production of furniture. The integrated design of the article for both esthetic and functional qualities is also a major part of the process of manufacturing furniture. Design services may be performed by the furniture establishment's work force or may be purchased from industrial designers. Furniture may be made of any material, but the most common ones used in North America are metal and wood. Furniture manufacturing establishments may specialize in making articles primarily from one material. Some of the equipment required to make a wooden table, for example, is different from that used to make a metal one. However, furniture is usually made from several materials. A wooden table might have metal brackets, and a wooden chair a fabric or plastics seat. Therefore, in NAICS, furniture initially is classified based on the type of furniture (application for which it is designed) rather than the material used. For example, an upholstered sofa is treated as household furniture, although it may also be used in hotels or offices. When classifying furniture according to the component material from which it is made, furniture made from more than one material is classified based on the material used in the frame, or if there is no frame, the predominant component material. Upholstered household furniture (excluding kitchen and dining room chairs with upholstered seats) is classified without regard to the frame material. Kitchen or dining room chairs with upholstered seats are classified according to the frame material. Furniture may be made on a stock or custom basis and may be shipped assembled or unassembled (i.e., knockdown). The manufacture of furniture parts and frames is included in this subsector. Some of the processes used in furniture manufacturing are similar to processes that are used in other segments of manufacturing. For example, cutting and assembly occurs in the production of wood trusses that are classified in Subsector 321, Wood Product Manufacturing. However, the multiple processes that distinguish wood furniture manufacturing from wood product manufacturing warrant inclusion of wooden furniture manufacturing in the Furniture and Related Product Manufacturing subsector. Metal furniture manufacturing uses techniques that are also employed in the manufacturing of roll formed products classified in Subsector 332, Fabricated Metal Product Manufacturing. The molding process for plastics furniture is similar to the molding of other plastics products. However, plastics furniture producing establishments tend to specialize in furniture. NAICS attempts to keep furniture manufacturing together, but there are notable exceptions: concrete, ceramic, or stone furniture; seating for transportation equipment; and specialized hospital furniture (e.g., hospital beds and operating tables). These are classified in Subsector 327, Nonmetallic Mineral Product Manufacturing; Subsector 336, Transportation Equipment Manufacturing; and Subsector 339, Miscellaneous Manufacturing, respectively.
english_labels: Furniture and Related Product Manufacturing Industry

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQm.label: Subsequent Remedial Measures Objection
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQm.definition: A Subsequent Remedial Measures Objection is raised when a party in a legal proceeding believes that evidence of repairs or changes made after an incident is being used to prove negligence, culpability, or a defect in a product. This objection aims to encourage parties to make safety improvements without fear of such actions being used against them in court.
english_labels: Objection to Evidence of After-the-Fact Repairs

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQs.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Delaware County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQs.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Delaware County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within Delaware County, Pennsylvania.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQu.label: Automatic Stay Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQu.definition: Automatic Stay Practice refers to the legal practice of obtaining and enforcing an automatic stay, which is a court order that stops creditors from taking certain actions against a debtor or the debtor's property during a bankruptcy proceeding.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQx.label: Joint Venture Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQx.definition: A Joint Venture Agreement is a legal document that outlines the terms and conditions of a business arrangement between two or more parties who agree to pool their resources and expertise to achieve a specific goal or project. It defines the terms under which multiple parties collaborate on a specific project or business venture, delineating responsibilities, profit-sharing, and decision-making processes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQy.label: Email Communication
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQy.definition: A communication that occurs via email.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQz.label: Expert Disclosure
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDQz.definition: Expert Disclosure refers to a document filed in a trial court that contains information about an expert witness and their opinions or findings related to the case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDR0.label: Procedural Unconscionability Permitting Contract Rescission
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDR0.definition: Procedural Unconscionability Permitting Contract Rescission: A legal concept that allows a contract to be cancelled due to unfair or oppressive terms or conditions that were imposed upon one party during the formation of the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDR1.label: Petition for Visa for Specialty Occupation Workers from Australia
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDR1.definition: The petition for a visa for specialty occupation workers from Australia (in the U.S., E-3 Visa) allows Australian citizens to work in the destination country (e.g., U.S.) in specialty occupations and requires an employer-sponsored petition along with certain qualifications and documentation
english_labels: Petition for Visa for Specialty Occupation Workers from Australia

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDR1.label: Antitrust - Horizontal Merger Claims

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDR4.label: Signage Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDR4.definition: A Signage Clause is a provision in a contract that specifies the rules and requirements for displaying signs on a property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDR5.label: Tax Tier Amount Tax
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDR5.definition: Tax Tier Amount Tax is a subcategory of Tax Tier Detail and refers to the specific amount of tax owed in a given tax tier.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDR5.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Adams County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDR5.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Adams County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering legal proceedings in the state of Pennsylvania.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Adams County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDR6.label: Georgia District Court - Baldwin County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDR6.definition: Georgia District Court - Baldwin County: A court of law in the state of Georgia that has jurisdiction over legal cases within Baldwin County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDR7.label: Employee Pension and Benefits Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDR7.definition: Law relating to retirement and welfare benefit plans, with particular emphasis on benefits arrangements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDR8.label: Breach of Employment Contract
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDR8.definition: The Breach of Employment Contract is a violation of the terms and conditions agreed upon by an employer and employee, resulting in legal claims and potential damages.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRC.label: Mergers and Acquisitions Objectives
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRC.definition: Mergers and Acquisitions (M&A) Objectives refer to the specific aims, goals, plans, and intentions constructed by parties involved in a merger or acquisition transaction, including deal structure, deal size, governing law, jurisdiction, deal protection, closing conditions, remedies, consideration, target industry, and material adverse effect (MAE) language.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRG.label: Friulian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRG.definition: Friulian is a written or spoken structured system of communication that belongs to the Language top-level class and is used in legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRG.label: Hash Identifier
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRG.definition: A hash identifier, also known as a document checksum, is a unique alphanumeric code generated by applying a cryptographic hash function to the content of a document or file. This identifier serves as a digital fingerprint, ensuring the integrity and authenticity of the document by allowing any alterations to be easily detected.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRJ.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Westmoreland County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRJ.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court located in Westmoreland County, responsible for administering legal proceedings within its jurisdiction.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Westmoreland County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRK.label: Forfeiture of Deposit Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRK.definition: A forfeiture of deposit clause is a provision in a contract that allows one party to keep the deposit paid by the other party if the contract is breached.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRM.label: Secured Credit Notice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRM.definition: A UCC Financing Statement is a legal form filed by a secured creditor to give public notice that it has or may have an interest in the personal property of a debtor (a borrower or buyer). This statement is mainly used in the United States under the Uniform Commercial Code (UCC) to perfect a security interest.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRQ.label: Romansh
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRQ.definition: Romansh is a written or spoken structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary, and is a specific language within the context of legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRT.label: Termination of Public Benefit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRT.definition: Termination of public benefit refers to the cessation of financial assistance or services provided to an individual or family under a specific public benefit program. This can occur for various reasons, including exceeding income or asset limits, failing to meet ongoing eligibility requirements, or fraudulent activity, and generally requires formal notification and may offer an appeals process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRV.label: Counterfeit Identification Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRV.definition: Counterfeit Identification Management refers to the process of managing and preventing the production and distribution of fake identification documents, such as passports or driver's licenses, in order to protect intellectual property rights.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRZ.label: AAA Consumer Arbitration Rules
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRZ.definition: The AAA Consumer Arbitration Rules are a set of guidelines and procedures established by the American Arbitration Association for resolving disputes between consumers and businesses through arbitration.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRa.label: Mining - Real Estate Asset
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRa.definition: A mining real estate asset is a type of property that includes land and any minerals or resources that can be extracted from it, such as coal or gold.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRb.label: Off-Road Vehicle
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRb.definition: An off-road vehicle is a type of motorized vehicle specifically designed for use on rough and unpaved terrain. Examples of off-road vehicles include All-Terrain Vehicles (ATVs), commonly known as four-wheelers, and dune buggies.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRk.label: Kansas District Court - Crawford County, Pittsburg
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRk.definition: Kansas District Court - Crawford County, Pittsburg is a specific court within the Kansas District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Crawford County and is located in the city of Pittsburg.
english_labels: Kansas District Court - Crawford County, Pittsburg

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRl.label: Georgia Superior Court - Murray County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRl.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Murray County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Murray County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRp.label: Hoarseness
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRp.definition: Hoarseness is a voice disorder characterized by a rough, raspy, or strained vocal quality, often resulting from inflammation, overuse, or irritation of the vocal cords. This condition can cause difficulties in speaking clearly and may be associated with underlying medical issues such as laryngitis, vocal cord nodules, or gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRq.label: Untenantability Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRq.definition: An untentantability clause is a provision in a contract that allows a party to terminate the agreement if the property becomes uninhabitable or unusable for its intended purpose due to circumstances beyond the control of either party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRt.label: Capital Infrastructure Risk
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDRt.definition: Capital Infrastructure Risk is the potential for financial loss or operational disruptions stemming from the failure, damage, or obsolescence of physical assets or structures, such as buildings, equipment, or transportation systems — apart from IT infrastructure (listed separately). These risks can result from natural disasters, accidents, poor maintenance, or insufficient investment in upgrades and replacements, impacting a company or government's ability to function effectively.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDS7.label: Motion to Enforce Settlement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDS7.definition: A Motion to Enforce Settlement is a legal request made to a court to enforce the terms of a previously agreed upon settlement between parties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDS8.label: Goods
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDS8.definition: Goods: Tangible or intangible items that are capable of being owned or possessed and that have value or usefulness to their owner.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSA.label: Crisis Management Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSA.definition: Crisis Management Practice refers to the specialized legal advisory services aimed at assisting clients in navigating and mitigating the impact of a crisis situation. This practice involves providing strategic advice, legal risk assessment, and comprehensive crisis response planning to ensure clients effectively manage legal challenges arising from crises.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSB.label: Property & Premises Liability Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSB.definition: Property & Premises Liability Claims refer to legal claims made against a property owner or occupier for injuries or damages suffered by individuals on their property due to unsafe or hazardous conditions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSB.label: Arkansas District Court - Hot Spring Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSB.definition: A court located in Hot Spring County, Arkansas that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its designated area.
english_labels: Arkansas District Court - Hot Spring Cty.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSG.label: Subpoena Assertion Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSG.definition: Subpoena Assertion Practice refers to the legal work performed by a Legal Services Provider in the course of a legal matter related to the assertion of a subpoena, including the preparation, filing, and enforcement of such subpoenas.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSG.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Alexander County (1st Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Alexander County (1st Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSJ.label: Citation to the Record
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSJ.definition: A document's citations to the record (e.g., exhibits, appendices, deposition transcripts, declarations).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSK.label: New Mexico Magistrate Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSK.definition: The New Mexico Magistrate Court is a court within the New Mexico State Courts system that has jurisdiction over minor criminal offenses, civil cases, and traffic violations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSO.label: Rules of Appellate Procedure
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSO.definition: A court's body of procedural rules governing appeals.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDST.label: Age Discrimination
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDST.definition: Discrimination against an individual or group based on their age, typically in the workplace or other professional settings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSX.label: Public Sexual Activity
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSX.definition: Public Sexual Activity: Engaging in sexual acts or conduct in a public place, which is considered a criminal misdemeanor offense.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSY.label: Decisionmaker for Legal Disputes
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSY.definition: A person, entity, or group that makes legal or factual determinations in a legal proceeding.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSa.label: New Jersey Superior Court - Essex County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSa.definition: The New Jersey Superior Court - Essex County is a trial court within the New Jersey court system that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases in Essex County.
english_labels: New Jersey Superior Court - Essex County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSd.label: Patient's Duty to Provide for Own Well-being
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSd.definition: Patient's duty to provide for own well-being requires a plaintiff to use reasonable care to provide for their own well-being.
english_labels: Patient's Duty to Provide for Own Well-being

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSe.label: Document Attributes
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSe.definition: Document attributes refer to the properties or characteristics associated with a document, often used for identification, categorization, sorting, and retrieval. These might include aspects like the document's title, author, creation date, file type, size, and any other metadata that may be useful or relevant to the document's management or organization.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSk.label: Total Amount - Fee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSk.definition: Total, cumulative amount paid in fees.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSl.label: Right of Set Off Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSl.definition: A right of set off clause is a provision in a contract that allows a party to offset or deduct a debt owed to them by the other party from any amount owed to that party under the same contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSm.label: Termination Without Cause Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSm.definition: A Termination Without Cause Clause is a provision in a contract that allows one party to end the agreement without providing a reason or justification.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSn.label: M.D. (Doctor of Medicine)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSn.definition: The suffix "M.D." stands for "Doctor of Medicine" and is used after a person's name to indicate that they have completed the requisite training and education to practice medicine. This suffix signifies the individual's medical credentials and is commonly used in healthcare settings, academic environments, and formal documents.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSy.label: Spend Down Strategy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDSy.definition: A spend-down strategy refers to the deliberate reduction of personal assets in order to qualify for means-tested public benefits (e.g., Medicaid). The strategy involves incurring allowable medical expenses or transferring assets within legal guidelines to meet the eligibility criteria for assistance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDT0.label: Malicious Criminal Prosecution
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDT0.definition: The concept of Malicious Criminal Prosecution refers to the intentional and wrongful initiation of criminal proceedings against an individual without probable cause, with the intention of causing harm or injury to that individual.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDT0.label: JF20 Obtaining and reviewing documents (UK J-CODE)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDT0.definition: Obtaining and reviewing documents to determine relevance (applicable to both manual and e-disclosure).
english_labels: JF20 Obtaining and reviewing documents (UK J-CODE)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDT5.label: Contractor Negligence Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDT5.definition: A claim made against a contractor for their failure to exercise reasonable care in the construction process, resulting in harm or damage to a party involved in the project.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDT9.label: Collateral
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDT9.definition: Collateral is an asset or property pledged by a borrower to a lender as security for a loan or other obligation, to mitigate the risk of default. If the borrower fails to meet the obligations, the lender has the right to seize the collateral.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTA.label: Justice of the Peace
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTA.definition: A judicial officer who in some jurisdictions is permitted to enforce the laws for the preservation of the public peace.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTD.label: LINE_ITEM_DESCRIPTION
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTD.definition: A LINE_ITEM_DESCRIPTION is a component of the LEDES98BI V5 Format Rev 1-2020 standard that provides a description of a specific item or service being billed.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTG.label: Ultrahazardous Activities
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTG.definition: An activity that is so inherently dangerous that the person engaging in it is strictly liable for any resulting harm, regardless of whether they were negligent or not.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTH.label: Burial
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTH.definition: Burial is the process of placing a deceased person's body into the ground, typically accompanied by a funeral ceremony. It involves legal and cultural practices that vary widely across different societies and legal systems.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTJ.label: Arkansas Circuit Court - Newton Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTJ.definition: A court located in Newton County, Arkansas that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its designated geographical area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTJ.label: Franchise Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTJ.definition: A Franchise Agreement is a legally binding contract between a franchisor and a franchisee that outlines the terms and conditions of the franchise relationship, including the rights and obligations of both parties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTJ.label: Bihari languages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTJ.definition: Bihari languages are a group of languages spoken in the Indian state of Bihar and neighboring regions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTL.label: Marshallese
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTL.definition: Marshallese (Language) is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary used in the Marshall Islands.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTM.label: Amended and Restated Agreement Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTM.definition: An Amended and Restated Agreement Clause is a provision in a legal document that outlines the changes made to an existing agreement and replaces it in its entirety with a new agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTP.label: Prevailing Wage
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTP.definition: The "Prevailing Wage" is the hourly wage, typically established by government authorities, that is paid to workers in a specific locality or industry for a particular type of labor. It is intended to ensure that workers on government-funded projects or in certain sectors receive a fair and competitive wage, often based on the average wage rates for similar work in the region.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTQ.label: Notice of Hearing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTQ.definition: A Notice of Hearing is a written communication that informs a party of a scheduled hearing or proceeding.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTR.label: Pharmacovigilance
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTR.definition: Pharmacovigilance is the scientific and systematic process of monitoring, assessing, detecting, and preventing adverse effects or any other drug-related problems, primarily focusing on the safety of pharmaceutical products after they have been released on the market. It aims to enhance patient care and safety in relation to the use of medicines and to support public health programs by providing reliable, balanced information for the effective assessment of the risk-benefit profile of medicinal products.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTe.label: Florida Circuit Court - Gulf County - 14th Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTe.definition: A court located in Gulf County, Florida that is part of the larger Florida Circuit Court system.
english_labels: Florida Circuit Court - Gulf County - 14th Circuit Court

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTh.label: Arkansas District Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTh.definition: The Arkansas District Court is a court of limited jurisdiction within the Arkansas State Courts system, responsible for hearing cases related to civil and criminal matters within specific counties in Arkansas.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTk.label: Psychotic Disorder
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTk.definition: Psychotic Disorder is a broad category of mental health conditions characterized by a loss of contact with reality, which can manifest through symptoms such as hallucinations, delusions, disorganized thinking, and impaired insight. Individuals with psychotic disorders may experience significant disturbances in perception, thought processes, and behavior, affecting their ability to function in daily life.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTk.label: Indiana City Court - Hamilton County, Carmel City
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTk.definition: Indiana City Court - Hamilton County, Carmel City is a specific court located in Hamilton County, Carmel City, Indiana that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical boundaries.
english_labels: Indiana City Court - Hamilton County, Carmel City

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTs.label: Public Records Act Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTs.definition: A Public Records Act Claim is a legal claim made against a government agency for failure to provide access to public records as required by law.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTu.label: Domain Name Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDTu.definition: Domain Name Management refers to the legal management and protection of internet domain names, including registration, transfer, and dispute resolution.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDU2.label: Minnesota District Court - Lake of the Woods County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDU2.definition: Minnesota District Court - Lake of the Woods County: A specific court within the Minnesota District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Lake of the Woods County.
english_labels: Minnesota District Court - Lake of the Woods County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDU7.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Juniata County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDU7.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court in Juniata County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court system that has jurisdiction over minor criminal offenses and civil cases.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Juniata County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDU9.label: Analysis of Cash Collateral
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDU9.definition: Analysis of Cash Collateral refers to the examination and evaluation of the cash or cash equivalents that are pledged as collateral in a legal matter, typically in the context of bankruptcy proceedings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDUD.label: Waiver of Moral Rights Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDUD.definition: A Waiver of Moral Rights Clause is a provision in a legal agreement where an individual relinquishes their right to be credited as the author of their work or to object to any changes made to their work.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDUG.label: Progressive Muscular Atrophy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDUG.definition: Progressive muscular atrophy (PMA) is a neurodegenerative condition characterized by the gradual degeneration and atrophy of lower motor neurons, leading to progressive muscle weakness and wasting. Unlike Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), PMA primarily affects lower motor neurons and often has a slower progression.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDUJ.label: Motion to Extend Time to File Opposition
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDUJ.definition: A Motion to Extend Time to File Opposition is a request made to a court to allow additional time beyond the original deadline for a party to submit their opposition to a motion or appeal.
english_labels: Motion to Extend Time to File Opposition

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDUX.label: Lead Poisoning Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDUX.definition: A claim for damages resulting from exposure to toxic levels of lead, typically in the context of personal injury litigation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDUb.label: Continuous Matching Rights
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDUb.definition: The Continuous Matching Rights concept refers to the ongoing entitlement of a party to have their rights matched with those of another party, as outlined in the Matching Rights Language.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDUe.label: JC00 Initial and Pre-action protocol work (UK J-CODE)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDUe.definition: Work relating to the obtaining of instructions, identification of witnesses, dealing with locus and evidential issues, dealing with and identifying legal issues arising from the case and strategy, and dealing with any protocol related matters, if not covered elsewhere.
english_labels: JC00 Initial and Pre-action protocol work (UK J-CODE)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDUf.label: Termination of Lease Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDUf.definition: A Termination of Lease Clause is a provision in a lease agreement that outlines the circumstances under which the lease can be terminated before the end of its term.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDUh.label: Abuse of Discretion
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDUh.definition: The abuse of discretion is a legal concept that refers to a situation where a judge or other decision-maker has acted in a manner that is unreasonable, arbitrary, or capricious, and has therefore exceeded the bounds of their lawful authority.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDUp.label: Sole Remedy Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDUp.definition: A Sole Remedy Clause is a provision in a contract that limits the available remedies to only those specified in the clause, thereby excluding any other legal remedies that may be available.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDUw.label: Florida Circuit Court - Broward County - 17th Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDUw.definition: The Florida Circuit Court - Broward County (17th Circuit Court) is a specific court within the Florida Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Broward County.
english_labels: Florida Circuit Court - Broward County - 17th Circuit Court

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDUw.label: A101 Plan and prepare for
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDUw.definition: To "Plan and prepare for" (A101) means to engage in activities that involve creating a strategy or course of action in anticipation of a future event or task, as part of a larger set of activities (A100).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDV2.label: Patent Concept Objectives
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDV2.definition: Patent Concept Objectives encompass key criteria like Novelty, Obviousness, and Inventive Step that an invention must satisfy to be patentable. These objectives ensure the invention is new, non-obvious, and represents a significant step beyond existing knowledge or technology.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDV3.label: Petition for Rehearing En Banc
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDV3.definition: A Petition for Rehearing En Banc is a legal document filed with an appellate court requesting a full panel of judges to review and reconsider a prior decision made by a smaller panel of judges.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDV7.label: Litigation Burdens of Proof
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDV7.definition: Burden that a party must bear to prove its claims, defenses, and/or remedies (e.g., beyond a reasonable doubt, clear and convincing).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDV9.label: Resisting Arrest
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDV9.definition: Resisting Arrest refers to the act of using force or violence to prevent a law enforcement officer from lawfully arresting or detaining an individual.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDVA.label: Vacated Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDVA.definition: The previously effective law has been vacated by some authority (e.g., appellate court, judge, regulator).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDVI.label: Iranian languages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDVI.definition: Iranian languages are a group of languages spoken in Iran and other parts of the world, including Afghanistan and Tajikistan.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDVK.label: New York City Court - Plattsburgh
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDVK.definition: New York City Court - Plattsburgh is a specific court located in Plattsburgh, New York that falls under the jurisdiction of the larger New York City Court system.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDVQ.label: Police Officer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDVQ.definition: A member of a police force or other organization of a municipality who is responsible for the prevention and detection of crime and the enforcement of the general criminal laws of the state. Aldazabal v. Carey, 396 N.Y.S.2d 84, 58 A.D.2d 120 (N.Y. App. Div. 1977)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDVa.label: New York City Court - Albany
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDVa.definition: New York City Court - Albany is a specific court located in Albany, New York that falls under the broader category of New York City Court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDVb.label: Right to Life
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDVb.definition: The right to life is a fundamental human right that protects individuals from arbitrary or unlawful deprivation of life. This right is upheld by various international legal instruments, such as the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, and prohibits practices like extrajudicial killings, enforced disappearances, and the death penalty in some contexts

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDVd.label: Rule Type
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDVd.definition: A Rule Type is a specific type of Litigation Procedural Rule that outlines the procedures and requirements for a particular type of legal case, such as a pilot case or a case with complex issues.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDVn.label: Legislative Branch
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDVn.definition: The legislative branch is responsible for creating, amending, and repealing laws. It is typically composed of one or more bodies, such as a parliament, congress, or assembly, with elected representatives.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDVr.label: L250 Other Written Motions and Submissions
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDVr.definition: A written request or argument submitted to a court or other legal authority during the pre-trial phase of a case, which does not fall under the category of a formal pleading.
english_labels: L250 Other Written Motions and Submissions

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDVt.label: Underwriter
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDVt.definition: An underwriter is an individual or institution that underwrites a financial transaction. Underwriting is the process by which an underwriter takes on financial risk for a fee. The risk most typically involves loans, insurance, or investments.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDVw.label: matter_billing_type
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDVw.definition: "Code indicating how the matter is billed. Valid values and their descriptions are: CT - Contingency Fee - When the law firm's fee is based on a percentage of the amount recovered by the law firm client in a plaintiff's action. FF - Flat Fee - When the firm is paid a flat fee on the matter only. GW - Goodwill Work - Where the firm has performed services for free for the client on a matter and provides information on the work performed in a separate $0 invoice to the client. MPF - Multi-Payor Fees - When the cost of services provided on a matter is split by multiple clients of the firm regardless of any other matter_billing_type that may apply. TM - Time & Materials - When the bill is based on hours worked, or where there may be a combination of hourly billing plus a flat fee by task arrangement. A null value defaults to ""TM"". "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDW3.label: Debtor-In-Possession
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDW3.definition: A debtor in possession in United States bankruptcy law is a person or corporation who has filed a bankruptcy petition, but remains in possession of property upon which a creditor has a lien or similar security interest.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDW9.label: Motion for Joint Administration
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDW9.definition: A Motion for Joint Administration is a request made in a bankruptcy case to consolidate multiple related cases into one administrative proceeding.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDW9.label: Order, Resolution, or Vote Clause Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDW9.definition: An Order, Resolution, or Vote Clause claim refers to a legal argument challenging the constitutionality of an action taken by a legislative body, such as a Congress or a state legislature, based on the requirements outlined in the Order, Resolution, or Vote Clause of the United States Constitution. This claim asserts that a particular action, such as passing a resolution or adopting a vote, violates the constitutional procedures outlined in the Clause, potentially rendering it invalid or unconstitutional.
english_labels: Order, Resolution, or Vote Clause Claim

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWD.label: Asset Redeemability Structure
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWD.definition: Asset Redeemability Structure indicates whether units of an investment are traded on the secondary market or whether the fund continually stands ready to sell new units and redeem outstanding units on demand. Closed-end units are typically sold on an organized exchange or over-the-counter market and are usually not redeemed, while open-end funds continually sell new units to the public and redeem outstanding units on demand, resulting in fluctuating levels of outstanding capital.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWD.label: Public Policy and Government Affairs Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWD.definition: Rules surrounding lobbying and political advocacy.
english_labels: Public Policy and Government Affairs Law

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWI.label: Permitted Disclosure Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWI.definition: A Permitted Disclosure Clause is a provision in a contract that allows for the sharing of confidential information between parties under certain circumstances.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWI.label: Request for Physical or Mental Examination
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWI.definition: A Request for Physical or Mental Examination is a type of Discovery Document that asks for an individual to undergo a medical examination to provide evidence in a legal case.
english_labels: Request for Physical or Mental Examination

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWJ.label: Volunteers
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWJ.definition: Volunteers, in a military context, are individuals who willingly enlist or offer their services to the armed forces without being conscripted or otherwise compelled. This category encompasses those who join the military of their own accord, often driven by patriotism, career opportunities, or a desire to serve their country.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWJ.label: E116 Trial transcripts
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWJ.definition: Trial transcripts (E116) are a type of expense (E100) incurred during legal proceedings, which involve a written or recorded record of the trial proceedings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWM.label: Life or Health Insurance Obtained by Fraud
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWM.definition: Life or Health Insurance Obtained by Fraud: Insurance policies for life or health that are acquired through deceitful means, such as providing false information or concealing relevant facts, with the intention of obtaining benefits that would not have been granted otherwise.
english_labels: Life or Health Insurance Obtained by Fraud

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWO.label: Admiralty Clause Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWO.definition: An Admiralty Clause claim is a legal argument asserting that a law or government action violates the Admiralty Clause of the United States Constitution. This claim contends that the law or action infringes upon the federal government's exclusive jurisdiction over admiralty and maritime matters, which are governed by the federal admiralty laws, and thus exceeds the authority of the enacting entity.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWV.label: Dismissal With Prejudice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWV.definition: Dismissal with prejudice is a legal ruling that permanently prevents the same case from being brought to court again, due to a decision made on the merits of the case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWW.label: Motion to Amend Complaint
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWW.definition: A Motion to Amend Complaint is a formal request made to a court to modify or change the allegations or claims made in a legal complaint.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWZ.label: Debtor Repayment Plan
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWZ.definition: A Debtor Repayment Plan is a legal document that outlines a debtor's proposed plan to repay their debts to creditors, typically filed as part of a bankruptcy or restructuring proceeding.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWa.label: Statutory Tax Districts Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWa.definition: A Statutory Tax Districts Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the specific tax districts that are applicable to the agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWb.label: Construction of Buildings Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWb.definition: The Construction of Buildings subsector comprises establishments primarily responsible for the construction of residential and non-residential buildings. The work performed may include new work, additions, alterations, or maintenance and repairs. The onsite assembly of precut, panelized, and prefabricated buildings and construction of temporary buildings are included in this subsector. Part or all of the production work for which the establishments in this subsector have responsibility may be subcontracted to other construction establishments'usually specialty trade contractors.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWi.label: Big Sandy Rancheria of Western Mono Indians of California
english_labels: Big Sandy Rancheria of Western Mono Indians of California

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWl.label: Caddo
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWl.definition: A Native American language spoken by the Caddo people, primarily in Oklahoma and Texas.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWn.label: Chronic Hyperglycemia
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWn.definition: Chronic Hyperglycemia refers to longstanding abnormally high levels of blood glucose, which leads to long-term diabetic complications by disrupting nerve and blood vessel functioning. This disruption affects multiple body systems, resulting in various complications such as diabetic peripheral neurovascular disease, diabetic retinopathy, coronary artery disease, peripheral vascular disease, diabetic gastroparesis, diabetic nephropathy, poorly healing skin infections, diabetic neuropathies, and cognitive impairments, including depression and anxiety.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWo.label: Material Business Change
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWo.definition: Material Business Changes refer to significant alterations in a company's structure, operations, or financial position that could substantially impact its value, performance, or risk profile. These changes are often substantial enough to require disclosure to shareholders and potentially regulatory bodies.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWr.label: Prosecutor
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDWr.definition: A prosecutor is a legal professional responsible for representing the government in criminal cases by presenting evidence, building a case against the defendant, and seeking their conviction. Prosecutors also have a duty to ensure that justice is served and that defendants' rights are upheld throughout the legal process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDX5.label: Life Estate
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDX5.definition: A Life Estate is a form of property ownership where an individual holds the rights to use, occupy, and benefit from a property for the duration of their life. Upon the individual's death, ownership of the property reverts back to the original owner or a designated remainderman, as stipulated in the life estate agreement

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDX6.label: Reckless Driving
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDX6.definition: Reckless Driving: A criminal misdemeanor offense that involves operating a vehicle with a willful or wanton disregard for the safety of others on the road.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDX7.label: Georgia District Court - Troup County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDX7.definition: A court located in Troup County, Georgia that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDXA.label: Georgia District Court - Effingham County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDXA.definition: A court located in Effingham County, Georgia that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographic area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDXG.label: Aerospace Product and Parts Manufacturing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDXG.definition: This industry group comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing aircraft, missiles, space vehicles and their engines, propulsion units, auxiliary equipment, and parts thereof.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDXM.label: Mohegan Tribe of Indians of Connecticut
english_labels: Mohegan Tribe of Indians of Connecticut

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDXU.label: matter_total_detail_fees
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDXU.definition: "Sum of all FEE.total_amounts billed to this matter/invoice. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDXW.label: Arkansas Circuit Court - Boone Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDXW.definition: A court located in Boone County, Arkansas that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its designated area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDXX.label: Breach of Implied Warranty of Good & Workmanlike Services - Repair & Modification
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDXX.definition: The Breach of Implied Warranty of Good & Workmanlike Services - Repair & Modification refers to a violation of the implied promise that a service provider will perform repairs or modifications in a competent and skillful manner, resulting in harm or damages to the recipient of the service.
english_labels: Breach of Implied Warranty of Good & Workmanlike Services - Repair & Modification

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDXY.label: Interstate Commerce Clause Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDXY.definition: An Interstate Commerce Clause claim is a legal argument asserting that a state law or regulation violates the authority of the federal government to regulate commerce among the states. This claim is based on the interpretation that the Interstate Commerce Clause grants Congress the power to regulate trade and commerce that crosses state boundaries, thereby restricting state interference in this domain.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDXg.label: LAW_FIRM_ADDRESS_2
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDXg.definition: The concept LAW_FIRM_ADDRESS_2 refers to the second line of the address of a law firm and is a component of the LEDES98BI V5 Format Rev 1-2020 standard for electronic legal invoicing.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDXk.label: Emergency Medicine Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDXk.definition: Negligence or wrongdoing by a medical professional in the emergency medicine setting, resulting in harm or injury to a patient.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDY4.label: Court Forms Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDY4.definition: Court Forms Management refers to the process of organizing and maintaining legal forms used in court proceedings, including their creation, storage, and retrieval.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDY5.label: Psychiatrist Negligence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDY5.definition: Psychiatrist Negligence refers to a legal claim of medical negligence against a psychiatrist, where the patient alleges that the psychiatrist failed to provide the appropriate standard of care resulting in harm or injury.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDY8.label: Definition of Environmental Laws Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDY8.definition: A provision in a contract that outlines the legal requirements and obligations related to the protection and preservation of the natural environment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYC.label: Motion to Set Last Day to File Proofs of Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYC.definition: A Motion to Set Last Day to File Proofs of Claim is a request made in a bankruptcy case to establish a deadline for creditors to submit their claims for payment.
