english_labels: Motion to Set Last Day to File Proofs of Claim

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYJ.label: Pennsylvania Supreme Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYJ.definition: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court is the highest court in the state of Pennsylvania and serves as the final court of appeals for all cases arising in the state.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYK.label: Uncontested Divorce
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYK.definition: An Uncontested Divorce is a type of divorce in which both spouses mutually agree on all the key terms and issues related to the dissolution of their marriage. This includes matters such as property division, child custody and support, spousal support, and any other relevant issues. In an uncontested divorce, the spouses often work together to create a settlement agreement, making the divorce process more efficient and less adversarial than a contested divorce.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYL.label: Successor Trustee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYL.definition: A trustee who accepts ownership, power, and responsibility of a trust from a prior trustee.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYM.label: Appellate Filings
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYM.definition: A document filed by a party in an appellate proceeding.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYM.label: Fiduciary Duty
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYM.definition: Fiduciary duty is a legal obligation requiring one party, the fiduciary, to act in the best interest of another party, typically a beneficiary or principal, with loyalty and care. This duty is paramount in relationships involving trust and confidence, such as those between trustees and beneficiaries, corporate directors and shareholders, or financial advisors and clients.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYO.label: Quantum Meruit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYO.definition: A claim for quantum meruit is a legal action seeking payment for the reasonable value of services or goods provided, when there is no contract or the contract is unenforceable, and is typically brought under the category of equitable relief or quasi-contract claims.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYP.label: Company Constitution
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYP.definition: A Company Constitution is a legal document that sets out the rules and regulations governing the internal management of a corporation. It is a comprehensive framework encompassing everything from director duties to shareholder rights.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYR.label: Right of First Refusal Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYR.definition: A Right of First Refusal Agreement (ROFR) is a legal contract that grants a specified party the priority to purchase a particular asset before the owner is allowed to sell the asset to others. This agreement is often utilized in business ventures and real estate transactions to give existing stakeholders a chance to maintain their stake in the face of potential external interest.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYS.label: JL10 Advocacy (UK J-CODE)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYS.definition: Preparation by advocates of written and oral openings, closings or skeleton arguments; preparation for examination of witnesses; preparation of and for all applications made during trial; considering all submissions of other parties; attendance of advocates during trial. Includes all dealings by advocates with others (e.g. solicitors, clients, witnesses) for these purposes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYU.label: Motion to Compel
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYU.definition: A Motion to Compel is a legal request made to a court to force the opposing party to comply with a discovery request or court order.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYX.label: Sealed Document
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYX.definition: A sealed document is a legal record that is kept confidential and is not accessible to the public or even to parties in a case unless permitted by the court. The sealing of a document restricts its availability to protect sensitive information, trade secrets, or to comply with privacy laws and regulations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYX.label: Kurdish
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYX.definition: Kurdish (Language) is a structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary specific to the Kurdish language, used in legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYf.label: Diabetic Ketoacidosis
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYf.definition: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) is an acute, potentially life-threatening complication of diabetes mellitus characterized by dangerously high blood glucose levels and acidosis. It results from severe insulin deficiency, which can be caused by missed or inadequate insulin therapy or acute illness. DKA typically requires hospitalization to address complications such as dehydration, electrolyte imbalance, and insulin deficiency. Serious treatment-related complications may include cardiac arrhythmias, intestinal necrosis, and cerebral edema with seizures. Recurrent episodes can stem from mood or eating disorders.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYg.label: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYg.definition: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that affects motor neurons in the brain and spinal cord, leading to muscle weakness, atrophy, and eventually paralysis. This condition results in the loss of voluntary muscle control and can impact speaking, swallowing, and breathing.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYh.label: Military Veteran
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYh.definition: A military veteran is an individual who has previously served in the armed forces of a country, including the army, navy, air force, or other branches of service, and has completed their active duty or reserve obligations. Military veterans may have served in various capacities, ranks, and locations during their time in service. In many countries, including the United States, veterans are protected from discrimination and are eligible for various benefits, such as healthcare, education, and employment support, in recognition of their service.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYj.label: Kabyle
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYj.definition: A Berber language spoken by the Kabyle people in Algeria and other parts of North Africa.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYo.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Martin County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYo.definition: Indiana Circuit Court - Martin County: A court of general jurisdiction in Indiana that hears civil and criminal cases within Martin County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYt.label: New Jersey Superior Court - Appellate Division
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYt.definition: The New Jersey Superior Court - Appellate Division is a specific court within the New Jersey State Courts system that hears appeals from lower courts and administrative agencies.
english_labels: New Jersey Superior Court - Appellate Division

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYt.label: Vendor Advisory Services
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDYt.definition: Vendor Advisory Services refers to professional advice and guidance provided by a consultant or manager to vendors, aimed at improving their business operations and strategies.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDZ1.label: Chronic Pulmonary Hypertension
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDZ1.definition: Chronic pulmonary hypertension is a condition characterized by persistently high blood pressure in the pulmonary arteries, which carry blood from the heart to the lungs. This condition leads to increased workload on the right side of the heart and can cause symptoms such as shortness of breath, fatigue, and chest pain.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDZ5.label: Minnesota District Court - Cottonwood County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDZ5.definition: Minnesota District Court - Cottonwood County: A specific court within the Minnesota District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Cottonwood County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDZ6.label: Federal-Question Jurisdiction
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDZ6.definition: Federal-Question Jurisdiction refers to the authority of federal courts to hear cases that involve federal law or the U.S. Constitution.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDZA.label: Motion for Relief due to Mistake, Inadvertence, Surprise, and Excusable Neglect
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDZA.definition: A Motion for Relief due to Mistake, Inadvertence, Surprise, and Excusable Neglect is a legal request to the court to set aside a previous order or judgment due to a mistake, oversight, unexpected event, or reasonable excuse.
english_labels: Motion for Relief due to Mistake, Inadvertence, Surprise, and Excusable Neglect

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDZD.label: Change Management Risk
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDZD.definition: Change Management Risk refers to the potential for negative outcomes or disruptions when an organization undergoes transformations, such as implementing new processes, technology, or organizational structures. These risks may arise from poor planning, ineffective communication, resistance to change, or inadequate training, ultimately impacting employee morale, productivity, and the overall success of the change initiative

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDZJ.label: Vegetative State
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDZJ.definition: A vegetative state is a condition in which a person is awake but shows no signs of awareness or response to the environment. It is characterized by the presence of sleep-wake cycles without cognitive function, often resulting from severe brain injury. This concept involves complex issues related to medical decision-making, guardianship, and end-of-life care. Legal challenges may arise in determining the rights and best interests of individuals in a vegetative state, particularly regarding life-sustaining treatments and the recognition of advance directives.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDZX.label: Afrikaans
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDZX.definition: A language spoken in South Africa and Namibia, derived from Dutch and characterized by its use of double negatives and the placement of the verb at the end of a sentence.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDZh.label: Mandingo
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDZh.definition: A language spoken primarily in West Africa, including in countries such as Guinea, Sierra Leone, and Liberia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDZn.label: Acute Leukemia
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDZn.definition: Acute leukemia is a rapidly progressing cancer of the blood and bone marrow characterized by an excessive accumulation of immature white blood cells. This condition includes subtypes such as acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) and acute myeloid leukemia (AML), with specific criteria for disability consideration depending on the treatment timeline and residual impairments.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDZo.label: Loss of Spousal Consortium
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDZo.definition: The loss of the benefits and companionship of a spouse due to injury or death caused by the negligence or wrongful act of another.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDZq.label: Firm Partner / Shareholder
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDZq.definition: A Firm Partner/Shareholder is a lawyer who holds an ownership interest in a law firm, either as an equity or non-equity partner.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDZw.label: Applied Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDZw.definition: The legal authority (e.g., judicial opinion, statute, regulation) has been applied by some decisionmaker (e.g., judge, regulator).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDZz.label: Permanent Injunction
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDZz.definition: A Permanent Injunction is a court order that prohibits a party from performing a specific act or engaging in certain conduct, and remains in effect indefinitely or until modified or dissolved by the court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDZz.label: US Chapter 9 Bankruptcy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDZz.definition: Chapter 9 bankruptcy is a bankruptcy for municipalities ' cities, towns, counties and school districts, for example. Municipalities that file chapter 9 earn protection from creditors while they develop a plan for adjusting their debts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDa0.label: Settlement, Demand, and Collection Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDa0.definition: Settlement and Demand Practice refers to the legal work performed in the course of a legal matter related to resolving disputes and negotiating settlements, including the drafting and sending of demand letters and the negotiation of settlement agreements, as well as collection of debts and judgments.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDa0.label: Senior Citizen Healthcare Coverage
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDa0.definition: This refers to healthcare plans specifically designed to cater to the needs of individuals who are in their senior years, generally those 65 and older. In the U.S., Medicare is the primary provider of healthcare coverage for seniors, offering various plans that include hospital stays, medical services, and prescription drugs.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDa2.label: Gujarati
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDa2.definition: Gujarati (Language) is a structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary specific to the Gujarati-speaking community.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDa3.label: Submarine
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDa3.definition: A Submarine is a watercraft capable of underwater operation, designed for long-duration submersion and navigation below the surface. Submarines are used for military purposes, scientific research, exploration, and underwater construction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDa4.label: Discount Amount - Fee or Expense
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDa4.definition: Discount Amount - Fee or Expense refers to a reduction in the amount charged for legal services or expenses incurred during the engagement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDa9.label: Lis Pendens
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDa9.definition: A Lis Pendens is a legal notice filed in the public records to give notice of pending litigation concerning real property, and is considered a provisional remedy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDaA.label: End-to-End Case Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDaA.definition: End-to-End Case Management refers to the process of managing a legal case from start to finish, including all aspects of litigation management.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDaG.label: Anders Brief
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDaG.definition: An Anders Brief is a type of appellate brief filed by court-appointed counsel when they believe there are no non-frivolous issues to raise on appeal and seek to withdraw from representation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDaL.label: Anti-Money Laundering Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDaL.definition: An Anti-Money Laundering (AML) Claim arises when an individual or entity is accused of violating regulations designed to prevent and detect money laundering activities. This claim involves allegations of failing to implement adequate controls, procedures, and reporting mechanisms to prevent the laundering of illicit funds.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDaM.label: E112 Court fees
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDaM.definition: Court fees are expenses related to the cost of filing and processing legal documents and cases in court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDaM.label: Syndicated
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDaM.definition: Syndicated refers to a financial arrangement where multiple lenders or investors jointly provide funds to a borrower or project, sharing the associated risks and returns. This structure is commonly used in large loans, debt issues, or investments that exceed the capacity or risk tolerance of a single lender or investor.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDaN.label: Rules of Civil Procedure
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDaN.definition: A court's body of procedural rules governing criminal actions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDaO.label: Scenic and Sightseeing Transportation Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDaO.definition: Industries in this group utilize transportation equipment to provide recreation and entertainment. These activities have a production process distinct from passenger transportation carried out for the purpose of other types of for-hire transportation. transport may be by ground, air, rail water or other means. This process does not emphasize efficient transportation; in fact, such activities often use obsolete vehicles, such as steam trains, to provide some extra ambiance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDaS.label: JJ40 Applications concerning evidence (UK J-CODE)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDaS.definition: Work performed related to applications concerning evidence

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDaT.label: Motion to Remove to State Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDaT.definition: A Motion to Remove to State Court is a legal request to transfer a case from a federal court to a state court.
english_labels: Motion to Remove to State Court

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDaX.label: Illegal Re-Entry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDaX.definition: The concept of "Illegal Re-Entry" refers to the act of a person who has been deported from a country, returning to that country without proper authorization, which is considered a crime against the government and falls under the category of immigration claims.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDad.label: 443 Housing/Accommodations (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDad.definition: Action filed under the Fair Housing Act (Title VII), 42 U.S.C. § 3601 & 3602.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDae.label: New York City Court - Beacon
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDae.definition: A court located in Beacon, New York City that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDae.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Stone County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDae.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Stone County: A court of law in Missouri that has jurisdiction over legal cases within Stone County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDah.label: Rules Binding Lawyers
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDah.definition: "Rules binding lawyers" refer to the set of ethical, procedural, and evidentiary regulations that govern the conduct and practice of attorneys. These rules include professional responsibility standards, civil and criminal procedure rules, and evidence rules, all of which guide lawyers in their representation of clients, litigation processes, and courtroom conduct.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDai.label: Macedonian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDai.definition: Macedonian (Language) is a structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary specific to the Macedonian region.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDaj.label: Community Property Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDaj.definition: A community property claim relates to the legal concept of community property in certain jurisdictions. In divorce or dissolution of a marriage, community property refers to assets and debts acquired during the marriage that are considered jointly owned by both spouses. A community property claim involves asserting a legal right to an equitable division of these shared assets and liabilities between the divorcing parties

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDaj.label: Yiddish
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDaj.definition: Yiddish is a structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary, and is a language used in legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDam.label: Georgia District Court - Mitchell County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDam.definition: Georgia District Court - Mitchell County: A specific court within the Georgia District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Mitchell County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDar.label: Kansas District Court - Montgomery County, Independence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDar.definition: The Kansas District Court - Montgomery County, Independence is a specific court within the Kansas District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Montgomery County, Kansas.
english_labels: Kansas District Court - Montgomery County, Independence

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDas.label: Land Dayak languages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDas.definition: Land Dayak languages are a group of languages spoken by the indigenous Dayak people in Borneo, characterized by their unique grammar and vocabulary.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDas.label: Georgia Superior Court - Burke County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDas.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Burke County is a specific court within the Georgia Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Burke County, Georgia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDat.label: Buddhist Religion
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDat.definition: The Buddhist religion is a spiritual tradition and philosophical system originating in ancient India, centered around the teachings of Siddhartha Gautama, known as the Buddha. In legal contexts, it may relate to the recognition of Buddhist principles in laws, the protection of Buddhist religious practices and sites, and the accommodation of Buddhist beliefs in various legal frameworks.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDaw.label: German, Old High
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDaw.definition: Old High German (ca.750-1050) is a historical language that was spoken in parts of Europe during the early Middle Ages.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDb5.label: Matter Resolution
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDb5.definition: A matter's resolution — the point at which the legal matter is resolved. Some Providers refer to this as a "pencils down" period. This event may differ from `Matter Closure`, which may occur later.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDb7.label: Interlingue; Occidental
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDb7.definition: A constructed language designed to be easy to learn and understand, with a simplified grammar and vocabulary, intended for use as a universal second language.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDb7.label: Labor Rights
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDb7.definition: Labor rights are the legal and social protections designed to ensure fair treatment, equitable wages, and safe working conditions for workers. These rights can include the freedom to organize and join labor unions, the right to collective bargaining, and protection from unlawful discrimination or harassment in the workplace.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDb8.label: Real Property Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDb8.definition: Law that governs the various forms of ownership and tenancy in real property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDbA.label: Georgia Superior Court - Union County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDbA.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Union County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Union County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDbD.label: Broker-Dealer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDbD.definition: A Broker-Dealer is a financial firm or individual that buys and sells securities on behalf of clients (acting as a broker) or for its own account (acting as a dealer). Broker-dealers are essential in facilitating securities transactions, providing market liquidity, and offering investment advice and services to individual and institutional investors.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDbL.label: Ocularist Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDbL.definition: Negligent or wrongful conduct by an ocularist, such as improper fitting or fabrication of an artificial eye, resulting in harm to the patient, which may give rise to a medical malpractice claim.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDbP.label: Job Search
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDbP.definition: Job search refers to the process of looking for employment opportunities in a specific field or industry. This activity often involves creating a resume, applying for jobs through various channels such as online job boards or company websites, networking, and participating in interviews. It is frequently a requirement for receiving certain types of public benefits, such as unemployment insurance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDbP.label: US Chapter 11 - Small Business Debtors
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDbP.definition: Chapter 11 of the United States Bankruptcy Code allows small businesses to restructure their debts while continuing operations under court supervision. It provides a mechanism for small businesses to create a repayment plan to satisfy creditors and emerge as a viable entity.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDbT.label: Georgia Superior Court - Fayette County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDbT.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Fayette County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has the authority to hear and decide civil and criminal cases within Fayette County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDbY.label: Special Economic Zone
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDbY.definition: A Special Economic Zone (SEZ) is a designated geographic area that is subject to unique economic regulations and policies, distinct from the rest of the geography, to promote foreign investment, economic growth, and job creation. These zones often offer tax incentives, simplified export-import procedures, and other regulatory relaxations to attract businesses.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDba.label: 690 Other Nature of Suit (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDba.definition: Action primarily based on Acts or Bills that cannot be classified under any other nature of suit, such as: Endangered Species Act, Federal Hazardous Substance Act 15:1261, Game & Wildlife Act 15:256C et seq. (Penalty), Federal Trade Commission Act 15:41-51 (Penalty), Federal Coal Mine Health & Safety Act 30:801 et seq. (Penalty), Load Line Act 46:85-85G, McGuire Bill (Federal Fair Trade) 15:45L Penalty, Marihuana Tax Act 50 STAT 551, Motorboat Act 46:526-526T, National Traffic & Motor Vehicle Safety Act penalty 49:1655, Veterans' Benefit Act, Title 38 Penalty.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDbb.label: Women's Suffrage Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDbb.definition: A Women's Suffrage claim is a legal assertion that a government has denied or restricted the right to vote to citizens on the basis of sex, effectively providing women the right to vote.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDbb.label: Assumption of Lease Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDbb.definition: An Assumption of Lease Clause is a provision in a contract that obligates a party to take over the rights and obligations of an existing lease agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDbh.label: Liability for Breach of Contract Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDbh.definition: Liability for Breach of Contract Clause refers to the legal responsibility that arises when a party fails to fulfill their obligations as outlined in a specific clause within a contract.
english_labels: Liability for Breach of Contract Clause

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDbm.label: Production of Documents Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDbm.definition: The Production of Documents Practice refers to the specific legal practice of collecting and producing documents in the course of a legal matter, which falls under the broader category of Document Collection and Production Practice.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDbn.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Monroe County (20th Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Monroe County (20th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDbr.label: Recognition of Foreign Restructuring Objectives
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDbr.definition: Recognition of foreign restructuring involves the acknowledgment and enforcement of a foreign insolvency proceeding by domestic courts. In the U.S., Chapter 15 of the Bankruptcy Code facilitates this process, allowing foreign debtors to access U.S. courts to protect their assets and restructure their debts under international cooperation principles.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDbw.label: Reverse Mortgage Foreclosure
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDbw.definition: Reverse Mortgage Foreclosure is the legal process in which a lender takes possession of a property after the borrower, typically an older homeowner, fails to meet the conditions of the reverse mortgage agreement. This can occur due to reasons like the death of the borrower, failure to pay property taxes or insurance, or permanently moving out of the home. The property is then sold to repay the loan balance and any associated costs

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDby.label: Agent’s Liability for Principal’s Obligation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDby.definition: The concept of "Agent's Liability for Principal's Obligation" refers to the legal responsibility of an agent to fulfill the obligations of their principal, such as paying debts or fulfilling contracts, and being held liable for any failure to do so.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDbz.label: Civil Remedies / Relief Sought
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDbz.definition: Civil Remedies/Relief Sought refers to the legal actions or requests made by a party in a civil litigation case to obtain a specific remedy or relief, such as monetary damages, injunctions, or declaratory judgments.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDc0.label: Retaliatory Constructive Discharge
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDc0.definition: An employer's action of making working conditions intolerable for an employee with the intention of forcing them to quit, in response to the employee's protected activity, such as reporting discrimination or harassment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDc1.label: Central Khmer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDc1.definition: Central Khmer is a language that belongs to the Language top-level class and is spoken in Cambodia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDc3.label: Vacancy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDc3.definition: Vacancy refers to the state of a property or space being unoccupied or not in use. This can occur in both residential and commercial real estate, indicating that no tenant or occupant currently resides or operates in the property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDc5.label: Indiana Superior Court - Montgomery County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDc5.definition: Indiana Superior Court - Montgomery County: A court of general jurisdiction in Indiana that has the authority to hear and decide a wide range of legal cases within Montgomery County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDc5.label: Legend On Stock Certificates Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDc5.definition: A Legend On Stock Certificates Clause is a contractual clause that requires certain information to be printed on stock certificates, such as restrictions on transfer or ownership.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDc7.label: Prime Brokerage Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDc7.definition: A Prime Brokerage Agreement is a contract between a prime brokerage firm and a client, usually a large institutional investor such as a hedge fund, wherein the firm agrees to provide a range of services. These services often include securities lending, leveraged trade execution, cash management, and custodial services, tailored to support the client's investment operations and risk management strategies.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDc9.label: Nation-Provided Public Benefit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDc9.definition: Nation-provided public benefit refers to social assistance programs that are administered and funded by a country's federal or national government. Examples include national healthcare systems, unemployment insurance, and pension schemes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDcE.label: Wolof
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDcE.definition: Wolof is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary, and is a language used in legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDcH.label: Big Valley Band of Pomo Indians of the Big Valley Rancheria
english_labels: Big Valley Band of Pomo Indians of the Big Valley Rancheria

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDcM.label: Mississippi Court of Chancery
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDcM.definition: The Mississippi Court of Chancery is a specific court within the Mississippi State Courts system that has jurisdiction over equity cases, such as trusts and estates, and is responsible for administering proceedings related to those cases.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDcQ.label: Cumulative Objection
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDcQ.definition: An Objection to Cumulative Evidence is raised when a party in a legal proceeding believes that the evidence being presented is repetitive and does not add any new information to the case. This objection aims to prevent the unnecessary prolongation of the proceeding and to avoid undue emphasis on certain evidence.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDcQ.label: Consignee Liability for Damaged Art
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDcQ.definition: The legal responsibility of the recipient of art to compensate for any damage that occurs during transportation or storage, as a subset of the broader concept of agent liability.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDcV.label: Tibetan
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDcV.definition: A language spoken in Tibet and surrounding regions, characterized by its unique grammar and vocabulary.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDcY.label: Florida County Court - Okeechobee County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDcY.definition: A court located in Okeechobee County, Florida that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within the county.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDca.label: UTBMS MF31 Executive Compensation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDca.definition: UTBMS MF31 Executive Compensation refers to a specific code within the UTBMS Mergers and Acquisitions (M&A) classification system used to categorize legal services related to executive compensation in corporate mergers and acquisitions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDci.label: Specialized Design Services Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDci.definition: This industry group comprises establishments providing specialized design services (except architectural, engineering, and computer systems design).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDci.label: Motion in Limine to Exclude Evidence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDci.definition: A Motion in Limine to Exclude Evidence is a request made by a party in a legal case to prevent certain evidence from being presented at trial.
english_labels: Motion in Limine to Exclude Evidence

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDcp.label: Khasi
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDcp.definition: Khasi is a language that belongs to the Language top-level class and is spoken in parts of India and Bangladesh.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDcp.label: Oromo
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDcp.definition: A language spoken by the Oromo people, primarily in Ethiopia and Kenya.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDcq.label: Interference with Economic Relations
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDcq.definition: The concept of Interference with Economic Relations refers to the intentional and unjustified interference with a business relationship or contract, resulting in economic harm to one or more parties involved.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDcu.label: Vague and Ambiguous Objection
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDcu.definition: A Vague and Ambiguous Objection is raised when a party in a legal proceeding believes that a question posed by the opposing counsel is unclear, lacks specificity, or could be interpreted in multiple ways. This objection aims to ensure that questions are precise and understandable, facilitating accurate and relevant responses.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDcw.label: Reentry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDcw.definition: The concept of "Reentry" refers to the process of a tenant returning to a rental property after being evicted or leaving voluntarily, and the legal issues that may arise in relation to this return.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDcx.label: Probate Reason of Modification/Change in Guardianship or Conservatorship
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDcx.definition: A Probate Reason of Modification/Change in Guardianship or Conservatorship refers to the specific reason for a subsequent probate filing related to a change or modification in the appointed guardian or conservator for an individual.
english_labels: Probate Reason of Modification/Change in Guardianship or Conservatorship

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDcy.label: Commodities Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDcy.definition: Law governing commodities and futures trading activities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDcz.label: Emergency Doctrine
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDcz.definition: Defendant did not have to obtain the patient's informed consent to perform the medical procedure because an emergency existed.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDd4.label: Non-Litigation Recovery Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDd4.definition: A Non-Litigation Recovery Practice is a specialized area of legal practice that involves the analysis and recovery of assets outside of the courtroom setting.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDd5.label: Salvage
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDd5.definition: The concept of Salvage refers to the legal remedy of recovering property or goods that have been lost or damaged, typically through the efforts of a third party who is entitled to compensation for their services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDd6.label: Class Action Notice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDd6.definition: A Class Action Notice is a formal written communication that informs a group of people that they are part of a legal action and provides them with information about their rights and options in the case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDd8.label: Washington Superior Court - Spokane County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDd8.definition: Washington Superior Court - Spokane County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Washington, located in Spokane County and responsible for hearing civil and criminal cases within its jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdF.label: Ransomware Attack
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdF.definition: In a ransomware attack, malicious software encrypts a victim's data and demands payment (usually in cryptocurrency) to restore access. Failure to pay often results in the permanent loss of the encrypted data.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdG.label: Cybersecurity Negligence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdG.definition: Failure to exercise reasonable care in protecting computer systems and data from unauthorized access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification, or destruction, resulting in harm or damage to individuals or organizations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdL.label: Hobbies Market Segment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdL.definition: The hobbies market segment refers to a division of the market that is specifically targeted towards consumers who are interested in activities and products related to leisure and recreational pursuits. This segment encompasses products and marketing strategies that are designed to cater to the needs, preferences, and interests of individuals who seek to engage in hobbies for relaxation, enjoyment, and personal fulfillment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdL.label: Municipal Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdL.definition: A Municipal Court is a type of court that has jurisdiction over cases involving violations of local ordinances and state laws within a specific city or town.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdM.label: Intellectual Property Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdM.definition: Law protecting the legal rights to inventions, designs, and artistic works.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdR.label: Minnesota District Court - Waseca County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdR.definition: Minnesota District Court - Waseca County: A specific court within the Minnesota District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Waseca County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdU.label: Consular Dependent Application
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdU.definition: "Consular Dependent Application" relates to the process by which family members of valid non-immigrant visa holders (in the U.S., A-1, A-2, A-3) apply for their own visas to accompany the principal visa holder to the destination country (e.g., U.S.).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdW.label: Early Termination Right Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdW.definition: An Early Termination Right Clause is a provision in a contract that allows one or both parties to end the agreement before its scheduled expiration date under certain circumstances.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdY.label: Santee Indian Nation of South Carolina
english_labels: Santee Indian Nation of South Carolina

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdZ.label: Article 2 Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdZ.definition: An Article II claim refers to a legal assertion grounded in the provisions of Article II of the U.S. Constitution, which defines the powers and responsibilities of the Executive Branch, primarily the President. A claim could arise when there's a dispute over the interpretation or application of these powers, including issues related to executive orders, presidential authority, or the conduct of foreign affairs.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdb.label: Massachusetts Superior Court - Norfolk County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdb.definition: The Massachusetts Superior Court - Norfolk County is a court of general jurisdiction in Massachusetts that hears civil and criminal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdg.label: Corporation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdg.definition: An organization formed with state governmental approval to act as an artificial person that is empowered with legal rights usually only reserved for individuals, such as to sue and be sued, issue shares of stock to raise funds (unless it is non-profit), own property, hire employees or loan and borrow money.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdj.label: Fee Billed
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdj.definition: Fee Billed: The amount of money charged by a lawyer to a client for legal services rendered, as specified in the engagement fee detail.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdo.label: Alternative Monthly Report
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdo.definition: An Alternative Monthly Report is a disclosure document typically filed by insiders or significant shareholders to report on their activities and holdings. It is often required by securities regulators on a monthly basis.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdo.label: Treble Damages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdo.definition: Treble damages refer to a type of monetary damages that are awarded to a plaintiff in a lawsuit and are three times the amount of actual damages suffered.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdq.label: Other Specific Goods and Services Tax Payment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdq.definition: Other Specific Goods and Services Tax Payment includes taxes on the extraction of minerals, fossil fuels, and other exhaustible resources from privately-owned deposits or those owned by another government, along with any other unallocable receipts from taxes on specific goods and services. These taxes are typically assessed as a fixed amount per unit of quality or weight, but can also be a percentage of value, and are recorded when the resources are extracted. Payments from the extraction of resources from government-owned deposits are classified as rent.
english_labels: Other Specific Goods and Services Tax Payment
Other Taxes on Specific Goods and Services

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdr.label: By Capped Fee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdr.definition: Engagement fee model where the parties agree upon a maximum cost (i.e., “cap”).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdt.label: Civil Court Proceeding
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdt.definition: A lawsuit; all or some part of a cause heard and determined by a court. Any legal step or action taken at the direction of, or by the authority of a court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdt.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Wright County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdt.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Wright County refers to a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Wright County, Missouri.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdy.label: Deed Restriction Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdy.definition: A deed restriction clause is a provision in a contract that limits the use or development of a property, typically in order to maintain certain standards or preserve certain rights.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdy.label: Polymyositis and Dermatomyositis
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdy.definition: Polymyositis and dermatomyositis are related disorders that are characterized by an inflammatory process in striated muscle, occurring alone or in association with other autoimmune disorders or malignancy. The most common manifestations are symmetric weakness, and less frequently, pain and tenderness of the proximal limb-girdle (shoulder or pelvic) musculature. There may also be involvement of the cervical, cricopharyngeal, esophageal, intercostal, and diaphragmatic muscles.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdz.label: Property Surface Right
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDdz.definition: Property Surface Right refers to the legal entitlement to use and control the surface of a piece of land, but not the air above it or the minerals below it. This right is often relevant in land leasing situations, such as when the subsurface rights are leased for mineral extraction while the surface rights are used for agricultural or residential purposes

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDe0.label: Contractual Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDe0.definition: A contract's clauses (e.g., choice of venue, force majeure, disclaimers).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDe2.label: New York City Court - Johnstown
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDe2.definition: A court located in Johnstown, New York that operates under the jurisdiction of the New York City Court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDe3.label: Clawback Provision Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDe3.definition: A Clawback Provision Clause is a contractual clause that allows a party to recover previously paid compensation or benefits from an employee or executive in certain circumstances, such as a financial restatement or misconduct.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDe6.label: Act of Co-employee Not Within the Scope of Employment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDe6.definition: An act of a fellow employee that falls outside the scope of their job duties and is not related to the employer's business or interests, which may not be compensable under industrial injury claims.
english_labels: Act of Co-employee Not Within the Scope of Employment

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDe9.label: Receipt Event
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDe9.definition: A Receipt Event refers to when a person or entity receives a letter, filing, or other document in a legal or administrative process. This event marks the point at which the relevant entity or authority officially acknowledges the submission, initiating the subsequent steps in the process, such as review, assessment, or response.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDeC.label: source_app
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDeC.definition: "The name of the program used to generate this invoice, e.g. ""Elite"". "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDeH.label: Visa for Diplomats and Foreign Government Officials
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDeH.definition: A visa for diplomats and foreign government officials is a specialized type of visa that allows individuals representing their home country's government to enter another country for official duties. These visas often come with certain privileges and immunities, as outlined by international law, to enable the holders to perform their roles effectively without legal hindrance.
english_labels: Visa for Diplomats and Foreign Government Officials

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDeH.label: Cree
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDeH.definition: A language spoken by the Cree people, which is a member of the Algonquian language family.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDeI.label: Mortgage Holder Breaching Escrow Obligations
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDeI.definition: The Mortgage Holder Breaching Escrow Obligations concept refers to the situation where a party who holds a mortgage fails to fulfill their obligation to properly manage and disburse funds held in escrow for taxes, insurance, or other related expenses.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDeJ.label: Civil Union
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDeJ.definition: A civil union is a legally recognized arrangement similar to marriage, which provides some of the legal and social protections afforded to married couples. However, it may lack some of the federal benefits and recognition that come with marriage.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDeR.label: Accommodation and Food Services Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDeR.definition: The Accommodation and Food Services industry group comprises establishments providing customers with lodging and/or preparing meals, snacks, and beverages for immediate consumption. The sector includes both accommodation and food services establishments because the two activities are often combined at the same establishment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDeT.label: Exchange
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDeT.definition: An exchange is a marketplace where securities, commodities, derivatives and other financial instruments are traded.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDeW.label: Spousal Support
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDeW.definition: Spousal support refers to the financial assistance provided by one spouse to the other after separation or divorce, typically to maintain the standard of living established during the marriage.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDeX.label: Rest Break Violation Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDeX.definition: A rest break violation claim is a legal action initiated by an employee against their employer for not complying with the legal requirement to provide rest breaks of a certain duration during the workday. The claim typically arises when an employer either denies or interrupts the rest break, does not provide the break in accordance with applicable labor laws, or requires the employee to perform work duties during the rest break. In some cases, employers may also be liable for rest break violations if they do not compensate employees for certain types of work performed during rest breaks.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDeZ.label: Student
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDeZ.definition: A student is an individual who is enrolled in an educational institution, such as a school, college, or university, for the purpose of acquiring knowledge, skills, and qualifications. Students engage in a structured learning process to pursue academic or vocational goals, typically under the guidance of teachers or instructors.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDeb.label: Missouri Circuit Court - McDonald County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDeb.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - McDonald County refers to a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in McDonald County, Missouri.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDef.label: Small Intestine Transplantation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDef.definition: Small intestine transplantation is a surgical procedure where a diseased or non-functional small intestine is replaced with a healthy donor intestine. This transplant is typically performed for patients with severe intestinal failure or dysfunction who cannot absorb nutrients effectively through other means.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDef.label: Breakup Fee Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDef.definition: A Breakup Fee Clause is a provision in a contract that requires one party to pay a specified amount of money to the other party if the contract is terminated before completion.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDej.label: Commodities - Assets
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDej.definition: Commodities are basic goods or raw materials that are interchangeable with other goods of the same type and used as a basis for creating other goods and services. As investment assets, they can be traded on exchanges and include metals, energy resources, agricultural products, and more, offering diversification benefits but also subject to market volatility.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDes.label: Intern
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDes.definition: An intern is an individual, often a student, who works temporarily for an organization to gain practical experience in a specific industry. Internships can be paid or unpaid and are often seen as a stepping stone to full-time employment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDes.label: Wetland
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDes.definition: A Wetland Area is a type of land area characterized by the presence of water, either permanently or seasonally, and hosts specific types of vegetation and wildlife adapted to saturated conditions. Wetland areas are often subject to environmental regulations aimed at their protection, management, and conservation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDf1.label: Indiana Town Court - Marion County, Center Twp.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDf1.definition: A court located in Marion County, Center Township, Indiana that has limited jurisdiction over minor criminal offenses, traffic violations, and small claims cases.
english_labels: Indiana Town Court - Marion County, Center Twp.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDf1.label: Dual Capacity Doctrine
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDf1.definition: The Dual Capacity Doctrine is a legal concept that allows an injured employee to sue their employer in a capacity other than their employer, such as a manufacturer or seller of a defective product, in addition to receiving workers' compensation benefits.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDf2.label: Rights of the Disabled
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDf2.definition: Rights of the disabled refer to the legal and ethical entitlements designed to ensure that individuals with disabilities have equal access to opportunities and resources, free from discrimination. These rights may include accessible public facilities, reasonable workplace accommodations, and equal educational opportunities, and are often supported by both international treaties and national laws.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDf4.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Greene County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDf4.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court in Greene County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court system that has jurisdiction over minor criminal offenses and civil cases.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Greene County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDf4.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Gentry County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDf4.definition: A Missouri Circuit Court in Gentry County is a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Gentry County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDfE.label: A100 Activities
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDfE.definition: A100 Activities refer to the specific tasks involved in the UTBMS Litigation code set, including communicating with clients and outside counsel, managing data and files, conducting research, drafting and revising documents, and appearing for/attending hearings or meetings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDfP.label: County Liability
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDfP.definition: County Liability refers to the legal responsibility of a county government for any harm or damage caused to individuals or property due to the actions or negligence of the county or its employees.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDfQ.label: Maine Superior Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDfQ.definition: The Maine Superior Court is a court of general jurisdiction within the Maine State Courts system, with authority to hear civil and criminal cases.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDfQ.label: Motion to Dismiss Case for Abuse
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDfQ.definition: A Motion to Dismiss Case for Abuse is a legal request made by a party in a bankruptcy case to terminate the proceedings due to the debtor's alleged abuse of the bankruptcy system.
english_labels: Motion to Dismiss Case for Abuse

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDfV.label: Subject Person Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDfV.definition: A Subject Person Clause is a clause in a contract that identifies a specific individual or group of individuals who will be affected by the terms of the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDfV.label: Washington Superior Court - Lewis County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDfV.definition: Washington Superior Court - Lewis County is a specific court within the Washington Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Lewis County, Washington.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDfW.label: New York Supreme Court - St. Lawrence County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDfW.definition: The New York Supreme Court - St. Lawrence County is a court of general jurisdiction located in St. Lawrence County, New York, with authority to hear and decide legal disputes within its geographical jurisdiction.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - St. Lawrence County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDfZ.label: Physical Intrusion
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDfZ.definition: Physical intrusion, also known as Breaking and entering, is the act of entering a building or other property without authorization. It can also include entering through fraud, threats, or collusion.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDfd.label: Variable Rate Dividend Payment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDfd.definition: Variable Rate Payment, also known as Adjustable Rate Payment, refers to a type of dividend income where the dividend rate is periodically adjusted, typically based on a benchmark yield or market interest rates. This adjustment allows the dividend payments to fluctuate with changing economic conditions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDfd.label: Retail Trade Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDfd.definition: The Retail Trade industry group comprises establishments engaged in retailing merchandise, generally without transformation, and rendering services incidental to the sale of merchandise. The retailing process is the final step in the distribution of merchandise; retailers are, therefore, organized to sell merchandise in small quantities to the general public. This sector comprises two main types of retailers: store and nonstore retailers.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDfe.label: Underage Betting
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDfe.definition: Underage Betting refers to the illegal practice of individuals below the legal age limit participating in gambling activities, either online or at physical venues. This activity violates gambling laws and regulations designed to protect minors from the risks associated with gambling.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDfg.label: matter_tax_on_fees
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDfg.definition: "Sum of all TAX_SUMMARY.total_tax_on_fees for matter/invoice. This figure includes Withholding Taxes but not Tiered Taxes. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDfi.label: Finno-Ugrian languages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDfi.definition: The Finno-Ugrian languages are a group of languages that belong to the Language class and include Finnish, Estonian, and Hungarian, among others.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDft.label: Virginia State Bar District Committee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDft.definition: A Virginia State Bar District Committee is a sub-division of the Virginia State Courts responsible for administering and overseeing legal proceedings within a specific geographic area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDfw.label: Pets
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDfw.definition: Pets are domesticated animals kept primarily for companionship, enjoyment, or protection rather than for commercial or agricultural purposes. They include a wide variety of animals such as dogs, cats, birds, and reptiles, each governed by specific regulations and care standards.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDg7.label: Grand Traverse Band of Ottawa and Chippewa Indians
english_labels: Grand Traverse Band of Ottawa and Chippewa Indians

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgB.label: Probate due to Financial Exploitation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgB.definition: Probate due to Financial Exploitation: The legal process of distributing the assets of a deceased person who was financially exploited during their lifetime, as a reason for filing a probate case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgE.label: Exclusivity Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgE.definition: An exclusivity clause is a provision in a contract that restricts one or more parties from engaging in certain activities or relationships with others, as agreed upon in the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgG.label: State Legislator
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgG.definition: A State Legislator is an elected official who serves as a member of a state's legislative body, responsible for drafting, debating, and voting on state laws and policies. This individual represents a specific district or constituency within the state and participates in the legislative process, including committee work, budget approval, and oversight of state agencies.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgL.label: Marital Status
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgL.definition: Marital Status refers to the legal state of being single, married, divorced, separated, or widowed, for an individual person. This concept is considered in several areas of law (e.g., Tax Law, Bankruptcy Law)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgM.label: Excludes National Entitlements
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgM.definition: In immigration law, the term "Does Not Establish Federal Benefits" often appears on identification documents issued by states to indicate that these documents are not sufficient to establish eligibility for federal benefits or entitlements. In the U.S., this is relevant in the context of the Real ID Act, which sets forth the federal standards that state-issued identification must meet for various purposes, including access to certain federally regulated facilities and federal benefits

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgO.label: Washington Superior Court - Douglas County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgO.definition: Washington Superior Court - Douglas County refers to a specific court within the Washington Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Douglas County, Washington.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgV.label: Motion to Supplement Record
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgV.definition: A Motion to Supplement Record is a formal request made to a higher court to add additional evidence or information to the existing record on appeal.
english_labels: Motion to Supplement Record on Appeal

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgW.label: Document Collection and Production Events
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgW.definition: Document Collection and Production Events refer to the events that occur during the process of collecting and producing documents in the context of legal discovery.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgY.label: No Contact
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgY.definition: No Contact: A condition of a criminal disposition that prohibits any communication or physical contact between the offender and the victim or other specified individuals.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgZ.label: Non-Hearsay Out-of-Court Statement Objective
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgZ.definition: A Non-Hearsay Out-of-Court Statement Objective refers to a purpose for admitting an out-of-court statement into evidence that does not rely on the truth of the content of the statement itself. This includes statements not offered for the truth of the matter asserted, nonassertive conduct, non-propositions, verbal acts, and "statements" made by a declarant that is not a person, such as a machine or device.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgb.label: Curfew, Loitering, and Vagrancy Violations
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgb.definition: The violation of a court order, regulation, ordinance, or law requiring the withdrawal of persons from the streets or other specified areas; prohibiting persons from remaining in an area or place in an idle or aimless manner; or prohibiting persons from going from place to place without visible means of support.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgc.label: INVOICE_NUMBER
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgc.definition: A unique identifier assigned to an invoice, as defined in the LEDES98BI V5 Format Rev 1-2020 standard.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgc.label: Cash Management Motion
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgc.definition: A Cash Management Motion is a request made in a bankruptcy case for authorization to continue managing and using cash and financial assets in the ordinary course of business.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgf.label: Florida Circuit Court - Lee County - 20th Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgf.definition: The Florida Circuit Court - Lee County (20th Circuit Court) is a specific court within the Florida Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Lee County.
english_labels: Florida Circuit Court - Lee County - 20th Circuit Court

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgf.label: Counter-Claimant
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgf.definition: A person who brings a counterclaim (e.g., a defendant who asserts a claim against a plaintiff).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgj.label: Motor Vehicle Dealership Liability
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgj.definition: Motor Vehicle Dealership Liability refers to the legal responsibility of a car dealership for any harm or damages caused to a customer or third party as a result of the dealership's actions or negligence in the sale or maintenance of a vehicle.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgo.label: War or Terrorism Language
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgo.definition: War or Terrorism Language refers to clauses in contracts, often in merger and acquisition agreements, that address the implications or consequences of war, acts of terrorism, or related geopolitical events. These provisions can dictate how risks associated with such events are allocated between parties, specify circumstances under which obligations might be suspended or terminated due to these events, or provide conditions for renegotiation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgp.label: Brokerage Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgp.definition: A Brokerage Agreement is a contract between an investor and a brokerage firm allowing the latter to act as the investor's agent in buying and selling securities. The agreement stipulates commission fees, account terms, and other conditions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgr.label: Trainee Visa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgr.definition: A Trainee Visa is a type of visa that allows foreign nationals to enter a country for the purpose of participating in a training or internship program. This type of visa is often designed to provide individuals with an opportunity to gain practical experience, skills, and knowledge in a specific field.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgt.label: New Jersey Superior Court - Sussex County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgt.definition: The New Jersey Superior Court - Sussex County is a specific court within the New Jersey Superior Court Appellate Division that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Sussex County, New Jersey.
english_labels: New Jersey Superior Court - Sussex County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgx.label: Visa for Families of Specialty Occupation Workers from Australia
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgx.definition: The visa for families of Specialty Occupation Workers from Australia, often associated with the E-3D visa in the United States, allows the spouse and dependent children of an E-3 visa holder to accompany them to the U.S. While the primary E-3 visa holder is authorized to work in a specialty occupation, the family members may also apply for work authorization, subject to certain conditions and limitations.
english_labels: Visa for Families of Specialty Occupation Workers from Australia

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgz.label: Nogai
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDgz.definition: Nogai is a language that belongs to the Turkic language family and is spoken primarily in Russia and Kazakhstan.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDh0.label: Matrimonial Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDh0.definition: Laws relating to marriage, civil unions, and domestic partnerships.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDh4.label: 04_3 Bankruptcy (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDh4.definition: 04_3 Bankruptcy (PACER NoS) refers to the specific category within the PACER Nature of Suit (NoS) Codes that deals with bankruptcy cases filed in federal court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDh5.label: Deficiency Judgment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDh5.definition: A deficiency judgment is a legal ruling issued by a court when the proceeds from the sale of a foreclosed property are insufficient to cover the outstanding debt owed by the borrower to the lender. This judgment allows the lender to pursue the borrower for the remaining balance of the debt after the sale of the property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDh5.label: 370 Other Fraud (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDh5.definition: Action primarily based on fraud relating to personal property that cannot be classified under any other nature of suit. (Excludes any property that is not real property)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDh6.label: Motion for Interlocutory Appeal
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDh6.definition: A Motion for Interlocutory Appeal is a request made to a higher court to review a decision made by a trial court before the trial has concluded.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDhA.label: New Mexico Magistrate Court - Quay County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDhA.definition: A court located in Quay County, New Mexico that has limited jurisdiction over certain types of cases.
english_labels: New Mexico Magistrate Court - Quay County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDhD.label: Fax Communication
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDhD.definition: A communication that occurs via facsimile (fax).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDhK.label: Lockup Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDhK.definition: A Lockup Agreement is a contract between a company's insiders and underwriters that prohibits the insiders from selling their shares for a specified period post-initial public offering (IPO). This helps stabilize the stock price after the IPO by preventing an influx of shares onto the market.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDhT.label: Divorce
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDhT.definition: The legal process of ending a marriage, either due to fault or without fault, including issues such as property division, child custody, and spousal support.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDhT.label: Agoraphobia
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDhT.definition: Agoraphobia is an anxiety disorder characterized by an intense fear of being in situations where escape might be difficult or help unavailable during a panic attack. This fear often leads to avoidance of a variety of situations, such as being outside alone, being in a crowd, or traveling in a vehicle, which can significantly impair daily functioning and social interactions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDhX.label: Use of Proceeds Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDhX.definition: A Use of Proceeds Clause is a provision in a contract that specifies how the funds received from a transaction will be allocated and used.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDhZ.label: Motor Vehicle Negligence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDhZ.definition: Motor Vehicle Negligence refers to a legal claim for damages resulting from the careless or reckless operation of a motor vehicle, which causes injury or harm to another person.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDhh.label: Finance and Lending Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDhh.definition: Law supporting the function of providing loans or other financing to businesses or individuals.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDho.label: Motion to Request Publication of Memorandum Disposition
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDho.definition: A Motion to Request Publication of Memorandum Disposition is a formal request made to an appellate court to publish a memorandum disposition, which is a written statement summarizing the court's decision, in order to make it available for citation in future cases.
english_labels: Motion to Request Publication of Memorandum Disposition

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDhu.label: Binding Effect Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDhu.definition: A Binding Effect Clause is a clause in a contract that ensures that the terms and obligations of the contract are legally enforceable by all parties involved.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDhv.label: Regulatory Investigation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDhv.definition: A regulatory investigation is a formal inquiry conducted by a governmental or regulatory agency to examine whether laws, regulations, or industry standards have been violated. It aims to ensure compliance, enforce rules, and protect public interests in various sectors such as finance, healthcare, and environmental protection.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDi3.label: Sunflowers
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDi3.definition: Sunflowers are flowering plants from the Helianthus annuus species, known for their large, bright yellow blooms and edible seeds. They are cultivated for their seeds, which are used to produce oil, snacks, and bird feed, and are valued for their high nutritional content, including healthy fats and vitamins.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDi7.label: International Organization Employee Visa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDi7.definition: International Organization Employee Visa is a visa category for employees of designated international organizations (e.g., NATO, World Bank), allowing them to enter the U.S. to perform official duties. This category includes G-1 to G-5 visas, each corresponding to different levels and types of employees.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDi9.label: Sac and Fox Nation of Missouri in Kansas and Nebraska
english_labels: Sac and Fox Nation of Missouri in Kansas and Nebraska

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDiA.label: Motion to Dismiss Charge
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDiA.definition: A Motion to Dismiss Charge is a formal request made by a party in a legal case to dismiss a specific charge against them, typically due to a lack of evidence or legal basis for the charge.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDiB.label: Trial Transcripts Expense
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDiB.definition: Trial Transcripts Expense refers to the costs incurred for obtaining a written or recorded verbatim record of the proceedings that took place during a trial, including the testimony of witnesses, arguments of counsel, and rulings of the court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDiC.label: Monarch
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDiC.definition: A Monarch is a sovereign head of state, typically a king or queen, who reigns over a country or territory by hereditary right or election. This individual holds a position of supreme authority within a monarchy, often serving as both the ceremonial figurehead and, in some cases, an active participant in governance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDiD.label: Shadow Docket
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDiD.definition: The Shadow Docket refers to a set of decisions and orders issued by a court (e.g., the Supreme Court of the United States), without full briefing or oral argument. These decisions, often related to emergency appeals and procedural orders, can have significant legal implications but receive less public scrutiny and transparency than cases on the court's regular docket.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDiL.label: Matter Commentary
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDiL.definition: A Matter Commentary refers to comments or notes provided on a specific legal matter, often related to a filing or application.
