In the context of immigration, it could involve written remarks, explanations, or clarifications provided alongside documents or submissions to provide additional context or information for the reviewing authorities or parties involved

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDiL.label: Florida Circuit Court - Citrus County - 5th Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDiL.definition: A court located in Citrus County, Florida that is part of the larger Florida Circuit Court system.
english_labels: Florida Circuit Court - Citrus County - 5th Circuit Court

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDiR.label: Outlicense Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDiR.definition: An outlicense clause is a provision in a contract that allows one party to grant a license to use or sell a product or technology to another party outside of the original agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDiV.label: Receiver
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDiV.definition: A neutral person (often a professional trustee) appointed by a judge to take charge of the property and business of one of the parties to a lawsuit and receive his/her rents and profits while the right to the moneys has not been finally decided.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDiY.label: Invoice Start Date
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDiY.definition: The Invoice Start Date is a specific detail within the broader category of Fee Invoice Detail, referring to the date on which invoicing for legal services begins.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDif.label: Property Right to Profit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDif.definition: In civil law systems, the Right to Profit ("droit de prendre") refers to a real right that allows an individual or entity to enter another's land to extract resources like minerals, timber, or fish. This right is usually granted through a contract or license and is subject to the terms and conditions specified therein, as well as overarching legal regulations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDig.label: Dispute Service
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDig.definition: A process that describes a conflict/adversarial event potentially or actually involving a second party. This can include government entity or internal investigation

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDig.label: Lower Sioux Indian Community in the State of Minnesota
english_labels: Lower Sioux Indian Community in the State of Minnesota

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDin.label: Demotion
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDin.definition: Demotion is the reassignment of an employee to a lower rank, position, or salary grade, typically as a disciplinary measure or due to performance issues. This action reduces the employee's responsibilities, authority, and often their compensation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDiv.label: Long Form
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDiv.definition: A Long Form is an extensive version of a document that provides detailed terms, conditions, and provisions. It is used in various legal contexts, such as contracts, agreements, and reports, to ensure thorough coverage of all relevant aspects and legal requirements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDj7.label: Foreign Representative
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDj7.definition: A person or body authorized in a foreign proceeding to administer the reorganization or the liquidation of the debtor's assets or affairs or to act as a representative of such foreign proceeding. 11 U.S.C. § 101(24).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjA.label: Drag Along Rights Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjA.definition: A Drag Along Rights Clause is a provision in a contract that allows majority shareholders to force minority shareholders to sell their shares in the company if a certain percentage of the majority shareholders agree to sell their own shares.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjG.label: Tortious Breach of Contract
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjG.definition: The Tortious Breach of Contract is a legal concept that occurs when one party breaches a contract and causes harm or damages to the other party, resulting in a tort claim in addition to a breach of contract claim.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjG.label: Adversarial Machine Learning
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjG.definition: Adversarial Machine Learning refers to the study and design of algorithms that can withstand intentional manipulation or adversarial attacks. These attacks aim to deceive machine learning models by supplying deceptive inputs, highlighting vulnerabilities and the need for robust defenses in AI systems.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjM.label: Rescue of Prisoner
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjM.definition: The Rescue of Prisoner is a criminal act against the government that involves the unlawful liberation of a person who is being held in custody.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjN.label: Pre-Hearing Statement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjN.definition: A pre-hearing statement is a written document submitted before a legal proceeding that outlines the facts and arguments that a party intends to present at the hearing.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjO.label: Australian languages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjO.definition: Australian languages are a group of structured systems of communication, consisting of grammar and vocabulary, used in Australia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjR.label: Loan Consent Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjR.definition: A "Loan Consent Agreement" is a formalized contract that modifies the terms of an existing loan agreement, often requiring the consent of the lender, borrower, and sometimes third parties involved. The document specifies the changes to be made to the original terms, conditions, or covenants of the loan and serves as an official authorization for those modifications.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjS.label: Georgia District Court - Fulton County Magistrate Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjS.definition: A court located in Fulton County, Georgia that has limited jurisdiction over certain civil and criminal cases.
english_labels: Georgia District Court - Fulton County Magistrate Court

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjU.label: Parental Leave
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjU.definition: Parental leave is a type of leave granted to employees who are becoming parents, either through childbirth or adoption. It allows parents to take time off from work to care for and bond with their new child. Parental leave can be paid or unpaid, depending on company policies and government regulations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjU.label: Heir
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjU.definition: An heir is an individual legally entitled to inherit some or all of the estate of a deceased person under the laws of intestacy. The status of an heir typically depends on the relationship to the deceased and the hierarchy of succession established by law.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjZ.label: Timeshare Asset
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjZ.definition: Timeshares are a form of fractional ownership where multiple parties hold rights to use a property, typically a vacation home or resort unit, for a specific period each year. The ownership structure and usage rights can vary, but generally, timeshare owners are obligated to pay an initial purchase price along with recurring maintenance fees, and they may be able to exchange their timeshare for different locations through a network.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDje.label: Academic Publisher
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDje.definition: An academic publisher produces, distributes, and often oversees the peer-review process for scholarly works such as books, journals, and conference proceedings. In the legal field, academic publishers play a crucial role in disseminating legal scholarship, ensuring the quality and integrity of academic discourse by managing the peer-review process, and providing a platform for legal scholars, practitioners, and students to share their research and insights with the broader academic community and professionals in the field.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjf.label: Director Emeritus Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjf.definition: A Director Emeritus Clause is a provision in a contract that grants a former director of a company an honorary title and certain privileges, such as attending board meetings, without having any voting rights or responsibilities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjg.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Tioga County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjg.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Tioga County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering legal proceedings in Tioga County, Pennsylvania.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Tioga County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjm.label: Estimated Duration
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjm.definition: The Estimated Duration is a concept within Project Management Objectives that refers to the anticipated length of time required to complete a project or task.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjt.label: Bankruptcy Disbursement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjt.definition: The distribution of funds to creditors in a bankruptcy or restructuring event.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjy.label: School Expulsion
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDjy.definition: School expulsion is a severe disciplinary action taken by educational institutions in response to serious or persistent student misconduct or rule violations. It involves the permanent removal of a student from the school, preventing them from attending classes and participating in school activities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkB.label: Appendix
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkB.definition: An appendix is a document attached to a legal brief or filing that provides additional information or evidence to support the arguments made in the main document.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkF.label: Kansas District Court - Riley County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkF.definition: A court located in Riley County, Kansas that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkG.label: UTBMS MF40 Environmental
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkG.definition: A category within the UTBMS coding system used to classify legal services related to environmental issues in the context of mergers and acquisitions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkH.label: Motion to Exclude Hearsay Witness
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkH.definition: A Motion to Exclude Hearsay Witness is a legal request to prevent a witness from testifying in court based on the fact that their testimony is based on hearsay evidence.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkI.label: Private Placement Memorandum
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkI.definition: An Offering Memorandum is a legal document outlining the objectives, risks, and terms of an investment involved in a private offering. It is not registered with public securities regulators and is intended for accredited or sophisticated investors.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkK.label: Election
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkK.definition: An election is a formal decision-making process in which eligible individuals, often referred to as voters, select a choice or representative from among multiple candidates or options. Elections are used in democracies to fill various public offices or decide on legislation and public policy issues, ensuring that the will of the people is reflected in governance and leadership.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkL.label: Court-Appointed Expert
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkL.definition: An expert who is appointed by a court, judge, or judicial body.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkM.label: Failure to Signal Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkM.definition: A Failure to Signal Claim involves allegations that a driver has not used proper turn or lane change signals as required by traffic laws, leading potentially to misunderstandings or accidents on the road. Such claims are typically processed through traffic courts or administrative bodies and may result in fines or other penalties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkM.label: Nil Paid Letters
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkM.definition: Nil Paid Letters, also known as Unpaid Share Subscription Rights, are temporary documents issued by a company offering new shares to existing shareholders. These letters allow shareholders to trade the rights to subscribe to the new shares before payment is required, but they do not represent ownership until the shares are fully paid.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkQ.label: Provider First Name
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkQ.definition: The concept of "Provider First Name" refers to the given name of an individual who is a legal services provider.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkR.label: Quechua
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkR.definition: Quechua is a structured system of communication, both written and spoken, that is used in certain regions of South America and is a member of the Language top-level class.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkR.label: Motion to Deconsolidate Case Association
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkR.definition: A Motion to Deconsolidate Case Association is a request made in a bankruptcy case to separate it from another related case that was previously consolidated, allowing it to proceed independently.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkT.label: Estoppel by Deed
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkT.definition: A legal principle that prevents a party from denying the truth of a statement made in a deed or other legal document, when that party's previous actions or words have relied upon the truth of that statement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkW.label: Reserve Based Lending Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkW.definition: Reserve Based Lending Practice involves legal work focused on asset-based lending where the loan is secured by the value of a borrower's reserves.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkY.label: Plums
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkY.definition: Plums are smooth-skinned stone fruits from the Prunus genus, known for their juicy flesh and sweet-tart flavor. They are consumed fresh, dried as prunes, or used in cooking, baking, and preserves, valued for their vitamins, antioxidants, and dietary fiber.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkZ.label: Real Estate Lease
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkZ.definition: A Real Estate Lease is a contract wherein the owner (lessor) grants the right to occupy and use their property to another party (lessee) for a specified period in exchange for rental payments.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkZ.label: Demolition
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkZ.definition: Demolition is the process of tearing down or dismantling a building or structure, often to clear land for new construction or to remove unsafe or obsolete buildings. This process involves various techniques and machinery, including manual labor, wrecking balls, and controlled explosives, to safely and efficiently bring down the structure. The demolition may be the result of a legal proceeding (e.g., condemnation).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDka.label: Museums, Historical Sites, and Similar Institutions Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDka.definition: Industries in the Museums, Historical Sites, and Similar Institutions subsector engage in the preservation and exhibition of objects, sites, and natural wonders of historical, cultural, and/or educational value.
english_labels: Museums, Historical Sites, and Similar Institutions Industry

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDka.label: Application to Defer Fee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDka.definition: An Application to Defer Fee is a request made in the context of a bankruptcy proceeding to delay payment of a fee.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkc.label: L400 Trial Preparation and Trial
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkc.definition: L400 Trial Preparation and Trial refers to the process of preparing for and conducting a trial, including tasks such as drafting written motions, preparing expert witnesses, attending hearings, and making post-trial submissions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkc.label: No Parking Zone Violation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkc.definition: This infraction takes place when a vehicle is parked in an area explicitly designated as a "No Parking" zone, usually marked by signs or pavement markings. The driver is generally subject to a fine and may also have their vehicle towed.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkc.label: Analysis of Vendor Communications
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkc.definition: The concept of Analysis of Vendor Communications refers to the examination and evaluation of communications between a company and its vendors in order to assess the legal implications and potential risks associated with their commercial arrangements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDke.label: Purpose Specification Principle
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDke.definition: Purpose Specification is the privacy principle that the purposes for which personal data are collected should be specified not later than at the time of data collection and the subsequent use limited to the fulfilment of those purposes or such others as are not incompatible with those purposes and as are specified on each occasion of change of purpose.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkg.label: Status Report
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkg.definition: A status report is a written document that provides an update on the current state of a particular matter or situation, typically used in the context of legal proceedings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkj.label: Hostile Work Environment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkj.definition: A Hostile Work Environment is a type of work environment harassment where an employee is subjected to unwelcome and discriminatory behavior or conduct that is severe or pervasive enough to create an intimidating, hostile, or offensive work environment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkj.label: Telugu
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkj.definition: Telugu is a structured system of communication, consisting of grammar and vocabulary, used in legal matters, which is a member of the Language class and is primarily spoken in the Indian states of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkk.label: Examination Under Oath
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkk.definition: A formal proceeding often used by insurance companies to obtain information about a claim — usually before a suit is filed.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkk.label: Georgia District Court - Early County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkk.definition: Georgia District Court - Early County is a specific court within the Georgia District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Early County, Georgia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkn.label: Retention Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkn.definition: A Retention Related Agreement is a legally binding contract between an employer and an employee, often a key or high-value employee, with the aim of retaining the employee within the company for a specified period. This type of agreement typically includes provisions for financial incentives, such as bonuses or stock options, and may also outline conditions or obligations the employee must meet to receive these incentives. The primary goal is to encourage employee loyalty and discourage them from leaving the organization during a critical period.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkq.label: Article 1 Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkq.definition: An Article I claim refers to a legal argument based on the provisions of Article I of the U.S. Constitution, which outlines the powers, limits, and functions of the legislative branch. Such a claim might arise when there is a dispute over the exercise or limitation of these powers, including matters related to taxation, regulation of commerce, or the creation and enforcement of laws.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkw.label: Action Prohibited/Omission Required by the Agreement Language
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkw.definition: A requirement to refrain from certain actions or to perform certain omissions as specified in the language of an agreement, which is a carveout from the definition of Material Adverse Effect (MAE).
english_labels: Action Prohibited/Omission Required by the Agreement Language

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkw.label: Discrimination Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkw.definition: Protection from discrimination on grounds such as race, gender, sexual orientation, national origin, color, age, political affiliation, ethnicity, religion, and disability.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkx.label: LEDES98BI V5 Format Rev 1-2020
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkx.definition: LEDES98BI V5 Format Rev 1-2020 is a standardized format for electronic legal invoices, including specific data elements such as invoice date, client name, matter name, timekeeper information, and line item details.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkx.label: Private Attorneys General Act Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDkx.definition: The Private Attorneys General Act (PAGA) is a California law that allows employees to bring claims on behalf of the state against their employers for labor code violations. By acting as private attorneys general, employees can seek penalties for themselves and their co-workers, thereby helping to enforce labor laws when government agencies may lack the resources to do so.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDky.label: Central Council of the Tlingit and Haida Indian Tribes
english_labels: Central Council of the Tlingit and Haida Indian Tribes

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDl6.label: Promise to Appear
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDl6.definition: A Promise to Appear is a legal document filed in trial court practice that requires a defendant to appear in court at a specified time and date.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDl9.label: Foster Parent
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDl9.definition: A parent through the foster-care system.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlD.label: Minnesota District Court - Court of App.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlD.definition: Minnesota District Court - Court of App. is a specific court within the Minnesota District Court system that hears appeals from lower courts.
english_labels: Minnesota District Court - Court of App.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlE.label: New York City Court - Rome
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlE.definition: A court located in Rome, New York City that operates under the jurisdiction of the New York City Court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlJ.label: Dargwa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlJ.definition: Dargwa is a language that belongs to the Language top-level class and is spoken in the North Caucasus region of Russia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlL.label: Malagasy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlL.definition: Malagasy is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary, used in legal matters, that is specific to the Malagasy people and culture.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlM.label: Sole Proprietorship
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlM.definition: A sole proprietorship, also known as the sole trader, individual entrepreneurship or proprietorship, is a type of enterprise that is owned and run by one person and in which there is no legal distinction between the owner and the business entity. The sole trader receives all profits (subject to taxation specific to the business) and has unlimited responsibility for all losses and debts. Every asset of the business is owned by the proprietor and all debts of the business are the proprietor's. It is a "sole" proprietorship in contrast with partnerships (which have at least two owners).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlM.label: Government Contracts Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlM.definition: Laws relating to contracts in which the government is a party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlM.label: Government Representative
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlM.definition: A Government Representative refers to any individual who acts on behalf of a governmental body, whether they are an elected official, an appointed official, or a regular employee. The term encompasses a wide range of roles, from high-ranking government officials who make policy decisions to government employees who carry out administrative tasks, all serving the interests of the state or public they represent.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlO.label: Storm in Progress
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlO.definition: A "Storm in Progress" is a legal concept within the context of civil defenses and litigation, referring to a situation where a legal matter is currently ongoing and actively being pursued.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlU.label: Farmland
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlU.definition: In legal services, Farmland relates to areas designated for agricultural activities, with specific legal frameworks for land use, agricultural labor, and contractual agreements for sale or lease. Issues can range from zoning laws to crop patents.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlY.label: Committed Relationship Partner
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlY.definition: A Committed Relationship Partner is an individual who is in a stable, long-term relationship characterized by mutual commitment, love, and shared responsibilities, but not necessarily legally recognized as a spouse. This status implies a serious, ongoing partnership that may include cohabitation and joint decision-making in various aspects of life.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlb.label: Spouse Liable for Other Spouse’s Debt
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlb.definition: When one spouse is responsible for the debt of the other spouse, typically due to a joint account or co-signing a loan.
english_labels: Spouse Liable for Other Spouse’s Debt

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlh.label: Pleura or Mediastinum Cancer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlh.definition: Pleura or mediastinum cancer refers to malignant tumors originating in the pleura, the thin tissue covering the lungs and lining the chest cavity, or in the mediastinum, the central compartment of the thoracic cavity. These cancers can significantly affect respiratory function and often require complex diagnostic and therapeutic approaches due to their proximity to vital structures.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlj.label: JD00 ADR / Settlement (UK J-CODE)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlj.definition: Work that is directed to settlement including ADR

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlk.label: Prior Identification
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlk.definition: Prior Identification is a statement made by a witness identifying a person after perceiving them, which is admissible as non-hearsay evidence if the witness testifies at a trial or hearing and is subject to cross-examination concerning the statement. This rule allows for the admission of identification statements made by a witness during or shortly after observing the person in question, including statements made while identifying the person in a photo or lineup.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlp.label: inv_currency
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlp.definition: "The currency for this invoice. Use ISO 4217 currency codes set forth by International Standards Organization (www.iso.org.). "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlr.label: Chinese
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlr.definition: Chinese (Language) is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary, used in legal matters as a means of document, artifact, evidence, testimony, proceeding, or any other legal aspect.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlv.label: Petition
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlv.definition: A petition is a formal written request submitted to a court or other authority, typically seeking a specific legal action or remedy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlz.label: Lobbying
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlz.definition: The act of pleading for or arguing in favor of something or actively supporting a cause or proposal; the act of attempting to influence the actions, policies, or decisions of officials in their daily life, most often legislators or members of regulatory agencies.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlz.label: Investment Adviser Registration Document
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDlz.definition: An Investment Adviser Registration Document is a formal document filed with the country's financial regulator (e.g., U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)) by investment advisers or other entities to register their services and provide essential information to the public and regulatory authorities. The document typically includes details about the entity's business practices, conflicts of interest, disciplinary information, and background of the principals.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDm1.label: Covenant in Deed Violated
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDm1.definition: A covenant in deed violated refers to a breach of a legally binding agreement related to property ownership or use, which can result in liability claims against the responsible party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDm4.label: Breach of Implied Warranty Against Infringement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDm4.definition: The Breach of Implied Warranty Against Infringement refers to a violation of an implied promise that a product or service does not infringe on the intellectual property rights of others, which can result in legal action against the party responsible for the breach.
english_labels: Breach of Implied Warranty Against Infringement

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDm4.label: Death Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDm4.definition: A Death Claim is a legal action seeking compensation for the death of an individual caused by the negligence or intentional act of another party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDm6.label: Savings Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDm6.definition: A savings clause is a clause in a contract that preserves certain rights or obligations even if other parts of the contract are found to be invalid or unenforceable.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDm9.label: Domestic Terrorism
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDm9.definition: The unlawful use of violence and intimidation, often against civilians, in order to achieve political or social objectives within the borders of a particular country.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmA.label: North American Tribes
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmA.definition: North American tribes refer to the various indigenous groups native to the North American continent, including tribes like the Navajo, Cherokee, Sioux, and Iroquois among many others. Each tribe has its own unique culture, language, and history, and they are recognized as the original inhabitants of specific regions within North America

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmC.label: Indiana Superior Court - Floyd County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmC.definition: Indiana Superior Court - Floyd County is a specific court within the Indiana Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over cases in Floyd County, Indiana.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmG.label: Impact Assessment Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmG.definition: Assessment of the environmental consequences (positive and negative) of a plan, policy, program, or actual projects prior to the decision to move forward with the proposed action.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmH.label: Appellate Practice Documents
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmH.definition: A document used in appellate practice.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmM.label: Small Estate Probate
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmM.definition: Small Estate Probate refers to a type of probate filing where the estate being administered is of relatively low value and can be settled without the need for a full probate process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmO.label: Shoeprint Evidence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmO.definition: Shoeprint evidence consists of marks or impressions left by shoes on various surfaces. These impressions can reveal patterns, sizes, and unique characteristics or wear of the shoe. Forensic experts analyze shoeprints to determine the type and brand of shoe, and sometimes even link it back to a specific pair of shoes or individual.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmP.label: Motion for Observation on Cross-Examination
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmP.definition: A Motion for Observation on Cross-Examination is a formal request made by a party in a trial court to allow them to observe the opposing party's cross-examination of a witness.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmQ.label: 08_3 Federal Tax Suits (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmQ.definition: 08_3 Federal Tax Suits (PACER NoS) refers to a specific category of legal cases related to federal tax disputes, as classified by the PACER Nature of Suit (NoS) Codes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmQ.label: Equity Commitment Letter
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmQ.definition: Equity Commitment Letter is a written promise by an investor or financial institution to provide a specified amount of equity capital to a company, usually under certain conditions. It's typically used to show commitment during financing rounds or mergers.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmU.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Macon County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmU.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Macon County refers to a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Macon County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmW.label: Appellate Court Judge
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmW.definition: A judge in an appellate court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmW.label: Minnesota District Court - Faribault County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmW.definition: Minnesota District Court - Faribault County refers to a specific court within the Minnesota District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Faribault County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmZ.label: Commitment to a Mental Health Facility
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmZ.definition: Commitment to a mental health facility refers to the legal process by which an individual is placed into a psychiatric hospital or clinic for treatment. This can be voluntary, with the individual's consent, or involuntary, often due to concerns about the person's safety or the safety of others, based on established legal criteria and medical evaluations.
english_labels: Commitment to a Mental Health Facility

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmb.label: Document Components
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmb.definition: A document's legally relevant, substantive contents (e.g., clauses, citations, legal issues, facts) that contribute to the document's relevance substantively.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmp.label: Expert Engagement Type
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmp.definition: A collection of the types of arrangements for which a party may engage an expert.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmq.label: Motion to Remand Case
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmq.definition: A Motion to Remand Case is a formal request made by a party in a legal case to send the case back to a lower court for further proceedings or reconsideration.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDms.label: Order
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDms.definition: An Order, also known as a Ruling, is a written document issued by a trial court that directs parties to take certain actions or makes a decision on a specific matter in a legal case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmt.label: Barona Group of Capitan Grande Band
english_labels: Barona Group of Capitan Grande Band

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmv.label: Indiana Superior Court - Knox County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDmv.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Indiana that has the power to hear and decide a wide range of legal cases within Knox County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDn0.label: Kongo
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDn0.definition: Kongo (Language) is a structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary used in the Kongo region of Africa.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDn0.label: Bipolar Disorder
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDn0.definition: Bipolar Disorder is a psychiatric condition characterized by extreme mood swings that include emotional highs (mania or hypomania) and lows (depression). These mood swings can affect energy levels, activity, behavior, and the ability to carry out daily tasks, often requiring long-term treatment to manage symptoms.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnC.label: oasis:Violation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnC.definition: A violation is a type of deontic specification within the OASIS ontology, indicating a breach of a legal or ethical obligation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnD.label: International Organization Visa - Attendants, Servants, and Personal Employees
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnD.definition: An International Organization Visa for attendants, servants, and personal employees is a specialized visa category that allows individuals to accompany representatives or officials of international organizations while they are stationed in a host country for official duties. This visa is generally subject to specific conditions and may require the sponsoring international organization or official to assume certain responsibilities for the employee's welfare and legal status in the host country.
english_labels: International Organization Visa - Attendants, Servants, and Personal Employees

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnE.label: Peaches
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnE.definition: Peaches are juicy, sweet stone fruits from the Prunus persica species, characterized by their fuzzy skin and aromatic flesh. They are consumed fresh, canned, or used in culinary applications such as desserts, jams, and beverages, valued for their vitamins, antioxidants, and dietary fiber.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnI.label: Miscellaneous Provisions Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnI.definition: A Miscellaneous Provisions Clause is a contractual clause that includes additional terms and conditions that are not covered by other clauses in the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnI.label: Rice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnI.definition: Rice is a cereal crop belonging to the species Oryza sativa (Asian rice) or Oryza glaberrima (African rice), known for its edible starchy grains that are a staple food for more than half of the world's population. Cultivated primarily in flooded fields called paddies, rice provides essential carbohydrates, proteins, and vitamins, and is used in a variety of culinary dishes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnJ.label: "Intervening Event" Language
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnJ.definition: Intervening Event Language refers to the specific language used to describe a triggering event that causes a change in recommendation in a legal matter, such as a breach or violation of fiduciary duties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnL.label: Minnesota District Court - Polk County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnL.definition: Minnesota District Court - Polk County: A specific court within the Minnesota District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Polk County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnL.label: Judge
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnL.definition: A judge is a public official appointed to decide cases in a court of law.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnL.label: Notice of Appeal
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnL.definition: A Notice of Appeal is a formal document filed with a court of law to challenge a decision made by a lower court or administrative agency.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnM.label: New York Supreme Court - Broome County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnM.definition: The New York Supreme Court - Broome County is a court of general jurisdiction located in Broome County, New York, with authority to hear and decide a wide range of legal disputes within its geographic jurisdiction.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - Broome County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnO.label: Forward Looking Statements Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnO.definition: A Forward Looking Statements Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the expectations or projections of future events or performance, and typically includes a disclaimer that actual results may differ.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnX.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Greene County (7th Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Greene County (7th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnb.label: Ambulatory Health Care Services Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnb.definition: Industries in this group provide health care services directly or indirectly to ambulatory patients and do not usually provide inpatient services. Health practitioners in this subsector provide outpatient services, with the facilities and equipment not usually being the most significant part of the production process. This group includes offices of physicians, dentists, chiropractors, optometrists, psychologists, mental health practitioners, podiatrists, etc.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnc.label: Memorandum of Understanding
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnc.definition: A Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) is a non-binding agreement between two or more parties that outlines the terms and conditions of a potential future relationship or partnership. While generally not legally enforceable, it serves to clarify the expectations and responsibilities of each party involved.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnp.label: Leveraged Buyout
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnp.definition: A Leveraged Buyout (LBO) is a financial transaction where a company is acquired primarily using borrowed funds, often by taking on substantial debt. The assets of the company being acquired, and often those of the acquiring company, are used as collateral for the loans.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnr.label: Termination of Service Agreement Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDnr.definition: A Termination of Service Agreement Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the conditions under which the agreement can be ended by one or both parties, specifically related to the provision of services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDo0.label: Hyperglycemia
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDo0.definition: Hyperglycemia is an abnormally high level of blood glucose that can result from inadequate insulin production or insulin resistance. It may produce both acute and long-term complications affecting various body systems.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDo0.label: Qualified Privilege
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDo0.definition: Qualified Privilege: A legal protection that allows a person to make a statement without fear of being sued for defamation, as long as the statement was made in good faith and for a legitimate purpose.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDo0.label: Oil and Gas Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDo0.definition: Law pertaining to the acquisition and ownership rights in oil and gas both under the soil before discovery and after its capture, and adjudication regarding those rights.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDo1.label: Purchase Order
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDo1.definition: A Purchase Order is a formal document issued by a buyer to a seller, indicating types, quantities, and agreed prices for products or services. It serves as an official offer to buy products or services and becomes a legally binding contract once accepted by the seller.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDo3.label: Indictment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDo3.definition: An indictment is a formal accusation of a crime, issued by a grand jury based on evidence presented by a prosecutor.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDo4.label: International Trade Commission Dispute
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDo4.definition: An International Trade Commission (ITC) Dispute, also known as ITC, refers to a legal conflict brought before the U.S. International Trade Commission regarding unfair import investigations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDo8.label: Interference with Prospective Business Relationship
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDo8.definition: The Interference with Prospective Business Relationship is the intentional or negligent interference with a party's potential economic advantage by a third party, causing harm to the party's business relationship.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDo8.label: Response
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDo8.definition: A Response is a type of Litigation Document that is filed by a party in a legal case to answer or reply to a complaint or petition filed by the opposing party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDoB.label: Class Size
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDoB.definition: The number of individuals or entities included in a putative class action, representing the potential members of the class if the class is certified by the court. Class size affects both the scope of the lawsuit and the procedural requirements for class certification.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDoD.label: Marriage Creation Event
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDoD.definition: From the state-court filing standard (NODS) dataset.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDoG.label: Family-Based Immigration Request
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDoG.definition: A Family-Based Immigration Request is a type of immigration application where an individual seeks to enter or remain in a destination country based on their familial relationship to a citizen or legal resident of that country. This usually involves sponsorship by the relative and can include spouses, children, parents, and sometimes more extended family, depending on the country's immigration laws

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDoL.label: Ordinances
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDoL.definition: A law enacted by a local government (usually a city or municipality).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDoL.label: Reversed Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDoL.definition: The previously effective law has been reversed by some authority (e.g., appellate court, judge, regulator).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDoR.label: Motion for Extension of Time Regarding Transcript
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDoR.definition: A Motion for Extension of Time Regarding Transcript is a request made in a bankruptcy case to extend the deadline for submitting a written or recorded copy of court proceedings.
english_labels: Motion for Extension of Time Regarding Transcript

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDoU.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Will County (12th Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Will County (12th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDoV.label: Corrected Appendix
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDoV.definition: A corrected appendix is a section added to a document that contains additional information or corrections, and is a subset of the larger category of appendices.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDoc.label: Defensive Asylum
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDoc.definition: Defensive asylum is a form of asylum claimed by individuals who are in removal proceedings before an immigration court. Unlike affirmative asylum, defensive asylum is raised as a defense against being removed from the destination country (e.g., United States) and requires the applicant to present their case before an immigration judge.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDog.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Venango County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDog.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Venango County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within Venango County.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Venango County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDog.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Indiana County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDog.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Indiana County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering legal proceedings in the state of Pennsylvania.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Indiana County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDoj.label: Process Server
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDoj.definition: A person who serves legal process, bringing a defendant into a legal matter.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDoq.label: Promissory Estoppel
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDoq.definition: A legal doctrine that prevents a party from going back on a promise made to another party, even if the promise was not supported by consideration, when the other party relied on the promise to their detriment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDos.label: Product Warranty Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDos.definition: A product warranty clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the terms and conditions of a manufacturer's promise to repair or replace a product if it fails to meet certain standards or expectations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDp0.label: New Jersey Superior Court - Mercer County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDp0.definition: The New Jersey Superior Court - Mercer County is a court of general jurisdiction within the New Jersey state court system, located in Mercer County and serving the surrounding area.
english_labels: New Jersey Superior Court - Mercer County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDp2.label: tax_on_tax_id
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDp2.definition: "In a ""tax-on-tax"" situation (described above), the tax_on_tax_id is the tx_id of the tax that should be included in the tax calculation for the current tx_id. For example, in Canada the TVQ tax includes not only the line items taxed, but also the GST tax for these line items. The proper response to this tax_on_tax_id field would be the tx_id for the GST tax. Although we are currently not aware of any such situation, it may be the case in a jurisdiction that there is a tax-on-tax-on-tax situation. It is anticipated that this field would hierarchically grow as necessary. Using the example in the previous paragraph, say that tax3 includes TVQ and GST taxes. Since the TVQ tax already shows the hierarchical relationship with GST in the tax_on_tax_id field, tax 3 would list the tx_id for TVQ in this tax_on_tax_id field. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDp7.label: Pardon Proceeding
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDp7.definition: A Pardon Proceeding is a legal process within Criminal Proceedings that seeks to grant forgiveness or clemency to a convicted individual by a government authority.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDp8.label: Claims Against Real Estate Agents and Brokers
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDp8.definition: Claims Against Real Estate Agents and Brokers refers to legal actions taken against individuals or companies who act as intermediaries in real estate transactions, alleging breach of duty or negligence in their representation of clients.
english_labels: Claims Against Real Estate Agents and Brokers

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpA.label: Motion for Order to Show Cause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpA.definition: A Motion for Order to Show Cause is a legal request made in a bankruptcy case asking the court to require a party to appear and explain why they should not be held in contempt for failing to comply with a court order or other legal obligation.
english_labels: Motion for Order to Show Cause

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpD.label: Stipulation to Continue Hearing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpD.definition: A Stipulation to Continue Hearing is a legal agreement between parties involved in a case to postpone a scheduled hearing to a later date.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpJ.label: General / Summary Probate
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpJ.definition: General/Summary Probate is a type of probate filing that is used for small estates with limited assets and straightforward distribution processes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpN.label: Control Position
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpN.definition: An M&A Control Position refers to a stake in a company acquired through mergers and acquisitions that gives the holder significant influence over corporate decisions. This control is often achieved by obtaining a majority of voting shares or a significant minority stake sufficient to influence board decisions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpO.label: ADR Judicial Settlement Conference
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpO.definition: A settlement conference facilitated by a judge or a neutral third party in an Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) forum to resolve disputes outside of the court system.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpP.label: Aggravated
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpP.definition: An unlawful attack by one person upon another wherein the offender uses a weapon or displays it in a threatening manner, or the victim suffers obvious severe or aggravated bodily injury involving apparent broken bones, loss of teeth, possible internal injury, severe laceration, or loss of consciousness. This also includes assault with disease (as in cases when the offender is aware that he/she is infected with a deadly disease and deliberately attempts to inflict the disease by biting, spitting, etc.).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpS.label: Motion for Conditional Use of Cash Collateral
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpS.definition: A Motion for Conditional Use of Cash Collateral is a request made in a bankruptcy case to allow a debtor to use cash collateral under certain conditions.
english_labels: Motion for Conditional Use of Cash Collateral

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpa.label: Conflicts Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpa.definition: Conflicts Management refers to the process of identifying and resolving potential conflicts of interest within a law firm or legal department, in order to ensure ethical and professional conduct in the provision of legal services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpd.label: Avoidant/Restrictive Food Disorder
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpd.definition: Avoidant/Restrictive Food Intake Disorder (ARFID) is an eating disorder characterized by an extreme avoidance or restriction of food intake, which can lead to significant nutritional deficiencies, weight loss, or impairment in social and occupational functioning. Unlike Anorexia Nervosa, ARFID does not involve a distorted body image or an intense fear of gaining weight but may include aversions to certain foods or fear of adverse consequences from eating.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpd.label: State Governmental Body
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpd.definition: A regional governmental body, such as a state or provincial government, operates at a level below the national government but above local governments like cities or municipalities. These bodies have jurisdiction over a specific geographic area and possess their own set of powers and responsibilities, often delineated by a constitution or charter. They typically consist of executive, legislative, and judicial branches, and they manage issues more localized than those of the national government but broader than those of city or town governments. Examples include U.S. state governments, Canadian provincial governments, or Indian state governments.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDph.label: Albanian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDph.definition: A language spoken in Albania and other parts of the Balkans, characterized by its unique grammar and vocabulary.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDph.label: DEPRECATED Passive Income, favoring Unearned Income
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDph.definition: Passive Income refers to earnings derived from activities in which the individual is not actively involved. This includes income from investments, rental properties, dividends, interest, royalties, and other sources that do not require continuous effort or direct labor to maintain.
english_labels: DEPRECATED Passive Income, favoring Unearned Income

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpi.label: Forward-looking Material Adverse Effect Standard
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpi.definition: A Forward-looking Material Adverse Effect (MAE) Standard is a legal language used in contracts that refers to a future event or circumstance that could have a negative impact on a party's ability to fulfill their obligations under the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpj.label: inv_reference
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpj.definition: "If the firm is submitting a Credit Note (an instrument required by statute or regulation that corrects a previously issued Tax Invoice -- see INVOICE.tax_invoice for more discussion) or is submitting an invoice that corrects an invoice previously rejected by a bill reviewer, enter the inv_id of the original invoice being corrected. As described above, law firms are required by regulation to supply the Tax Invoice number being corrected. It is therefore expected that the receiving system will store this information and display it to bill reviewers. In addition, in situations where the submission corrects an invoice rejected by a bill reviewer, this field can be used by the receiving system to electronically verify the correction submitted so that these submissions could be approved electronically instead of being routed to a bill reviewer for approval. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpj.label: Governmental Monitoring Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpj.definition: Governmental Monitoring Practice entails the systematic observation and analysis of activities and decisions across various branches of government to ensure transparency, accountability, and compliance with legal standards. This practice helps organizations and individuals stay informed about legislative, executive, and judicial developments that may impact their interests.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpj.label: Motion to File Amended Proof of Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpj.definition: A Motion to File Amended Proof of Claim is a request made in a bankruptcy case to modify or update a previously filed claim.
english_labels: Motion to File Amended Proof of Claim

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpl.label: Breach of Implied Contract
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpl.definition: The Breach of Implied Contract is a legal claim that arises when one party fails to fulfill an obligation that was not explicitly stated in a contract, but was understood to be a part of the agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDps.label: Price Changes Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDps.definition: A Price Changes Clause, also known as a Price Adjustment Clause, is a provision in a contract that allows for adjustments to the price of goods or services based on certain conditions or events.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDps.label: Motion for More Definite Statement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDps.definition: A Motion for More Definite Statement is a legal request made by a party in a bankruptcy case or in response to a complaint, asking the opposing party to provide a clearer and more specific statement of their claims or defenses.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpt.label: Co-Sale Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpt.definition: A Co-Sale Agreement, also known as a Tag-Along Agreement, is a legal document that allows minority shareholders to join a sale initiated by majority shareholders. This agreement ensures that the minority shareholders receive the same terms and conditions as the majority shareholders in a sale, thereby protecting their interests during significant corporate transactions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpw.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Dauphin County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpw.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court in Dauphin County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court system that handles minor criminal offenses, traffic violations, and civil cases involving amounts up to $12,000.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Dauphin County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpx.label: Intervening Event - Occurs After Signing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpx.definition: An intervening event that occurs after the signing of a legal agreement, which may affect the execution or performance of the agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpy.label: Ownership of Proprietary Information Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpy.definition: A clause in a legal agreement that specifies the ownership rights of confidential or proprietary information.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpy.label: Motion to Consolidate for Trial
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDpy.definition: A Motion to Consolidate for Trial is a request made in bankruptcy proceedings to combine two or more related cases into a single trial.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqC.label: UK Legal Aid Agency
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqC.definition: The Legal Aid Agency, formerly known as the Legal Services Commission, is an organization responsible for providing legal aid and ensuring that individuals who cannot afford legal representation have access to legal assistance. It oversees the funding and administration of legal aid services, promoting equal access to justice.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqD.label: Acupuncture Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqD.definition: Acupuncture Malpractice refers to a type of medical malpractice claim that arises from the improper or negligent use of acupuncture treatment by a healthcare provider.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqI.label: La Posta Band of Diegueno Mission Indians
english_labels: La Posta Band of Diegueno Mission Indians

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqK.label: Georgia District Court - Sumter County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqK.definition: Georgia District Court - Sumter County: A specific court within the Georgia District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Sumter County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqK.label: Donning and Doffing Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqK.definition: A "Donning and Doffing Claim" is a legal term typically used in employment and labor law. It refers to a situation where employees claim that they should be compensated for the time spent putting on (donning) and taking off (doffing) specialized work attire or equipment required by their job, such as uniforms, safety gear, or tools. These claims often involve disputes over whether such activities should be considered part of the workday and eligible for compensation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqS.label: Tort Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqS.definition: Tort Claims are civil claims that arise from a wrongful act or omission that causes harm or injury to another person, property, or reputation, and for which the injured party may seek compensation or damages.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqU.label: Notice of Appearance
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqU.definition: A Notice of Appearance is a written document filed with a court or administrative agency by an attorney or party indicating that they are representing a party in a legal matter.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqV.label: C.F.A. (Chartered Financial Analyst)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqV.definition: The suffix "C.F.A." stands for "Chartered Financial Analyst" and is used after a person's name to indicate that they have passed a series of exams and met other requirements set forth by the CFA Institute. This designation signifies the individual's expertise in investment management and financial analysis, and it is commonly used in finance, investment, and academic settings

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqZ.label: Spinal Muscular Atrophy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqZ.definition: Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) is a genetic disorder characterized by the progressive degeneration and loss of motor neurons in the spinal cord, leading to muscle weakness and atrophy. This condition primarily affects the muscles used for activities such as crawling, walking, sitting up, and controlling head movement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqa.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Putnam County (10th Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Putnam County (10th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqb.label: Performance Improvement Plan
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqb.definition: A Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) is a formal document outlining specific goals and actions an employee must take to improve their performance to meet organizational standards. This plan typically includes a timeline, measurable objectives, and support resources to help the employee achieve the required improvements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqc.label: Florida Circuit Court - Pasco County - 6th Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqc.definition: A court located in Pasco County, Florida that is part of the larger Florida Circuit Court system.
english_labels: Florida Circuit Court - Pasco County - 6th Circuit Court

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqf.label: Mayor
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqf.definition: A Mayor is the highest-ranking official in a municipal government, typically elected by the public or appointed by a city council. This individual serves as the chief executive officer of a city or town, responsible for overseeing local government operations, implementing policies, and representing the municipality in various capacities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqf.label: M&A F6 Real Property Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqf.definition: M&A F6 Real Property Practice refers to the legal work performed by a Legal Services Provider in the course of a merger and acquisition transaction that involves real estate property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqg.label: Avestan
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqg.definition: Avestan is an ancient language used in Zoroastrian scriptures and rituals.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqs.label: Cumberland County Association for Indian People
english_labels: Cumberland County Association for Indian People

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqs.label: Osteopathic Medicine Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqs.definition: Negligent or improper treatment by an osteopathic physician that results in harm to a patient, giving rise to a legal claim for damages.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqv.label: Rules of Evidence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqv.definition: Procedural rules governing the use of evidence.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqv.label: Rental and Leasing Services Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDqv.definition: Industries in this group include establishments that provide a wide array of tangible goods, such as automobiles, computers, consumer goods, and industrial machinery and equipment, to customers in return for a periodic rental or lease payment. thee include those that are engaged in renting consumer goods and equipment and those that are engaged in leasing machinery and equipment often used for business operations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDr1.label: Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDr1.definition: Claims made under the Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, which regulates the safety and labeling of food, drugs, and cosmetics.
english_labels: Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act Claims

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDr2.label: Nervous System Cancer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDr2.definition: Nervous system cancer encompasses malignant tumors originating in the central nervous system (CNS), which includes the brain and spinal cord, as well as primary cancers of the peripheral nerves or spinal roots. This category includes high-grade tumors such as glioblastoma multiforme, ependymoblastoma, diffuse intrinsic brain stem gliomas, and other aggressive malignancies that may be primary, metastatic, progressive, or recurrent following initial anticancer therapy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDr6.label: 14th Amendment Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDr6.definition: Fourteenth Amendment claims are legal actions initiated by an individual alleging that their rights under the Fourteenth Amendment of the United States Constitution have been violated by the government or a government actor. The Fourteenth Amendment guarantees equal protection under the law and due process of law to all persons, and applies to actions taken by state and local governments. Fourteenth Amendment claims may arise in various contexts, such as when an individual is discriminated against on the basis of race, gender, national origin, or other protected categories, when an individual is deprived of their liberty or property without due process of law, or when an individual is denied equal protection of the law.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDr8.label: Motion to Compel Discovery
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDr8.definition: A Motion to Compel Discovery is a legal request made by one party to another party in a lawsuit, asking the court to order the other party to provide information or evidence that has not been previously disclosed or produced.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrC.label: Child Support Guidelines
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrC.definition: Child Support Guidelines are legal regulations or guidelines established by a government authority to determine the amount of financial support that a non-custodial parent is required to provide for their child or children. These guidelines take into account factors such as the parents' incomes, the child's needs, and the cost of living. They provide a standardized method for calculating child support payments, ensuring fairness and consistency in support orders.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrC.label: Deposition Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrC.definition: Deposition Practice refers to the legal process of obtaining sworn testimony from a witness outside of court, typically conducted in a lawyer's office or other location, as part of the discovery process in a legal matter.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrO.label: Managing Member
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrO.definition: A managing member is an individual or entity responsible for the day-to-day operations and decision-making of an organization. This role includes overseeing business activities, making strategic decisions, and ensuring compliance with legal and regulatory requirements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrZ.label: Sale of Personal Property
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrZ.definition: The sale of personal property refers to the transfer of ownership of tangible items that are not considered goods under the law, such as vehicles or furniture, in exchange for payment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrb.label: 07 Labor (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrb.definition: 07 Labor (PACER NoS) refers to a category of legal cases related to labor disputes, including issues such as fair labor standards, employee retirement benefits, and labor-management relations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrb.label: Peoria Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma
english_labels: Peoria Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrc.label: Other Expense
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrc.definition: An "Other Expense" is a type of cost that is not categorized under any specific expense category, but is still necessary and reasonable for the completion of a legal matter.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrd.label: Litigation Finance Company
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrd.definition: A Litigation Finance Company is a specialized financial institution that provides funding to plaintiffs or law firms to cover legal costs in exchange for a share of any potential recovery or settlement from a lawsuit.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrg.label: Data Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrg.definition: Data Management refers to the process of organizing, storing, protecting, and maintaining data in a way that allows for efficient retrieval and use, specifically within the context of legal use cases such as API and API Management, IP Analytics Management, Market Intelligence Management, Data Extraction Management, Judicial Analytics Management, Data Analytics Management, and Data Visualization Management.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrj.label: Impress a Trust
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrj.definition: To "Impress a Trust" means to create an equitable claim on property by demonstrating that it was intended to be held in trust, even if it was not formally declared as such.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrk.label: Failure to Provide Personnel Records Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrk.definition: A failure to provide personnel records claim is a legal action initiated by an employee against their employer for not complying with the legal requirement to provide access to or copies of the employee's personnel file. Personnel files often contain important employment-related documents such as performance evaluations, disciplinary actions, and employment contracts, and the claim arises when an employer refuses or fails to provide the requested records within the time frame mandated by applicable laws.
english_labels: Failure to Provide Personnel Records Claim

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrn.label: Eligible Compensation Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrn.definition: An Eligible Compensation Clause is a provision in a contract that specifies the types of compensation that are considered eligible for certain benefits or purposes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDro.label: Employment Warning
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDro.definition: An Employment Warning is a formal notice issued by an employer to an employee, indicating that their behavior or performance is unacceptable and needs improvement. This warning serves as an official record of the issue and a step in the disciplinary process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDro.label: Wholesale Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDro.definition: A "Wholesale Agreement" is a contractual arrangement between a supplier or manufacturer and a wholesaler, specifying the terms under which goods will be purchased in bulk for resale to retailers or direct to end consumers. The agreement typically addresses pricing, payment terms, delivery, and other obligations of both parties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrq.label: Tamashek
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrq.definition: Tamashek is a language that belongs to the Language top-level class and is spoken in parts of North Africa.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrr.label: Ugaritic
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrr.definition: A language used in ancient Ugarit, which was located in modern-day Syria.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrs.label: Gerrymandering Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrs.definition: A gerrymandering claim alleges that electoral district boundaries have been drawn in a way that intentionally advantages or disadvantages a particular political party or group. This manipulation, often based on party affiliation, race, or ethnicity, seeks to distort the electoral process to favor one group over another, thereby undermining the principle of fair representation. Such claims challenge the legitimacy and fairness of the redistricting process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrx.label: Dissolution
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrx.definition: Dissolution is the process of legally dissolving a business entity, such as a company or nonprofit, involving the winding down of operations, settling of debts, and distribution of remaining assets. It marks the formal termination of the entity's legal existence and cessation of business activities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrx.label: Obligation Analysis
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDrx.definition: Obligation Analysis is the process of examining and evaluating the legal responsibilities and duties of a debtor in a bankruptcy or financial restructuring matter, including the analysis of various considerations such as vendor agreements, utilities, securities reporting, liens, financial reports, insurance, cash usage, debt agreements, dischargeability, employee benefits, pensions, and environmental issues.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDry.label: LINE_ITEM_TOTAL
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDry.definition: The LINE_ITEM_TOTAL concept refers to the total amount charged for a specific line item in the LEDES98BI V5 Format Rev 1-2020 standard.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDry.label: Workers' Compensation Retaliation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDry.definition: Retaliation by an employer against an employee for filing a workers' compensation claim.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDs4.label: Project Manager
