https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDs4.definition: In project management, a person who oversees a project's planning an execution.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDs4.label: Survey
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDs4.definition: A survey in a legal context refers to a comprehensive review or analysis of laws, regulations, or practices. It aims to identify trends to inform legal strategy, compliance, or research.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDs5.label: Antitrust - Vertical Agreement/Conspiracy Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDs5.definition: A claim made under antitrust law alleging an agreement or conspiracy between parties at different levels of a supply chain to restrain trade or competition.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDs9.label: Neurosurgery Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDs9.definition: Negligent or wrongful conduct by a neurosurgeon that results in harm or injury to a patient, and which is the subject of a legal claim for damages.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsA.label: Sense Impression Objectives
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsA.definition: Sense Impression Objectives refer to the purposes for admitting out-of-court statements that describe or explain an event or condition while the declarant was perceiving it or immediately thereafter, as well as statements relating to a startling event or condition made while the declarant was under the stress of excitement caused by the event or condition. These objectives, which include present sense impressions and excited utterances, are exceptions to the hearsay rule due to the reliability of statements made in the moment or under the influence of a startling event.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsA.label: Patent Search Process
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsA.definition: The Patent Search Process involves systematically searching through patent databases to identify existing patents and patent applications that are relevant to a particular invention or technology. This process helps determine the novelty and patentability of the invention, guiding subsequent patent application strategies.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsC.label: Taxing Jurisdiction Country
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsC.definition: A Taxing Jurisdiction Country is a specific country that has the authority to impose and collect taxes on a particular entity or individual, as defined within the context of Tax Detail.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsD.label: Violation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsD.definition: A violation is an act or instance of breaking or failing to comply with a rule, regulation, contract, or law, which can lead to legal consequences.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsG.label: Statement of Good Faith
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsG.definition: A Statement of Good Faith is a written declaration made in a Bankruptcy and Restructuring Document, expressing the honest intention of the declarant to act in good faith towards the other parties involved in the proceedings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsK.label: Stuttering
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsK.definition: Stuttering, also known as stammering, is a speech disorder characterized by disruptions in the normal flow of speech, including repetitions of sounds, syllables, or words, prolongations of sounds, and involuntary pauses or blocks. These disruptions can vary in frequency and severity and often cause significant communication challenges and anxiety.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsN.label: Limited Guardianship of Adult
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsN.definition: A Limited Guardianship of Adult is a legal arrangement where a guardian is appointed to make decisions for an adult who is unable to make decisions for themselves, but only in specific areas as determined by the court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsO.label: Motion to Exclude Fact Witness
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsO.definition: A Motion to Exclude Fact Witness is a legal request to prevent a witness from testifying in court based on the fact that their testimony is not relevant or admissible as evidence.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsQ.label: No Third Party Beneficiaries Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsQ.definition: A No Third Party Beneficiaries Clause is a provision in a contract that specifies that the agreement is only between the parties involved and does not confer any rights or benefits to any third party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsU.label: Bicyclist Liability
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsU.definition: The legal responsibility of a person riding a bicycle for any harm or injury caused to others, as part of a claim for personal injury.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsW.label: Risk Management Objective
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsW.definition: Risk Management Objective refers to a specific goal or target that an organization aims to achieve through the identification, assessment, and prioritization of potential risks and the implementation of strategies to mitigate or manage those risks.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsX.label: Present Sense Impression
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsX.definition: A Present Sense Impression is a statement describing or explaining an event or condition made while or immediately after the declarant perceived it. This hearsay exception is based on the belief that statements made in the moment, without time for reflection or fabrication, are inherently reliable.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsa.label: International Organization Meeting Visa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsa.definition: A International Organization Meeting Visa (in the U.S., a G-2 visa) is issued to representatives of recognized foreign governments traveling to the U.S. temporarily to attend meetings of designated international organizations. This visa category also includes their immediate family members.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsh.label: Texas District Court - Williamson County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsh.definition: A Texas District Court located in Williamson County, which is a trial court of general jurisdiction in Texas, responsible for hearing civil and criminal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsi.label: Georgia Superior Court - Berrien County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsi.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Berrien County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsp.label: Elements of Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsp.definition: Elements of Claim: The essential components that must be proven in a legal action in order to establish a valid claim, including but not limited to the specific facts, legal theories, and evidence necessary to support the claim.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsp.label: Visitation of Grandparents
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsp.definition: The concept of Visitation of Grandparents refers to the legal right of grandparents to visit their grandchildren, which is often a part of custody and visitation claims.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDss.label: Asthma
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDss.definition: Asthma is a chronic respiratory condition characterized by inflammation and narrowing of the airways, leading to recurrent episodes of wheezing, shortness of breath, chest tightness, and coughing. It requires long-term management through medication, lifestyle changes, and avoidance of triggers to control symptoms and prevent attacks.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsw.label: Insurance Regulatory Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsw.definition: Insurance Regulatory Practice involves representing companies, brokers, and other entities in complying with the regulatory requirements imposed by insurance regulatory authorities. This legal service includes obtaining licenses, navigating regulatory changes, and ensuring adherence to financial solvency, consumer protection, and reporting obligations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsx.label: Respondent
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDsx.definition: The respondent is the party against whom a petition is filed, especially one on appeal. The respondent can be either the plaintiff or the defendant from the court below, as either party can appeal the decision thereby making themselves the petitioner and their adversary the respondent.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDt4.label: "Change of Control" Definition - Credit Agreement
english_labels: Change of Control Definition - Credit Agreement

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDt4.label: Document / Artifact
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDt4.definition: A written, drawn, presented, or memorialized representation of thought or expression, including evidence such as recordings and other artifacts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDt6.label: Unemployment Compensation Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDt6.definition: A claim made by an individual who has lost their job and is seeking financial assistance from the government to support themselves while they search for new employment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDtF.label: Motion to Disqualify Judge
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDtF.definition: A Motion to Disqualify Judge is a legal request to remove a judge from a case due to a conflict of interest or bias, which may prevent a fair trial.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDtF.label: Obligation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDtF.definition: An obligation is a legal or moral duty that requires a certain course of action or behavior, often enforceable by law or ethical principles.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDtG.label: Petition for Treaty Investor Visa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDtG.definition: An E-2 petition refers to the application process for obtaining an E-2 Treaty Investor Visa in the United States. The E-2 visa is available to individuals from countries that have a qualifying treaty with the U.S. It allows foreign nationals who are making a substantial investment in a U.S. enterprise to enter the U.S. for the purpose of developing and managing that investment. The E-2 visa can be applied for by investors, employees of the investor's enterprise, or the enterprise itself. The petition involves demonstrating the substantiality of the investment and meeting other eligibility criteria as outlined by U.S. immigration laws and regulations

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDtG.label: General Ticket (Party Block) Electoral System
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDtG.definition: The general ticket, also known as the party block electoral system, is a voting method in which voters select a party rather than individual candidates, and the party receiving the majority of votes wins all the seats available. This system is designed to ensure cohesive party representation but can result in the overrepresentation of the majority party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDtL.label: Collateral Order Appeal
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDtL.definition: Collateral Order Appeals are a type of appeal that can be made during a legal proceeding, which allows a party to challenge a specific issue that is separate from the main case and cannot be resolved later, even if the main case is still ongoing.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDtN.label: Juvenile Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDtN.definition: A Juvenile Court is a specialized court that has jurisdiction over cases involving minors, typically those under the age of 18, who have been accused of committing a crime or engaging in delinquent behavior.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDtT.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Carroll County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDtT.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Carroll County refers to a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Carroll County, Missouri.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDtY.label: Partial Vision Loss
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDtY.definition: Partial Vision Loss refers to a significant reduction in vision that cannot be fully corrected with conventional glasses, contact lenses, or surgery. This condition affects the ability to perform everyday tasks and may involve difficulties with visual acuity, contrast sensitivity, peripheral vision, or depth perception.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDtg.label: Judicial Arbitration and Mediation Services
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDtg.definition: Judicial Arbitration and Mediation Services (JAMS) is an alternative dispute resolution (ADR) venue that provides arbitration and mediation services to parties in legal disputes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDth.label: M&A J Post-Closing Requirements, Disputes & Adjustments Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDth.definition: A practice area within M&A law that deals with the requirements, disputes, and adjustments that arise after a merger or acquisition has been completed.
english_labels: M&A J Post-Closing Requirements, Disputes & Adjustments Practice

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDth.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Linn County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDth.definition: A Missouri Circuit Court in Linn County is a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Linn County, Missouri.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDu2.label: Endocrine Disorders
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDu2.definition: Endocrine disorders involve conditions that affect the endocrine glands, which produce hormones regulating various physiological processes in the body, including metabolism, growth, and reproduction. These disorders can disrupt hormonal balance, leading to a wide range of symptoms and health issues.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDu9.label: Monoplegia
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDu9.definition: Monoplegia is the paralysis of a single limb or a specific region of the body, often resulting from nerve damage, brain injury, or neurological disorders. It typically affects either an arm or a leg and requires medical treatment and physical therapy to manage symptoms and improve functionality.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDuC.label: Overpayment on Contract Recovered
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDuC.definition: The concept of "Overpayment on Contract Recovered" refers to a legal claim made by a party who has paid more than what was owed under a contract or quasi-contract, and seeks to recover the excess amount paid.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDuH.label: Illinois Circuit Court - McDonough County (9th Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - McDonough County (9th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDuS.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Delaware County Circuit 3
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDuS.definition: Indiana Circuit Court - Delaware County Circuit 3 refers to a specific court within the Indiana Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over cases in Delaware County.
english_labels: Indiana Circuit Court - Delaware County Circuit 3

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDuT.label: 03_2 Personal Property (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDuT.definition: 03_2 Personal Property (PACER NoS) refers to a category of cases within the PACER Nature of Suit (NoS) Codes that involve disputes over personal property, such as damage to personal property or other related issues.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDuW.label: Indemnification of Consultant Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDuW.definition: A clause in a contract that requires one party to compensate and protect a consultant from any losses, damages, or liabilities that may arise from their work on the project.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDub.label: Motion in Limine to Prevent Discussion of Excluded Evidence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDub.definition: A Motion in Limine to Prevent Discussion of Excluded Evidence is a legal request made by a party to prevent the opposing party from mentioning or presenting evidence that has been previously excluded from trial.
english_labels: Motion in Limine to Prevent Discussion of Excluded Evidence

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDub.label: Ndebele, North; North Ndebele
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDub.definition: North Ndebele is a written or spoken structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary, and is a specific language within the broader category of Language.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDud.label: Governing Law and Jurisdiction Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDud.definition: A Governing Law and Jurisdiction Clause is a provision in a legal document that specifies the law that will govern the agreement and the jurisdiction where any disputes will be resolved.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDud.label: Providing Alcohol to Intoxicated Adult
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDud.definition: Providing Alcohol to Intoxicated Adult: The act of giving or serving alcoholic beverages to an adult who is already intoxicated, which can result in legal liability for the provider.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDuf.label: Bank’s Wrongful Dishonor of Negotiable Instrument
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDuf.definition: The Bank's Wrongful Dishonor of Negotiable Instrument refers to the act of a bank refusing to pay a negotiable instrument, such as a check or promissory note, without a valid reason, resulting in damages to the party presenting the instrument.
english_labels: Bank’s Wrongful Dishonor of Negotiable Instrument

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDuf.label: Georgia Superior Court - Macon County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDuf.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Macon County, Georgia, with authority over civil and criminal cases within its geographic jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDug.label: Probate Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDug.definition: A probate claim is a legal action brought to settle the estate of a deceased person, including the distribution of assets and payment of debts, and is a type of civil claim.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDug.label: Washington Superior Court - Klickitat County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDug.definition: Washington Superior Court - Klickitat County refers to a specific court within the Washington Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Klickitat County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDuk.label: Subrogation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDuk.definition: Subrogation is a legal concept where an insurance company steps into the shoes of its insured and assumes their rights to recover damages from a third party who caused the loss, after the insurance company has paid out a claim to the insured.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDuk.label: Motion for Arbitration
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDuk.definition: A Motion for Arbitration is a formal request made to a court or arbitrator to resolve a dispute through arbitration rather than litigation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDum.label: Notice of Abandonment of Property
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDum.definition: A Notice of Abandonment of Property is a written communication that informs interested parties that a property has been abandoned by its owner and is available for possession by another party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDut.label: Investigator / Examiner
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDut.definition: An investigator or examiner is person or group that conducts investigations or examinations on behalf of a governmental criminal or regulatory agency, court, or self-regulatory organization, or in connection with internal, congressional, or other investigations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDuv.label: Visual Field Loss
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDuv.definition: Visual Field Loss refers to a reduction or loss of the normal field of vision, affecting peripheral or central sight. This condition can result from various underlying causes such as glaucoma, stroke, or retinal damage, significantly impacting daily activities and the ability to navigate environments.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDuw.label: Release of Medical Records Form
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDuw.definition: A Release of Medical Records Form is a legal document signed by a patient or their legal representative to authorize the sharing of their medical records with specified parties. This can be for the purpose of transferring care, obtaining a second opinion, or for legal needs.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDuy.label: Negligent Infliction of Emotional Distress on a Bystander
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDuy.definition: The concept of Negligent Infliction of Emotional Distress on a Bystander refers to a legal claim made by a person who has suffered emotional harm as a result of witnessing an injury or harm caused to another person due to someone else's negligence.
english_labels: Negligent Infliction of Emotional Distress on a Bystander

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDuz.label: Tax Tiers
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDuz.definition: Tax Tiers refer to the different levels or brackets of taxation that are applied to different income or asset levels, as defined in Tax Tier Detail.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDv8.label: Appeal
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDv8.definition: An appeal is a legal process in which a higher court reviews a decision made by a lower court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvD.label: Perinatology Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvD.definition: Perinatology Malpractice refers to medical malpractice claims related to the care of pregnant women and their fetuses, including issues related to prenatal testing, labor and delivery, and neonatal care.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvL.label: Expert Witness Deposition
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvL.definition: An expert witness deposition is a legal proceeding where an expert witness is questioned under oath outside of court, typically in a lawyer's office, in order to obtain evidence for a trial or other legal proceeding.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvQ.label: Organization Representation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvQ.definition: An Organization Representation is a statement made by a party in a legal matter regarding the status, structure, or operations of a company or other entity, which is supported by a warranty that the information provided is accurate and complete.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvQ.label: Texas District Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvQ.definition: Texas District Court is a court of general jurisdiction in the state of Texas that hears civil and criminal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvT.label: Discount Amount - Fee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvT.definition: Discount Amount - Fee refers to a reduction in the fee charged for legal services provided, either as a percentage or a fixed amount.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvU.label: Negative Advertisement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvU.definition: A Negative Advertisement is a type of advertising that focuses on criticizing or discrediting a competitor, individual, or opposing viewpoint rather than promoting the advertiser's own product or message. These advertisements are often used in political campaigns and competitive business markets to highlight perceived flaws, mistakes, or negative attributes of the target.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvV.label: Governmental Civil Law Division
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvV.definition: A Governmental Civil Law Division is a governmental entity that handles civil legal matters involving the government. It provides legal advice to government agencies, represents the government in civil litigation, and ensures compliance with civil laws and regulations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvY.label: Consideration Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvY.definition: A consideration clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the exchange of something of value between parties, which is necessary for the contract to be legally binding.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvd.label: Tenancy in Common
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvd.definition: Tenancy in Common is a form of concurrent property ownership where multiple individuals hold separate and undivided interests in the same property. Each tenant in common has the right to sell, transfer, or bequeath their individual share without the consent of the other co-owners, and upon death, their interest passes to their heirs rather than the remaining co-owners.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvg.label: Instance
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvg.definition: An FOLIO Instance - A document that fully describes one or more legal matters

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvo.label: Wagoner Rule
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvo.definition: The Wagoner Rule is a legal defense in civil litigation that prevents a trustee from suing third-party professionals for damages caused by the trustee's own misconduct.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvp.label: Colorado River Abstention
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvp.definition: A legal doctrine that allows federal courts to abstain from hearing cases that involve complex state water rights issues in the Colorado River Basin.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvq.label: Role in Project Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvq.definition: An individual's role in the matter in project management terms.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvq.label: DOCX
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvq.definition: A Microsoft Word file that was introduced by Microsoft with the release of Microsoft Office 2007.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvs.label: Basal Cell Carcinoma
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvs.definition: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is the most common type of skin cancer, originating in the basal cells found in the epidermis, the skin's outermost layer. It typically grows slowly and rarely metastasizes but can cause significant local damage if not treated, often requiring surgical excision or other localized treatments.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvu.label: Statutory Compliance Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDvu.definition: A Statutory Compliance Clause is a provision in a legal agreement that requires the parties to comply with specific laws and regulations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDw3.label: Profitability Metrics
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDw3.definition: Profitability metrics are financial measures used to assess a business's ability to generate profit relative to its revenue, assets, equity, or other financial metrics. These metrics evaluate the net financial gains or losses relative to the costs and investments made.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwA.label: Right to Bear Arms Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwA.definition: A right to bear arms claim is a legal action initiated by an individual or group alleging that their right to keep and bear arms, as protected by the Second Amendment of the United States Constitution, has been violated by the government or a government actor. The Second Amendment guarantees the right of individuals to keep and bear arms for self-defense and other lawful purposes. A right to bear arms claim may arise in various contexts, such as when a government enacts a law or regulation that unduly restricts the right to own or possess firearms, when a government actor denies a permit or license to possess firearms, or when an individual or group is punished for exercising their Second Amendment rights.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwD.label: Disturbing the Peace
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwD.definition: The act of disturbing the peace refers to behavior that disrupts public order and tranquility, and is classified as a criminal misdemeanor offense.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwG.label: South Carolina Supreme Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwG.definition: The South Carolina Supreme Court is the highest court in the state of South Carolina, responsible for hearing appeals and making final decisions on legal disputes within the state court system.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwI.label: Reckless Involuntary Manslaughter
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwI.definition: The unlawful killing of a person without intent, caused by a reckless disregard for human life.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwK.label: Tic Disorders
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwK.definition: Tic Disorders involve the presence of repetitive, involuntary movements or vocalizations. They may include simple motor tics, such as blinking or head jerking, and complex tics, such as jumping or uttering words or phrases.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwK.label: Rajasthani
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwK.definition: Rajasthani (Language) is a written or spoken structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary, specifically used in the region of Rajasthan, India.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwN.label: firm segment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwN.definition: "Information on the firm whose invoices have been submitted. There will be 1 or more FIRM segments per file. Allows for the submission of invoices for more than one firm in the same invoice file. Each file should begin with the FIRM segment. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwX.label: Medical Device Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwX.definition: Medical Device Malpractice refers to a type of medical malpractice claim that arises from the use of a faulty or defective medical device during a medical procedure.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwY.label: Contributory Negligence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwY.definition: Contributory Negligence: A legal defense that asserts that the plaintiff's own negligence contributed to their injury or damages, and therefore the defendant should not be held fully liable.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwa.label: Eminent Domain
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwa.definition: The concept of Eminent Domain (Taking) refers to the power of the government to take private property for public use, with just compensation to the owner, as authorized by the Constitution.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwd.label: Auditability of an AI System
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwd.definition: Auditability refers to the ability of an AI system to undergo an assessment of its algorithms, data, and design processes to determine whether the system is functioning as intended. Auditability does not necessarily imply that information about business models and intellectual property must always be openly available, but ensuring traceability and logging mechanisms from the early design phase can help enable the system's auditability

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwl.label: oasis:LogicalFormula
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwl.definition: A logical formula is a statement in legal language that expresses a relationship between different elements, such as conditions, actions, or outcomes, and is defined within the LegalXML OASIS SCHEMA.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwm.label: Adyghe; Adygei
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwm.definition: Adyghe or Adygei is a language belonging to the Language top-level class, spoken by the Adyghe people in the North Caucasus region of Russia, and is used in legal matters as a means of communication or evidence.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwq.label: Equitable Estoppel
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwq.definition: Equitable Estoppel is a legal principle that prevents a party from denying or asserting a right, claim, or fact that is inconsistent with their previous conduct or representations, when such denial or assertion would result in injustice or harm to another party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwr.label: Tupi languages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwr.definition: A group of languages spoken in Brazil, characterized by complex phonetics and grammar, and historically used by indigenous peoples in the region.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDww.label: Arkansas Circuit Court - Cleveland Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDww.definition: The Arkansas Circuit Court - Cleveland Cty. is a specific court within the Arkansas Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Cleveland County, Arkansas.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwy.label: Motion to File Joint Brief
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDwy.definition: A Motion to File Joint Brief is a formal request made to the court by two or more parties in a legal case, seeking permission to submit a single brief that represents their collective arguments and positions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDx4.label: Fruit Crops
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDx4.definition: Fruit crops are plants cultivated primarily for their edible fruits, which are consumed fresh, processed, or used in various food products. These crops contribute significantly to human nutrition, providing essential vitamins, minerals, and dietary fiber.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDx9.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Clark County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDx9.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Clark County refers to a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Clark County, Missouri.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDxG.label: Intent
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDxG.definition: The concept of Intent refers to the state of mind of a person who acts with a purpose or goal in mind, and is an essential element of a legal claim.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDxQ.label: matter_disc_bill_pct_fees
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDxQ.definition: "MATTER_DISC_CRED.disc_cred_percent where MATTER_DISC_CRED.disc_credit_type equals ""Percent"" and MATTER_DISC_CRED.disc_credit_category equals ""Fee"" and MATTER_DISC_CRED.disc_cred equals ""MIDB"" "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDxV.label: Minnesota District Court - Watonwan County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDxV.definition: A Minnesota District Court located in Watonwan County, which is a court of general jurisdiction in Minnesota that hears civil and criminal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDxX.label: Household Motor Vehicle Tax Payment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDxX.definition: Household Motor Vehicle Tax Payment refers to user taxes levied on motor vehicles owned by households. These taxes are typically paid at regular intervals and may include vehicle registration fees, road use taxes, and other related charges that households must pay to legally operate their motor vehicles.
english_labels: Taxes paid by households in respect of motor vehicles

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDxZ.label: Motion for Relief from Stay
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDxZ.definition: A Motion for Relief from Stay is a legal request made in bankruptcy proceedings to lift the automatic stay that prevents creditors from taking collection actions against the debtor or the debtor's property.
english_labels: Motion for Relief from Automatic Stay

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDxZ.label: Written Form Requirement Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDxZ.definition: A Written Form Requirement Clause is a clause in a contract that specifies that any modifications or waivers to the contract must be in writing to be valid.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDxa.label: Auditory Processing Disorder
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RDxa.definition: Auditory Processing Disorder (APD) is a condition where the brain has difficulty interpreting and processing sounds, even though the individual's hearing is typically normal. https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RE2D.label: Publishing Industries
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RE2D.definition: Industries in the Publishing Industries subsector group establishments engaged in publishing newspapers, magazines, other periodicals, books, directories, and software. In general, establishments known as publishers issue copies of works for which they usually possess copyright. Works may be in one or more formats including print form, CD-ROM, proprietary electronic networks, or exclusively on the Internet. Publishers may publish works originally created by others for which they have obtained the rights and/or works that they have created in-house. Publishers may publish only and license rights to others to distribute their content, or they may publish and distribute content they create or own. Software publishing is included here because the activity, creation of a copyrighted product and bringing it to market, is equivalent to the creation process for other types of intellectual products. In NAICS, publishing--the reporting, writing, editing, and other processes that are required to create an edition of a newspaper, for example--is treated as a major economic activity in its own right, rather than as a subsidiary activity to a manufacturing activity, printing. Thus, publishing is classified in the Information sector; whereas, printing is in the Manufacturing sector. The Publishing Industries subsector excludes printed products, such as manifold business forms and appointment books, for which information is not the essential component. Establishments producing these items are included in Subsector 323, Printing and Related Support Activities. Reproduction of prepackaged software is treated in NAICS as a manufacturing activity, and custom design of software to client specifications is included in the Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services sector. These distinctions arise because of the different ways that software is created, reproduced, and distributed. Music publishers and establishments primarily engaged in the production, or production and distribution, of motion pictures and sound recordings are included in Subsector 512, Motion Picture and Sound Recording Industries. Establishments not engaged in publishing and exclusively obtaining rights from publishers to broadcast and distribute content are included in Subsector 516, Broadcasting and Content Providers.

This organization typically operates in coastal waters, ports, and inland waterways, serving both military and civilian functions depending on the country's structure.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RFjY.label: Impersonation / Identity Theft
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RFjY.definition: Falsely representing one’s identity or position, and acting in the character or position thus unlawfully assumed, to deceive others and thereby gain a profit or advantage, enjoy some right or privilege, or subject another person or entity to an expense, charge, or liability which would not have otherwise been incurred.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RFpB.label: Period of Duration Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RFpB.definition: A period of duration clause is a provision in a contract that specifies the length of time that the agreement will remain in effect.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RFpH.label: Public Health Emergency
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RFpH.definition: Public health emergency refers to an occurrence or imminent threat of a health condition, usually caused by bioterrorism, a pandemic, or a large-scale natural disaster, that poses a substantial risk of harm to a community. In such cases, governments often mobilize resources and implement special measures to protect public health and safety

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RFqn.label: Little Traverse Bay Bands of Odawa Indians
english_labels: Little Traverse Bay Bands of Odawa Indians

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RFri.label: Shoplifting
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RFri.definition: The act of taking merchandise from a store without paying for it, which is classified as a criminal offense of a minor nature.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RFxt.label: Fee Charge Description
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RFxt.definition: A Fee Charge Description is a specific detail within an Engagement Fee that outlines the amount and nature of the fees charged for legal services provided.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RFzB.label: New York City Court - Elmira
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RFzB.definition: A court located in Elmira, New York that operates under the jurisdiction of the New York City Court system.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RG06.label: oasis:Metadata-Actor
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RG06.definition: An oasis:Metadata-Actor is a type of agent that is defined within the LegalXML OASIS SCHEMA and can be further classified as a dctermsAgent, oasis:Expression, oasis:LegalRuleMLDocument, oasis:collection, or oasis:actor.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RG0f.label: Georgia Superior Court - Pickens County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RG0f.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Pickens County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has the authority to hear and decide civil and criminal cases within Pickens County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RG0k.label: 06 Forfeiture / Penalty (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RG0k.definition: The concept of "06 Forfeiture/Penalty (PACER NoS)" refers to a specific category within the PACER Nature of Suit (NoS) Codes that deals with the legal process of seizing property as a penalty for drug-related offenses under 21 U.S.C. § 881.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RG8K.label: PA230 Clearance Investigation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RG8K.definition: All actions associated with determining whether a proposed product or process might be covered by the claims of patents and/or published patent applications, including definition of the scope and field of the search, searching, search field integrity checking, analysis of search results, and reporting to client. Also known as a "right-to-use" or "non-infringement" search, the field of a clearance search is often limited to the patent claims in a very narrow technical area. The purpose of an infringement search is to determine whether there are claims in those patent documents that might be broadly construed to cover a well-defined, commercial embodiment of a product or process. Since interpretation of the patent claims may require review of the disclosure, patentability and clearance investigations are sometimes performed concurrently. Work of outside vendors in conducting searches or otherwise assisting the investigation should be an expense under E100. Any formal clearance opinion directed at specific patents should be prepared separately under PA710.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RG8k.label: New York City Court - Ithaca
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RG8k.definition: A court located in Ithaca, New York that operates under the jurisdiction of the New York City Court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGCp.label: Reasonable Belief
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGCp.definition: A reasonable belief is a standard of proof in litigation where a party must demonstrate that they held a belief that was objectively reasonable under the circumstances, in order to meet their burden of proof.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGD2.label: Mesa Grande Band of Diegueno Mission Indians
english_labels: Mesa Grande Band of Diegueno Mission Indians

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGD5.label: Recovery of a Chattel / Replevin
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGD5.definition: The concept of Recovery of a Chattel or Replevin refers to the legal action taken to recover personal property that has been wrongfully taken or detained by another party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGDe.label: Genetic Evidence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGDe.definition: Genetic evidence, commonly known as DNA evidence, refers to the unique genetic material found in cells, body fluids, or tissues. It is used in forensic science to identify or exclude individuals as sources of the material, providing a powerful tool for linking suspects to crime scenes or victims.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGEg.label: "Superior Offer, or Acquisition Proposal reasonably likely/expected to result in a Superior Offer" Language
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGEg.definition: A "Superior Offer, or Acquisition Proposal reasonably likely/expected to result in a Superior Offer" is a proposal made during a legal matter that is expected to be better than any other offers made, and triggers an exception to a previously agreed upon no-shop covenant.
english_labels: "Superior Offer, or Acquisition Proposal reasonably likely/expected to result in a Superior Offer" Language
Superior Offer, or Acquisition Proposal reasonably likely/expected to result in a Superior Offer Language

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGEo.label: Texas District Court - Randall County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGEo.definition: A Texas District Court located in Randall County, which has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGEv.label: Annuity
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGEv.definition: An annuity is a financial product or arrangement that provides a series of payments made at equal intervals over a specified period. Annuities are commonly used for retirement income, insurance, and investment purposes, and can be structured as fixed, variable, immediate, or deferred, depending on the timing and variability of payments.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGFG.label: Statement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGFG.definition: A statement is a written or spoken declaration of facts or opinions, typically made under oath or affirmation, and used as evidence in a legal proceeding.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGI4.label: Buyer Consent Not Unreasonably Delayed
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGI4.definition: The concept of "Buyer Consent Not Unreasonably Delayed" refers to the requirement that a buyer's consent to a legal matter must be given in a timely manner, without any unnecessary or unreasonable delays.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGJ5.label: Washington Superior Court - Clark County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGJ5.definition: Washington Superior Court - Clark County refers to a specific court within the Washington Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Clark County, Washington.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGK6.label: Work Break
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGK6.definition: "Work Break" typically refers to a short period of rest or pause during the workday, allowing employees to recharge or relax briefly before resuming their tasks. It can vary in duration and purpose, such as a coffee break, lunch break, or a quick break to stretch and refocus.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGMt.label: Amendment to Promissory Note Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGMt.definition: An Amendment to Promissory Note Clause is a specific provision added to a promissory note that modifies the terms of the original agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGOL.label: PA210 State-of-the-Art Investigation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGOL.definition: All actions associated with determining the state of the art in a particular area of technology, including definition of the scope and field of the search, searching, analysis of search results, and reporting to client. Also known as a "collection" search, a state-of-the- art search is the broadest and most general type of patent search with a field that may include published patent applications, expired and unexpired patents, non-patent literature, and/or other sources. State-of-the-art searches are typically conducted, if at all, during the conceptual design phase when the scope of the investigation is least defined. State-of-the-art searches may also be used to help identify technology that is disclosed in expired patents and may therefore be freely copied by anyone. Work of outside vendors in conducting searches or otherwise assisting investigation should be an expense under E100.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGOU.label: Employment Attributes
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGOU.definition: Employment Attributes describe the various statuses and characteristics that define an individual's current or past relationship with an employer. These attributes can include whether the employment is full-time or part-time, and the employee's current status such as active, inactive, or terminated, which helps in administrative tracking and benefits allocation

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGPW.label: Additional Rent Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGPW.definition: An Additional Rent Clause is a provision in a contract that requires a tenant to pay for expenses beyond the base rent, such as property taxes or maintenance costs.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGPb.label: Annual Incentive Plan Bonus Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGPb.definition: An Annual Incentive Plan (AIP) Bonus Clause is a specific provision within a contract that outlines the terms and conditions for receiving a bonus payment based on the achievement of certain performance goals over a one-year period.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGPj.label: TR740 Licensing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGPj.definition: All actions associated with negotiating and preparing trademark license.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGRl.label: Immigrant Visa
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGRl.definition: An immigrant visa is issued to foreign nationals who intend to live permanently in the U.S. This visa category includes various types, such as family-based, employment-based, and diversity lottery visas, leading to permanent resident status.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGSV.label: Transfer Stipulation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGSV.definition: Transfer Stipulation refers to a legal agreement between parties involved in an appellate case, outlining the terms and conditions of transferring the case from one court to another.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGSY.label: U.S. Code
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGSY.definition: A law enacted and codified by the United States Congress.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGT3.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Monroe County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGT3.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Monroe County refers to a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Monroe County, Missouri.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGUf.label: Arkansas District Court - Crawford Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGUf.definition: A court located in Crawford County, Arkansas that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGVC.label: Compensation Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGVC.definition: A Compensation Clause, also known as a Payment Clause, is a provision in a contract that outlines the terms and conditions for payment in the event of a breach or termination of the agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGVp.label: Bantu languages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGVp.definition: A group of languages spoken in sub-Saharan Africa, characterized by their use of Bantu grammar and vocabulary.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGVr.label: Election Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGVr.definition: Legal procedures and regulations governing elections.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGWm.label: Miniwarehouses and Self-Storage Units - Real Estate Asset
english_labels: Miniwarehouses and Self-Storage Units - Real Estate Asset

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGXy.label: U.S. President
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGXy.definition: The U.S. President is the head of state and government, responsible for executing federal laws, commanding the armed forces, and representing the United States in diplomatic matters. Elected to a four-year term, the President serves as both the chief executive officer of the federal government and the commander-in-chief of the military.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGYa.label: Status - Responded
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGYa.definition: Status of "Responded" typically indicates that a response or action has been provided in relation to a previous request, inquiry, or communication. This could refer to providing additional information, documentation, or clarification in response to a query from authorities (e.g., immigration authorities, patent office, trademark office) or other relevant parties during the application process

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGby.label: Release
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGby.definition: A Release is a legal defense used in civil litigation that involves the relinquishment or surrender of a claim or right by one party to another. A Release can also be a legal document in which one party agrees not to pursue legal action against another party in exchange for compensation or other considerations. It signifies the conclusion of a claim or potential claim.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGcH.label: B220 Employee Benefits/Pensions
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGcH.definition: Review issues such as severance, retention, 401K coverage and continuance of pension plan

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGcq.label: Motion for Summary Judgment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGcq.definition: A Motion for Summary Judgment is a request made by a party in a legal case asking the court to rule in their favor without a trial, based on the evidence presented in the case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGgW.label: Tip Violation Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGgW.definition: A tip violation claim refers to a legal action initiated by an employee, usually in the service industry, alleging that their employer has violated federal, state, or local laws governing tipped employees. Common examples of tip violations include employers improperly pooling tips, taking a portion of tips, or failing to pay the required minimum wage to tipped employees.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGgu.label: Jewish Religion
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGgu.definition: The Jewish Religion, or Judaism, is a monotheistic faith rooted in the covenantal relationship between the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and the children of Israel, as detailed in the Hebrew Bible. In legal contexts, it often involves issues related to religious freedoms, accommodations for religious observances, and the recognition of Jewish holidays and dietary laws.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGhP.label: Indiana Superior Court - White County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGhP.definition: The Indiana Superior Court - White County is a specific court within the Indiana Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over cases within White County, Indiana.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGhc.label: Physician Violation of Patient Confidentiality
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGhc.definition: The concept of Physician Violation of Patient Confidentiality refers to the breach of trust by a medical professional who discloses private information about a patient without their consent, potentially resulting in legal claims for medical malpractice and privacy violations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGio.label: A126 Evidence/Exhibit Creation and Preparation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGio.definition: For discovery and eDiscovery, the creation, export or delivery of trial evidence or exhibits including: creation of video clips and other demonstrative evidence from the collection.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGkD.label: Government-Regulated Defined Contribution Account
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGkD.definition: A Government-Regulated Defined Contribution Account, such as a 401(k) or Thrift Savings Plan, is a retirement savings account where an individual contributes a fixed amount or a percentage of their salary into a fund. The government regulates these accounts to provide tax advantages, and the ultimate benefit received is dependent on the performance of the investments chosen within the account.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGlE.label: PA299 Other Patent Investigation and Analysis
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGlE.definition: Use only for patent investigation and analysis activities that can not be included under a previous code, under PA710 (Opinion Preparation), or as instructed by the client.
english_labels: PA299 Other Patent Investigation and Analysis

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGm7.label: Malpractice Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGm7.definition: Malpractice Claims refer to civil claims of negligence or malfeasance brought against a professional or tradesperson, such as a doctor, lawyer, accountant, or architect, for failing to meet the standard of care expected in their field.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGmC.label: DEPRECATED: Formerly Tax Risk
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGmC.definition: Deprecated concept that was formerly related to tax risk.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGoY.label: DEPRECATED Status - Active
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGoY.definition: Active Status refers to the current operational condition or state of an entity, such as an account, membership, or project, indicating that it is in good standing and fully functional. In legal and business contexts, an entity with active status is generally compliant with all requirements and obligations, allowing it to engage in its designated activities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGpj.label: Washington Commission on Professional Ethics
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGpj.definition: The Washington Commission on Professional Ethics is a government entity within the Washington State Courts that oversees and regulates ethical conduct of legal professionals.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGpq.label: Arizona Superior Court - Santa Cruz Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGpq.definition: Arizona Superior Court - Santa Cruz Cty. is a specific court within the Arizona Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Santa Cruz County, Arizona.
english_labels: Arizona Superior Court - Santa Cruz Cty.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGrD.label: Will Contest
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGrD.definition: A Will Contest is a legal claim challenging the validity of a will, typically based on allegations of fraud, undue influence, lack of capacity, or improper execution.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGrN.label: Arizona Superior Court - Pima Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGrN.definition: The Arizona Superior Court - Pima County is a specific court within the Arizona Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases in Pima County, Arizona.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGrP.label: Court Costs
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGrP.definition: Court Costs: Expenses incurred in the course of a legal proceeding that are typically paid by the losing party, including fees for court clerks, marshals, and reporters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGrX.label: Consensual Lien
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGrX.definition: A consensual lien is a type of lien that is created by agreement between the parties involved, allowing the lienholder to have a security interest in the property of the debtor until the debt is paid off.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGsU.label: M&A B Purchase / Merger Agreement Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGsU.definition: The M&A B Purchase/Merger Agreement Practice refers to the legal work involved in negotiating and drafting agreements for the purchase or merger of companies, as a component of the broader M&A practice.
english_labels: M&A B Purchase / Merger Agreement Practice

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGsi.label: Florida Circuit Court - Washington County - 14th Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGsi.definition: The Florida Circuit Court - Washington County (14th Circuit Court) is a specific court within the Florida Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Washington County.
english_labels: Florida Circuit Court - Washington County - 14th Circuit Court

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGvD.label: Reasonable Accommodation Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGvD.definition: This claim is brought forward when an employer, school, or service provider fails to make reasonable adjustments or modifications that would allow an individual with a disability to access employment opportunities, services, or benefits. The nature of the accommodation depends on the individual's needs and the context, but it aims to ensure equal opportunities and non-discrimination.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGwP.label: Equipment Lease
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGwP.definition: An equipment lease is a contractual agreement in which one party (the lessor) grants another party (the lessee) the right to use and possess specific equipment for a predetermined period in exchange for periodic rental payments. These agreements often include terms related to maintenance, insurance, and the lessee's responsibilities during the lease term.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGwW.label: Restructuring Support Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGwW.definition: Document where parties agree to terms that will expedite the restructuring process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGwo.label: Matching Rights Period
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGwo.definition: A Matching Rights Period is a specific period of time during which a party has the right to match the terms of a proposed transaction or agreement, as outlined in the Matching Rights Language.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGxK.label: Turkish, Ottoman
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGxK.definition: Turkish, Ottoman (1500-1928) is a language used during the Ottoman Empire period in Turkey and surrounding regions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGxo.label: New York Supreme Court - New York County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RGxo.definition: The New York Supreme Court - New York County is a court of general jurisdiction located in New York County, which is a subdivision of the New York Supreme Court.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - New York County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RH2W.label: Lead
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RH2W.definition: Person or organization leading an aspect of the matter (e.g., Lead Counsel, Lead Businessperson, etc.).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RH3E.label: Short Form
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RH3E.definition: A Short Form is a condensed version of a longer document, capturing the essential terms and conditions without the extensive detail. It is used in various legal contexts, such as contracts, agreements, and reports, to provide a succinct overview of the main points.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RH8j.label: Commercial Publisher
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RH8j.definition: A commercial publisher operates to produce and distribute various types of publications, such as books, magazines, or digital content, with the primary goal of generating profit. Unlike academic publishers, commercial publishers often focus on broader audiences and market-driven topics. In the legal sector, commercial publishers might produce legal texts, practice guides, or public-facing materials that appeal to professionals, students, or the general public, with revenue generated through sales, subscriptions, or advertising.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHBA.label: One-Step Merger
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHBA.definition: A One-Step Merger is a type of merger where the acquiring company merges directly with the target company, without the need for a separate shareholder vote on the merger agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHDM.label: task_code
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHDM.definition: "Task code for this line item, e.g. ""L110"". Only one code per line item. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHEB.label: Non-consensual Pornography Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHEB.definition: A revenge porn claim is a legal assertion that an individual's private, sexually explicit images or videos have been distributed without their consent, typically as an act of revenge or harassment. This claim seeks redress for the invasion of privacy, emotional distress, and potential reputational harm caused by the unauthorized dissemination.
english_labels: Unauthorized Distribution of Intimate Images Claim

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHKy.label: WC510 Appellate Proceedings/Motions Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHKy.definition: Research appellate issues, Draft response to motions/other filings, Arguing motions/other findings, Attend motion hearing, Travel to & from motion hearing, Prepare notice of appeal, Designing appellate record, Extraordinary writs/appellate proceedings, Review responses to appellate petition, Prepare response to appellate petition, Prepare petition appendix

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHMe.label: Dogri
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHMe.definition: A language spoken primarily in the Indian state of Jammu and Kashmir, characterized by its unique grammar and vocabulary.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHNT.label: Fee Simple Subject to a Condition Subsequent
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHNT.definition: A fee simple subject to a condition subsequent is a type of freehold estate in real property that grants ownership rights to the holder, subject to a specified condition, with the potential for forfeiture if the condition is violated. Unlike fee simple determinable, this estate does not automatically revert to the grantor upon breach of the condition; instead, the grantor retains the right to re-enter and reclaim the property, but must take affirmative action to enforce this right.
english_labels: Fee Simple Subject to a Condition Subsequent

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHQC.label: Georgia Superior Court - Rabun County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHQC.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Rabun County, Georgia, with authority over civil and criminal cases.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHQz.label: Surgical Negligence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHQz.definition: Surgical Negligence refers to a type of medical malpractice where a surgeon fails to provide the expected standard of care during a surgical procedure, resulting in harm or injury to the patient.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHSZ.label: Business Torts and Actions
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHSZ.definition: Business Torts and Actions are civil claims related to wrongful acts committed by one business against another, including unfair competition, false advertising, theft of intellectual property, and interference with contracts or business relationships.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHU1.label: By Stage / Segment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHU1.definition: Engagement fee model where a client pays a predetermined fee through a matter's stages (e.g., "through initial pleadings" or "through discovery" or "through dispositive motions" or "through trial")

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHUI.label: Monthly Retainer Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHUI.definition: A Monthly Retainer Clause is a provision in a contract that requires one party to pay a fixed amount of money to the other party on a monthly basis in exchange for services or goods provided.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHVF.label: Motion to Suppress
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHVF.definition: A Motion to Suppress is a legal request made by a party in a trial to exclude evidence from being presented in court, typically due to a violation of the defendant's constitutional rights.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHXD.label: Unfair Trade Practices
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHXD.definition: Unfair Trade Practices refer to any deceptive or fraudulent business practices that harm consumers or competitors, and are considered illegal under competition law.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHYW.label: L609 Quality assurance and control
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHYW.definition: Activities and actions related to ensuring that the process and practices used to perform analysis meet an acceptable level of defensibility.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHZT.label: Pre-Closing Covenants
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHZT.definition: "Pre-Closing Covenants" are commitments or obligations that parties agree to fulfill or abide by prior to the completion of a transaction, such as a merger or acquisition. These covenants ensure that the parties maintain certain conditions, avoid specific actions, or perform particular tasks leading up to the transaction's formal closure, preserving the deal's integrity and value.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RH_1.label: TR250 Publication Watches
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RH_1.definition: All actions associated with planning, completing, and reporting the results of periodic searches for conflicting trademarks. For example, this may include monitoring the file history of trademark applications, and/or publication for opposition. Work of outside vendors in conducting searches or otherwise assisting the investigation should be expensed under E100.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHag.label: Statutes
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHag.definition: A law enacted by a government's legislative branch.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHba.label: Credit Report
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHba.definition: A credit report is a detailed record of an individual's or entity's credit history, including information about their borrowing and repayment activities, outstanding debts, and any instances of late payments or defaults. Lenders and financial institutions use credit reports to assess the creditworthiness of a borrower before extending credit or loans.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHcR.label: Georgia Superior Court - Early County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHcR.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Early County refers to a specific court within the Georgia Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Early County, Georgia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHdD.label: L653 First pass document review
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHdD.definition: Activies and actions related to performing first pass document review such as determining relevancy, issue coding, tagging, and initial privilege determination.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHds.label: Georgia Superior Court - Glascock County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHds.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Glascock County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHfe.label: invoice segment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHfe.definition: "Information on the Invoices submitted by the Firm for the Client. There will be 1 or more INVOICE segments per CLIENT segment. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHkm.label: Insurance Carrier Bad Faith
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHkm.definition: The concept of Insurance Carrier Bad Faith refers to the intentional or reckless failure of an insurance company to fulfill its contractual obligations to its policyholders, such as denying a valid claim or failing to investigate a claim in a timely manner.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHlJ.label: Additional Matching Rights Period
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHlJ.definition: A period of time granted to a party in a legal matter, allowing them the opportunity to match the terms of a proposed transaction before it is finalized, in addition to the previously established matching rights period.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHpE.label: Employer's Breach of Implied Covenant of Good Faith and Fair Dealing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHpE.definition: The Employer's Breach of Implied Covenant of Good Faith and Fair Dealing refers to a legal claim made by an employee against their employer for violating the implied promise of good faith and fair dealing in the employment relationship.
english_labels: Employer's Breach of Implied Covenant of Good Faith and Fair Dealing

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHqS.label: Motion to File Supplemental Excerpts of Record
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHqS.definition: A Motion to File Supplemental Excerpts of Record is a formal request made to a court to allow additional evidence to be added to the record of a case, beyond what was originally submitted.
english_labels: Motion to File Supplemental Excerpts of Record

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHqT.label: Business Partner Breaching Fiduciary Duty to Co-Partner
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHqT.definition: When a business partner fails to uphold their legal obligation to act in the best interest of their co-partner, they are breaching their fiduciary duty and can be held liable for any resulting damages.
english_labels: Business Partner Breaching Fiduciary Duty to Co-Partner

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHqm.label: Writ of Attachment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHqm.definition: A Writ of Attachment is a court order to seize or take control of a specific property or assets before the final judgment in a lawsuit, ensuring that the property will not be disposed of or hidden by the defendant.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHrI.label: Hemiplegia
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHrI.definition: Hemiplegia is a condition characterized by paralysis or severe weakness on one side of the body, typically resulting from brain injuries such as stroke, traumatic brain injury, or neurological diseases. This condition affects motor function, coordination, and sensation on the affected side, significantly impacting daily activities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHvP.label: TR799 Other Trademark Prosecution
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHvP.definition: Use only for other trademark related tasks that can not be included under a previous code, or as instructed by the client.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHwC.label: Information Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RHwC.definition: The Information industry group comprises establishments engaged in the following processes: producing and distributing information and cultural products, providing the means to transmit or distribute these products as well as data or communications, and processing data.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RI17.label: Korean
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RI17.definition: Korean (Language) refers to the structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary specific to the Korean language.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RI1g.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Hancock County (9th Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Hancock County (9th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RI2a.label: Board Chair
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RI2a.definition: A Corporate Chair, or Chairman of the Board, is the presiding officer of a company's board of directors, responsible for leading board meetings and ensuring effective board governance. The Chair facilitates discussions, oversees board functions, and often acts as a liaison between the board and executive management.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RI3Q.label: Judicial Dissent
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RI3Q.definition: Judicial Dissent refers to a written opinion by a judge or judges who disagree with the majority decision in a legal case, outlining their reasoning and arguments for a different outcome.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RI3S.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Clay County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RI3S.definition: The Indiana Circuit Court - Clay County is a specific court within the Indiana Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Clay County, Indiana.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RI3r.label: Early Neutral Evaluation Event
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RI3r.definition: An Early Neutral Evaluation Event is a phase within a Mediation Event where a neutral third party evaluates the strengths and weaknesses of each party's case to facilitate settlement negotiations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RI5h.label: Subsequent Probate Filing Reason
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RI5h.definition: Subsequent Probate Filing Reason refers to the specific reasons for filing a probate case after the initial filing, such as financial exploitation, restoration, death, incapacity, abuse, neglect, abandonment, fees and costs, modification, or substance abuse.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RI63.label: Washington Superior Court - Thurston County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RI63.definition: Washington Superior Court - Thurston County refers to a specific court within the Washington Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Thurston County, Washington.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RI6K.label: Escrow Letter Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RI6K.definition: An Escrow Letter Clause is a provision in a contract that requires a third party to hold funds or property until certain conditions are met, typically used in real estate transactions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIBB.label: Pardon
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIBB.definition: A pardon is an official act by a government authority, typically the executive branch, that absolves an individual of any legal consequences for a crime they have been convicted of. It effectively erases the conviction from the individual's criminal record, signifying forgiveness and allowing the individual to regain rights lost due to the conviction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIBF.label: Mediation Forum
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIBF.definition: A Mediation Forum is a type of Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) Forum that facilitates communication and negotiation between parties in a dispute, with the goal of reaching a mutually acceptable resolution.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RICb.label: Physician Negligence
