https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RICb.definition: Physician Negligence refers to the failure of a medical practitioner to provide the standard of care expected of them, resulting in harm or injury to a patient.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RICv.label: Prosecutorial Misconduct
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RICv.definition: Prosecutorial misconduct refers to unethical or illegal actions committed by a prosecutor during a criminal case. This misconduct can include hiding evidence, making false statements, engaging in improper witness coaching, or other actions that violate a defendant's rights or the rules of legal ethics. When proven, prosecutorial misconduct can lead to the dismissal of charges, mistrial, or disciplinary action against the prosecutor.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RICy.label: Analysis of Pre-Petition Auto Financing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RICy.definition: An Analysis of Pre-Petition Auto Financing involves reviewing and assessing automobile financing agreements and related financial activities conducted before the filing of a bankruptcy petition. This analysis helps determine the validity, priority, and enforceability of claims against the debtor’s vehicle within the bankruptcy proceedings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIE2.label: JD10 Mediation (UK J-CODE)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIE2.definition: Work related to proposals for mediation, preparation and attendance at the mediation and any follow-up work.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIEd.label: Blue Pencil Doctrine Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIEd.definition: A Blue Pencil Doctrine Clause is a provision in a contract that allows a court to modify or remove any unenforceable or illegal portions of the contract while leaving the rest of the agreement intact.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIGj.label: Norwegian Nynorsk; Nynorsk, Norwegian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIGj.definition: Norwegian Nynorsk is a written or spoken structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary, and is a variation of the Norwegian language.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIID.label: Real Estate Design Review
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIID.definition: Real Estate Design Review is the process by which proposed architectural and site designs for a development project are evaluated for their adherence to local design standards, aesthetics, and land use compatibility. This review is usually conducted by a designated committee or governing body and may involve public hearings, expert consultations, and revisions to the initial plans.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIJ4.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Cambria County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIJ4.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Cambria County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering civil and criminal proceedings at the county level in Pennsylvania.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Cambria County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIJd.label: Samoan
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIJd.definition: A language spoken in Samoa and other Pacific islands, characterized by a unique phonology and grammar.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIKY.label: Employee Fraud
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIKY.definition: Employee Fraud refers to the deliberate act of deception by an employee aimed at obtaining unauthorized benefits, such as stealing assets, manipulating financial statements, or misappropriating company funds, often resulting in financial loss and legal liability for the organization.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RILQ.label: Law Enforcement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RILQ.definition: A department of persons who enforce laws, investigate crimes, and make arrests.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RILt.label: Irrelevant Evidence Objection
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RILt.definition: An Irrelevant Evidence Objection is raised when a party in a legal proceeding believes that the evidence being presented is not related to the issues at hand or does not have any probative value. This objection aims to prevent the introduction of extraneous information that could distract or mislead the decision-maker.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RILu.label: Visa for Families of Skilled Workers
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RILu.definition: A Visa for Families of Skilled Workers, such as the U.S. H-4 Visa, is a category of visa that allows the immediate family members (spouse and dependent children) of skilled workers with certain types of visas to accompany them to the host country. These family members are often granted the right to reside in the country and, in some cases, may be eligible to apply for work authorization.
english_labels: Visa for Families of Skilled Workers

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIMz.label: Pro Bono Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIMz.definition: Pro Bono Management refers to the management of legal services provided by lawyers and law firms on a voluntary basis, typically for individuals or organizations who cannot afford legal representation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIOj.label: Major Weight-Bearing Joint Surgery
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIOj.definition: Reconstructive surgery or surgical arthrodesis of a major weight-bearing joint involves surgical procedures aimed at repairing or stabilizing large joints that support significant body weight, such as the hip, knee, or ankle. This type of surgery is performed to restore function, alleviate pain, and improve stability in joints severely affected by injury, disease, or degeneration.
english_labels: Reconstructive Surgery or Surgical arthrodesis of a Major Weight-bearing Joint

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIPG.label: Suburban Market Segment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIPG.definition: The suburban market segment refers to a group of consumers or businesses located in the suburbs, areas that are typically situated on the outskirts of urban centers and characterized by a mix of residential and commercial zones. This segment is distinguished by its unique lifestyle and consumption patterns, often blending urban convenience with a more spacious and family-oriented environment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIPy.label: Chairman Emeritus Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIPy.definition: A Chairman Emeritus Clause is a contractual provision that grants a former chairman of a company certain privileges or rights, such as a seat on the board of directors or an honorary title.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIQn.label: Equal Protection Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIQn.definition: An equal protection claim is a legal action initiated by an individual or group alleging that their Fourteenth Amendment right to equal protection under the law has been violated by the government or a government actor. The Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment prohibits the government from treating individuals or groups differently based on their race, gender, national origin, or other protected categories. An equal protection claim may arise in various contexts, such as when a government enacts a law or policy that treats certain individuals or groups unfairly or unequally, or when a government actor engages in discriminatory conduct. Examples of unequal treatment can include unequal enforcement of laws, unequal access to public services or benefits, or unequal treatment in the criminal justice system.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RISX.label: Kashmiri
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RISX.definition: Kashmiri (Language) is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary used in the Kashmir region, including in legal documents, artifacts, evidence, testimony, proceedings, and other legal aspects.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RITV.label: Lease Agreements
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RITV.definition: A Lease Related Agreement refers to any supplementary contract or document associated with a primary lease agreement, addressing specific terms, conditions, or scenarios that might arise during the lease period. Examples include lease renewals, extensions, terminations, subleases, assignments, and guaranties, among others. These agreements provide clarity and legal framework for particular aspects or contingencies of the lease relationship.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIVI.label: Lead Matter Designation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIVI.definition: Designation as parent-level matter, where one or more other matters may be subsidiary matters or subset matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIVi.label: Oregon Circuit Court - Union County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIVi.definition: Oregon Circuit Court - Union County: A specific court within the Oregon Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Union County, Oregon.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIWf.label: Hearing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIWf.definition: A hearing is a legal event within the context of litigation, where parties present arguments and evidence to a judge or other decision-maker.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIZ1.label: Proceeding Reopened
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIZ1.definition: The concept of "Case Reopened" refers to a legal matter that was previously closed or resolved, but has now been reopened for further proceedings or consideration.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIaH.label: L654 Second pass document review
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIaH.definition: Activities and actions related to second pass QC of data and documents coded for relevancy, issue codes, tagging, and initial privilege determination during the first pass review.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIbk.label: Massachusetts Superior Court - Barnstable County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIbk.definition: The Massachusetts Superior Court - Barnstable County is a court of general jurisdiction in Massachusetts that hears civil and criminal cases within Barnstable County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIcJ.label: Action for Commission on Exclusive Right to Sell Listing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIcJ.definition: A legal claim made by a real estate agent or broker against another agent or broker for the exclusive right to sell a property.
english_labels: Action for Commission on Exclusive Right to Sell Listing

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIdM.label: Motion to Dismiss Case for Failure to Make Plan Payments
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIdM.definition: A Motion to Dismiss Case for Failure to Make Plan Payments is a legal request made by a party in a bankruptcy case to dismiss the case due to the debtor's failure to make payments as required by the bankruptcy plan.
english_labels: Motion to Dismiss Case for Failure to Make Plan Payments

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIeC.label: Arkansas Circuit Court - Lincoln Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIeC.definition: A court located in Lincoln County, Arkansas that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its designated geographical area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIeT.label: Independent Contractor Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIeT.definition: A legal concept that pertains to the classification and treatment of individuals who provide services to a company or organization as non-employees, typically in the context of labor and employment law.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIfT.label: Contested Adoption
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIfT.definition: A Contested Adoption occurs when one or more parties object to the adoption of a child, challenging the suitability or rights of the prospective adoptive parents. Such disputes often arise from biological parents who have not consented to the adoption, disagreements among family members, or concerns regarding the child's best interests.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIiA.label: Income Fund
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIiA.definition: An Income Fund is an investment fund that regularly distributes its investment profits to shareholders in the form of dividends or interest payments. These funds aim to provide a steady income stream to investors by focusing on assets that generate regular income.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIl8.label: Loitering
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIl8.definition: The act of remaining in a public place for an extended period of time without a clear purpose or legitimate reason, often in violation of local laws or ordinances related to curfew, loitering, or vagrancy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIox.label: Florida Circuit Court - Madison County - 3rd Circuit Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIox.definition: A court located in Madison County, Florida that is part of the larger Florida Circuit Court system.
english_labels: Florida Circuit Court - Madison County - 3rd Circuit Court

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIq5.label: Castle Doctrine
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIq5.definition: The Castle Doctrine is a legal principle derived from English Common Law that gives individuals the right to use force, including deadly force, to protect themselves against an intruder in their home. This doctrine essentially states that a person's home is their castle, and they have the right to defend it without the duty to retreat first, under certain conditions depending on jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIqm.label: Board Vice Chair
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIqm.definition: A Board Vice Chair is a board officer who assists the Board Chair in leading the board of directors and may assume the Chair's duties in their absence. The Vice Chair supports board governance, facilitates meetings, and collaborates with other board members to advance the organization’s strategic objectives.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIr4.label: C.P.A. (Certified Public Accountant)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIr4.definition: The suffix "C.P.A." stands for "Certified Public Accountant" and is used after a person's name to indicate that they have met the educational and examination requirements to be certified as a public accountant. This designation signifies the individual's expertise in accounting practices and is commonly used in professional, academic, and formal settings

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIrs.label: AAA Labor Arbitration Rules
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIrs.definition: The AAA Labor Arbitration Rules are a set of rules created by the American Arbitration Association specifically for labor disputes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIrv.label: Plaintiff Case-in-Chief
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIrv.definition: Plaintiff Case-in-Chief refers to the presentation of evidence and arguments by the plaintiff in a trial, before the defendant presents their own case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIs6.label: WC230 Conferences with Judge
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIs6.definition: Preparing for conference, attending conference, reporting on conference with Judge

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIvz.label: New York Supreme Court - Washington County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIvz.definition: The New York Supreme Court - Washington County is a court of general jurisdiction located in Washington County, New York, with authority to hear and decide a wide range of legal disputes within its geographic jurisdiction.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - Washington County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIx4.label: Security Offerings and Capital Markets Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIx4.definition: Corporate debt and equity issuance (public and private) and markets.
english_labels: Security Offerings and Capital Markets Law

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIxC.label: M.S. (Master of Science)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIxC.definition: The suffix "M.S." stands for "Master of Science" and is used after a person's name to indicate that they have earned an advanced academic degree in a science-related field. This designation signifies the individual's specialized knowledge and research skills in their area of study, and is commonly used in academic, research, and professional settings

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIxQ.label: New York Supreme Court - Albany County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIxQ.definition: The New York Supreme Court - Albany County is a court of general jurisdiction located in Albany County, New York, with authority to hear and decide a wide range of legal disputes within its geographical jurisdiction.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - Albany County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIxZ.label: Citrus Fruits
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIxZ.definition: Citrus fruits are a group of fruits from the Citrus genus, known for their juicy segments, aromatic rinds, and distinctive sour to sweet flavors. They are cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions and are rich in vitamin C, antioxidants, and essential nutrients, widely consumed fresh or used in juices, culinary applications, and flavorings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIyp.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Montgomery County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RIyp.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Montgomery County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within Montgomery County, Pennsylvania.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Montgomery County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJ1z.label: Contract Modification Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJ1z.definition: A contract modification clause is a provision in a contract that allows for changes to be made to the original agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJ2s.label: Refundable Deposit Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJ2s.definition: A refundable deposit clause is a provision in a contract that requires one party to provide a deposit to the other party, which will be returned if certain conditions are met.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJ4c.label: Immigration Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJ4c.definition: Immigration Court is an administrative forum that handles legal proceedings related to immigration matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJ5q.label: Investment Bank
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJ5q.definition: An investment bank is a financial institution that specializes in providing advisory services for mergers and acquisitions, underwriting new debt and equity securities, and facilitating the buying and selling of securities for both institutional and individual investors. Investment banks play a critical role in capital markets by helping companies raise capital and providing strategic advisory services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJ61.label: 840 Trademark (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJ61.definition: Action filed in support or to dispute a trademark claim

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJ7A.label: Wrongful Discharge in Violation of Public Policy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJ7A.definition: The concept of "Wrongful Discharge in Violation of Public Policy" refers to the termination of an employee by an employer in a manner that violates public policy, such as firing an employee for refusing to engage in illegal activities or for reporting illegal conduct.
english_labels: Wrongful Discharge in Violation of Public Policy
Wrongful Dismissal in Breach of Public Policy

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJ7M.label: Motion to Sell Property Free and Clear
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJ7M.definition: A Motion to Sell Property Free and Clear is a legal request made in a bankruptcy case to sell a property without any liens or claims against it, allowing the proceeds to be used to pay off creditors.
english_labels: Motion to Sell Property Free and Clear

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJ7P.label: Tax Incentive
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJ7P.definition: A Tax Incentive is a provision in tax law designed to encourage specific behaviors or activities by reducing a taxpayer's tax burden. It encompasses various mechanisms such as tax credits, deductions, exemptions, and preferential rates aimed at promoting certain economic or social objectives.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJ7p.label: New York Supreme Court - Cayuga County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJ7p.definition: The New York Supreme Court - Cayuga County is a court of general jurisdiction located in Cayuga County, New York, with authority to hear and decide a wide range of civil and criminal cases.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - Cayuga County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJ9O.label: Modality
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJ9O.definition: Modality refers to the way in which a statement or proposition is expressed, indicating the degree of possibility, necessity, or contingency.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJAV.label: Defamation Per Se
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJAV.definition: Defamation Per Se is a type of defamation that is inherently harmful and does not require proof of damages to be awarded compensation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJBC.label: Captive Insurance Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJBC.definition: Captive Insurance Law governs the formation, regulation, and operation of captive insurance companies, which are wholly-owned subsidiaries created to insure the risks of their parent companies or related entities. This legal practice involves compliance with jurisdictional regulations, financial solvency requirements, and risk management strategies specific to captive insurers.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJBX.label: B240 Tax Issues
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJBX.definition: Analyses and advice regarding tax-related issues, including the preservation of net operating loss carry forwards

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJC4.label: Pennsylvania Municipal Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJC4.definition: The Pennsylvania Municipal Court is a court of limited jurisdiction within the Pennsylvania State Courts system that handles minor criminal offenses, traffic violations, and civil cases involving small amounts of money.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJDv.label: L602 Interviews
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJDv.definition: Activities and actions related to the conducting of interviews with custodians, data stewards, or other individuals or groups within the organization.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJEh.label: Mistake in Contract
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJEh.definition: A Mistake in Contract is a legal claim that arises when one or both parties to a contract make an error in the terms of the agreement, which can render the contract void or unenforceable.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJGM.label: Washington Superior Court - San Juan County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJGM.definition: Washington Superior Court - San Juan County is a specific court within the Washington Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within San Juan County, Washington.
english_labels: Washington Superior Court - San Juan County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJGl.label: Oregon Board of Governors
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJGl.definition: The Oregon Board of Governors is a governing body within the Oregon State Courts system responsible for overseeing and regulating various legal proceedings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJHW.label: New York Supreme Court - Greene County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJHW.definition: The New York Supreme Court - Greene County is a court of general jurisdiction located in Greene County, New York, with authority to hear and decide a wide range of legal disputes within its geographic jurisdiction.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - Greene County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJIW.label: A119 Culling & Filtering
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJIW.definition: For discovery and eDiscovery, activities associated with grouping and filtering documents for processing. Includes deduplication, deNIST*, etc. Excludes culling and filtering associated with the creation of a Privilege Log (A124).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJKp.label: Child Care Cost Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJKp.definition: A Child Care Cost Claim is a request made by a parent or guardian to receive financial assistance or reimbursement for expenses related to the care of their child. This may include costs associated with daycare, after-school programs, or babysitters. Such claims are often made to government agencies or employers through childcare subsidy programs or flexible spending accounts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJL4.label: Intellectual Property Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJL4.definition: Intellectual Property Claims refer to legal actions taken by a party to protect their exclusive rights to intangible assets such as patents, trademarks, copyrights, and trade secrets.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJMH.label: Oregon Circuit Court - Umatilla County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJMH.definition: The Oregon Circuit Court - Umatilla County is a specific court within the Oregon Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Umatilla County, Oregon.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJNj.label: Expert System Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJNj.definition: Expert System Management refers to the use of artificial intelligence and computer technology to improve and streamline legal processes, specifically in the management of expert systems.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJO4.label: Oregon Circuit Court - Multnomah County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJO4.definition: Oregon Circuit Court - Multnomah County: A specific court within the Oregon Circuit Court system located in Multnomah County, responsible for administering legal proceedings within its jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJON.label: Emergency Hearing Motion
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJON.definition: An Emergency Hearing Motion (Bankruptcy) is a legal request made in a bankruptcy case for an urgent court hearing to address a specific issue or matter related to the bankruptcy proceedings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJOT.label: Fraud Prevention Regulation Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJOT.definition: A Fraud Prevention Regulation Claim (aka Red Flags Rule) stems from regulations by a regulator (e.g., U.S. FTC) that requires certain businesses and organizations to implement a written identity theft prevention program. Such rules are designed to detect, prevent, and mitigate identity theft by identifying and responding to "red flags," which are patterns, practices, or specific activities that indicate the possible existence of identity theft.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJPm.label: Motion to Expedite
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJPm.definition: A Motion to Expedite is a request made to the court to accelerate the proceedings of a legal case, typically due to time-sensitive circumstances or the need for a prompt resolution.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJR5.label: LAW_FIRM_POSTCODE
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJR5.definition: A law firm's postal code as defined in the LEDES98BI V5 Format Rev 1-2020 standard.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJR8.label: Financial Contagion Risk
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJR8.definition: The risk that financial instability in one sector or region spreads to others.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJSl.label: Ripeness
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJSl.definition: Ripeness refers to the readiness of a case for judicial review, usually meaning that the issues are sufficiently clear and well-defined to be considered by a court. A case that is not ripe is generally dismissed because taking it up prematurely would involve the court in abstract or hypothetical questions, rather than an existing dispute.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJUE.label: RPA Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJUE.definition: RPA Management refers to the process of managing and optimizing Robotic Process Automation (RPA) technology in order to improve legal processes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJUI.label: Description of Asset Exposure
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJUI.definition: For a given dispute, a description of the assets that are potentially exposed.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJV2.label: Private Nuisance
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJV2.definition: A private nuisance is a type of legal wrong that occurs when one person's use of their property interferes with another person's use and enjoyment of their own property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJWx.label: Litigation Hold Event
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJWx.definition: A Litigation Hold Event is a specific event within the context of a legal dispute where a party is required to preserve relevant evidence.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJX2.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - McKean County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJX2.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - McKean County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering legal proceedings in the state of Pennsylvania.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - McKean County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJXa.label: Financial Expert
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJXa.definition: An expert who opines on areas of finance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJYP.label: Employee Recruitment Event
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJYP.definition: An employee recruitment event where an employer seeks to attract and identify potential candidates for employment. This relates to immigration law, where for some matters, employers must demonstrate that there are no qualified U.S. workers available for the position and that hiring a foreign worker will not adversely affect the wages and working conditions of similarly employed U.S. workers.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJZX.label: Poison Pill Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJZX.definition: A poison pill clause is a provision in a contract that is designed to deter or prevent a hostile takeover by making the target company less attractive to the acquiring company.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJbD.label: Official Aramaic ; Imperial Aramaic
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJbD.definition: Official Aramaic and Imperial Aramaic are ancient languages used between 700-300 BCE in official and imperial contexts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJcs.label: No Agency Relationship Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJcs.definition: A "No Agency Relationship Clause" is a provision in a contract that explicitly states that no agency relationship is created between the parties, meaning that neither party has the authority to act on behalf of the other.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJcv.label: Freedom from Arbitrary Detention
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJcv.definition: Freedom from arbitrary detention is a human right that prohibits the unlawful or unjustifiable arrest or imprisonment of individuals. This right is upheld by various international legal instruments, such as the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, and aims to ensure due process and legal protections for those accused of crimes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJgC.label: Standalone Material Adverse Effect Termination Right
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJgC.definition: A Standalone Material Adverse Effect (MAE) Termination Right, is a legal provision that allows a party to terminate a contract if an event or circumstance occurs that has a significant negative impact on the value or profitability of the subject matter of the contract, and this provision is not tied to any other termination rights in the contract.
english_labels: Standalone Material Adverse Effect Termination Right

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJgD.label: Arkansas Circuit Court - Chicot Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJgD.definition: A court located in Chicot County, Arkansas that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its designated geographic area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJgl.label: Engagement Fee Description
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJgl.definition: Freeform text describing the engagement fee model.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJk2.label: Disease-Related Fractures
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJk2.definition: Pathologic fractures occur when a bone breaks in response to minimal or no trauma due to an underlying disease or condition that weakens the bone structure. These fractures are typically associated with conditions such as osteoporosis, tumors, or infections that compromise bone integrity.
english_labels: Pathologic Fractures Due to Any Cause

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJlp.label: Disorderly House
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJlp.definition: A Disorderly House is a type of crime against the public that involves maintaining a dwelling or establishment where illegal activities, such as prostitution or gambling, take place.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJma.label: N'Ko
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJma.definition: A writing system used to write the Mande languages of West Africa, characterized by a distinctive script with geometric shapes and lines.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJnI.label: Oil Spill Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJnI.definition: A claim made under environmental law for damages resulting from an oil spill.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJnZ.label: PPT
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJnZ.definition: A Microsoft PowerPoint file from from Microsoft Office 2003 or earlier.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJnx.label: State Destruction of Private Property
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJnx.definition: The State Destruction of Private Property is the legal concept where the government takes possession of private property for public use without the owner's consent, and compensates the owner for the fair market value of the property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJoZ.label: Unreasonable Search and Seizure Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJoZ.definition: Unreasonable search and seizure refers to a violation of an individual's rights under the constitution, protecting individuals from unwarranted government intrusions into their privacy by requiring that searches and seizures conducted by law enforcement or government agents must be reasonable and, in most cases, based on probable cause supported by a warrant. An unreasonable search and seizure may occur when law enforcement officers or government agents conduct a search or seizure without a warrant, without probable cause, or when the scope of the search or seizure exceeds the limits of the warrant. Examples of unreasonable searches and seizures include warrantless searches of a person's home, an arrest without probable cause, or an overly invasive search of a person or their belongings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJqP.label: Patent Infringement - Plant Patents
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJqP.definition: The unauthorized use, sale, or importation of a patented plant variety without the owner's permission.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJrr.label: Accrued Rights Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJrr.definition: An Accrued Rights Clause is a provision in a contract that ensures the preservation of rights that have already been acquired by the parties involved, even if the contract is terminated or modified.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJvI.label: Consent Judgment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJvI.definition: A Consent Judgment is a legal decision made by a court that is agreed upon by both parties involved in a dispute, rather than being imposed by the court itself.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJwV.label: OFAC Certification Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJwV.definition: A provision in a contract that requires a party to certify that they are not on the list of individuals or entities sanctioned by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJwi.label: Theft from Building
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJwi.definition: A theft from within a building which is either open to the general public or where the offender has legal access.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJwx.label: Minnesota District Court - Roseau County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RJwx.definition: Minnesota District Court - Roseau County refers to a specific court within the Minnesota District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Roseau County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RK0Q.label: Elective Share
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RK0Q.definition: A legal right of a surviving spouse to claim a portion of their deceased spouse's estate, regardless of what is stated in the deceased spouse's will, in order to prevent disinheritance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RK0i.label: Stillbirth
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RK0i.definition: The concept of Stillbirth refers to the loss of a fetus after the 20th week of pregnancy, which may be attributed to medical malpractice and can result in legal claims.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RK3a.label: A113 Communicate (witnesses)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RK3a.definition: Any communication by letter, fax, email, telephone, meetings and conferences with witnesses in the legal matter

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RK3d.label: Motion to Stay Execution of Judgment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RK3d.definition: A Motion to Stay Execution of Judgment is a request made to temporarily halt the enforcement of a court order or judgment, typically to allow for further legal proceedings or to provide time for the party to comply with the order or judgment.
english_labels: Motion to Stay Execution of Judgment

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RK5P.label: Nonverbal Learning Disability
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RK5P.definition: Nonverbal Learning Disability (NVLD) is a neurological condition characterized by significant difficulties with visual-spatial, motor, and social skills, despite strong verbal abilities. Individuals with NVLD may struggle with tasks requiring coordination, interpreting nonverbal cues, and spatial awareness, impacting their academic and social functioning.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RK6e.label: New York Supreme Court - Suffolk County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RK6e.definition: The New York Supreme Court - Suffolk County is a court of general jurisdiction located in Suffolk County, New York, with authority to hear and decide a wide range of legal disputes.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - Suffolk County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKAu.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Henry County 3
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKAu.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Henry County, Indiana, with authority over civil and criminal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKBl.label: Motor Neuron Disorder
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKBl.definition: Motor neuron disorders are a group of progressive neurological diseases that affect the motor neurons, which are the nerve cells responsible for controlling voluntary muscles. These disorders lead to muscle weakness, atrophy, and eventual paralysis as the motor neurons degenerate and die.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKDB.label: Support Personnel of Athletes or Entertainers
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKDB.definition: This visa (in the U.S., P-1S Visa) is designated for support personnel who are an integral part of the performance of an athlete or entertainer or entertainment group (in the U.S., P1A or P-1B). In the United States, this visa allows these essential support personnel to accompany the principal visa holder for the duration of the event, competition, or performance. The initial period of stay is tied to the P-1 or P-1B visa holder's duration, with the possibility of extensions
english_labels: Support Personnel of Athletes or Entertainers

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKDE.label: Matter Tax on Expenses
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKDE.definition: Matter Tax on Expenses: A specific type of tax detail that pertains to the engagement fee detail and is related to the expenses incurred during the provision of legal services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKHo.label: German
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKHo.definition: German (Language) is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary, used in legal matters as a means of document, artifact, evidence, testimony, proceeding, or any other legal aspect, and is a subcategory of the Language top-level class.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKIJ.label: Aviation Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKIJ.definition: A type of civil claim that arises from incidents related to aviation, such as accidents or injuries, and involves seeking compensation for damages.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKIY.label: Proceeding Open / Pending
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKIY.definition: The legal state of a court case that has been filed and is awaiting further action or resolution, including cases that have been transferred to a new forum or reopened.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKJ5.label: Prejudgment Attachment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKJ5.definition: Prejudgment Attachment refers to the legal process of seizing a defendant's property before a judgment is made in a lawsuit, in order to secure payment of a potential judgment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKKR.label: License (Agreement)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKKR.definition: A License (Agreement) is a legal document that grants permission to use a particular product or service under certain terms and conditions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKNm.label: Luba-Katanga
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKNm.definition: Luba-Katanga (Language) is a structured system of communication spoken in the Katanga region of the Democratic Republic of Congo.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKPv.label: Chipewyan; Dene Suline
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKPv.definition: Chipewyan and Dene Suline are indigenous languages spoken in Canada by the Chipewyan and Dene Suline peoples.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKSx.label: Automatic Termination Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKSx.definition: An automatic termination clause is a provision in a contract that specifies the circumstances under which the agreement will end without the need for further action by either party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKTU.label: Judicial Legal Conclusion
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKTU.definition: An asserted legal argument, proposition, or point of law, as adopted by a decisionmaker (e.g., judge, magistrate, arbitrator).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKU1.label: Assignment of Magistrate Judge
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKU1.definition: The "Assignment of Magistrate Judge" concept refers to the process of assigning a magistrate judge to a case, which falls under the broader category of assigning judges to cases.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKUC.label: Cybersecurity Incident
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKUC.definition: A Cybersecurity Incident is an event that compromises the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of information systems, data, or networks. These incidents can result from malicious activities such as data breaches, data tampering, denial of service attacks, malware infections, phishing attacks, or ransomware attacks.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKUS.label: Minnesota District Court - Isanti County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKUS.definition: Minnesota District Court - Isanti County: A specific court within the Minnesota District Court system located in Isanti County, responsible for administering legal proceedings within its jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKWm.label: Response to Counterclaim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKWm.definition: A response filed by a defendant in a lawsuit against a counterclaim made by the plaintiff, falling under the category of legal pleadings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKXO.label: Negligent Interference with Contractual Relationship
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKXO.definition: Negligent Interference with Contractual Relationship is a legal claim that arises when a third party's careless actions cause a breach of contract between two parties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKY2.label: Immigration Petitions and Applications
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKY2.definition: Immigration petitions and applications are formal requests submitted to immigration authorities for specific immigration benefits, such as visas, green cards, or naturalization. In the United States, for example, forms like the I-130 (Petition for Alien Relative) or the I-485 (Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status) are commonly used for family-based immigration, while the I-129 (Petition for a Nonimmigrant Worker) is used for employment-based visas.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKYw.label: matter_tax_on_exp
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKYw.definition: "Sum of all TAX_SUMMARY.total_tax_on_expense for matter/invoice. This figure includes Withholding Taxes but not Tiered Taxes. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKar.label: Employee Layoff Event
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKar.definition: Employee layoff event refers to the temporary or permanent separation of employees from their jobs due to economic conditions, organizational restructuring, or other non-performance-related factors. Unlike terminations for misconduct or performance issues, layoffs are generally not the fault of the employee.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKbN.label: Board Treasurer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKbN.definition: A Board Treasurer is a board officer responsible for overseeing the financial affairs of an organization, including budget planning, financial reporting, and ensuring sound financial governance. The Treasurer works closely with management to monitor financial performance and ensure compliance with financial policies and regulations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKbp.label: Elamite
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKbp.definition: A language that was spoken in ancient Elam, which is now modern-day Iran.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKcU.label: L610 Preservation (NOS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKcU.definition: "NOS" = Not Otherwise Specified (catch-all, includes the subcategories) Primarily hourly charges.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKcw.label: Disclosure Schedules
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKcw.definition: Disclosure Schedules are documents that provide detailed information about a company's assets, liabilities, contracts, and other important information that is relevant to a merger or acquisition transaction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKex.label: Apricots
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKex.definition: Apricots are small, golden-orange stone fruits from the Prunus armeniaca species, characterized by their smooth, velvety skin and sweet-tart flavor. They are consumed fresh, dried, or processed into jams, juices, and desserts, valued for their high vitamin A and fiber content, as well as their antioxidant properties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKgO.label: UTBMS MF50 Intellectual Property and Technology
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKgO.definition: A legal billing code used to categorize services related to the acquisition or transfer of intellectual property and technology assets, falling under the broader category of UTBMS Mergers and Acquisitions (M&A).
english_labels: UTBMS MF50 Intellectual Property and Technology

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKj3.label: 8th Amendment Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKj3.definition: An Eighth Amendment claim is a legal argument asserting that an individual's constitutional protection against cruel and unusual punishment, as guaranteed by the Eighth Amendment of the United States Constitution, has been violated. Such claims typically involve disputes over the conditions of confinement, the use of excessive force, or the imposition of excessive fines or bail, and aim to protect the basic human rights and dignity of individuals subject to punishment or detention.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKlw.label: 04_2 Immigration (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKlw.definition: Immigration (PACER NoS) refers to the category of legal cases related to immigration matters, as classified by the PACER Nature of Suit (NoS) Codes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKnJ.label: Antitrust - Tying Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKnJ.definition: A tying claim in antitrust law refers to a situation where a seller requires a buyer to purchase a second product or service as a condition of purchasing the first product or service, which may be considered anti-competitive behavior.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKoM.label: Deemed Contribution and Distribution Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKoM.definition: A Deemed Contribution and Distribution Clause is a provision in a contract that specifies how contributions and distributions will be treated as if they were made on a certain date, regardless of when they were actually made.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKpF.label: Invoice Other ISO
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKpF.definition: A type of fee invoice detail that pertains to non-ISO charges on an invoice for legal services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKpp.label: Professional Conduct Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKpp.definition: Professional Conduct Claims refer to legal claims or allegations made against laypersons or professionals, asserting that they have breached established standards of practice, ethics, or legal requirements for a field. These claims can encompass a range of violations, including malpractice, unauthorized practice, and other breaches of professional duties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKqM.label: Legal Opinion Document
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKqM.definition: A legal opinion document is a written statement by a legal expert, usually an attorney or a law firm, expressing their professional judgment on the legal aspects of a transaction, agreement, or legal issue. It provides an analysis of the legality, enforceability, or compliance of the matter in question with applicable laws and regulations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKqx.label: Administration of Environmental Quality Programs Industry
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKqx.definition: The Administration of Environmental Quality Programs subsector groups government establishments primarily engaged in the administration of environmental quality.
english_labels: Administration of Environmental Quality Programs Industry

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKsQ.label: False Advertising Act Violation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKsQ.definition: A False Advertising Act Violation is a claim that a party has made false or misleading statements in connection with the promotion or sale of a product or service, in violation of the False Advertising Act and related laws and regulations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKwy.label: Payment of Public Benefit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKwy.definition: Payment of public benefit refers to the disbursement of financial assistance or provision of services to eligible recipients under a specific public benefit program. Payments can be made through various methods such as direct deposit, checks, or electronic benefit transfer (EBT) cards, and are generally subject to periodic reviews or re-certifications to confirm ongoing eligibility

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKzL.label: Transactional Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RKzL.definition: Any process that involves two or more parties in creation of a contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RL3g.label: Information Technology Outsourcing Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RL3g.definition: An Information Technology Outsourcing Agreement is a contractual arrangement where a company engages an external service provider to manage and deliver its information technology services. This agreement may specify the scope of IT services, performance standards, and data security measures.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RL5k.label: Due Diligence Request List
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RL5k.definition: A Due Diligence Request List is a compilation of questions and document requests directed towards the party undergoing due diligence, typically furnished by the buyer or auditor. This list guides the gathering of information and serves as a framework for what will be scrutinized in the due diligence process.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RL5m.label: Georgia Superior Court - Dodge County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RL5m.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Dodge County is a specific court within the Georgia Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Dodge County, Georgia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RL6I.label: 368 Asbestos Personal Injury Product Liability (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RL6I.definition: Action alleging personal injury or death caused by exposure to asbestos products.
english_labels: 368 Asbestos Personal Injury Product Liability (PACER NoS)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RL7I.label: Amortized Asset
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RL7I.definition: An Amortized Asset is a financial instrument where the principal amount is gradually reduced through regular payments over the life of the asset. These payments typically include both interest and principal, leading to a decrease in the outstanding balance until the loan is fully repaid by the maturity date.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RL7s.label: Notary Public
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RL7s.definition: A person authorized by a state to administer oaths, certify documents, attest to the authenticity of signatures, and perform official acts in commercial matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RL81.label: Credit Card Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RL81.definition: A Credit Card Agreement is a legally binding contract between a credit card issuer and a cardholder outlining the terms and conditions under which the cardholder may use the credit card. This agreement specifies the interest rates, fees, billing processes, and cardholder obligations associated with the card.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RL8u.label: High School Diploma
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RL8u.definition: A High School Diploma is an academic credential awarded upon successful completion of a secondary education program. It signifies the completion of basic education requirements and prepares individuals for higher education or employment

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLBM.label: TR750 Domain Names gTLDs Domain Name Filing Generic
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLBM.definition: All actions associated with completing a domain name application (including renewal) that is to be filed as a generic top-level domain (gTLD), e.g., .com. The domain name applications should be filed through the current domain name provider unless otherwise instructed.
english_labels: TR750 Domain Names - gTLDs Domain Name Filing - Generic
TR750 Domain Names gTLDs Domain Name Filing Generic

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLC0.label: Materiality Scrape Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLC0.definition: A Materiality Scrape Clause is a provision in a contract that specifies that in the event of a conflict between the materiality definition in the contract and that in another agreement, the definition in the other agreement will be used.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLCg.label: Turnover and Other General Goods and Services Tax Payment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLCg.definition: Turnover and Other General Goods and Services Tax Payment refers to multi-stage cumulative taxes and taxes where elements of consumption taxes are combined with multistage taxes. These taxes are levied each time a transaction takes place, without deduction for taxes paid on inputs. Multi-stage taxes can incorporate elements of value-added or sales taxes, leading to taxation at multiple points in the supply chain.
english_labels: Turnover and Other General Goods and Services Tax Payment
Turnover and other general taxes on goods and services

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLFu.label: A117 Special Handling Copying/Scanning/Imaging (Internal)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLFu.definition: Any special oversized copying, binding, scanning, imaging and photograph reproduction which requires manual handling

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLFy.label: Employer Improperly Handling Employee Wages
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLFy.definition: Employer Improperly Handling Employee Wages: The act of an employer mishandling or failing to properly pay an employee for their work, which may include withholding wages, failing to pay overtime, or other violations of wage and hour laws.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLHy.label: African Union
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLHy.definition: AU (African Union): A continental union consisting of 55 member states located in Africa, aimed at promoting economic, social, and political integration, and resolving conflicts among member states.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLIU.label: STEM Training Plan
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLIU.definition: In United States immigration law, the F-1 STEM Training Plan refers to the plan developed by an international student pursuing studies in a Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics (STEM) field in the U.S. This plan is a component of the Optional Practical Training (OPT) extension for F-1 students, which allows them to work in the U.S. for an additional 24 months after completing their degree. The STEM Training Plan outlines how the student's employment will be related to their field of study and how it will contribute to their practical training and skill development.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLIW.label: Real Estate Zoning Modifications
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLIW.definition: Real Estate Zoning Modifications refer to changes in the zoning classifications or rules governing the use, development, or characteristics of a specific parcel of land. These modifications are generally initiated by property owners and require approval from local zoning authorities, often after public hearings, assessments, and legal evaluations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLIv.label: Paternity / Parentage Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLIv.definition: A Paternity/Parentage Claim is a legal action brought to establish the identity of a child's biological father or mother, typically in the context of family law or matrimonial claims.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLJT.label: Bank’s Wrongful Payment of Negotiable Instrument
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLJT.definition: The Bank's Wrongful Payment of Negotiable Instrument refers to a situation where a bank makes a payment on a negotiable instrument without proper authorization or without verifying the authenticity of the instrument, resulting in a loss to the rightful owner of the instrument.
english_labels: Bank’s Wrongful Payment of Negotiable Instrument

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLLg.label: Resume
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLLg.definition: A "Resume," also known as a "Curriculum Vitae (CV)," is a concise and structured document that provides an overview of an individual's education, work experience, skills, achievements, and qualifications. It is typically used for job applications and serves as a summary of an individual's professional background.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLNc.label: Chiropractor Malpractice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLNc.definition: Chiropractor Malpractice refers to a type of medical malpractice claim that arises from the negligent or intentional actions of a chiropractor, resulting in harm or injury to a patient.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLNl.label: Indemnification
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLNl.definition: Indemnification is a legal remedy sought by a party to be protected from financial loss or liability resulting from a specific event or action, and may be implied or granted by contract or court order.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLQe.label: Amputation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLQe.definition: Amputation is the surgical removal of a limb or extremity, such as an arm, leg, foot, hand, toe, or finger. This procedure is often performed to treat severe injuries, infections, diseases like diabetes or cancer, or as a result of traumatic accidents, leading to significant changes in mobility and functionality.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLQh.label: Makasar
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLQh.definition: Makasar is a language that belongs to the Austronesian language family and is primarily spoken in the South Sulawesi province of Indonesia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLS5.label: Promotion Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLS5.definition: A promotion clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the terms and conditions for an individual or entity to receive a promotion or advancement in their position or status.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLU1.label: Application to Have Filing Fee Waived
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLU1.definition: An Application to Have Filing Fee Waived is a request made by an individual or entity to waive the fee required to file for bankruptcy.
english_labels: Application to Have Filing Fee Waived

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLUh.label: Georgia District Court - Stephens County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLUh.definition: Georgia District Court - Stephens County: A specific court within the Georgia District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Stephens County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLUl.label: Oregon Circuit Court - Washington County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLUl.definition: Oregon Circuit Court - Washington County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Oregon, located in Washington County and responsible for hearing civil and criminal cases within its jurisdictional boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLZa.label: PA440 Quasi-Judicial Administrative Proceedings - Domestic
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLZa.definition: All action associated with completing a quasi-judicial proceeding before an administrative tribunal associated with the Patent Office of the home country of the applicant in connection with an application filed under PA300, including Appeals, Oppositions, Interferences, and other ex-parte and inter-partes proceedings. Includes collecting evidence, preparing and filing motions, briefs, responses, replies, surreplies, and other documents, attending conferences, depositions, hearings, and other proceedings. Does not include requests for supervisory action ("Petitions" in the U.S.) under PA430. Note that external expenses (or "disbursements" in the U.S.) are included under E100.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLZk.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Monroe County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLZk.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court located in Monroe County, which is responsible for handling minor criminal offenses, traffic violations, and civil cases within its jurisdiction.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Monroe County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLZy.label: Minnesota District Court - Kanabec County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLZy.definition: A court located in Kanabec County, Minnesota that has jurisdiction over cases within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLcS.label: Standing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLcS.definition: Lack of Standing: A defense raised in a civil lawsuit where the plaintiff does not have the legal right to bring the claim because they are not directly affected or harmed by the defendant's actions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLeo.label: WC420 Expert Witnesses
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLeo.definition: Preparing for examination of expert witness, Interview/meeting with expert witness, Preparing for cross-examination of expert witness, Review & analysis of deposition /trial transcripts

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLfo.label: Dangerous Condition of Public Property
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLfo.definition: A Dangerous Condition of Public Property refers to a situation where a government entity fails to maintain its property in a safe condition, resulting in harm or injury to the public.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLgH.label: Assignment of Security Interest Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLgH.definition: An Assignment of Security Interest Clause is a provision in a legal agreement that allows a creditor to transfer their security interest in a property to another party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLjU.label: Variable Rate Interest Payment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLjU.definition: A Variable Rate Interest Payment is a type of interest payment structure where the interest rate can change over the life of the debt instrument. This structure allows for interest rate adjustments based on predetermined factors such as market indices, step-up/step-down schedules, or other benchmarks, providing flexibility in response to changing economic conditions or issuer circumstances.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLkZ.label: New York Appellate Division - 2d Dept.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLkZ.definition: The New York Appellate Division - 2d Dept. is a specific court within the New York Supreme Court - Appellate Division that hears appeals from lower courts in the second department of New York State.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLl5.label: Gondi
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLl5.definition: Gondi (Language) is a structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary, and is a member of the Language class.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLlK.label: PA530 Design Application Preparation - International
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLlK.definition: All actions associated with completing a design patent (but not utility or utility model) applications or design registration applications that are to be filed outside the ('domestic') home country or region of the applicant, including translations, review of any invention disclosure materials or parent applications, drafting of application including pre-filing revision of parent applications, preparation and execution of formal documents (such as assignments, declarations, information disclosure statements, and transmittals) filing of application, and reporting to the client. Note that government fees and other external drafting expenses are included under E100.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLm5.label: California Superior Court - Sacramento Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLm5.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Sacramento County, California, with the power to hear and decide a wide range of legal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLmM.label: X128 Trial Transcripts
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLmM.definition: Any court reporter and transcript fees associated with trail transcripts

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLmW.label: Dismissal for Failure to Prosecute
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLmW.definition: Dismissal for Failure to Prosecute: A court order dismissing a legal case due to the plaintiff's failure to take necessary actions to move the case forward.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLo6.label: matter_net_exp
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLo6.definition: "Using the Math Statement on the next tab: The total for pre-split non-taxable expense items on the bill + The total for pre-split Tax1 expense items on the bill + ... repeated for each pre-split tax expense items on the bill + The total for post-split non-taxable expense items on the bill + The total for post-split Tax1 expense items on the bill + ... repeated for each post-split tax expense items on the bill tax_total_detail_exp "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLoM.label: Employment Leave
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLoM.definition: "Employment Leave" refers to authorized periods of time when an employee is permitted to be absent from work while retaining their employment status. This can include various types of leave, such as vacation leave, sick leave, parental leave, or other forms of time off that employees may be entitled to based on their employment contracts or labor laws.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLoV.label: Executive Branch Monitoring Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLoV.definition: Executive Branch Monitoring Practice entails the systematic observation and analysis of actions and decisions made by the executive branch of government, including regulatory agencies and administrative bodies. This practice ensures that executive activities comply with legal standards and provides stakeholders with insights into regulatory changes and administrative actions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLoX.label: Connecticut Court of Common Pleas - Appellate Division
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLoX.definition: The Connecticut Court of Common Pleas - Appellate Division is a specific court within the Connecticut State Courts system that hears appeals from lower courts.
english_labels: Connecticut Court of Common Pleas - Appellate Division

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLp6.label: Execution Sale
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLp6.definition: The Execution Sale is a legal process of selling assets to satisfy a debt or judgment, typically ordered by a court, and falls under the broader category of Liquidation of Assets.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLrq.label: Personal Income
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLrq.definition: Personal income refers to the total earnings an individual receives from various sources, including wages, salaries, investments, and business activities. It encompasses all monetary inflows before taxes and deductions and serves as the basis for calculating tax liabilities and evaluating financial well-being.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLrt.label: Grebo
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLrt.definition: A language spoken by the Grebo people in Liberia and Ivory Coast.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLrx.label: Exterior Signage Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLrx.definition: Exterior Signage Clause: A provision in a contract that specifies the terms and conditions related to the display of signs or other advertising materials on the exterior of a building or property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLsl.label: Personality Disorder Discharge
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLsl.definition: A Military Personality Disorder Discharge refers to the release of a service member from active duty based on the diagnosis of a personality disorder that interferes with their ability to effectively serve in the military. This type of discharge is typically considered administrative and is based on the assessment that the disorder existed prior to service and was not a result of or aggravated by military duties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLvh.label: Crimes Against the Public
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLvh.definition: Crimes Against the Public are offenses that harm or disrupt the general welfare and safety of society, including but not limited to prostitution, disorderly conduct, rioting, weapons offenses, unlawful assembly, criminal gang participation, unlawful gaming and lotteries, curfew violations, loitering, vagrancy, disorderly house, failure to disperse, and drug crimes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLwl.label: X400 Software License/User Access Fee
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLwl.definition: Any software licensing or user access fees associated with subscription- or SaaS-based fees. Indicate # of users as units; if different rates depending on user type, split into multiple expense lines by rate.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLxL.label: Equity Agreements
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLxL.definition: Equity Related Agreement is an umbrella term for agreements related to ownership interest in a company. It outlines terms and conditions associated with equity ownership, including rights and responsibilities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLyr.label: Georgia Superior Court - Ben Hill County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RLyr.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia, located in Ben Hill County and having authority over civil and criminal cases within its jurisdiction.
english_labels: Georgia Superior Court - Ben Hill County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RM0X.label: Witness List
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RM0X.definition: A witness list is a document that contains the names of individuals who may be called upon to testify in a legal proceeding related to bankruptcy and restructuring.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RM13.label: Kansas District Court - Marion County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RM13.definition: Kansas District Court - Marion County: A specific court within the Kansas District Court system located in Marion County, responsible for administering legal proceedings within its jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RM35.label: Mass Torts Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RM35.definition: Mass torts law is an area of law that deals with legal actions involving numerous plaintiffs against one or a few defendants, where the plaintiffs allege harm caused by common actions or products. These cases often involve complex negotiations and litigation due to the large number of claimants, extensive evidence, and significant legal and financial stakes.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RM46.label: Texas District Court - Guadalupe County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RM46.definition: A court located in Guadalupe County, Texas that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RM5N.label: Annual Information Form
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RM5N.definition: The Annual Information Form, also known as Form 10-K in the U.S., is an extensive disclosure document filed annually that includes a detailed account of a company's financial performance and operations. It is required by securities regulators and is intended for shareholders and potential investors.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RM6K.label: Caselaw and Common Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RM6K.definition: The law as established by the outcome of previously decided court cases (e.g., judicial opinions).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RM6V.label: Uniformity Clause Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RM6V.definition: A Uniformity Clause claim refers to a legal argument challenging the constitutionality of a tax or revenue-related law based on the requirements outlined in the Uniformity Clause of a particular jurisdiction's constitution. This claim asserts that the law violates the Uniformity Clause by imposing taxes or burdens in a manner that is not uniform or equal across the affected individuals or entities, potentially rendering it invalid or unconstitutional. The Uniformity Clause typically aims to ensure fairness and equality in taxation or revenue measures.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RM83.label: Death Certificate
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RM83.definition: A Death Certificate is an official document issued by a government authority that records the details of a person's death. It typically includes information such as the deceased individual's name, date and place of death, cause of death, and the attending physician's or coroner's signature. Death certificates are important for legal and administrative purposes, including the settlement of the deceased person's estate and handling matters related to inheritance, insurance, and funeral arrangements.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RM8M.label: New Jersey Superior Court - Somerset County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RM8M.definition: The New Jersey Superior Court - Somerset County is a court of general jurisdiction within the New Jersey state court system, located in Somerset County and serving the surrounding area.
english_labels: New Jersey Superior Court - Somerset County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RM8u.label: Religious Law System
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RM8u.definition: A Religious Law System is a legal framework grounded in religious beliefs, texts, and traditions, governing both the moral and legal aspects of the lives of its adherents. These systems derive their authority from sacred scriptures and religious institutions, and often encompass both private conduct and public law.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RM9x.label: Legal Aid Organization
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RM9x.definition: A Legal Aid Organization is a non-profit entity that provides free or low-cost legal assistance to individuals who cannot afford private legal representation. These organizations typically serve low-income clients, offering services on matters such as family law, housing, and employment issues.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RMAQ.label: Intellectual Property Indemnification Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RMAQ.definition: A provision in a contract that requires one party to compensate the other for any legal costs or damages resulting from a claim of intellectual property infringement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RMCO.label: Forum Selection Clause Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RMCO.definition: A forum selection clause claim is a legal argument or plan that asserts a specific venue for resolving a dispute, and is supported by legal or other professional frameworks.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RMDF.label: Presumption of Death From Absence
