https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rea9.definition: A type of therapy that is designed to address issues within a family unit, specifically in the context of criminal disposition conditions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/ReaS.label: Indiana Superior Court - LaGrange County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/ReaS.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Indiana that hears civil and criminal cases within LaGrange County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RedX.label: Privacy Shield Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RedX.definition: A Privacy Shield Clause is a provision in a data privacy agreement that ensures the protection of personal information transferred between the European Union and the United States.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Redq.label: Arson
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Redq.definition: To unlawfully and intentionally damage, or attempt to damage, any real or personal property by fire or incendiary device

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Ref4.label: Family Health Insurance Plan
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Ref4.definition: A family health insurance plan covers not just an individual policyholder but also members of their family, such as a spouse and/or children. These plans often have higher premiums but may offer a cost advantage on a per-person basis.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Reh0.label: WC340 Expert Discovery
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Reh0.definition: Preparing expert discovery and deposition notices, Communicating with expert and opposing counsel, Preparing subpoena to secure experts (vocational/ medical/other) appearance at deposition/trial, Discussing deposition strategy, Preparation for and consultation with expert, Reviewing expert documents/records and/or films review, Drafting expert summaries, Preparation for and consultation with expert, Arranging and scheduling Independent Medical Examinations (IME) and Impairment Rating Evaluations (IRE), Review & Analysis of Independent medical examination (IME) & impairment rating evaluation (IRE), Communicating with expert (vocation/medical and other) and obtaining vocational documents

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RehK.label: Clearing Title
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RehK.definition: Clearing title refers to the process of resolving legal issues, claims, or encumbrances that could cloud the ownership status or legal rights associated with a particular property or piece of real estate. This process typically involves investigating and addressing any outstanding liens, disputes, or defects in the property's title to establish a clean and unambiguous ownership status. Clearing title is often necessary when buying or selling real estate to ensure that the buyer receives clear and marketable title to the property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rej9.label: Fund Management Company
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rej9.definition: A Fund Management Company is a business entity that pools money from individual and institutional investors to invest in financial securities such as stocks, bonds, or other assets. The company is responsible for making investment decisions, administering the fund, and providing asset management services, typically in exchange for management fees and performance-based compensation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RekH.label: Surface Water Rights
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RekH.definition: These rights pertain to the use of water from sources that exist on the surface of the land, such as lakes, rivers, and streams. The allocation and usage of these rights can be based on factors like historic use, regional laws, and treaties.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Ren2.label: Skateboard and Hover Board Liability Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Ren2.definition: A Skateboard and Hover Board Liability Claim is a legal claim for damages resulting from injuries caused by the use of a skateboard or hover board, falling under the category of Personal Injury Claims.
english_labels: Skateboard and Hover Board Liability Claim

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Reoi.label: PA420 Preliminary Amendment - Domestic
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Reoi.definition: All action associated with revising an application prior to the examination of the application on its merits in the home country of the applicant for an application filed under PA300, including preparation of amendments and revised drawings that do not affect the scope of the disclosure. Note that Preliminary Amendments that are filed with a continuing application without affecting the scope of the disclosure are included under PA350. Also note that preliminary amendments extending the scope of the disclosure ("new matter" in the U.S.) in an earlier-filed application and requiring the issuance of a new application number ("continuation-in-part" or "CIP" applications in the U.S.) are included under PA310-340.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Repz.label: Indigent
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Repz.definition: Indigent refers to an individual who is financially unable to afford the basic necessities of life, including the costs associated with legal proceedings. In a legal context, indigent status may qualify a person for free legal representation or the waiver of court fees under the principle of in forma pauperis.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RerE.label: Refinancing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RerE.definition: Refinancing is the process of replacing an existing loan with a new loan, typically with different terms, to reduce interest rates, change the loan duration, or access equity. Borrowers use refinancing to improve their financial situation, often to lower monthly payments or reduce the total interest paid over the loan's life.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RerZ.label: New York Supreme Court - Columbia County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RerZ.definition: The New York Supreme Court - Columbia County is a court of general jurisdiction located in Columbia County, New York, with authority to hear and decide a wide range of legal disputes within its geographic jurisdiction.
english_labels: New York Supreme Court - Columbia County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Resw.label: Subject-Matter Jurisdiction
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Resw.definition: Subject-Matter Jurisdiction refers to the authority of a court to hear and decide a particular type of legal dispute, based on the subject matter of the case and the laws governing it.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Retc.label: Motion to Allow Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Retc.definition: A Motion to Allow Claims is a request made in a bankruptcy case to permit creditors to assert their claims against the debtor's estate.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Revs.label: State Upper House Legislator
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Revs.definition: A State Senator is an elected official who serves as a member of the upper chamber of a state's bicameral legislature. This individual is responsible for proposing, debating, and voting on state laws, policies, and budgets, as well as representing the interests of constituents from their specific senatorial district.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rey5.label: Directly or Indirectly Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rey5.definition: A Directly or Indirectly Clause is a provision in a contract that either explicitly or implicitly imposes obligations or restrictions on a party, and is a subcategory of a Contractual Clause.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rf0s.label: B160 Fee/Employment Applications
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rf0s.definition: Preparations of employment and fee applications for self or others; motions to establish interim procedures

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rf6V.label: Financial Advisor Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rf6V.definition: Financial Advisor Practice refers to the professional services provided by a financial advisor in analyzing and managing assets for clients.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rf6v.label: Georgia District Court - Candler County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rf6v.definition: A court located in Candler County, Georgia that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfAE.label: Grant of Right of First Offer Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfAE.definition: A Grant of Right of First Offer Clause is a provision in a contract that gives a party the opportunity to purchase a specific asset before it is offered to others.
english_labels: Grant of Right of First Offer Clause

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfBd.label: Amount in Controversy / Dispute
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfBd.definition: The amount at stake in a dispute, particularly where the jurisdictional requirements for certain courts (e.g., federal courts, small claims courts) require either maximum or minimum amounts in controversy — including both plaintiffs' claims and defendants' counterclaims.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfEl.label: po_number
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfEl.definition: "The alphanumeric, client-assigned purchase order number or code. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfFv.label: UTBMS MF60 Real Property
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfFv.definition: A legal billing code used to classify services related to the acquisition, sale, or lease of real property, which falls under the broader category of UTBMS Mergers and Acquisitions (M&A).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfFz.label: L633 Foreign language translation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfFz.definition: Activities and actions related to foreign language translation of both electronic and paper documents.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfHx.label: Oregon Circuit Court - Coos County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfHx.definition: The Oregon Circuit Court - Coos County is a specific court within the Oregon Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Coos County, Oregon.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfIB.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Pulaski County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfIB.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Pulaski County: A specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Pulaski County, Missouri.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfJO.label: Minnesota District Court - Lyon County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfJO.definition: Minnesota District Court - Lyon County is a specific court within the Minnesota District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Lyon County, Minnesota.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfJi.label: Legal Clinic
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfJi.definition: A Legal Clinic is an organization that provides free or low-cost legal services to individuals and communities, often staffed by law students under the supervision of licensed attorneys. It offers practical legal education to students while serving the legal needs of underserved populations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfNc.label: Settlement Documents
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfNc.definition: Settlement Documents are written or recorded representations of agreements made between parties in a legal dispute, including settlement agreements, plea agreements, settlement offers, and settlement authorities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfOg.label: Regulatory Guidance
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfOg.definition: Regulatory Guidance refers to formal recommendations or interpretations issued by a regulatory body to clarify or explain laws and regulations. This guidance assists organizations in understanding their legal obligations and how to achieve compliance.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfP0.label: Due Process Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfP0.definition: A due process claim is a legal action initiated by an individual or entity alleging that their right to due process, as protected by the Fifth and Fourteenth Amendments of the United States Constitution, has been violated by the government or a government actor. Due process refers to the legal requirement that the government must respect and uphold the legal rights of individuals when carrying out actions that may affect their life, liberty, or property. A due process claim can arise in two contexts: procedural due process and substantive due process. Procedural due process claims involve allegations that the government has failed to provide adequate notice, a fair hearing, or other procedural safeguards before depriving an individual of their rights. Substantive due process claims, on the other hand, involve allegations that the government has infringed on fundamental rights or acted arbitrarily, even if proper procedures were followed.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfP8.label: Washington Superior Court - Pacific County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfP8.definition: Washington Superior Court - Pacific County: A specific court within the Washington Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Pacific County, Washington.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfRb.label: Counter-Defendant
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfRb.definition: A person against whom a counterclaim is brought.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfSV.label: Lithuanian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfSV.definition: Lithuanian (Language) is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary used in Lithuania and by Lithuanian speakers.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfTo.label: PA350 Continuing Application Preparation - Domestic
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfTo.definition: All actions associated with completing a continuing patent application (claiming priority to an earlier-filed, parent application in the same country, without adding any new disclosure) that are to be filed in the ("domestic") home country or region of the applicant, including review of parent application, drafting and execution of any formal documents (such as transmittals and information disclosure statements), filing of application, and reporting to the client. Includes Divisional and Reissue Applications, and Reexamination Requests. Also includes PCT National Phase entry where the parent PCT International Application was previously filed in the same country. For PCT National Phase entry in other (non-domestic or "international") countries, use PA500. Note that (so-called "continuation-in-part") patent applications extending the scope of the disclosure (or adding "new matter" in the U.S.) in an earlier-filed application are included under PA310- 340. Also note that government fees (and other "disbursements" in the U.S.) and external imaging expenses are included under E100.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfUn.label: Washington Superior Court - Whatcom County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfUn.definition: Washington Superior Court - Whatcom County: A specific court located in Whatcom County, Washington that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical boundaries.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfUz.label: No Contest
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfUz.definition: No Contest (aka Nolo contendere) is a legal plea in which a defendant in a criminal case neither admits nor disputes the charges against them. This plea is often used as an alternative to pleading guilty or not guilty, allowing the defendant to avoid admitting guilt while still accepting punishment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfVO.label: Exclusive Supplier Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfVO.definition: An Exclusive Supplier Clause is a provision in a contract that grants one party the exclusive right to supply goods or services to another party, thereby prohibiting the other party from obtaining those goods or services from any other source.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfXf.label: Equipment Agreements
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfXf.definition: An Equipment Related Agreement is a legally binding contract that governs the use, rental, purchase, or maintenance of specific equipment or machinery. These agreements detail terms such as ownership, responsibilities for maintenance and repair, payment arrangements, and conditions for returning or replacing the equipment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfYM.label: Counterpart Signatures Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfYM.definition: A Counterpart Signatures Clause is a provision in a contract that allows for multiple copies of the same document to be signed separately, but still be considered as one original document.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rf_V.label: PA320 Non-Provisional Application Preparation - Domestic
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rf_V.definition: All actions associated with completing a non-provisional utility or utility model (but not design or provisional) patent application that are to be filed in the ("domestic") home country or region of the applicant, including review of invention disclosure materials and prior art, interviews with the inventors, drafting and revision of application, preparation and execution of formal documents (such as assignments, declarations, information disclosure statements, transmittals, and biological deposits) filing of application, and reporting to the client. Includes preparation of PCT, European and other regional applications when filed in the home country of the applicant. Note that government fees and external drafting expenses (or "disbursements" in the U.S.) are included under E100.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rfcf.label: Sedition
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rfcf.definition: Sedition is a crime against the government that involves inciting rebellion or resistance against lawful authority.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfdF.label: Implicit Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfdF.definition: An Implicit Agreement is a contract or understanding inferred from the actions, behavior, or circumstances of the parties involved rather than from direct, explicit communication. Such agreements rely on the assumption that the parties have a mutual understanding based on their conduct and the surrounding context.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfdN.label: Appellate Procedural Motions
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfdN.definition: Appellate Procedural Motions are requests made to an appellate court regarding the procedures of a case, such as substituting a party or expediting an appeal.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rfds.label: Luiseno
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rfds.definition: A Native American language spoken by the Luiseno people in Southern California.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rfgt.label: Red Light Violation Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rfgt.definition: A Red Light Violation Claim involves a legal assertion that a driver has failed to comply with a red traffic light regulation, potentially leading to civil or administrative penalties. This claim can be part of broader traffic enforcement actions or disputes, often requiring adjudication or settlement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rfl9.label: Joint Defense Group Member
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rfl9.definition: A member of a Joint Defense Group.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rflf.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Vernon County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rflf.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Vernon County refers to a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Vernon County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfnY.label: PA610 Information Disclosure Statement - International
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfnY.definition: All action associated with bringing prior art, or other information, to the attention of an Examiner outside the home country of the applicant in connection with an application filed under PA500. Note that Information Disclosure Statements that are filed with the application are included under PA500.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rfo8.label: Tax Invoice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rfo8.definition: A tax invoice is a type of fee invoice detail that provides a breakdown of the taxes charged for legal services rendered.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rfp3.label: Right of First Negotiation Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rfp3.definition: A Right of First Negotiation Clause is a provision in a contract that grants one party the exclusive right to negotiate with the other party before any other potential buyers or sellers, typically in regards to a specific asset or property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfpJ.label: PA640 Quasi-Judicial Administrative Proceedings - International
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfpJ.definition: All action associated with completing a quasi-judicial proceeding before an administrative tribunal associated with a Patent Office outside of the home country of the applicant in connection with an application filed under PA500, including Appeals, Oppositions, Interferences and other ex-parte and inter-partes proceedings. Includes collecting evidence, preparing and filing motions, briefs, responses, replies, surreplies, and other documents, attending conferences, depositions, hearings, and other proceedings. Does not include requests for supervisory action ("Petitions" in the U.S.) under PA630. Note that external expenses are included under E100

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfqS.label: Achinese
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfqS.definition: Achinese is a language that belongs to the Austronesian language family and is spoken in the Aceh province of Indonesia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rfrr.label: Testicle Cancer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rfrr.definition: Testicle cancer, also known as testicular cancer, is a malignant tumor that originates in the tissues of one or both testicles, the male reproductive glands located in the scrotum. It includes various subtypes, such as seminomas and non-seminomas, and can cause symptoms like testicular lumps, swelling, and discomfort, often requiring treatments like surgery, chemotherapy, and radiation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RftL.label: Bermudan Call Option Style
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RftL.definition: A Bermudan Call Option Style is a type of option contract that can be exercised on specific dates during its life, typically more than one date but fewer than the continuous exercise rights of American options. This style offers a middle ground between the flexibility of American options and the strict single-date exercise of European options.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfuC.label: Credit Arrangement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RfuC.definition: Credit Arrangement (also known as Creditor Priority or Investment Guarantee or Ranking) refers to the security, priority, or guarantee associated with a financial instrument, determining the order and likelihood of repayment in various scenarios, particularly in case of default or liquidation. This classification encompasses a range of assurances and hierarchical positions, from secured arrangements to government-backed guarantees to various levels of seniority and subordination in the capital structure.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rfwj.label: Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rfwj.definition: A COBRA claim is a legal action initiated by a former employee against their former employer for not complying with the U.S. law called the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act (COBRA). COBRA requires employers with 20 or more employees to offer certain terminated employees and their eligible dependents the opportunity to continue their group health insurance coverage for a limited time after their employment ends. The claim typically arises when an employer does not comply with applicable COBRA requirements, which can result in the loss of health insurance coverage for the affected individual and their dependents. Employers can face liability for violating COBRA, which can result in significant damages for the affected individual.
english_labels: Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act Claim

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rg0e.label: Firm Administrator
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rg0e.definition: A Firm Administrator is a non-timekeeping provider who manages the operations and administrative tasks of a law firm.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rg1F.label: L630 Processing (NOS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rg1F.definition: "NOS" = Not Otherwise Specified (catch-all, includes the subcategories) Primarily charges on a per GB, per custodian, or a flat/fixed fee basis.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rg51.label: Amharic
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rg51.definition: Amharic is a structured system of communication, consisting of grammar and vocabulary, used in legal matters, specifically referring to the language spoken in Ethiopia and its legal context.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rg7L.label: Mississippi Workers Compensation Opinions
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rg7L.definition: Mississippi Workers Compensation Opinions are legal decisions made by the Mississippi State Courts regarding workers' compensation cases in Mississippi.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rg84.label: tk_level
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rg84.definition: "The level of the timekeeper. A full list of the codes to use can be found in the LEDES Revised Timekeeper Classifications Reference Document available on LEDES.org. "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rg8E.label: Spanish; Castilian
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rg8E.definition: A Romance language originating in the Iberian Peninsula and spoken by over 500 million people worldwide, including in Spain, Latin America, and parts of the United States.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rg9o.label: E117 Trial exhibits
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rg9o.definition: Trial exhibits are expenses related to the presentation of evidence in a legal proceeding.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgBl.label: Motion for Relief due to Earlier Judgment's Release or Vacation
english_labels: Motion for Relief due to Earlier Judgment's Release or Vacation

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgBq.label: Material Adverse Effect Definition - Exceptions Language
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgBq.definition: Material Adverse Effect (MAE) is a term used in legal agreements to describe a significant negative change or event that could affect the value or operations of a company or asset.
english_labels: Material Adverse Effect Definition - Exceptions Language
Material Adverse Effect Definition - Relational Language

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgDC.label: Verbal Act
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgDC.definition: Verbal Acts, also known as "operative words," are statements that have legal significance or create legal consequences independently of the truth of the content asserted in the statement. These statements are not considered hearsay because their relevance lies in the fact that they were made, rather than in the truthfulness of the content.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgF7.label: Texas District Court - Brazoria County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgF7.definition: A Texas District Court - Brazoria County is a specific court within the Texas District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Brazoria County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgFO.label: Event Scheduled
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgFO.definition: Event Scheduled refers to the status of an event that has been planned and has a set date and time.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgG2.label: Theft from Motor Vehicle
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgG2.definition: The theft of articles from a motor vehicle, whether locked or unlocked.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgGJ.label: L639 Quality assurance and control
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgGJ.definition: Activities and actions related to ensuring that the process and practices used to perform analysis meet an acceptable level of defensibility.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgHK.label: Individualized Restructuring
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgHK.definition: Individualized restructuring involves private negotiations between a debtor and one or more creditors to modify the terms of existing debt agreements. This process allows parties to tailor solutions to their specific needs without court intervention, often resulting in revised payment schedules, reduced interest rates, or partial debt forgiveness.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgHU.label: Suspension of Sentence
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgHU.definition: A Suspension of Sentence is a legal provision where a court imposes a sentence but delays or refrains from executing it, typically on certain conditions. This approach allows the offender to remain in the community under supervision, with the understanding that violating the conditions may result in the original sentence being imposed.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgI0.label: Matter Fees Discount or Credit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgI0.definition: A Matter Fees Discount or Credit is a type of discount or credit applied to the fees charged for a specific legal matter or case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgIk.label: Turkish
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgIk.definition: Turkish (Language) refers to the written or spoken structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary specific to the Turkish language.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgJO.label: TR310 Application Preparation and Filing - Domestic
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgJO.definition: All actions associated with completing a trademark or service mark application (including renewal applications) that is to be filed in the ("domestic") home country or region of the applicant, including obtaining the specimen of use from the client, scanning the specimen for electronic filing, discussion with the client to ascertain the dates of first use and first use in commerce, drafting and revision of the application, preparation and filing of the application by electronic or paper formats, and reporting the results to the client. This section includes all domestic trademark and service mark applications filed on the Principal or Supplemental Register. Note that government fees and external expenses (or "disbursements" in the U.S.) are included under E100.
english_labels: TR310 Application Preparation and Filing - Domestic

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgOD.label: Trial and Post-Trial Motion Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgOD.definition: Trial and Post-Trial Motion Practice refers to the legal procedures and actions taken by parties after a trial has concluded, including motions for a new trial, appeals, and other post-trial motions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgPG.label: Cruel and Inhuman Treatment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgPG.definition: The concept of "Cruel and Inhuman Treatment" refers to a claim made in a divorce case where one spouse alleges that the other has subjected them to severe physical or emotional abuse, making it impossible for them to continue the marriage.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgPO.label: B210 Business Operations
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgPO.definition: Issues related to debtor-in-possession operating in chapter 11 such as employee, vendor, tenant issues and other similar problems

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgQL.label: Recoupment of Public Benefit
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgQL.definition: Recoupment of public benefit refers to the action taken by a government agency to recover funds that have been overpaid to an individual or family under a public benefit program. This process may involve reducing future benefit payments, establishing repayment plans, or legal actions, and is aimed at maintaining the integrity and financial sustainability of the benefit program.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgRC.label: Assault Law
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgRC.definition: Law relating to inflicting physical harm or unwanted physical contact upon a person or a threat or attempt to commit such an action.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgS5.label: Intranet Implementation Services
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgS5.definition: Intranet Implementation Services refers to the provision of consulting and management services for the development and deployment of internal computer networks within an organization.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgT3.label: Expert
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgT3.definition: An expert is a person engaged on behalf of a party or party in interest to a dispute to provide services as a consulting or testifying expert. (A testifying expert would also be a "witness.")

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgTA.label: Time of Performance Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgTA.definition: A Time of Performance Clause is a provision in a contract that specifies the deadline or timeframe within which a party must fulfill their obligations under the agreement.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgTP.label: D.C. Court of Appeals
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgTP.definition: The D.C. Court of Appeals is a court that hears appeals from lower courts in the District of Columbia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgUz.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Berks County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgUz.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Berks County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering civil and criminal proceedings at the county level in Pennsylvania.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Berks County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgV0.label: Billing Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgV0.definition: The concept of Billing Management refers to the process of managing and organizing the financial transactions and records related to legal services provided by a law firm or legal department.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgV5.label: Responsible Author
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgV5.definition: The Responsible Author is the individual accountable for the creation of a document. This person ensures the content's accuracy, completeness, and adherence to an organization's standards (e.g., legal standards, stylistic standards).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgWT.label: Post-Argument Brief
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgWT.definition: A post-argument brief is a written document submitted to an appellate court after oral arguments have been made, providing additional legal arguments or clarifications to support the party's position.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgZ0.label: PA130 Document/File Management
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgZ0.definition: A narrowly defined task that includes creating and populating document and other databases or filing systems, that does not fit under other task codes below. Includes the planning, design, and overall management of this process. Work of outside vendors in building litigation support databases should be an expense under E100. Calendaring (or "docketing" in the U.S.) should be included under the appropriate task codes below for each matter unless, otherwise instructed by the client.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rgb1.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Mifflin County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rgb1.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court in Mifflin County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court system that handles minor criminal offenses, traffic violations, and civil cases involving amounts up to $12,000.
english_labels: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Mifflin County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rgc3.label: Access Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rgc3.definition: An Access Clause is a provision in a contract that grants or restricts the right to enter or use a property or facility.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgcO.label: Georgia District Court - Forsyth County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgcO.definition: A court located in Forsyth County, Georgia that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographic area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgcY.label: Employment Status
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgcY.definition: Employment Status indicates the current state of an employee's relationship with an organization and is generally categorized as active, inactive, leave of absence, or terminated. This status is important for payroll, benefits administration, and compliance with labor laws, helping organizations manage their workforce effectively

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rgde.label: 871 IRS-Third Party 26 USC 7609 (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rgde.definition: Action filed under the Internal Revenue Code - Tax Reform Act of 1976 (P.L. 94-455) Third Party

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rgdt.label: Press Release
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rgdt.definition: A Press Release is an official statement issued to the media and other public platforms by an organization, company, or individual to disseminate news, announcements, or other information. It serves as a controlled method for conveying newsworthy updates to the public and/or stakeholders.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rge3.label: Investment Grade
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rge3.definition: Investment Grade refers to a credit rating assigned to debt securities that are considered to have a relatively low risk of default. This classification indicates that the issuer of the security is likely to meet its payment obligations, making it suitable for more conservative investors. These ratings are assigned by credit rating agencies and generally include ratings from AAA to BBB on the Standard & Poor's and Fitch scales, and Aaa to Baa3 on the Moody's scale.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgfC.label: Application to Employ
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgfC.definition: An Application to Employ is a formal request made by an individual or entity seeking employment in a bankruptcy case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RggP.label: Military Reserve Duty
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RggP.definition: Military Reserve Duty refers to the service in a military reserve force, which is composed of citizens who undergo training but typically serve part-time. Members of the reserve may be called to active duty during emergencies, conflicts, or other situations requiring additional manpower, and are otherwise obligated to participate in periodic training exercises.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgkK.label: Client Tax ID
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgkK.definition: The buyer's tax id number to which provider's taxes are charged.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgkT.label: Environmental Representation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgkT.definition: Environmental representation is a clause in merger and acquisition agreements where the selling party attests to the environmental condition of the assets being sold and ensures compliance with environmental laws. It serves to protect the buyer from unforeseen environmental liabilities and obligations that may arise post-acquisition.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgoF.label: Illegality Doctrine
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgoF.definition: The Illegality Doctrine is a legal defense used in civil litigation that argues that a plaintiff should not be able to recover damages if their claim is based on an illegal act or transaction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rgos.label: Country of Birth
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rgos.definition: Country of Birth refers to the nation where an individual was born. This information is often used for legal purposes, such as determining nationality, eligibility for citizenship, or for various forms of identification. It is commonly recorded on birth certificates and passports.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rgp4.label: Tax Tier Taxable Amount
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rgp4.definition: Tax Tier Taxable Amount refers to the portion of income or assets subject to taxation within a specific tax tier, as defined in the context of Tax Tier Detail.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rgsv.label: Mediation Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rgsv.definition: A mediation clause is a provision in a contract that requires the parties to attempt to resolve any disputes through mediation before pursuing legal action.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rgta.label: C300 Analysis and Advice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rgta.definition: This phase includes all tasks associated with analysis of both the facts and research performed (under C100 and C200) and communicating related opinions or advice to clients. Written communication, meetings, and telephone conversations during which advice is conveyed would all be captured by this phase.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rgtl.label: Shelf Registration
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rgtl.definition: Shelf Registration is a process that allows a company to register a new issue of securities without having to sell the entire issue at once, enabling the company to sell portions of the issue over time. This method provides flexibility and efficiency in accessing capital markets as conditions become favorable.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgvO.label: Georgia Superior Court - Troup County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgvO.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Troup County: A specific court within the Georgia Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases in Troup County, Georgia.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgwX.label: Survivability Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RgwX.definition: A Survivability Clause is a provision in a contract that specifies which obligations and rights of the parties will continue to be in effect after the termination or expiration of the contract.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rh1Z.label: Beans
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rh1Z.definition: Beans are seeds from various species of the legume family (Fabaceae), known for their high protein, fiber, and nutrient content. They are consumed worldwide in a variety of culinary applications and are valued for their ability to improve soil fertility through nitrogen fixation.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rh44.label: Missouri Circuit Court - Howell County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rh44.definition: Missouri Circuit Court - Howell County: A specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Howell County, Missouri.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rh4V.label: extend_data
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rh4V.definition: "Used to provide the name value pairs. (See EXTEND_DATA Segment below) "

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rh51.label: Non-Hearsay Documents
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rh51.definition: Non-hearsay documents are written records that are admissible in court without the need for the author to testify, as they are considered exceptions to the hearsay rule. Examples include business records, public records, and learned treatises, which are deemed reliable due to their regular and official nature.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rh8k.label: Deponent
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rh8k.definition: A person who is deposed in a deposition or makes an affidavit under oath.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhA1.label: PA140 Budgeting
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhA1.definition: Covers developing, negotiating, and revising the budget for a matter that does not fit under other task codes below. Cost estimates which are included as part of other activities, such as reporting an Official Communication from a patent Office, should be included under the appropriate task codes below, unless otherwise instructed by the client.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhBg.label: Financial Concepts and Metrics
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhBg.definition: Financial and operational indicators designed to evaluate the performance of engagements or transactions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhBv.label: Supervised Release
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhBv.definition: In criminal justice, parole is the conditional release of an offender from incarceration, allowing them to serve the remainder of their sentence under community supervision, provided they comply with certain terms and conditions set by a parole board

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhCL.label: Subordination Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhCL.definition: A subordination clause is a provision in a contract that places one obligation or agreement below another in priority, typically used in real estate transactions to subordinate a lease to a mortgage.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhDP.label: Legal Engineering Services
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhDP.definition: Legal Engineering Services refers to the provision of consulting and management services specifically tailored to the legal industry.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhDf.label: Liquidator
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhDf.definition: A person appointed by law to liquidate assets.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhDq.label: EXP/FEE/INV_ADJ_TYPE
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhDq.definition: A type of adjustment made to an invoice or fee statement, as defined within the LEDES98BI V5 Format Rev 1-2020 standard.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhHL.label: New York Justice Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhHL.definition: The New York Justice Court is a lower-level court within the New York State Courts system that handles minor civil and criminal cases.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhIQ.label: PA620 Preliminary Amendment - International
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhIQ.definition: All action associated with revising an application prior to the examination of the application on its merits outside the home country of the applicant in an application filed under PA500, including preparation of amendments and revised drawings that do not affect the scope of the disclosure. Note that Preliminary Amendments that are filed with a continuing application, but do not affect the scope of the disclosure are included under PA550. Also note that preliminary amendments extending the scope of the disclosure in a parent application, and requiring the issuance of a new application number, are included under PA510-540.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhJ6.label: Amendment of Bylaws Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhJ6.definition: An Amendment of Bylaws Clause is a provision within a legal document that allows for changes to be made to the bylaws of an organization or entity.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhJC.label: C100 Fact Gathering
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhJC.definition: This phase includes all initial inquiries, meetings and instructions and the identification and collection of information relevant to the assignment.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhM0.label: Eviction for Nonpayment of Rent
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhM0.definition: Eviction for nonpayment of rent is a legal process through which a landlord seeks to remove a tenant from a rented property because the tenant has failed to pay the agreed-upon rent. This eviction process typically involves the landlord providing notice to the tenant, initiating legal proceedings, and obtaining a court order to regain possession of the property.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhMj.label: Domain Name Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhMj.definition: A domain name claim is a legal assertion by an individual or entity regarding the right to use a specific internet domain name. This claim often arises in the context of trademark disputes, cybersquatting, or domain name registration conflicts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhNl.label: Dangerous Condition of Premises
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhNl.definition: A dangerous condition of premises refers to a hazardous situation or circumstance on a property that poses a risk of harm or injury to individuals who are lawfully present on the premises.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhOD.label: Main Proceeding (Foreign Insolvency)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhOD.definition: A main proceeding in foreign insolvency is the primary insolvency case initiated in the debtor's center of main interests (COMI), typically where the debtor's principal place of business is located. This proceeding takes precedence over other insolvency proceedings and serves as the primary forum for administering the debtor's assets and restructuring efforts.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhPI.label: U.S. Bureau of Justice Assistance
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhPI.definition: The U.S. Bureau of Justice Assistance (BJA) is a specific governmental organization within the Office of Justice Programs that provides funding, training, and technical assistance to support law enforcement, courts, and other justice-related agencies.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhPV.label: Capitalization Representations and Warranties
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhPV.definition: A Capitalization Representations and Warranties is a legal concept that refers to the specific promises and guarantees made by a party in a contract regarding the accuracy and completeness of information related to the capitalization of a company.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhPm.label: B.B.A. (Bachelor of Business Administration)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhPm.definition: A B.B.A. (Bachelor of Business Administration) is a four-year undergraduate degree centered on business and management studies. It signifies expertise in business principles and can lead to various corporate roles

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhSS.label: Neutral Reference Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhSS.definition: A Neutral Reference Clause is a clause in a contract that provides for a third-party to resolve disputes between the parties in an impartial manner, without favoring either party.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhUK.label: Water Quality Rights
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhUK.definition: Water Quality Rights pertain to the legal entitlements and standards set to ensure the cleanliness and safety of water sources. This concept encompasses the right of individuals, communities, and ecosystems to have access to clean and uncontaminated water, as well as the regulatory measures imposed on entities to prevent pollution, manage waste discharge, and uphold the health and environmental standards associated with water sources.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhUj.label: WC530 Oral Argument
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhUj.definition: Preparing for oral argument, Argue an appeal, Travel to & from, Pre and post argument communication re appeal.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhUw.label: Acquiror
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhUw.definition: An acquiror is the surviving company or entity once a merger takes place. Also known as an M&A Buyer, an Acquiror is a person or entity that acquires another company or business through a merger or acquisition, and can be classified as a Strategic Buyer, Financial Sponsor, or Management.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhYn.label: Florida Court of Appeals - 2d District
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhYn.definition: The Florida Court of Appeals - 2d District is a specific court within the Florida District Court of Appeals that hears appeals from trial courts in its jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhZI.label: PA250 Publication Watches
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhZI.definition: All actions associated with planning, completing, and reporting the results of periodic searches for new publications in connection with a specific assignee, area of technology, patent application, or issued patent. For example, this may include watching the file history of published applications for new Official Communications, responses, and/or publication for opposition. Work of outside vendors in conducting searches or otherwise assisting the investigation should be an expense under E100.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhaZ.label: Urethane and Other Foam Product (except Polystyrene) Manufacturing
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhaZ.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing plastics foam products (except polystyrene).
english_labels: Urethane and Other Foam Product (except Polystyrene) Manufacturing

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rhal.label: 530 General (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rhal.definition: Action by a federal or state prisoner currently in custody challenging the legality of confinement or other punishment. This includes claims alleging illegalities that occurred in trial (for example, ineffective assistance of counsel), sentencing (including fines and restitution orders), or disciplinary proceedings in prison (for example, loss of good time credits). Habeas petition under 28 U.S.C. § 2254 or prisoner habeas under 28 U.S.C. § 2241.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rham.label: B310 Claims Administration and Objections
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rham.definition: Specific claim inquiries; bar date motions; analyses, objections and allowances of claims

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rhc0.label: Visa for Specialized Knowledge Worker
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rhc0.definition: This visa (in the U.S., L-1B visa) is designed for foreign workers with specialized knowledge related to the field, products, or processes of their destination-country-based employer (e.g., U.S.-based employer). In the United States, this non-immigrant visa allows these specialized knowledge employees to be transferred from a foreign office to a U.S. office within the same company for up to five years.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhcI.label: Injury by Fellow Servant
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhcI.definition: An injury caused by a co-worker or fellow employee, which may be used as a defense in a civil litigation case.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rhce.label: Mortgage Agreement
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rhce.definition: A Mortgage Agreement is a legal contract between a lender and borrower that outlines the terms and conditions of a loan used to purchase a property, including the repayment schedule and consequences of default.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rhf2.label: Tobacco Liability Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rhf2.definition: Tobacco Liability Claims are legal claims brought against tobacco companies for harm caused by their products, typically involving allegations of product liability and personal injury.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhkG.label: Tax Total Detail Expense
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhkG.definition: Tax Total Detail Expense refers to a specific type of expense related to tax details, which is a subcategory of the broader concept of tax details.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhnH.label: Barley
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhnH.definition: Barley is a cereal crop belonging to the species Hordeum vulgare, known for its versatility and use in food, animal feed, and brewing. It is one of the oldest cultivated grains and plays a significant role in various culinary traditions and industrial applications.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rhoy.label: Contact County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rhoy.definition: Contact County refers to the geographic location of a person or entity's contact information, specifically the county in which they are located.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhpB.label: Usufruct
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhpB.definition: Usufruct is a legal right granted to an individual to use, enjoy, and derive benefit from another's property without altering its substance or depleting its value. Common in civil law systems, this arrangement allows the usufructuary to exploit the property for a specified period or for their lifetime, after which the property reverts back to the owner or another designated party

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhpH.label: Exemption of Presumption of Abuse Form
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhpH.definition: A form used in bankruptcy cases to request exemption from the presumption of abuse, which assumes that a debtor's income is too high to qualify for Chapter 7 bankruptcy.
english_labels: Exemption of Presumption of Abuse Form

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rhpd.label: Employment and Labor Agreements
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rhpd.definition: An employment-related agreement refers to a broad category of legally binding contracts that govern various aspects of the employer-employee relationship, such as Collective Bargaining Agreements (CBAs) negotiated between labor unions and employers to set terms and conditions of employment, Compensation Related Agreements detailing how compensation and benefits are structured, and Retention Related Agreements designed to retain key employees through incentives or contractual obligations. These agreements serve to define the rights, responsibilities, and expectations of both parties involved in the employment relationship.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rhpz.label: Landscape Buffer Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rhpz.definition: A Landscape Buffer Clause is a provision in a contract that requires the preservation of a natural area between two properties to provide a visual or physical barrier.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rhq_.label: TR620 Preliminary Amendment - International
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rhq_.definition: All action associated with revising an application prior to the examination of the application on its merits in the home country of the applicant for an application filed under TR500, including preparation of amendments and revised drawings that does not materially alter the original drawing.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rhra.label: X303 Bates Stamping/ Control Numbers
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rhra.definition: Any Bates labels costs or other type of image or numbering associated with a document collection

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhsO.label: Limited Partnership Certificate Containing Falsehood
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhsO.definition: A Limited Partnership Certificate Containing Falsehood is a legal claim related to contracts and quasi-contracts, where a party has provided false information in a certificate related to a limited partnership.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rhsq.label: Florida County Court - Washington County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rhsq.definition: Florida County Court - Washington County: A court of limited jurisdiction in Florida that handles civil and criminal cases within the geographical boundaries of Washington County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhwO.label: San Carlos Apache Tribe of the San Carlos Reservation
english_labels: San Carlos Apache Tribe of the San Carlos Reservation

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhxD.label: Annual Bonus Eligibility Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RhxD.definition: A provision in a contract that outlines the conditions under which an employee is eligible to receive an additional payment on an annual basis.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Ri0Y.label: Theft from Coin-Operated Machine
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Ri0Y.definition: A theft from a machine or device which is operated or activated by the use of coins.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Ri4L.label: Hemolytic Anemias
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Ri4L.definition: Hemolytic Anemias are a group of conditions characterized by the premature destruction of red blood cells, leading to a decreased number of circulating red blood cells and a resultant anemia. The condition can be caused by intrinsic factors, such as genetic defects, or extrinsic factors, such as autoimmune reactions or infections.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Ri4V.label: Contact Physical Address
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Ri4V.definition: A physical location where a person or entity can be reached, which is a subcategory of contact information.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Ri5h.label: Critical Vendor Motion
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Ri5h.definition: A Critical Vendor Motion is a request made by a bankrupt company to pay certain vendors in full, rather than in accordance with the usual bankruptcy payment schedule, in order to ensure the continued supply of essential goods or services.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Ri5y.label: Squamous Cell Carcinoma
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Ri5y.definition: Squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) is a type of skin cancer that originates in the squamous cells, which make up the middle and outer layers of the skin. It can grow more rapidly than basal cell carcinoma and has a higher risk of spreading to other parts of the body, requiring treatments such as surgical excision, radiation therapy, and, in some cases, chemotherapy.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Ri7B.label: Teacher-Pupil Privilege
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Ri7B.definition: A legal privilege that protects confidential communications between a teacher and their student from being disclosed in court proceedings.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiAR.label: Cryptocurrency
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiAR.definition: A cryptocurrency is a digital or virtual currency that is secured by cryptography, which makes it nearly impossible to counterfeit or double-spend.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiB9.label: Personal Watercraft
english_labels: A Personal Watercraft (PWC) is a small, motorized watercraft designed for individual use, where the rider typically sits or stands on the vessel rather than inside it. PWCs are commonly used for recreational activities, including racing, touring, and water sports.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiEb.label: Physical Incapacity
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiEb.definition: Physical incapacity refers to a person's inability to perform certain tasks or engage in specific activities due to physical limitations, often caused by illness, injury, or disability. This condition can impact an individual's daily life, work, or participation in legal processes, and may require accommodations or adjustments under applicable laws, such as the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA).

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiH6.label: PA270 Status Investigation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiH6.definition: All actions associated with determining the status of a published or unpublished patent application, or issued patent, including application and/or database review and forwarding report to client. Includes annuity and/or maintenance fee status investigations. Work of outside vendors in conducting searches or otherwise assisting the investigation should be an expense under E100.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiKV.label: New Mexico Magistrate Court - Luna County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiKV.definition: A court located in Luna County, New Mexico that has limited jurisdiction over certain types of cases.
english_labels: New Mexico Magistrate Court - Luna County

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiMM.label: Invoice Description
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiMM.definition: A description of the services provided by a lawyer or law firm, included in an invoice for fees charged.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiPQ.label: X142 Settlement Costs
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiPQ.definition: Any settlement costs paid by the law firm or legal vendor on behalf of the client that have not been prepaid by the client

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiPv.label: Blood Disorders Treated by Transplantation
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiPv.definition: Hematological disorders treated by bone marrow or stem cell transplantation involve diseases of the blood or bone marrow that require transplantation as a primary treatment option. These disorders typically include severe cases of leukemia, lymphoma, and other blood cancers, where conventional treatments have proven insufficient or are unsuitable.
english_labels: Blood Disorders Requiring Stem Cell Transplantation
Hematologic Disorders with Stem Cell Therapy
Hematological Disorders Treated by Bone Marrow or Stem Cell Transplantation

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiQE.label: Erzya
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiQE.definition: Erzya is a Finno-Ugric language spoken by the Erzya people in Russia and is a subcategory of the Language class in the ontology.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiQH.label: Bid
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiQH.definition: A Bid refers to a formal offer submitted by an individual or entity to undertake a specific project or provide certain goods or services at a stated price, often in response to an invitation to bid or request for proposal. This process is commonly used in public and private sector procurement to ensure competitive and fair selection of contractors or suppliers.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiQm.label: 400 State Reapportionment (PACER NoS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiQm.definition: Action filed under the Reapportionment Act of 1929 Ch. 28, 46 Stat. 21, 2 U.S.C. § 2a.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiRZ.label: Law Firm
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiRZ.definition: A law firm is a business entity with one or more lawyers and allied legal professionals to engage in the practice of law. It provides legal services to clients, including legal advice, representation in legal proceedings, and assistance with various legal matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiSe.label: Retainage Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiSe.definition: A retainage clause is a provision in a contract that allows the withholding of a portion of payment until the completion of the project or fulfillment of certain conditions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiTU.label: Catastrophic Health Insurance Policy
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiTU.definition: Catastrophic health insurance is a type of health coverage geared towards young adults under 30 and some low-income individuals who are exempt from other insurance requirements. These policies usually have lower premiums but higher out-of-pocket costs and are designed to protect the insured from major medical expenses, such as those incurred from severe accidents or illnesses.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiTk.label: Antidumping Duty Payment
english_labels: An Antidumping Duty Payment refers to the payment made by importers to the government as a result of antidumping duties imposed on imported goods sold below fair market value. These payments are collected to offset the effects of dumping and protect domestic industries from unfair competition.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiU7.label: Irrevocable Power of Attorney Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiU7.definition: An irrevocable power of attorney clause is a provision in a contract that grants authority to act on behalf of another person that cannot be revoked by the grantor.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiV5.label: Motion to Supplement Pleading
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiV5.definition: A Motion to Supplement Pleading is a formal request to add additional information or documents to a previously filed legal document, such as a complaint or answer, in order to provide more complete or accurate information to the court.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiVf.label: Injunctions, Restraining Orders, and Provisional Remedies Practice
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiVf.definition: The practice of seeking and obtaining court orders, such as injunctions, restraining orders, and provisional remedies, before a trial takes place, as part of pretrial motion practice.
english_labels: Injunctions, Restraining Orders, and Provisional Remedies Practice

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiYE.label: address_info segment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiYE.definition: "This is not an actual segment of the file, per se, like the rest of the segments listed above. This segment contains a list of fields that will be used to represent address information. When an address is requested in a segment, that element will be listed and all fields in this segment will be the children of that element. The EXTEND_HEADER option was purposely omitted from this segment."

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiYw.label: Wage
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiYw.definition: A wage is a payment or income earned by an individual in exchange for their labor or services, typically provided on an hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly basis. It represents the compensation received for work performed and is often subject to taxes and deductions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiZJ.label: Benefits a Party
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiZJ.definition: Whom does Contractual Directionality benefit? Example: Party A indemnifying Party B benefits Party B. Example: Party A receiving Party B's goods benefits Party A.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Ridb.label: Data Model Risk
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Ridb.definition: Risk of incorrect decision making due to reliance on faulty or misapplied mathematical models.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Ridu.label: Choice of Forum Clause
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Ridu.definition: A choice of forum clause is a contractual provision that designates a specific jurisdiction or court where any disputes arising from the contract will be resolved.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rif2.label: Queer
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rif2.definition: Queer is an umbrella term used to describe a sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression that does not conform to heteronormative definitions and expectations. The term has been reclaimed by some in the LGBTQIA+ community and is often used for its inclusivity, though its meaning can vary among individuals and communities.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rigr.label: Firm Information Services Personnel
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rigr.definition: Firm Information Services Personnel, also known as Firm IT Personnel, are professionals responsible for managing and maintaining the information technology infrastructure within a law firm or legal organization. They ensure the availability, security, and efficient operation of computer systems, networks, and data resources to support the firm's legal and administrative functions.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RihN.label: Criminal Court
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RihN.definition: A Criminal Court is a specific type of court that has jurisdiction over criminal cases and is responsible for administering proceedings related to criminal law violations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Riij.label: Arkansas Circuit Court - Madison Cty.
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Riij.definition: A court located in Madison County, Arkansas that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its designated geographical area.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RijI.label: Defendant
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RijI.definition: A defendant or respondent is a person or group against whom a criminal or civil action is brought. Actions include dispute matters (litigation, arbitration or mediation) or bankruptcy matters.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rijn.label: Spinal Cord Disorders
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rijn.definition: Spinal cord disorders involve conditions that affect the spinal cord, impairing its function and potentially causing a range of neurological and physical disabilities. These disorders can result from trauma, disease, or degeneration, impacting the transmission of nerve signals between the brain and the rest of the body.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rijo.label: Georgia Superior Court - Mitchell County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rijo.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Mitchell County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has the authority to hear and decide civil and criminal cases within Mitchell County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rijz.label: Litigation Risk
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rijz.definition: Litigation Risk refers to the potential for negative consequences arising from legal disputes, claims, or lawsuits involving an organization or its representatives. This can result from contractual breaches, regulatory noncompliance, intellectual property infringement, or negligence, potentially leading to financial losses, reputational damage, or operational disruptions, ultimately impacting the organization's overall performance, credibility, and sustainability.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rikj.label: Rent Control Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rikj.definition: A rent control claim typically involves a dispute or legal action related to rent control regulations imposed by local or state governments. These claims can arise when landlords or tenants believe that the rent control policies have been violated, whether through excessive rent increases, failure to provide required services, or other alleged breaches of rent control laws. The resolution of such claims often involves legal proceedings, where the rights and responsibilities of landlords and tenants are assessed in light of applicable rent control regulations.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RinX.label: UTBMS MH00 Closing Matters
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RinX.definition: The UTBMS MH00 Closing Matters is a subcategory of the UTBMS Mergers and Acquisitions (M&A) code set, which pertains to the legal tasks and activities involved in finalizing a merger or acquisition transaction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rink.label: Knowledge Management Risk
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rink.definition: The threats and opportunities associated with an organization's collection and management of knowledge, including intellectual property, organizational or operational information and records, and scientific data. This includes the potential for negative consequences arising from an organization's inability to effectively capture, store, share, and leverage its collective knowledge and expertise. This can result from poor knowledge management practices, inadequate systems, or employee turnover, potentially leading to inefficiencies, loss of intellectual capital, or reduced innovation and competitiveness.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rinq.label: Personal Jurisdiction
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rinq.definition: The concept of Personal Jurisdiction refers to the power of a court to hear and decide a case involving a particular defendant, based on the defendant's connection to the forum state, as determined by the legal rules and principles governing jurisdiction.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RioW.label: L600 Identification (NOS)
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RioW.definition: "NOS" = Not Otherwise Specified (catch-all, includes the subcategories) Primarily hourly charges.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Risf.label: Surety
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Risf.definition: A person or entity who promises to pay another's debt.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiuB.label: Proposed Court Filings
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RiuB.definition: Proposed Court Filings are documents submitted to a court for consideration, which include proposed instructions, conclusions of law, orders, and findings of fact, and are part of the trial court practice documents.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RixO.label: Motion to Abstain and Remand
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RixO.definition: A Motion to Abstain and Remand is a request made in a bankruptcy case to temporarily halt proceedings and send the case back to a lower court for further review or action.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rixn.label: Stand Your Ground Claim
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rixn.definition: A Stand Your Ground Claim asserts a person's right to use force, including lethal force, in self-defense without the duty to retreat when faced with a perceived threat. This legal concept is grounded in the broader principle of self-defense and is often associated with gun rights and the use of firearms for personal protection.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RizX.label: Palauan
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/RizX.definition: Palauan is a language spoken in Palau, characterized by its unique grammar and vocabulary.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rize.label: Inupiat Community of the Arctic Slope
english_labels: Inupiat Community of the Arctic Slope

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rizz.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Fayette County
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rizz.definition: The Indiana Circuit Court - Fayette County is a court of general jurisdiction in Indiana that hears civil and criminal cases within Fayette County.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rj1p.label: Traffic Violation Claims
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rj1p.definition: A traffic violation claim is a type of criminal claim that involves the violation of traffic laws, such as speeding or running a red light, and the legal proceedings that follow.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rj1s.label: CLIENT_COUNTRY
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rj1s.definition: The concept of CLIENT_COUNTRY refers to the country of origin or location of a client, as defined within the LEDES98BI V5 Format Rev 1-2020 standard for electronic legal invoicing.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rj2X.label: Fear
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rj2X.definition: Fear is an emotion experienced in anticipation of some specific pain or danger, usually accompanied by a desire to flee or fight.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rj2e.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Stark County (10th Circuit Court)
english_labels: Illinois Circuit Court - Stark County (10th Circuit Court)

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rj3K.label: Motion for Judgment
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rj3K.definition: A Motion for Judgment is a request made by a party in a trial court asking the judge to make a decision in their favor based on the evidence presented, without the need for a trial.

https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rj3z.label: Criminal Fine
https://folio.openlegalstandard.org/Rj3z.definition: A criminal fine is a monetary penalty imposed as a punishment for a criminal offense.
